text: distribution_formats: DICOM medical imaging files (application/dicom), Comma-separated values tables (text/csv), JSON metadata files (application/json), Markdown documentation files (text/markdown); notes adds manifest.tsv per data type and a root participants.tsv, and states all files are readable with freely available software Formats paired with correct MIME types, supplemented by per-collection conforms_to naming WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth and the ESDS ASCII guidelines. Media types are correct for their formats. The format list is coherent with the subcrate conformance declarations; the TSV members are described in notes rather than given their own entry with text/tab-separated-values, a minor structural inconsistency.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: four typed entries; external_resources: https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048 Six external resources spanning documentation, code, community deposits, the governing specification and the trial registration, with the documentation's CC-BY 4.0 licensing stated separately from the data license. All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains. The record identifies an upstream error in which BMJ Open gave the IRB protocol number where a ClinicalTrials.gov number belonged.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms: 'grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; intended_uses permits model development explicitly; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research Reuse rights are affirmative and unusually explicit about the AI case: models trained on the data may be distributed provided they do not contain the data and memorisation risk has been minimised. Not an off-the-shelf CC license, and the record does not pretend otherwise: it names a custom agreement, gives its DOI, and reconciles the FAIRhub label 'Health Data License' with the dataset-description name 'AI-READI custom license v2.0'. The disease-specific restriction is a genuine limit on reuse and is disclosed in intended_uses rather than buried.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: conforms_to_standard: CDS, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS; file_collections each declare conforms_to, e.g. cardiac_ecg to 'WaveForm DataBase (WFDB), within the Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1 directory layout'; distribution_formats give media types Every modality is mapped to a domain-standard format rather than a bespoke one, and the mapping is declared per subcrate rather than only in aggregate. Each standard is appropriate to its modality: DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, WFDB for ECG waveforms, Open mHealth for wearable streams, OMOP CDM for clinical tables, ESDS for environmental time series. Character encoding is stated nowhere, flagged as a low-severity gap affecting the CSV, TSV, JSON and Markdown members.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1'; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; conforms_to_standard lists six standards; external_resources links the CDS specification at https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/ Conformance is versioned and resolvable — the governing specification is pinned to v0.1.1 and linked, so a reuser can verify the layout claims rather than take them on trust. The declared schema URI matches the datasheet standard in use, and the CDS version in conforms_to matches the version in every file_collections entry and in the preprocessing description. RxNorm coding of medications and OMOP concept mapping supply terminology-level conformance beneath the format level.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: 26 entries each with variable_name and data_type, most with unit and measurement_technique, e.g. hba1c (float, %, 'Whole blood assay performed at the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center on stored, frozen samples'); contrast_sensitivity_log_cs carries a derivation ('number of errors prior to the final correct letter is multiplied by 0.04 and subtracted from the log CS value'); moca_total_score carries maximum_value 30.0 and interpretive notes Variables are documented with the instrument, the protocol conditions and, where relevant, the direction of the scale and the derivation formula — enough for a reuser to know that lower logMAR is better and that BMI is computed rather than measured. Units are correct for their measures (mg/dL glucose, mm Hg pressure, logMAR acuity, diopters refraction). No per-variable ontology or concept identifier is attached and the 26 entries are a representative selection rather than the full OMOP inventory; flagged as a low-severity gap. variable_name functions as the identifier, which satisfies the sub-element at the documentation level.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three categories with examples and usage_notes, including the memorisation-minimisation obligation before disseminating models; prohibited_uses: seven distinct prohibitions covering clinical decision-making, re-identification, third-party model-vendor sharing, onward transfer, bulk republication, watermark removal and out-of-institution storage Among the most operationally specific use guidance available — the third-party model prohibition distinguishes prohibited training from permitted short-term prompting under a BAA, and the publication limit is quantified at five illustrative figures per paper. Prohibitions align with the privacy commitments they protect: the re-identification bar matches participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, and the storage bar matches the HIPAA BAA framing in the license. No discouraged_uses block, which is not required given the coverage of the other two.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: true; irb_approval: 'University of Washington IRB protocol STUDY00016228. Initial approval was received on 20 December 2022, with reliance agreements with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego'; ethics_review_board gives the hsdrely@uw.edu reliance contact and postal address; ethical_reviews adds a second entry naming bioethicists Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans and an eleven-person Community Advisory Board; data_protection_impacts: 'No data protection impact analysis has been conducted' Protocol number, approval date, reliance structure, renewal obligation and a contact route, with the approval letter published alongside the release; ethical oversight extends past the IRB to named bioethicists and a community board. The consistency requirement holds: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated IRB detail. The DPIA is absent but documented as absent rather than silently missing, and the related expectation is met because participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is assessed. The reviewing body is rendered as 'Washington University IRB' in one source and University of Washington in others; the record treats these as one body under two names, which is right for the IRB but is the same conflation that produces the institutional-attribution issue.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; method: 'no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary, and ... the project checked that no identifiable data per US HIPAA were present'; identifiers_removed: 'Protected Health Information; additionally sex, race/ethnicity and medications used'; deidentification_details records deIdentType NoDeIdentification with deIdentDirect and deIdentHIPAA true alongside the Nature Metabolism Safe Harbor description A named method, an explicit list of what was removed, and the rationale for the demographic withholding (preventing stigmatisation of findings) — with the conflicting source accounts preserved side by side rather than collapsed. Both consistency expectations are met: method is specified and identifiers_removed is listed. The method is appropriate to the data type given that field suppression alone cannot address imaging and wearable re-identification, which is why watermarking and access control supplement it. The NoDeIdentification-versus-Safe-Harbor tension and the unanswered healthsheet question are recorded as a low-severity consistency issue; disclosure mitigates but does not erase it.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (PHI removal plus demographic withholding); privacy_techniques ('verified ID system; a strict license agreement ...; and static data watermarking identifying the licensee, applied to both the public and controlled sets'); reidentification_risk: 'A theoretical risk of future re-identification is acknowledged. AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification'; data_linkage describes the participant identifier and what the controlled set adds The risk assessment names the specific mechanism it fears — AI inference of individual characteristics — and each control is traceable to it, rather than asserting a generic low risk. Satisfies the expectation that a populated data_protection_impacts block be accompanied by a re-identification assessment. The data_linkage disclosure is candid about the controlled set holding ZIP code, genomic data and medical records against the same participant identifier, which is the honest framing of where residual risk sits.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: 'Written informed consent, obtained either as electronic consent with an electronic signature through REDCap before the visit, or in person'; consent_scope covers open-repository deposit and biospecimen banking, with the FAIRhub consent type and the absence of non-commercial, geographic, research-type and methods-development restrictions enumerated; consent_documentation names the published PDF 'AI-READI Consent_Form_Standard_Mod17May2023_useforpilot.pdf'; withdrawal_mechanism plus consent_revocations state that data already shared remains The actual consent form is published with the release, and the withdrawal limitation is stated plainly rather than elided — participants may withdraw but distributed data stays, and the consent document says so. Consistent with the IRB record (single UW form used under reliance with minor institution-specific language) and with the license's permitted uses: consent not restricted to non-commercial use matches a license granting commercial rights, so the downstream permission does not exceed what participants agreed to.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false, with special_protections detailing the 40-to-85 age eligibility excluding minors, exclusion of pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes, a capacity-to-consent requirement, and incidental-findings management ('suspected retinal detachment, tumour or optic disc oedema triggers immediate follow-up'); participant_compensation: US$200 stipend, paid after device return, not prorated, plus transport reimbursement capped at $25 and rideshare assistance The negative finding on vulnerable groups is substantiated by the eligibility criteria that produce it, and compensation is documented down to payment timing and the retention-support arrangements. Internally consistent: the stated age floor of 40 matches subpopulations (mean 60.8, eligibility 40 to 85) and the exclusion criteria match human_subject_research.special_populations. The incidental-findings protocol corroborates the retinal imaging technician role in data_collectors and the blood-pressure thresholds in variables.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: four entries — race/ethnicity ('Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836'), biological sex ('Male 951, female 1,329'), diabetes status in four defined categories ('No diabetes 776, lifestyle 560, oral 686, insulin 258'), and age ('Mean age 60.8 ± 11.3 years'), each with identification, distribution and a subpopulation_elements_present flag Each subpopulation carries a definition as well as a count — the four diabetes categories are defined by control modality rather than left as labels — and the flags distinguish the two withheld demographic variables from the two released ones. All four distributions sum exactly to 2,280, matching instances.counts, and race and sex reconcile exactly with the per-split counts in splits. source_caveats reconciles the apparent contradiction with the healthsheet's 'No' answer on demographic sub-populations by explaining that the counts come from the release README while the variables themselves are withheld.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances.counts: 2280; instance_type: 'Individual study participant'; notes: 'Version 1.0.0 held 204 instances and version 2.0.0 held 1,067'; total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; per-subcrate file_count values from 7 to 173,721; splits totals 1,576 / 352 / 352 Counted at three levels — participants, files and bytes — with per-modality file counts and the historical trajectory across versions. Arithmetic verified: subcrate file counts sum to 356,334, nine short of the declared total, exactly the nine root metadata files named in notes; subcrate bytes sum to 3,815,969,360,064 against 3,815,969,779,678, and source_caveats explains the 419,614-byte residual as root metadata not covered by the per-collection sums.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: 26 documented measures; is_tabular: false; splits.split_details: 'recommended split into training (70%), validation (15%) and testing (15%) partitions, supplied in the participants.tsv file', with full race, sex, diabetes-status and age breakdowns per partition; subpopulations carry subpopulation_elements_present flags All three components are present, and the split is not merely declared but shipped in participants.tsv with its balancing rationale — the partitions are balanced on variables the public release does not contain, which is the only way public-set users could evaluate fairness at all. is_tabular false is correct for a release dominated by DICOM imaging and waveform data despite containing CSV tables. Every split marginal reconciles: 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280, and the per-stratum sums across partitions reproduce the subpopulations totals exactly for race, sex and diabetes status.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances.notes: 'survey data, clinical data (laboratory values, cognitive and monofilament testing, physical and vision assessments), retinal imaging data, 12-lead electrocardiography, environmental sensor data, continuous glucose monitor data, and wearable activity monitor data ... tabular data, imaging data, and physiological signal or waveform data; no unstructured text data is included'; conditions covered include T2DM in four control categories, pre-diabetes, peripheral neuropathy (monofilament), cognitive status (MoCA) and retinal disease Topics are enumerated by domain and by data form, and the explicit statement that no unstructured text is present is useful negative information for anyone scoping an NLP reuse. source_caveats states that no enumerated topic or substrate term is asserted because the bundle supplies none and no single term spans the modalities — a defensible refusal to force a controlled term. The topical content is nonetheless fully recoverable from the prose, subpopulations and file_collections, so the sub-element's purpose is served.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: six entries including 'the Garmin Vivosmart 5 battery had to be charged every two to three days, producing gaps in the activity record' and the FLIO constraint that 'the device cannot tolerate more than one centimetre of movement'; sampling_strategies documents non-probability sampling with why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy Quality documentation is mechanistic rather than generic: it explains which device fails how and why, and the missing-data patterns are quantified against per-modality file counts. The anomalies and missing_data_causes entries are mutually reinforcing rather than duplicative, and both are consistent with the wide spread in per-subcrate file counts (2,232 environmental files against 173,721 OCTA files). handling_strategy that missing values are not imputed is consistent with the absence of an imputation_protocols block.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '3.0.0'; description: 'this release is version 3.0.0 of its flagship dataset'; status: published Semantic three-part version, consistent with the versioning scheme used across the release history. Matches the version cited in citation, version_access.versions_available and the documentation references; no conflicting version string appears anywhere in the record.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; versions_available: 'Version 1.0.0, DOI 10.60775/fairhub.1, released 3 May 2024; version 2.0.0, DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2, released 8 November 2024; version 3.0.0, DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3, released 17 November 2025'; version_details: 'Each version has its own DOI and its own documentation, navigable from a version dropdown', with v2.0.0 recorded as no longer accessible and per-version size figures Every version is individually resolvable by DOI with its own documentation set, and the record states which one has been withdrawn rather than leaving a dead DOI to be discovered. Version DOIs are sequential under the same valid FAIRhub prefix and match the related_datasets is_new_version_of targets. The withdrawal of 2.0.0 sits in tension with its listing as an available version and a relationship target; flagged as a low-severity consistency issue.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: updates.update_details: 'Version 1.0.0 held 204 participants, version 2.0.0 held 1,067 and version 3.0.0 holds 2,280. Changes between versions are detailed in the CHANGELOG file included in the dataset'; known_limitations: 'The Snellen visual acuity variables present in the previous version were dropped in version 3.0.0'; splits.notes: 'This recommended split is new in version 3.0.0; the datasheet for that version states it introduces no new tasks or labeling but does introduce this split'; notes lists CHANGELOG.md among the root metadata files Substantive change description in the record itself, including a breaking change (dropped Snellen variables) and an addition (the recommended split), not merely a pointer to an external changelog. No errata slot is populated and the CHANGELOG is referenced rather than summarised exhaustively; the in-record changes are nonetheless specific and version-attributed, and the participant counts quoted match instances.notes exactly. The sub-element's alternative of change descriptions via updates is met.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Approximately once a year'; update_details: 'The dataset is released as static versions and is not updated in place. New versions are released with additional instances as more study participants complete the study visit ... Enrollment is ongoing and future versions are expected' States both the cadence and the release model — immutable versioned snapshots rather than in-place mutation — which is the information a reuser needs to decide whether to pin a version. The stated annual cadence is corroborated by the actual release dates (May 2024, November 2024, November 2025) and by the collection_timeframes anticipated completion of 1 January 2027, so continued releases are plausible rather than aspirational.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: eight entries with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details, e.g. 'Topcon Maestro2 and Topcon Triton ... raw_data_format: .fda, access_details: Converted to DICOM for the dataset'; raw_sources explains that raw data are preserved but not shared because they are unmapped and may contain PHI in free-text fields; updates.update_details and notes carry release-specific detail Provenance is traced per modality from the device-native export format through to the released standard, with the retention position on raw data and the reason for withholding it both stated. The raw_data_sources conversions correspond one-to-one with the conversions described in preprocessing_strategies (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, XML to WFDB, .FIT to Open mHealth), so the provenance chain is consistent across blocks. No was_derived_from slot, but this is primary collection rather than derivation from an existing dataset, so the raw-source framing is the correct one.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four responses including 'To create and publicly share a flagship, ethically sourced, AI-ready multimodal dataset on type 2 diabetes mellitus ... including salutogenic pathways to return to health' and 'To establish and disseminate standards, best practices and guidelines'; addressing_gaps: four responses including a meta-epidemiological finding that T2DM studies from 2000 to 2020 lacked racial and ethnic diversity Motivation is paired with the specific gaps it answers, including a cited literature basis for the diversity gap and the methodological gap around pseudotime manifold analysis. The stated purposes explain design choices elsewhere in the record: the salutogenesis aim explains the four-category diabetes recruitment, the diversity gap explains the deliberate departure from US demographic proportions, and the standards aim explains the CDS specification development.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: three entries including 'Pseudotime manifold analysis, an approach used to predict disease trajectories by collecting and learning from complex, multimodal data from participants with differing disease severity, from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM'; other_tasks records that the dataset is deliberately hypothesis agnostic with no labels and a recommended 70/15/15 split for arbitrary downstream tasks Named analytic methods rather than generic AI aspirations, and the hypothesis-agnostic stance is stated as a design decision with its consequence (no labels) made explicit. Consistent with instances.label false and with the absence of labeling_strategies; the tasks are supportable by the modalities actually collected, and the cross-sectional single-visit design is acknowledged in known_limitations as constraining the trajectory objective.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: four entries — National Institutes of Health with OT2OD032644 ('Awarded through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program under the project title Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project'), NIH with P30DK035816, NIH with UL1TR003096, and Research to Prevent Blindness; notes records in-kind device loans from Topcon, Optomed, iCare and Zeiss, research discounts from Heidelberg, Dexcom and Garmin, and Microsoft AI for Good Lab cloud support Both the funding agency and the mechanism are identified — Common Fund other-transaction award, NIDDK center grant, CTSA — and non-monetary support is separately acknowledged. The funding-alignment check passes: purposes match the Bridge2AI salutogenesis project title and the Common Fund mandate. The in-kind support correctly carries no grants block, which is the right representation for donated devices and cloud services rather than a missing-grant defect.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants.name: OT2OD032644, with notes giving 'application ID 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, an award amount of $5,026,499 for fiscal year 2022 ... and a project period of 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2025'; funders[1].grants.name: P30DK035816; funders[2].grants.name: UL1TR003096 Three award numbers plus the fully qualified project number, the application ID, the award amount and the project period — well beyond the bare identifier. All three match NIH structure of activity code, institute code and serial: OT2 + OD (Office of the Director, correct for a Common Fund other-transaction award), P30 + DK (NIDDK center, correct for a diabetes study), UL1 + TR (NCATS CTSA, correct for the UAB translational science center that banks the biospecimens). The qualified form 1OT2OD032644-01 carries the correct application-type prefix and support-year suffix. grant_number_format valid_nih.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: AI-READI Consortium (organizational) and principal_investigator Aaron Y. Lee with ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648 and a ROR-identified affiliation; created_by: AI-READI Consortium; maintainers names the supporting team and contacts; data_collectors documents six distinct roles; notes acknowledges the seven device manufacturers and Microsoft AI for Good Lab Creator attribution reaches the individual level with an ORCID, and acknowledgement extends to in-kind contributors and to the operational roles that produced the data. ORCID is well-formed and the ROR identifier resolves to a real institution, but ROR:01yc7t268 is Washington University in St. Louis while the same record places this principal investigator in the University of Washington Department of Ophthalmology and names the University of Washington as IRB, awardee organization and central laboratory. Recorded as a medium-severity content_accuracy issue; the sub-element is nonetheless met because creators are identified, credited and caveated.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: eleven entries with device and protocol settings, e.g. 'Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph ... with the position recorded relative to supine as 0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees'; 'Dexcom G6 ... capturing readings every five minutes ... Worn for ten continuous days; participants were masked to the results'; 'standard 10 g monofilament applied to three locations on the plantar surface of each foot, ten times per location, with the participant's eyes closed' Replication-grade detail: sampling intervals, wear durations, body positions, viewing distances, filter densities and testing order are all specified, and the custom environmental sensor's capabilities and deliberate non-capabilities (no video, audio or GPS) are stated. Devices named here match those in file_collections descriptions, raw_data_sources formats and variables measurement_technique without contradiction, so the collection account is coherent across four separate blocks.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true, was_reported_by_subjects true, was_validated_verified true, with details 'Verification of data entry was performed where possible, for example by cross-referencing entered medications against medications that were physically brought in or photographed by each study participant'; direct_collection describes EHR-based recruitment screening and extraction of driving records and prior medical records; raw_data_sources gives eight device-native and system-native sources The acquisition modes are distinguished per data type and the verification claim is backed by a concrete procedure rather than left as a boolean. source_caveats notes that no value is asserted for inferred or derived acquisition while flagging that BMI, waist-hip ratio and log contrast sensitivity are in fact computed — and those three do carry derivation entries in variables, so the caveat is accurate and self-consistent.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: seven entries covering OMOP CDM mapping with RxNorm medication coding, .fda and .sdt conversion to DICOM, .FIT conversion to Open mHealth, XML conversion to WFDB, environmental conversion to the NASA ASCII format, CDS v0.1.1 directory organisation, watermarking and PHI removal; cleaning_strategies: three entries including REDCap range-flagging with PI-approved editing, internal PII review, and 'An OMOP Common Data Model data quality analysis is distributed with the release as dqd_omop.json ... more than 3,500 data quality checks' The cleaning protocol states its decision rules — credibility range checks, skip-pattern checks, within-record fills, duplicate handling — and its authority structure, with edits only under site PI approval. A machine-readable quality report ships with the release. No labeling_strategies or annotation_analyses blocks, which is correct rather than missing: instances.label is false with the stated rationale that the hypothesis-agnostic design precludes labeling. The record also states that no instances were excluded at preprocessing, closing an otherwise open question. The DQD artifact is validation of the released data, and is credited here as quality documentation rather than as processing software.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: No software is named for any step that produced or transformed the released data. None of the seven preprocessing_strategies or three cleaning_strategies carries a used_software attachment; machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are absent. The transformations are described agentlessly — 'Topcon Maestro2 and Triton exports in .fda format and the Heidelberg FLIO export in .sdt format are converted to DICOM', 'exported from the Philips device as XML, to the WaveForm DataBase format', 'The Garmin Vivosmart 5 exports in .FIT format and is converted to the mHealth standard', 'each CSV file in the clinical_data directory a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP CDM table', 'Application of static data watermarking' — with no converter, pipeline or library named for any of them. external_resources gives only the organisation root https://github.com/AI-READI. A reader cannot tell what software produced the distributed artifacts. Scored 0: the software the record does name falls entirely in the excluded roles — (a) capture and instrumentation for REDCap and the MoCA Duo application, (b) hosting for FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure, and (d) validation for the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard behind dqd_omop.json. REDCap also hosted the range-flagging through which cleaning decisions were made, but it is the data-entry application named in role (a), and the human edits made through it are not the conversion pipeline that produced the DICOM, WFDB, Open mHealth and OMOP outputs being distributed. The GitHub pointer identifies the publisher rather than naming a tool, which per the threshold neither earns nor forfeits the point. This is the record's one substantive documentation gap and the one place where its otherwise strong replicability claim breaks: the collection side is specified to device-setting granularity while the processing side, which is where 356,343 released files acquired their formats, is specified without agents. Naming the converters and their versions, or linking the specific repositories under the AI-READI organisation, would close it.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: six entries including the CDS specification v0.1.1, the documentation site, the GitHub organisation, the Zenodo community and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048; conforms_to and conforms_to_standard name six standards; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: 'Missing values are not imputed. Missing data that can be directly filled from other portions of an individual's record were filled during cleaning under site principal investigator approval' Standards are linked to their governing specifications rather than merely named, and the imputation position is stated explicitly, including the bounded exception for within-record fills and the fallback of PI-adjudicated removal. Satisfies the sub-element's alternative of explicitly documenting that imputation was not used; the statement lives in missing_data_documentation rather than an imputation_protocols block, which is a slot-placement difference rather than an evidential gap. The no-imputation claim is consistent with the anomalies and missing-data blocks, which report gaps as present rather than filled.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: seven typed entries — representativeness_limitation ('does not include other races and ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans'), coverage_limitation (English-language requirement), temporal_limitation ('cross-sectional and there is currently only one visit per participant'), three scope_limitations (interim imbalance, dropped Snellen variables, finite biorepository) and methodological_limitation (multi-device variation) Typed, with scope_impact and recommended_mitigation on the principal entry, and candid about the limitation that most constrains the project's own stated aim — a cross-sectional design cannot directly observe the trajectories the salutogenesis objective targets. The limitations are consistent with the design facts elsewhere: the English requirement matches the noted recruitment difficulty for Hispanic and Asian participants, and the device-variation limitation matches the seven distinct retinal imaging devices in collection_mechanisms.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: three entries with bias_type selection_bias ('volunteer bias'), sampling_bias ('screening the electronic health records of three academic health systems ... so the study base is patients already engaged with those health systems') and representation_bias ('deliberately balanced across four self-reported race/ethnic categories ... rather than mirroring the demographic distribution'), two carrying mitigation_strategy; future_use_impacts supplies the social-impact analysis Enum-aligned bias types with mechanisms rather than labels, and the representation entry is notably self-aware — it identifies the project's deliberate balancing as itself a departure from population representativeness, and cites the documented difficulty of recruiting Black men into health research. bias_type values align with BiasTypeEnum categories. The sampling_bias description is consistent with sampling_strategies (ICD-10 E11.X and R73.09 screening of health-system encounters) and the representation entry is consistent with subpopulations, where the four groups appear at 380/545/519/836 rather than at US population proportions.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: six entries covering skipped survey responses, wearable battery and malfunction failures, imaging noise and transfer failures, modality-level missingness from non-participation and device returns, Optomed handheld quality variation under undilated conditions, and FLIO discomfort, movement tolerance and light contamination Explains the mechanism behind each anomaly rather than noting its existence — a user encountering gaps in the Garmin record or a poor Optomed image can trace both to a documented cause. Consistent with missing_data_documentation, which reuses the same causal account and quantifies its consequences against per-modality file counts, and with the device protocols in collection_mechanisms. No anomaly claim contradicts the quality controls described in cleaning_strategies.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: false, with sensitivity_details enumerating what is withheld — '5-digit ZIP code, sex, race, ethnicity, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications, and traffic and accident reports'; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false with 'no personally identifiable information is included'; content_warnings.content_warnings_present: false The negative findings are substantive rather than empty: each is accompanied by the reasoning and, for sensitive elements, by an explicit inventory of what was moved to controlled access and why. Explicit false flags treated as meaningful documentation per the instrument. The three flags are mutually consistent and consistent with is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present false and with the description's claim that the release contains no PHI. The withheld inventory matches participant_privacy.data_linkage exactly.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: the UW IRB entry plus a second entry recording named bioethicists (Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans) and an eleven-person Community Advisory Board drawn from the three sites; future_use_impacts: two entries, one on re-identification risk and the countermeasures, one stating that 'because the public release omits sex and race/ethnicity, models developed on it cannot be audited directly for disparity across those groups by users of the public set' The second future-use entry is an unusually honest piece of impact analysis — it identifies a fairness cost created by the project's own privacy decision and describes the balanced split as the mitigation, rather than presenting the privacy choice as costless. The social-impact analysis is consistent with the split design it cites: the validation and test partitions are in fact balanced at 88 per race group and 176 per sex, so the stated mitigation is verifiable in the record rather than merely asserted. Ethical review extends beyond regulatory compliance to community consultation, matching the project's stated ELSI commitment.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers: 'It is hosted on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure'; citation names FAIRhub as the repository FAIRhub is the recognised Bridge2AI data platform, and the hosting arrangement beneath it is stated. Publisher, landing page, DOI registrant prefix and citation all agree on FAIRhub. notes records that both FAIRhub and the documentation site display a notice that the repository 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' — a material availability caveat the record surfaces rather than suppresses.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; license_and_use_terms requires acknowledgement of the licensor, source and funder in any paper reporting use A complete formatted citation with author, year, version, resource type, repository and resolvable DOI, backed by a contractual acknowledgement obligation. Citation year 2025 matches issued 2025-11-17; version string matches version 3.0.0; the DOI matches the top-level doi and version_access.latest_version_doi. Two documenting publications are additionally cross-referenced by DOI in related_datasets.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: 'Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1'; conforms_to_standard: CDS, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; per-subcrate conforms_to declarations; RxNorm coding of medications; RO-Crate packaging with ARK-identified subcrates Six community standards, each applied to the modality it governs and declared at the subcrate level, plus a terminology standard and a metadata-packaging standard. Standards are correctly matched to modalities and consistently declared between the top-level list and the nine subcrate declarations. The project also contributes a standard of its own (CDS), which purposes identifies as a deliberate output.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: documentation at https://docs.aireadi.org/ 'with a separate documentation set for each dataset version' covering citation, access and training prerequisites, the mini-subset, Azure Storage access, per-domain documentation including the healthsheet and AI-readiness considerations; project website https://aireadi.org/; https://github.com/AI-READI; https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; purposes describes a year-long research internship program Documentation is versioned in parallel with the data and is itself openly licensed under CC-BY 4.0, so it can be reused independently; outreach extends to a training program and a community deposit space. All URLs are well-formed on plausible domains. The documentation licensing is correctly distinguished from the restrictive data license, which prevents a reader from assuming the data terms govern the docs.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: relationship_type is_new_version_of to doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; relationship_type is_documented_by to doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 Four typed relationships with resolvable DOI targets, covering both version lineage and the documenting literature. Version targets match version_access.versions_available exactly. The record discloses that is_documented_by was chosen as the closest available term for the publication links because no source asserts a typed relation — a typing caveat rather than a fabricated relationship. Tension noted separately that the 2.0.0 target is recorded elsewhere as no longer accessible.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; prior versions 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2 A registered DOI is present and carried consistently in three slots, with sibling DOIs for both prior versions. Format check passes: matches 10.XXXXX/suffix. Prefix plausibility passes: 10.60775 is FAIRhub's registrar prefix and agrees with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3. No RRID is present, which is not required by this disjunctive criterion.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~2,000 characters) covering 2,280 adults, three named sites (UAB, UCSD, UW), collection window 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, all modalities with their formats, 356,343 files totalling ~3.82 TB, CDS v0.1.1 organisation, and the public/controlled-access split Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: cohort size, sites, dates, modality-to-format mapping, file counts and what is withheld are all stated rather than gestured at. Description content is semantically appropriate for a multimodal clinical AI-readiness dataset and matches the keywords, instances and file_collections without contradiction. The stated 2,280 participants agrees with instances.counts.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection] Nine keywords, above the five-keyword threshold, spanning condition (diabetes), methods (ML/AI), and specific modalities (ECG, CGM, retinal imaging). Every keyword is corroborated by actual dataset content: ECG by the cardiac_ecg collection, CGM by wearable_blood_glucose, retinal imaging by four retinal collections. No aspirational or off-topic tags.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections lists ten datatype collections each with id, path, collection_type, file_count, total_bytes, description and conforms_to; subsets lists three access tiers with ids An accessible landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical resource structure: ten collections with per-collection counts and sizes, and a documented directory hierarchy of datatype/modality/device/participant. Landing page URL is well-formed and its numeric path (datasets/3) is consistent with the DOI suffix fairhub.3. Collection ids use DOI fragment syntax (doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#cardiac_ecg) that correctly subordinates them to the parent.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: four typed entries — is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2, is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1, is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, is_described_by doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child id 4 Version lineage is explicit and typed, with each target identified by DOI and described by release date and participant count. The parent/child relation to the mini-subset is also recorded. Relationship types are used correctly for the version chain. The two is_described_by targets are journal articles rather than datasets, which the record itself flags; this is a slot-fit compromise recorded transparently, not a miscategorisation, and is logged as a low-severity issue.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'AI-READI Data License Agreement, Version 2.0, with Washington University in St. Louis as Licensor (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036)' with storage, secondary-sharing and derivative-work conditions; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Title to the data, and all industrial and intellectual property rights therein, remain solely and exclusively with the Licensor'; data_governance.access_review_process: 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' Access policy is operational rather than nominal: it states what a user must do (verified-ID login, T2DM-use attestation, licence agreement), where data may be stored (institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud), and what terminates the licence. The policy is internally coherent and proportionate to the sensitivity claimed elsewhere: a restricted confidentiality level and a controlled-access tier gated by data use agreement match the restrictiveness of the licence terms.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions list citing the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security best practices and watermarking obligations; other_compliance: not FDA-regulated (isFDARegulatedDrug 'No', isFDARegulatedDevice 'No'), no data monitoring committee, public release de-identified under HIPAA Safe Harbor; data_governance.accountable_organization ROR:01yc7t268 Classification, HIPAA status and additional regulatory frameworks are all present and substantively described, with the RO-Crate's non-mappable 'HL7:2N (normal)' value preserved in notes rather than discarded. Disjunctive criterion met on four of five listed paths. Gap: no data_governance.committee_contact or governance_committee_contact; the only reachable addresses are contact@aireadi.org (maintainers) and hsdrely@uw.edu (IRB reliance). Logged as a low-severity completeness issue. Both the confidentiality_level and hipaa_compliant values are author-derived rather than quoted, which the record discloses; the derivations are defensible and logged as a low-severity correctness note.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available

text: purposes: three entries — enabling AI/ML research into T2DM 'including salutogenic pathways to return to health', creating 'a model and blueprint for developing large, scalable, ethically sourced datasets' following FAIR principles, and workforce development; addressing_gaps: three entries citing the lack of AI-ready multimodal diabetes datasets and 'A meta-epidemiological review of type 2 diabetes studies published from 2000 to 2020 indicated that samples lacked racial and ethnic diversity' Motivation is stated as a specific scientific gap with supporting evidence, not as a generic aspiration, and the methodological purpose (a blueprint for AI-ready data generation) is distinguished from the scientific one. The stated purposes are coherent with the dataset's actual design choices: the balanced-recruitment strategy in sampling_strategies and the hypothesis-agnostic, label-free construction described in description both follow directly from the stated gaps.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: three entries — 'Downstream pseudotime manifold analysis, an approach used to predict disease trajectories by collecting and learning from complex, multimodal data from participants with differing disease severity'; 'Reconstruction of a temporal atlas of type 2 diabetes development and reversal towards health'; general multimodal AI/ML model development across the named modalities Named analytic methods and concrete objectives rather than a vague 'supports research' statement; the first two tasks are specific enough to evaluate the dataset design against. The tasks explain otherwise puzzling design decisions coherently: pseudotime manifold analysis requires participants spanning a severity gradient, which matches the four-category diabetes severity balancing, and a hypothesis-agnostic atlas explains the deliberate absence of labels.

The disjunctive criterion is satisfied on external_resources and conforms_to independently; the slot gap is logged as a low-severity issue.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: six typed entries — representativeness_limitation (urban, hospital-based recruitment; Pacific Islanders and Native Americans absent), coverage_limitation (interim releases may not be balanced), scope_limitation (public release omits PHI, sex, race/ethnicity, medications; raw data not shared), temporal_limitation ('there is currently only one visit per participant, so within-person change over time cannot be studied in this release'), scope_limitation (eligibility 40-85, English-speaking, T1DM and pregnancy excluded), methodological_limitation (Snellen acuity dropped in 3.0.0) Limitations are typed, and several carry scope_impact or recommended_mitigation, so the reader learns not just what the limitation is but what it prevents and what to do about it. The limitations are consistent with, and derivable from, the design facts stated elsewhere: the temporal limitation matches relationships ('only one visit per participant'), and the scope limitation matches the subsets and is_deidentified descriptions of what is withheld.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: four entries with bias_type drawn from the enum — selection_bias (volunteer bias), sampling_bias (EHR-screened, urban hospital-based recruitment pools), representation_bias (with affected_subsets listing the race/ethnicity and diabetes severity groups), measurement_bias (multiple device models per measure across sites) — each with bias_description and mitigation_strategy; future_use_impacts supplies the social-impact analysis Four distinct taxonomy categories, each with a mechanism-level description and a specific, non-generic mitigation (wave-based recruitment adjustment, triple-balanced targets, uniform protocols across sites, device documentation for repeatability). Bias types are applied correctly to their mechanisms rather than interchangeably: volunteer self-selection is labelled selection_bias, the EHR screening frame is labelled sampling_bias, and cross-site device heterogeneity is labelled measurement_bias. The measurement_bias mitigation is notable for reframing device heterogeneity as a deliberate generalizability choice while still disclosing it as a bias.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: seven entries covering survey skips and incomplete responses, wearable battery and malfunction gaps, imaging noise and participant non-cooperation, device data loss and collisions, variable Optomed image quality undilated, Heidelberg Spectralis operator dependence leading to skipped modalities, and FLIO compliance and movement sensitivity Anomalies are specific to device and modality and explain the causal mechanism, including candid statements such as FLIO 'exposes participants to uncomfortable levels of light; because of this, participants may not be at their best possible compliance for this modality'. The anomalies are consistent with missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes, which reports the same device-loss and collision mechanisms, and with the known_limitations entry on the Optomed. No contradiction between the quality narrative and the completeness narrative.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: two entries — the healthsheet reading (sensitive_elements_present false for the public release, with details enumerating what is held under controlled access: 'racial and ethnic origins, location (5-digit zip code), and motor vehicle accident reports, as well as sex, genetic sequencing data, past health records and medications') and the RO-Crate reading (sensitive_elements_present true, listing EHR, wearable monitoring, ECG, environmental sensor, CGM and wearable accelerometer categories); confidential_elements records no confidential data in the public release Rather than choosing between two same-rank sources that appear to disagree, the record carries both and diagnoses the apparent disagreement as the two sources enumerating different things — data-source categories versus sensitive attributes — and states which reading governs for the released data. Explicit false flags are meaningful documentation here rather than an absence: the false value is accompanied by an enumeration of exactly what was withheld to make it true, which is more informative than a bare true. No content_warnings slot, which the disjunctive criterion does not require.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: three entries (UW IRB with protocol number and reliance agreements; four named ELSI reviewers with 'Ethical, legal and social implications are considered at every stage of the project cycle'; Native Biodata Consortium engagement on American Indian and Alaska Native data governance); future_use_impacts: 'no uses of the dataset are currently anticipated that could result in unfair treatment or harm. However, there is a theoretical risk of future re-identification' and 'AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification. To prevent re-identification attempts, the project implements a robust data dissemination system, a strict licence agreement and data watermarking' Ethical review extends beyond regulatory IRB approval to a standing ELSI function and to community-engagement governance work, and the social-impact analysis names a concrete downstream harm mechanism with the mitigations actually implemented. future_use_impacts is consistent with participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, which raises the same AI-inference threat and the same mitigations, so the risk claim is coherent across elements. The Native Biodata Consortium entry is correctly scoped with a note that no Native American cohort data are present in version 3.0.0, preventing a reader from inferring coverage the dataset does not have.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; distribution_formats notes 'The dataset is distributed through the FAIRhub platform'; maintainers note hosting 'on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure' A recognised domain repository is identified, with the hosting arrangement and the specific dataset page both recorded. Publisher, landing page and DOI prefix (10.60775, FAIRhub's prefix) are mutually consistent — three independent signals identifying the same platform.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3', with the note that 'users must follow the citation instructions published at https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/citation, which are the operative requirement'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3 Both a formatted citation string and a DOI are present, and the record distinguishes the convenience citation from the authoritative citation instructions — the third component the rubric notes as expected for Bridge2AI datasets. Citation elements are internally consistent: the year 2025 matches the 2025-11-17 release date, the version 3.0.0 matches the version field, the publisher matches FAIRhub, and the DOI matches the doi field.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE]; conforms_to prose mapping each standard to the datatype it governs; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; per-collection conforms_to_standard on all ten file_collections Seven community standards are declared with versions where applicable, and conformance is asserted at collection granularity rather than only for the dataset as a whole. OMOP CDM conformance is the strongest interoperability signal here and is substantiated rather than asserted: clinical CSVs are described as one-to-one mappings to OMOP CDM tables, and a Data Quality Dashboard artifact is shipped to let users verify conformance themselves.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: https://docs.aireadi.org with per-version selection and a described contents inventory, https://aireadi.org with team, data-sharing-goals and contact pages, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, and the CDS specification; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; notes describe the year-long research internship programme with its inaugural cohort composition Documentation, project outreach, a community collection and a code organisation are all linked, and the documentation contents are summarised so a user knows what they will find before following the link. All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains, and the versioned documentation pattern is consistent across v1, v2 and v3. The training-programme detail in notes is genuine outreach evidence corroborating the third stated purpose.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 with release dates and scale for each; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 with full bibliographic descriptions; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child id 4 Relationships are typed, targets are DOI-identified, and each carries a description explaining what the target is and why it is related, including the note that v2.0.0 is no longer accessible. Version-lineage typing is correct and complete for the release chain. The two is_described_by targets are journal articles rather than datasets; the record flags this itself and explains that is_described_by is the relationship the sources attest. Logged as a low-severity semantic-understanding issue, not a scoring failure, since the relationship assertion is accurate even though the target class is not a dataset.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; prior versions carry 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2 A resolvable, version-specific DOI, reused consistently as the record id and as the stem of every file_collection identifier (e.g. doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#retinal_oct), so sub-resources are addressable too. Matches 10.XXXXX/... ; prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's registered prefix and is consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and with the citation. No RRID is present, which is expected for a dataset rather than a resource registry entry.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~1,700 chars) naming three collection sites, 2280 participants, 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, 356,343 files, 3.82 TB, twelve modalities, the recruitment balancing design and the removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications from the public release Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: counts, dates, sites, modalities, data kinds present and absent ('no unstructured text'), visit structure (2.5-4 hours plus 10 days at home) and scientific framing (salutogenesis). Description content matches the claimed dataset type at every point checked against file_collections, instances and collection_timeframes; the participant count and date window recur identically in three other blocks.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam] Seven keywords spanning condition, method family and three specific modalities; each is discoverable vocabulary rather than project jargon. Every keyword is corroborated by content elsewhere (ECG in cardiac_ecg, CGM in wearable_blood_glucose, retinal imaging in four collections). Coverage is thinner than the modality list — no keyword for OCT/OCTA, wearables, environmental sensing, OMOP or the AI-READI/Bridge2AI programme itself — but the threshold of five meaningful terms is comfortably met.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections: ten collections with path, collection_type, file_count, total_bytes and conforms_to, the root_metadata collection nesting nine resources each with id, name, format and file_type A live landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical resource tree: data-type collections with byte and file counts, and a named, typed inventory of the nine root metadata files. Directory structure described in conforms_to (data type / modality / device / participant) matches the collection paths and the device names given in collection_mechanisms.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 (1067 participants, 2024-11-08), is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 (204 participants, 2024-05-03), has_part 'AI-READI mini-subset version of the dataset' Typed relationships with target identifiers and per-target notes giving release date and cohort size, so the version lineage is reconstructable from the record alone. Relationship types are used correctly and the source_caveats on the mini-subset explains why a containment rather than derivation relation was chosen and why no DOI is given — the one unidentified target is disclosed rather than fabricated.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with storage limited to institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud, derivative and synthetic data bound by the same terms, NIH GDS security standards, automatic termination on breach; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions.restrictions: title and IP remain with the Licensor, models may be distributed if they do not contain the data, copyright '© 2026 AI-READI' An access policy stated at operational detail — what may be stored where, what survives termination, what a derived model may contain — not a licence label. data_use_permission: disease_specific_research is consistent with intended_uses (T2DM-only attestation) and with informed_consent.consent_scope; the licence archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 is a well-formed Zenodo DOI.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions: NIH GDS Policy security best practices, watermark-preservation obligation, export-control questions answered by reference to the licence; other_compliance: not FDA-regulated for drug or device, RO-Crate HL7:2N; data_governance.committee_contact: Aaron Lee, ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org All five evidence slots are populated, including the governance contact the source rubric asks for, with a named person, ORCID and address rather than a generic mailbox. The record explains the tension between the RO-Crate's 'normal' HL7 level and its own 'restricted' classification by reference to verified-ID gating — the classification is reasoned rather than asserted. Counted as a warning, not a failure, because the reasoning is stated.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; data_governance.access_review_process: 'logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms ... access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired ... conditions of access at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; external_resources: 'FAIRhub dataset access page'; third_party_sharing.is_direct distribution via FAIRhub under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element also admits platform access instructions, and these are complete and actionable: the platform, the exact gate (verified ID, attestation, licence assent), the access-conditions URL and the access-type code are all given. A reader can retrieve the data from this record. Flagged as a low-severity completeness issue: a machine client must parse prose to find the retrieval route. The access route is consistent with the restricted confidentiality level and with third_party_sharing.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: DICOM/application/dicom, CSV/text/csv, JSON/application/json, Markdown/text/markdown, each with a description of which content uses it; file_collections.resources formats MD, JSON, TXT, TSV per metadata file Formats paired with correct IANA media types and mapped onto specific content (imaging to DICOM, OMOP tables to CSV, documentation to Markdown), plus per-file formats for the metadata inventory. Partial mismatch recorded as a warning: WFDB, Open mHealth and the ESDS ASCII environmental files appear in conforms_to and file_collections but have no distribution_formats entry, and no character encoding is stated anywhere. The populated entries are correct; the list is incomplete rather than wrong.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: three typed entries; external_resources: nine, including docs.aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org, the FAIRhub access page, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, the licence at doi 10.5281/zenodo.17555036, Nature Metabolism doi 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, BMJ Open doi 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048 Both slots are rich, and the external resources carry descriptions and, for the documentation, its own reuse terms (CC-BY 4.0) rather than bare URLs. Both publication DOIs are well formed with plausible registrant prefixes (10.1038 Springer Nature, 10.1136 BMJ); NCT06002048 matches the NCT8-digit pattern; all URLs are structurally valid on plausible domains.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms: 'non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; intended_uses records the same permission with the T2DM-only attestation for the public version Reuse is affirmatively granted, including commercially and for derivative works, with the boundaries (secondary sharing, model-vendor transfer, storage location) spelled out — a reuser can determine what is permitted without reading the licence. Custom licence rather than a standard CC instrument, so reuse permissions cannot be inferred from a well-known label; the record compensates by restating the grant and the restrictions. The licence-name discrepancy between the FAIRhub API and dataset page is disclosed and adjudicated.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: conforms_to: WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical, DICOM for FLIO/OCT/OCTA/photography, Open mHealth for wearables and CGM, NASA ESDS ASCII guidelines for environmental sensors, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with FAIRscape profile 0.1; distribution_formats with media types; per-collection conforms_to on all ten file_collections Every modality is mapped to a recognised community format, and the mapping is repeated at collection level so a reuser knows which standard governs which directory. Format choices are domain-appropriate throughout (WFDB for waveforms, DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, OMOP for clinical tables). Character encoding is never stated, which is the one gap against this sub-element's explicit mention of encoding; it is not sufficient to fail an otherwise exemplary standardisation record.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to (prose, naming CDS v0.1.1, WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth, ESDS, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape 0.1); conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset Conformance is stated three ways — prose, an enumerated standard list, and the schema the datasheet itself conforms to — with versions given for CDS, RO-Crate and FAIRscape. Standard names and version strings are used correctly; the OMOP claim is corroborated by file_collections.clinical_data describing one-to-one CSV mappings to CDM tables and a dqd_omop.json for the Data Quality Dashboard.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: 20 entries, each with variable_name, data_type and description, most with unit (mg/dL, logMAR, %, log contrast sensitivity) and measurement_technique naming the device or laboratory; MoCA total score carries maximum_value 30.0; best-corrected visual acuity carries quality_notes recording that Snellen variables were dropped in 3.0.0 Variable-level metadata is substantive and reuse-relevant: types, units, instruments and, in one case, a version-specific quality caveat. Enough for a reuser to interpret the headline measures of each modality. Recorded as a low-severity gap rather than a failure: no ontology or concept identifiers (LOINC, OMOP concept_id) are attached, variable_name is the only identifier, and source_caveats concedes the authoritative per-domain dictionary was not consulted, so 20 variables stand in for a much larger released schema.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: two categories with usage_notes and an example; prohibited_uses: six reasoned prohibitions (no clinical treatment decisions, no re-identification or contact, no transfer to third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, no onward conveyance outside the licensee set, publication limited to five figures of representative samples, no watermark removal); other_tasks notes the absence of formal guidelines for user-defined tasks The strongest use-guidance block in the record: each prohibition states its reason, and the model-vendor and watermark clauses give reusers concrete operational rules that are rarely written down. Prohibitions are proportionate to and consistent with the stated re-identification risk and with participant_privacy; no discouraged_uses block, but intended and prohibited uses together answer the sub-element.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews[0]: University of Washington IRB, protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 2022-12-20, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs, approval letter published with the 3.0.0 documentation, contact hsdrely@uw.edu; ethical_reviews[1]: AI-READI ethics team review by Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans; human_subject_research.irb_approval and regulatory_compliance Oversight is documented at the level a replicator would need — protocol number, approval date, renewal cadence, reliance structure, named reviewers and a working contact — and extends beyond the IRB to a standing bioethics review of the release. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated IRB evidence. No data_protection_impacts (DPIA) block exists; the alternative fields carry the sub-element, and the absence is logged as a low-severity gap. The RO-Crate's 'Washington University IRB' label contradicts the UW address and contact it gives; the record flags this rather than silently adopting it.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: HIPAA Safe Harbor; identifiable_elements_present: false; identifiers_removed: 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule; participant sex; race/ethnicity; medications used'; deidentification_details recording the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' statement, the RO-Crate deidentified statement, the Safe Harbor stripping, and that review was internal rather than externally audited A named method with an explicit removed-identifier list and an honest statement of assurance level (internal review, no formal external audit) — the method field is backed by content, not a label. Method is appropriate to the data type: Safe Harbor plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications exceeds Safe Harbor's requirements and is coherent with the imaging and waveform content. The three-way source conflict over whether deidentification was performed at all is counted as a failed consistency check, mitigated by full disclosure.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor removal; participants appear only under study IDs used as folder names); privacy_techniques (removal of sex, race/ethnicity, medications, 5-digit zip, genetic data, past health records, traffic reports; static watermarking; licence prohibitions on identification or contact; verified-ID gating; encrypted servers and locked storage during collection); reidentification_risk ('theoretical risk of future re-identification'); data_linkage (participant-ID linkage across modalities) All four privacy slots are populated, and the risk assessment is candid rather than reassuring: it names a residual risk and future_use_impacts explains the mechanism (AI inference of patient characteristics) and the countermeasures. Consistency check passes — a re-identification risk statement exists alongside the privacy block. data_linkage correctly discloses that per-participant folder structure enables cross-modality linkage, which is the main residual vector for a de-identified multimodal release.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: written, electronically via REDCap e-consent with electronic signature or in person; consent_documentation: signed forms, UW form published with the 3.0.0 documentation; consent_scope: FAIRhub 'ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised', public version limited to T2DM research; withdrawal_mechanism: withdrawal permitted at any time with already-shared data retained, communicated in the consent document; corroborated by collection_consents and consent_revocations Consent is documented end to end — procedure, modality, artifact, scope and the limits of withdrawal — and the consent form itself is published, which is the strongest available evidence for this sub-element. Consistency check passes: IRB approval and consent procedures are both present, as the element's rules require. consent_scope aligns with license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: disease_specific_research and with the T2DM-only access attestation — the consent, the licence and the access gate say the same thing.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false with special_protections (minors excluded by the 40-year minimum; pregnancy and gestational diabetes excluded; IRB protocol records no recruitment of known prisoners and low likelihood of subjects becoming prisoners); participant_compensation: $200 stipend, transport and rideshare costs covered, paid after devices are returned, not prorated, transport above $25 possibly unreimbursed The false flag is substantiated by the eligibility criteria that produce it rather than asserted, and compensation is documented down to payment timing and the reimbursement ceiling — the level of detail that lets a reader judge undue inducement. at_risk_groups_included: false is consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations (adults 40-85, able to consent, English-speaking) and with the exclusion criteria repeated in preprocessing_strategies. The English-language requirement is separately and correctly surfaced as a selection bias in known_biases rather than hidden here.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: four entries (self-reported race/ethnicity, biological sex, diabetes status group, age), each with subpopulation_elements_present, identification and distribution — 380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White; 951 male, 1329 female; 776 no diabetes, 560 lifestyle-controlled, 686 oral/non-insulin, 258 insulin-controlled; mean age 60.8 ± 11.3, eligibility 40-85 Cohort composition is quantified on four axes with inclusion criteria, and the flags honestly distinguish the two axes used for recruitment balancing but withheld at participant level from the two released. All four distributions sum to the stated 2280 instances. subpopulation_elements_present: false for race and sex is correct given those variables were removed from the public release, and is consistent with instances.missing_information and known_limitations.scope_limitation.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances.counts: 2280 with instance_type 'Individual study participant'; total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; per-collection file_count and total_bytes for all ten collections; splits: 1576 training, 352 validation, 352 test Counts at three granularities — participants, files per collection, and split membership — with sizes in bytes, so a reuser can plan storage and sampling before download. Split counts sum to 2280. The file-count and byte-count discrepancies against the per-directory sums are disclosed in source_caveats and reconcile once the nine root metadata files are added, which is a correctness check the record performed on itself.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
