text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence 'to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works, for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; models trained on the data may be distributed subject to memorization safeguards; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research Reuse is not merely permitted but delimited: the boundary between distributable models and non-distributable data, the five-figure publication allowance and the requirement that recipients be co-licensees are each stated, so a prospective user can determine in advance whether their intended reuse is lawful. The record flags a genuine tension it did not paper over - the grant text covers commercial use while the access condition narrows the public release to type-2-diabetes research - and encodes the narrower condition in the controlled-vocabulary slot, which is the conservative and correct choice.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats gives DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown and TSV with MIME types; file_collections carry per-collection conforms_to of WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth and the NASA ASCII Earth Science guidelines, each with conforms_to_standard enum values Every collection is in an open, domain-standard format with the standard named at collection level rather than only in aggregate, which is what makes the release genuinely integrable rather than merely open. Format-to-standard pairings are semantically correct for each modality (DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, WFDB for ECG waveforms, Open mHealth for wearable streams, OMOP for clinical tables). Character encoding is not declared for the text-based formats, a small gap against the sub-element's explicit mention of encoding, not sufficient to fail given the strength of the format declarations.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: CDS v0.1.1 organization plus RO-Crate 1.2 draft packaging, with DICOM, OMOP CDM, WFDB, Open mHealth and NASA ESDS named per data type; conforms_to_standard: [CDS, RO_CRATE, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset Conformance is stated at three distinct levels - packaging, directory structure and per-modality content standard - and the metadata record itself declares the schema and class it instantiates. The prose conforms_to and the enum list agree item for item. OMOP conformance is corroborated concretely by the clinical_data collection's one-to-one CSV-to-OMOP-table mapping and the included dqd_omop.json.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: twenty entries including participant_id (data_type identifier, is_identifier true), recommended_split with its three categories, blood_glucose (float, mg/dL, Dexcom G6 five-minute sampling), moca_total_score (integer, maximum_value 30) with interpretation thresholds, visual_acuity_logmar and contrast_sensitivity_log_cs with units and directionality, plus the environmental analytes Variables carry types, units, measurement technique and, where relevant, interpretation guidance ('lower numbers indicate better resolution'; MoCA below 24 indicates impairment with confounders named). The linking identifier is explicitly flagged, which is what enables cross-dataset integration. Units are appropriate to each measure (mg/dL for glucose, logMAR and log contrast sensitivity for vision). The hba1c entry withholds units rather than guessing, explaining that the source table's column alignment could not be read unambiguously - a correctness-preserving abstention. Twenty variables is a curated sample of a release containing whole OMOP tables, not an exhaustive dictionary; the documentation site is cited for the remainder.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: two categories with examples (multimodal T2DM model development, trajectory prediction, salutogenesis) and the AI-ready usage note; prohibited_uses: seven entries each with a prohibition_reason, covering clinical treatment decisions, re-identification and group-membership inference, sharing with third-party model vendors, onward conveyance, publication beyond five figures, storage outside institutional or BAA-covered systems, and watermark removal Exceptionally strong: every prohibition is paired with its rationale, which lets a user reason about edge cases rather than merely pattern-match. The distinction drawn between prompting a third-party model (permitted) and supplying data to it for training (prohibited) is the kind of guidance that actually resolves real disputes. Prohibitions are faithful restatements of license clauses and are consistent with the re-identification risk acknowledged in participant_privacy. No discouraged_uses are recorded, but the intended/prohibited pair is comprehensive.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: University of Washington IRB, protocol STUDY00016228, initially approved 20 December 2022, approval letter published with the documentation, reliance agreements covering UAB and UCSD IRBs, reliance contact hsdrely@uw.edu; a second entry names Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans as responsible for ethical review of the release; human_subject_research.irb_approval repeats the protocol with the annual renewal requirement; data_protection_impacts records that no DPIA was conducted, as an explicit negative answer A named protocol number, a dated approval, the reliance architecture across three sites, a working contact address and named ethics reviewers. The DPIA answer is a documented negative rather than a silence, which is itself useful information. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated IRB and ethics review. The record flags that the RO-Crate mislabels the body 'Washington University IRB' while giving a University of Washington address and uw.edu contact, and adopts the UW attribution corroborated by both publications and the healthsheet - the right resolution. The absent DPIA is defensible given the record's position that no identifiers entered the release, though a GDPR-style assessment would have strengthened it.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: FAIRhub classifies the release NoDeIdentification with direct and HIPAA identifiers addressed - no identifiers were collected into the released data, and the release was checked to confirm no HIPAA-identifiable data were present; the Nature Metabolism comment describes Safe Harbor stripping. identifiers_removed: beyond HIPAA identifiers, sex, race/ethnicity and medications are removed, with ZIP code, genomics, past health records and traffic reports held under controlled access. deidentification_details: date shifting, non-arrangement and k-anonymity were not applied The method is described at the level of specific named techniques and, unusually, specifies which techniques were NOT used - date shifting, non-arrangement, k-anonymity - which tells a reuser what residual temporal and quasi-identifier structure survives in the data. identifiers_removed is enumerated rather than gestured at. Scored 1 on descriptive specificity, with a medium consistency issue logged: 'NoDeIdentification', RO-Crate deidentified:true and Safe Harbor stripping are three different claims about one release, and the record surfaces rather than resolves the conflict. The source_caveats note that the UW protocol shows the study itself collected name, MRN, date of birth, address, phone, email and driver's licence number under code-linkage is exactly the disclosure a risk assessor needs. Method appropriateness for the data type is only partly addressed: no-deidentification plus HIPAA screening does not speak to the quasi-identifier risk in retinal images and continuous CGM and accelerometer traces, which is why the acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk carries real weight.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: watermarking of both public and controlled sets, strict license agreement, dissemination system designed to deter re-identification, take-home devices selected to capture no video, audio or GPS and not synced to participant-owned devices, study procedures in private rooms with identifiers on encrypted servers or in locked cabinets; reidentification_risk: a theoretical risk of future re-identification is acknowledged, with the license prohibiting identification attempts, extraction of identifying information and group-membership inference; data_linkage: records linked only by study participant identifier, one visit per participant, identifiers held separately under code in the study itself All three limbs are populated with operational detail. The device-selection rationale is a genuine privacy-by-design disclosure rather than boilerplate, and the separate treatment of in-study identifier handling versus released-data linkage is the correct distinction to draw. Cross-field check passes: data_protection_impacts is present (as an explicit negative) and reidentification_risk is nonetheless assessed. The risk statement is proportionate rather than a denial, which is appropriate for imaging and continuous-sensor data. It remains qualitative - no quantitative or adversarial re-identification analysis is reported.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: written, either via REDCap e-consent before the visit or in person, classified by FAIRhub as ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised with no geographic, research-type or genetic-only restrictions flagged; consent_documentation: the approved UW consent form published at a stated docs.aireadi.org URL, with other sites operating under reliance using the same form; consent_scope: covers questionnaires, biospecimen banking for future research and placement of data in an open-source repository; consent_revocations: withdrawal permitted at any time, with the consequence that already-shared data remain in the dataset clearly communicated in the consent document; collection_consents describes the pre-consent enrolment pathway Complete across type, documentation, scope, mechanism and withdrawal. The scope explicitly covers open-repository deposition, which is the consent element that actually authorises this release, and the withdrawal clause states the limit of withdrawal honestly rather than implying full retraction. Consistency check passes: IRB approval documented and consent procedures documented. The published consent form URL makes the claim verifiable rather than merely asserted. The alternative telephone enrolment route for those without internet access shows the pathway was not exclusionary by design.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false, with special_protections enumerating that minors were excluded by the age-40 minimum, prisoners were neither targeted nor likely to arise, pregnancy and gestational diabetes were exclusion criteria, cognitively impaired adults and adults unable to consent were not included so no surrogate consent process applied, and no tribal-organisation recruitment of indigenous populations took place; participant_compensation: $200 stipend paid from NIH award OT2OD032644, plus parking, transit and rideshare costs and rideshare assistance for participants reporting travel barriers, issued after device return and not prorated, with the caveat that transport costs above $25 are not reimbursed The negative flag is backed by a category-by-category account of how each protected class was handled rather than being left bare, and compensation is specified with amount, source of funds, ancillary support, timing and its limits - enough for a reader to judge whether the amount was coercive. Internally consistent: the age-40 floor asserted here matches the eligibility described in subpopulations and human_subject_research. The exclusion of cognitively impaired adults sits oddly beside the MoCA cognitive testing of enrolled participants, but the protocol logic (capacity to consent at enrolment, cognition measured as a study variable) is coherent. The compensation source traces to the same award recorded in funders, which cross-validates.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: four entries - race/ethnicity (380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White), biological sex (951 male, 1,329 female), diabetes status across the four study arms (776 none, 560 pre/lifestyle, 686 oral or non-insulin injectable, 258 insulin), and age (adults 40-85, mean 60.8, SD 11.3); two entries carry subpopulation_elements_present: false to mark that individual values are withheld from the public release Full distributions for four stratifying dimensions, each with the identification basis stated (self-reported at screening) and the crucial caveat that the aggregate tables come from the README rather than from per-instance labels in the release. Every distribution sums exactly to 2,280. The subpopulation_elements_present: false flags are semantically correct and consistent with is_deidentified.identifiers_removed and the scope_limitation - the record does not claim to release what it says it withholds. The healthsheet's 'No' answer about identifying sub-populations is reconciled against the published aggregates rather than ignored.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: instance_type 'individual study participant', counts 2280; subsets: three entries with is_data_split true carrying counts 1,576 / 352 / 352; total_file_count 356343; total_size_bytes 3815969779678; per-collection file_count and total_bytes for all nine collections Counts are given at participant, split, collection and file level, so a user can size both the cohort and the download before committing to 3.8 TB. Arithmetic verified: split counts sum to 2,280; collection file counts sum to 356,334, nine short of the total, and the record derives the nine root metadata files from precisely that difference and labels the derivation as its own. The 70/15/15 claim checks out at 69.1/15.4/15.4.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: twenty typed entries with units and measurement techniques; is_tabular: false; subsets: three entries with is_data_split: true and per-split demographic composition; subpopulations carry subpopulation_elements_present flags; splits.split_details describes the 70/15/15 per-participant assignment in participants.tsv and how it was balanced; the recommended_split variable documents the Train/Val/Test categories All limbs populated and mutually reinforcing: the split flag on the subsets, the variable that carries the assignment, the file it lives in and the balancing rationale are all connected. is_tabular: false is the semantically correct call for a release dominated by DICOM imaging and waveform data even though OMOP CSV tables are included. Per-split demographics reconcile with the cohort-level subpopulation totals for every group. The splits note honestly states the assignment is a recommendation, not a constraint, and that no formal guidance exists for users defining new tasks.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances.data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43; instances.notes: each instance is all data for one participant spanning tabular, imaging and physiological signal/waveform data with no unstructured free text; instances.label: false with label_description explaining the hypothesis-agnostic design; description and subpopulations establish type 2 diabetes across four severity arms from no diabetes to insulin-dependent The condition and its severity spectrum are unambiguous, and the composition of a single instance is described in a way that tells a user what they actually get per participant. The explicit statement that no free text is included is useful negative information. The coded topic B2AI_TOPIC:43 is an unresolvable bare CURIE with no label - logged as a low-severity semantic_understanding issue. The sub-element passes on the substantive topic description elsewhere in the instances block and the record as a whole, not on the code.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: three entries covering survey skips and incomplete responses, wearable battery failure with the specific note that the Garmin required charging every two to three days producing gaps, and imaging anomalies including operator dependence on the Spectralis, undilated handheld variability on the Optomed and FLIO's intolerance of more than one centimetre of movement; sampling_strategies with is_sample, is_random, is_representative and why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation with patterns, causes and handling_strategy stating no imputation was applied Anomalies are described mechanistically - why each modality degrades and under what conditions - rather than as a generic quality disclaimer. The missing-data account names five distinct causes and states the handling rule explicitly. Anomaly causes are consistent with the instruments named in collection_mechanisms (the FLIO movement sensitivity matches the note that FLIO is performed last because it is uncomfortable). The handling strategy is coherent with imputation_protocols being absent by design. sampling_strategies.is_sample: false conflicts with the wave-based recruitment described in the same block; logged as a warning, with the record's own scope qualifier noted.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '3.0.0'; status: published; the description opens by identifying itself as version 3.0.0 A semantic version string, repeated consistently in the description, citation and version_access, with publication status declared. The version matches the DOI suffix (fairhub.3) and the citation string, and the major version is consistent with the record's account of a main-study release succeeding pilot and year-one releases.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available: 1.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.1, 3 May 2024), 2.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2, 8 November 2024), 3.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3, 17 November 2025); latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_details: each version carries its own DOI and its own documentation set at docs.aireadi.org selectable from a version dropdown, and version 2.0.0 is marked as no longer accessible Every version is individually addressable by DOI and date, the access mechanism for historical documentation is named, and - unusually candid - the record states that one prior version can no longer be obtained, which is exactly what a reproducibility-minded user needs to know. Release dates ascend with version numbers and DOI suffixes. The withdrawal of 2.0.0 is corroborated in the related_datasets note, so the two slots agree.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: updates.update_details: 'Changes between versions are recorded in detail in the CHANGELOG file included in the dataset and mirrored at docs.aireadi.org'; file_collections lists CHANGELOG.md among the nine root files; known_limitations records the concrete change that 'Snellen visual acuity variables were dropped in version 3.0.0, so only logMAR visual acuity measurements are available'; preprocessing_strategies.notes reports the CHANGELOG summary table showing v1.0.0 was custom ad hoc processing while year 2, year 3 and the v3.0.0 main-study release used automated plus custom processing; related_datasets records participant counts for each prior version Passes on substantive, specific change information rather than on a pointer alone: a named variable removal with its downstream consequence, a documented shift in processing methodology across releases, and the accrual of participants version by version. Scored on release-specific content per the source-rubric mapping. No errata slot is populated and no corrections to previously released values are reported; logged as a low-severity completeness issue, since silence here is indistinguishable from 'no errata issued'.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'approximately annually'; updates.update_details: 'released as static versions and is not updated in place; instead new versions are released with additional data from participants enrolled since the previous release ... Further versions are expected because enrollment is ongoing' States both the cadence and the update model - immutable versioned releases rather than in-place mutation - and gives the reason further releases are expected, which lets a user judge whether to pin a version. The stated annual cadence is corroborated by the actual release dates (May 2024, November 2024, November 2025) and by the ongoing enrolment against a 4,000-participant target recorded in purposes and known_limitations.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_sources.raw_data_details: raw device and REDCap exports are retained and expected to be preserved at least for the project's duration but are not shared, because they are unmapped to standardized terminologies and may contain PHI or PII in free-text fields, with possible inclusion in future controlled-access releases; related_datasets: is_new_version_of the two prior release DOIs; preprocessing_strategies describes the device-native-to-standard conversion chain (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to mHealth, ECG XML, MoCA CSV); data_collectors names the three site teams that generated the data The provenance chain is traceable end to end: who collected it, on what instruments, in what native formats, through what conversions, into which standardized release, derived from which predecessor version - and where the unreleased raw layer sits, with the reason it is withheld. Raw-source information is carried in the raw_sources slot rather than a raw_data_sources slot and derivation in related_datasets rather than was_derived_from; the concepts the source rubric names are present under these alternative spellings, which the schema-path mapping permits. The stated reason for withholding raw data (free-text PHI risk) is consistent with instances.notes recording that no unstructured free text is present in the release.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: three entries - to create and publicly share a flagship, ethically sourced, AI-ready multimodal T2DM dataset including salutogenic pathways back to health; to serve as a blueprint establishing standards and best practices for AI-ready clinical datasets including the Clinical Dataset Structure; and to assemble a cohort balanced across race/ethnicity, sex and disease stage so models are not skewed by earlier cohorts' imbalances. addressing_gaps adds three specific gaps including a meta-epidemiological review of 2000-2020 T2DM studies finding samples lacking racial and ethnic diversity Motivation is stated at three levels - the scientific artefact, the methodological blueprint and the equity objective - and the gaps block cites concrete evidence for the deficiency being addressed rather than asserting novelty. The stated purposes are borne out by the record's own content: the CDS standards claim is corroborated by conforms_to and the root metadata files, and the balancing claim by the subpopulation distributions and the deliberately balanced validation and test splits.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: downstream pseudotime manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories from multimodal data spanning normal to insulin-dependent T2DM; and reconstruction of a temporal atlas of type 2 diabetes development and reversal towards health from a dataset agnostic to existing classification criteria Two named analytic approaches rather than generic aspirations, each tied to a specific scientific question about disease trajectory and salutogenesis. The tasks are coherent with the cohort design: pseudotime trajectory analysis requires exactly the severity spectrum the four study arms provide. They are also consistent with the record's insistence that no labels are supplied, since both tasks are unsupervised or self-defined.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: National Institutes of Health with the mechanism named - 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project', awarded through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program - plus Research to Prevent Blindness, sourced to the BMJ Open funding statement Both the agency and the specific funding programme and project title are named, and a second, non-federal funder is included with its source. The Common Fund Bridge2AI mechanism is consistent with the OT2 award type, which is the Other Transaction vehicle the Common Fund uses. Alignment between funding goals and purposes is direct: the award title names salutogenesis and the purposes name salutogenic pathways.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: OT2OD032644 (with the note that the RO-Crate cites it as 1OT2OD032644 and a reconciliation of two differing NIH RePORTER links), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096 Three award numbers, with the discrepancy in how the primary award is cited across sources recorded explicitly and the provenance of the two supporting awards attributed to the BMJ Open acknowledgement. All three validate against NIH patterns and the institute codes are semantically appropriate: OT2-OD (Other Transaction, Office of the Director - correct for Common Fund), P30-DK (NIDDK centre grant - correct for diabetes), UL1-TR (NCATS CTSA - correct for clinical research infrastructure). The 1OT2OD032644-01 form is a valid application-number rendering of the same core project.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: AI-READI Consortium as organizational creator of record with nameType Organizational, carrying principal_investigator Aaron Lee with ORCID 0000-0002-7452-1648 and contact email; data_collectors: the three named site teams with their roles and the note that their effort was supported by OT2OD032644 in proportion to percentage effort; maintainers: AI-READI Consortium with hosting and contact detail; funders acknowledgement of Research to Prevent Blindness; external_resources names the team roster page Creator, PI with a persistent person identifier, the three collecting site teams with what each contributed, the maintainer, and the funders are all distinguishable - a reader can tell who made the data, who keeps it and who paid. The ORCID is well formed and repeated consistently in data_governance.committee_contact. The record explains why no affiliations are asserted for the consortium-as-creator (the ROR-identified institutions appear as sponsors, collaborators and locations rather than creator affiliations) - a defensible abstention rather than an omission. Two affiliations are retained for the PI because two tier-1 sources disagree; logged as a low-severity issue.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: twenty entries. Examples: 'Heidelberg Spectralis HRA+OCT ... AI-READI protocols are optic nerve head radial circle high resolution, posterior pole macula 61-line high resolution, and 20x20 macular OCTA'; 'Mars Letter Contrast Sensitivity test ... read monocularly at a designed 50 cm viewing distance with near correction, under background luminance of 60 to 120 cd/m2 and illuminance of 189 to 377 lux, in the standardized order photopic right eye, photopic left eye, mesopic right eye, mesopic left eye, all undilated'; 'Philips PageWriter TC30 ... with the participant reclining or supine and the chair position (0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees relative to supine) recorded'. collection_timeframes gives the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window with the project timeline; direct_collection describes the EHR-screening-to-invitation recruitment pathway Among the most replicable collection documentation possible in a datasheet: manufacturer, model, city, named scan protocols, illumination and luminance ranges, testing order, dilation state, body position. Where instruments vary by site the record says which vary and how. Devices named here reconcile with the device directories in file_collections (philips_tc30, heidelberg_flio, garmin_vivosmart5, dexcom_g6, leelab_anura) and with the anomaly causes in anomalies. Collection dates precede the release date and follow IRB approval.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true, enumerating laboratory tests, vitals, vision testing, retinal imaging, 12-lead ECG, monofilament, CGM, wearable and environmental sensing; a second entry with was_reported_by_subjects true and was_validated_verified true covering REDCap survey responses, with verification described as 'cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed by the participant'; raw_sources describes the retained unshared raw exports; the laboratory mechanism specifies CLIA-certified local labs for CBC on fresh whole blood and the UW Nutrition and Obesity Research Center for assays on frozen samples batch-shipped on dry ice quarterly Distinguishes observed from self-reported acquisition, flags which was verified and describes the verification procedure concretely. The laboratory logistics - which assays ran locally on fresh samples versus centrally on frozen batch-shipped samples - is the kind of detail that determines whether analyte values are comparable across sites. The observed/self-reported split is consistent with the variables block, where instrument-measured analytes carry measurement_technique and survey content does not. Raw-source retention is consistent with the provenance account in Element 6.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: mapping of all data to standardized terminologies and formats (OMOP for clinical, DICOM for retinal imaging, WFDB for ECG, Open mHealth for wearable and CGM); device-native conversion before upload (.fda from Topcon Maestro2 and Triton and .sdt from Heidelberg FLIO converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT converted to mHealth, ECG exported as XML and MoCA as CSV); 'Version 3.0.0 was produced by a combination of automated and custom processing'. cleaning_strategies: REDCap range flagging surfaced in reports reviewed by coordinators and data managers, credibility checks against prespecified ranges, skip-pattern checks, fill-from-record for recoverable missing values, duplicate and omission checks, editing only under site PI approval, PI decision on removal where no correction exists; plus site data-manager QC before upload and central review confirming no PII was included. labeling: instances.label false with label_description explaining the deliberate hypothesis-agnostic absence of labels. imputation: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states no imputation was applied Preprocessing and cleaning are documented as governed processes with named decision authority (the site PI approves every edit and every removal), not just as a list of steps. The absence of labelling and of imputation are each documented as deliberate choices with reasons, which is the correct treatment of a non-applicable limb. The conversion targets match the formats actually distributed and the per-collection conforms_to declarations, so the pipeline description is corroborated by the release structure. The PII-confirmation step in cleaning is consistent with the is_deidentified position that no identifiers entered the release. What is missing is the identity of the converting software, which this sub-element does not require but sub-element 4 does.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Software named anywhere in the record: REDCap (electronic data capture, e-consent, coordinator entry of vitals, medications, monofilament and CBC results); the MoCA Duo application on iPad (cognitive test administration); FAIRhub (hosting platform, 'a cloud-based data management, curation and sharing platform'); RO-Crate 1.2 draft packaging; the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, supported by the included dqd_omop.json; https://github.com/AI-READI (organization root). Processing described without naming software: '.fda ... and .sdt ... were converted to DICOM, and Garmin exports (.FIT) were converted to the mHealth standard'; 'Version 3.0.0 was produced by a combination of automated and custom processing'. Scored 0 under the processing-role threshold: no software that produced or transformed the distributed data is named. The conversions that created the released DICOM and mHealth files, and the OMOP ETL that produced the clinical tables, are described as having happened but the tools that performed them are never identified, so a reader cannot tell what transformed the bytes they download. Every named tool occupies an excluded role - REDCap and MoCA Duo are capture and instrumentation (a), FAIRhub is hosting and serving (b), RO-Crate packaging wraps the release without transforming its contents (c), and the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard is a validation aid for downstream users (d). The GitHub pointer identifies the publisher rather than a named tool, which neither earns nor forfeits the point on its own. The gap is specific and not a general documentation weakness: this record is otherwise exceptionally detailed about instruments, protocols and governance. Naming the converters with versions, or linking the specific repositories under the AI-READI GitHub organization, would move this to 1 without any other change. Slot check: used_software is absent from preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies and every other processing slot; machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are absent; external_resources carries only the organization root.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org with version-specific documentation and its CC-BY 4.0 licence, the project website with team and contact pages, the GitHub organization, the Zenodo community, the Nature Metabolism comment (DOI 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x) and the BMJ Open protocol (DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, CC BY-NC 4.0), and the CDS v0.1.1 specification at cds-specification.readthedocs.io; conforms_to names seven standards with per-modality assignment; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states 'No imputation was applied' with the alternative handling described (fill from elsewhere in the record during cleaning; PI review for removal otherwise) Standards are cited to their specifications, the methodology is documented in two peer-reviewed publications with DOIs, and the imputation question receives an explicit negative with the actual missing-value handling described in its place - which the sub-element expressly accepts. Both publication DOI prefixes match their named publishers. The record notes that the dataset is otherwise self-contained but depends on the documentation site for provenance, variable and format detail - an accurate statement of the dependency, and one that makes the CC-BY licensing of that documentation material.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: six typed entries - representativeness (urban, hospital-based recruitment, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans), coverage (English-language eligibility, with the reason that all materials and device instructions would have needed translation), temporal (cross-sectional, one visit, the ten-day window as the only longitudinal element, part-way through a 4,000-participant target), scope (public release omits sex, race, ethnicity, medications, ZIP, genomics, past health records and traffic reports; biospecimens excluded), methodological (no labels or targets, no guidance for users creating labels) and integration (Snellen visual acuity dropped in 3.0.0) Six distinct limitation types, each typed, most carrying an explicit scope_impact or recommended_mitigation. The scope entry states the operational consequence - users cannot stratify by sex or race/ethnicity or audit models for disparities - rather than merely listing what is absent. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere in the record: the withheld fields match is_deidentified.identifiers_removed, the cross-sectional design matches relationships ('one study visit per participant, so instances are not linked across visits'), and the Snellen removal matches the variables block, which carries only visual_acuity_logmar.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: four entries typed selection_bias (volunteer bias, with the note that the protocol 'describes no measure taken against it'), representation_bias (urban hospital-based recruitment, missing Pacific Islanders and Native Americans, English-language requirement; mitigated by three geographically distinct sites), sampling_bias (pilot release unbalanced, interim releases may not achieve balance; affected_subsets naming v3.0.0 and noting the training partition is unbalanced while validation and test are balanced; mitigated by uniform protocols across sites) and measurement_bias (blood pressure monitors and lensometers differ by site, imaging across multiple manufacturers, so device may be confounded with site; mitigated by documenting make, model and scan modality); future_use_impacts adds the downstream social-impact analysis Four recognized bias categories with mitigation attached to three and an explicit admission that no mitigation exists for the fourth. The affected_subsets field pinpointing the training partition as the unbalanced one is unusually precise. The sampling_bias claim about split balance is verifiable in the record and checks out: validation and test carry 88 per race/ethnicity group and 176 per sex, while training does not. The measurement_bias entry is consistent with the multiple device models named in collection_mechanisms.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: survey skips and incomplete responses; wearable improper use and technical failure, with the Garmin's two-to-three-day charging requirement producing gaps in the activity record; imaging anomalies covering participant uncooperation, obscuring noise, system malfunction and transfer failures, plus device-specific issues - undilated handheld Optomed variability within and between participants, operator-dependent Spectralis acquisition that could lead to a skipped modality, and FLIO's intolerance of more than one centimetre of movement combined with its position last in an uncomfortable visit Mechanistic rather than generic: each anomaly is tied to the instrument or procedure that causes it and to the resulting data defect, which lets a user anticipate where gaps and artefacts will appear. Anomaly causes reconcile with missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes and with instances.missing_information, so the three slots tell one coherent story rather than three unrelated ones.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: true, with the RO-Crate enumeration of categories - electronic health record data, wearable monitoring, ECG, environmental sensor data, continuous glucose monitor data and wearable accelerometer data - and a source_caveats recording the contrary FAIRhub healthsheet position that the public dataset contains no sensitive data, locating race and ethnicity, ZIP code, genomics, past health records, medications and traffic reports in the controlled-access release; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false with the HL7:2N classification The categories of sensitive content are enumerated rather than gestured at, and the conflicting source position is recorded in full rather than suppressed, so a reader can form their own view. The affirmative flag with an enumerated category list is the more defensible reading for a release containing retinal images and continuous physiological streams. Logged as a low-severity consistency warning that sensitive_elements_present: true and confidential_elements_present: false coexist without adjudication. No separate content_warnings slot is populated, which is of little consequence for clinical measurement data containing no distressing media.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: the UW IRB entry with protocol, date and reliance architecture, plus a second entry naming Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans as responsible for ethical review of the release and recording that ELSI considerations run through every stage of the project cycle with bioethicist guidance in the standards work; future_use_impacts: no currently anticipated unfair-treatment or harm uses but an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk; and the analysis that withholding sex, race and ethnicity from the public release prevents users from stratifying or auditing model performance across those groups, mitigated by a recommended split whose validation and test sets are balanced for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status with the stated aim of reducing model disparities The social-impact limb is the strongest part of this element: it identifies a genuine tension between privacy protection and fairness auditing, states the harm that follows, and describes a concrete design response. Named ethics reviewers, rather than an anonymous committee, make the oversight claim checkable. The fairness-auditing impact is consistent with the scope_limitation in known_limitations and with is_deidentified.identifiers_removed, and the mitigation is verifiable in the subsets block, where the validation and test splits are indeed demographically balanced.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers describes FAIRhub as a platform running on Microsoft Azure 'developed for this project as a cloud-based data management, curation and sharing platform'; third_party_sharing confirms public distribution through FAIRhub The hosting platform is named, resolvable and consistent with the DOI prefix, and the record additionally explains what the platform is and on what infrastructure it runs. FAIRhub is a recognized Bridge2AI data platform and the 10.60775 DOI prefix is registered to it, so publisher, page and DOI mutually corroborate. The record discloses that the RO-Crate names the AI-READI Consortium as publisher instead, and explains that it followed the FAIRhub structured metadata and recorded the platform URL in the uriorcurie-ranged slot in place of the bare name - a transparent handling of both the source conflict and the range coercion.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access lists a distinct DOI per version A complete, correctly formed data-citation string with creator, year, title, version, resource type, repository and resolvable DOI - directly usable without reconstruction. Every component of the citation agrees with the corresponding slot: creator matches creators, year matches issued 2025-11-17, version matches version, repository matches publisher and the DOI matches doi. Version-level DOIs make precise cross-referencing possible.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to names CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2 draft, DICOM, OMOP CDM, WFDB, Open mHealth and the NASA ASCII File Format Guidelines for Earth Science Data, each assigned to the data type it governs; conforms_to_standard carries the same seven as enum values; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; per-collection conforms_to repeats the assignment at collection level Seven community standards spanning packaging, structure, imaging, clinical modelling, waveforms, mobile health and environmental data, each bound to specific content rather than listed in aggregate. Standard-to-modality assignments are all semantically correct, and the collection-level declarations agree with the dataset-level ones. Using the ESDS guidelines for indoor environmental sensor readings is an unusual but defensible reuse of an Earth-science format convention.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org with a per-version documentation set ('see "Dataset v3.0.0" for this version') under CC-BY 4.0, aireadi.org with team and contact pages, the GitHub organization, the Zenodo community, and the two publications; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers points to the README, https://aireadi.org/contact and contact@aireadi.org; file_collections lists README.md, healthsheet.md and CHANGELOG.md at the release root Documentation exists at three tiers - in-release README and healthsheet, a versioned external documentation site, and peer-reviewed publications - with contact routes and a community presence. The record also states what the documentation is needed for, which is more useful than a bare link list. All URLs are structurally valid on plausible project-controlled domains. Version-specific documentation is the correct pattern for a dataset with immutable versioned releases, and it corroborates the version_access claim of a documentation dropdown.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of 10.60775/fairhub.2 (8 November 2024, 1,067 participants, recorded as no longer accessible), is_new_version_of 10.60775/fairhub.1 (3 May 2024, 204 pilot participants, custom ad hoc processing), is_source_of the AI-READI mini-subset (FAIRhub child dataset 4, for pipeline development), is_supplemented_by the AI-READI controlled-access dataset with its withheld-field inventory and access conditions Four relationships using three distinct relationship types, each annotated with dates, counts or content so the relationship is interpretable rather than merely asserted. Version targets carry resolvable DOIs in the same series. For the two targets with no identifier in the sources, the record names them in prose and says explicitly that no DOI is given - preferable to fabricating an identifier. Participant counts across the version chain (204, 1,067, 2,280) are monotonic and consistent with ongoing accrual.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset. No doi field; no RRID. source_caveats: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset.' The only identifier is the project homepage with a '#dataset' fragment, which identifies a web page rather than a dataset release and carries no resolver or persistence commitment. Nothing distinguishes the 50,000-admission current release from the anticipated 100,000-admission final dataset at the same URI. DOI pattern 10.XXXX/... : absent. RRID pattern RRID:SCR_/AB_ : absent. URI resolves syntactically but fails the persistence criterion, so the sub-element's semantic check is not satisfied.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description is ~1,900 characters covering contributing sites (14 of 20 academic centers), nine modalities, per-modality formats, scale figures, storage architecture and the sequestered holdout set. Far beyond the 200-character threshold and non-boilerplate throughout: it states what is released, in what format, at what scale, and what is still in process as of August 2025. Title and description agree on programme (Bridge2AI), domain (acute/critical care) and access posture (controlled). No semantic drift between them.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [critical care, acute illness, critical illness, electronic health record, OMOP Common Data Model, waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, imaging, clinical notes, social determinants of health, multimodality, AI-ready data set, Bridge2AI] Thirteen keywords spanning clinical domain, modality, standard and programme — well above the five-keyword threshold and each one discriminating. Every keyword is corroborated by content elsewhere in the record (OMOP in conforms_to, EEG in acquisition_methods, SDOH in raw_data_sources); none is aspirational filler.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; external_resources describes it as 'the public-facing CHoRUS project webpage, with pages on the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources'. A real, described landing page with an enumerated site structure. The `resources` slot for nested sub-resources is unused, so the nine modalities are not exposed as addressable child resources, but the landing page alone satisfies the sub-element. Domain chorus4ai.org is plausible and consistent with id and external_resources. The record also notes a site banner about review for potential modification, which is a caveat on stability rather than on existence.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: No parent_datasets and no related_datasets fields anywhere in the record. The dataset is explicitly one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and explicitly provisions a sequestered holdout test set (splits), so at least two typed relationships exist in substance but none is expressed. `splits` carries a prose note only, with no typed link. Cross-check against splits and description confirms real relationships that the structured fields do not represent — an expressivity gap, not an absence of relationships in the world.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Every data modality is released under controlled access rather than an open license. Users must sign a licensing agreement before gaining access... access through the AIM-AHEAD training program additionally requires a ".edu" email address.' notes clarifies that the MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses 'govern the CHoRUS software repositories and not the dataset itself.' An unambiguous and actionable access policy: a prospective user learns that no open license exists, that a signed agreement is a precondition, and — importantly — that the repository licenses they might find on GitHub do not apply to the data. The software/data license disambiguation is a genuine quality signal rarely present. Consistent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', third_party_sharing.is_shared true under controlled access, and confidential_elements. ip_restrictions is unpopulated but the licensing terms carry the substance.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; regulatory_restrictions lists 'Access to all data modalities is controlled and conditional on a signed licensing agreement' and 'The project establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape'. data_governance.committee_contact: Jared Houghtaling; access_review_process names dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. A sensitivity classification, two stated constraints, and a named governance contact with reachable addresses and a described review workflow (general route and AIM-AHEAD training route). Sufficient for the sub-element, though hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unstated for data derived from US hospital PHI, and the record concedes no committee, decision timeframe or appeal process is named. Classification 'restricted' is proportionate to the content (critically ill patients' records including notes, imaging, waveforms and geographic SDOH). Missing HIPAA status is recorded as a completeness warning rather than a contradiction.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: No download_url field. data_governance.access_review_process directs requests to 'dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org'; description states 'OMOP and telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave' without naming or linking that enclave. Access instructions exist and are procedurally specific, but there is no download URL, no request portal and no link to the hosting platform — the enclave is described but never identified. Retrieval depends entirely on emailing two individuals, which is neither a durable nor a machine-actionable access path. Contrast with the well-formed links present elsewhere (page, GitHub org, NIH RePORTER) confirms this is a genuine gap in the access chain rather than a formatting artefact.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: 'OMOP Common Data Model tables' (with flowsheet extensions), 'OHNLP open source schema' (tokenized notes), 'DICOM' (imaging from PACS), 'WFDB' (telemetry, 'a PhysioNet schema extended'), 'EDF+ and Persyst' (EEG). Five formats, each bound to the modality it carries and each annotated. Media types and byte sizes are absent, but a user can tell exactly what software they need per modality. Each format is the domain-standard container for its modality and matches raw_data_sources.raw_data_format entry for entry. The 'extended WFDB' and flowsheet-extension caveats are disclosed rather than hidden behind a bare standard name.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: external_resources lists https://chorus4ai.org/, https://github.com/chorus-ai ('28 repositories of software and tooling for clinical data, validated semantic mappings, standard operating protocols'), https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824, and 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'. Four distinct, described external resources covering documentation, code, funding provenance and programme context. related_datasets is empty, but the sub-element is satisfied by the external resources. Three of four URLs are well-formed and the domains are plausible and verifiable in kind; the fourth lacks a scheme and is flagged as reproduced verbatim from the source.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms (controlled access, signed licensing agreement, '.edu' requirement for the AIM-AHEAD route, with the note that program administrators assist and the requirement 'is not a barrier to acceptance'); notes separating software licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0) from the dataset. Reuse is permitted and the conditions for it are stated precisely enough to act on, including who may apply and what they must sign. No named license instrument or DUA template is linked and no term expresses downstream redistribution or publication rules, which is the main shortfall. Restrictiveness is proportionate to the content and consistent with confidentiality_level 'restricted'. The one tension is with purposes' claim of a 'publicly available' dataset, recorded as a content_accuracy issue.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: OMOP CDM tables, OHNLP open source schema, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. Every released modality uses an established community format, which is the strongest interoperability signal in the record. Character encoding is never stated — a real gap for the tokenized note outputs and for OMOP text columns. Formats are correctly matched to modalities and consistently reported across description, distribution_formats, raw_data_sources and preprocessing_strategies. Persyst is a proprietary format, which slightly qualifies 'standardized' for EEG; this is visible in the record.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'Structured EHR data conform to the OMOP Common Data Model (with extensions for nursing flowsheets); imaging conforms to DICOM; waveform telemetry conforms to WFDB...; EEG conforms to EDF+ and Persyst; tokenized clinical notes conform to the OHNLP open source schema.' conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Per-modality conformance rather than a single blanket claim, plus the metadata schema the record itself conforms to. The disclosed extensions (flowsheets, 'extended' WFDB) are exactly the information an integrator needs. All named standards exist and are used correctly for their modality; OMOP is the appropriate CDM for structured EHR harmonization across 14 hospitals. The single OTHER enum term covering three standards is an expressivity limitation, disclosed in source_caveats.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field. The closest content is instances entries carrying data_substrate and data_topic codes (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37, B2AI_TOPIC:9, etc.) at the modality level, not the variable level. No data dictionary, no column list, no waveform channel inventory, no token-schema field list. OMOP conformance supplies column semantics for the standard structured tables by reference, but the nursing-flowsheet extensions, the OHNLP token schema and the telemetry/EEG channel sets are precisely the parts that are local and therefore precisely the parts left undocumented. Cross-check with the claim of 1.6 billion OMOP rows across nine modalities shows the scale at which this omission bites; recorded as a high-severity completeness issue.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three use categories — ML/AI model development for acute and critical care (with examples 'Prediction of complications and deterioration', 'Measurement of treatment response'), external validation against the holdout set, and training/workforce development in the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud with Jupyter notebooks and OHDSI/OMOP instruction. Concrete, category-typed guidance with worked examples and usage notes. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent, which for a controlled-access critical-care dataset including neonates is a notable omission (no statement on re-identification attempts, clinical deployment without validation, or commercial use), but the positive guidance is substantive enough to pass. intended_uses align with tasks and purposes without contradiction, and the training use is corroborated by existing_uses (AIM-AHEAD Cohort 2, up to 30 trainees).

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews (2 entries) name reviewing_organization 'CHoRUS consortium' and describe 'community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing' and an 'Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)' pillar. Their own source_caveats: 'The bundle names no IRB, ethics committee, or approval identifier, and does not state that any body performed a formal ethical review of the dataset.' data_protection_impacts absent. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: true. What is documented is ethics *activity* by the project (community engagement, legal-landscape analysis) — genuine and non-boilerplate, but it is not oversight of this dataset. For a 50,000-admission multicenter extraction of identifiable clinical records including minors, no IRB, no approval or exemption number, no waiver determination, no site-level oversight statement and no DPIA are recorded. The mandatory semantic check for involves_human_subjects=true is therefore unmet. The named governance contact is, by the record's own caveat, an access contact who is not stated to chair or sit on any body. FAILED consistency check: involves_human_subjects=true with no ethics approval evidence. Also failed: data_protection_impacts absent despite restricted, high-sensitivity human data.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP toolkit, retention of clinical notes at the local site with only tokens released, de-identification of imaging (in process for the larger cohort as of August 2025), and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification.' deidentification_details adds the August 2025 imaging status. Method is described per modality with named tooling, and the architectural choice (notes never leave the site; only tokens centralize) is a concrete, verifiable control rather than a slogan. Against that: no recognized determination is named (neither HIPAA Safe Harbor nor Expert Determination), no identifiers_removed list is given, 'approaches that limit re-identification' is vague for the structured and waveform data, and the record concedes it 'does not state whether identifiable elements remain present'. Passes on the strength of the modality-specific, tool-named content. Method appropriateness: tokenization plus local retention is well matched to free-text re-identification risk, and DICOM de-identification is the right control for imaging. Appropriateness for structured EHR and for date/geography (SDOH includes distance to nearest hospital, a quasi-identifier) is not established — recorded as a warning.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: 'Tokenization of unstructured EHR text; Local retention of clinical notes at contributing sites, with only tokens centralized; A privacy scan tool for medical records, maintained in the privacy_scan_tool repository; A de-identification component maintained in the CTP-deid repository.' reidentification_risk: 'The project transforms data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused ethics and legal work determines the approaches used to manage privacy.' Four named, locatable protections — two of them specific code artefacts a reuser could inspect — carry this sub-element. The re-identification *risk assessment* half does not: the reidentification_risk text restates the mitigation without characterizing residual risk, naming a threat model, or reporting any quantitative measure. Scored 1 for the protections while flagging the risk statement as circular. WARNING: reidentification_risk is non-assessive. The record's own caveat that CTP-deid has no description in the source is a further limit on what a reuser can verify. Protections are nonetheless consistent with is_deidentified and with the local-retention architecture stated in description and raw_data_sources.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: No informed_consent field anywhere in the record. direct_collection.is_direct is false with collection_details 'clinical data are extracted from hospital clinical systems... rather than gathered directly from patients for research purposes', but no consent basis follows from that statement. For retrospective EHR extraction the expected documentation is a waiver of informed consent or a broad-consent/opt-out basis, together with the body that authorized it. None is recorded — not the consent type, not the waiver, not any withdrawal mechanism for patients whose records were extracted. Nothing tells a reuser on what legal basis these records may be analysed. FAILED consistency check: involves_human_subjects=true with no consent or waiver documentation, compounding the missing ethics approval in sub-element 1.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: No at_risk_populations field and no participant_compensation field. The only related content is human_subject_research.special_populations: 'The cohort consists of acutely and critically ill hospital patients, and the released admissions include pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) patients.' The vulnerable populations are correctly identified — critically ill adults, children and neonates — but identification is where the documentation stops. No additional safeguard for minors is described (no parental-permission basis, no age-shifting, no restricted-access tier for pediatric records), and compensation is neither reported nor declared inapplicable. The sub-element asks for protections and compensation documented, and neither is. FAILED consistency check: special_populations names minors while the dedicated at_risk_populations and participant_compensation slots are empty and no protective measure appears in any other field.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations (2 entries, both with subpopulation_elements_present: true): 'Admissions in the current release are drawn from adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric intensive care (PICU), and neonatal intensive care (NICU) settings'; and 'Demographics are captured as one of the nine data modalities and standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; social determinants of health and contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are acquired alongside them.' Identifies three clinically meaningful care-setting strata spanning neonatal to adult, and states that demographic and SDOH attributes are available for further stratification. It stops short of any actual composition — no age, sex, race/ethnicity or payer distribution, and no inclusion/exclusion criteria — so a reuser can name the strata but cannot judge their balance. Consistent with description (ICU/PICU/NICU), with human_subject_research.special_populations, and with known_biases' representation concern. The absence of distributions is what makes the representation_bias entry hard to verify.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: 50,000 'Patient admission from ICU, PICU, and NICU'; 1,600,000,000 'Row of EHR data in the OMOP Common Data Model'; 7,642 'Admission with radiology data'; waveform telemetry recordings noted as '23 Tb of waveform data'; plus EEG recordings and tokenized notes as instance types. Counts are specific, given per instance type rather than as a single headline, and are accompanied by explicit source_caveats recording where the tier-2 and tier-4 sources disagree (50,000 vs 'over 45K'; 7,642 admissions with radiology vs 1000 images, in different units). Two instance types carry no count, but the reported figures are ample and honestly qualified. Counts are internally consistent with the description and mutually plausible (7,642 radiology admissions is a credible subset of 50,000; 1.6e9 OMOP rows is ~32,000 rows per admission, plausible for high-frequency flowsheet and medication data). The disclosed conflict is recorded as a low-severity warning.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables absent. is_tabular: false (an explicit, meaningful flag for a multimodal release). splits: 'The dataset provisions a holdout test set, sequestered from the released data and accessible for external validation of models.' No subsets.is_data_split or is_subpopulation flags; subpopulations carry subpopulation_elements_present: true. Two of the four evidence slots carry real content — the tabular flag is correctly false rather than missing, and the holdout split is described with its purpose — but the substantive requirement, variable-level metadata, is entirely absent. A reuser cannot learn what columns, channels or token fields exist, nor the size or selection rule of the holdout split. The compound is half-met at best, and the half that is missing is the one that determines whether the structure can be understood. is_tabular: false is semantically correct for a DICOM/WFDB/EDF+/text release and is credited as documentation, not treated as absence. The split description lacks any flag or count, so the roles of subsets are known in prose only.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances entries carry data_topic codes (B2AI_TOPIC:4, :9, :15, :37, :32) and data_substrate codes (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37, :11, :49, :43) across six instance types; description enumerates the nine data types (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging, waveform telemetry, EEG waveform) and the ICU/PICU/NICU clinical context. Topics are represented both as controlled-vocabulary codes and as readable prose, and the clinical domain (acute and critical illness, deterioration, treatment response) is clear from description, purposes and tasks. What is absent is any diagnosis-level breakdown — no conditions or phenotype distribution within the critical-care cohort. Substrate codes are used consistently (the same B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49 for both telemetry and EEG waveform, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43 for text), indicating the vocabulary is applied with understanding rather than decoratively.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies absent; missing_data_documentation absent. sampling_strategies (2 entries): is_sample true with 'Sampling at scale across data contributing centers to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies' and 'Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort'. The only populated field is sampling_strategies, and both entries are aspirational rather than procedural — one states an aim, the other is in the future tense ('will enable'). Neither describes how admissions were actually selected at the 14 sites. Meanwhile the dataset has a large, known and quantified missingness structure (per known_limitations: imaging available for a fraction of admissions, EEG extraction in process, notes present only as tokens) and none of it is recorded as missing-data documentation or as a data anomaly. FAILED cross-check: known_limitations.coverage_limitation describes exactly the missingness that missing_data_documentation should carry, so the information exists in the record but not where a reuser assessing data quality would find it structured. No quality-assessment results, no per-site completeness, no outlier handling for waveforms.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: No version field. status: 'partially released'. source_caveats: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset.' A release status is not a version. Because the enclave contents are actively growing toward 100,000 admissions, the absence of a version identifier means no analysis conducted on this data can be pinned to a reproducible snapshot. FAILED consistency check against status 'partially released' and updates.update_details, which together describe a moving target that only versioning could make citable.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: No version_access field. data_governance.access_review_process describes how to obtain access to the data, but says nothing about obtaining a particular version of it. With no versions defined there is no mechanism to reach a prior state, and nothing states whether earlier extracts are retained in the enclave at all. A reuser returning to reproduce a published result has no documented route back to the data as it stood. Consistent with, and consequent on, the absent version field; not a contradiction but a compounded gap.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: No errata field. updates.update_details is forward-looking ('The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions... As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG waveforms were in process'). There is no change log: nothing records what a past release contained, what changed between releases, or what was corrected. The one forward-looking statement is credited under sub-element 4 as a maintenance plan rather than counted twice here. Given the disclosed conflict between a tier-2 count of 50,000 admissions and a tier-4 count of 'over 45K', an erratum or dated-snapshot note is exactly what is needed and exactly what is missing. No dated release history exists against which errata could be anchored; the gap is structural rather than an oversight in a single field.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.update_details: 'The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG waveforms were in process, and published metadata schemas were planned but not yet available for clinical notes, imaging, and EEG.' funders.notes gives a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. Not a cadence, but a substantive maintenance plan: a named target scale, the specific work items in flight, a status date, and — via the award period — an outer horizon. That is enough for a reuser to decide what to expect and when to re-check, which is the purpose of the sub-element. A stated release frequency would be stronger. The August 2025 status is consistent with the same date used in description, known_limitations and is_deidentified; the growth target of 100,000 is consistent with the NIH abstract's 'more than 100,000 critically ill patients' as an anticipated rather than achieved figure.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources (6 entries) with source_description, source_type and raw_data_format: hospital EHR systems (site-specific formats mapped to OMOP), unstructured notes (free text, tokenized with OHNLP, with access_details 'Notes are stored locally at the contributing site; only tokens are made available centrally'), hospital PACS (DICOM), bedside monitoring infrastructure (WFDB), hospital EEG databases (EDF+ and Persyst), and contextual/geospatial SDOH linked to OMOP Location entities. The strongest provenance content in the record: every released modality is traced to the clinical system it came from, in its pre-transformation format, with the note-token access restriction attached to the source it constrains. was_derived_from is unused, but raw_data_sources carries the substance the sub-element asks for. Raw formats align one-to-one with distribution_formats and with the transformations named in preprocessing_strategies, so the source-to-release chain is traceable end to end for each modality.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes (4 entries) including 'Meet the need of generating data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response' and 'Develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness'. addressing_gaps (3 entries) names the gaps: absent AI infrastructure in critical care, insufficient diversity and resolution in existing critical care data, and unharmonized multi-modal EHR/waveform/imaging/text data. Purpose and the research gap it addresses are both stated, and the gaps are specific to the field rather than generic. The separate addressing_gaps block turns a mission statement into a testable rationale. Purposes align with the Bridge2AI programme goals corroborated by funders.notes, and with the tasks and intended_uses downstream. One tension noted: 'publicly available' in purposes versus fully controlled access in practice.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks (5): characterizing acute and critical care illness; predicting complications and clinical deterioration; measuring treatment response; external validation of AI/ML models against a sequestered holdout test set; labeling data with prediction targets in a visualization and annotation environment. Concrete and modelling-ready: each task maps to an identifiable ML formulation on this data, and the holdout-validation task is unusual and specific enough to be verifiable against the splits field. Tasks are consistent with intended_uses and with splits (the holdout set exists to serve task 4); no task requires data the record does not claim to hold.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund'; notes 'Awarded under the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program... awarded to Massachusetts General Hospital, fiscal year 2022, award amount USD 5,880,300, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.' notes (top level) reproduces the site funding statement and disclaimer. Agency, programme, mechanism, recipient institution, fiscal year, amount and period are all present — well beyond naming a funder. The reproduced NIH disclaimer is appropriate acknowledgement practice. Grantor, mechanism (OT2 Other Transaction award) and programme are mutually consistent, and the recipient (MGH) matches data_governance.accountable_organization and the PI's affiliation.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: name 'OT2OD032701', id 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'; notes 'Project number 1OT2OD032701-01, core project number OT2OD032701, application ID 10472824'. Both the core project number and the fully-qualified project number are given, plus the application ID and a resolvable NIH RePORTER link that lets a reader verify the award independently. VALID NIH pattern: activity code OT2 (Other Transaction research award, the correct mechanism for Bridge2AI), institute code OD (Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund), serial 032701; the 1...-01 prefix/suffix form is the correct fully-qualified variant. Grantor and grant number are mutually consistent.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: six named principal investigators with affiliations — Eric S. Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital, named as PI on NIH RePORTER for application 10472824), Azra Bihorac and Yulia Strekalova and Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University). maintainers name Ciera McCrary (MGH, Program Manager) and the two access contacts. Named individuals with institutional affiliations and a stated basis for each attribution, plus programme-level acknowledgement via the reproduced NIH funding statement. The record is candid that contributions are not expressed in CRediT terms and that roles beyond the lead PI are not stated — a limitation on precision, not on presence. The lead PI attribution is cross-checked against NIH RePORTER in the record's own caveat, and the MGH affiliation is consistent with the award recipient and the accountable organization. No creator identifiers (ORCID) are present.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms (5): bedside physiologic monitors with hospital gateway/middleware for telemetry; hospital PACS for imaging; hospital EEG databases; the OHNLP toolkit for extracting and tokenizing notes; and 'The chorus-extract-upload Python tool in the chorus-ai GitHub organization provides tools to create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract at contributing sites.' data_collectors adds that 14 of 20 academic centers act as Data Acquisition centers following SOPs in the Chorus_SOP repository 'which have undergone an internal validation and review process'. Each mechanism names the actual clinical system it draws from, and the site-side workflow is documented down to a published SOP repository and a progress-reporting process. This is replicable at the level of 'a new site could follow it'. Mechanisms map one-to-one onto the modalities in distribution_formats and raw_data_sources.
