The settings (ICU/PICU/NICU at 14 hospitals) are consistent across description, subpopulations and known_limitations.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods (5 entries, all was_directly_observed: true) covering structured EHR extraction ('medication administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation'), telemetry via bedside monitors and gateway/middleware in WFDB, PACS imaging in DICOM, EEG in EDF+ and Persyst ('extraction was still in process as of August 2025'), and note extraction/tokenization with OHNLP. raw_data_sources repeats the chain at source level. Instrument- and system-level detail per modality, including the granularity of the structured data (per-infusion-change timestamps) that determines what temporal modelling is possible. Readiness caveats are attached to the modality they affect rather than buried. was_directly_observed: true is semantically defensible — the data were observed at the point of care — and is reconciled with direct_collection.is_direct: false, which correctly states that collection was retrospective rather than research-initiated. The two flags read together are coherent, not contradictory.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies (5): OMOP standardization with flowsheet extensions; OHNLP tokenization into the OHNLP open source schema; transformation 'using approaches that limit re-identification'; waveform preparation and conversion 'using the waveform conversion scripts and documentation in the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories'; geocoding of OMOP Location entities 'via DeGauss using the open source UF-Geocoding code, a fork of bihorac-LAB/Exposome'. cleaning_strategies (2): characterization reports returned to sites via the CHoRUSReports repository; validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping under a clinical validation SOP. labeling_strategies (1): a visualization and annotation environment for labeling prediction targets. All three core stages are documented with named, locatable artefacts, and the cleaning loop (characterization reports returned to sites so they can resolve issues) is a real quality process rather than a claim. Weaker on labeling: one sentence, with no annotator counts, guidelines or agreement statistics — and annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all unused. The compound passes on the strength of preprocessing and cleaning. Each preprocessing step corresponds to a released format (OMOP tables, OHNLP tokens, WFDB/EDF+ waveforms, geocoded Location entities), so the pipeline accounts for the distribution as stated. The re-identification-limiting step is the one described without a named method.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Software named in processing roles, carried by preprocessing_strategies prose and corroborated by external_resources: the OHNLP toolkit (tokenizes the released note tokens); waveform conversion scripts in the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories (produce the released WFDB/EDF+ outputs); DeGauss with the open source UF-Geocoding code, a fork of bihorac-LAB/Exposome (geocodes the released OMOP Location entities); chorus-mapping (validated semantic mappings applied in the OMOP transformation); and, in participant_privacy, the CTP-deid de-identification component. external_resources gives the organization root https://github.com/chorus-ai. The threshold is met: multiple tools are named that produced or transformed the data being distributed, not merely captured, hosted, packaged or validated it. Tooling in non-qualifying roles also appears — chorus-extract-upload (capture/packaging), CHoRUSReports (validation), privacy_scan_tool (quality/screening) — and neither adds to nor subtracts from the judgement. Shortfall: no version numbers or release tags for any tool, and the only URL is the organization root rather than per-repository links, so exact reproduction is not possible from the record alone. Evidence slot: preprocessing_strategies (primary), participant_privacy and external_resources (corroborating). Tool-to-output mapping is coherent — each named tool is tied to a specific released artefact. No software DOI or citation is provided for any tool.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources (4): the project website with its enumerated documentation pages, the chorus-ai GitHub organization (28 repositories including SOPs and validated semantic mappings), the NIH RePORTER award record, and the Bridge2AI CHoRUS page. conforms_to names OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+, Persyst and the OHNLP schema. extension_mechanism adds a contribution_url and a described contribution workflow. Standards and external documentation are both well covered, and the SOP and mapping repositories are the kind of external resource that actually supports replication. Two gaps: imputation_protocols is unused, so the record neither documents imputation nor states that none is performed for a dataset with substantial modality-level missingness; and no peer-reviewed publication or preprint DOI is cited for the methods. The named standards exist and are used correctly for their modalities; the resource links are plausible and typed by description. Recorded warning: no imputation statement despite documented uneven coverage.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations (4, each typed): coverage_limitation (uneven modality availability, 1000 images with de-identification in process, EEG extraction in process, metadata only planned for notes/imaging/EEG) with recommended_mitigation 'Confirm current modality availability with the CHoRUS data access contacts before planning analyses'; scope_limitation (50,000 of an anticipated 100,000 admissions); integration_limitation (notes not centralized, only OHNLP tokens available, 'which constrains analyses requiring raw narrative text'); representativeness_limitation (14 hospitals drawn from 20 academic centers, so the cohort reflects academic-center case mix). The strongest disclosure in the record: four distinct limitation types, each stated in terms of what analyses it prevents, with an actionable mitigation on the most consequential one. The integration and representativeness entries name consequences a reuser would otherwise discover only after committing. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere (notes architecture in raw_data_sources; scale in instances; site count in description) — the disclosure is consistent with the rest of the record rather than a detached caveat block.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: bias_type 'representation_bias' with bias_description ('The project treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed... while accounting for social determinants of health') and mitigation_strategy ('Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort, and sampling at scale is designed to capture comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies'). future_use_impacts is also populated. A taxonomy-aligned bias type with a paired mitigation, which satisfies the sub-element. It is thin for a dataset of this shape, though: only one bias entry, its mitigation is partly future-tense, and the obvious candidates raised by the record's own content — academic-center selection bias (flagged as a limitation but not as a bias), measurement bias across 14 heterogeneous EHR and monitoring vendors, and the geographic/SDOH linkage — are not categorized. The representation_bias claim cannot be checked against any demographic distribution, since subpopulations reports no composition. Mitigation overlaps verbatim with sampling_strategies, indicating a single underlying statement reused rather than two independent assessments.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: No anomalies field. cleaning_strategies mentions that 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to sites following their data submissions... so that contributing sites can identify and resolve issues in their extracts', but no issue, outlier or artefact is itself reported. A quality process is described without any quality findings. For multicentre waveform and flowsheet data — where dropout, clock drift, duplicate admissions, vendor artefacts and implausible physiologic values are routine — nothing is recorded that a reuser could guard against. The characterization reports evidently exist and contain exactly this information; none of it is surfaced. Cross-check: the record acknowledges harmonization across 14 heterogeneous sites and extensive format conversion, both of which reliably generate anomalies, yet reports none. The gap is in disclosure, not plausibly in the data.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present true, with sensitivity_details enumerating 'demographics, diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, clinical note tokens, radiology images, telemetry and EEG waveforms, social determinants of health, and contextual geographic factors such as distance to the nearest hospital'. confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present true, noting all nine modalities carry controlled access and that notes cannot be released centrally. Sensitivity is enumerated element by element rather than asserted in the abstract, and the inclusion of geographic distance as a sensitive contextual factor shows genuine awareness of quasi-identifier risk. content_warnings is unused — defensible for clinical records, though critical-care content including neonatal mortality might warrant one. Consistent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', with the controlled-access licensing terms, and with the privacy architecture in participant_privacy. Restrictiveness matches stated sensitivity.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews (2): 'community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing', evaluation of 'community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI', and 'Patient-focused efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches used to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. future_use_impacts: sequestering holdout datasets 'to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care, and to catalyze the biomedical research and expertise necessary to promote the patient-focused deployment of AI'. Read as disclosure rather than as oversight, this is substantive: community engagement that shapes what may be shared is a real ethical practice, and an anticipated downstream impact is stated. Scored separately from Element 4 sub-element 1, which fails because it carries a mandatory check for IRB approval under involves_human_subjects=true that this content does not satisfy. Weaknesses here: future_use_impacts frames benefit only, with no anticipated harm, no mitigation, and no conflict-of-interest disclosure. The social-impact statement is consistent with tasks and intended_uses (holdout validation for marketplace adoption). WARNING: no reviewing body is named in either ethical_reviews entry, as their own source_caveats state, so 'review' here means project activity, not external scrutiny.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: No publisher field. created_by: 'CHoRUS Consortium'; data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital. description states 'OMOP and telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave' without naming it; intended_uses mentions 'the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud' as a training environment. No recognized data repository — no PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo or named institutional repository — and the hosting enclave is never identified. An accountable organization and a consortium are recorded, which establishes responsibility but not publication on a discoverable platform. Cross-checked against download_url (absent), doi (absent) and citation (absent): the record is consistent in describing a dataset distributed by direct arrangement rather than through a platform, which is the substantive finding rather than a metadata slip.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: No citation field and no doi field. source_caveats: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset.' The only DOI-adjacent identifier is the NIH RePORTER URL for the award, which identifies the grant, not the data. There is no way to cite this dataset in a publication, and no persistent handle by which another dataset or paper could reference it. Controlled access is no obstacle here: metadata-only DOIs are standard practice for restricted clinical datasets. Compounds the Element 1 persistent-identifier failure and, with no version identifier either, means a citation could not even name which state of the growing dataset was used.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to gives per-modality conformance (OMOP CDM with flowsheet extensions, DICOM, WFDB described as an extended PhysioNet schema, EDF+ and Persyst, the OHNLP open source schema); conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Conformance to four or five widely adopted community standards, declared both as prose and as controlled terms, and the metadata record itself declares the schema it conforms to. This is the clearest ecosystem connection the dataset has, and OMOP adoption in particular makes the structured data interoperable with the OHDSI community's tooling. Standards are real, correctly matched to modality, and consistent with distribution_formats. The single OTHER term standing for EDF+, Persyst and OHNLP understates the count, and the 'extended' qualifications on OMOP and WFDB mean conformance is not strict — both disclosed in source_caveats.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; external_resources describes site sections on 'the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources' and the GitHub organization's SOPs and project-management overviews. intended_uses describes 'hands-on AI/ML coursework, canonical Jupyter Notebooks, and OHDSI/OMOP instruction'; existing_uses records the AIM-AHEAD Cohort 2 training programme for up to 30 trainees. extension_mechanism documents how outside collaborators contribute via chorus-mapping and GitHub Discussions. Documentation, learning resources, a training programme with a named cohort, and a documented route for external contribution. This goes well past a bare landing-page link and shows an active community around the dataset. Outreach claims are mutually corroborating across intended_uses, existing_uses, external_resources and extension_mechanism. One link ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus') lacks a scheme, noted as a low-severity correctness issue.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: No related_datasets field and no parent_datasets field. splits describes a sequestered holdout test set in prose only; description places the dataset among 'four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program' without linking any sibling. Two classes of relationship plainly exist — the sequestered holdout set as a sibling of the released cohort, and the three sibling Bridge2AI data generation projects — and neither is expressed as a typed link. A machine reading this record cannot traverse to anything related. Consistent with the Element 1 hierarchical-structure failure: the record's relationships are described in prose throughout but never instantiated in the relational fields designed to carry them.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; no doi field anywhere in the record; the only registry-style identifier present is the funder's NIH RePORTER link (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824), which identifies the award, not the dataset. The id is the project homepage, which is also given as `page`. A homepage URL is not a persistent identifier: it carries no registration commitment, resolves to a site the record itself says is 'under review for potential modification', and cannot survive the resource moving. DOI pattern 10.XXXX/... : absent. RRID pattern RRID:SCR_XXXXX : absent. id is a bare https URI at the organisation root, failing the persistence criterion.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description runs ~1,800 characters covering 20 academic centers, 14 data acquisition sites, 50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 imaging admissions, 23 Tb waveform, nine modalities anticipated, and the per-modality standards (OMOP, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst). Far beyond the 200-character threshold and dense with dataset-specific quantities and modality detail; a reader can tell what the dataset contains, how big it is, and how it is stored without leaving the field. Description content matches the claimed dataset type (multicenter retrospective critical care) and is internally consistent with instances, distribution_formats and conforms_to.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: critical care; intensive care unit; acute illness; electronic health records; OMOP Common Data Model; physiologic waveforms; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; social determinants of health; Bridge2AI; AI-ready dataset. Twelve keywords spanning clinical domain, care setting, every data modality, the data standard and the programme affiliation; well above the five-keyword expectation and non-redundant. Each keyword is substantiated elsewhere in the record (e.g. 'social determinants of health' appears in sensitive_elements and intended_uses); no keyword stuffing detected.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; status notes the site banner; external_resources also gives https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus as the programme page. A real project landing page is given and corroborated by a second programme-level page. No hierarchical `resources` tree is provided, but the sub-element is satisfied by an accessible landing page. Domain is plausible and consistent with the project name; URL structure well formed.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: parent_datasets: absent. related_datasets: absent. The only links out are external_resources entries pointing at a GitHub organisation and a programme webpage, neither of which is a dataset relationship. No parent dataset, no sibling Bridge2AI data generation project links, and no relationship between the released 50,000-admission subset and the anticipated 100,000-admission dataset or the sequestered holdout set — all of which are natural typed relationships this record could express. The record describes a holdout test set (splits) and a growing release (updates) without modelling either as a dataset relationship; structural information exists in prose but not in the relationship fields.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program must sign a licensing agreement, included in the program registration form, before gaining access to the dataset; that program also requires an institutional (".edu") email address for dataset access. All data types are described as controlled access.' data_governance.access_review_process adds the enclave arrangement and the registration/provisioning workflow. An access policy is genuinely described — controlled access in a cloud enclave, signed agreement, institutional email, notes never leaving the site — and its limits are stated honestly (the terms attested are programme-specific). Actionable for a prospective user deciding whether they can obtain the data. Access restrictiveness is consistent with sensitive_elements and confidential_elements; no contradiction between 'controlled access' and third_party_sharing.is_shared=true, which is scoped to controlled release.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: data_governance.committee_contact: 'Jared Houghtaling (jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org)'; data_governance.notes gives a second access-request address dbold@emory.edu; confidential_elements.confidentiality_details: 'Clinical notes are not held in the cloud enclave... All listed data types are released under controlled access'; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance describes an established legal framework for collecting data at scale. A named, reachable governance contact plus an explicit statement that every modality is controlled access and that notes are confined to originating sites. This addresses the sub-element's contact and confidentiality scope with specific content, though the formal apparatus is thin. Partial: regulatory_restrictions, confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are all unset. For US hospital PHI the absent HIPAA status is a real gap, recorded as a content_accuracy issue; the governance contact and uniform controlled-access classification are nonetheless present and specific, and the record marks the missing committee structure in source_caveats rather than fabricating one.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: download_url: absent. The nearest content is data_governance.access_review_process, which describes a registration form and email provisioning for training-programme participants but gives no URL, and page: https://chorus4ai.org/, which is informational. No retrieval route is linkable. A user who satisfies the access conditions still has no address to apply at, only two email contacts on a GitHub page; the registration form and the enclave are named but not located. Consistent with controlled access (no direct download expected), but the sub-element also accepts a platform access link, and none is given.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats lists five entries: OMOP CDM tables (demographics, medication administration, procedures, diagnoses, nursing flowsheets); tokenized clinical notes in the OHNLP open-source schema; DICOM imaging from PACS; WFDB waveform telemetry ('extended PhysioNet schema... 23 Tb'); EEG in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Every modality has a named, standard format together with the access condition and, where known, the published metadata schema. Specific enough that a user can tell what tooling they would need per modality. media_type/MIME is not given for any entry, but each `format` value is a recognized standard matched correctly to its modality (DICOM for imaging, WFDB for telemetry, EDF+ for EEG); formats agree with conforms_to and conforms_to_standard.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: external_resources: https://github.com/chorus-ai ('Organization hosting 28 repositories... chorus-mapping, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-container-apps, CHoRUSReports...'), and https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus. The GitHub entry is exceptionally informative, naming the individual repositories and what each does, so a user can find the SOPs, mappings and conversion scripts directly. related_datasets is empty, but the sub-element is satisfied by substantive external resource linkage. Both URLs are well formed and plausible; the repositories named are consistently referenced from preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, is_deidentified and extension_mechanism.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.source_caveats: 'The bundle states no general license for the data themselves and no access terms outside the training program context. The MIT License stated on the chorus-ai GitHub organization page applies to that project's software repositories.' No license governs the data. What is documented is a signed agreement requirement for one training cohort, plus an MIT/Apache-2.0 licence that the record correctly attributes to the software repositories rather than the data. A reuser cannot determine their permissions, which is exactly what this sub-element asks. The record earns credit for not conflating the repository licence with a data licence — a common error — but transparency about an absent licence does not supply reuse terms.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats formats (OMOP CDM tables, OHNLP-schema tokens, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst); conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; raw_data_sources record native formats ('DICOM', 'EDF+ and Persyst', 'Free text'). All five released modalities use open, community-standard, tool-supported formats, and the record distinguishes native source format from released format. Character encoding is never stated, a minor gap for the tokenized text, but format standardization is unambiguous. Format-to-modality assignments are technically correct; WFDB with an 'extended PhysioNet schema' and OMOP 'with extensions' are flagged as extended rather than presented as vanilla, which is accurate practice.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'Structured electronic health record data... standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with schema extensions used for nursing flowsheets; clinical notes follow the OHNLP open-source schema; imaging follows DICOM; waveform telemetry follows WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema; EEG follows the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas.' conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; conforms_to_class: Dataset ; instances carry B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology codes. Conformance is stated per modality rather than as a single blanket claim, extensions are disclosed, the metadata record itself declares its schema, and ontology term identifiers are used for topics and substrates. Strong on every dimension this sub-element asks about. OMOP/DICOM/WFDB/EDF+ are used correctly as terms of art; the w3id schema URI is well formed and resolves to the Bridge2AI data sheets schema namespace.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: absent. No data dictionary, no column list, no variable identifiers; the closest content is instance_type prose ('Row of structured electronic health record data... covering demographics, medication administration, provider-documented procedures and diagnoses, and high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation'). For 1.6 billion rows of tabular data there is no variable-level metadata at all. OMOP conformance tells a reuser which standard tables could exist, but not which are populated, at what completeness, or how the declared nursing-flowsheet extensions are structured — precisely the extension that departs from the standard. Inconsistency: the record claims OMOP 'schema extensions' for nursing flowsheets while providing no definition of those extended variables, so the extension is unusable by an external reuser.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: four categories with notes — 'Model development for acute and critical care', 'External validation of models' against the sequestered holdout set, 'Training and workforce development', 'Equity and social determinants research'. existing_uses documents the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 training programme (up to 30 trainees, Nov 2025 to Jul 2026) and the OHDSI tool stack used. Intended uses are specific, tied to concrete artefacts (the holdout set, the collaborative cloud) and paired with documented existing uses, which is stronger evidence of realistic scope than aspiration alone. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both empty, which is a notable omission for a re-identifiable clinical corpus (recorded as a completeness issue); the sub-element is nonetheless met by substantive intended-use guidance.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: [1] 'Community-facing ethics focus groups are performed to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing' (reviewing_organization: 'CHoRUS consortium, Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar'); [2] evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape. human_subject_research.source_caveats: 'The bundle does not state IRB approval for the dataset or name an ethics review board of record.' data_protection_impacts: absent. What is documented is ethics research and community engagement conducted by the consortium, not review or approval of this data collection. No IRB, no reliance agreement, no waiver, no protocol number, no DPIA for a cloud enclave holding PHI from 14 hospitals. The record is commendably explicit that the information is missing, but the sub-element asks whether oversight is documented, and it is not. Consistency check FAILED: involves_human_subjects=true with no ethics approval evidence. Scored 0 for missing oversight evidence rather than excluded, exactly as the applicability rules direct when E1 establishes human subjects.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification; de-identification of imaging.' is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'As of August 2025, roughly 1,000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort. Supporting tooling in the chorus-ai organization includes a privacy scan tool for medical records and a CTP-deid repository. Clinical notes are kept at the contributing site and only tokens are released into the enclave.' Method is described per modality with named tooling (CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool) and a genuine architectural control — notes never leave the site — plus an honest statement of what is still in progress. Non-trivial and actionable, though no formal standard is named. Method appropriateness: tokenization plus site-local retention is a defensible control for free text, and CTP is the standard DICOM de-identification toolkit, so the methods match the data types. Gap: neither Safe Harbor nor Expert Determination is asserted, and the waveform/EEG modalities have no de-identification treatment described at all.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy: absent; no reidentification_risk field anywhere. Adjacent content: preprocessing_strategies 'Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification'; confidential_elements notes that clinical notes stay at contributing sites. Protections exist in fragments elsewhere, but there is no privacy analysis and, critically, no assessment of residual re-identification risk for a corpus containing high-frequency waveforms, EEG, DICOM imaging, geographic contextual factors and distance-to-hospital variables — a combination with well-known linkage risk. Consistency check FAILED: de-identification is claimed and sensitive elements are flagged, yet residual risk is never characterized; the assertion that transformations 'limit re-identification' is unquantified and unevaluated.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent: absent. direct_collection.is_direct=false with collection_details 'Data are obtained from hospital clinical systems... rather than directly from patients' — which explains the collection route but says nothing about consent or a waiver. Nothing at all is recorded about the legal basis for using identifiable patient data: no consent, no waiver of consent, no notice-of-privacy-practices reliance, no site-level variation. For a 14-hospital retrospective extraction this is the single most conspicuous documentation gap. Consistency check FAILED: involves_human_subjects=true without any consent or waiver documentation.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations: absent; participant_compensation: absent. human_subject_research.special_populations: ['Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions', 'Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions']. Two vulnerable populations are correctly identified — critically ill children and neonates, who cannot consent and whose data carry heightened protection requirements — but no protections whatever are described for them: no additional safeguards, no parental permission arrangements, no restrictions on pediatric subset access. Identification without protection does not meet the sub-element. Naming PICU/NICU cohorts while documenting no corresponding safeguard, and no IRB or consent framework anywhere, compounds the Element 4 failures rather than mitigating them. Compensation is plausibly inapplicable for retrospective records, but that is never stated.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: [subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Admissions in the released dataset are drawn from ICU, PICU, and NICU.'; source_caveats: 'The bundle does not give the distribution of admissions across ICU, PICU, and NICU, nor any demographic breakdown of the cohort.'] The only cohort characterization is the three care-unit types, which the description already states. No demographics, no age or sex distribution, no race/ethnicity, no site mix, no inclusion or exclusion criteria, no severity or diagnosis mix — and the record says so. For a dataset whose stated purpose includes equity research and social determinants, the absence of any demographic breakdown is disabling. Content is at the marginal level the scoring standard illustrates ('Data collected from multiple sites'): true, dataset-specific, but not sufficient to characterize the cohort. The explicit caveat is good documentation practice and is credited in the assessment narrative, not in the score.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances counts: 50,000 hospital admissions (ICU/PICU/NICU); 1,600,000,000 rows of OMOP-standardized EHR data; 7,642 admissions with radiology data; waveform instance noted as '23 Tb of waveform data'; description adds the anticipated 100,000 admissions and nine modalities from 14 hospitals. Counts are given per instance type with units that make sense for each modality, and the anticipated final scale is distinguished from the current release. Divergent source counts (over 45K admissions, ~1,000 images as of August 2025) are recorded on the affected entries with a stated source ranking rather than averaged away. Arithmetic plausibility holds: 1.6e9 OMOP rows across 50,000 ICU admissions is ~32,000 rows per admission, consistent with high-frequency flowsheet and infusion-level documentation. The 7,642/50,000 imaging fraction is plausible for retrospective PACS linkage.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: absent; is_tabular: unset; no subsets block. splits: [split_details: 'The project sequesters a holdout test set that is accessible for external validation of models, intended to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models...']. Only one of the three components is addressed. The holdout split is described in purpose but not in extent — no size, no sampling rule, no statement of whether it is drawn from the same sites or held out by site — and there is no variable metadata or tabular flag at all despite 1.6 billion tabular rows. OMOP conformance partially compensates by implying standard table structure, but the declared nursing-flowsheet extensions are undefined, so even the implied structure is incomplete. A user cannot tell which fraction of the 50,000 admissions is sequestered.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry ontology-coded topics: B2AI_TOPIC:4 (admissions), B2AI_TOPIC:9 (structured EHR), B2AI_TOPIC:15 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11 (imaging), B2AI_TOPIC:37 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49 (waveform telemetry and EEG), B2AI_TOPIC:32 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43 (clinical notes); instance_type prose names the clinical content of each. Topics are expressed as resolvable ontology terms rather than free text and are paired with substrate codes, so the modality coverage is machine-readable as well as human-readable. Clinical conditions are characterized at the care-setting level (acute and critical illness) rather than by diagnosis mix, which is a limitation but leaves the represented topic clear. Topic/substrate pairings are internally consistent across the six instance entries and agree with distribution_formats and raw_data_sources.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: absent; missing_data_documentation: absent. sampling_strategies: 'Sampling designed to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies across the multi-center network. Federated access enabling sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort.' The single populated field reads as programme aspiration rather than an account of what was sampled: no sampling frame, no inclusion rule, no achieved balance figures. Nothing documents missingness, which in multi-site EHR data is structured, site-dependent and decisive for any model built on it, and no anomalies or quality issues are recorded despite waveform telemetry and flowsheet data being notoriously artefact-laden. Inconsistency with the record's own strengths: cleaning_strategies describe per-site characterization reports (CHoRUSReports) that would generate exactly this quality information, yet none of their findings are surfaced here.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: absent from the record entirely. No version label of any kind, despite the record describing a partially released dataset actively growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions with modalities arriving at different times. Two users analysing 'CHoRUS' months apart would have no way to state they used different data. Absence is materially worse here than for a static release, because updates.update_details confirms the contents change over time.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access: absent. data_governance.access_review_process describes how to obtain access but says nothing about obtaining a particular snapshot or an earlier state of the enclave. No mechanism for reaching a prior version, no statement of whether snapshots are retained, no guidance for reproducing an analysis performed before the cohort grew. For a growing enclave dataset this blocks reproducibility outright. Consistent gap with the missing version number; the two together mean no temporal reference point exists for the data.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: absent. updates.update_details records the forward trajectory ('growing from the current released 50,000 admissions toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions and 9 data modalities') and in-progress work as of August 2025, but no release history and no corrections. There is no changelog: nothing states what changed between the state reported in the project documentation and the August 2025 webinar state, even though the record itself surfaces two divergent count sets that a changelog would explain. No errata or corrections are recorded. The record documents the existence of differing counts across sources but attributes them to source disagreement rather than to dataset change, leaving the change history genuinely unstated.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.update_details: 'The dataset is growing from the current released 50,000 admissions toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions and 9 data modalities across 14 contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process, and published metadata for some data types was planned. The NIH project period runs to 2026-11-30.' A maintenance plan is genuinely conveyed: the direction and target of growth, which modalities are still arriving, what metadata is planned, and the funded horizon that bounds the work. A user can infer that the dataset will change and by roughly when, which is the sub-element's purpose, even though no cadence is stated. Temporal consistency holds: award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 encloses the August 2025 status report; no date ordering conflicts anywhere in the record.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: five typed entries — hospital EHR structured data; unstructured notes ('Notes remain stored locally at contributing sites; only tokenized output is moved into the enclave'); PACS radiology in DICOM; bedside monitor telemetry via gateway/middleware; hospital EEG database in 'EDF+ and Persyst'. acquisition_methods adds 'site-specific clinical data extracts prepared according to validated standard operating procedures and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling'. updates.update_details supplies release-state notes. Provenance is traceable from originating clinical system through named SOPs and upload tooling to the released artefact, per modality and with native formats. This is the strongest provenance content in the record; only was_derived_from as a structured field is missing, and the prose fully covers its role. Raw sources align one-to-one with collection_mechanisms and distribution_formats; no modality appears in one list and not the others.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: five responses, including 'To meet the need for data supporting machine learning and artificial intelligence applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response', 'To provision a holdout test set, accessible for model external validation, to aid marketplace adoption', and workforce cultivation. addressing_gaps adds three gap statements, including that 'Existing clinical data lack unified standards across modalities'. Motivation is stated at both the scientific and infrastructural level and is paired with explicit gap analysis; the purposes are distinguishable from one another rather than restatements, and each maps to something the dataset actually contains. Purposes align with the Bridge2AI Common Fund mandate identified in funders, satisfying the funding-alignment consistency check.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Characterizing acute and critical care illness'; 'Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness'; 'Measuring treatment response'; 'External validation of machine learning models against a sequestered holdout test set'; 'Labeling data with targets important for prediction using a visualization and annotation environment'. Five concrete tasks spanning characterization, prediction, causal/treatment-response analysis and benchmarking; the external-validation task is tied to a real artefact (the holdout set) rather than left abstract. Tasks are coherent with the modalities held (deterioration prediction requires the high-frequency flowsheet and waveform data the record documents).

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; funders[0].notes records the standard disclaimer that site content 'does not necessarily represent the official views of the NIH'. The funding agency and the specific funding programme are both named, which distinguishes the Common Fund Bridge2AI mechanism from generic NIH support, and the funder disclaimer is captured. Grantor is consistent with the OT2 award type recorded in funders.grants and with the consortium framing in description.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants[0]: id https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824 ; name 'OT2OD032701'; description 'NIH award OT2OD032701 (project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824) to Massachusetts General Hospital; fiscal year 2022 award amount USD 5,880,300; project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30.' Award number, full project number, application ID, awardee institution, dollar amount, project period and a resolvable RePORTER link — substantially more than the sub-element requires and independently verifiable. NIH format VALID: 'OT2' activity code (Other Transaction, the mechanism Bridge2AI uses), 'OD' Office of the Director as the administering institute (correct for Common Fund awards), six-digit serial 032701, with the '1...-01' new-award/year-one suffix correctly formed. Consistent with the stated grantor.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: six entries — Eric S. Rosenthal (principal_investigator, Massachusetts General Hospital, 'Named in NIH RePORTER as principal investigator of OT2OD032701'), plus Azra Bihorac and Parisa Rashidi and Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University), each noted as Leadership Team members. created_by: 'CHoRUS consortium, a Bridge2AI data generation project'. maintainers names the program manager and the GitHub organisation. Named individuals with institutional affiliations and an explicit statement of the evidential basis for each role. The record deliberately declines to assert PI status for the five leadership-team members, recording in source_caveats that 'no principal investigator role is asserted for them here' — attribution discipline that strengthens rather than weakens the documentation. Affiliations are consistent with the 20-center collaboration described; the PI's institution matches the MGH awardee institution in the grant record.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: five entries — EHR extraction 'covering demographics, medication administration recorded at each infusion change or dose administration, provider documentation of procedures and diagnoses, and high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation'; PACS imaging extraction; 'Capture of waveform telemetry from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware'; EEG extraction from the hospital EEG database; note extraction and tokenization via the OHNLP toolkit. collection_timeframes and data_collectors add the retrospective framing, the August 2025 reporting date, and the roles of the 14 acquisition sites and the Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams. Every modality has its own described mechanism with the granularity of capture stated (per infusion change, high-frequency flowsheets), the institutional setting identified, and the retrospective nature made explicit through direct_collection.is_direct=false. Mechanisms map one-to-one onto raw_data_sources and distribution_formats; the retrospective claim is consistent with direct_collection and with the absence of participant recruitment.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: 'Retrospective extraction of clinical data recorded during routine hospital care at the data contributing sites, delivered to CHoRUS as site-specific clinical data extracts prepared according to validated standard operating procedures and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling.' raw_data_sources names the originating systems (EHR, PACS, bedside physiologic monitoring, hospital EEG database) with native formats. The acquisition route is specified end to end — instrument/system of origin, governing SOPs, and the named upload tool — so an outside site could in principle follow the same path. Specific device makes and models for monitors and EEG are not given, a residual gap for waveform reproducibility. chorus-extract-upload and the SOP repositories (Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP) named here are the same artefacts listed in external_resources, so the acquisition claim is corroborated by a locatable resource.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies (four): OMOP standardization with flowsheet extensions; note tokenization via OHNLP with notes retained on site; transformations that limit re-identification; waveform conversion 'using the waveform conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories'. cleaning_strategies (two): per-submission characterization reports returned to sites (CHoRUSReports); semantic mappings in chorus-mapping 'reviewed by clinical collaborators following an associated clinical validation standard operating procedure'. labeling_strategies: 'A visualization and annotation environment is used to label data with targets important for prediction.' machine_annotation_tools: OHNLP toolkit with tool_descriptions. All four facets are covered, with the pipeline anchored to named, inspectable repositories and an explicit clinical validation step for the semantic mappings — the hardest part of OMOP conversion to get right. Labeling is the weakest strand: the annotation environment is unnamed and no inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality analysis is reported. annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols are absent; the OHNLP claim is consistent across machine_annotation_tools, preprocessing_strategies, distribution_formats and conforms_to.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Slot carrying the evidence: machine_annotation_tools.tools: ['OHNLP toolkit'] — the toolkit that extracts and tokenizes the clinical notes whose tokens are in the release; preprocessing_strategies prose names 'the waveform conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories' used to prepare waveforms for release; is_deidentified.deidentification_details names 'CTP-deid' and a 'privacy scan tool' applied to released records and images; cleaning_strategies names chorus-mapping for the validated semantic mappings applied to the OMOP conversion. Software that produced or transformed the distributed data is named in several places: tokenization (OHNLP), waveform conversion (chorus_waveform), de-identification (CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool) and semantic mapping (chorus-mapping). Versions are not pinned for any of them, which weakens reproducibility, but the disclosure question this sub-element asks is answered. Roles checked against the exclusion list: chorus-extract-upload is closer to capture/transfer (role a) and CHoRUSReports to validation (role d), and neither is relied on here; the scoring evidence is transformation software in the release path. A package status page listing 'versions, maintainers, and other metadata' is referenced, so versions are locatable even though not stated inline.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: the chorus-ai GitHub organisation with 28 repositories itemized by function, a package status page, and a contributor guide in chorus-developer; plus the Bridge2AI CHoRUS programme page. conforms_to names OMOP CDM, OHNLP schema, DICOM, WFDB/extended PhysioNet schema, EDF+ and Persyst. extension_mechanism documents the contribution workflow and its URL. External standards are named per modality and the supporting documentation is not merely linked but characterized repository by repository, so a user can find the SOPs, mappings and conversion code they would need. imputation_protocols is absent and no statement is made about whether imputation was used, which is a gap given the missingness inherent in flowsheet data. Standards cited are the correct community standards for each modality; no published paper or protocol DOI is cited, so the external documentation is all project-internal.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: three typed entries — coverage_limitation ('as of August 2025 imaging de-identification was in process for the larger cohort with about 1,000 images available, and EEG extraction was still in process'); integration_limitation ('Clinical notes are stored locally... only tokens are available centrally, so full text cannot be analyzed alongside the other modalities in the enclave'); scope_limitation ('restricted to retrospectively collected admissions of critically ill patients (ICU, PICU, NICU) at 14 contributing hospitals, and is available only under controlled access'). Limitations are typed, specific and consequential — each states not just a fact but what a user cannot do because of it. The integration limitation in particular anticipates a real multimodal analysis a reuser would attempt and explains why it fails. Each limitation is corroborated by the field it constrains (instances, confidential_elements, is_deidentified), so the disclosures are consistent rather than decorative.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: absent; future_use_impacts: absent. Bias appears only as a topic of ongoing work — ethical_reviews mentions 'ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health', and intended_uses includes 'Equity and social determinants research'. No bias is categorized, named or assessed. The obvious candidates go unaddressed: selection into ICU care, representation across the 14 contributing hospitals, documentation and measurement bias in flowsheet data, and the equity implications of a cohort with no reported demographic composition. Intending to study bias is not the same as disclosing the dataset's own. Inconsistency: the record claims an equity mission ('Equitable AI' in the title, equity research among intended uses) while providing neither a demographic profile (Element 5) nor any bias characterization here, so the equity claim cannot be evaluated.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: absent. The nearest content is cleaning_strategies, which describes characterization reports 'produced from each site data submission and returned to the contributing site', but reports no finding from them. Not one anomaly, artefact, outlier or quality defect is recorded, for a corpus of bedside telemetry, EEG, PACS imaging and nurse-entered flowsheets where sensor dropout, clock misalignment, duplicate studies and implausible vital values are routine. The machinery to detect them is documented; its output is not. Consistency warning: existence of a per-site characterization pipeline (CHoRUSReports) implies quality findings that the datasheet does not surface.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: [sensitive_elements_present: true; 'The dataset consists of patient-level clinical data from critically ill patients, including demographics, diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheet documentation, clinical notes, radiology imaging, physiologic waveform telemetry, EEG, and social determinants of health together with geographic contextual factors.'] confidential_elements: [confidential_elements_present: true; notes kept on site, all types controlled access]. The sensitivity declaration is itemized modality by modality and explicitly includes the two highest-risk categories — social determinants and geographic contextual factors — rather than settling for a general 'contains PHI'. Paired with a confidentiality entry describing the handling that follows from it. content_warnings is absent, but the sensitivity detail is substantive and consistent with the controlled-access posture and with is_deidentified. Naming geographic context alongside clinical detail is also what makes the missing re-identification assessment in Element 4 significant.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: [1] 'Community-facing ethics focus groups are performed to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing' (CHoRUS Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar); [2] 'The consortium evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI... Patient-focused efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.' purposes include creating 'best practices for AI in health'. This sub-element asks about ethical review documentation together with anticipated downstream social impact, and that is substantively what the content is: community engagement on what should be shared, work on trustworthiness and provenance, and analysis of the legal landscape for clinical AI, with named reviewing organizations. Scored differently from Element 4 sub-element 1 deliberately — the same text fails there because it is not oversight or approval of the human-subjects data collection, while here it is exactly the social-impact and ethics-programme evidence sought. future_use_impacts is absent, so no structured rai:dataSocialImpact entry exists and no mitigation is tied to a specific anticipated harm; conflicts of interest are not addressed. Credit rests on the prose social-impact content, which is dataset-specific rather than boilerplate.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: absent. The hosting arrangement is described only as 'a cloud enclave' (description, data_governance) and, for trainees, 'the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud' (existing_uses); chorus-container-apps implies Azure, but no repository or publisher is named. No recognized data repository — PhysioNet, Dataverse, FAIRhub, Zenodo, an institutional repository — and no named operator of the enclave. The organisation accountable for the data over time is unidentified, a gap the record itself flags in data_governance.source_caveats ('no organization formally accountable for the data over time'). Consistent with the absent DOI and citation: the dataset has no identified publishing venue, so nothing anchors its long-term availability.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: absent; doi: absent. The only citable string in the record is the funding acknowledgement language in funders.notes, and the only resolvable persistent link is the NIH RePORTER award page. A user who analyses this shared dataset has no recommended citation and no DOI to cite, so credit and cross-referencing are impossible. This is scored 0, not N/A: the dataset is shared and the requirement applies. DOI format validation: not_present. Compounded by the missing version (Element 6), a citation could not even specify which snapshot was used.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to names OMOP Common Data Model (with nursing-flowsheet extensions), the OHNLP open-source schema, DICOM, WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema, and EDF+/Persyst; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; existing_uses notes trainees use 'the OHDSI tool stack, and the OHDSI/OMOP common data model'. Conformance to five distinct community standards, expressed both in prose and as enumerated values, plus demonstrated ecosystem participation through the OHDSI tool stack. This is the record's clearest route into a wider data ecosystem. Standards are correctly matched to modalities and consistently repeated in distribution_formats and preprocessing_strategies; the extensions to OMOP and WFDB are disclosed rather than hidden behind a bare conformance claim.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: chorus-ai GitHub organisation, including 'A package status page [that] lists versions, maintainers, and other metadata for CHoRUS packages, and a web guide for contributors and users... compiled in the chorus-developer repository'; the Bridge2AI CHoRUS page. page: https://chorus4ai.org/. existing_uses documents the AIM-AHEAD training programme with canonical Jupyter Notebooks, posters at Bridge2AI and AIM-AHEAD annual meetings, and mentorship. extension_mechanism documents contributor workflow and discussion spaces. Documentation and outreach are both real and locatable: developer guides, SOP repositories, a package status page, a structured training programme with cohorts and dates, and conference presentation routes. Substantially more than a bare landing-page link. URLs well formed; the training programme described in existing_uses corroborates the outreach claim with dates and participant counts rather than asserting it.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: absent. No typed relationship of any kind — no link to the other three Bridge2AI data generation projects named in the description as part of the same consortium, no relation between the released subset and the holdout test set, no relation to the anticipated 100,000-admission dataset. The record describes a consortium of four data generation projects and an internal holdout split, both of which are natural typed relationships, yet none is expressed. Cross-dataset discovery therefore depends entirely on prose. Same gap as Element 1 sub-element 5; the missing relationships are ones the record's own description implies exist.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: id: "https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset"; no doi field; source_caveats: "No version identifier, DOI, citation, release date, retention policy, or errata for the dataset appear anywhere in the bundle" The only identifier is a fragment URI on the project homepage. It is unique within the record but carries no persistence guarantee, no registration with a resolver, and no DOI or RRID exists. The record's notes add that the site 'is under review for potential modification', which is precisely the fragility a persistent identifier is meant to survive. DOI pattern 10.XXXX/... : not present. RRID pattern RRID:SCR_/AB_ : not present. id is a syntactically valid HTTPS URI but fails the persistence requirement of this sub-element.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: "Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI"; description ~1,500 characters covering programme context, 14 contributing hospitals within 20 academic centers, 50,000 admissions across adult/pediatric/neonatal ICU, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 imaging admissions, 23 Tb waveform, nine planned modalities, per-modality formats and the controlled-access enclave model. Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: it names scale, modalities, standards, the access model and the note-tokenization arrangement, so a reader can decide relevance without opening another field. Description content matches the claimed dataset type (multimodal critical-care EHR) and is consistent with instances, distribution_formats and conforms_to; no term is used in a non-standard sense.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: 14 terms including 'critical care', 'intensive care unit', 'electronic health record', 'OMOP Common Data Model', 'physiologic waveforms', 'electroencephalography', 'medical imaging', 'clinical notes', 'social determinants of health', 'AI-ready dataset', 'Bridge2AI', 'multimodal data', 'controlled access' Well above the five-keyword threshold and spread across domain, modality, standard, programme and access model, which is the spread that actually supports retrieval. Every keyword is substantiated elsewhere in the record (for example 'social determinants of health' by the geocoding preprocessing step and sensitive_elements), so none is decorative.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: "https://chorus4ai.org/"; external_resources: "CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/), with pages for the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources" A landing page is given and its structure is itemised, so the reader knows a dataset page and learning resources exist behind it. No hierarchical resources/ subresource tree is modelled, but the sub-element is satisfied by either. URL well formed and domain consistent with the id namespace and with external_resources.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: No parent_datasets and no related_datasets anywhere in the record. splits describes a sequestered holdout test set in prose only, with no typed relationship to a dataset entity. The record sits inside a four-project Bridge2AI programme and provisions a separate holdout set, both of which are natural typed relationships, yet neither is expressed. A consumer cannot machine-resolve the holdout set, the sibling Bridge2AI resources, or any per-site constituent dataset.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: "All data types are made available under controlled access only. Users ... must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset, and must have a '.edu' email address to gain access"; contact_person: "Ciera McCrary"; data_governance.access_review_process names the request route (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org) and the registration/provisioning sequence. The access policy is concrete and actionable: who to ask, what must be signed, what eligibility gate applies, and what happens after approval. ip_restrictions is unpopulated, but the sub-element is satisfied by a clear access policy. Controlled-access assertion is consistent across license_and_use_terms, regulatory_restrictions, every distribution_formats entry and third_party_sharing — no field contradicts the restriction.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; regulatory_restrictions: "The project established a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape to manage privacy and bias; all data types are distributed under controlled access only"; data_governance.committee_contact: "Jared Houghtaling" with request emails in access_review_process. A concrete sensitivity classification plus a named governance contact and request route carry this sub-element. The regulatory narrative itself is thin — a legal framework is asserted rather than characterised — and the most load-bearing statement for US hospital data, HIPAA compliance status, is absent, which is recorded as a separate issue rather than as a failure of the whole sub-element. confidentiality_level 'restricted' is semantically appropriate for patient-level PHI-derived data and consistent with sensitive_elements and confidential_elements; hipaa_compliant and other_compliance unpopulated.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: No download_url field. The only retrieval information is data_governance.access_review_process: "Access is requested from the named CHoRUS contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org)" and, for training-programme trainees, a registration form. The cloud enclave is referred to throughout but never given a URL. Two email addresses are a request channel, not a download or platform link: the record identifies no enclave endpoint, no data portal and no repository page from which an approved user retrieves the data. The gap is the more visible because distribution_formats, third_party_sharing and the holdout provision all assert that data is being delivered to external users. Consistency check: is_shared=true and five distribution_formats entries, yet no resolvable retrieval location — recorded as a failed shared-but-unretrievable check.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: five entries — OMOP CDM tables (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses); OHNLP toolkit output for tokenized notes; DICOM for PACS imaging; WFDB for telemetry; EDF+ and Persyst for EEG — each with a notes field naming the published metadata schema. Formats are named per modality with their governing schema, which is what a reuser needs to size tooling. Media types and byte sizes are absent, but the format specification itself is specific and complete across all released modalities. Every named format is a real standard appropriate to its modality (DICOM/imaging, WFDB/waveform, EDF+/EEG), and each matches the corresponding raw_data_sources.raw_data_format entry.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: external_resources: five entries — chorus4ai.org, https://github.com/chorus-ai, https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824, www.bridge2ai.org/chorus, and the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 informational webinar (September 09, 2025). Substantive and varied: documentation site, code and SOP repository, funding record, programme page and a training webinar. related_datasets is empty, but the sub-element is satisfied by either, and the external resources given are resolvable and each annotated with what it contains. URLs well formed; the RePORTER link's project id 10472824 matches the application ID recorded in funders.notes.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms describes only an access gate (controlled access, signed licensing agreement inside the training-programme registration form, '.edu' email requirement). notes: "the chorus-ai GitHub organization states that its project code is licensed under the MIT License ... these terms govern CHoRUS software rather than the dataset." No license is identified for the data and no reuse permission is stated: nothing on redistribution, derivative works, attribution, publication or retention once a user is inside the enclave. The record is careful to say the MIT/Apache terms cover software only, which is accurate and which leaves the data with no license at all. Scoring this 0 while Element 2 sub-element 1 scores 1 is deliberate — an access policy exists, reuse terms do not. No SPDX or Creative Commons identifier present; the only signed instrument mentioned is scoped to AIM-AHEAD training-programme participants rather than to reusers generally.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats and conforms_to together specify OMOP Common Data Model (with flowsheet extensions), DICOM, WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended, EDF+ and Persyst, and OHNLP output; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. Every modality is delivered in the open community standard for its data type — this is the record's strongest interoperability property. Character encoding is not stated for the tokenized text, which is a real if minor gap for the one textual modality. Format-to-modality assignments are all semantically correct; enumerated conforms_to_standard values agree with the prose conforms_to.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: "Structured clinical data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with nursing flowsheets using the OMOP schema with extensions; imaging follows DICOM; waveform telemetry follows WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended; EEG follows the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas; tokenized clinical notes follow the OHNLP open-source schema."; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset Conformance is stated per modality rather than as a single blanket claim, and extensions are flagged where the standard was not sufficient — exactly the granularity a reuser needs to know where their OMOP tooling will and will not work. OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and OHNLP are all correctly named real standards for their stated data types; the metadata schema URI is well formed.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field anywhere in the record. The closest content is instances[].data_topic (B2AI_TOPIC:4, :6, :7, :8, :9, :15, :32, :37) and data_substrate codes, which classify record types rather than define variables. No variable-level metadata, no data dictionary and no identifiers for fields. OMOP conformance supplies a schema for the structured tables by reference, but the record itself defines no variables, no derived contextual elements (the geocoded distance-to-hospital measure is described only in prose) and no flowsheet extension columns — and the extensions are precisely what OMOP-by-reference does not cover.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three categories with examples — clinical AI/ML model development; external model validation via the sequestered holdout test set; education and workforce development (Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI tool-stack workshops). Also other_tasks (downstream analytics, mapping/interoperability tooling) and existing_uses (AIM-AHEAD cohort training, publications). Intended uses are categorised and illustrated concretely, and existing uses corroborate them. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both empty, which is a notable omission for controlled-access patient data — no bar on re-identification attempts, on redistribution or on clinical deployment is stated — but the sub-element is satisfied by the substantive intended-use guidance. intended_uses align with purposes and tasks (characterising illness, predicting complications, measuring treatment response) with no divergence between stated motivation and stated permitted use.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: "Ethics is one of the project's three pillars (Ethical and Trustworthy AI). The consortium performs community-facing ethics focus groups ... and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape", reviewing_organization: "CHoRUS consortium ethics pillar", with the entry's own caveat: "No source names an institutional review board, ethics committee approval, or protocol number for the dataset." human_subject_research and data_protection_impacts both unpopulated. What is documented is an ethics research programme, not an ethics review of this dataset. For patient-level records drawn from 14 hospitals, the questions this sub-element exists to answer — which board reviewed the collection, under what protocol, with what determination, and was any DPIA performed — are all unanswered, and the record says so itself. The named governance contact and accountable organization establish an operational owner but not ethical oversight. The transparency of the caveat is creditable documentation practice but does not supply the missing oversight evidence. Failed consistency check: patient data present per E1, yet human_subject_research is unpopulated and no IRB approval, protocol number or DPIA exists to satisfy the oversight expectation.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: "Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification of imaging prior to release; data transformations that limit re-identification." deidentification_details: notes retained locally with only tokens transferred; imaging de-identification in process as of September 2025; a privacy scan tool maintained in the chorus-ai organization. A method is described concretely and per modality, naming the tool that performs the text transformation and the architectural choice that keeps note text out of the enclave — this is specific, verifiable-in-principle content rather than an unqualified 'deidentified' flag. It falls short of the standard the sub-element asks for: no recognized framework (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) and, by the record's own caveat, no statement of which identifier categories are removed. Scored 1 on the strength of the described method, with the standard-and-categories gap recorded as a content_accuracy issue. Method appropriateness: tokenization is suitable for free text and de-identification is appropriate for DICOM headers, but no deidentification treatment is described for waveform/EEG signals or for the geocoded Location derivatives, both of which carry residual identifiability.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (OHNLP tokenization, imaging de-identification), privacy_techniques ("Controlled access to all data types through a cloud enclave, local retention of clinical notes at contributing sites, transformation approaches that limit re-identification, and a privacy scan tool for medical records"), data_linkage ("Data from 14 hospitals are harmonized to the OMOP Common Data Model and linked across modalities at the admission level; OMOP Location entities are geocoded"). Protections are described as an implemented architecture — enclave, local note retention, privacy scanning — and the record is candid about linkage, which is the honest thing to disclose since linkage is what raises risk. The re-identification risk half of the sub-element is unmet: no risk level, no assessment, no mitigation tied to the geocoding or the high-resolution signals, and is_deidentified.source_caveats concedes that no source quantifies residual risk. Scored 1 on documented protections, with the unassessed risk recorded as a medium consistency issue. Warning: data_linkage discloses admission-level linkage across nine modalities plus geocoded location, which materially raises re-identification risk, while reidentification_risk remains unassessed — the two statements sit in tension within the same field group.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: No informed_consent field. direct_collection.is_direct=false with the explanation that data were 'obtained retrospectively from records already held by contributing hospitals ... rather than gathered from individuals'. source_caveats: "No source states whether the dataset is governed as human subjects research, nor describes protections, assent, or guardian consent." Nothing is documented about the consent basis. Retrospective collection commonly proceeds under a waiver of consent and of HIPAA authorization, but the record does not say that a waiver was obtained, from whom, or under what criteria, so a reuser cannot establish the legal basis on which 50,000 patients' records entered the enclave. Explaining that collection was indirect describes the mechanism, not the permission.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: No at_risk_populations and no participant_compensation field. subpopulations does identify 'pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)' cohorts; source_caveats states at_risk_populations was 'left unpopulated'. The record identifies two canonical vulnerable groups in its composition — minors, including neonates — and additionally involves critically ill adults who by definition often lack decisional capacity, yet documents no protections, no assent or guardian-permission arrangement and no differential handling. Compensation is plausibly inapplicable to retrospective record extraction, but the vulnerable-population half of the sub-element is squarely applicable and entirely unaddressed.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
