text: subpopulations: two entries with subpopulation_elements_present=true — care setting ("adult intensive care unit (ICU), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)") with distribution noting 50,000 released admissions combined 'without a per-unit breakdown'; and contributing hospital ("14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers"). Two axes of cohort structure are identified with the subpopulation flag set, and the record is explicit about which breakdown it cannot supply, which is more useful than silence. The content is nonetheless thin for an equity-framed resource: no demographics (age, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance), no inclusion or exclusion criteria, and no counts per unit or per site, so a reuser cannot assess cohort composition. Subpopulation axes are consistent with the description and with the ICU/PICU/NICU framing; no contradiction, but no distributional detail to check.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: counts 50000 patient admissions; counts 1600000000 OMOP EHR rows; counts 7642 admissions with radiology data; waveform entry notes 23 Tb; anticipated final 100,000 admissions across nine modalities. splits documents a sequestered holdout test set. Counts are specific, multi-level (admissions, rows, modality coverage, volume) and separate released from anticipated scale. The record also surfaces the competing 45K figure from a lower-tier source and states its preference rule, so the number is traceable rather than merely asserted. Counts in instances match those in the description exactly. One unreconciled figure remains: 7,642 imaging admissions against ~1000 images available as of September 2025, recorded as a low-severity content_accuracy issue.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: is_tabular: false; splits: "The project provisions a sequestered holdout test set, accessible for external model validation"; subpopulations[].subpopulation_elements_present: true (x2); eleven instance types each typed with data_topic and, where applicable, data_substrate codes. Two of the three components are genuinely documented: the tabular flag is set and semantically correct for a nine-modality resource, and both the split role (holdout test set) and the subpopulation flags are present with stated purposes. The variable half is absent — no data dictionary, no column definitions, no identifiers — and OMOP/DICOM/WFDB conformance substitutes only by reference and not for the flowsheet extensions or derived contextual elements. Scored 1 on the documented structure flags and splits; the missing variable metadata is scored 0 at Element 3 sub-element 4, where it is the sole requirement. is_tabular=false is consistent with the modality mix; the holdout split is corroborated by the external-validation task.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances entries typed with B2AI_TOPIC:4 (admissions, procedures, flowsheets), :6 (demographics), :7 (diagnoses), :8 (medication administration), :9 (structured EHR rows), :15 (imaging), :32 (clinical notes), :37 (waveforms, EEG), plus data_substrate codes B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :43, :49; clinical scope stated as critical and acute illness across ICU, PICU and NICU. Topic coverage is expressed with controlled ontology identifiers rather than free text, across all eleven instance types, and the clinical domain is clearly bounded. What is not represented is the condition mix inside the cohort: no diagnosis categories, phenotypes or case counts, so a reuser can see which data types exist but not which illnesses they cover. Topic codes are used consistently — the same code recurs for semantically related instance types (:37 for both waveform and EEG) — with no evident miscoding.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: No anomalies field and no missing_data_documentation. sampling_strategies has a single entry: is_sample=true, strategies "Sampling is designed to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies across contributing sites, and federated access enables sampling methods intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort", source_data describing the 14 acquisition centers. The sampling entry is aspirational rather than descriptive — it states an intent ('designed to ensure', 'intended to ensure') without a selection rule, a frame or an achieved distribution — and neither data quality issues nor missingness is documented at all. This is a serious gap for ICU data specifically, where missingness in flowsheets and waveform gaps is informative and drives modelling decisions, and where the record elsewhere concedes that modality coverage is partial and that site characterization reports exist but are not summarised here. Failed expectation: cleaning_strategies mentions characterization reports returned to sites after each submission, so quality findings demonstrably exist upstream but none is surfaced in anomalies or missing-data documentation.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: No version field. status: "Partial release available under controlled access as of August 2025, with acquisition and modality expansion continuing"; source_caveats confirms "No version identifier ... appear[s] anywhere in the bundle". A release state and an as-of month are given, but no version identifier of any kind. Since the record simultaneously describes a growing dataset, a user who obtains data in one month cannot name what they received or distinguish it from a later extraction — the precise problem versioning exists to solve.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: No version_access field, and no statement anywhere about whether earlier extractions remain retrievable from the enclave. With no versions defined there is also no mechanism to request or pin one. For a dataset explicitly described as growing toward 100,000 admissions, the absence of any snapshot or freeze mechanism directly undermines reproducibility of analyses run against it.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: No errata field. updates.update_details describes site status reporting and forward-looking growth ("imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process as of September 2025") but records no change between releases, no corrections and no change log. Nothing states what changed, when, or what was corrected — there is no release to compare against another. The update_details content is prospective status reporting and is credited under the update-schedule sub-element; crediting the same prose twice would treat one piece of evidence as answering two distinct questions.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: "Ongoing during the project period, with regular status updates from contributing sites"; updates.update_details describes the submission workflow (GitHub interface or a Google Form triggering issue and status-board updates) and the trajectory toward 100,000 admissions and nine modalities, bounded by the award period ending 2026-11-30. The maintenance model is described concretely enough to be actionable: continuous site submission, a named reporting mechanism, an end-point target and a project horizon. It is a cadence rather than a calendar, which suits a rolling accrual, and it is corroborated by status and known_limitations. Consistent with status ('acquisition and modality expansion continuing') and with the partial-coverage limitations; the horizon matches the funders project period.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: five entries, each with source_description, source_type (hospital EHR, hospital PACS, bedside monitoring/telemetry infrastructure, hospital EEG database), raw_data_format (source EHR formats mapped to OMOP; free text tokenized with OHNLP; DICOM; WFDB with PhysioNet schema extended; EDF+/Persyst) and access_details. acquisition_methods second entry carries was_inferred_derived=true for tokenization, OMOP mapping and re-identification-limiting transformations. Provenance is the strongest part of this element: every released modality is traced to the upstream hospital system it came from, in its native format, with the access condition attached, and derived products are flagged as derived. This is genuine source-derivation information and not incidental notes. raw_data_sources entries correspond one-to-one with collection_mechanisms and with distribution_formats; no orphan modality on either side.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four entries (generate data for ML/AI characterising acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, measuring treatment response; develop a publicly available AI-ready critical care dataset promoting privacy, accountability and clinical benefit; create ethically sourced datasets and best practices as one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects; build network, tools, standards, data and education). addressing_gaps: three entries on the absence of high-resolution multi-center critical care infrastructure and the legal/standards work required. Motivation is stated at both the scientific and the programme level, and addressing_gaps articulates what was missing before this dataset existed — the research-gap framing the sub-element asks for, not a restatement of the description. purposes align with the Bridge2AI funding goals named in funders.grantor, satisfying the funding-to-purpose consistency check.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: characterizing acute and critical care illness; predicting complications and deterioration; measuring treatment response; external validation of AI models against a sequestered holdout test set to aid marketplace adoption. Four specific, distinguishable objectives, three of them modelling tasks and one an infrastructure task that is corroborated by the splits entry. They are concrete enough to judge whether the dataset supports them. The external-validation task is consistent with splits and with intended_uses; no task claims a modality the dataset does not contain.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: "National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund, Bridge2AI program"; notes add the awardee institution (Massachusetts General Hospital), award amount 5,880,300 for FY2022 and project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The funding agency, the specific Common Fund programme, the mechanism type (an OT2 other-transaction award, implied by the award number), the amount and the period are all recorded — considerably more than a bare agency name. Grantor, awardee and PI affiliation are mutually consistent (MGH appears in funders.notes, creators.affiliations and data_governance.accountable_organization).

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants: [name: OT2OD032701]; notes: "Project number 1OT2OD032701-01 (core project number OT2OD032701), NIH application ID 10472824 ... https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824" The award is given in both core and full application form, with the application ID and a resolvable RePORTER link, so the funding claim is independently checkable — the strongest form this sub-element can take. NIH pattern validation passes: activity code OT2, administering institute OD (Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund), six-digit serial 032701, with the full form 1OT2OD032701-01 carrying the correct application type and support year prefixes. The RePORTER project id matches the stated application ID.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: principal_investigator "Eric S. Rosenthal" affiliated with Massachusetts General Hospital and identified as PI of OT2OD032701; a consortium entry naming the leadership team (Azra Bihorac, University of Florida; Xiaoqian Jiang, UTHealth Houston; Yulia Strekalova, University of Florida; Parisa Rashidi, University of Florida; Manlik Kwong, Tufts University) and the 60+ member, 20-institution scope. maintainers names the consortium and the program-manager contact. Attribution is specific at both individual and institutional level, and the record explains its own modelling choice — leadership members are recorded in prose rather than as principal_investigator because no source names them as PIs — which prevents a misreading of roles. No ORCID or ROR identifiers are present, transparently caveated; this weakens machine attribution but not the documentation of who created the dataset. PI attribution is consistent with the funders record; the contact email recorded for the program manager contains an apparent domain typo, flagged separately as a low-severity correctness issue.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: five entries — structured EHR extraction into OMOP; note extraction and tokenization with OHNLP so that only tokens enter the enclave; imaging obtained from hospital PACS into DICOM; waveforms captured from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware into WFDB and EEG from hospital EEG databases into EDF+/Persyst; and site-side extract creation and upload via the chorus-extract-upload repository and the interactive Chorus_SOP workflow, with dockerized services on Azure. Each modality has its own mechanism described end to end, from the hospital system of origin to the enclave, and the fifth entry documents the operational workflow that sites actually follow. Clinical setting is bounded (ICU, PICU, NICU across 14 hospitals). The calendar timeframe of the encounters is the one missing setting element, flagged separately. Mechanisms map one-to-one onto raw_data_sources and distribution_formats with no modality unaccounted for.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: retrospective extraction of already-recorded clinical data across EHR, notes, PACS imaging, bedside-monitor/gateway telemetry and hospital EEG databases; plus a derived-data entry (was_inferred_derived=true) covering tokenization, OMOP mapping and re-identification-limiting transformation. raw_data_sources adds the five upstream systems with their native formats and access conditions. Instruments and systems of capture are named at the level a replicator needs — bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, PACS, hospital EEG databases — and the record correctly separates primary acquisition from derivation. direct_collection.is_direct=false is consistent with retrospective extraction; no claim of prospective instrumentation contradicts it.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: five entries (OMOP standardization via validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping; OHNLP tokenization of unstructured text; transformations limiting re-identification plus imaging de-identification; waveform conversion via chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources; geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss using UF-Geocoding). cleaning_strategies: characterization reports from CHoRUSReports returned to sites after each submission; clinical validation of semantic mappings under a validation SOP. labeling_strategies: a visualization and annotation environment labelling data with prediction targets. machine_annotation_tools: OHNLP toolkit, UF-Geocoding. The pipeline is traceable step by step and tied to the repository implementing each step, which is what makes it replicable in principle. The weak points are annotation quality and labelling detail: annotation_analyses is absent, so no inter-annotator agreement or accuracy evidence exists, and the labelling entry describes an environment rather than a label taxonomy or procedure. imputation_protocols is likewise absent. The sub-element is nonetheless well satisfied by the preprocessing and cleaning content. Preprocessing claims are consistent with is_deidentified.method and with participant_privacy.anonymization_method; the geocoding step is consistent with the SDOH keyword and with sensitive_elements.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: machine_annotation_tools.tools: "OHNLP toolkit" ("Used to extract and tokenize clinical notes; outputs conform to the OHNLP open source schema") and "UF-Geocoding" ("Open source code to geocode OMOP Location entities via DeGauss"). preprocessing_strategies additionally names chorus-mapping (validated semantic mappings driving the OMOP standardization) and chorus_waveform / chorus_waveform_resources ("conversion scripts and documentation" for preparing and releasing waveforms). Software is named in the role this sub-element asks about: the OHNLP toolkit produces the tokens that are actually distributed in place of note text, chorus_waveform's conversion scripts produce the released WFDB waveforms, chorus-mapping produces the released OMOP tables, and UF-Geocoding/DeGauss produces the geocoded contextual elements. Evidence is carried by machine_annotation_tools and preprocessing_strategies. No versions, commit pins or software DOIs are given, which is what 'Look for' asks for and weakens reproducibility, but the tooling that transformed the released data is disclosed by name, which is the question. Software in excluded roles is also present and neither adds nor subtracts: chorus-extract-upload (capture/upload, role a), Azure and dockerized services (hosting/packaging, roles b and c), CHoRUSReports characterization (validation, role d). Tool-to-output mapping is coherent across fields — OHNLP appears consistently in collection_mechanisms, preprocessing_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, is_deidentified and conforms_to, describing the same transformation each time.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: project website with documentation sections, chorus-ai GitHub organization hosting SOPs and mappings, NIH RePORTER award record, Bridge2AI programme page, AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 webinar. conforms_to: per-modality standards (OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB/PhysioNet extended, EDF+, Persyst, OHNLP). External standards and supporting documentation are both substantial and each resource is annotated with what it contains, so a reader knows why to follow a link. imputation_protocols is entirely absent — the record does not describe imputation nor state that none was performed, which matters for ICU flowsheet and waveform data where gaps are pervasive; the sub-element is satisfied by the standards and resources components. Standards cited are the correct community standards for each modality; external URLs are well formed and topically consistent with their descriptions.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: four typed entries — coverage_limitation (imaging ~1000 available with de-identification in process, EEG extraction in process) with scope_impact; integration_limitation (notes held locally, only tokens in the enclave) with scope_impact 'Full note text cannot be analyzed centrally alongside the other modalities'; representativeness_limitation (14 hospitals within a 20-center academic network, ICU/PICU/NICU only) with a recommended_mitigation; scope_limitation (50,000 released against 100,000 anticipated). Limitations are typed, specific and consequential, and three of the four state the analytic impact rather than merely the fact. They are also candid about shortfalls against the project's own targets, which is the harder kind of disclosure. Each limitation is corroborated by another field (instances notes, preprocessing, subpopulations, status) — none is a generic disclaimer.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: No known_biases field. The nearest content is a single representativeness_limitation in known_limitations and a passing reference in future_use_impacts to work that 'determines approaches to manage privacy and bias'. No bias is categorised, typed or characterised. For a resource titled 'for Equitable AI', keyworded with social determinants of health, and drawn exclusively from academic medical centers, the absence is conspicuous: selection bias from the academic sampling frame, representation bias with no demographic distribution reported, and measurement bias across heterogeneous site instrumentation are all unaddressed. A one-line mitigation intent inside a limitation entry is not a bias taxonomy. Failed consistency check between the equity framing in title/keywords and the absence of any bias documentation.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: No anomalies field. cleaning_strategies notes that characterization reports are produced from CHoRUSReports and returned to contributing sites after each submission, but no finding from those reports is recorded. Nothing about outliers, artifacts, implausible values, monitor disconnection gaps, mapping failures or cross-site inconsistency — all expected in multicenter ICU data harmonised from heterogeneous EHRs. The record establishes that a quality characterization process exists and returns findings upstream, which makes the absence of any surfaced finding a documentation gap rather than an absence of information.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: three entries with sensitive_elements_present=true — patient-level hospital records spanning demographics, diagnoses, medications, procedures, flowsheets, notes, imaging and waveforms; social determinants of health and geocoded contextual factors such as distance to nearest hospital; unstructured notes carrying heightened identifiability risk, hence local retention. confidential_elements: all data types under controlled access, with community focus groups determining what is appropriate for public sharing. Sensitivity is not merely flagged but reasoned: the record identifies which elements are sensitive, why the geocoded and free-text elements are the sharpest risks, and what handling follows from each. That linkage between sensitivity and mitigation is what makes the disclosure useful. Consistent with confidentiality_level='restricted', with the note-tokenization architecture and with the geocoding preprocessing step; no content_warnings field, which is of low relevance for this data type.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: the Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar, community-facing ethics focus groups determining what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape. future_use_impacts: two entries — methods intended to promote privacy, accountability and clinical benefit with patient-focused ethical and legal work on privacy and bias accounting for SDOH; and community perspectives shaping the scope of data available for future use. Read as this sub-element asks — ethical review activity and anticipated downstream social impact — the content is genuinely responsive: a standing ethics programme, a described community-engagement mechanism with a concrete effect on what gets shared, and a stated framing of downstream impact. Scoring this 1 while Element 4 sub-element 1 scores 0 is deliberate and not a contradiction: that sub-element asks whether an oversight body approved this dataset, which remains unanswered, whereas this one asks whether ethical review and social impact were analysed, which is documented. The impacts are framed as intentions rather than as identified risks with mitigations, and no conflicts of interest are disclosed. future_use_impacts is consistent with purposes and with sensitive_elements; it does not however substitute for the missing bias taxonomy, which is scored separately.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: No publisher field. Hosting is described only as a project-operated 'cloud enclave' with 'dockerized container applications support[ing] CHoRUS services deployed on Azure'; github.com/chorus-ai hosts software rather than data. No recognized data repository is named — not PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo or an institutional repository — and no publishing organization is recorded. A self-operated enclave on generic cloud infrastructure, reachable only by emailing two individuals, does not place the dataset in a discoverable ecosystem, and it leaves long-term custody unstated. Notable given that the waveform modality explicitly uses 'the PhysioNet schema extended' while no PhysioNet deposition or any other repository is claimed.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: No citation field and no doi field; source_caveats: "No version identifier, DOI, citation, release date, retention policy, or errata for the dataset appear anywhere in the bundle." A user who obtains and analyses this data has no recommended citation, no DOI and — combined with the absent version — no way to identify in a publication which resource and which state of it was used. existing_uses states that CHoRUS datasets are already supporting publications, which makes the absence of citation guidance an active rather than a latent problem. DOI format validation: not present. The only funder-side identifier (the RePORTER award link) identifies the grant, not the dataset.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to names OMOP Common Data Model (with flowsheet extensions), DICOM, WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended, EDF+, Persyst and the OHNLP open-source schema; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema. Conformance to established community standards is asserted per modality, in both prose and enumerated form, and extended to the metadata record itself. This is the record's clearest tie to wider data ecosystems — OHDSI/OMOP in particular brings an entire analytic toolchain with it, and intended_uses confirms the project runs OHDSI tool-stack workshops. Enumerated and prose conformance agree; each standard is correctly matched to its modality.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/; external_resources include the project website with 'pages for the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources', the chorus-ai GitHub organization with SOPs and mappings, the Bridge2AI programme page and the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 informational webinar (September 09, 2025). intended_uses describes canonical Jupyter notebooks and OHDSI tool-stack workshops; extension_mechanism points contributors to https://github.com/chorus-ai. Outreach is real and varied — a documentation site with a learning-resources section, a training programme with a dated webinar, workshops, notebooks and a contributor guide in the chorus-developer repository. A reader has multiple concrete entry points into the community around the dataset. Links well formed and consistent with the page field and with maintainers; the webinar is dated, which aids provenance of the figures drawn from it.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: No related_datasets field. The sequestered holdout test set appears only as prose in splits, and the three sibling Bridge2AI data generation projects are referenced only as programme context in the description. No typed relationship of any kind is expressed — not 'has part' to the holdout set, not 'is part of' to the Bridge2AI programme, not 'derives from' to the contributing site extracts. The relationships plainly exist in the record's own prose, so this is an encoding gap rather than an absence of relationships, and it leaves the dataset unlinked to the ecosystem it belongs to.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; no doi field; no RRID anywhere in the record. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema identifies the metadata schema, not the dataset. The only identifier is the project homepage URL, which is byte-identical to the landing page and names the project rather than the dataset or any released version. No DOI, ARK, Handle or RRID is present, so the dataset cannot be uniquely resolved or cited; for a partially released, growing collection this also means no version-level identity. DOI pattern check: not applicable, no candidate string. RRID pattern check: no RRID:SCR_ or RRID:AB_ token present. id resolves as a syntactically valid https URI but fails the persistence and dataset-specificity criteria; a w3id.org value appears only as conforms_to_schema and is correctly used there for the schema, not misappropriated as a dataset identifier.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'CHoRUS Dataset'; description (approx. 1,500 characters): 'multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of acute and critical care hospital admissions ... collected retrospectively from 14 contributing hospitals drawn from a network of 20 academic centers ... standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with imaging from PACS in DICOM, bedside telemetry in WFDB, EEG in EDF+ and Persyst, and clinical notes extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit ... 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data'. Far beyond the 200-character threshold and dense with specifics rather than boilerplate: scale, modality-by-modality standards, setting, access model (enclave versus local note storage), governing program, and intended analytic uses. A reader can decide relevance without opening another document. Description content matches the claimed dataset type throughout: critical-care terminology, standards, and unit choices are used correctly and are consistent with instances, file_collections and distribution_formats. Title is generic ('CHoRUS Dataset', no version or scope qualifier) but unambiguous given the description.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [critical care, intensive care, acute illness, electronic health records, OMOP Common Data Model, waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, medical imaging, clinical notes, multimodal clinical data, Bridge2AI, AI-ready dataset, social determinants of health] Thirteen keywords, well above the five-term expectation, spanning clinical domain, care setting, each data modality, the standard used, the funding program, and an equity dimension. Discovery from any of the modality, domain or program directions would surface the record. Keyword set is semantically consistent with description, instances and distribution_formats: every modality keyword (waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, medical imaging, clinical notes) has a corresponding instance type and file collection. 'social determinants of health' is corroborated by sensitive_elements rather than being an unsupported tag. Program context is inferred from the keyword 'Bridge2AI' and the funders.grantor value, not from filename or prior knowledge.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; file_collections: five hierarchical collections with stable ids and descriptions (#collection-omop, #collection-waveform-telemetry, #collection-imaging, #collection-clinical-notes, #collection-eeg); external_resources notes the site's pages on team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources. A plausible, project-owned landing page is given and the record supplies a genuine hierarchical resource structure beneath it: five modality collections each with a collection_type, description, conformance statement and release status. This is more structure than a bare page URL would provide. URL syntactically valid with plausible domain matching the project name. Collection ids are fragment identifiers under that domain, which is internally consistent, though they are anchors rather than independently resolvable endpoints. A banner quoted in notes ('under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives') is a stability caveat, not a validity failure.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: No parent_datasets field. No related_datasets field. The description states the project is 'one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium', and external_resources lists the GitHub organization and NIH RePORTER record, but no dataset-to-dataset relationship is typed anywhere. The sibling Bridge2AI datasets and the relationship between the released 50,000-admission snapshot and the anticipated 100,000-admission final dataset are both described only in prose. No parent, derivation, version-of or supplement relationship is expressed in a field a system could traverse. file_collections provides intra-dataset hierarchy but not the inter-dataset relationships this sub-element asks for; crediting it here would conflate the two and duplicate the evidence already scored under sub-element 4.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Access to the dataset is controlled and conditioned on a signed licensing agreement: all participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care training program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset, and a ".edu" email address is required for dataset access. The chorus-ai GitHub organization states that its project code is licensed under the MIT License.' data_governance.access_review_process: registration form (name, email, institution), signed licensing agreement, .edu requirement, compute provisioning notification, and request contacts dbold@emory.edu / jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. The access policy is defined concretely enough to act on: who may apply, what they must sign, what credential is required, who to contact, and what happens once granted. The accompanying source_caveats correctly warns that the MIT statement covers code and that these are one route's terms. Consistent with regulatory_restrictions (every data type controlled access) and with confidential_elements (notes not releasable). The IP position is only partially resolved: the MIT License is correctly attributed to software, and the record states plainly that no license is named for the data itself, which is a gap carried into Element 3 sub-element 1 rather than double-penalized here.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted. regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: ['Every data type in the project\'s data inventory is listed with controlled access control.', 'Clinical notes may not leave the contributing site; only tokens are shared.'] source_caveats: 'The source documents do not state a HIPAA determination, export control status, or GDPR applicability for this dataset; the training curriculum lists HIPAA/GDPR compliance for OMOP/FHIR data as a workshop topic rather than as a statement about the dataset.' Confidentiality is explicitly classified and the restrictions are stated as operative, enforceable constraints rather than as an empty block: one of them (notes may not leave the site) is a hard data-residency rule that materially shapes what a reuser can do. The absence of a HIPAA determination is a real gap, disclosed rather than papered over, and it is charged as a completeness issue rather than negating the classification that is present. hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are absent, which for US multicenter clinical data is a notable omission; no data_governance.committee_contact is designated, though individual access contacts and an accountable_organization (Massachusetts General Hospital) are named. This block states constraints that apply, so it satisfies the governance condition that gates Element 4 sub-elements 1 and 2.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: No download_url field. The analysis environment is named in prose only: 'OMOP and telemetry data are worked with inside the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud enclave' and 'CHoRUS services are deployed on Azure through dockerized container applications'. Access requests are directed to two email addresses; page resolves to the project site, not to a data endpoint. There is no download URL and no link to the platform where the data is reached. A prospective user learns that access exists and whom to email, but not where the enclave is, how to reach a request portal, or what URL to visit after approval; the one concrete route documented (the AIM-AHEAD training registration form) is given without a link. Controlled access explains why there is no direct download but not why no request or platform URL is provided. Distinguished from sub-element 1, which is satisfied: the terms of access are defined, the location of access is not. The GitHub organization URL in external_resources points to tooling, not to the data.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: five entries with per-modality notes — 'OMOP Common Data Model' (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses; metadata in OMOP schema with extensions for flowsheets), 'OHNLP' (tokenized notes; metadata planned), 'DICOM' (PACS imaging; access-control metadata planned), 'WFDB' (telemetry; metadata described as the PhysioNet schema extended), 'EDF+ and Persyst' (EEG). file_collections carry matching conforms_to_standard values [OMOP_CDM, WFDB, DICOM, OTHER, OTHER]. Every released modality has a named, specific format together with the metadata schema published alongside it and an honest marker of which metadata are still planned. This is well past a bare format list and lets a reuser judge tooling requirements per modality. Formats are modality-appropriate and correctly used (WFDB for telemetry, DICOM for PACS, EDF+/Persyst for EEG, OMOP for structured EHR). MIME media types and byte sizes are absent, and no file-level encoding is given, which limits machine actionability but does not undercut the format specification itself.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: external_resources: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai — the CHoRUS for Equitable AI GitHub organization, holding 28 repositories including chorus-extract-upload, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, chorus-container-apps, CHoRUSReports, privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid'; 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'; 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'; 'https://www.aim-ahead.net/media/jnzdnid3/bridge2ai-for-clinical-care-informational-webinar-cohort-2.pdf'. extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai. Five distinct external resources across four purposes — code and SOPs, project documentation, funder record, and the access/training webinar — each annotated with what it contains. The GitHub entry names the specific repositories a reuser would need, which is materially more useful than an organization link alone. related_datasets is absent, so the sub-element is carried entirely by external_resources, which the rubric permits. One entry ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus') lacks a URI scheme; the remaining four are well-formed with plausible domains (github.com, chorus4ai.org, reporter.nih.gov, aim-ahead.net), and the RePORTER project id 10472824 matches the application ID recorded under funders.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.source_caveats: 'The MIT License statement is made about the GitHub software project, not about the data; the source documents do not name a license for the dataset itself, and the access terms described are those of the training program registration route.' license_terms names only a signed licensing agreement inside the AIM-AHEAD registration form, whose contents are not described. No license governs the data. The one licensing instrument mentioned is an unpublished agreement embedded in a training-program registration form, so a prospective reuser cannot determine redistribution rights, derivative-work rights, publication conditions or attribution requirements. The record is commendably explicit that this is absent, but the sub-element asks whether reuse terms are stated, and they are not. Scored separately from Element 2 sub-element 1, which asks whether an access policy is defined (it is) rather than whether reuse is licensed (it is not). No CC, ODC, or custom DUA identifier appears anywhere in the record.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: OMOP Common Data Model, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst. file_collections[].conforms_to: 'OMOP Common Data Model', 'WFDB, with metadata published as an extended PhysioNet schema', 'DICOM', 'OHNLP open source schema', 'EDF+ and Persyst'. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. Every modality is delivered in a widely adopted, tool-supported community format, and the format is stated at both dataset and collection level consistently. A reuser can select existing toolchains (OHDSI, pydicom, wfdb, MNE) without bespoke parsing. Character encoding is nowhere specified, and no media types or file-level attributes are given, which matters most for the OHNLP token output where tokenization and encoding interact. The format claims themselves are internally consistent across description, file_collections, distribution_formats and raw_data_sources.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'Structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets and diagnoses) are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with published metadata in the OMOP schema and, for nursing flowsheets, the OMOP schema with extensions. Imaging from PACS follows DICOM. Waveform telemetry follows WFDB ... EEG waveforms use EDF+ and Persyst. Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized against the OHNLP open source schema.' conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; conforms_to_class: Dataset ; instances carry ontology-coded data_topic (B2AI_TOPIC:9, 15, 32, 37) and data_substrate (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, 43, 49) terms. Conformance is stated per data element class rather than as a blanket claim, including the honest qualification that flowsheet metadata extends the standard schema. Ontology term identifiers on instances add machine-resolvable semantic typing beyond the prose. Standard names are used correctly and match the modalities they are attached to. Extension points (OMOP with flowsheet extensions, PhysioNet schema extended) are declared, which is exactly what a harmonizing reuser needs to know; the specific extension content is not documented.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field anywhere in the record. The closest content is instance-level typing ('Row of electronic health record data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model', data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:9) and prose enumeration of domains covered: 'demographics, medication administration time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and diagnoses documented by providers'. No variable-level metadata, no data dictionary, no field identifiers, units or value sets, for a release whose principal component is 1.6 billion rows of tabular data. OMOP conformance substitutes by reference for standard tables but leaves the declared CHoRUS extensions and the waveform, EEG and token outputs undocumented at variable level. Domain-level prose is real information but operates at a coarser granularity than this sub-element requires; crediting it would also duplicate the evidence scored under sub-element 3 and Element 5 sub-element 4.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three entries with use_category and usage_notes — 'Machine learning model development for acute and critical care' ('models can be built to improve the care and outcomes of patients requiring critical care, using multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging and text data harmonized under unified standards'), 'External validation of AI models' (with source_caveats 'The source documents do not report that this holdout set has been released'), and 'AI/ML workforce training and education' (AIM-AHEAD trainees developing use cases in the enclave). existing_uses records training activities and publications as of the September 2025 webinar. Intended uses are categorized, described concretely, and calibrated: the holdout-validation use is explicitly marked as not yet realized rather than advertised as available. A reuser can tell which uses the dataset supports today. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent, which for controlled-access critical-care data is a meaningful omission — no prohibition on re-identification attempts, on removing data from the enclave, or on clinical deployment of models trained on it is recorded, even though those constraints are implied by the access regime described elsewhere. The rubric satisfies this sub-element on any of the three fields, and the intended_uses content is substantive enough to pass; the missing prohibitions are logged as an issue.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews[0].review_details: 'Ethics is one of three project pillars (Ethical and Trustworthy AI). The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI ... establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale, and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape.' ethical_reviews[0].source_caveats: 'The source documents do not name an IRB or ethics committee of record for the dataset and do not report an approval number or determination.' human_subject_research.source_caveats repeats that no IRB approval, ethics review board of record, or regulatory compliance determination is stated. No data_protection_impacts field; no governance committee contact. What is documented is a project ethics workstream — focus groups, legal-landscape analysis, community engagement — not review or approval of this dataset. For a 14-site retrospective extract of critically ill patients including minors and neonates, a reuser cannot identify the reviewing body, the approval or determination, the reliance arrangement across sites, or any DPIA. The field is populated with genuine content that does not answer the oversight question the sub-element asks. Fails the stated consistency check: involves_human_subjects=true requires IRB or equivalent oversight evidence, and none is present. The gap is one the record itself discloses twice, so this is an absence in the documented dataset governance rather than an evaluator inference.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text, transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, and de-identification of imaging prior to release.' is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'As of August 2025, 1000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger imaging cohort. Supporting tooling in the chorus-ai organization includes a privacy scan tool for medical records and a CTP-deid repository.' source_caveats: identifiers removed are not enumerated, no standard is stated for structured data, and no residual risk assessment is reported. The method is described per modality with named implementing tooling — OHNLP tokenization for notes, CTP-deid (a recognized DICOM de-identification toolkit) and a privacy scan tool for imaging and records — and the state of completion is dated. That is specific and actionable, above the boilerplate threshold, even though it is not a formal standard. Method is appropriate to the data types: tokenization is the right control for free-text notes and pixel/header de-identification via a CTP-based pipeline is the right control for DICOM. Two gaps remain: no HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination claim for the structured OMOP data, and no identifiers_removed enumeration, both flagged as a medium consistency issue. The enclave-only access model partially compensates for the weaker structured-data claim.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy[0].anonymization_method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record data and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, with clinical notes retained at the contributing site.' participant_privacy[0].reidentification_risk: 'The project states that data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; no quantitative residual risk is reported in the source documents.' notes: 'Patient-focused efforts within the project determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.' Corroborated by confidential_elements (note text not releasable) and regulatory_restrictions (all modalities controlled access). Concrete, verifiable protections are documented and layered: notes never leave the contributing site, only tokens enter the enclave, analysis happens inside the enclave, and every modality is controlled access. This is a substantive privacy architecture rather than an assertion of care. The reidentification_risk slot is populated but reports a qualitative claim and an explicit absence of quantification rather than an assessment — a real weakness for high-resolution waveform and imaging data, which are known to carry re-identification potential even after header scrubbing. The honest negative statement is credited as documentation of the risk position; the missing quantitative assessment is logged as an issue rather than treated as an empty field.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: No informed_consent field anywhere in the record. direct_collection[0].is_direct: false, 'Data are acquired retrospectively from clinical systems at contributing hospitals rather than gathered directly from patients for this project'. human_subject_research.source_caveats notes that no IRB approval or determination is stated; at_risk_populations.source_caveats states the sources 'describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections'. Nothing is documented about the legal basis on which patient data left 14 hospitals: no consent procedure, no broad consent for secondary use, no waiver determination, no opt-out mechanism, and no withdrawal route. Retrospective collection makes a waiver likely, but likelihood is not documentation, and a reuser of a controlled-access critical-care dataset needs the basis stated. Fails the stated consistency check: involves_human_subjects=true is expected to be accompanied by documented consent procedures. Combined with the absent IRB record under sub-element 1, the two failures compound — neither the oversight body nor the consent basis can be identified.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true ; notes: 'Admissions from pediatric intensive care units and neonatal intensive care units are part of the current released dataset.' human_subject_research.special_populations: 'The released dataset includes admissions from pediatric and neonatal intensive care units, so minors and neonates are represented.' source_caveats: 'The value is an inference from the reported PICU and NICU admissions; the source documents do not characterize the cohort as including at-risk or vulnerable populations and describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections.' No participant_compensation field. The record affirmatively identifies the vulnerable groups present and names them specifically (minors, neonates), tying the determination to the reported PICU and NICU admissions and marking it as inference. For a reuser planning analyses or applying for access, knowing that pediatric and neonatal records are in scope is the operative fact, and it is documented in two mutually consistent fields. Identification is present and non-trivial; protections are absent, and participant_compensation is absent without comment — defensible for retrospective record collection, where no participant interaction occurs, but not stated. Scored 1 on the strength of the specific, cross-corroborated identification, with the missing protections logged as a medium consistency issue rather than double-counted here.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: three entries each with subpopulation_elements_present: true and identification — 'Admissions to intensive care units (ICU)', 'Admissions to pediatric intensive care units (PICU)', 'Admissions to neonatal intensive care units (NICU)' — each carrying source_caveats: 'The released figure of 50,000 patient admissions is reported for ICU, PICU and NICU combined; no per-setting breakdown is given.' Contributing cohort context: '14 contributing hospitals drawn from a network of 20 academic centers'. Three clinically meaningful subpopulations are identified and flagged, spanning adult, pediatric and neonatal critical care, with the site network described. This is real cohort structure, and the repeated caveat that counts are combined is accurate rather than evasive. No demographic characterization at all — no age, sex, race, ethnicity, payer or geography distribution — and no inclusion or exclusion criteria, for a project whose stated purpose is equitable AI and whose keywords include social determinants of health. The subpopulation identification passes the threshold; the demographic silence is logged as a high-severity completeness issue and echoed in the record's own representativeness_limitation.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: 'Hospital admission of a critically ill patient' counts: 50000; 'Row of electronic health record data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model' counts: 1600000000; 'Hospital admission with associated radiology imaging' counts: 7642; 'Bedside monitor waveform telemetry record' (no count, notes '23 Tb of waveform data; no record or file count is given for the waveform modality'); plus tokenized clinical note and EEG instance types. Anticipated final dataset: 100,000 admissions across 9 modalities. Counts are specific, per instance type, and given with their units, distinguishing admissions from rows from terabytes. Where no count exists (waveform records, notes, EEG) the record says so explicitly instead of leaving the reader to guess, and the released-versus-anticipated distinction is maintained. One unresolved discrepancy: source_caveats records the webinar figure of 'over 45K unique admissions' against the website's 50,000, and imaging is counted as 7,642 admissions in one source and 1,000 available images in another. The record ranks its sources and reports both figures rather than silently reconciling them, which is good practice, but the released cohort size remains ambiguous — logged as a content_accuracy issue.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: No variables field. No is_tabular field. No is_data_split or is_subpopulation flags on dataset subsets (subpopulation_elements_present appears on subpopulations, not as a subset flag). splits[0].split_details: 'The award abstract states that the project will sequester holdout datasets and will provision a holdout test set accessible for model external validation', with source_caveats: 'This is described in the award abstract as a planned capability; the source documents do not report the size or availability of the holdout partition.' The primary ask — variable-level metadata or a data dictionary — is entirely absent for a release dominated by 1.6 billion rows of tabular OMOP data, and the tabular flag is unset. The only split content is a planned holdout with no size, no composition and no availability, which cannot orient a user to a role any subset currently plays. Scoring 0 despite the populated splits field: the field describes a future capability rather than a realized partition, and no variable or flag evidence exists to combine with it. Consistent with Element 3 sub-element 4, which fails on the same absent variables field.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry ontology-coded topics and substrates: data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:9 (EHR admissions and OMOP rows), B2AI_TOPIC:15 with data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11 (radiology imaging), B2AI_TOPIC:37 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49 (waveform telemetry and EEG), B2AI_TOPIC:32 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43 (tokenized clinical notes). Content domains enumerated: 'demographics, medication administration ... procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and diagnoses documented by providers'; sensitive_elements adds social determinants of health and geographic distance to the nearest hospital. Six instance types cover the represented topics with machine-resolvable ontology identifiers plus prose enumeration of the clinical content domains, so a reuser can tell which modalities and which classes of clinical information are present. Ontology term identifiers are consistently applied and modality-appropriate (imaging substrate on the imaging instance, waveform substrate on both telemetry and EEG). Specific disease conditions or phenotypes are not enumerated — no diagnosis distribution or condition list — which limits topical discovery to the setting and modality level rather than the clinical-condition level.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: instances[2].missing_information: missing 'Imaging beyond the approximately 1,000 images reported as available in August 2025', why_missing 'De-identification was in process for a larger imaging cohort.' instances[4].missing_information: missing 'Full clinical note text', why_missing 'Clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites; only tokens leave the site.' sampling_strategies[0].strategies: 'Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies. Federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort', with source_caveats that both statements describe intended approaches and the sampling actually applied is not reported. Missing data is documented where it exists, per instance type, with the reason for the absence — a structural gap (notes never leave the site) and a temporal one (imaging de-identification in progress). Combined with the sampling strategy entry, a reuser can anticipate the principal holes in the release. No anomalies field and no missing_data_documentation block; the missing-information content sits on instances, which the rubric's field list for this sub-element reaches via missing_data_documentation's concept. The sampling entry is aspirational and marked as such. Sufficient for this sub-element, but the absence of any data-quality anomaly reporting is scored against Element 9 sub-element 3 rather than forgiven there.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: No version field. status: 'partially released'. The nearest temporal anchors are narrative: 'as of August 2025' in collection_timeframes and updates, and 'the current released dataset' in description and updates.update_details. No version identifier of any kind for a dataset the record describes as actively growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions with two modalities still being ingested. Work performed against the August 2025 state cannot be distinguished from work performed against a later state, which undermines reproducibility of any analysis built on it. The 'partially released' status is a lifecycle stage, not a version. Dated snapshot language ('as of August 2025') is used consistently and is the closest functional substitute, but it is prose rather than an assigned, citable version.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: No version_access field. data_governance.access_review_process describes how to obtain access to the dataset but says nothing about obtaining a particular state of it; updates.source_caveats: 'The source documents do not state a release cadence or versioning policy for the dataset itself.' With no versions assigned, there is correspondingly no mechanism documented for retrieving a prior state, pinning an analysis to a snapshot, or determining which state an enclave workspace holds. This is a compounding gap for an enclave-hosted dataset where users cannot keep their own copy. Consistent with sub-element 1: the absence is structural rather than an oversight in one field, and the record states the policy gap explicitly.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: updates.update_details: 'Data acquisition is ongoing. The current released dataset covers 50,000 patient admissions, while the anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. Imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process as of August 2025. Contributing sites provide regular status updates on their progress in creating and curating a CHoRUS-specific clinical data extract.' Corroborated by known_limitations (coverage_limitation) and instances[2].missing_information. The dedicated update_details field carries actual release-state information: what is in the current release, what the target is, and which two modalities are mid-ingestion as of a stated date. A reuser can tell how the content differs now from what it will contain, which is the substance of a change description even without a formal changelog. No errata field and no per-version change log; nothing is recorded about corrections to previously distributed data, which matters because characterization reports returned to sites (cleaning_strategies) imply that site resubmissions occur. Credited on the strength of substantive, dated release-state documentation, not on the mere presence of an updates block.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.source_caveats: 'The source documents do not state a release cadence or versioning policy for the dataset itself.' The only cadence language is 'Data acquisition is ongoing' and 'Contributing sites provide regular status updates on their progress', which describes site reporting to the consortium, not dataset releases to users. No schedule, frequency, or next-release expectation for the dataset. A user cannot plan around whether the imaging and EEG modalities arrive in a month or a year, nor learn how they would be notified. Correctly distinguished from sub-element 3: an account of what is changing is present, an account of when it will be published is not. The record's own caveat confirms the absence rather than leaving it to inference, and the internal site-reporting cadence is not repurposed as a release cadence.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Clinical source systems at the 14 CHoRUS data contributing hospitals, comprising electronic health records, PACS imaging archives, bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, and hospital EEG databases.' raw_data_sources: five structured entries — hospital EHR systems (site-native formats mapped to OMOP before delivery; only the standardized extract is delivered), unstructured note text (free text; notes stay local, only OHNLP tokens available), PACS (DICOM), bedside monitors with gateway/middleware (waveform telemetry converted to WFDB), hospital EEG database (EDF+ and Persyst). created_by: CHoRUS Consortium. The strongest element of the record: every released modality is traced to its originating clinical system, with the native format, the transformation applied before delivery, and the access condition on the source stated per entry. A reuser can reconstruct the chain from bedside instrument to distributed file. raw_data_sources aligns one-to-one with was_derived_from, file_collections, distribution_formats and the preprocessing_strategies that perform each conversion — no orphan source and no modality lacking a source. Formal PROV-O structure is absent but the rubric accepts structured text, and the entity-activity relationships are recoverable from the text as written.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four responses — 'Generate data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response'; 'Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit'; 'Provision a holdout test set accessible for model external validation, to aid marketplace adoption'; 'Create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and establish best practices for AI in health'. addressing_gaps: three responses including 'There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine learning in critical care' and 'Unified standards are needed to harmonize multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging, and text data across institutions'. Purpose is stated at both the scientific and the infrastructural level, and addressing_gaps articulates the specific research gap the dataset exists to close. Together they explain not just what the dataset is for but why it needed to be built. Purposes align with the funding mechanism (Common Fund Bridge2AI, whose stated aim is ethically sourced AI-ready data) and with the tasks, intended_uses and description — no divergence between the motivation claimed and the dataset delivered.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Characterizing acute and critical care illness'; 'Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness'; 'Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness'; 'External validation of AI-developed models against a sequestered holdout test set, which the award abstract states the project will provision.' Four distinct, well-formed analytic objectives spanning characterization, prediction and treatment-response estimation, phrased concretely enough to map onto modelling problems. The fourth is attributed to the award abstract and marked as a project commitment. Tasks are consistent with the modalities actually released (high-frequency flowsheet and waveform data support deterioration prediction; OMOP structured data supports treatment-response measurement). No task requires data the record says is unavailable, except the holdout validation task, which is correspondingly flagged as not yet released in intended_uses.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grant notes record 'fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01 and project end 2026-11-30' and 'The project website states that the project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701.' The funder is named at both agency and program level, with the mechanism evident from the award type, the award amount, and the full project period. notes also record the disclaimer that website content does not necessarily represent official NIH views. Funder identity is corroborated independently by the RePORTER URL in external_resources (project-details/10472824, matching the application ID recorded here) and by the Bridge2AI keyword. The OT2 other-transaction mechanism is the one the Common Fund uses for Bridge2AI data generation projects, so agency, program and mechanism are mutually consistent.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants[0].grant_number: 'OT2OD032701'; notes: 'NIH RePORTER lists project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01 and project end 2026-11-30.' A structured grant_number is supplied together with the fully qualified project number, the application ID, and the award period, so the award can be verified against RePORTER without ambiguity. Format check passes for NIH: OT2 (other transaction activity code) + OD (Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund awards) + six digits 032701, and the qualified form 1OT2OD032701-01 correctly adds the application type prefix and support-year suffix. The grantor named is NIH Common Fund, so agency and number pattern match. Application ID 10472824 matches the RePORTER URL in external_resources.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: seven entries — Eric Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital, with principal_investigator block and id https://chorus4ai.org/#person-eric-rosenthal, sourced to both the webinar leadership slide and the RePORTER record), Azra Bihorac and Yulia Strekalova and Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University), and 'CHoRUS Consortium' ('More than 60 CHoRUS consortium members across 20 different institutions'). maintainers: program manager at MGH and GitHub organization access contacts. data_collectors: Data Acquisition centers and CHoRUS sub-teams. Named individuals with affiliations, an explicit PI designation, the collective consortium credit, and separately documented maintainer and collector roles. Each attribution carries a provenance note stating where the name was found, which is unusually traceable. Creator affiliations are consistent with the accountable_organization (MGH) and with the RePORTER organization recorded under funders ('MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL HOSPITAL'). One recorded contact address, cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu, has a suspect domain that the record flags verbatim; it affects contactability, not attribution, and is logged as a low-severity correctness issue. No ORCIDs are present.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: 'Contributing sites create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract using the tooling in the chorus-extract-upload repository, following an interactive workflow diagram with links to validated standard operating procedure documents'; 'Bedside monitors with gateway/middleware supply waveform telemetry'; 'Imaging is drawn from hospital PACS'; 'EEG waveforms are drawn from hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst formats'; 'Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit'. collection_timeframes: retrospective collection, snapshot 'as of August 2025, covering 14 different hospitals', with a caveat distinguishing the award period from the encounter period. direct_collection: is_direct false, with details. Mechanisms are given per modality and name the actual tooling and workflow a site follows, including the SOP-driven extract-and-upload path. The settings are specified (14 contributing hospitals, ICU/PICU/NICU, retrospective) and the timeframe caveat prevents a reader from misreading the award dates as the encounter window. Consistent with raw_data_sources and acquisition_methods, which describe the same five pathways from the source side. One genuine gap, disclosed rather than hidden: the calendar range of included clinical encounters is nowhere stated, which limits assessment of practice-era drift.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true — 'Retrospective acquisition of clinical data recorded in the course of care ... including provider documentation of procedures and diagnoses, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, medication administration time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, PACS imaging, bedside monitor telemetry and hospital EEG recordings'; was_inferred_derived true — tokenization of unstructured text and OMOP standardization 'so that delivered records are derived from rather than identical to the site source records'; was_validated_verified true — 'Semantic mappings ... are validated, and standard operating procedures used by contributing sites undergo an internal validation and review process within the Chorus_SOP repository'. raw_data_sources adds five entries with source_type and raw_data_format. Acquisition is described with the schema's provenance flags set correctly and each flag justified in prose, covering observation, derivation and validation. The instrument and system classes are named (bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, PACS, hospital EEG databases, EHR systems), and the granularity of medication timestamping is specified. The three flags are mutually consistent and match the pipeline described in preprocessing_strategies. Specific device manufacturers, monitor models and EHR vendors are not named, which limits exact replication of the capture stage but does not leave the acquisition method unstated.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: OMOP standardization 'using validated semantic mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository'; note extraction and tokenization with the OHNLP toolkit plus transformation limiting re-identification; waveform conversion 'using the conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform repository, with supporting materials in chorus_waveform_resources'. cleaning_strategies: 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, using the CHoRUSReports repository'; validated semantic mappings with 'a clinical validation standard operating procedure' and internally reviewed site SOPs. labeling_strategies: annotation environment described, with source_caveats that it is future tense and no labels are reported in the current release. The pipeline is documented stage by stage and each stage points at the repository that implements it, so the transformations between site source records and distributed files are traceable and, in principle, inspectable. Quality control is genuine — characterization reports fed back to sites and a clinical validation SOP for mappings. Labeling is honestly marked as not yet realized rather than claimed, and no annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols are recorded. The preprocessing and cleaning content is substantive enough to carry the sub-element; the forward-looking labeling entry is logged as a low-severity tense issue rather than credited as delivered.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Named software in processing roles, carried by preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, is_deidentified and external_resources: the 'OHNLP toolkit', which extracts and tokenizes the clinical notes that are the distributed note artifact; the 'chorus_waveform' conversion scripts, which convert waveform data for release into WFDB; 'chorus-mapping', holding the pooled tabular semantic mappings by which site data are standardized to OMOP; 'CTP-deid' and a 'privacy scan tool', which de-identify imaging and records before release; and 'CHoRUSReports', which generates the characterization reports driving site resubmission. A reader can tell what transformed the data being distributed. Each named tool is tied to the modality it acts on — OHNLP to notes, chorus_waveform to telemetry, chorus-mapping to OMOP structured data, CTP-deid to imaging — and each is locatable within the chorus-ai organization named in external_resources. Threshold satisfied on processing-role software, not on capture, hosting, packaging or validation tooling: the Azure deployment and dockerized container applications (hosting, role b), the OHDSI tool stack and Jupyter Notebooks used by trainees in the enclave (analysis by consumers), and chorus-extract-upload (site-side capture and transfer, role a) are present but were not relied on. No version numbers, commit pins or software DOIs are given for any tool, and the individual repository URLs are not listed — the pointer identifies the organization root only — which weakens reproducibility; the sub-element asks whether the tooling is disclosed, and it is, by name.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: the chorus-ai GitHub organization with 28 named repositories and its licensing note; https://chorus4ai.org/ with its documentation pages; www.bridge2ai.org/chorus; https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824; the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 informational webinar PDF. conforms_to: per-modality standards statement (OMOP CDM with extensions, DICOM, WFDB with extended PhysioNet metadata schema, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP). extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai, with the chorus-mapping contribution path and Standards / Data Acquisition discussion spaces. External standards and supporting resources are both well covered: the standards are named per modality, the implementing SOPs and code are pointed at, the funder record is linked, and a contribution route is documented for external collaborators to extend the semantic mappings. No imputation_protocols field, and the record does not state whether imputation was applied or deliberately avoided — a real gap for high-frequency flowsheet and waveform data where gaps are ubiquitous. The standards and resource evidence is strong enough to carry the sub-element; peer-reviewed publications describing the dataset are also absent from the resource list.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: four typed entries — coverage_limitation ('as of August 2025 imaging was limited to about 1,000 available images with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was still in process', scope_impact 'Analyses requiring imaging or EEG at scale are not yet supported by the released data'); integration_limitation (note text remains local, only tokens in the enclave); representativeness_limitation (14 of 20 centers contribute; achieved demographic, geographic and clinical distribution unreported); scope_limitation (ICU/PICU/NICU settings only). Limitations are categorized by type, described concretely, and at least one carries an explicit scope_impact telling a reuser which analyses are foreclosed. They cover the four dimensions that actually matter here — modality coverage, data locality, representativeness and clinical scope — and none is boilerplate. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere in the record rather than asserted in isolation: coverage by instances[2].missing_information, integration by confidential_elements and raw_data_sources, representativeness by the sampling_strategies caveat, scope by subpopulations. The representativeness entry is notably candid in conceding that the achieved distribution is unknown.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: No known_biases field. No future_use_impacts field. The nearest content is known_limitations[2] (representativeness_limitation, noting that the distribution achieved is not reported) and participant_privacy[0].notes ('Patient-focused efforts within the project determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'). No bias is identified, let alone categorized.
