The nearest content is instances, which describe modality-level units ('Nursing flowsheet entry (high-frequency documentation)', 'Medication administration record, time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration') with data_substrate and data_topic codes, but no field, column or concept-level metadata. No data dictionary, no variable identifiers, no value ranges or units. For a 1.6-billion-row multimodal release this is a substantial reuse barrier, only partly mitigated by the OMOP CDM's externally published table and field definitions, which the record does not link. The absence is consistent with the rest of the record, which documents at modality rather than variable granularity; no contradictory claim of variable-level documentation is made anywhere.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three categories with examples and usage_notes - 'Clinical AI/ML model development' (characterising acute and critical care illness, predicting complications and deterioration, measuring treatment response); 'External validation of clinical AI models' (evaluating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout, intended to aid marketplace adoption); 'Workforce training and AI literacy' (trainee research on the Collaborative Cloud, canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP workshops, clinical deep learning exercises). existing_uses records training activities, publications and site characterization reports. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses: absent. Intended uses are specific, categorised and paired with usage notes that convey the project's own framing of each use. The complete absence of prohibited or discouraged uses is notable for restricted critical-care data - no statement bars re-identification attempts, clinical deployment without validation, or redistribution - but the sub-element is satisfied by any of the three fields and the intended-use guidance is substantive. Intended uses align with purposes and tasks without contradiction, and the training-programme use is corroborated by third_party_sharing. Flagged as a warning rather than a failure: restrictive access terms imply constraints that are nowhere written as prohibited uses.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: two entries - 'The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing' and 'The consortium evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI'. human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance: 'The project establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape'. data_protection_impacts: absent. source_caveats: 'the bundle names no institutional review board, ethics committee or reviewing organization for the dataset' and 'does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the dataset'. What is documented is community engagement and legal-landscape analysis - project ethics activity, not review or oversight of this dataset. For a multi-site retrospective study of identifiable ICU records, no reviewing body, approval, reliance agreement or DPIA is named. A user cannot tell under what authority the data were assembled or shared. Fails the instrument's explicit check: involves_human_subjects is true, so this sub-element must be populated with oversight evidence and is not. The ethics focus groups are real content and are credited at Element 9 sub-element 5, where the question is ethical review documentation together with social impact analysis; they do not answer the oversight question asked here.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; unstructured EHR text is tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit rather than shared as free text; imaging de-identification was in process as of August 2025.' is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'Clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens placed in the shared enclave, so that identifiable narrative text is not distributed with the dataset.' source_caveats note that identifiers removed are not enumerated, no standard is named, and a privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid repository exist without a statement that either was applied. Scored 1 on the strength of two concrete, named, verifiable mechanisms - OHNLP tokenization of narrative text and site-local retention of note text so identifiable prose never enters the enclave - which are well above boilerplate and are architecturally specific. The generic clause about 'approaches that limit re-identification' would not have sufficed alone, and the gap for structured OMOP data is flagged as a medium-severity issue. Method appropriateness: tokenization plus local retention is the right control for the highest-risk modality and is consistent with distribution_formats, confidential_elements and known_limitations (full-text analyses impossible on shared data). Unresolved: no HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination claim, no identifier list, and imaging de-identification reported as incomplete at the snapshot date.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method: 'Tokenization of unstructured EHR text, de-identification of imaging, and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification.' participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: 'Local retention of clinical note text at contributing sites, with only tokens shared. Controlled access to all modalities within a cloud enclave.' participant_privacy.notes: patient-focused consortium work determines the ethical and legal approaches used to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health. No reidentification_risk assessment; data_protection_impacts absent. Protections and mitigations are documented as an architecture rather than an assertion: enclave-only analysis, controlled access across all nine modalities, narrative text that never leaves the site. That is actionable for a reuser assessing exposure. The explicit re-identification risk assessment the sub-element also asks for is missing, and for timestamped ICU data with waveforms that is a real gap, recorded as a warning. Consistent with confidential_elements, regulatory_restrictions and the enclave access model; no privacy claim here exceeds what is stated elsewhere. Failed sub-check: data_protection_impacts absent and reidentification_risk unassessed despite participant_privacy being populated.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent: absent from the record entirely. The nearest related content is direct_collection.is_direct: false, with collection_details stating data are obtained retrospectively from hospital clinical systems 'rather than collected directly from individuals for research purposes'. No waiver, no notice-of-privacy-practices basis, no opt-out mechanism, no withdrawal procedure is recorded. Nothing is documented. Retrospective EHR research commonly proceeds under an IRB waiver of consent, and that would be a legitimate answer - but the record does not say so, does not name who granted it, and does not describe any alternative basis. Combined with the missing IRB, a user cannot establish the consent footing of the data at all. Fails the instrument's explicit check: involves_human_subjects is true, so consent procedures are expected and none are described. This is the record's most consequential documentation gap and is recorded as a high-severity consistency issue.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true, with source_caveats: 'Inclusion of minors follows from the released dataset covering PICU and NICU admissions; the bundle describes no assent procedures, guardian consent procedures or special protections.' human_subject_research.special_populations notes PICU and NICU patients. participant_compensation: absent. The flag correctly identifies that minors and neonates are in the release, which is worth having, but the sub-element asks for protections and compensation and neither is documented. No assent or guardian-permission basis, no additional safeguards on paediatric subsets, no statement that compensation is inapplicable to retrospective collection. The identification alone leaves a reuser of paediatric ICU records without any protective framing. The true flag is internally consistent with the ICU/PICU/NICU cohort described in subpopulations and instances, so the record is accurate about who is present; it simply documents nothing about how they are protected. Recorded as a medium-severity consistency issue alongside the missing consent and IRB evidence.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Released admissions are identified by care setting as adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) admissions'; source_caveats: 'The bundle does not report the distribution of admissions across these settings.' description adds 14 contributing hospitals within a 20-institution collaboration. Three clinically distinct subpopulations are named explicitly and the subpopulation flag is set, so a reuser knows the release spans adult, paediatric and neonatal critical care - a consequential structural fact for any modelling task. Demographic composition (age, sex, race, ethnicity) and inclusion/exclusion criteria are not reported and the missing stratum distribution is honestly flagged, which keeps this at the lower end of a passing score. Consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations and at_risk_populations, both of which independently identify PICU/NICU patients. A 'demographics' modality is listed in instances while no demographic summary is given - a coverage rather than a correctness problem.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: 50,000 patient admissions (ICU/PICU/NICU) for the current release; 1,600,000,000 rows of OMOP-standardized EHR data; 7,642 admissions with radiology data. description adds 23 Tb of waveform data and the 100,000-admission anticipated final size. splits describes a sequestered holdout test set. Each contested figure carries a source_caveats entry naming the disagreeing source. Specific counts at several granularities - admissions, rows, modality-specific admission counts, storage volume - with the release/target distinction made explicit. The per-instance source_caveats make the provenance of every contested number auditable rather than presenting a single unsourced figure. Two disagreements are retained rather than reconciled (50,000 vs >45,000 admissions; 7,642 admissions with radiology vs ~1,000 images), and the 1.6 billion row integer is disclosed as the record's own expansion of a rounded source figure. These are recorded as content_accuracy issues; the disclosure is correct practice and does not undermine the sub-element.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: absent. is_tabular: absent. splits: one entry stating the award abstract's intention to 'provision a holdout test set, accessible for model external validation', with source_caveats: 'Stated as a project intention in the 2022 award abstract; the bundle does not state the size, composition or availability of the holdout set.' subpopulations carries subpopulation_elements_present: true. The sub-element's primary requirement - variable or column descriptions and a data dictionary - is entirely absent, and no tabular flag is set even though the OMOP component is explicitly relational. The split is documented only as a four-year-old stated intention with no size, composition or availability, so it does not identify the role of any actual subset. Only the subpopulation flag is genuinely present, which is not enough to carry the sub-element. Internally consistent: nothing elsewhere in the record claims variable-level documentation exists. The record accurately marks the holdout as aspirational rather than presenting it as a released split, which is the correct representation of a weak fact.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry data_topic codes across eleven entries (B2AI_TOPIC:4 critical care procedures/flowsheets, :6 demographics, :7 diagnoses, :8 medication administration, :9 EHR, :15 imaging, :32 clinical text, :37 waveform) and data_substrate codes (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :37, :43, :49), with each instance describing its clinical content. keywords add acute illness, ICU, EEG, medical imaging and social determinants of health. other_tasks and sensitive_elements identify SDOH and contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital. Topic coverage is both enumerated in prose and coded against an ontology, so it is machine-actionable as well as readable. Specific disease conditions or phenotype distributions are not enumerated, which limits condition-level discovery, but the topics and clinical content areas represented are clearly conveyed. Topic and substrate codes are well-formed CURIEs and each is semantically plausible for the instance it annotates (waveform substrate on telemetry and EEG instances, text substrate on clinical notes, imaging substrate on radiology). No mis-assigned code detected.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: missing_data_documentation.missing_data_patterns: 'Modality coverage was uneven at the August 2025 snapshot: OMOP data and telemetry were in the enclave, clinical notes were stored locally with only tokens shared, roughly 1,000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was still in process. Published metadata existed for demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses and waveform telemetry, while metadata for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was marked planned.' missing_data_causes names the in-progress de-identification, extraction and metadata workflows. sampling_strategies describes sampling for comprehensive conditions and a balanced, diverse cohort via federated access, with a caveat that the sampling frame is not described operationally. anomalies: absent. Missing-data documentation is dated, modality-specific and causally explained, which is exactly what a reuser needs to decide whether a given analysis is feasible on the current release. Sampling strategy is thinner and honestly caveated, and the anomalies field is empty; the missing-data content alone carries the sub-element. Coverage statements agree with distribution_formats notes, known_limitations and instances across every modality - the same August 2025 snapshot is reported consistently in four places. No contradiction between the claimed and the caveated coverage.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: absent. The only release-state signal is status: 'Partially released under controlled access; acquisition, de-identification and curation continuing under NIH award OT2OD032701'. No version number, tag or release date is assigned to the data a user would receive today. Given that the record itself distinguishes a current release (50,000 admissions) from an anticipated final dataset (100,000), the absence of a version label makes it impossible to cite what was analysed. Consistent with updates.source_caveats, which state that no versioning policy is documented. An acknowledged absence, not a contradiction.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access: absent. Nothing in data_governance.access_review_process, updates or external_resources describes how to obtain or pin a prior state of the data; the chorus-ai package status page is described as tracking software versions and maintainers, not dataset releases. No mechanism for retrieving an earlier snapshot is documented, which matters more than usual here because the enclave contents are actively growing - two analyses run months apart would silently use different data with no way to reference the difference. No contradictory claim: the record nowhere asserts that versioned access exists. Software package versioning in the GitHub organisation is correctly not conflated with dataset versioning.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: absent. updates.update_details is entirely forward-looking ('The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions... de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process'). No changelog, no record of what changed between past states, no corrections issued. Nothing documents what has already changed or been corrected. The forward-looking plan in updates is credited at sub-element 4, where a maintenance plan is what the rubric asks for; it does not answer the retrospective change-and-errata question posed here. Consistent with the absence of version and version_access - the record has no release history to attach errata to, which is a coherent if unsatisfactory state.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.update_details: 'The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process, and metadata publication for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was planned.' status records the award project period ending 2026-11-30. extension_mechanism describes regular site status updates feeding the Standards and Data Acquisition projects. updates.source_caveats: no update frequency or versioning policy is stated. Scored 1 on the maintenance-plan alternative the sub-element explicitly admits: a reuser learns the growth target, which specific modalities are pending, what stage each is at, the snapshot date, and the funded horizon within which the work will complete. No calendar schedule or frequency is given, which keeps this at the lower end of a passing score. The plan is consistent with missing_data_documentation and known_limitations, which report the same pending modalities and the same August 2025 snapshot. Temporal ordering is coherent: award start 2022-09-01, snapshot August 2025, webinar September 2025, award end 2026-11-30.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: five entries, each with source_description, source_type and raw_data_format - structured EHR systems at 14 hospitals (site-native extracts mapped to OMOP); unstructured clinical notes (free text, tokenized with OHNLP, with access_details recording site-local retention); hospital PACS (DICOM); bedside physiologic monitors and gateway/middleware (telemetry converted to WFDB); hospital EEG databases (EDF+ and Persyst). acquisition_methods describes the extract-standardize-tokenize-store-label-deliver chain into the shared enclave. was_derived_from: absent. Provenance back to the originating hospital systems is documented per modality, naming the upstream system type, its native format and the transformation applied. This is the substance the sub-element seeks; the absence of a formal was_derived_from link is a modelling omission rather than an information gap. Every raw source maps coherently onto a distribution format and a preprocessing strategy, so the provenance chain is traceable end to end without gaps or orphan modalities. Source types are correctly distinguished (clinical imaging archive, monitoring device stream, neurophysiology database).

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: five entries including generating data for ML/AI characterising acute and critical care illness, predicting complications and measuring treatment response; developing a publicly available AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring methods promote privacy, accountability and clinical benefit; provisioning a holdout test set for external validation; creating ethically sourced datasets and best practices as one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects. addressing_gaps: four entries naming the specific deficits - lack of AI/ML infrastructure in critical care, absence of a diverse high-resolution ethically sourced AI-ready dataset, unharmonized multimodal data across centres, and scarce sequestered holdout data. Motivation is stated as a scientific rationale tied to identified gaps, not as a generic mission statement. The pairing of purposes with addressing_gaps lets a reader see both what the dataset is for and what was missing without it. Purposes align with funding goals (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI's remit to produce ethically sourced AI-ready datasets), with tasks, and with intended_uses. No purpose is asserted that the modality inventory could not support.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: five entries - characterizing acute and critical care illness; predicting complications and clinical deterioration; measuring treatment response; external validation of ML models against a sequestered holdout; labeling data with prediction targets using a visualization and annotation environment. other_tasks adds analyses incorporating social determinants of health. Concrete, distinguishable analytic objectives rather than restatements of the purpose. Each maps onto a recognisable clinical ML task family and, with the exception of the annotation environment, onto data that the modality inventory actually contains. Tasks are consistent with instances (timestamped medications and flowsheets support deterioration prediction; waveforms and EEG support high-resolution physiologic modelling). The labeling task is correctly flagged elsewhere as future-tense project intention rather than a released capability.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program', with grant notes recording the Other Transaction award, the award amount (5,880,300 US dollars for fiscal year 2022), the project period (2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the awardee organization (Massachusetts General Hospital); funder notes reproduce the NIH disclaimer that site content is the authors' responsibility. The funding agency, the specific programme and the mechanism are all identified, with award amount, period and awardee organisation - well beyond naming a sponsor. The OT2 activity code in the grant number is consistent with the stated Common Fund Other Transaction mechanism, and the awardee organization matches the PI's affiliation and the accountable_organization in data_governance. No funder/mechanism mismatch.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants.grant_number: OT2OD032701; notes add the full funded-application project number 1OT2OD032701-01 and NIH application ID 10472824. The award is also cited in description and status. The core project number, the application-specific project number and the internal application ID are all supplied, which is enough to locate the award in NIH RePORTER unambiguously. NIH pattern check passes: OT2 (activity code) + OD (Office of the Director, the correct issuing component for Common Fund awards) + 032701 (six-digit serial), with the 1...-01 prefix/suffix form correctly applied to the funded application. Agency and pattern agree.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: six named individuals with identifiers and affiliations - Eric S. Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac, Yulia Strekalova and Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University) - each with notes stating the basis for the attribution. created_by: CHoRUS Consortium. funders.notes carry the NIH acknowledgement disclaimer. source_caveats explains that only Rosenthal is independently attested as PI and that principal_investigator is the only person-valued field the Creator class declares. Named creators with institutional affiliations and an explicit, auditable account of how each attribution was derived. The caveat about role over-assignment is a genuine modelling limitation, disclosed rather than hidden. The PI attribution for Rosenthal is corroborated by the award record and by MGH's role as awardee organization and host of the program manager. The record correctly avoids asserting individual roles for the other five leaders beyond what the source supports.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: six entries - extraction of structured EHR at contributing sites and standardization to OMOP supported by the OHDSI tool stack; extraction and tokenization of notes with the OHNLP toolkit with text remaining on site; retrieval of imaging from hospital PACS in DICOM; capture of waveform telemetry from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware, converted to WFDB using the chorus_waveform scripts; extraction of EEG as EDF+ and Persyst; site-side tooling (chorus-extract-upload, chorus-container-apps on Azure) for building and delivering submissions. Supported by collection_timeframes, data_collectors (14 acquisition centres plus consortium sub-teams, with the Chorus_SOP workflow) and direct_collection. Each modality's collection path is described from the originating hospital system through to enclave delivery, with the specific tooling named at each step and the contributing roles identified. A site engineer could follow this narrative to understand what is expected of them; the Chorus_SOP reference points at the operational detail. Settings and timeframe are partially characterised: 14 hospitals, retrospective collection, August 2025 snapshot, award period. The record correctly flags that the calendar range of the clinical encounters themselves is not stated - a real gap, honestly disclosed.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: 'Retrospective collection: clinical data generated during routine care are extracted at contributing hospitals, standardized, tokenized, stored, visualized and labeled through a multi-center network, then delivered as a CHoRUS data extract to the shared cloud enclave.' raw_data_sources names the acquisition instruments and systems per modality: hospital EHR systems, PACS, bedside physiologic monitors and their gateway/middleware, hospital EEG databases. The acquisition chain is stated end to end and the capture devices and source systems are identified per modality. Device makes, models and sampling rates are not given, which limits replication of the waveform and EEG components specifically, but the instruments and systems are named. Acquisition methods are consistent with direct_collection.is_direct=false and with the retrospective framing throughout; no claim of prospective or research-purpose collection appears anywhere to contradict this.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: five entries - OMOP standardization using validated semantic mappings with pooled tabular mappings in chorus-mapping; OHNLP extraction and tokenization of unstructured text; transformation limiting re-identification including imaging de-identification; conversion of telemetry to WFDB using the waveform conversion scripts; geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss using UF-Geocoding. cleaning_strategies: characterization reports produced and returned to sites, with site status tracking to identify and resolve blocking issues. labeling_strategies: a visualization and annotation environment for prediction targets, with data_annotation_protocol referencing clinical collaborator contribution under a clinical validation SOP, and source_caveats marking the environment as future-tense. machine_annotation_tools: OHNLP toolkit, with tool_descriptions. annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols: absent. Preprocessing is documented step by step with the responsible repository named for each transformation, and cleaning is described as a concrete feedback loop rather than an assertion of quality. Labeling is honestly marked as aspirational, and annotation quality analyses are absent - but the sub-element spans several fields and the preprocessing and cleaning content is specific and substantial. Each preprocessing step maps to a declared distribution format (OMOP tables, OHNLP tokens, WFDB) so the pipeline and the outputs are mutually consistent. The record correctly declines to claim released labels, matching the absence of labeled-data claims elsewhere.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Processing-role software named by name: the OHNLP toolkit (machine_annotation_tools.tools and preprocessing_strategies - extracts and tokenizes clinical notes, and the tokens are what the enclave distributes); the OHDSI tool stack (collection_mechanisms - supports standardization of structured EHR to OMOP); chorus-mapping (preprocessing_strategies and external_resources - pooled tabular mappings that effect the OMOP transformation); the chorus_waveform conversion scripts (preprocessing_strategies and collection_mechanisms - convert bedside telemetry into the distributed WFDB form); DeGauss via the UF-Geocoding code (preprocessing_strategies - geocodes OMOP Location entities in the released data). Scored 1: a reader can tell what software produced and transformed the distributed data, at the level of named tools mapped to specific transformation steps. Versions, software DOIs and per-tool repository URLs are not given, which is what 'Look for' additionally asks and what would strengthen this, but the tooling is disclosed rather than left unstated. Role check applied per #1059/#1082. Counted: OHNLP, OHDSI, chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform scripts, DeGauss/UF-Geocoding - all transform data that is in the release. Excluded as not answering the question: chorus-extract-upload (packaging and delivery, role c), chorus-container-apps on Azure (hosting and serving, role b), CHoRUSReports (characterization and quality assessment, role d), and privacy_scan_tool/CTP-deid, which the record explicitly states are not asserted to have been applied to the released data. The qualifying evidence stands on the processing-role tools alone.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: nine entries covering the project website's documentation pages, the chorus-ai GitHub organization (28 repositories), Chorus_SOP with an interactive step-by-step workflow diagram, chorus-mapping with its clinical validation SOP, chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources, chorus-extract-upload and chorus-container-apps, privacy_scan_tool/CTP-deid/UF-Geocoding, CHoRUSReports, and the Bridge2AI project page plus the AIM-AHEAD training call. conforms_to documents the standards per modality. imputation_protocols: absent, with no statement that imputation was not used. External documentation is abundant and each resource is described by what it contains, so a user can choose which to consult. Standards conformance is documented in detail. The missing imputation protocol - not even a statement that no imputation was performed on a dataset with documented coverage gaps - is the one shortfall, and the sub-element's other two components carry it. Resource names referenced in preprocessing, collection and annotation fields all reappear in external_resources with consistent descriptions, so the tooling narrative is corroborated rather than asserted. URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: five typed entries - two coverage_limitation (partial imaging with ~1,000 images and de-identification in process; EEG extraction still in process); integration_limitation (notes held locally so analyses requiring full text cannot be performed on shared data); representativeness_limitation (14 hospitals within a 20-centre collaboration, acute and critical care admissions only, not a general hospital or population sample); scope_limitation (released 50,000 admissions against the 100,000 target, incomplete modality metadata) with a scope_impact noting analyses may not generalize to the completed dataset and a source_caveat identifying the comparison as the record's own juxtaposition. Limitations are typed, specific, consequence-bearing and traceable to the evidence behind them. Each tells a reuser something that would change an analysis decision rather than restating a generic caveat, and the record marks which inference is its own. Every limitation is corroborated by another field - coverage by missing_data_documentation, integration by is_deidentified and participant_privacy, scope by instances. No limitation is asserted without support and none contradicts a claim made elsewhere.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: absent from the record entirely; no BiasTypeEnum categorization appears anywhere. The only bias mention is inside future_use_impacts: 'patient-focused work determining the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. known_limitations carries a representativeness_limitation, but as a limitation entry rather than a categorized bias. No bias is identified, categorized or assessed. For a 14-hospital academic critical-care cohort this is a material omission: selection into academic ICUs, differential documentation intensity across sites, device availability driving waveform coverage, and demographic skew are all foreseeable and none is named. A single clause about managing bias as a project activity is not a bias assessment. Fails on content rather than contradiction. The representativeness limitation shows the record is aware of generalizability constraints, which makes the absence of any structured bias categorization more conspicuous, not less.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: absent. cleaning_strategies mentions site status tracking to 'identify and resolve blocking issues in the creation and curation of a site's data extract', which describes a process rather than any documented anomaly. No outliers, implausible values, site-to-site inconsistencies, missing-timestamp problems or measurement artefacts are reported for the released data. Nothing is documented about the quality of the data itself. Missing-data coverage is documented and is credited at Element 5 sub-element 5; that answers what is absent, not what is present but wrong. For multi-site EHR and waveform data, the absence of any anomaly reporting leaves a reuser unable to anticipate cleaning burden. The characterization reports returned to sites (CHoRUSReports) imply that quality findings exist and are circulated internally, but no finding is surfaced in the datasheet. Recorded as an evidence gap rather than an inconsistency.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: two entries - hospital records of critically ill patients including demographics, diagnoses, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, imaging, physiologic waveforms, EEG and tokenized clinical notes; and social determinants of health plus contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital. confidential_elements: two entries - clinical note text confidential to the contributing site, and every documented modality marked controlled with the dataset not openly downloadable. content_warnings: absent. Sensitivity is described at the level of specific elements rather than a blanket label, and the SDOH/geographic entry correctly identifies a re-identification vector that is easy to overlook. The distinction drawn between sensitive and confidential elements is meaningful and well applied. Consistent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', with the enclave access model and with is_deidentified. The identification of geographic distance as sensitive is semantically coherent with the DeGauss geocoding step in preprocessing_strategies - the record recognises the risk that its own processing introduces.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: future_use_impacts: three entries - the sequestered holdout intended to support external validation and thereby aid marketplace adoption of AI models in acute and critical care; privacy, accountability and clinical benefit framed as conditions on future use because the data derive from critically ill patients, with patient-focused work determining the approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for SDOH; and community perspectives gathered through ethics focus groups determining what data is appropriate for public sharing, so the shareable scope of future releases depends on those findings. ethical_reviews: community-facing ethics focus groups and consortium evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy. Downstream social impact is analysed substantively: anticipated benefits, the conditions the project places on future use, and an explicit mechanism (community findings) by which impact considerations feed back into what gets released. That last point is a genuine mitigation pathway rather than an aspiration. Scored 1 here while Element 4 sub-element 1 scored 0, and the two are not in tension: this sub-element asks for ethical review documentation together with social impact analysis, and the community ethics engagement plus three-part impact analysis answer it; Element 4 sub-element 1 asks for institutional oversight of a human-subjects dataset - an IRB, an approval, a DPIA - which the same content does not supply.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: absent. The hosting arrangement is described only in prose: data sit in a controlled 'cloud enclave', and trainees work with them 'on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud', with chorus-container-apps 'deployed to support CHoRUS services on Azure'. No repository - PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo, FAIRhub or an institutional archive - is named as publisher. No publisher is recorded and the dataset is not deposited in a recognised data repository; it is held in a project-operated enclave. The enclave is a real and named access environment, but it is infrastructure rather than a publishing platform, and without a publisher field the dataset has no repository identity for cross-platform discovery. Internally consistent with the absence of download_url and a DOI, and with the controlled-access model. This is a coherent access architecture that nonetheless leaves the dataset outside the repository ecosystem the sub-element measures.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: absent. doi: absent. No recommended citation string, citation instructions, or cross-referenceable identifier appears anywhere; existing_uses notes that 'the datasets are being used for training activities and publications' without supplying the citation those publications would use. A dataset already being cited in publications provides no canonical way to cite it. With no DOI and no version identifier either, a paper can reference only the project homepage, which will not resolve to the data actually analysed. Consistent with the Element 1 finding that id duplicates page and no persistent identifier exists. Scored 0, not excluded: the record's own existing_uses confirms citation need is live.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model with published OMOP-schema metadata and extensions for nursing flowsheets; OHNLP open-source schema for tokenized notes; DICOM for imaging; WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema for telemetry; EDF+ and Persyst for EEG. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema. collection_mechanisms name the OHDSI tool stack, tying the dataset to the OHDSI community. Conformance to recognised community standards is documented per modality and the standards named are the ones their communities actually use, which is what makes the data poolable with other OMOP, PhysioNet and DICOM resources. Extensions are declared rather than glossed over. Standards usage is technically correct throughout and consistent with distribution_formats and preprocessing_strategies. The declared OMOP extensions for nursing flowsheets are an honest signal that pooling will require handling non-core tables.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/. external_resources: the project website's pages on team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset and learning resources; the chorus-ai GitHub organization; Chorus_SOP's documentation site with an interactive workflow diagram; the chorus-developer repository compiling contributor and user documentation; the Bridge2AI project page; and the AIM-AHEAD training call. intended_uses cite canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP workshops and clinical deep learning exercises; third_party_sharing describes the Cohort 2 training programme (17 November 2025 to 31 July 2026, up to 30 trainees) and the record draws on a September 2025 informational webinar. Documentation and outreach are unusually well developed: SOPs with a workflow diagram, developer documentation, teaching notebooks, workshops, webinars and a structured training programme with dates and capacity. A newcomer has several genuine entry points. Outreach claims are corroborated across third_party_sharing, intended_uses, external_resources and extension_mechanism, with consistent dates and programme names. URLs are structurally valid.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: absent. source_caveats: 'The bundle states that CHoRUS is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and collaborates with the other three, but names no sibling dataset, so no dataset relationships are recorded.' No typed relationship (supplements, derives from, is version of) appears anywhere. No dataset-to-dataset link of any kind, typed or untyped. The three sibling Bridge2AI data generation datasets are acknowledged to exist and are not identified, so the record offers no path into the wider Bridge2AI data ecosystem it belongs to. A disclosed non-assertion rather than an error: the record declines to name relationships its sources did not support. Scored 0 on content, with the transparency noted.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the dataset id, the DOI, and the latest-version pointer, and subset ids are minted as fragments beneath it. Matches 10.XXXX/... ; prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse registrant, plausible for a dataset whose publisher is ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and whose access URL is dataverse.lib.virginia.edu. Valid.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of ~1,900 characters naming the modalities (Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence), the cell lines and treatment conditions, the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging, the three-pillar/six-module organization, and the nine collaborating institutions Far beyond the 200-character threshold and substantively informative: a reader learns which modalities cover which cell lines and conditions before opening a file. Description content matches the claimed dataset type (multi-modal proteomics/imaging/perturbation) and matches file_collections one-for-one. Consistent.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: 27 terms including AI, AP-MS, Bridge2AI, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, perturb-seq, SEC-MS, paclitaxel, vorinostat, subcellular imaging Well above the five-keyword threshold and spans domain, method, cell line, reagent and program dimensions, including both spelled-out and abbreviated forms. Every keyword is corroborated by content elsewhere in the record; no orphan or aspirational tags. Program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is inferred from quoted keyword values only.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections lists 10 named archives with paths, sizes and MD5 checksums; total_file_count: 10 Both a project-level landing page and a repository record are given, and the resource structure is enumerated down to per-file checksums. Both URLs are well formed with plausible domains; total_file_count (10) equals the number of file_collections entries. Consistent.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: six typed relationships — four is_new_version_of (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5), one is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), one is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734); subsets: seven subset ids beneath the dataset DOI The release lineage is fully navigable and each relationship carries a resolvable target DOI and a human-readable name; seven internal subsets give the within-dataset hierarchy. All target DOIs are well formed; the 10.1101 prefix correctly denotes bioRxiv preprints for the two literature relationships. parent_datasets is unused, but the is_new_version_of chain conveys the same lineage. Consistent.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 statement with attribution, non-commercial and share-alike conditions; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; contact_person: Trey Ideker. ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Copyright is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; spatial proteomics raw image data is copyright the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University. Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation...' Actionable rather than boilerplate: it names the license, the per-package copyright holders, the excluded use, and a person to contact for a commercial licence. License, data_use_permission enum, prohibited_uses and ip_restrictions all state the same non-commercial restriction without contradiction. Consistent.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No'; hipaa_compliant: not_applicable; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486); data_governance.committee_name: CM4AI Data Access Committee, committee_contact and access_review_process; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false with reasoning The regulatory determinations are negative but reasoned, and the record supplies both a named governance committee and a named contact with an institutional email — the governance-contact scope of this sub-element is met. hipaa_compliant: not_applicable is semantically correct for non-clinical cell-line proteomics; a HIPAA-compliant claim would have been the implausible answer here. No confidentiality_level enum value is set, which is the one gap. Consistent.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C with notes 'Individual files below the download size limit may be downloaded directly; the Data Access API is available for programmatic access' A resolvable repository link plus explicit instructions for both interactive and programmatic retrieval, including the size-limit caveat that matters for the 3.8-4.6 GB image archives. The dedicated `download_url` slot is empty and the link lives in distribution_formats.access_urls; the sub-element asks for a direct link or platform access instructions and both are present, so the point is earned, with the slot placement recorded as a low-severity correctness issue.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: [format: 'ZIP Archive', media_type: application/zip], [format: 'RO-Crate']; file_collections: 10 entries each with compression: zip, a path, a size and an MD5; conforms_to: RO-Crate Container format, MIME type, compression and per-file checksums are all given, which is enough to retrieve and verify the distribution. media_type application/zip is the correct MIME type for the stated format. Only the container is described — the formats of the files inside the archives are nowhere stated — which is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue and constrains Element 3 rather than this retrieval-focused sub-element.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: 6 typed entries; external_resources: 11 entries including MassIVE deposits for iPSC and cancer-cell mass spectrometry, AP-MS deposits, SRA via NCBI BioProject, Figshare CRISPRi atlas, https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, http://integrativemodeling.org Unusually thorough: raw deposits, code, documentation and modelling software are all linked, and embargo status is attached to the one resource that is restricted. All URLs are well formed with plausible domains; archival: true flags distinguish permanent deposits from project pages. The embargo note on the Perturb-seq resource matches the integration_limitation in known_limitations. Consistent.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material, provided appropriate credit is given, a link to the license is provided, changes are indicated, the material is not used for commercial purposes, and contributions are distributed under the same license' A named, standard, machine-recognisable license whose permissions and conditions are spelled out, plus a stated route to commercial licensing. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is a real Creative Commons identifier and the paraphrase of its terms is accurate. Non-commercial and share-alike conditions limit but do not block reuse. Valid.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: format 'ZIP Archive' with media_type application/zip; format 'RO-Crate' with notes 'CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE] The distribution is packaged in an open, community-standard research-object format (RO-Crate, a JSON-LD profile) inside plain ZIP with a declared MIME type, so a consumer can unpack and interpret the package structure by standard tooling. Partial: the packaging layer is standardised and correctly identified, but no inner file format and no character encoding are recorded anywhere in the record (raw_data_format says only 'Confocal microscopy image with four color channels'). Scored 1 on the strength of the RO-Crate/MIME declarations, with the missing inner formats raised as a low-severity completeness issue.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology-coded slots data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 / B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63 and data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15 / :26 / :12 Conformance is asserted at three levels — packaging standard, metadata schema with a resolvable w3id URI, and class — and content-level annotation uses program ontology CURIEs rather than free text. The w3id URI is well formed and the CURIE prefixes are used consistently. Cell-map annotation is separately stated to align to Gene Ontology and Reactome. Valid.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No `variables` slot anywhere in the record. The nearest content is instances[].notes (image channel composition, gene counts) and file_collections[].description. A reuser cannot learn the columns, units or identifiers of the SEC-MS elution tables, the AP-MS interaction records, or the Perturb-seq atlas without downloading and inspecting the archives. This is the record's largest interoperability gap. Absent field; not excusable by is_tabular: false, since the SEC-MS, AP-MS and Perturb-seq archives plainly contain tabular result files. Fails.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: 5 categories (AI-ready research data, AI model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation and disease-context analysis, bioinformatics analysis of component datasets); prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making without regulatory oversight, and commercial use; discouraged_uses: use without domain expertise, use as a complete cell-map resource All three registers are populated with reasons rather than labels, and the guidance is candid about what this interim release is not good for. The prohibition on commercial use matches the CC BY-NC-SA license and ip_restrictions; the discouragement against treating this as a complete cell-map resource matches the scope_limitation in known_limitations. Consistent.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: two entries — 'Ethical review for the CM4AI project is led by the Ethics Module, which developed a plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets, balancing openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property...' (contact Vardit Ravitsky, ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and a second review contact (Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon, Simon Fraser University). data_governance: CM4AI Data Access Committee with committee_contact, access_review_process and stewardship_roles. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with reasoning on ethically sourced lines (ATCC; HipSci MTA). Oversight is described as a standing function with named, contactable people and a stated remit (licensing, dissemination, data-access supervision), not as a one-line assertion. Appropriate to a dataset with governance but no participants. Consistency check: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false, so no IRB protocol number is expected and none is demanded. data_protection_impacts is absent, which is defensible where no personal data are processed. The ethics-review contacts named here also satisfy Element 9 sub-element 5. Consistent.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are distinctive within Bridge2AI in that they are non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' Corroborated by direct_collection: 'commercially available, de-identified human cell lines: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), available from ATCC, and KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3), available from the HipSci resource.' The record states the deidentification status, the basis for it (tissue-culture material with no linkage to a subject under current knowledge), the sourcing of both lines, and the residual-knowledge caveat. For immortalized and donor-derived lines that is the semantically appropriate answer. Method appropriateness: naming HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination or k-anonymity would be semantically wrong here, since no record-level suppression was performed — the material arrives deidentified from ATCC and HipSci. Scored 1 on that basis; the failure to cite the providers' deidentification/consent basis is raised as a medium-severity consistency issue rather than treated as absence.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy absent; no reidentification_risk assessment. The nearest statement, sensitive_elements: 'CM4AI data are non-clinical, derived from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject', concerns material rather than participants. Excluded from the denominator: there are no participants whose privacy this sub-element could assess, so scoring 0 would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than its documentation.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent absent. Upstream donor consent is referenced only indirectly, via the HipSci MTA note in human_subject_research.notes. Excluded from the denominator: no participants were enrolled by this dataset's producers, so there is no consent process of theirs to document. (Documenting the upstream donor-consent basis of the two cell lines would nonetheless strengthen the deidentification claim, and is recommended under sub-element 2.)

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation both absent. sampling_strategies.source_data records donor attributes of the source lines ('a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma'; 'a healthy male Northern European donor') as provenance, not as a participant population. Excluded from the denominator: with no enrolled participants there is no at-risk population to protect and no compensation to report.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present: true, identification by cell type and treatment condition (MDA-MB-468 untreated / paclitaxel / vorinostat; KOLF2.1J undifferentiated, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte), with a distribution statement mapping each modality onto the conditions it covers; subsets: seven entries each with an id, name, description and is_subpopulation: true The 'cohort' here is a matrix of cell lines by treatment and differentiation state, and it is described exhaustively and at the right granularity, including which assay covers which cell. The subsets enumeration matches the subpopulations.distribution prose and matches the file_collections: AP-MS archives exist only for the two treated MDA-MB-468 conditions, exactly as stated. Consistent.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: '464 proteins of interest imaged per treatment condition in MDA-MB-468 cells'; 'transcriptional and fitness phenotypes associated with 11,739 targeted genes'; sampling_strategies: '100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes'; total_file_count: 10; file_collections carry per-archive sizes (3.8 GB, 4.6 GB, 4.2 GB, 113.3 KB ...) Specific, modality-appropriate counts rather than a single headline number, and the record is explicit about the count it cannot give ('The bundle states the number of targeted genes; it does not state the number of profiled cells'). The 464 figure is used identically in instances, subpopulations.distribution and three file_collections descriptions, and the record reconciles it against a conflicting 563 in an older release page. Project-level aggregates are deliberately kept out of the slot values. Consistent.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: is_tabular: false; subsets: seven entries with is_subpopulation: true; instances[].notes describing the four-channel image structure ('protein of interest (green), nucleus stained with DAPI (blue), endoplasmic reticulum stained with a calreticulin antibody (yellow), and microtubules stained with a tubulin antibody (red)') Two of the composite's signals are populated and informative — the tabular flag and seven flagged subpopulation subsets — and image channel semantics are documented, so the structural shape of the release is legible. Partial: `variables` is absent (scored 0 at Element 3 sub-element 4) and no is_data_split flag appears, which is semantically correct since the release defines no train/test partition. is_tabular: false is flagged in source_caveats as inferred rather than stated, a minor provenance weakness. Scored 1 on the populated signals; the missing data dictionary is penalised once, at Element 3.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances: three instance_type entries (immunofluorescence confocal microscopy image; protein-protein interaction measurement; single-cell CRISPRi perturbation transcriptional profile) with data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:15, :26, :12 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, :63; conditions include triple-negative breast cancer, paclitaxel and vorinostat exposure, iPSC differentiation to NPC, neuron and cardiomyocyte Topics are given as ontology CURIEs and as readable prose, and the disease relevance (cancer, neuropsychiatric, cardiac) is tied back to the selection rationale. The topics match the modalities in the description and the assays in acquisition_methods; the CURIE prefixes are used consistently across instances. Consistent.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: sampling_strategies: two entries — is_sample: true, is_random: false, is_representative: false with why_not_representative ('derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'), the targeted-selection strategy, and source_data describing both lines' origins; second entry describing protein-level targeting and the 11,739-gene CRISPRi screen. acquisition_methods records antibody quality scoring 'according to a standard Human Protein Atlas protocol' with was_validated_verified: true. The sampling account is unusually complete — it states the sampling frame, denies randomness and representativeness, and explains why — and antibody validation is a genuine quality control for the imaging modality. Partial: `anomalies` and `missing_data_documentation` are both absent, and cleaning_strategies reports only that QC was 'ongoing at the time of the CM4AI preprint'. Scored 1 on the substantive sampling_strategies content, with the missing anomaly and missing-data documentation raised as a low-severity completeness issue and penalised at Element 9 sub-element 3.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; issued: 2026-06-17 A version number is present, well formed, and paired with a release status and publication date. Consistency failure flagged: version_access lists the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases at version '2.1', so this later release carries a lower number, and the citation string ends 'V2'. The number is present and parseable, so the point stands, but the sequence is contradictory (medium-severity issue).

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available: 'The June 2026 Data Release is at version 2.0. Prior CM4AI releases include the May 2024 Data Release, the March 2025 Data Release (Beta) at version 1.4, the June 2025 Data Release (Beta) at version 2.1, and the October 2025 Data Release (Beta) at version 2.1. Version history is maintained in the University of Virginia Dataverse.'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C States both where version history lives (UVA Dataverse) and how to reach the current version (DOI), and enumerates the prior releases; the related_datasets is_new_version_of chain supplies each prior DOI. The four prior releases named here correspond one-to-one with the four is_new_version_of relationships in related_datasets. Consistent apart from the version-number ordering noted above.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: absent. updates.update_details describes cadence and scope of future updates ('regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis') but states no change relative to the October 2025 release. No release-note field carries per-release changes. A reader cannot learn what this release adds, removes or corrects relative to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM without diffing two Dataverse records. The description enumerates current contents but never frames them as changes, and no corrections are recorded. Assessed against the dedicated update_details field, updates.description and notes, as the release-note concept requires actual release or derivation information; the cadence statement is not change documentation. Fails.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: quarterly; updates.update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis. CM4AI releases data quarterly, ensuring continuous updates to the cell maps and input data streams.'; retention_limit.retention_details: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds.' Frequency, end date and post-project preservation commitment are all stated, which is what a reuser needs to plan around the schedule. The quarterly cadence is corroborated by the observed release dates (March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, June 2026 — with one gap), and the embargo-lift expectation in known_limitations is consistent with continued augmentation. Consistent.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: two entries naming the Krogan Laboratory and Lundberg Laboratory deposition archives as the sources processed by the MuSIC pipeline, one with raw_data_format; raw_sources: four entries (MassIVE deposits for iPSC and cancer-cell mass spectrometry, SRA via NCBI BioProject, Figshare CRISPRi atlas); description: output data 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata ... in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; related_datasets: four is_new_version_of links to predecessor releases Provenance is traceable in both directions — upstream to the generating laboratories and public raw deposits, and backwards through the release lineage — and machine-readable provenance graphs ship with the data. was_derived_from is unused, but the derivation is expressed through raw_data_sources, raw_sources and the is_new_version_of chain, which the sub-element's evidence list accepts as alternative representations. Consistent.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four responses, including 'To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders...' and 'To stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems ... which are not black boxes'; addressing_gaps: three responses naming the black-box problem, the uncharted state of cell structure, and workforce needs Motivation is stated as a scientific argument with the gap it addresses, not as a mission-statement platitude. The purposes align with the funding goals of the named Bridge2AI Functional Genomics award and with the tasks and intended_uses. Consistent.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: four responses — construction of hierarchical cell maps as directed acyclic graphs; interpretable genotype-phenotype learning including variant interpretation; development of visible neural networks; integrative structure modeling of protein communities using the Integrative Modeling Platform; other_tasks adds structure modelling detail and training/workforce activity Concrete and technically specific, each naming the representation or method involved rather than a research theme. The tasks match the tools documented (HiDeF for the DAG, IMP for structure modelling) and the existing_uses examples. Consistent.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: three entries — National Institutes of Health (Bridge2AI: Cell Maps for AI Data Generation Project), National Institutes of Health (Bridge2AI Bridge Center), and University of Virginia (Frederick Thomas Fund) Both the primary data-generation award and the supporting centre award are listed, plus institutional support, each with the mechanism and programme named. Funding logic check: each grantor is paired with award information in funders[].notes (the alternative prose representation accepted in place of a structured grants block), and the stated purposes align with the Bridge2AI programme goals. Consistent.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].notes: 'Award 1OT2OD032742-01 ... NIH RePORTER lists core project number OT2OD032742, application ID 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2, principal investigator Trey Ideker, organization University of California, San Diego, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, and a fiscal year 2025 award amount of 5,289,382'; funders[1].notes: 'Award 5U54HG012513-02' Beyond the award numbers, the record supplies the application ID, project period, PI and award amount — enough to verify the award independently in RePORTER. NIH pattern check: 1OT2OD032742-01 parses as application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01; 3OT2OD032742-01S2 is the type-3 supplement of the same core project; 5U54HG012513-02 parses as type 5, U54, NHGRI, year 02. All match NIH construction and the institutes (OD for the Common Fund Bridge2AI programme, HG for the Bridge Center) are plausible for the stated programme. Valid.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: 47 entries, the large majority with ORCID iDs and institutional affiliations (UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA with ROR:0153tk833, Yale, UAB, KTH, Simon Fraser, Montreal); principal_investigator: 'Trey Ideker (ORCID:0000-0002-1708-8454), University of California San Diego'; funders entries double as acknowledgements; maintainers lists three named contacts with emails and roles Attribution is machine-actionable (ORCIDs, RORs) and roles are differentiated — PI, maintainers, programme manager, website support, corresponding author. ORCID checksum-shaped identifiers are well formed throughout. The record flags and adjudicates one affiliation conflict for Andrej Sali (UCSD in release metadata versus UCSF in the preprint) rather than silently choosing. Consistent and transparently sourced.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: four entries naming the performing laboratory and the protocol — SEC-MS 'performed in the Nevan Krogan laboratory at the University of California San Francisco'; AP-MS 'on endogenously tagged cell lines'; ICC-IF and confocal microscopy 'in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford University, using automated fixation and permeabilization protocols on a pipetting robot'; single-cell CRISPR screens 'using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit' Settings are concrete: named laboratories, automation, library design (6 gRNAs per gene), and the dCas9 induction system. A competent lab could reproduce the design from this. The four mechanisms map one-to-one onto the four acquisition_methods and onto the data_collectors entries, with the same laboratories named. Consistent.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: four entries with was_directly_observed: true — SEC-MS for proteome-wide complex mapping; AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines; ICC-IF confocal microscopy with per-channel reagents (DAPI, calreticulin, tubulin, antibody against the protein of interest) using Human Protein Atlas antibodies, was_validated_verified: true with antibody quality 'scored according to a standard Human Protein Atlas protocol'; Perturb-seq 'using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit'. raw_data_sources names the two laboratory deposition archives feeding the pipeline. Instruments, kits, reagents and antibody validation are all named, and the imaging channel assignment is specified at reagent level. The 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is a real and appropriate instrument for single-cell CRISPRi readout; HPA antibody scoring is an appropriate validation for ICC-IF. Methods match the claimed modalities. Valid.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: four steps (node2vec PPI embedding; HPA deep-learning image embedding; contrastive co-embedding integration reconstructing both inputs with minimal information loss; community detection over co-embedding similarities yielding the map hierarchy). cleaning_strategies: QC of MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J single-cell CRISPR screen data. labeling_strategies: two-pronged annotation aligning maps to Gene Ontology and Reactome and naming assemblies via an LLM with a confidence score; data_annotation_platform: 'Gene Set AI (GSAI) pipeline guiding the GPT-4 model'. machine_annotation_tools: four entries with descriptions. The pipeline is described step by step with the rationale for each transformation and with an annotation-quality mechanism (name confidence score, referenced analysis essay), which is more than most records supply. Content-accuracy caveat: this pipeline produces the predicted cell maps that known_limitations states are not in this release, so the documented preprocessing describes the project's method rather than the transformation history of the distributed files. Scored 1 because the fields are richly and correctly populated; the mismatch is recorded as a medium-severity content-accuracy issue and is decisive at sub-element 4. annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols are absent.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Software named in the record: node2vec, DenseNet-121, GPT-4 (via the Gene Set AI pipeline) and HiDeF in machine_annotation_tools and preprocessing_strategies; Cell Mapping Toolkit (https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline), FAIRSCAPE and the Integrative Modeling Platform in external_resources. Distributed files per file_collections: AP-MS archives, SEC-MS archives, the Perturb-seq cell atlas (collection_type processed_data), raw SRA sequences, IF image archives, and release metadata. A reader cannot tell what software produced or transformed the data actually being distributed. No search or quantification software is named for the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives, and no alignment or quantification software is named for the processed_data Perturb-seq cell atlas; cleaning_strategies reports QC without naming a tool. The record documents its tooling prominently, but in roles the threshold excludes. Role analysis: node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI and the Cell Mapping Toolkit fall under role (e) — the record itself states in known_limitations that 'It does not contain predicted cell maps', so this pipeline's outputs are not in this release; FAIRSCAPE falls under role (c), packaging the release as RO-Crate with provenance metadata without transforming the data inside; the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit and the pipetting robot fall under role (a), capture and instrumentation; the UVA Dataverse falls under role (b), hosting; the Integrative Modeling Platform is downstream modelling whose outputs are likewise not in this release. No slot carries the name of software that produced or transformed a distributed file, so the sub-element scores 0.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: 11 entries with archival flags — MassIVE deposits (SEC-MS for iPSC lineages; SEC-MS for cancer cells; AP-MS paclitaxel; AP-MS vorinostat), SRA via NCBI BioProject, Figshare CRISPRi atlas, the embargoed Perturb-seq resource with its restriction stated, https://cm4ai.org, the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository and readthedocs documentation, FAIRSCAPE (MIT License), and the Integrative Modeling Platform. conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema. related_datasets links the describing preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311. External standards and resources are enumerated with their access routes, licences where relevant, and restrictions where they apply; the describing publication is linked separately. imputation_protocols is absent and the record nowhere states that imputation was not used, which is the one unmet part of this composite; the external-resource and standards scope is met comprehensively. Scored 1.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: four typed entries — scope_limitation ('This is an interim release. It does not contain predicted cell maps') with scope_impact; coverage_limitation ('SEC-MS, IF imaging, and CRISPRi Perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'); integration_limitation on the pre-publication embargo with a recommended_mitigation; methodological_limitation ('Requires domain expertise for meaningful analysis') Candid and specific, including the limitation most likely to disappoint a reuser (no cell maps yet) and the incomplete protein overlap across modalities, each with a type and, where possible, a mitigation. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the scope limitation matches discouraged_uses, the embargo matches the restricted external_resource, and the expertise caveat matches discouraged_uses. Consistent.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: bias_type: representation_bias; bias_description: 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'; affected_subsets names all data in the release. future_use_impacts: two entries on integrating anticipated applications into governance frameworks and on the Ethics team's tooling for ELSI awareness. Only one bias category is offered — batch or antibody-selection bias in the imaging arm goes unmentioned — which is a warning, not a failure. Consistent.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: No `anomalies` slot in the record. The nearest content is cleaning_strategies ('Single-cell CRISPR screen data ... were reported as undergoing quality control at the time of the CM4AI preprint') and the coverage_limitation on incomplete protein overlap. No outliers, failed assays, low-confidence antibodies, dropped guides or batch effects are documented, and the one quality statement reports a process as unfinished at preprint time rather than an outcome for the released files. A reuser gets no per-file quality signal beyond MD5 checksums. Absent field; the general limitations do not substitute for anomaly documentation. Fails.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: two entries with named contacts (Vardit Ravitsky; Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon) describing the Ethics Module's plan for 'ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets, balancing openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property'. future_use_impacts: 'Anticipating potential applications of the data and derived AI/ML systems, integrating them into data governance frameworks to optimize benefits and mitigate potential risks...' and the Ethics team's ELSI tooling.
