Ethics claims are proportionate to the data type: oversight focuses on licensing, dissemination and downstream AI risk rather than on participant protections that would be inapplicable here. No conflicts-of-interest statement is present, a minor gap. Consistent.

text: publisher: ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia); citation names 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds'; raw deposits additionally in MassIVE, SRA and Figshare An established institutional Dataverse with a stated preservation commitment, plus domain repositories for the raw data — publication is both recognised and durable. text: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; labeling_strategies aligns cell maps to Gene Ontology and Reactome; instances use B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs; creators use ORCID and ROR Conformance spans packaging (RO-Crate), metadata schema, content ontologies (GO, Reactome) and identifier standards (ORCID, ROR, DOI, Cellosaurus RRIDs) — a genuinely multi-layered standards posture. text: keywords: 29 terms including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, single-cell RNA sequencing, protein-protein interaction, protein localization, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, iPSC, breast cancer, paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPR/Cas9, Bridge2AI, CM4AI, subcellular imaging Well above the five-keyword threshold and spread across the axes a searcher would use: assay/method, cell line, perturbagen, biological entity, disease area and programme. name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 clause by clause (Attribution, NonCommercial, ShareAlike, no additional restrictions) with a citation obligation; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions names the Regents of the University of California as copyright holder, Stanford for raw spatial proteomics images, the commercial negotiation route, and MTA availability of the KOLF2.1J line A reuser can determine both what they may do and whom to approach for anything outside it, including the non-obvious detail that copyright is split by data package. name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records the dataset as not FDA regulated, not involving human subjects, and comprising de-identified samples'; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker; data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker with committee_name 'Data Access Committee' and an access_review_process; confidential_elements records the pre-publication embargo on Perturb-seq depositions The regulatory determination is stated affirmatively on three axes (FDA, human subjects, deidentification) rather than left blank, a named governance contact is given in both the regulatory and governance slots, and the one genuine access constraint — the embargo on specific depositions — is identified by modality and cell line. No confidentiality_level enum, hipaa_compliant or other_compliance value is supplied; HIPAA is not germane to non-clinical cell-line data, so its absence is appropriate, but a formal confidentiality classification would still be expected. Governance contact agrees across regulatory_restrictions and data_governance, and matches creator ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: page: Dataverse persistent-identifier URL; distribution_formats.notes: 'Individual files below the repository's 1.9 GB download limit may be downloaded directly; the dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP, and the Dataverse Data Access API is offered for programmatic access'; per-file path and MD5 for all ten archives Scored on the 'platform access instructions' branch of the criterion. The instructions are specific and operationally useful — they name the access route, state the per-file size ceiling, warn that whole-dataset ZIP download will fail, and give filenames and checksums to verify against. The dedicated download_url slot is empty and no API endpoint URI is given, recorded as a low-severity completeness issue. Access is nonetheless determinate: the landing page resolves from the DOI and the retrieval mechanism is named.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: format 'ZIP archive' / media_type application/zip, and format 'RO-Crate metadata package' / media_type application/ld+json; dataset-level compression: zip; each file_collection carries compression: zip; release metadata archive carries conforms_to: RO-Crate and conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE] Two distribution formats are declared with correct MIME types, and the packaging standard is identified by both a free-text and an enumerated value. The record is explicit that RO-Crate provenance packaging travels with the data. application/zip and application/ld+json are correct media types for the stated formats. Content-level formats inside the archives (image, mass-spectrometry, single-cell matrix) are not declared — flagged as a medium-severity completeness issue rather than scored here, since this sub-element asks for distribution formats and file types, which are supplied.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: five typed entries; external_resources: eleven entries covering four MassIVE depositions (SEC-MS iPSC, SEC-MS MDA-MB-468, AP-MS paclitaxel, AP-MS vorinostat), the NCBI BioProject/SRA deposition with its embargo restriction, Figshare, https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with readthedocs documentation, https://fairscape.github.io, https://integrativemodeling.org, https://ndexbio.org Exceptionally thorough: the underlying primary depositions are enumerated per modality with archival: true flags, embargo status is attached to the affected resource rather than stated generically, and tooling, portal and network-sharing endpoints are all reachable. All URLs are well-structured and their domains are plausible for the named resources. MassIVE and SRA are the domain-appropriate repositories for mass-spectrometry and sequence data respectively, so the routing of each modality is semantically correct.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share ... and adapt (remix, transform, and build upon the material)' subject to Attribution, NonCommercial and ShareAlike Reuse is affirmatively permitted and the permissions are enumerated rather than named by reference alone, so a reuser can determine compliance without consulting the licence deed. The NonCommercial limit and its negotiation route are clearly stated. Licence identifier, enumerated permissions and data_use_permission enum are mutually consistent; ShareAlike obligation is correctly propagated to derivatives.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: 'ZIP archive' (application/zip) and 'RO-Crate metadata package' (application/ld+json); file_collections[release-metadata].conforms_to: RO-Crate with conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; description: 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework' RO-Crate with a JSON-LD media type is a genuine community packaging standard rather than a nominal format declaration, and it is asserted with a controlled enumeration value. Scored 1 on that basis. Weakened by two gaps recorded as issues: the content formats inside the ZIPs are unnamed (raw_data_sources says only 'Multi-channel confocal microscopy image files'), and no character encoding is stated. A reuser can open the packages but cannot predict the internal file types before download.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections[release-metadata]: conforms_to: RO-Crate, conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; instances use ontology CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64 and B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34 Conformance is asserted at three levels — the datasheet's own schema, the data package's RO-Crate standard, and Bridge2AI substrate/topic ontology terms on every instance — with the record honestly confining the RO-Crate claim to the metadata archive rather than over-claiming it for the image and mass-spectrometry content. The w3id URI and the RO_CRATE enum are well formed; CURIE prefixes are used consistently. source_caveats explicitly explains why no dataset-level conforms_to is asserted, which is a correct rather than evasive scoping decision.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables slot anywhere in the record; is_tabular: false; no data dictionary in file_collections, whose descriptions characterise each archive's biological content but not its columns or fields Nothing describes the variable-level structure of the distributed processed data. The AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq atlas packages are inherently tabular result sets, so a reuser cannot determine column identifiers, units or semantics without opening the archives. is_tabular: false is coherent with the absence of variables at dataset level, but it is inconsistent with the processed_data packages' evident tabular content — recorded as a completeness issue. Scored 0 on absence of the evidence this sub-element requires.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: five categories with examples (AI-ready research data, model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation/disease analysis, interpretable ML with a usage_notes on downstream human-genomics applications); prohibited_uses: 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; discouraged_uses: integrated cell-map analysis (maps not in this release) and use without domain expertise All three registers are populated and each is substantive. The discouraged_uses entries are especially useful because they steer users away from precisely the misreading this interim release invites — expecting computed cell maps — rather than offering generic caution. Guidance is consistent with the data type and with known_limitations; the clinical prohibition is proportionate for non-clinical cell-line research data and does not contradict the open CC BY-NC-SA licence.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: two entries with review_details and contact_person (Vardit Ravitsky; Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon, described as working with the project's Ethics module on guidelines, best practices and governance milestones); human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives both reviewers' contact e-mail addresses; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance records the formal determination; data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker For a dataset with no human participants, the oversight actually available is a named ethics function and a governance committee, and both are documented with named, contactable individuals and a description of the Ethics module's remit. A reader can identify who reviewed the release and whom to raise an ethical concern with — the actionable core of this sub-element. No IRB number is present, which is correct rather than missing: involves_human_subjects is false and the record states the determination explicitly, so no IRB approval is expected. data_protection_impacts is absent; a DPIA is not expected where no personal data is processed. Ethics contacts are corroborated by matching creator entries (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153).

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject. The June 2026 release record states that samples are de-identified and that the dataset does not involve human subjects.' The record states both the determination and the reasoning that supports it — non-clinical tissue-culture origin, no feasible linkage to an individual with current knowledge — which is the substantive answer for donor-derived cell-line material. It is not boilerplate and it tells a reuser what identifiability risk they are inheriting. No named standard (Safe Harbor, expert determination, k-anonymity) is invoked, and subpopulations.notes does publish donor attributes for both lines; these are the publicly catalogued Cellosaurus/HipSci descriptors rather than newly disclosed identifiers, but the tension is recorded as a low-severity content_accuracy issue. Deidentification claim is consistent with sensitive_elements_present: false and with involves_human_subjects: false.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk are absent; there are no participants in this dataset whose privacy could be protected or whose re-identification risk could be assessed Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter — cell lines rather than people — instead of its documentation quality. Exclusion is grounded in positive external evidence of non-participation, not in the emptiness of this sub-element's own fields, so the anti-circular rule is not engaged.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent is absent; no individuals were enrolled, so no consent procedure, consent type or withdrawal mechanism exists to document Excluded from the denominator. The record's own ip_restrictions note that the KOLF2.1J line is distributed to not-for-profit organisations under a simple MTA, i.e. material governance rather than participant consent, which is the appropriate instrument for this material. Consistent with involves_human_subjects: false and direct_collection.is_direct: false; no consistency violation arises from the absence of consent documentation here.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false with the note that 'all data derive from established human cell lines rather than from living individuals, so no at-risk population protections apply'; participant_compensation absent Excluded from the denominator because there are no participants who could be vulnerable or compensated. The record nonetheless addresses the question explicitly with a reasoned negative, which is good practice even though it is not scored here. The populated at_risk_populations block is coherent with the rest of the human-subjects documentation; excluding this sub-element neither credits nor penalises that content.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification names the two cell lines and every condition arm (MDA-MB-468 untreated/DMSO control, paclitaxel, vorinostat; KOLF2.1J undifferentiated plus NPC, neuron and cardiomyocyte derivatives); distribution gives per-condition archive sizes; notes give donor provenance with RRIDs (MDA-MB-468 RRID:CVCL_0419, from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female; KOLF2.1J RRID:CVCL_B5P3, from a healthy male Northern European donor) The biological analogue of a cohort description is fully worked: which lines, which perturbations, which differentiation states, and the donor characteristics behind each line, with resolvable cell-line identifiers. The distribution field is candid that coverage is uneven across modalities rather than implying a balanced design. Subpopulation structure is consistent with instances, acquisition_methods and file_collections; the asymmetry it reports (AP-MS treated-only, IF MDA-MB-468-only) matches the archives actually listed.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: total_file_count: 10 with per-archive sizes and MD5s; instances notes report ~7,000 proteins captured by SEC-MS for both flagship datasets and 11,739 targeted genes in the KOLF2.1J Perturbation Cell Atlas; acquisition_methods report 17 genes endogenously tagged for AP-MS (34 more in progress), 72 of 100 chromatin modifiers identified by SEC-MS, and >700 protein complexes in iPSCs and neurons Concrete scale figures are given for three of the four modalities and for the distribution itself, which is enough for a user to judge whether the release is worth retrieving. Counts are internally consistent and total_file_count: 10 matches the ten file_collections exactly. The imaging instance count for this release is not asserted — source_caveats deliberately withholds project-level figures (53,788 images) and attributes the 464/563 per-condition protein counts to prior releases. Recorded as a low-severity completeness issue; the restraint is honest but leaves the imaging scale of this release unstated.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: is_tabular: false is present; variables absent entirely; no subsets block and therefore no is_data_split or is_subpopulation flags on any subset; file_collections describe archive contents biologically but define no fields or columns Only one of the four evidence sources is present, and it is a bare negative flag. Nothing documents variable identifiers, column semantics, or the analytic role of any subset, so the internal structure of the distributed packages is opaque. is_tabular: false is an explicit flag rather than a missing value, but it does not support this sub-element's purpose and sits oddly against the tabular processed_data packages. The subpopulation structure is carried in the Subpopulation class, not as subset flags, so no split/subpopulation role information is available at the file level.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances: four instance_type entries (IF confocal image, SEC-MS elution profile, AP-MS interaction, single-cell CRISPRi Perturb-seq profile), each with data_substrate (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/59/58/64) and data_topic (B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/26/34) CURIEs, a label flag and notes describing staining channels, conditions and coverage; purposes and addressing_gaps name the disease areas (cancer, neuropsychiatric, cardiac disorders) Topics are given both as controlled ontology terms and as readable descriptions, and the conditions represented (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat, differentiation states) are traceable from instance notes through to individual archives. Substrate and topic CURIEs are applied consistently — the two mass-spectrometry modalities share B2AI_TOPIC:26, which is semantically appropriate — and the disease framing matches the targeted protein selection described in sampling_strategies.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: 'The release is not yet in completed final form. Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo; protein-protein interaction, protein localization and CRISPRi Perturb-seq data interrogate incompletely overlapping sets of proteins; and computed cell maps are not included in this release.'; sampling_strategies: is_sample true, is_random false, is_representative false, with strategies, why_not_representative and source_data Both quality caveats and sampling design are documented with specifics rather than disclaimers. The incomplete protein overlap across modalities is exactly the defect that would silently break a naive multimodal join, and it is stated plainly. missing_data_documentation is absent — no account of missing values within the distributed tables — but the two populated sources carry substantive, non-boilerplate content that addresses the sub-element's purpose. Anomalies are consistent with known_limitations and confidential_elements.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' A version string is present and reinforced by the release status and the citation's V2 designation, so a user can cite an exact state of the dataset. Flagged as a low-severity consistency issue: version_access records the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases as version 2.1, so this newer release carries a lower version string. version_details explains that each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset with its own counter, which resolves but does not remove the confusion.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available lists the May 2024, March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, v1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, v2.1) and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, v2.1) releases; latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_details: 'Each quarterly release is deposited as a distinct Dataverse dataset with its own persistent DOI and internal version history; the Dataverse record exposes version differences and per-version publication dates' Every prior release is separately citable by DOI and the mechanism for retrieving any of them is stated explicitly, including where to see per-version differences. This is a complete answer to 'how do I get version X'. All listed DOIs share the 10.18130 Dataverse prefix and are mirrored in related_datasets with is_new_version_of relationships — the two slots agree.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata absent; updates.update_details carries only forward-looking cadence ('regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'); updates has no description field; top-level notes describes the project's pillar/module structure and AI-readiness criteria, not release changes Nothing states what the June 2026 release changed relative to October 2025. The description enumerates release contents but is not a change log, and no errata or corrections are recorded. Applying the instrument's release-notes rule: updates.update_details and notes must carry actual release or derivation information, and neither does. The one genuine change narrative in the record — related_datasets noting that the June 2025 release was revised to add RGB images, correct RO-Crate metadata and change naming conventions — concerns an earlier release and cannot be credited here. The instances note on the 563→464 protein count across releases is likewise attributed to prior releases.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: quarterly; updates.update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis. CM4AI releases data quarterly, ensuring continuous updates to the cell maps and input data streams.'; retention_limit.retention_details: long-term preservation in the UVA Dataverse with committed institutional funds Both cadence and horizon are stated, and the maintenance commitment is backed by a named preservation arrangement — a user can plan around both future releases and long-term availability. Flagged as a low-severity consistency issue: the observed release dates (March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, June 2026) include an eight-month gap that does not match the stated quarterly cadence. collection_timeframes also records a conflict between the RePORTER project end (2026-08-31) and the November 2026 maintenance horizon, which the record itself discloses.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Multimodal experimental interrogation of the MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cell line and the KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cell line and their differentiated derivatives, by AP-MS, SEC-MS, CRISPRi Perturb-seq, and immunofluorescence confocal microscopy'; raw_data_sources: four entries with source_description, source_type and access_details naming MassIVE, NCBI SRA/BioProject and Figshare depositions; file_collections distinguish raw_data from processed_data; release metadata archive carries RO-Crate provenance graphs Provenance is traceable in both directions: upstream to the named primary depositions per modality, and downstream through the RO-Crate provenance graphs shipped with the release. Raw versus processed status is marked on every archive, and the generating laboratory is named for each modality in data_collectors. Repository routing is domain-appropriate (mass spectrometry to MassIVE, sequence data to SRA) and embargo status is attached to the specific affected depositions, consistent with confidential_elements and known_limitations.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: five entries (AI-ready hierarchical cell-architecture maps; mapping spatiotemporal cell architecture toward interpretable genotype-phenotype learning; stimulating 'visible' ML research; FAIR standards with deep provenance and replication packages; an ethical-AI research programme and training portfolio); addressing_gaps: three entries on black-box ML in genomics, uncharted subcellular architecture, and the separate application of cell-mapping technologies Motivation is stated at the level of the scientific problem, not the deliverable: the addressing_gaps entries articulate specific deficiencies in the field that this data is meant to remedy, which is exactly the rationale a reuser needs to judge fitness for purpose. Purposes align with the Bridge2AI funding remit evident in funders and keywords, and with the intended_uses and tasks declared elsewhere — no mismatch between why the data exists and what it is offered for.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: four entries (interpretable genotype-phenotype learning via visible neural networks; hierarchical cell maps as directed acyclic graphs; variant and mutation interpretation; multi-resolution protein community detection from self-supervised multimodal embeddings); other_tasks: three further entries (integrative structure modelling using PDB/AlphaFold/crosslinking MS, cell-type specificity analysis, protein multi-localization analysis) Seven concrete analytical objectives are named, each specific enough to be recognisable as a research programme rather than a topic label, and several identify the method as well as the question. Tasks are technically coherent with the modalities collected: community detection and VNN construction genuinely follow from PPI plus imaging plus perturbation data, so the stated objectives are achievable from the described inputs.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: four entries — National Institutes of Health (1OT2OD032742-01, CM4AI Data Generation Project), National Institutes of Health (3OT2OD032742-01S2, with RePORTER application 11211616, FY2025 award 5,289,382, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, awarded to UC San Diego), National Institutes of Health (5U54HG012513-02, Bridge2AI Bridge Center), and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia Each funder entry names the agency, the award, the funded project and the provenance of the statement; the RePORTER entry adds award amount, period and recipient institution. This exceeds a bare agency list. The Frederick Thomas Fund entry correctly carries a grantor and acknowledgement note with no grants block — appropriate for non-grant institutional support and not a missing-award defect. Funding sources align with the stated purposes (Bridge2AI functional genomics).

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants ids: '1OT2OD032742-01', '3OT2OD032742-01S2', '5U54HG012513-02', each paired with a grant name Three distinct award numbers are given with their project titles and with notes identifying where each was sourced, including the distinction between the core CM4AI award, its supplement, and the Bridge2AI Bridge Center award that co-funds the work. All three parse against NIH conventions [application type][activity code][institute][serial]-[support year]: 1-OT2-OD-032742-01 (new, Office of the Director), 3-OT2-OD-032742-01S2 (revision, supplement S2 of the same core project OT2OD032742), 5-U54-HG-012513-02 (non-competing continuation, NHGRI). Activity codes and institute codes are real and appropriate; the supplement number is consistent with the core project number cited in a creator note. grant_number_format: valid_nih.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: 38 entries, nearly all with ORCID identifiers and affiliations, including principal_investigator designation for Trey Ideker (ORCID:0000-0002-1708-8454) with the RePORTER project number, the depositor (Justin Niestroy), the Data Governance contact (Jillian Parker), the Program Manager (Swathi Thaker) and the two ethics contacts; maintainers lists four contact routes with e-mail addresses; citation reproduces the full author list Roles are attributed, not merely listed: the record distinguishes PI, depositor, governance contact, programme manager and ethics contacts, so a user knows whom to approach for which kind of question. Affiliations carry ROR identifiers where available. ORCID strings are well formed; the single creator without an identifier (Axelsson U) carries an explicit source_caveat explaining why none is supplied, and a conflicting affiliation (Andrej Sali) is disclosed with the source ranking used to resolve it. Creator names reconcile with the citation author list.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: four entries — mass spectrometry instrumentation for AP-MS and SEC-MS workflows on whole-cell extracts; confocal microscopy with multi-channel immunofluorescence using HPA primary antibodies plus DAPI, anti-calreticulin and anti-tubulin reference markers; 10x Genomics 3'HT single-cell kit with lentiviral gRNA library and inducible dCas9; automated pipetting robot for fixation and permeabilization Each modality's collection setup is described concretely enough to be recognised and approximately reproduced, down to the specific reference channels used in imaging and the automation step in sample preparation. data_collectors additionally names the generating laboratory for each modality. Mechanisms correspond one-to-one with the four instance types and with the acquisition_methods entries; the imaging channel description matches the instances note exactly (DAPI blue, calreticulin yellow, tubulin red, target green). No participant recruitment appears here, which is consistent with the cell-line nature of the dataset.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: four entries with was_directly_observed flags and quantitative detail (17 genes endogenously tagged in MDA-MB-468 with AP-MS under three conditions, 34 more in progress; SEC-MS identifying 72 of 100 chromatin modifiers and >700 complexes in iPSCs and neurons; HPA antibody-based IF with robot-automated fixation; CRISPR lentiviral library targeting 100 chromatin factors at 6 gRNAs per gene with inducible dCas9 and 10x 3'HT readout); raw_data_sources: four entries naming the primary depositions Instruments, reagents, library design parameters and yields are all stated, and the was_directly_observed/was_inferred_derived flags make the measurement status explicit rather than leaving it to inference. Acquisition detail is technically coherent for each assay and consistent with the raw_data_sources routing. One minor mismatch is recorded: AP-MS acquisition is described under three conditions while only the two treated conditions are distributed in this release.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: five staged entries (node2vec PPI embedding; HPA deep-learning image embedding; contrastive co-embedding with reconstruction objective; community detection over co-embedding similarities yielding the map hierarchy; annotation by alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome plus LLM naming); labeling_strategies with a data_annotation_protocol describing the GSAI engineered prompt (chain-of-thought, one-shot, name plus confidence score plus reasoning essay) and a note on human curation jamborees; machine_annotation_tools: GPT-4, node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, each with a tool_description The pipeline is described as an ordered sequence with the objective of each stage stated, and the annotation protocol goes beyond naming a method to describe the prompting strategy and the confidence score it emits. This is substantive, reproducible-in-principle documentation. Flagged as a medium-severity consistency issue: this pipeline produces cell maps, which the record states are not in this release, while the derivation of the distributed processed_data packages from raw acquisitions goes undescribed. cleaning_strategies, annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols are all absent, so no annotation quality analysis is available. Scored 1 on the substantial preprocessing and labeling content actually present.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Named software, by slot: machine_annotation_tools — GPT-4, node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF; preprocessing_strategies — node2vec, a Human Protein Atlas deep-learning model, contrastive integration, Gene Ontology and Reactome alignment; labeling_strategies — the GSAI pipeline; external_resources — Cell Mapping Toolkit (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline), FAIRSCAPE, Integrative Modeling Platform, NDEx/Cytoscape/HiView/ndex2; extension_mechanism — pip-installable Cell Mapping Toolkit packages. No used_software is attached to any processing strategy. No software is named that produced or transformed the data being distributed. The AP-MS, SEC-MS and Perturb-seq atlas packages are released as processed_data, yet nothing names the mass-spectrometry search and quantification software or the single-cell processing software that produced them. Every named tool falls into an excluded role. Primarily (e): node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI, the Cell Mapping Toolkit and IMP belong to the pipeline the record itself states produced cell maps that are 'not included in this release' (known_limitations, anomalies, discouraged_uses), so what produced this release remains unstated. Also (c): FAIRSCAPE produced the RO-Crate packaging and provenance metadata without transforming the data inside it. Also (a): the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit, confocal microscope and pipetting robot are capture instrumentation. Also (b): the UVA Dataverse is the hosting platform. Score 0.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: eleven entries with archival flags and URLs (four MassIVE depositions, NCBI BioProject/SRA with embargo restriction, Figshare, cm4ai.org, cellmaps_pipeline GitHub plus readthedocs, fairscape.github.io, integrativemodeling.org, ndexbio.org); conforms_to: RO-Crate with conforms_to_standard RO_CRATE on the metadata archive; related_datasets links the describing bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311) and the Perturbation Atlas paper (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734); use_repository points to the project publications page Standards, primary depositions, tooling documentation and describing publications are all reachable, and the resources are differentiated by role (archival deposition versus documentation versus sharing endpoint) rather than dumped as a link list. imputation_protocols is absent and the record does not state that imputation was not used — a gap against the full sub-element scope. The remaining evidence is extensive and specific enough to score 1. All URLs are well formed and domain-plausible.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: four typed entries — scope_limitation (interim release, no predicted cell maps), coverage_limitation (PPI, localization and Perturb-seq interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets) with scope_impact 'Integrated multimodal analysis is constrained to the subset of proteins measured in more than one modality', methodological_limitation (domain expertise required), representativeness_limitation (embargoed datasets, not final form) with recommended_mitigation to consult the External Data Links for current availability Limitations are categorised, and two carry either a scope_impact or an actionable mitigation. They describe consequences for analysis rather than merely admitting imperfection — the coverage entry tells a reuser precisely what will constrain a multimodal join. Consistent with anomalies, discouraged_uses and confidential_elements; the same three defects (interim status, non-overlapping coverage, embargo) are reported coherently across all four slots without contradiction.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: bias_type selection_bias ('derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large') and bias_type sampling_bias ('Proteins interrogated were selected for their involvement in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders — specifically 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes') with affected_subsets naming the AP-MS, SEC-MS and IF targets in the MDA-MB-468 arm; future_use_impacts carries the downstream generalizability consequence Both entries use enumerated bias types and name the mechanism of the bias, and one identifies the affected subsets. The target-selection bias is a genuinely non-obvious disclosure that a reuser building a proteome-wide model would need. bias_type values align with BiasTypeEnum categories; the biases stated are consistent with sampling_strategies (is_random false, is_representative false) and are carried forward into future_use_impacts as a social/scientific impact — the RAI chain from bias to impact is intact.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: 'The release is not yet in completed final form. Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo; protein-protein interaction, protein localization and CRISPRi Perturb-seq data interrogate incompletely overlapping sets of proteins; and computed cell maps are not included in this release.' Three distinct, concrete quality issues are disclosed in a single candid statement, each of which materially affects what an analyst can do with the release. Corroborated by known_limitations, confidential_elements and discouraged_uses; the record is consistent in not over-claiming completeness anywhere.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present: false with sensitivity_details 'The release states that no human subjects are involved and samples are de-identified. Data derive from established human cell lines rather than from identifiable individuals.'; content_warnings: content_warnings_present: false; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present: true with the embargo detail naming the affected Perturb-seq depositions The negative determination is reasoned rather than bare — it states why no sensitive content is present — and the one genuine handling constraint, the pre-publication embargo, is separately flagged with its scope. Explicit false flags with justification are meaningful documentation here. Consistent with involves_human_subjects: false, is_deidentified and at_risk_populations. content_warnings carries no justification text, a minor thinness, but the sensitivity determination it accompanies is substantiated.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: two entries with named contacts (Vardit Ravitsky; Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon, working with the Ethics module on guidelines, best practices and governance milestones); future_use_impacts: three entries — non-generalizability of models trained on cell-line data, the Ethics module's anticipation of downstream applications and integration into governance frameworks with tools to raise ELSI awareness, and the explicitly forbidden clinical misuse Social impact is analysed in both directions: the scientific limitation that propagates into deployed models, and the governance apparatus set up to anticipate and mitigate downstream effects. The forbidden-use entry ties impact analysis back to an enforceable restriction in prohibited_uses. Ethical review contacts are corroborated by matching creator entries and by human_subject_research.ethics_review_board; future_use_impacts is consistent with known_biases and prohibited_uses. No conflicts-of-interest statement is present, a minor gap against the full sub-element scope.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia); page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/...; third_party_sharing: 'The archival release is distributed via the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), an NIH-approved generalist repository'; distribution_formats.notes refers to the same repository and its Data Access API The hosting platform is a recognised institutional Dataverse instance, identified by a resolvable ROR for the publishing organisation and named in prose with its NIH-approved generalist repository status. The complementary domain repositories (MassIVE, SRA, Figshare, NDEx) are documented alongside. ROR:0153tk833 resolves to the University of Virginia, consistent with the DOI prefix registrant (10.18130) and the landing-page host. Publisher is given only as a CURIE, but the repository is named unambiguously in third_party_sharing.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: full author list of ~45 names, year 2026, exact title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license_and_use_terms adds the obligation that 'publications referencing this data or derived products should cite the related publication as well as directly citing the data collection'; related_datasets identifies the describing preprint A complete, copy-ready citation string is supplied with version designation and resolvable DOI, and the citation instruction goes further by specifying that both the data and the describing publication must be cited. All three components the rubric asks of Bridge2AI datasets — formatted string, DOI, instructions — are present. The DOI in the citation matches the doi, id and version_access.latest_version_doi fields exactly; the V2 designation matches version '2.0'; author names reconcile with the creators list.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: file_collections[release-metadata]: conforms_to: RO-Crate, conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema with conforms_to_class: Dataset; description states RO-Crate packaging via FAIRSCAPE; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC ontology CURIEs; identifiers follow ORCID, ROR and RRID/Cellosaurus conventions RO-Crate is a genuine community packaging standard for AI-ready data and is asserted with a controlled enumeration value, not merely in prose. Community identifier standards are applied consistently across people, organisations and cell lines. The record honestly scopes the RO-Crate claim to the metadata archive and explains in source_caveats why no dataset-level conforms_to is asserted for the image and mass-spectrometry content. Domain content standards (e.g. OME-TIFF, mzML) are not named, which limits but does not negate the conformance claim.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: 'CM4AI project web portal at https://cm4ai.org, providing data releases, tools, product documentation, publications, and training materials'; Cell Mapping Toolkit documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/; FAIRSCAPE tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io; use_repository: https://cm4ai.org/publications/; page landing URL; notes describes the March 2024 CM4AI CodeFest with tutorials on how the data were derived and integrated, and an in-person internship at Yale and UCSD Documentation spans reference material (readthedocs, tutorials), a project portal explicitly offering training materials, a publications register, and named outreach events with described curricula. A newcomer has several concrete routes into the data. All URLs are well formed with plausible domains for the named resources; the training activities described in notes are consistent with the training purpose declared in purposes.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM (October 2025), is_new_version_of doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R (June 2025, with a note on its post-deposit revision), is_new_version_of doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX (March 2025), is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (the CM4AI preprint, 'required for citation by users of the data'), is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (Perturbation Cell Atlas, PMCID PMC11580897) Five relationships, each typed and each annotated with what the target is and why it matters. The distinction between the describing publication and a merely referencing one is drawn correctly, and the citation obligation attached to the former is stated. Relationship types are semantically apt for each target; all DOIs are well formed; the version lineage agrees with version_access.versions_available, and the PMCID is correctly formatted.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; raw_data_sources carry RRID:CVCL_0419 (MDA-MB-468) and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 (KOLF2.1J) A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the DOI, the record id and the latest-version pointer, and the four prior releases are identified by sibling DOIs under the same prefix. Cell-line RRIDs additionally identify the source material. DOI matches the 10.XXXXX/... pattern; the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) registrant and is corroborated by the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu landing page and by the repository named in the citation, so the prefix is plausible rather than merely well-formed. CVCL_ is the Cellosaurus RRID namespace and both cell-line RRIDs are well-formed.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of roughly 1,600 characters naming the two cell lines, the three MDA-MB-468 treatment conditions, the four KOLF2.1J differentiation states, the four assay modalities (perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence), the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging, the archive, the scientific objective and the nine collaborating institutions Far beyond the 200-character threshold and substantive throughout: a reader learns what was measured, on what material, under which perturbations, in what packaging and to what end. The title disambiguates the release from its siblings by date and status. Description content matches the claimed dataset type: every modality it names reappears in instances, file_collections and acquisition_methods, and the cell lines it names reappear in raw_data_sources with RRIDs. No overclaiming: the description does not assert computed cell maps, which known_limitations confirms are absent.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: 29 terms including AI, AP-MS, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, neural progenitor cell, paclitaxel, perturb-seq, protein-protein interaction, protein localization, scRNAseq, SEC-MS, subcellular imaging, vorinostat Well above the five-keyword threshold, spanning programme (Bridge2AI, CM4AI), biological material (two named cell lines and four cell types), assay methods (five), perturbagens (two named drugs) and analysis domain. Both expanded and abbreviated forms are given for several terms, which aids retrieval. Terms are used correctly and are consistent with description and instances. 'mass spectroscopy' is a mild misnomer for mass spectrometry but is a common search variant and does not impair discovery. No clinical or patient terminology appears, which is consistent with the cell-line subject matter and is the evidence relied on for Element 4 applicability.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections enumerates five named sub-resources (immunofluorescence image archives, AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, release metadata) each with its own id, description, collection_type, file_count and compression The landing page is a well-formed persistent-id resolver URL on the hosting repository, and the release is decomposed into five described collections with sizes, giving a genuine hierarchical view of what the ten files are. Landing page host matches the DOI registrant prefix. The five collection ids are fragments on the release DOI, which is a reasonable local naming scheme for sub-resources even though the fragments do not resolve independently.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: seven typed entries - four is_new_version_of (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM October 2025, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R June 2025, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX March 2025, doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5 initial release), two is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734) and one references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3) The release is placed precisely in a quarterly lineage and tied to its describing literature, each link carrying a relationship type, a target DOI and a human-readable name. parent_datasets is not used, but the version lineage conveys the same hierarchy more informatively. Relationship types are used correctly: the prior quarterly releases are versions, the two preprints describe the data, and the Nature paper is a reference rather than a description, a distinction the record makes explicitly in a source_caveat because that study used U2OS cells rather than the lines in this release. The four version DOIs agree with version_access.versions_available.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with its attribution, non-commercial, ShareAlike and no-further-restrictions conditions and the commercial-negotiation route; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions lists four items including 'Copyright to the datasets is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise indicated' and 'Raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University'; data_governance.access_review_process states no access request is required for published files Both the licence and the intellectual-property position are stated concretely, including which institution holds copyright over which part of the release and who supervises commercial relicensing. The access route is unambiguous: public download, no application. The IP allocation is consistent with data_collectors, which attributes the immunofluorescence imaging to the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and the mass-spectrometry work to UCSF. The record discloses that the copyright wording is transcribed from the March 2025 release because the June 2026 landing page does not restate it, which is a transparent provenance caveat rather than an unsupported assertion.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: unrestricted; regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions states the dataset does not involve human subjects, samples are de-identified and the data are not FDA regulated, and separately that clinical decision-making or patient-care use 'requires appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance cites FAIR Principles compliance as an NIH requirement and names Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) as the Data Governance Committee contact A confidentiality classification is asserted from an enumerated vocabulary, the regulatory posture is stated across three specific axes (human subjects, de-identification, FDA), an applying use constraint is recorded, and a named governance contact with an email address is given, which is the governance-contact evidence the source rubric asks for. confidentiality_level: unrestricted is consistent with the public licence and with access_review_process requiring no application, and it is a semantically appropriate classification for cell-line laboratory data. hipaa_compliant is unstated, which is defensible since no PHI is claimed to be present. The clinical-use constraint is the E2 evidence that opens Element 4 sub-elements 1 and 2, and it is a constraint that applies rather than a record that none does.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; distribution_formats[1] describes 'Programmatic file access through the Dataverse data access API, recommended for archives above the web download size limit' with access_urls https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/; page gives the same landing page Scored on the 'platform access instructions' reading of this sub-element. The hosting platform is named, a resolvable landing page is supplied, and a second access route is given with an explicit reason for using it, which matters here because three archives are multi-gigabyte. A user can act on this. The dedicated download_url slot is empty and the API base is a truncated endpoint that requires a datafile identifier the record never supplies for any of the ten archives, so the programmatic route is described rather than usable as printed. Recorded as a warning; the landing-page route is sufficient for the point.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats[0].format: 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata' with media_type: application/zip; file_collections each carry compression: zip with sizes (4.6 GB, 3.8 GB, 4.2 GB for the image archives; 113.3 KB and 135.8 KB for AP-MS; 171.8 KB and 93.9 KB for SEC-MS; 30.2 KB and 73.3 KB for perturb-seq; 1.1 MB for metadata); conforms_to names JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema serialisations A container format and a valid MIME type are stated explicitly, the packaging standard is named, and every archive carries a size so a user can plan a download. This is specific rather than boilerplate. application/zip is a correct IANA media type for the stated format. The payload formats inside the archives are not specified anywhere, so a user knows the container and the metadata serialisation but not how to parse the images or tables; recorded as a medium-severity issue and carried into Element 3 sub-element 2.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: seven typed entries with DOIs; external_resources: five groups covering two preprints with DOIs and a PMCID, four MassIVE deposits and a Figshare deposit, two embargoed perturb-seq links with a restrictions note, the CM4AI portal and data-releases page, and four tool links (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, fairscape.github.io, integrativemodeling.org) An unusually complete web of links: sibling releases, describing literature, the mirror deposits of the underlying raw data in MassIVE and Figshare, the project portal and the tooling documentation. The archival flag distinguishes durable deposits from project web pages. The embargo status of the two perturb-seq external links is recorded rather than left as a dead link, with a source_caveat explaining that the June 2025 release listed SRA links and the June 2026 release supersedes them. This is consistent with known_limitations and third_party_sharing, both of which record the same embargo.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/. Users are free to share and adapt the material provided they give appropriate credit...'; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 A named, versioned, standard open licence with a resolvable URL, its permissions and its three conditions written out, plus the attribution expectation and the route for uses the licence does not cover. A reuser can determine what they may do without consulting another document. The licence name, the URL, the enumerated permission value and the prohibited_uses entries agree with one another. The non-commercial and ShareAlike restrictions are real limits on reuse but are clearly disclosed, which is what this sub-element asks for.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats[0]: format 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata', media_type application/zip; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to states provenance is 'expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema'; file_collections carry compression: zip The formats that are named are genuinely standard and are exactly the ones that matter for machine consumption of the package: ZIP, RO-Crate, JSON-LD, RDF-XML, JSON-Schema. RO-Crate is itself an interoperability standard, and an RO-Crate carries per-file format declarations in its own metadata, so the packaging choice is substantive for reuse rather than nominal. Character encoding is stated nowhere and the payload file formats are absent, so a reuser knows the container and metadata layer but not the parse format of the images or tables. Scored 1 because the named standards are specific, correct and actionable, with the payload gap recorded as a medium-severity issue.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate (Research Object Crate)... each RO-Crate is assigned an ARK persistent identifier and carries an end-to-end provenance record expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset Four distinct conformance assertions at three levels: the packaging standard, the provenance ontology, the metadata schema of this datasheet itself with a resolvable w3id URI, and the class within it. This is among the strongest conformance statements the rubric contemplates. The named standards are used correctly and coherently: RO-Crate as the package, EVI as the provenance vocabulary, JSON-LD/RDF-XML as serialisations of it, JSON-Schema for per-dataset schemas, and ARK as the within-crate identifier scheme. The conforms_to_schema URI is well-formed and matches the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema this record is written against.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables block anywhere in the record. instances describes four instance types in prose (image, SEC-MS elution profile, AP-MS measurement, single-cell transcriptome) with data_substrate and data_topic codes, but no variable identifiers, names, types, units or descriptions. Nothing in the record tells a reuser what the columns of the AP-MS, SEC-MS or perturb-seq tables are called, what they contain, or in what units. This is the single largest interoperability gap in an otherwise strongly interoperable record, and it bears directly on the element question about integrating this dataset with others. The gap is consequential rather than formal: the release distributes quantitative tabular outputs whose reuse depends on column semantics, and the record supplies none. Scored 0 on the sub-element's own fields being absent with no substitute elsewhere.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: four categories, three with usage_notes (AI-ready functional genomics research, AI model training, cellular process analysis, analysis of architectural change under disease/treatment/perturbation); prohibited_uses: three with reasons (no clinical decision-making or patient care without regulatory oversight; no commercial use without separate negotiation; no redistribution under other terms); discouraged_uses: three (analyses requiring the absent computed cell maps, analysis without domain expertise, generalisation to the population at large) All three guidance registers are populated, and the discouraged_uses are notably well judged: they warn against precisely the three mistakes this release invites, namely expecting cell maps that are not there, over-reading data that needs domain expertise, and generalising from two cell lines. Guidance is internally consistent with the rest of the record: the cell-map discouragement matches known_limitations and missing_data_documentation, the generalisation discouragement matches known_biases representation_bias and sampling_strategies.is_representative: false, and the commercial prohibition matches the licence and ip_restrictions.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews[0].review_details describes the CM4AI Ethics module's Value-Sensitive Design methodology, normative standards, axiological repository of values, CM4AI Life Cycle framework of governance milestones, and mixed qualitative/quantitative empirical research; reviewing_organization: 'CM4AI Ethics module'; contact_person: ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801; data_governance.stewardship_roles names the Data Governance Committee contact (Jillian Parker, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) and two ethical review contacts (Vardit Ravitsky, Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon) with emails; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board explains the oversight route and why no IRB approval is recorded Oversight is documented as a named body with a described methodology and three contactable individuals, and the absence of an IRB approval is explained rather than left as a hole. For a dataset with no human participants this is a substantive and appropriate account of ethical governance. Consistent with involves_human_subjects: false: the record does not claim an IRB it should not have, and states affirmatively that 'no institutional review board approval is recorded for the release, consistent with its statement that no human subjects are involved'. The contact_person ORCID resolves to the creators entry for Ravitsky V, a genuine internal cross-reference. data_protection_impacts is absent, which is defensible where no personal data is processed, though a short DPIA-equivalent note would have closed the loop. data_governance.source_caveats correctly declines to equate the 'Data Governance Committee' named in the release with the 'Data Access Committee' described in the future tense in the preprint.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release states that samples are de-identified. All data derive from commercially available human cell lines, MDA-MB-468 obtained from ATCC and KOLF2.1J iPSCs from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative resource. The project states that such data are non-clinical and are considered de-identified because they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.'; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance repeats the basis from the preprint The de-identification claim is not left bare: it is attributed, its basis is stated (provenance from commercially distributed cell lines rather than from individuals), and the standard applied is articulated as non-matchability to a human subject with current knowledge. That is specific, non-boilerplate content that tells a reuser why the claim holds. Appropriateness for the data type is the right question here, and a formal HIPAA method would in fact be the wrong instrument for immortalised cell-line material, so the absence of Safe Harbor or Expert Determination is not itself disqualifying. Two gaps are recorded as warnings: no identifiers_removed list, and no residual-risk assessment of genotype-based linkage, which is a live question because the record itself notes MDA-MB-468 has public whole-genome sequencing data and the release distributes single-cell transcriptomic data. Consistent with sensitive_elements_present: false and with confidentiality_level: unrestricted.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk are absent, and there are no participants in this dataset whose privacy they could describe. Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation. The related question that does apply to this record, the basis of the de-identification claim for donor-derived material, is assessed under sub-element 2, where the missing residual-risk assessment is recorded.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent is absent. The record states the cell lines are obtained from ATCC and the HipSci resource, the latter 'available for access by non-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA', so the governing instrument is a material transfer agreement rather than participant consent. Excluded from the denominator. There are no participants from whom consent could have been obtained for this release; donor consent sits with the originating cell-line repositories and is outside the scope of this datasheet's consent field.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation are absent. No participants were enrolled, so no population could be at risk and no compensation could be due. Excluded from the denominator. The donor characteristics that do appear (a 51-year-old black female donor for MDA-MB-468, a healthy male Northern European donor for KOLF2.1J) are recorded in raw_data_sources and credited under Element 5 sub-element 1 as cohort characterisation; they do not constitute an enrolled population for this sub-element.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: raw_data_sources describes MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) as 'established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma' and KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) as 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'; description and instances enumerate the treatment arms (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat) and the four KOLF2.1J states (undifferentiated, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte); known_biases.affected_subsets characterises 'two donor-derived cell lines' with the same demographics For a cell-line dataset the cohort is the set of lines and conditions, and both are characterised concretely: donor age, sex, ethnicity and disease status for one line, donor health status and ancestry for the other, plus RRIDs, provenance repositories and the full factorial of treatment and differentiation states. Scored on the 'population characteristics and demographics' reading of the sub-element. The dedicated subpopulations slot and subsets.is_subpopulation flags are both empty, so the information is recoverable but not organised as subset metadata, and no per-subset counts are given; recorded as a warning. The demographics are consistent between raw_data_sources and known_biases.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: total_file_count: 10; file_collections file_counts of 3, 2, 2, 2 and 1 with per-archive sizes (4.6 GB, 3.8 GB, 4.2 GB, 113.3 KB, 135.8 KB, 171.8 KB, 93.9 KB, 30.2 KB, 73.3 KB, 1.1 MB); instances records that 'the KOLF2.1J iPSC perturbation cell atlas maps transcriptional and fitness phenotypes associated with 11,739 targeted genes'; collection_mechanisms reports 17 genes endogenously tagged for AP-MS with 6 guide RNAs per gene in the CRISPR screens; notes separates project-wide totals (53,788 images, 1,374 interactions, 7,023 proteins, 21.4 TB) from release scope A complete file-level inventory with sizes, plus one genuine release-scope sample count in the 11,739-gene atlas, gives a workable picture of how large the release is and what it contains. The counting is scope-disciplined rather than inflated: notes states explicitly that the portal figures are cumulative across quarterly releases, and sampling_strategies.source_caveats explains why the 464 and 563 protein counts from earlier releases are not carried over, citing identical file sizes but different MD5 checksums for the regenerated image archives. Per-modality release-scope counts (images, cells, interactions) remain unstated; recorded as a warning. subsets.is_data_split is absent, which is appropriate for a release that defines no train/test partition. The file_count arithmetic sums to the declared total_file_count of 10.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: None of the four fields is present: no variables block, no is_tabular flag, and no subsets block carrying is_data_split or is_subpopulation. No data dictionary, no column-level documentation and no structural flags anywhere in the record, even though the AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq archives are tabular quantitative outputs whose interpretation depends entirely on knowing their fields. This is the same gap scored under Element 3 sub-element 4, which the source rubric assigns to both items; it is scored in each because each asks a different question of it, composition here and interoperability there. No substitute evidence exists elsewhere in the record: instances describes modalities, not variables.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances: four entries each carrying a data_topic and data_substrate code (B2AI_TOPIC:15 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:56 for imaging, B2AI_TOPIC:28 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:59 for SEC-MS, B2AI_TOPIC:26 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:58 for AP-MS, B2AI_TOPIC:12 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:64 for perturb-seq), with prose naming triple-negative breast cancer, paclitaxel and vorinostat treatment, and iPSC differentiation to NPCs, neurons and cardiomyocytes; description names cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders as the disease areas Topics are given both as controlled Bridge2AI ontology codes and as detailed prose, down to the staining channels of the imaging instances (DAPI nuclei, calreticulin ER, tubulin microtubules, target protein). Conditions represented are enumerated exhaustively. The four coded instances map one-to-one onto the four modalities in the description, in file_collections and in acquisition_methods, with no modality claimed in one place and absent in another. The disease framing in the description is consistent with the targeted protein selection described in sampling_strategies.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: sampling_strategies: is_sample true, is_random false, is_representative false, with a detailed strategies narrative (initially 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes, expanded; genome-scale screening of 11,739 expressed genes; 6 guide RNAs per gene) and a why_not_representative statement; missing_data_documentation gives missing_data_patterns (no computed cell maps, incompletely overlapping protein panels across the three modalities, embargoed perturb-seq links, AP-MS only for treated MDA-MB-468), missing_data_causes (pre-publication embargo, interim Beta release of an ongoing project) and a handling_strategy Two of the three listed paths are populated with substantive, specific content. The missing-data documentation is genuinely useful: it names each absence, attributes a cause to it and states what the project will do about it, which is more than most records manage. The sampling flags are consistent with known_biases, which records both representation_bias and selection_bias with matching wording, and with discouraged_uses, which warns against generalising to the population at large. The anomalies slot is empty and no anomaly documentation exists elsewhere; scored 1 on the strength of the other two paths, with the anomalies gap scored separately and directly under Element 9 sub-element 3.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; version_access.versions_available lists 'Version 2.0 (current): June 2026 Data Release (Beta)' An explicit version string, corroborated in two other fields, and qualified by a maturity status that tells a user this is a Beta release. version '2.0', the citation's 'V2' and version_access agree. The record also discloses that sibling releases carry their own independent version numbers (October 2025 at 2.1, June 2025 at 2.1, March 2025 at 1.4), so version numbers are per-release repository versions rather than a single monotonic project series; disclosing this avoids a real misreading.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.versions_available lists five releases each with its DOI; version_access.version_details: 'Quarterly releases are published as separate Dataverse datasets, each with its own DOI and its own internal version history; within a release, minor and major version updates are recorded by the repository and files are not removed from previously published versions. Software packages used to produce each release are versioned, and the version used to produce a dataset is referenced in that dataset's metadata.' A user can reach any prior version by DOI, and the versioning model is explained at two levels, across releases and within a release. The commitment that files are never removed from published versions is a concrete reproducibility guarantee. The five DOIs listed agree with the four is_new_version_of targets in related_datasets plus the current release. The statement that software versions are referenced in each dataset's metadata is a claim about the RO-Crate contents that this record does not itself demonstrate, which is noted under Element 8 sub-element 4.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: updates.update_details states what future releases will add ('computed cell maps, iPSC immunofluorescence images, and further AP-MS interactomes'); source_caveats records concrete changes against the prior release: AP-MS archives for treated MDA-MB-468 are now included where the portal marked them 'coming soon', the perturb-seq external links are now embargoed where June 2025 listed SRA links, and 'the three immunofluorescence image archives in the June 2026 release report the same file sizes as those in the October 2025 release but different MD5 checksums, indicating the archives were regenerated'; retention_limit states files are not removed from previously published versions Release-to-release change information is present and unusually concrete, including a checksum-level observation that the image archives were regenerated. Combined with the forward-looking update_details, a user can tell both what changed and what is coming. The errata slot is empty and there is no consolidated changelog, so the change information has to be assembled from source_caveats rather than read in one place; recorded as a warning. The changes described are consistent with missing_data_documentation and with the external_resources embargo entries.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Quarterly'; updates.update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'; collection_timeframes repeats that 'data collection and release continue on a quarterly basis through the end of the project in November 2026' A stated cadence, a stated horizon and a stated end date, corroborated across two fields. A user can plan around the release schedule. The quarterly cadence is corroborated by the observed release history in version_access: March 2025, June 2025, October 2025 and June 2026, which is roughly but not exactly quarterly, with a gap between October 2025 and June 2026 that the record does not explain. The November 2026 project end sits slightly after the NIH RePORTER project period end of 2026-08-31 recorded in collection_timeframes; a minor unreconciled difference between sources, not a contradiction the record asserts.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: four entries covering the two cell lines with RRIDs, source_type and access_details (ATCC; HipSci via simple MTA), the raw mass-spectrometry files deposited in MassIVE, and the raw single-cell sequence data with its embargo status; conforms_to describes an 'end-to-end provenance record expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology'; updates.update_details and notes carry release-scope derivation information; related_datasets records the derivation lineage from four prior releases Provenance is documented at three levels: the biological source material with persistent identifiers and access routes, the raw instrument data with its repository deposits, and the release lineage. The RO-Crate provenance graph is named as the machine-readable form. was_derived_from is not used, but raw_data_sources and the related_datasets lineage carry the same content in a more detailed form, which is what the source rubric's field list contemplates. The notes and update_details credited here carry actual release and derivation information rather than unrelated commentary. The MassIVE deposits named here agree with the external_resources archival entries.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four entries, including 'To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning' and 'To stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems that are informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than being black boxes'; addressing_gaps: three entries naming the black-box problem in genomics, the uncharted state of subcellular architecture and the separate application of complementary mapping technologies, and the absence of an agreed operational definition of AI-readiness Purpose and the research gap it answers are both articulated, and the gaps are stated as specific deficiencies in the field rather than as generic aspiration. The fourth gap, the lack of a definition of AI-readiness, is an unusually precise motivating claim. Purposes align with the funding: an NIH Bridge2AI data generation award, and the stated aims are data generation and AI-readiness rather than hypothesis testing, which matches the award mechanism. They also align with tasks and with intended_uses without merely repeating them.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
