text: tasks: three entries (construction of hierarchical multi-scale cell maps by integrating protein-protein interaction and imaging data; training and evaluation of visible machine learning systems including visible neural networks for interpretable genotype-phenotype prediction; interpretation of genetic variants against a structured representation of cellular components); other_tasks: two entries covering proteome-wide complex mapping and differential elution analysis, and integrative structure modelling of protein communities ranked by available structural information from the PDB, AlphaFold DB, crosslinking mass spectrometry and disorder prediction Tasks are specific and technically concrete, naming model classes (VNNs), integration targets and the secondary analyses each individual data stream supports independently of the cell-map objective. Technical terms are used correctly throughout. The distinction between tasks that require the integrated cell maps and other_tasks that the individual released streams support is drawn accurately, and it matches the discouraged_uses warning that this release is 'most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets'.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: three grantors - 'National Institutes of Health' with two grant entries, 'National Institutes of Health, Bridge2AI Bridge Center' with one grant entry, and 'Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia' with a note that it is 'Named in the project preprint as a funder of the work, alongside the NIH awards; no grant identifier is given' Three distinct funders are named, the mechanism is identifiable from the award numbers (an OT2 other-transaction award and a U54 centre award), and the unnumbered philanthropic funder is recorded as such rather than omitted. The absence of a grants block for the Frederick Thomas Fund is correctly handled: non-grant or unnumbered support does not require a grant number, and the record states explicitly that none is given rather than leaving the reader to wonder. Funders align with purposes, an NIH Bridge2AI data-generation programme producing AI-ready data.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants notes record 'Award number 1OT2OD032742-01' and 'NIH RePORTER core project number OT2OD032742 ... application 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2, awarded to the University of California, San Diego with Trey Ideker as principal investigator, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, fiscal year 2025 award amount 5,289,382'; funders[1].grants notes record 'Award 5U54HG012513-02' Four award identifiers with full NIH structure, plus the application number, awardee institution, principal investigator, project period and award amount. This is substantially more than the sub-element asks for. All award numbers match NIH pattern for their stated agency. OT2OD032742 parses as activity code OT2, administering institute OD, serial 032742; 1OT2OD032742-01 adds application type 1 and support year 01; 3OT2OD032742-01S2 is a type-3 supplement to the same project; 5U54HG012513-02 parses as a type-5 non-competing U54 centre award from NHGRI, consistent with its stated Bridge2AI Bridge Center grantor. The project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 is consistent with the collection_timeframes entry. The only defect is representational: the award numbers occupy notes while the grant id slots hold non-resolvable DOI fragments; recorded as a low-severity correctness issue.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: 47 entries, 38 with ORCIDs and 9 with locally minted identifiers whose notes carry the name and institution; five entries carry affiliations as ROR:0153tk833; maintainers: three entries naming Trey Ideker as point of contact and PI, Swathi Thaker as programme manager with email, and the UVA Dataverse as archival steward; citation lists all 47 authors; data_governance.stewardship_roles names five further contact roles with emails Attribution is thorough and machine-actionable where possible: persistent researcher identifiers for four fifths of the author list, institutional affiliations, distinct maintainer and stewardship roles with contact addresses, and full acknowledgement of the three funders. The nine authors without ORCIDs are handled transparently, with source_caveats explaining that they 'carry no ORCID in the bundle and are recorded with fragment identifiers minted on the release DOI, their names and affiliations held in notes'. The same caveat explains that the ROR URL appears in place of an institution name for five UVA authors. ORCID and ROR identifiers are well-formed; the minted DOI fragments do not resolve, recorded as a low-severity issue. The creator list is consistent with the citation and with the ethical_reviews contact ORCID.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: four entries - AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines with '17 genes in MDA-MB-468 ... with 34 additional genes in progress'; SEC-MS across three MDA-MB-468 conditions and the iPSC derivatives; immunofluorescence 'using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols implemented on a pipetting robot ... followed by confocal microscopy in four colour channels'; single-cell CRISPR screens 'using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 lines engineered to express inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit'; supported by collection_timeframes (two entries) and data_collectors (four institutions with roles) Collection settings are described at the level a methods section would use: reagent sources, automation, channel counts, library design, guide multiplicity, the dCas9 induction system and the specific commercial readout kit. Which laboratory performed which modality is stated. Mechanisms map one-to-one onto the four acquisition_methods and the four instances, and the institutional attributions in data_collectors match those in file_collections, where imaging is credited to the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and SEC-MS to the Krogan laboratory at UCSF. Technical terminology is used correctly throughout.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: four entries each with was_directly_observed: true and was_reported_by_subjects: false, covering AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, SEC-MS 'used as an orthogonal mass spectrometry-based approach to AP-MS', immunofluorescence staining with Human Protein Atlas antibodies followed by confocal microscopy, and single-cell CRISPR interference screens; raw_data_sources: four entries naming the source material with RRIDs and the repository deposits of the raw instrument files Both listed paths are populated. Instruments and assay platforms are named, the observational status of each method is flagged, and the raw inputs behind the released archives are identified with their own access routes. The was_reported_by_subjects: false flags are semantically correct for cell-line assays and are consistent with direct_collection.is_direct: false. Describing SEC-MS as orthogonal to AP-MS is a correct methodological characterisation. The MassIVE deposits named in raw_data_sources agree with the external_resources archival entries.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: four entries (node2vec PPI embedding, Human Protein Atlas image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection), each carrying a source_caveat that it is a MuSIC pipeline step and that 'the June 2026 release states that computed cell maps are not included in this release', the first adding 'so this step was not applied to the artifacts distributed here'. labeling_strategies: one entry (GO and Reactome alignment plus LLM naming with confidence scores), caveated 'This annotation procedure applies to the computed cell maps, which the June 2026 release states are not included in this release.' cleaning_strategies: two entries, the first caveated as describing the MuSIC pipeline, the second reading in full 'Data generated by the acquisition modules undergo quality control before release; the project preprint records that single-cell CRISPR screen data were being quality controlled at the time of writing.' annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are absent. By the record's own repeated statement, almost all of the processing documentation describes a pipeline that was not applied to the distributed artifacts. What remains applicable to this release is one unspecific sentence about quality control by the acquisition modules, with no procedure, threshold or criterion. Three of the five file_collections are typed collection_type: processed_data, so the released AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq archives were processed, yet the record describes no search or quantification step for the mass-spectrometry outputs, no alignment, guide assignment or filtering for the perturb-seq outputs, and no image processing for the imaging archives. A reader cannot replicate or understand how the released files were produced. This is a content-accuracy failure rather than an absence: well-formed, detailed content is present but is scoped by the record itself to outputs outside this release. Scored 0 because the sub-element asks about the preprocessing of the data being documented. The record deserves credit for disclosing the mismatch in six separate source_caveats rather than presenting the MuSIC pipeline as this release's provenance, and that candour is what makes the gap diagnosable; it does not fill it.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Slots examined for software evidence: no used_software is attached to preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies or any other property; machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are absent. Software that is named appears in preprocessing_strategies (node2vec, a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model, contrastive deep learning, community detection), cleaning_strategies ('the FAIRSCAPE client package to validate inputs and to create the output RO-Crate package'), labeling_strategies (an unnamed 'large language model approach'), external_resources (Cell Mapping Toolkit at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, fairscape.github.io, integrativemodeling.org), data_collectors ('AI-readiness packaging ... using the FAIRSCAPE framework') and collection_mechanisms (the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit). No software is named in a producing or transforming role for the data being distributed, so a reader cannot tell what made the released files. Every named item falls into an excluded role: FAIRSCAPE performs packaging, provenance-metadata production and input validation, roles (c) and (d); the UVA Dataverse is hosting and serving, role (b); the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is a capture reagent at acquisition, role (a); and node2vec, the HPA embedding model, the contrastive co-embedding, community detection, the Cell Mapping Toolkit and the Integrative Modeling Platform all belong to pipelines the record itself states produced outputs not in this release or that consume the release downstream, role (e). No version number is given for any named software. Scored 0 under the #1059/#1082 threshold: nothing is named in a producing or transforming role, and the roles that are documented are (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e). The gap is sharpened by version_access.version_details, which asserts that 'Software packages used to produce each release are versioned, and the version used to produce a dataset is referenced in that dataset's metadata' - a claim that the producing software is recorded inside the RO-Crates, which this datasheet does not surface. Naming the mass-spectrometry search software, the single-cell processing software and the image-handling software, with versions, would satisfy this sub-element.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: five groups covering two preprints with full author lists and DOIs (10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 with PMCID PMC11580897), four MassIVE deposits and a Figshare deposit, the two embargoed perturb-seq links with restrictions, the CM4AI portal and data-releases pages, and four tool and documentation links; conforms_to names RO-Crate, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, JSON-LD, RDF-XML, JSON-Schema and ARK identifiers Two of the three listed paths are populated richly. A reader is pointed to the describing literature, to the mirror deposits of the raw data, to the project documentation and to the tooling, with archival flags distinguishing durable from ephemeral resources. The DOIs are well-formed and the registrants are plausible (10.1101 bioRxiv, 10.1038 Springer Nature) and the PMCID is well-formed. imputation_protocols is absent and is not documented as unused, which matters because missing values are routine in the mass-spectrometry and single-cell outputs this release distributes; recorded as a low-severity issue rather than scored here, since the two other paths carry the sub-element.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: five typed entries - scope_limitation (interim release without predicted cell maps, with a recommended_mitigation pointing users to a later release or to the Cell Mapping Toolkit), coverage_limitation (the three modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap', with a scope_impact noting analyses are limited to the intersection), temporal_limitation (pre-publication embargo on the perturb-seq external links), methodological_limitation ('Meaningful analysis of these data requires domain expertise') and a second coverage_limitation (imaging covers only MDA-MB-468; iPSC images forthcoming) Five limitations, each typed from a vocabulary, several carrying an explicit mitigation or a statement of analytical impact. These are real constraints that would change how a user plans an analysis, not defensive boilerplate. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the cell-map absence in missing_data_documentation and in the preprocessing caveats, the embargo in external_resources and third_party_sharing, the incomplete panel overlap in missing_data_patterns, and the expertise requirement in discouraged_uses. No limitation is asserted here and contradicted there.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: two entries with bias_type values from the enumerated taxonomy - representation_bias, described as data 'derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines [that] do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', with affected_subsets naming both donor-derived lines and their donor demographics; and selection_bias, describing targeted rather than random selection of proteins and genes, with a mitigation_strategy citing the extension to a genome-scale screen of 11,739 genes; future_use_impacts: three entries including generalisation risk for models trained on these data and the Ethics module's governance framework Both entries use enumerated bias types, both explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the category, one carries a concrete mitigation, and the downstream social-impact dimension is covered in future_use_impacts. Bias categorisation is semantically correct: two donor lines is genuinely a representation problem, and a targeted protein panel is genuinely a selection problem. The representation_bias wording matches sampling_strategies.why_not_representative verbatim and is consistent with is_representative: false, so the taxonomy label and the underlying sampling description agree.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: The anomalies field is absent. No other field documents anomalies in the data that are present: known_limitations addresses scope, coverage, embargo and required expertise; missing_data_documentation addresses what is absent; sampling_strategies addresses how the panels were chosen. Nothing tells a user what is wrong with the data they will download. For a release combining confocal imaging, two mass-spectrometry modalities and single-cell sequencing, the expected content is substantial: antibody specificity failures or excluded targets, image quality exclusions, failed or outlier mass-spectrometry runs, batch effects across conditions, and cell or guide filtering thresholds in the perturb-seq screens. None of it appears. The one quality observation the record does make, that the June 2026 image archives share file sizes with the October 2025 archives but carry different MD5 checksums, is a packaging-integrity observation recorded in source_caveats for provenance reasons rather than an account of anomalies in the data content, and it is credited under Element 6 sub-element 3. The related claim in cleaning_strategies that acquisition-module data 'undergo quality control before release' asserts that quality control happened without reporting what it found.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements[0].sensitive_elements_present: false, with sensitivity_details: 'The release records no human subjects and de-identified samples; the released content consists of laboratory measurements on commercially available human cell lines (immunofluorescence images, mass spectrometry-derived interaction data and single-cell sequencing summaries) rather than personal identifiers or protected health information.' An explicit negative determination accompanied by a reason: the record states what the content actually is and why that content is not sensitive, rather than leaving an empty field or an unexplained false. Per the instrument, an explicit false flag with reasoning is meaningful documentation. Consistent with is_deidentified, with human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false and with confidentiality_level: unrestricted. content_warnings is absent, which is appropriate where no sensitive content is identified. The determination is plausible for the data types named, subject to the genotype-linkage caveat recorded under Element 4 sub-element 2.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews[0] describes the CM4AI Ethics module's Value-Sensitive Design methodology, 'an axiological repository of values, and a CM4AI Life Cycle framework elucidating governance milestones throughout data generation and AI system development', plus mixed qualitative and quantitative empirical research to capture community insights, with reviewing_organization and contact_person; future_use_impacts: three entries covering non-generalisation of models trained on two cell lines, the Ethics module's integration of anticipated applications into governance frameworks 'to optimize benefits, mitigate potential risks and promote use for the collective good', and clinical or patient-care application without regulatory oversight as an identified foreseeable misuse Both halves of the sub-element are substantive. The social-impact analysis is not generic: it names a specific foreseeable misuse, a specific generalisation risk tied to the dataset's own composition, and a governance apparatus with named deliverables. The foreseeable-misuse statement in future_use_impacts is consistent with the matching prohibited_uses entry and with the clinical-oversight constraint in regulatory_restrictions, three fields agreeing on the same risk. The generalisation impact is consistent with known_biases representation_bias. Conflicts of interest are not addressed, a minor gap within the sub-element's scope.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; description states the data 'are archived in the University of Virginia Dataverse'; maintainers names 'University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), School of Medicine collection'; retention_limit commits to 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse'; the DOI prefix 10.18130 is the UVA Dataverse registrant The hosting platform is a recognised institutional Dataverse repository and is identified unambiguously by five independent fields plus the DOI prefix, together with an explicit long-term preservation commitment backed by institutional funds. The dedicated publisher slot is empty, and source_caveats justifies this on the ground that 'The bundle names no publisher for the release', which sits awkwardly against the record's own citation naming the UVA Dataverse in the publisher position; recorded as a medium-severity consistency issue. Scored 1 because the platform is identified beyond doubt by the fields the sub-element asks a reader to consult. Separately, notes discloses that the hosting collection 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', an availability risk worth reading alongside the preservation commitment.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: a complete formatted data citation listing all 47 authors, the year 2026, the title in quotation marks, 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license_and_use_terms.notes adds that 'community norms and good scientific practices expect proper credit to be given via citation, using the data citation shown on the dataset page' and that publications should cite both the related publication and the data collection directly A ready-to-use citation string in repository-standard form, a resolvable DOI, and explicit citation instructions covering the dual obligation to cite both the data and the describing paper. This is the complete set the rubric's note for Bridge2AI datasets calls for. The citation's DOI, repository and version agree with the doi, page and version fields. The DOI resolves under a registrant prefix consistent with the named repository.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to names RO-Crate with ARK persistent identifiers, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, JSON-LD and RDF-XML serialisations and JSON-Schema dataset schemas; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance cites compliance with the FAIR Principles for data and software as an NIH requirement Conformance is asserted against five recognised community standards spanning packaging, provenance, serialisation, schema and identifier practice, plus the FAIR Principles. Each is named specifically enough to be checked. The standards named are real, current and used in the roles they actually serve; the combination of RO-Crate packaging with an EVI provenance graph in JSON-LD is coherent rather than a list of buzzwords. The w3id conforms_to_schema URI is well-formed and identifies the schema this record is written against.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: 'CM4AI project portal, including documentation, data releases, tools and training: https://cm4ai.org/', 'CM4AI data releases page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/', 'Cell Mapping Toolkit user documentation: https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/', 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, with tutorial and installation instructions: https://fairscape.github.io', 'Integrative Modeling Platform (IMP) package: http://integrativemodeling.org'; page gives the dataset landing page; maintainers gives a programme-management contact (snthaker@uab.edu) for project inquiries Documentation is linked at three levels: the project portal with training material, the tooling user documentation on readthedocs, and the framework tutorial and installation instructions, alongside the dataset landing page and a named human contact for inquiries. All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains, and the archival: false flag correctly marks these as project web resources rather than durable deposits. The distinction between archival and non-archival external resources is applied consistently across the five groups.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: seven entries, each with relationship_type, target_dataset DOI and name - is_new_version_of for doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX and doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5; is_described_by for doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; references for doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3 Every relationship is typed from a recognisable vocabulary and resolves to a DOI with a human-readable name. Three distinct relationship semantics are used, and each is the right one for its target. The typing is semantically careful. The Nature paper is typed references rather than is_described_by, and a source_caveat explains why: it 'reports a multimodal cell map of U2OS osteosarcoma cells ... it is a separate study rather than a description of the cell lines and conditions in this release'. The fourth is_new_version_of target carries a caveat declining to equate it with the portal's undated 'May 2024 Data Release' because no source makes that association. This is exactly the discrimination the sub-element rewards.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the record id, the doi field, the latest-version pointer and inside the citation string. Predecessor releases carry their own DOIs (10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, /F3TD5R, /B35XWX), so the identifier scheme is applied across the release series rather than to this record alone. Matches 10.XXXX/... ; prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) registrant and agrees with the page host dataverse.lib.virginia.edu and the citation's stated publisher. Cellosaurus RRIDs for the two source cell lines are additionally well formed.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description: ~1,100 characters naming the three modalities, both cell lines, the treatment and differentiation conditions, the ten ZIP archives, the distribution channel, and the interim status Well above the 200-character threshold and specific rather than promotional: it enumerates what is in the release (perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence, by cell line and condition) and, unusually, what is not ('computed cell maps are not included') and what is embargoed. Description content matches the file_collections tree modality-for-modality; no claim in the description is contradicted by the file listing. The title's 'June 2026' is consistent with issued: 2026-06-17 under the adjudication recorded in source_caveats.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: 30 terms including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, CRISPR/Cas9, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, paclitaxel, vorinostat, protein-protein interaction, subcellular imaging, Bridge2AI, CM4AI Far exceeds the five-keyword expectation and spans four retrieval axes: assay/method, cell line, perturbagen, and programme. Synonym pairs are supplied deliberately (mass spectroscopy/SEC-MS, scRNAseq/single-cell RNA sequencing, NPC/neural progenitor cell), which materially helps discovery. Every keyword is instantiated somewhere in the record's content; none is aspirational. 'Bridge2AI' and 'CM4AI' supply the programme context used elsewhere in this evaluation, read from keywords and funders rather than from the filename.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C ; file_collections: six named collections containing ten resources with ids, names, formats, checksums and issue dates Both halves of the sub-element are satisfied: a resolvable DOI-parameterised landing page, and a genuine hierarchy in which archives are grouped by modality (AP-MS, IF, SEC-MS, perturb-seq atlas, perturb-seq raw, metadata) with per-collection file_count and description. The landing-page URL embeds the same persistent identifier declared in doi/id, so the two discovery routes resolve to one object. Collection ids are minted as fragment identifiers under the dataset DOI, a coherent local scheme.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: relationship_type: is_new_version_of, target_dataset: doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, with a note explaining the delta; version_access.versions_available lists five releases with DOIs The relationship is typed, points at a resolvable DOI, and is accompanied by substantive content about what the newer release adds. The five-release enumeration lets a user walk the whole series. No parent_datasets entry is given, but the release-series relationship is the meaningful structure here. is_new_version_of is semantically correct for a quarterly release series where each release receives its own DOI; the target DOI shares the registrant prefix, consistent with sibling deposits in the same repository.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 prose with attribution, non-commercial and share-alike conditions and a citation obligation; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; contact_person: Trey Ideker (ORCID:0000-0002-1708-8454); ip_restrictions.restrictions: commercial use requires separate negotiation with UCSD/Stanford/UCSF; copyright held by the Regents of the University of California except raw spatial-proteomics images (Stanford) Not a bare licence label: the terms are spelled out, the commercial pathway is named with the institutions to approach, and copyright is apportioned per data package. A user can determine both what they may do and whom to contact to do more. The three statements are mutually consistent (NC licence, no_commercial_use enum, negotiated commercial licence). The record discloses that the IP detail comes from the preprint and earlier release pages rather than the June 2026 page — a provenance caveat, not a contradiction.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: data_governance.committee_name: Data Governance Committee; data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker, ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu, UC San Diego; human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance: 'Human Subjects: No' and 'FDA Regulated: No'; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: true with embargo detail; sensitive_elements_present: false The governance-contact limb of this sub-element is satisfied precisely: a named committee, a named contact with ORCID, institutional email and affiliation. Regulatory status is stated affirmatively in both directions (not human-subjects, not FDA-regulated), and confidentiality is classified at the component level via the embargo record. No regulatory_restrictions block or confidentiality_level enum is present, so the classification is expressed in prose and in confidential_elements rather than in the schema's dedicated slots. HIPAA compliance is neither claimed nor needed, which is semantically correct for non-clinical cell-line data; an unexplained HIPAA claim here would have been the error.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats.notes: 'The dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP; individual files below the 1.9 GB web download limit may be selected from the files table, and the Dataverse Data Access API provides programmatic access. MD5 checksums are published for each archive.' page: the Dataverse dataset landing page No download_url field is present, but the sub-element's stated scope admits platform access instructions, and what is given is unusually actionable: it warns that whole-dataset download will fail, states the per-file size ceiling that governs the web route, names the API route for the 4.6 GB image archives that exceed it, and points at the checksums needed to verify a transfer. The instructions are consistent with the file sizes recorded in file_collections (three IF archives at 3.8-4.6 GB, all above the stated 1.9 GB web limit), so the guidance is not boilerplate — it correctly anticipates the failure mode this specific release presents. Scored 1 on that content; a dedicated download_url would still be preferable for machine access.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip; each of the ten resources carries format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip, compression: zip, file_type (data_file/metadata_file), md5 and issued The distribution question — in what form does the repository hand the data over — is answered completely and per file, with a registered MIME type, a file-type role distinguishing the metadata archive from the nine data archives, and an integrity checksum for each. application/zip is the correct IANA media type for the declared container, and compression: zip is consistent with it. The limitation is scope rather than correctness: the container is specified, the contents are not — assessed under Element 3 sub-element 2, where internal format matters for reuse.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: typed link to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM; external_resources: five entries — the CM4AI preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), the project portal https://cm4ai.org/, the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas on Figshare, the Cell Mapping Toolkit on GitHub/Zenodo, and FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io; raw_sources names four MassIVE deposits Links span the full ecosystem a reuser needs: the methods publication, the project portal, the external repositories holding the raw mass-spectrometry and perturbation data, the processing toolkit and the packaging framework. Each carries a note stating what the resource is for. Domains and identifier forms are all plausible and match the named services (bioRxiv DOI prefix 10.1101, github.io for FAIRSCAPE docs). The MassIVE deposits are described but not given as accession numbers, which weakens machine-resolvability without affecting the score.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material provided they give appropriate credit ... may not use the material for commercial purposes ... must distribute contributions under the same license' A named standard licence with its permissions and conditions restated, plus the attribution and citation obligation. Reuse is permitted for non-commercial research without further permission, which is the question this sub-element asks. The share-alike and non-commercial conditions are correctly stated for CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and the statement that no additional legal or technological restrictions may be applied matches the licence text. The parallel commercial-negotiation route in ip_restrictions is compatible with, not contradictory to, an NC licence.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip (identical for all ten resources); no encoding field on any resource; file_collections.source_caveats: 'the June 2026 file listing carries no per-file descriptions' ZIP is a container, not a data format. The record never states what a reuser will find inside — whether the mass-spectrometry archives hold mzML or vendor-native files, whether the 4.6 GB image archives hold OME-TIFF or PNG, whether the perturb-seq atlas is h5ad, MTX or CSV. Character encoding is absent throughout. The interoperability question this sub-element asks therefore goes unanswered, even though the distribution question in Element 2 is answered well. Distinct from Element 2 sub-element 4 by design: that item asks how the data is handed over (ZIP, application/zip, checksummed — answered), this one asks whether the data is in standardised, harmonisable form (unanswerable from the record). The record's own caveat that per-file descriptions are absent confirms the gap is real rather than an artefact of where evidence sits.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC ontology codes Conformance is stated at three levels — packaging standard (RO-Crate), metadata schema (the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema, by w3id URI), and controlled vocabulary for instance substrates and topics. A dedicated release metadata archive is distributed alongside the data, so the claim is backed by a deliverable. RO-Crate is the appropriate packaging standard for the provenance-graph claim, and FAIRSCAPE is correctly characterised as the framework that produces it; the w3id URI is a persistent-identifier form appropriate for a schema reference. No domain data standard (e.g. mzML, OME, PSI-MI) is claimed, consistent with the unspecified internal formats noted above.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field anywhere in the record; file_collections.resources carry identity and integrity metadata (id, name, format, md5) but no column, channel or field descriptions There is no variable-level metadata of any kind: no data dictionary, no column names, no units, no identifier scheme for linking the SEC-MS elution profiles, AP-MS interactions and perturb-seq expression matrices to one another or to external resources. This is the clearest reuse gap in the record and is compounded by the absence of internal format documentation. The gap is consequential precisely because the stated purpose is multimodal integration: known_limitations already concedes that the modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets, and without shared identifiers a reuser cannot determine the overlap themselves.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: four categories including 'AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics', 'AI model training', 'Analysis of cell architectural changes and interactions in the presence of specific disease processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations'; prohibited_uses.prohibition_reason: 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; existing_uses cites a bioRxiv analysis with PMCID Both directions are covered, and the prohibition is reasoned rather than asserted — it names the context (clinical decision-making, patient care) and the condition under which it could change (regulatory oversight and approval). The existing-use citation shows the intended uses are realised, not hypothetical. The clinical prohibition is semantically appropriate and consistent with sensitive_elements ('data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures') and with the absence of FDA regulation: the record restricts a use its data type cannot support. No discouraged_uses are given, a minor omission.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: two named ethics contacts of record — Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153, jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca), both 'per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record'; data_governance.committee_name/committee_contact: Data Governance Committee, Jillian Parker (UC San Diego); human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with regulatory_compliance 'Human Subjects: No', 'FDA Regulated: No' For a dataset with no human participants, the meaningful oversight documentation is exactly this: an explicit human-subjects determination, a standing governance committee with a reachable contact, and named individuals accountable for ethics review — all with ORCIDs and institutional emails, so the accountability is verifiable rather than nominal. What is absent is any account of what the ethics review found or decided, and no data_protection_impacts assessment is recorded. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is false, so no IRB protocol number is expected and its absence is not a defect. The ethics contacts also appear in creators with matching ORCIDs, so the identities reconcile internally; the Ravitsky affiliation/email-domain mismatch is disclosed in source_caveats rather than papered over.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; deidentification_details: 'The release record answers "De-identified Samples: Yes". The project preprint states that CM4AI data are non-clinical, from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' The statement is reasoned and attributed to two sources rather than asserted as a flag, and it supplies the basis of the claim — non-clinical tissue-culture origin plus non-matchability under current knowledge, the latter appropriately hedged. Supporting provenance in raw_data_sources identifies both lines by Cellosaurus RRID with their donor descriptions, so a reader can assess the claim independently. No formal standard (Safe Harbor, expert determination, k-anonymity) is named, but none of those workflows applies to established commercial cell lines. Method appropriateness check passes: invoking HIPAA Safe Harbor for cell-line data would have been the semantic error, and the record avoids it. The claim is consistent with sensitive_elements_present: false and with involves_human_subjects: false. The residual re-identification vector for cell lines — genomic profile matching — is not discussed, which is the hedge the record's 'with current knowledge' phrasing gestures at without analysing.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: No participant_privacy or reidentification_risk fields; none expected, as the release contains no participant data Excluded from the denominator. Scoring 0 here would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation: there are no participants whose privacy could be protected.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: No informed_consent field; the cell lines were obtained from third-party repositories (ATCC, HipSci) whose own donor consent governs upstream Excluded from the denominator. Donor consent for MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J is a matter for the originating repositories, not for this redistribution of derived measurements.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: No at_risk_populations or participant_compensation fields; no participants were enrolled or compensated Excluded from the denominator. No at-risk population is enrolled; the donor characteristics that are disclosed (in known_biases and raw_data_sources) are treated as a representativeness matter and assessed under Element 9.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: known_biases.affected_subsets: 'MDA-MB-468, a triple negative breast cancer line established from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and KOLF2.1J, an iPSC line derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'; raw_data_sources: both lines with RRIDs, characterisation status and source repositories; description: treatment arms (untreated / paclitaxel / vorinostat) and differentiation states (undifferentiated iPSC, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte) The analogue of a cohort here is the set of cell lines, treatment arms and differentiation states, and all three are described concretely, with donor demographics for each line and the disease context that makes them relevant. A reuser can tell exactly which biological populations are represented and which are not. No subpopulations slot and no subsets flags are populated, so the content sits in known_biases and raw_data_sources; it is specific and non-boilerplate, and the donor-level detail is what the sub-element is asking for. Credited on content, with the structural gap noted as a weakness.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: five entries giving instance_type, data_substrate and data_topic but no counts; notes reports project-level figures (1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins, 11,739 genes, 21.4 TB) which source_caveats reads as cumulative project-wide holdings by inference, 'but that reading is an inference and the portal does not state it'; sampling_strategies.source_caveats declines to assert the 200-gene and 523-protein figures for this release No count of instances is stated for the ten archives actually distributed here: not images, not cells, not proteins, not interactions. Only file-level counts (ten archives, sizes from 30.2 KB to 4.6 GB) are release-specific. The record is commendably honest that the available figures cannot be attributed to this release, but honesty about an absence does not supply the number. The conflict the record surfaces — 523 proteins on the portal versus 464 on the October 2025 release page for same-named archives — confirms that no reliable per-release count exists in the sources, and that the differing MD5s mean the October figures cannot simply be carried over.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: No variables, no is_tabular, no subsets.is_data_split, no subsets.is_subpopulation anywhere in the record All four evidence routes for this sub-element are empty. Nothing describes the internal structure of any archive, whether any component is tabular, or whether any subset plays a training/test or subpopulation role — a notable omission for a release whose stated purpose is supplying AI-ready training data. Consistent with the absence of internal format documentation found under Element 3: the record documents the release at package granularity throughout and never descends to the record or field level.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances: five typed entries each with an ontology-coded substrate and topic — immunofluorescence confocal images (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 / B2AI_TOPIC:19), SEC-MS elution profiles (59/28), AP-MS interaction measurements (58/26), single-cell CRISPRi perturbation profiles (64/34), raw single-cell read sets (63/34); description gives the disease and perturbation context Each modality is described in a sentence that states what the measurement is of and in which cells and condition, and is bound to controlled vocabulary codes on two axes. The conditions represented — triple-negative breast cancer with two drug perturbations, iPSC with lineage differentiation — are clear from description and keywords. The five instance types map one-to-one onto the six file collections (the metadata archive aside), so the topical description and the distributed content agree. Substrate and topic codes are used consistently, with the two perturb-seq entries correctly sharing topic 34 while differing in substrate (processed profile versus raw read set).

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: sampling_strategies: two entries — targeted selection of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes in disease-relevant lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions (is_sample: true, is_random: false), and expressed genome-scale CRISPRi in KOLF2.1J covering 11,739 targeted genes (is_sample: false) — each with source_caveats delimiting what the sources actually support Sampling is documented substantively, including the non-random targeted design that shapes what the data can support, and the caveats tell a reuser which reported figures are release-specific and which are not. Against that, anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent: nothing addresses failed acquisitions, image or spectrum QC exclusions, or missing values in the atlas. is_random: false is correct for a curated 200-gene target list, and the is_sample: false on the genome-scale entry is flagged by the record as its own inference from 'expressed genome-scale', which is the right level of hedging. Credited on the strength of the sampling documentation; the anomaly and missing-data limbs are unmet and are reflected in the recommendations.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' A concrete version number that agrees with the version recorded in the citation string, and a maturity status (Beta) that is reinforced by the description's 'explicitly interim' framing. A user citing this release can pin exactly what they used. Consistent across version, citation and version_access. Note that neighbouring releases carry Dataverse versions 2.1 and 1.4 under different DOIs, so version numbers are per-deposit rather than a project-wide sequence — the record's enumeration makes this legible rather than confusing.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; versions_available: five entries (June 2026 /HIGT4C v2.0; October 2025 /K7TGEM v2.1; June 2025 /F3TD5R v2.1; March 2025 /B35XWX v1.4; May 2024); version_details: 'CM4AI issues quarterly data releases, each deposited in the University of Virginia Dataverse under its own DOI and separately versioned within Dataverse' Prior versions are not merely mentioned but individually addressable: each is given with its DOI and its Dataverse version, and the governing convention is explained, so a user can retrieve any earlier release rather than only the current one. The two-level scheme (release DOI plus in-Dataverse version) is described accurately and the latest-version pointer matches this record's own DOI. Only the May 2024 release lacks a DOI, a small gap in an otherwise complete lineage.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: No errata field; updates.update_details is wholly forward-looking ('will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'); the only comparative statement is in related_datasets.notes: 'The June 2026 release adds AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, which the October 2025 release did not include' There is no change log for this version and no errata. The single delta sentence describes a difference against a separate deposit under a different DOI, not what changed between Dataverse v1 and v2 of this DOI. Meanwhile the record itself surfaces three items an errata entry should carry and does not: description text carried forward from earlier releases with a stale '(2025-06-30)' stamp, three image archives published a month after the version date, and MD5s that differ from same-named October 2025 archives without explanation. Scored 0 on the change-documentation question specifically. The same discrepancy disclosures are credited under Element 9 sub-element 3, where the question is whether a user is warned of quality irregularities — a different question from whether the release documents its own changes and corrections.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Quarterly'; updates.update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis. The CM4AI project portal states that CM4AI releases data quarterly, ensuring continuous updates to the cell maps and input data streams.' Both a cadence and a horizon are given, with the end point tied to the project's conclusion. A user can judge both how often to re-check and when the series will stop growing. The quarterly claim is corroborated by the observed release history in version_access (March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, June 2026), which is broadly quarterly with one gap — consistent rather than contradicted. The November 2026 project end also sits close to the NIH project period ending 2026-08-31 recorded in funders.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419, from ATCC) and KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3, from HipSci under MTA); raw_sources: five raw deposits (three MassIVE SEC-MS/AP-MS sets, plus the in-release cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip); acquisition_methods includes a was_inferred_derived entry stating the KOLF2.1J atlas is a processed product of the co-distributed raw sequence archive; conforms_to: RO-Crate packaging 'with provenance graphs' Provenance runs from biological origin (named lines with RRIDs and their suppliers) through raw acquisition deposits (named repositories) to the derived product distributed here, with the derivation relationship stated explicitly for the atlas. A separate release metadata archive is distributed to carry the machine-readable provenance graphs. No was_derived_from slot is used, but the source rubric admits raw_data_sources and derivation prose as evidence, and both are substantive. The derivation claim is honestly labelled as inferred from paired archive names rather than read from a stated pipeline — a provenance caveat that slightly weakens, but does not negate, the chain. Release-specific notes were read from updates.update_details and notes, as the mapping requires.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: three entries — machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data from 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes; ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture; mapping spatiotemporal architecture toward interpretable genotype-phenotype learning. addressing_gaps: two entries on the black-box problem in genotype-phenotype models and on the absence of AI-Ready properties in existing biomedical data Motivation is stated at the level of a scientific problem, not a mission statement: the black-box character of genotype-phenotype prediction, and a definition of what AI-Ready requires (FAIR, known provenance, validated, machine-readable provenance graphs, explainable, ethically obtained). The purposes name the specific target sets and cell contexts, tying motivation to what was actually produced. Purposes align with the funding source: a Bridge2AI Data Generation Project funded to produce AI-ready data states exactly that goal, satisfying the funding-alignment consistency check. The 100+100 target protein sets in purposes match the targeted sampling strategy recorded under Element 5.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, in which predictions are traced to multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than produced by an opaque model'; 'Development of "visible" machine learning systems, including visible neural networks built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture' Two concrete ML tasks with a stated architectural commitment (visible neural networks over cell-architecture maps), specific enough that a reader can judge whether their own task is in scope. Tasks are consistent with intended_uses (AI model training, cellular process analysis) and with the known_limitations admission that the current release suits per-modality bioinformatics better than integrated analysis — the tasks are stated as project objectives, and the record does not overclaim that this interim release already achieves them.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health' with two awards and a note recording Trey Ideker (UC San Diego) as PI of the Bridge2AI CM4AI Data Generation Project per NIH RePORTER; grantor 'University of Virginia' with the Frederick Thomas Fund Both the federal funder and the institutional fund are named, with the award mechanism identifiable from the activity codes (OT2 Other Transaction for the data generation project, U54 for the Bridge Center) and the responsible PI recorded. The verification source (NIH RePORTER) is cited. Funding-logic check passes: the grantor is named and structured awards are supplied under funders.grants. The Frederick Thomas Fund is correctly represented as a named non-grant institutional fund with no numeric identifier, which is not a defect under the funding rule.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: grant_number '1OT2OD032742-01' with a note recording the RePORTER core project number OT2OD032742, application 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2 for FY2025, award amount 5,289,382 and project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31; grant_number '5U54HG012513-02' (Bridge2AI Bridge Center) Two fully specified award numbers including application type prefix, activity code, institute, serial and suffix, with the first cross-checked against an authoritative registry down to the supplement number and project period. Both parse correctly against NIH structure: 1-OT2-OD-032742-01 (type 1, OT2 Other Transaction, Office of the Director) and 5-U54-HG-012513-02 (type 5 non-competing continuation, U54 cooperative agreement centre, NHGRI). Institute codes are semantically apt — OD for the trans-NIH Bridge2AI Common Fund programme, HG for the genomics-led Bridge Center. The recorded project period is consistent with the November 2026 project end stated in updates.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: 47 named individuals, the large majority with ORCID identifiers and all with institutional affiliations spanning UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, University of Virginia, KTH, UAB, Yale, Simon Fraser, Montreal, Texas at Austin and Alabama; funders records institutional acknowledgement of the Frederick Thomas Fund; maintainers names the programme manager and website contact with emails Attribution is exhaustive and machine-resolvable: ORCIDs make the contributor list disambiguable, affiliations make the multi-institution structure visible, and the maintainer entries give a live route for project inquiries beyond the authorship list. The creator list reconciles with the citation string author-for-author, and with the separately named governance and ethics contacts (Parker, Ravitsky, Bélisle-Pipon) whose ORCIDs match their creator entries — an internal cross-reference that passes.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: four entries — AP-MS 'performed on endogenously tagged cell lines'; SEC-MS 'for proteome-wide protein complex and interaction mapping'; ICC-IF 'using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols established for the MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines'; single-cell CRISPRi 'performed using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit, with a CRISPR lentiviral library and cell lines expressing inducible dCas9' Each of the four modalities gets a mechanism description with the distinguishing experimental detail a reader needs to judge comparability: endogenous tagging for AP-MS, the antibody resource and automated staining protocol for imaging, the specific 10x chemistry and the inducible dCas9 system for the screens. Mechanisms map one-to-one onto the distributed modalities and use the terminology correctly (ICC-IF, dCas9 interference rather than knockout, size-exclusion chromatography upstream of MS). Settings are at protocol-family level; instrument models, acquisition parameters and timeframes are not given, which limits replication.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: a primary-measurement entry (was_directly_observed: true, was_reported_by_subjects: false) covering AP-MS, SEC-MS, confocal immunofluorescence and single-cell CRISPR screens, and a derived entry (was_inferred_derived: true) for the KOLF2.1J atlas; raw_data_sources: both cell lines with RRIDs and suppliers; raw_sources: five raw deposits in MassIVE and the in-release SRA archive Acquisition is documented on all three limbs the sub-element asks about — how measurements were made, what the material inputs were, and where the raw data underlying the released products can be obtained. The directly-observed and inferred-derived flags correctly separate primary measurement from downstream products. was_reported_by_subjects: false is consistent with the no-human-participants determination. MassIVE is the appropriate repository for raw mass spectrometry and SRA-format archives for sequencing, so the external deposit targets are semantically correct; accession numbers are not given, which weakens retrievability.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: a single entry stating that perturb-seq data are distributed both as a processed atlas and as raw sequence in separate archives, whose source_caveats reads 'Inferred from archive naming in the June 2026 file listing; that listing carries no per-file processing description'; no cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols The one preprocessing entry records that processing happened, not what it was — no alignment, guide assignment, QC filtering, normalisation, spectral search, image segmentation or annotation step is described for any modality, and the entry is explicitly an inference from two archive filenames. Four of the six evidence routes are entirely empty. The release therefore cannot be reproduced or audited at the processing level. The record is transparent about the gap rather than concealing it, and correctly notes that the computed cell maps produced by self-supervised multimodal embedding and multi-resolution community detection are not part of this release. Transparency about missing documentation does not substitute for the documentation.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Software named in the record: 'Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI data integration pipeline software ... via GitHub, with production-ready tools archived in Zenodo' (external_resources, notes: 'Software used to integrate CM4AI input data streams'); 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, https://fairscape.github.io' (notes: 'Framework used to package CM4AI data, software, metadata and provenance graphs'); conforms_to: RO-Crate 'produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'. No used_software on any preprocessing, cleaning, labeling or imputation entry; no machine_annotation_tools. Nothing named here produced or transformed the data being distributed. The Cell Mapping Toolkit integrates input streams into computed cell maps, and the record states in two places that those maps are not included in this release — role (e), a pipeline whose outputs are not what is shipped. FAIRSCAPE is packaging and provenance-metadata production over an already-formed release — role (c). The 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is reagent chemistry, not software. So the reader cannot tell what generated the SEC-MS elution profiles, the AP-MS interaction tables, the immunofluorescence image products or the KOLF2.1J cell atlas that the ten archives actually contain. Scored 0 under the #1059/#1082 threshold: software is prominently documented, with licences and archival DOIs, but occupies roles (c) and (e) rather than producing or transforming the released data. The GitHub and Zenodo pointers are to the publisher's toolkit rather than to a named per-modality processing tool with a version, so neither earns the point on its own.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: the CM4AI methods preprint (doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311) cited as the reference for this dataset, the project portal cm4ai.org, the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas on Figshare, the Cell Mapping Toolkit (BSD-3, GitHub/Zenodo) and FAIRSCAPE (MIT, https://fairscape.github.io); conforms_to: RO-Crate with provenance graphs; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; existing_uses cites the perturbation-atlas preprint with PMCID PMC11580897 Standards and external documentation are both covered and each link carries a note explaining its role, so a reader knows which resource answers which question — methods from the preprint, packaging from FAIRSCAPE, integration code from the toolkit, raw data from Figshare and MassIVE. The packaging standard (RO-Crate), the framework that implements it (FAIRSCAPE) and the distributed release metadata archive form a coherent set. imputation_protocols is absent and imputation is never addressed either way, which leaves one limb of the sub-element unanswered; the external-standards and external-resources limbs are met substantively.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: six typed entries — scope (interim release, not final form), coverage (no predicted cell maps; perturb-seq components under pre-publication embargo), integration (modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets; release best suited to per-modality rather than cross-modality analysis), methodological (meaningful analysis requires domain expertise) Unusually candid and directly actionable: the record tells a prospective reuser that the headline deliverable (computed cell maps) is absent, that the multimodal integration the project is named for is not yet supportable from this release, and which components they cannot obtain at all. Each entry is typed. Limitations are consistent with the rest of the record: the embargo limitation matches confidential_elements, the missing-cell-maps limitation matches preprocessing_strategies, and the integration limitation is corroborated by the absence of variable-level identifiers found under Element 3.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: bias_type 'representation_bias'; bias_description 'derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'; affected_subsets naming both lines with donor ancestry, sex, age and disease context A taxonomy term is used rather than free prose, the mechanism of the bias is stated, and the affected scope is pinned to the two specific cell lines with the donor characteristics that generate the representativeness limit. That is enough for a reuser to reason about generalisability of any model trained on these data. representation_bias is the correct category for a two-cell-line resource. Only one bias is recorded: no measurement, selection or annotation bias is discussed despite a targeted non-random 200-gene design and antibody-dependent imaging, both plausible sources. future_use_impacts is absent, so the RAI social-impact limb is unmet and is assessed under sub-element 5.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: source_caveats (dataset level): the portal/Dataverse release-date conflict; three immunofluorescence archives with a file publication date of Jul 15, 2026 later than the 2026-06-17 version publication date; a trailing '(2025-06-30)' description stamp identical to that on two earlier releases, 'indicating description text carried forward between releases'; no per-file descriptions in the June 2026 listing. file_collections.source_caveats: the June 2026 image archives 'carry different MD5 checksums from the October 2025 archives of the same names'. sampling_strategies.source_caveats: 523 versus 464 protein counts in conflict across sources These are concrete, release-specific irregularities a user genuinely needs: same-named archives whose contents differ from the previous release, files appearing a month after publication, and metadata text demonstrably stale. Each is localised to the affected archives or fields, so a user can act on them. Credited on the quality-irregularity question. The anomalies field itself is empty and no data-level anomalies (outliers, failed acquisitions, artefacts within images or spectra) are documented — the disclosures concern the release and its metadata rather than the measurements. This is distinct from Element 6 sub-element 3, which asks for a change log and errata correcting these items and finds none.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: false with sensitivity_details 'the dataset does not involve human subjects, that samples are de-identified, and that the data are not FDA regulated ... CM4AI data are non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures'; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: true with the embargo detail on the two perturb-seq external links; prohibited_uses warns against clinical decision-making The negative determination is explicit and reasoned across two sources rather than left blank, and it is paired with a positive confidentiality finding, so the record distinguishes 'nothing sensitive about the content' from 'some components are restricted'. The clinical-use warning supplies the one caution the content does warrant. An explicit false flag with supporting rationale is meaningful documentation and is not treated as missing. The pairing is internally consistent: sensitive_elements false and confidential_elements true describe different properties and do not conflict.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: two entries whose review_details read, identically, 'Named ethical review contact for the release, per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record' — contacts only, no findings, no review process, no determination; no future_use_impacts field; no conflict-of-interest statement The record identifies who is accountable for ethics but not what they reviewed or concluded, and there is no analysis of anticipated downstream social impacts or mitigations — notable for a project whose own purposes foreground 'ethical, AI-ready datasets' and which staffs a dedicated ethics team across two institutions. Distinct from Element 4 sub-element 1, which asks whether ethical oversight and governance are documented and where named contacts with a standing committee are exactly the evidence sought; this sub-element additionally requires review substance, conflicts of interest and social-impact analysis, and all three are absent.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: citation: '... University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C ; maintainers: 'Long term preservation is provided by the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), supported by committed institutional funds'; distribution_formats.notes references the Dataverse Data Access API; notes records the deposit by Justin Niestroy on 2025-02-27 The hosting platform is identified four independent ways and is a recognised institutional Dataverse repository, with an explicit institutional preservation commitment behind it — the sustainability element this sub-element is ultimately about. No dedicated publisher slot is used, which is a structural gap rather than an informational one. The DOI prefix 10.18130 belongs to the UVA Dataverse registrant and agrees with the landing-page host and the citation's publisher string, so the platform claim is corroborated by the identifier itself. The Dataverse collection notice recorded in notes ('under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives') is a flagged availability risk rather than a contradiction.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: full 47-author string with year 2026, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, 'University of Virginia Dataverse', and 'V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license_and_use_terms requires that 'publications referencing this data or derived products should cite the related publication as well as the data collection itself' All three components the rubric note asks of a Bridge2AI dataset are present: a formatted citation string, a resolvable DOI, and citation instructions embedded in the licence terms, including the dual obligation to cite both the methods publication and the deposit. The version marker in the citation makes the reference reproducible. Citation year, title, publisher and version all agree with issued, title, page host and version elsewhere in the record. The DOI appears in https:// resolvable form in the citation and in bare form in doi, both well formed.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; a release metadata archive is distributed as part of the deposit; instances use B2AI_SUBSTRATE/B2AI_TOPIC vocabularies Conformance is claimed against genuine community standards — RO-Crate for packaging, a published w3id-identified metadata schema, and Bridge2AI controlled vocabularies — and is backed by a shipped metadata archive rather than left as an assertion. RO-Crate and FAIRSCAPE are used in their correct relationship (framework producing crates), and the w3id URI form is appropriate for a persistent schema reference. No domain-specific community standard (PSI-MI for interactions, OME for imaging, MIAME-style reporting for the screens) is claimed, which is a missed integration opportunity rather than an error.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: the CM4AI project portal 'providing documentation, data release listings, tools and publications', the methods preprint, the FAIRSCAPE documentation site, and the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository; page: the Dataverse landing page; maintainers: named programme manager (snthaker@uab.edu) and website contact (zsembay8@uab.edu) for inquiries and site updates Documentation routes are layered — a landing page for the deposit, a project portal for programme-level documentation and release history, a preprint for methods, and a code repository for tooling — and there are named humans to contact when those do not answer the question. Each link is annotated with what it provides, so the set is navigable rather than a bare URL list. No tutorials, webinars or worked examples are cited, which is the outreach limb this record does not reach.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: relationship_type 'is_new_version_of', target_dataset 'doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM', with a note identifying it as the immediately preceding release and stating the content delta; version_access.versions_available enumerates four further releases with DOIs; raw_sources and external_resources point at the MassIVE and Figshare deposits holding the corresponding raw data The relationship is typed from a controlled vocabulary and resolves to a DOI, and the note explains what the relationship means in content terms. Beyond the formal link, the record connects the deposit to its raw-data counterparts in domain repositories, which is the cross-platform integration this element is about. is_new_version_of is semantically correct for consecutive quarterly releases. Only the immediate predecessor is formally typed — the earlier three releases and the external raw deposits appear in prose fields rather than as typed relationships, so machine traversal of the full graph is not possible.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; raw_data_sources carry RRID:CVCL_0419 (MDA-MB-468) and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 (KOLF2.1J); version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C A resolvable DOI is present and is reused consistently as the record id, the citation target, the latest-version pointer and the stem of every internal file and person identifier (e.g. doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#file-apms-paclitaxel). Format 10.XXXX/... satisfied. Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse prefix, plausible and consistent with publisher and page, both of which resolve to dataverse.lib.virginia.edu with the same persistentId. Cell-line RRIDs use the Cellosaurus CVCL_ namespace, a valid RRID authority alongside SCR_ and AB_.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,000 chars) enumerates the four modalities, the two cell systems, the treatment arms and exactly which modality covers which condition Well beyond the 200-character threshold and substantively informative: it names PPI, spatial localization and genetic perturbation data, both cell backgrounds, both drugs (paclitaxel, vorinostat), and the four iPSC differentiation states, then states per-modality coverage so a reader knows AP-MS is treated-only and imaging is MDA-MB-468-only. The description's modality/condition matrix agrees with file_collections, subpopulations.distribution and acquisition_methods; no modality is described that is not represented by files.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: 29 terms including AI, AP-MS, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, paclitaxel, perturb-seq, protein-protein interaction, scRNAseq, SEC-MS, subcellular imaging, vorinostat Far exceeds the five-keyword threshold and spans four distinct axes — programme (Bridge2AI, CM4AI), method (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, scRNAseq), biological material (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, NPC, cardiomyocyte) and perturbagen (paclitaxel, vorinostat) — with both abbreviations and expansions supplied for searchability. Every keyword is corroborated somewhere in the record; none is aspirational. Keywords contain no participant, patient or clinical-research terms, which is one input to the Element 4 human-subjects determination.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections: five typed collections (apms, ifimages, secms, perturbseq, metadata) each with nested resources carrying name, format, media_type, bytes, md5 and issued date Both halves of the sub-element are met: a single resolvable landing page, and a genuine two-level resource hierarchy of five collections over ten files, each file individually identified and checksummed. Collection file_count and total_bytes values reconcile exactly with their member resources; the landing-page URL matches publisher and distribution_formats.access_urls.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: seven entries with relationship_type values is_new_version_of (×4: doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3) parent_datasets is unused, but related_datasets carries the hierarchy far more informatively: a four-deep predecessor chain back to the May 2024 release, each annotated with what that release contained, plus the describing preprint and two citing papers. All seven targets are syntactically valid DOIs with plausible prefixes (10.18130 Dataverse, 10.1101 bioRxiv, 10.1038 Nature). The 'references' entry correctly distinguishes the Nature paper's U2OS map as a separate dataset rather than part of this release.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
