The licence, the prohibited_uses commercial entry, the data_use_permission enum and the ip_restrictions commercial-licence clause are mutually consistent; no contradiction between openness claims and restriction claims.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated for the release.' data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker, ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu; data_governance.access_review_process: 'A Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use.' The regulatory determination is explicit rather than silently omitted, and the governance contact required by this sub-element's full scope is present with ORCID and institutional email, alongside a described access-review process and named stewardship roles. confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unpopulated (recorded as a low-severity completeness issue). The explicit 'FDA Regulated: No' is treated as meaningful documentation rather than as an empty field, consistent with the instruction that explicit false flags are not to be scored as missing.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats.access_urls: ['https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/']; distribution_formats.notes: 'All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Files above the 1.9 GB browser download limit are obtained through the Data Access API.'; publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C Scored on the 'platform access instructions' limb of this sub-element: the resolvable DOI, the named repository and the specific operational instruction about the 1.9 GB browser limit together tell a user how to retrieve all ten archives, including the three multi-gigabyte image files. The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated and the access_urls entry is a bare API root with no datafile identifier appended, so it resolves to nothing on its own — flagged as a low-severity correctness issue. The point is earned on the instructions plus resolvable DOI, not on that URL.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip. file_collections: ten entries each with compression: zip, collection_type (raw_data / processed_data / metadata), MD5 checksum and size, e.g. cm4ai_ifimages_MDA-MB-468_untreated.zip, MD5 6d066e6b9d762284c6aa5d0b44565568, 4.6 GB. A format and a correct MIME type are specified and are carried down to every distributed object with checksums and sizes, which is enough for a user to plan retrieval and verify integrity. application/zip is the correct IANA media type for the declared format, and all ten MD5 values are well-formed 32-character hex. The container-only nature of the declaration — no internal payload format or encoding — is a genuine interoperability gap and is charged against Element 3 sub-element 2 rather than twice here.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: seven typed entries; external_resources: seven entries covering cm4ai.org, the MassIVE Repository, Figshare, NDEx, the Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with docs at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io, and IMP at http://integrativemodeling.org External links are specific and purposeful — each states what the resource holds or does (MassIVE for the MS raw files, Figshare for the CRISPRi atlas, NDEx for map visualisation) rather than listing bare URLs. All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains. The MassIVE and Figshare pointers are corroborated by matching raw_data_sources.access_details entries.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Users are free to share ... and adapt ... under the conditions that appropriate credit is given ...; that the material is not used for commercial purposes; and that contributions built upon the material are distributed under the same license' A named, standard, machine-recognisable licence with its permissions and all three conditions spelled out, plus the explicit statement that no additional legal or technological restrictions may be applied. Reuse is permitted in substance, not merely nominally; the non-commercial limit is consistently reflected in data_use_permission and prohibited_uses.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip; file_collections: compression: zip on all ten entries. No file_collections.resources entries, no internal format, no encoding anywhere in the record. Only the container is declared. For a release of confocal images, mass-spectrometry elution profiles and single-cell matrices, 'ZIP' tells a prospective integrator nothing about whether the payload is OME-TIFF or PNG, mzML or a vendor format, h5ad or MTX — so the information needed to harmonize these data with others is absent. Distinct from Element 2 sub-element 4, which credits that a format and MIME type are stated at all. This sub-element asks whether formats are standardized for reuse and integration; a container plus no encoding does not answer it, and no schema-level file description compensates.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate. The CM4AI preprint and the March 2025 and June 2025 Dataverse releases state that CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework ...'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. instances additionally carry ontology-coded data_substrate (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64) and data_topic (B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34) values. A recognised packaging standard is named and coupled to the FAIRSCAPE framework, and the instance-level Bridge2AI substrate and topic codes give machine-actionable ontology conformance beyond the packaging claim. The record honestly scopes its own RO-Crate claim, noting the June 2026 release page does not restate it — transparent, but it leaves the assertion unverified for this version (low-severity consistency issue). conforms_to_schema describes the datasheet, not the data payload.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: The variables slot is absent from the record. The closest content is instances entries carrying instance_type, data_substrate and data_topic codes, and subsets descriptions naming the archive each occupies — neither defines variables or their identifiers. No data dictionary, column definition, channel key or measurement-unit documentation exists at any level. A reuser opening cm4ai_mass-spec_MDA-MB-468.zip or the perturb-seq atlas has no documented description of the fields inside. The absence is not excused by is_tabular: false — the MS elution profiles and perturb-seq atlas are tabular products within a non-tabular release, and the IF images have a documented four-channel structure in instances.notes that is never formalised as variable metadata.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: four use_category entries with examples (AI-ready data for functional genomics research; AI model training; cellular process analysis; analysis of cell architecture under perturbation). prohibited_uses: two entries — clinical decision-making/patient care 'without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', and commercial use, each with a prohibition_reason. Both limbs are populated and the prohibitions carry reasons rather than bare bans, tying the clinical prohibition to the absence of regulatory oversight and the commercial prohibition to the licence and copyright position. Prohibitions are semantically consistent with the CC BY-NC-SA licence and with the non-clinical, cell-line provenance of the data. discouraged_uses is absent but the sub-element is satisfied by the two populated limbs.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: two entries. (1) 'Ethical Review for the release is carried out by Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca)', with contact_person carrying ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801. (2) 'The Ethics Module employs a methodology inspired by Value-Sensitive Design (VSD) ... including the construction of an axiological repository to guide the articulation of design standards'. Supported by data_governance.access_review_process and committee_contact (Jillian Parker, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu). Named, contactable ethics reviewers with ORCIDs and institutional emails, a described review methodology, and a governance committee with an access-review process — substantially more than a bare assertion that review occurred. No IRB number is present, which is semantically appropriate rather than a gap: with involves_human_subjects false and no participant recruitment, IRB approval would not be expected. data_protection_impacts is absent, consistent with the absence of personal data. No inconsistency is created by the false human-subjects flag.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are described as non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' Corroborated by direct_collection: 'commercially available, ethically sourced human cell lines ... MDA-MB-468 ... available from ATCC; the KOLF2.1J iPSC line was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor and is available from the ... HipSci resource.' States the deidentification status, the basis for it (tissue-culture provenance, unlinkability with current knowledge), and the sourcing of both lines. The 'with current knowledge' qualifier is an honest acknowledgement that genomic material is not unconditionally unlinkable. No formal method such as HIPAA Safe Harbor or k-anonymity is named, and none is expected for established cell lines rather than record-level human data — the described basis is appropriate to the data type. Consistent with sensitive_elements (false, with rationale) and human_subject_research. A residual gap, flagged as low severity, is that the consent provenance of the originating KOLF2.1J donation is not cited.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: No participants exist in this release; participant_privacy and reidentification_risk are consequently absent. The exclusion rests on E1, E8 and direct_collection evidence, not on the emptiness of this sub-element's own fields. Excluded from the denominator. Scoring participant privacy protections against a cell-line release would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent is absent, and no consent process from participants could apply — the material is commercially distributed MDA-MB-468 and HipSci KOLF2.1J lines. Excluded from the denominator. The separate observation that the originating KOLF2.1J donor's consent provenance is not cited is recorded as a low-severity semantic issue rather than scored here.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation are absent, which is the expected state for a release derived entirely from established cell lines. Excluded from the denominator.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Cell type and treatment condition. The release spans MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells under untreated, paclitaxel-treated, and vorinostat-treated conditions; undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes.'; distribution: modality-by-modality coverage statement. subsets: nine entries each with is_subpopulation: true. The population structure is expressed on the axis that matters for this data type — cell line by differentiation state by perturbagen — and the distribution field is explicit that coverage is uneven across modalities (AP-MS treated only; IF MDA-MB-468 only), which is precisely the kind of actionable detail a reuser needs. The subpopulation description agrees with the description field, the subsets list and the file_collections inventory; no modality is claimed in one place and missing in another.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: four instance_type entries (IF confocal image, SEC-MS elution profile, single-cell CRISPRi profile, AP-MS interaction measurement) with no counts. total_file_count: 10. source_caveats: project-level counts '(1,374 protein interactions; 53,788 immunofluorescent images; 7,023 total proteins ...)' are 'not asserted as release-level totals here'; sampling_strategies.notes: 'the June 2026 release page does not state how many targets this release actually covers'. No count of instances or samples is reported anywhere for this release: not images, not baits, not guides or cells, not proteins. total_file_count: 10 counts archives, not data instances, and the file sizes (4.6 GB, 3.8 GB, 4.2 GB of imaging) only imply scale. The omission is principled and self-disclosed — the record declines to reattribute cumulative project figures to a single release, which is good provenance hygiene — but the sub-element asks for specific counts and none are available. subsets.is_data_split is documented (uniformly false), which is meaningful but does not supply instance counts.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: is_tabular: false. subsets: all nine entries carry explicit is_subpopulation: true and is_data_split: false. instances.notes for the IF instance documents the four-channel structure: 'Nuclei were stained with DAPI (blue channel); endoplasmic reticulum with a calreticulin antibody (yellow channel); microtubules with tubulin antibody (red channel); and antibody against protein of interest (green channel).' Three of the four evidence limbs are substantively present: the tabular indicator is set and semantically correct for an imaging/MS/sequencing release, and every subset's role is explicitly typed as a subpopulation rather than a split, so a reader knows the nine partitions are biological conditions and not train/test folds. The variables slot is absent — charged once, at Element 3 sub-element 4, where variable metadata is the whole of the item. Here the split and subpopulation flags plus the tabular indicator carry the item. The uniform is_data_split: false is a meaningful explicit false flag, not an empty default, since it resolves what would otherwise be ambiguous about nine partitions.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances: data_topic codes B2AI_TOPIC:15 (IF imaging), B2AI_TOPIC:26 (SEC-MS and AP-MS), B2AI_TOPIC:34 (perturb-seq), with data_substrate codes B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64. Conditions are named throughout: triple-negative breast cancer (MDA-MB-468), paclitaxel and vorinostat treatment, iPSC differentiation to NPC, neuron and cardiomyocyte; purposes cite 'cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders'. Topics are both ontology-coded and described in prose, and the disease contexts targeted by the project are explicit, so a user can tell which disorders and which perturbation conditions the release speaks to. Substrate and topic codes are internally consistent by modality (the two mass-spectrometry instances share B2AI_TOPIC:26 while carrying distinct substrate codes for AP-MS and SEC-MS), which indicates deliberate coding rather than filler.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: sampling_strategies: is_sample: true, is_random: false, is_representative: false, why_not_representative: 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'; strategies: 'Targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets rather than random sampling'; source_data and notes distinguishing the project's stated 100-chromatin-modifier/100-metabolic-enzyme objective from this release's unstated coverage. known_limitations additionally records that the modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'. The sampling limb of this sub-element is documented thoroughly and honestly, including an explicit non-representativeness finding with its reason — the kind of statement that directly changes how a model trained on these data should be interpreted. anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent (recorded as a medium-severity completeness issue); the point is earned on sampling_strategies, one of the three named evidence fields, which is substantive rather than boilerplate. The incomplete-overlap limitation partially covers missingness across modalities but is not a missing-data protocol.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta; version_access: 'The June 2026 release page shows Version 2.0'; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' A concrete version string, qualified by an explicit maturity status of Beta, and echoed consistently in the citation. Consistent across version, version_access and citation. One oddity in the source is noted in the record itself: the June 2025 and October 2025 predecessors are both recorded as Version 2.1 while this later release is 2.0, an inconsistency the record faithfully reports rather than silently normalising.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available: 'Prior CM4AI data releases are separately published in the same University of Virginia Dataverse collection: May 2024, March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, Version 1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, Version 2.1), and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, Version 2.1)'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C Every prior version is individually citable by DOI, and the latest-version pointer tells a user which record supersedes the others — a user can reach any point in the release history directly. All listed DOIs share the 10.18130/V3 prefix pattern of the same Dataverse collection and are duplicated as typed is_new_version_of relationships in related_datasets; latest_version_doi matches the record's own DOI.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata is absent. updates contains only frequency: Quarterly and update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis.' No change log, no corrections, no statement of what V2.0 altered. The updates block is entirely prospective — it says how often changes will come, never what this release changed. The only change information in the record sits in related_datasets notes ('That release ... did not include AP-MS data'), which is a description of a different dataset rather than errata or a changelog for this one. Distinct from sub-element 4, which is satisfied by exactly the same frequency statement; crediting a forward-looking cadence twice would double-count it. No corrections or retractions are recorded for a Beta release that has superseded three predecessors, which is itself a notable silence.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Quarterly'; updates.update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis.' retention_limit.retention_details: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds.' A specific cadence with a stated end date for the update programme, plus a preservation commitment beyond it — a user can plan around both the update rhythm and the long-term availability. The quarterly claim is broadly corroborated by the observed release history (March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, June 2026), though the gap between October 2025 and June 2026 exceeds a quarter.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: seven entries with source_description, source_type and access_details, e.g. 'SEC-MS data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without treatment)' — 'Available at the MassIVE Repository'; two perturb-seq sources marked 'Embargoed'; 'CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs' — 'Available at Figshare'. notes: FAIRSCAPE 'assigns persistent, resolvable, globally unique identifiers using the ARK scheme, with provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology'. source_caveats documents the tiering of sources used to build the record. Raw upstream deposits are enumerated per modality with their external repository and availability status, and the provenance framework (ARK identifiers, EVI evidence graphs) is named. The record's own source_caveats adds a second, rarer layer: provenance of the metadata assertions themselves. was_derived_from is absent, but the raw_data_sources limb of this sub-element is populated substantively and the release-notes limb is met by update_details plus source_caveats carrying actual derivation information rather than unrelated prose. The embargo statuses agree with known_limitations.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four responses, including 'To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning' and 'To broadly stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems ... which are not black boxes'. addressing_gaps: two responses identifying the black-box deficiency in genotype-phenotype models and the lack of structural priors for variant interpretation. Motivation is given at three levels — scientific goal, deliverable, and the gap in the field being addressed — and is specific about the deficiency (black-box genotype-to-phenotype prediction) rather than generically invoking scientific value. Purposes align with the funder's programme (NIH Bridge2AI) and with the tasks and intended_uses; no mismatch between stated motivation and documented content.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: five responses — hierarchical cell map construction as 'directed acyclic graphs in which each node represents an assembly of proteins in proximity at a given scale'; self-supervised multimodal embedding of PPI and IF features into a shared low-dimensional space; multi-resolution community detection; development of visible neural networks; interpretation of genetic variants using cell maps as a structural prior. Technically concrete and methodologically specific — these are stated analyses with named representations and algorithmic families, not aspirational themes. The tasks correspond to the MuSIC pipeline described in notes and to the modalities actually released (PPI from AP-MS/SEC-MS, images from IF), so the objectives are traceable to the data. The record is candid that the resulting maps are not in this release.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: grantor: 'National Institutes of Health'; notes: 'Funding Information recorded on the release: National Institutes of Health, 1OT2OD032742-01. The CM4AI preprint additionally acknowledges NIH award 5U54HG012513-02 (Bridge2AI Bridge Center) and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia as supporting the project.' The primary funder is structurally recorded and two further support sources are named, with the record distinguishing what the release itself states from what the preprint acknowledges. The funding mechanism is identifiable from the award itself: OT2 is the NIH Other Transactions activity code used by the Common Fund Bridge2AI programme, consistent with the description's 'NIH Bridge2AI program'. Non-grant support (the Frederick Thomas Fund) is appropriately noted without a grant number.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: [grant_number: 1OT2OD032742-01]; funders.notes additionally cites '5U54HG012513-02'. related_datasets notes the Nature paper 'acknowledges Bridge2AI Program funding OT2 OD032742'. A structured grant_number is provided in the dedicated slot, not merely embedded in prose, and a second award is given in the notes. 1OT2OD032742-01 parses correctly against the NIH pattern: application type 1, activity code OT2, awarding institute OD (Office of the Director), serial 032742, support year -01. 5U54HG012513-02 likewise parses (type 5, U54, NHGRI, serial 012513, year -02). Both are plausible for a Bridge2AI Common Fund award; the core number matches the OT2 OD032742 cited independently in the related Nature publication, an internal cross-check that passes.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: 46 entries with affiliations; 40 carry ORCID identifiers (e.g. ORCID:0000-0002-1708-8454 for Ideker T) and six carry locally minted doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#person-* identifiers. Ideker T carries a structured principal_investigator block with email tideker@health.ucsd.edu and is noted as Point of Contact. maintainers names four roles including a program manager and the depositor. data_collectors attributes work to the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and the Krogan laboratory at UCSF. Exceptionally thorough attribution: individual contributors with persistent identifiers and affiliations, an identified PI and point of contact, named maintainers with contact emails, and laboratory-level credit for who generated which modality. Where an ORCID was unavailable the record mints a transparent local identifier rather than omitting the person. The creator list matches the citation string author order, and ROR identifiers are used for the University of Virginia (ROR:0153tk833). The record's caveat that several names are rendered as surname plus initial is disclosed in source_caveats, with full names supplied in per-creator notes.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: four entries — AP-MS 'on endogenously tagged cell lines'; SEC-MS 'for proteome-wide complex and interaction mapping'; 'Immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal microscopy, with four color channels: DAPI for nuclei (blue), calreticulin antibody for endoplasmic reticulum (yellow), tubulin antibody for microtubules (red), and antibody against the protein of interest (green)'; 'Single-cell CRISPR screens using a CRISPR lentiviral library with 6 guide RNAs per gene in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9, sequenced with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit'. Settings are given at the level of stains, channels, guide density and readout chemistry — enough for a domain reader to understand how each modality was captured and to compare protocols across studies. The four mechanisms map one-to-one onto the four instance types and onto the released archive families; the IF channel description is corroborated in instances.notes. Technical terms are used correctly throughout (dCas9 for CRISPRi, ICC-IF, SEC-MS).

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: three entries each with was_directly_observed: true, e.g. 'Protein-protein interaction data acquired by affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) on endogenously tagged cell lines and by size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) ... used as two orthogonal mass spectrometry-based approaches'; 'Spatial proteomics acquired by immunofluorescence (IF) subcellular microscopy, using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols on a pipetting robot'. raw_data_sources lists seven upstream deposits with repositories. Instruments, reagent resources and automation are named (HPA antibody resource, pipetting robot, 10x Genomics 3'HT kit), the orthogonality rationale for using two MS approaches is explained, and the raw sources are separately enumerated with their external repositories. was_directly_observed: true is semantically correct for instrument-captured measurements. Acquisition entries are consistent with collection_mechanisms rather than duplicating them at the same granularity.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent. The nearest content is notes, which describes the MuSIC pipeline (node2vec and HPA deep-learning embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, multi-resolution community detection, GO/Reactome alignment, LLM naming) but ends: 'this pipeline produces the computed cell maps that the June 2026 release states are not included in this release'. instances entries all carry label: false. Seven of the ten archives are typed processed_data, yet no processing step is documented for any of them — no spectral search parameters, no guide-assignment or QC thresholds, no image processing. The one pipeline described in detail is by the record's own statement not the pipeline that produced these files. Consistency failure: collection_type: processed_data asserts transformation that no field describes. label: false across all instances is consistent with the absence of labeling_strategies. The imputation limb is likewise silent — imputation_protocols is absent with no statement that imputation was not used.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Software named anywhere in the record: Cell Mapping Toolkit / cellmaps_pipeline (external_resources, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline) and the MuSIC pipeline (notes); FAIRSCAPE (external_resources, https://fairscape.github.io, MIT License); NDEx with Cytoscape, HiView and the ndex2 Python library (external_resources); Integrative Modeling Platform (external_resources, http://integrativemodeling.org); the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit (collection_mechanisms). No used_software is attached to any dataset property, and preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, imputation_protocols and machine_annotation_tools are all absent. Score 0: no software is named in a role that produced or transformed the data being distributed. Every named tool falls in an excluded role — the Cell Mapping Toolkit and MuSIC fall under (e), since the record itself states they produce computed cell maps 'not included in this release'; FAIRSCAPE falls under (c), packaging and provenance-metadata production over cm4ai_release_metadata.zip; NDEx, Cytoscape, HiView, ndex2 and the UVA Dataverse fall under (b), sharing and hosting; the 10x 3'HT kit falls under (a), capture instrumentation. IMP is a modelling package with no stated role in producing these archives. A reader therefore cannot tell what software turned the raw instrument output into the seven processed_data archives. The pointer https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline is a specific repository rather than an organisation root, so the deficiency is not a pointer-quality problem but a role problem: the record is explicit that this pipeline's outputs are absent from the release. No slot among used_software, machine_annotation_tools, preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, imputation_protocols or external_resources carries qualifying evidence.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: seven entries — cm4ai.org portal; MassIVE Repository holding the SEC-MS and AP-MS data; Figshare holding the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas; NDEx for map sharing and visualisation; the Cell Mapping Toolkit with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/; FAIRSCAPE with tutorial and installation instructions; IMP at http://integrativemodeling.org. conforms_to: RO-Crate / FAIRSCAPE packaging. related_datasets cites the describing preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and the Nature paper doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3 with MassIVE MSV000097168 and ProteomeXchange PXD052362 accessions. A rich and purposeful external landscape: standards (RO-Crate, EVI, ARK), repositories with the specific holdings named, documentation sites, and published papers with accession numbers a reader can follow. imputation_protocols is absent and no explicit statement that imputation was not used is made — a gap within this sub-element's full scope, outweighed here by substantive evidence on the external standards and resources limbs. All URLs are structurally valid; the MassIVE and ProteomeXchange accession formats (MSV*, PXD*) are well formed.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: four typed entries — scope_limitation ('This is an interim release and does not contain predicted cell maps ... Computed cell maps are not included in this release', with scope_impact 'most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets rather than for use of the integrated cell maps'); coverage_limitation (modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'); methodological_limitation ('Analysis of the release requires domain expertise'); coverage_limitation (embargo on the two perturb-seq datasets). Limitations are typed, specific and consequential — the first in particular warns a user that the headline product of the project, the integrated cell maps, is not in this release, with an explicit statement of what the release is therefore good for. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the missing cell maps in notes, the embargo in raw_data_sources.access_details, the partial overlap in the subpopulations distribution statement. No limitation contradicts a claim made elsewhere in the record.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: bias_type: representation_bias; bias_description: 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.' Reinforced by sampling_strategies.is_representative: false with the same reason. The bias is categorised with a taxonomy term rather than described in free text alone, and the substantive point — that two cell lines cannot stand for population-level biological variation — is the correct and material one for this data type. The bias_type value maps to the BiasTypeEnum representation category and is semantically apt. Only one bias is recorded: selection of chromatin modifiers and metabolic enzymes as targets, the single male Northern European donor origin of KOLF2.1J, and antibody-availability bias in the HPA-based imaging are all unaddressed. future_use_impacts is absent. Sufficient for the point, but the coverage is thin.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: The anomalies slot is absent. No outliers, batch effects, failed runs, discarded images, low-confidence baits or guides, or QC thresholds are recorded anywhere in the record. For a multi-modal release spanning mass spectrometry, high-content imaging and single-cell sequencing — all techniques with well-known, documentable failure modes — the complete absence of data quality reporting is a substantive gap. The coverage limitations that are documented concern what was measured, not how well. Not compensated by known_limitations, which addresses scope, overlap, expertise and embargo rather than data quality; nor by missing_data_documentation, which is also absent. Checksums in file_collections establish file integrity, not data quality.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present: false; sensitivity_details: 'The release records Human Subjects: No, De-identified Samples: Yes, and FDA Regulated: No. CM4AI data are described as non-clinical, derived from tissue cultures, and unable to be matched with current knowledge to a human subject.' An explicit negative determination with the reasoning behind it, rather than an omitted field. A reader learns not only that there is no sensitive content but why the creators concluded so, which is what makes the claim checkable. Per the instruction that explicit false flags can be meaningful documentation, this is scored as present. The determination is consistent with human_subject_research, is_deidentified and the cell-line provenance in direct_collection. content_warnings is absent, appropriately for laboratory assay data.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: named reviewers Vardit Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon with emails and ORCIDs, plus a methodology entry: 'The Ethics Module employs a methodology inspired by Value-Sensitive Design (VSD), facilitating the creation of normative standards and expectations aimed at ensuring the responsible design of datasets and AI technologies in alignment with core values, including the construction of an axiological repository'. data_governance.notes: the Ethics team's plan for 'ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision ... balancing the openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property', and the 'CM4AI Life Cycle, a framework designed to elucidate governance milestones throughout the data generation and AI system development processes'. The ethical-review limb is documented well beyond a compliance statement: an identified ethics function with a named methodology, a governance lifecycle framework, and contactable reviewers. future_use_impacts is absent, so anticipated downstream social impacts (rai:dataSocialImpact) are never analysed — a notable omission given a dataset explicitly built to train AI models and an ethics programme evidently capable of supplying it. Recorded as a low-severity issue; the point is earned on the substantively populated ethical_reviews limb.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/ (University of Virginia Dataverse / LibraData); citation: '... University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds.' name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: full 46-author string ending 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)', https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C. license_and_use_terms adds citation instructions: 'publications referencing the data or derived products should cite the related publication as well as directly citing the data collection.' name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: RO-Crate packaging 'with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets ... using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; notes: ARK persistent identifier scheme and 'provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology'; instances use B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC ontology codes; annotation by 'alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome' in the pipeline description. Multiple genuine community standards are named across packaging (RO-Crate), identifiers (ARK, DOI, ORCID, ROR), provenance (EVI/PROV-style evidence graphs) and biological ontologies (GO, Reactome, Bridge2AI vocabularies). The RO-Crate claim is self-flagged as carried from earlier releases and the preprint rather than restated on the June 2026 page (low-severity consistency issue), but the identifier and ontology conformance is directly evidenced in this record's own values.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: page: https://cm4ai.org/; external_resources: 'CM4AI project web portal at https://cm4ai.org/, providing project overview, data releases, tools, product documentation, publications, and learning materials'; 'user documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/'; FAIRSCAPE 'described with a tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io'. maintainers names a website support contact (zsembay8@uab.edu) and a program manager (snthaker@uab.edu). name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: seven entries, each with an explicit relationship_type — is_new_version_of (K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3, with NDEx uuid f693137a-d2d7-11ef-8e41-005056ae3c32, MassIVE MSV000097168 and ProteomeXchange PXD052362).
