name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License. Only credentialed PhysioNet users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement may access the files... Duplication as reasonably required to carry out the research project is permitted, but sale of all or part of the data on any media is not... respect the Fort Lauderdale Agreement. There are no fees'; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions describing copyright retention, the bar on IP claims, and permission to hold downstream IP subject to non-obstructive licensing The access policy is actionable rather than nominal: it names who may access (credentialed PhysioNet users), what they must sign, what they may do (duplicate for the project), what they may not do (sell), and that no fee applies. The IP block is unusually precise in distinguishing claims on the data itself, which are barred, from downstream discovery rights, which are permitted under non-obstructive licensing. Restrictiveness is coherent with the surrounding record: general_research_use with no non-commercial or geographic limit matches collection_consents, which states the consent imposes no such restrictions. The licence and the consent scope agree.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply'; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance: 'covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality, which must be asserted against compulsory legal demands such as court orders and subpoenas... NIH STRIDES cloud partners, which hold pre-negotiated agreements with the NIH for data privacy and HIPAA protection'; data_governance.committee_name: 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org in access_review_process All four limbs of the sub-element's scope are addressed: export control (explicitly none), HIPAA status, a restricted sensitivity classification, and a further regulatory instrument in the Certificate of Confidentiality with a statement of when it must be asserted. The governance contact required by the source-rubric scope is present as a named office with a working address, supported by accountable_organization and stewardship_roles. The governance contact is carried in data_governance rather than the deprecated regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact slot; per the schema-path mappings, data_governance.committee_contact is the current location and the substance is present. The restricted classification is consistent with the registered-access licence and the controlled-access audio route rather than contradicting them.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; data_governance.access_review_process: 'Registered access to the feature-only dataset requires registration on PhysioNet, confirmation of identity and signature of the Bridge2AI-Voice Registered Access Agreement. Controlled access to raw audio requires a completed Data Access Request Form and Data Use Agreement, submission... to the Data Access Compliance Office for review at DACO@b2ai-voice.org and, on approval, a Data Transfer and Use Agreement'; raw_data_sources.access_details naming https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ No download_url slot is populated, but the sub-element admits platform access instructions as an alternative and those instructions are exceptionally complete: two distinct tiers, the exact prerequisites for each, the reviewing office and its address, and the concrete distribution endpoint for the controlled tier. A user can act on this without further enquiry. Access routes are internally consistent with confidentiality_level: restricted and with third_party_sharing, which describes the same two-tier arrangement including the bar on onward transfer to collaborators at other organisations. The empty download_url slot is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue rather than scored against this sub-element.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: Apache Parquet ('ppgs.parquet, sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet and torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet, together with a per-recording metadata file'); Tab-separated values ('static_features.tsv, audio_quality_metrics.tsv and the phenotype tables'); JSON ('Every data file is accompanied by a JSON data dictionary with the same file stem') Format documentation descends to individual file names and states what each format carries, which is well past naming a format list. The JSON entry additionally establishes a naming convention (same file stem) that tells a user how to pair data with its dictionary. Formats are semantically appropriate to the content: Parquet for dense variable-length tensors, TSV for phenotype tables, JSON for dictionaries. media_type is absent throughout and is logged as a low-severity completeness issue; it does not obscure which file types are distributed.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: six DOI-resolvable typed entries; external_resources: six entries including https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap (MIT, Zenodo-archived), https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), https://github.com/sensein/senselab, https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ with source at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, the Synapse controlled-access endpoints, and FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker Both limbs are populated substantively. External resources carry licences, archival flags and, for the controlled-access entry, the approval requirement, so a user can tell which links are reusable code, which are archival, and which are gated. The final entry candidly notes that the FHIR profile source repository URL is not recorded in the bundle. All URLs are well formed with plausible domains (github.com, zenodo via DOI 10.5281, synapse.org, physionet.org). The record's own admission of one missing repository URL is a transparency signal rather than a defect in the linked set.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms (Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, duplication for the research project permitted, sale barred, Fort Lauderdale Agreement respected, no fees); data_use_permission: general_research_use; prohibited_uses enumerating five specific bars Reuse is permitted for general research under a named licence whose conditions are spelled out, and the boundaries are set by an explicit prohibited_uses list rather than left to inference. The absence of non-commercial, geographic, research-type or algorithm-development restrictions is affirmatively stated in collection_consents, which is what a prospective reuser needs to know. This is a bespoke registered-access licence rather than a standard Creative Commons instrument, so reuse terms must be read from the prose; the prose is specific enough to act on. Licence restrictiveness is consistent with the consent scope and with confidentiality_level: restricted.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: Apache Parquet, Tab-separated values, JSON; conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0, applied to the audio dataset layout and the phenotype folder organization'; raw_data_sources.raw_data_format: 'WAV audio, converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz... REDCap and ReproSchema exports converted to tab-delimited phenotype tables' Every distributed product is in an open, widely supported, non-proprietary format, and each JSON data dictionary describes the columns, the question asked of the participant and the response type, which is what makes the TSV tables actually interpretable rather than merely machine-readable. Formats are standard and correctly matched to content. Character encoding is nowhere stated for the TSV and JSON products; recorded as a low-severity completeness issue and counted as a warning rather than scored against the sub-element, since the dominant requirement — standardized, openly parseable formats — is met with file-level specificity.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0 with an explicit scope caveat; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology codes B2AI_TOPIC:4, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes' Conformance is asserted at three distinct levels — a community data-organisation standard (BIDS), a metadata schema (data-sheets-schema with a named class), and controlled vocabularies for topics, substrates and diagnoses (B2AI ontology codes, ICD-10). The scope caveat on BIDS is the mark of a careful claim rather than a weaker one. The caveat that BIDS applies to the audio layout and phenotype folders and not to the Parquet feature files of this release is semantically correct and prevents a conformance overclaim that the format list would otherwise invite. Ontology prefixes are used consistently with the Bridge2AI namespace.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: thirteen entries. participant_id and session_id carry data_type: identifier with is_identifier: true and notes describing the linkage ('links feature records to phenotype rows'; 'a participant may have more than one session'). Feature variables carry derivation (e.g. spectrogram: 'STFT of the 16 kHz monaural waveform with a 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point FFT, downsampled by a factor of two; dimension 201 by T'), measurement_technique, unit, minimum_value/maximum_value (sparc_pitch 50–550 Hz) and quality_notes on absence Identifier variables are flagged as such and their join semantics explained, which is precisely what cross-dataset integration requires. Feature variables carry reproducible derivation parameters and dimensionality, and several record why a value may be absent. source_caveats honestly states that these are the shared identifying and dense-feature columns rather than a complete column enumeration, with the JSON dictionaries carrying the remainder. Variable-level parameters agree with preprocessing_strategies (25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 mel bins, 50 Hz SPARC, 100 Hz ppgs across 40 phonemes) with no contradiction between the two blocks. The distinction drawn between torchaudio pitch and sparc_pitch as different algorithms over different ranges is technically coherent.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three research entries with examples and usage_notes ('No recommended splits are supplied; researchers should construct their own and should account for the skews in disorder category, site and demographics'); discouraged_uses: two entries (hiring, insurance, surveillance; uses assuming representativeness); prohibited_uses: five entries (re-identification attempts, harm or stigmatization, obstructive IP protection and sale, contacting subjects without IRB and consent, onward disclosure to third parties) All three registers are populated and each carries a reason rather than a bare prohibition. The three-way distinction is used correctly: legally binding bars sit in prohibited_uses, ethical cautions in discouraged_uses, and affirmative research applications in intended_uses. The usage note attaching split construction guidance to the intended use is the kind of guidance that changes what a reuser actually does. Prohibitions are consistent with the licence terms and the Registered Access Agreement described in license_and_use_terms, and the discouraged surveillance and insurance uses align with the stated ethical rationale for controlled access to raw voice.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: reviewing_organization 'University of South Florida Institutional Review Board' with review_details ('Reviewed and approved the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol and the sharing of the collected data. Subsites were approved through the single IRB process. The study is observational... no data monitoring committee was appointed'); human_subject_research.irb_approval ('Participating United States institutions were covered through the single IRB process; Canadian institutions obtained separate research ethics board approvals'); human_subject_research.ethics_review_board; data_protection_impacts; data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with DACO@b2ai-voice.org Ethics oversight is documented with the reviewing body named, the multi-jurisdictional structure explained (single IRB for US subsites, separate Canadian REBs, a further separate protocol for genomic collection), the study design characterised, and the absence of a data monitoring committee justified by the observational design. The governance contact required by the source-rubric scope is present. The data protection impact limb is weaker: the record states that no impact analysis on data subjects has been conducted, offsetting this with an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published ethical-justification memorandum. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects: true is matched by populated IRB approval, as required. The consistency rule 'IF data_protection_impacts present THEN EXPECT reidentification_risk assessed' also passes — participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is assessed in detail. Scored 1 on the strength of the ethics-review limb, which is the sub-element's primary requirement; the missing DPIA is logged as a medium-severity content_accuracy issue.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, removal of selected indirect identifiers and highly sensitive non-identifying elements, and withholding of all raw audio'; identifiers_removed enumerating names, civic addresses, SSNs, geography above country, dates finer than years, contact and device identifiers, biometric identifiers, narrative free-text and transcripts, and all raw voice recordings; deidentification_details: 'Dates were rebased or replaced by integers, geographic information was generalized... K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved, and voice itself can never be fully de-identified, which is why the waveforms are released only under controlled access' Among the strongest sections of the record. A named standard, an enumerated identifier list, the specific transformations applied, and — unusually — a statement of what the method does not achieve. Declaring that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not reached, and tying that residual risk to the decision to withhold waveforms, is the sort of disclosure that lets a reuser reason about risk rather than take reassurance on trust. Method appropriateness check passes emphatically: HIPAA Safe Harbor alone would be inadequate for voice data, and the record recognises this, layering indirect-identifier removal, free-speech feature exclusion and complete withholding of raw audio on top. Consistency rules 'deidentification claimed THEN method specified' and 'identifiers removed THEN identifiers_removed listed' both pass.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers, indirect identifiers, state/province removed with only country retained, date rebasing, narrative removal, withholding of raw voice); privacy_techniques ('a combined de-identified database hosted through a HIPAA-compliant NIH STRIDES partner, and federated learning, in which algorithms are run on data held at each institution and only model updates are shared'); reidentification_risk ('Voice is inherently identifying... K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved... users agree not to attempt re-identification'); data_linkage describing EHR access for gold-standard validation and datasheets kept only at the collecting institution Re-identification risk is assessed explicitly and honestly rather than asserted away, and the assessment drives a concrete mitigation (controlled access for waveforms) rather than ending in a disclaimer. The architectural protections — federated learning so data need not leave institutions, identifiable PHI confined to institution-local REDCap — are described at a level that lets a reader evaluate them. The risk assessment is technically correct about the data type: a voice waveform is a biometric and cannot be de-identified, and the record reaches the right conclusion from that premise. Consistent with is_deidentified.deidentification_details, which makes the same k-anonymity statement without contradiction.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: 'Prospective informed consent, obtained on paper, electronically within the application or through REDCap surveys, or by recorded video consent'; consent_documentation (paper uploaded to REDCap, electronic consent HIPAA compliant, stored a minimum of five years, video audio used to verify the acoustic data belong to the consented individual); consent_scope (recordings, linked health information, EHR access for gold-standard validation, registered and controlled sharing tiers); withdrawal_mechanism ('If a participant withdraws during or before the voice data collection their data are not included... once the collection is complete, research data including voice recordings cannot be removed'); plus collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations Consent is documented across type, modality, storage, scope and withdrawal, and the scope explicitly anticipates the two-tier dissemination the dataset actually uses — meaning the sharing arrangement is covered by what participants agreed to. The withdrawal limit is stated plainly rather than elided, including the point after which data cannot be removed. Consistency rule 'IF involves_human_subjects=True THEN EXPECT consent described' passes. The withdrawal account in informed_consent and the independent consent_revocations block agree with one another on the cut-off. Consent scope agrees with license_and_use_terms: both describe unrestricted research use with no commercial or geographic limit.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true; special_protections ('Adult enrollment is restricted to participants aged 18 to 120 who can provide informed consent in English... Cohorts include participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and with psychiatric diagnoses; the protocol notes that questions asked of the mood and psychiatric cohorts can cause discomfort or trigger negative emotions. No pediatric data collection was performed at the coordinating site'); participant_compensation.compensation_provided: true, compensation_type 'Electronic gift cards', compensation_amount '40 US dollars for a data collection session taking less than 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for a session taking over 90 minutes, for no more than three sessions and a maximum of 120 US dollars' At-risk groups are identified specifically (cognitive impairment, dementia, psychiatric diagnoses) rather than as a category, the capacity-to-consent boundary is stated, and a foreseeable harm — distress from psychiatric questionnaire content — is acknowledged. Compensation is quantified with its tiering and its cap, which is the level of detail needed to judge whether an inducement is undue. Consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations, which describes the same age restriction and the same cohorts, and with the pediatric exclusion asserted in subpopulations and in the related_datasets pediatric entry. No contradiction across the three statements of the adult-only scope.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: two entries with subpopulation_elements_present: true. First — identification: 'Disease cohort categories assigned at enrollment from a clinical diagnosis: voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, pediatric voice and speech disorders, and controls'; distribution: 'The public releases do not contain an equal distribution... the adult release contains no pediatric participants'. Second — demographic sub-populations 'age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status' with distribution 'skewed by site and by demographic factors' Both the clinical and demographic axes of subpopulation structure are described, each paired with an honest statement about distribution rather than only a list of categories. Telling a user that the cohorts are unequally represented and that they should consider the multivariate distribution is more useful than a count table would be on its own. Consistent with sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and with the representation_bias entry in known_biases, which describe the same skews without contradiction. The pediatric exclusion agrees with at_risk_populations and the related pediatric dataset entry.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances[0].counts: 833 (instance_type 'Study participant'); instances[1].notes: '29,278 records each for spectrograms, mel spectrograms and mel-frequency cepstral coefficients; 32,522 torchaudio pitch records; 28,640 sparc electromagnetic articulography records; 31,855 sparc loudness records; 31,872 sparc periodicity and sparc pitch records; and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram records'; collection_timeframes: '306 in version 1.0, a further 136 in version 2.0 and a further 391 in version 3.0.0, reaching 833 adult participants'; splits.split_details: 'No recommended train, validation or test splits are provided' Counts are given at both levels of the two-level instance structure, and the per-feature counts are reported separately rather than collapsed into a single figure — with the reason for their divergence stated. source_caveats explains why the per-feature counts are used in preference to the project documentation's single recording total, which is a rare degree of provenance discipline about a count. Arithmetic check passes: 306 + 136 + 391 = 833, matching instances.counts and the description. The split position is documented as a deliberate absence with guidance, not merely omitted.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: thirteen entries with variable_name, data_type, is_identifier, derivation, measurement_technique, unit, minimum_value/maximum_value and quality_notes; distribution_formats JSON entry: 'Every data file is accompanied by a JSON data dictionary with the same file stem, describing each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type'; splits.split_details stating no recommended splits with a rationale; subpopulations entries carrying subpopulation_elements_present: true; relationships.relationship_details explaining the participant_id/session_id linkage Variable metadata is detailed and a companion data dictionary is documented for every distributed file, so the enumeration in variables being partial does not leave a user without column-level documentation. Split roles and subpopulation flags are both documented, the former as a reasoned absence with construction guidance. is_tabular is not set, although TSV phenotype tables, static features and quality metrics are distributed alongside array-valued Parquet products; recorded as a low-severity completeness issue. The remaining limbs of the sub-element are met substantively, and the one-to-many participant-to-session relation is stated explicitly so a user will not mis-key a join.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances[0].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4 with label: true and label_description ('Each participant carries a diagnostic label corresponding to one of the disease cohorts (voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders) or to the control group, assigned by a clinician at the site of data collection'); instances[1].data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36; notes describing 22 acoustic tasks grouped as non-voice/non-speech, voice/non-speech and speech Conditions are represented both as controlled ontology codes and as readable cohort names, with the provenance of each label (a clinician at the collection site) attached. The task inventory in notes adds the acoustic-content dimension of the topic space, naming the specific elicitation tasks from the Rainbow Passage to animal fluency. B2AI topic and substrate codes are used in the Bridge2AI namespace consistently with the record's other ontology references. The label: true / label: false distinction between the participant-level and feature-record-level instances is used correctly — the diagnosis attaches to the person, not to the individual recording.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: five entries (differing site configurations and protocol change over the study; noise artifacts and variable headset microphone distance; varying diagnostic practice and possible questionnaire under-reporting; features unobtainable for some recordings; broken Parquet files in v3.0.0 fixed in v3.1.0); sampling_strategies (is_sample true, is_random false, is_representative false, with strategies, source_data and why_not_representative); missing_data_documentation (missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes, handling_strategy: 'No imputation is performed. A missingness table is included with the dataset, and generating missingness tables is the first step of the audit protocol applied before each release') All three limbs are populated with causally specific content. Missing data is explained structurally — phenotype rows exist only where a column is non-missing, disease-specific instruments are absent outside their cohort, and de-identification itself removed free-speech-derived features — so a user can distinguish missingness by design from missingness by failure. The no-imputation decision is stated and paired with a shipped missingness table. The anomaly about features unobtainable for some recordings is corroborated by the differing per-feature counts in instances.notes and by the quality_notes on individual variables; three independent parts of the record agree. The broken-Parquet anomaly agrees with the v3.1.0 erratum.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '3.1.0'; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; citation '(version 3.1.0)'; status: published; issued: '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z' A semantic version number is given and is corroborated by the landing page path, the citation string and the release date, so there is no ambiguity about which artifact the record describes. Version consistency check passes across four independent fields. The issued date 2026-05-01 matches the v3.1.0 release date recorded in distribution_dates.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available: 'Version 1.0 (Health Data Nexus, November 2024), and versions 1.1, 2.0.0, 2.0.1, 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 on PhysioNet'; version_details: 'Older versions continue by default to be supported, hosted and made available to researchers, and each version has a unique DOI, although the publishers reserve the right to remove access to older versions. A changelog for each dataset version is published online'; latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 The policy governing access to superseded versions is stated, including the reservation of the right to withdraw them, and the mechanism is concrete: a unique DOI per version plus a published changelog. The concept DOI is supplied for users who want the moving latest version rather than a pinned release. The version list is consistent with distribution_dates and with the related_datasets entries pointing at v3.0.0 and at v1.0 on the Health Data Nexus. The platform migration from Health Data Nexus to PhysioNet is handled coherently across version_access, maintainers and source_caveats.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: four entries — v2.0.0 reprocessed spectrograms and removed free-speech-derived spectrograms and MFCCs; v2.0.1 corrected the authorship list; v3.1.0 'fixed broken Parquet files carried in version 3.0.0, updated validated diagnosis information across conditions with back-filled information, rearranged some phenotype files and renamed certain gold-standard variable names'; and a candid note that 'No formal erratum is published; a changelog for each dataset version is published online'. updates.update_details records added participants, added SPARC and ppgs features, corrected processing and authorship errors, and file reorganisation Changes are described at the level a reanalyst needs: which files broke, which variables were renamed, which features were added or withdrawn, and in which version each occurred. The renaming of gold-standard variable names in v3.1.0 is exactly the kind of breaking change that is usually omitted from release notes. The v3.1.0 erratum corroborates the broken-Parquet anomaly recorded independently in anomalies. The fourth entry's admission that no formal erratum document exists is a transparency signal that does not contradict the three substantive change records.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Semi-annual (twice a year)'; updates.update_details: 'Further versions of the dataset are released as new versions on the hosting platform, and users are notified through news items on the platform and through standard communication channels' A definite cadence is stated rather than an aspiration, and it is paired with the notification channel through which users will learn of a new release — both halves of what the sub-element asks. The stated semi-annual cadence is consistent with the observed release history in distribution_dates (six releases between November 2024 and May 2026), so the schedule is corroborated by the record's own history rather than merely asserted.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw voice, speech, breathing and cough audio recordings captured with the Bridge2AI-Voice application, together with questionnaire and clinical data exported from REDCap'; raw_data_sources with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format ('WAV audio, converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz... REDCap and ReproSchema exports') and access_details (DACO review, DTUA, Synapse endpoint); updates.update_details and version_access.version_details serving as release notes; created_by: Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium The derivation chain is traceable end to end: raw WAV and REDCap exports, the named software that transformed them, the feature products distributed, and the gated route by which the raw layer can still be reached. Release-specific derivation detail is present in update_details and version_details rather than in an unrelated notes field. Read against the dedicated updates.update_details field as the schema mapping directs; it carries genuine release and derivation information (feature additions, reprocessing, file reorganisation) rather than unrelated commentary. Consistent with preprocessing_strategies, which describes the same 16 kHz monaural conversion, and with retention_limit, which states the de-identified raw data are retained but not publicly accessible.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four entries — a flagship standardized ethically sourced dataset of 10,000 voices linked to health information; enabling development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable ML models; developing new standards for acoustic data collection, analysis and interoperability including diversity-metric benchmarks; and developing ethical, legal and governance norms for voice data. addressing_gaps: four entries on small prior sample sizes, absent measurement standards, private industry holdings that cannot be audited, and limited existing open voice datasets Motivation is stated as four distinct objectives spanning data, methods, standards and ethics, and each is paired in addressing_gaps with the specific deficiency in the prior literature it responds to. This is a scientific rationale rather than a mission statement. The first purpose carries a source_caveat disclosing that two equal-ranked sources disagree on the target enrollment (10,000 versus 30,000) and recording both figures rather than silently choosing one. That is correct handling of a source conflict and strengthens rather than weakens the field.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Detection and classification of disease from voice, using diagnostic labels spanning vocal pathologies, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, psychiatric conditions and respiratory disorders'; 'Pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking and validation of artificial intelligence and machine learning models on voice, speech and respiratory audio features' Tasks are specified in machine-learning terms with the label space named, so a reader can tell what supervised problem the dataset supports. They are reinforced by intended_uses, which adds screening, diagnosis and monitoring as clinical research applications. Task definitions are consistent with the label structure documented in instances (participant-level diagnostic labels across five cohorts) and with the feature products actually released, so the stated tasks are supportable by the distributed data.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund'; notes: 'Bridge2AI program award OT2OD032720, "Bridge2AI: Voice as a Biomarker of Health - Building an ethically sourced, bioaccoustic database to understand disease like never before"... NIH RePORTER lists application 11376382 under project number 3OT2OD032720-01S3, with principal investigator Bensoussan, Yael Emilie at the University of South Florida, a fiscal year 2025 award amount of 4,660,942, a project start of 1 September 2022 and a project end of 30 November 2026' The funder is named along with the specific programme, the award title, the principal investigator and institution, the award amount and the project period. The funding mechanism (an OT2 Other Transaction under the Common Fund) is identifiable from the activity code. Funding logic check passes: the grantor is stated and the award is documented in funders.notes, which the instrument accepts as an alternative representation to a structured grants block. Funding goals align with purposes — the award title names exactly the ethically sourced bioacoustic database the dataset instantiates.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].notes: 'Bridge2AI program award OT2OD032720... The PhysioNet releases credit NIH project number 3OT2OD032720-01S1. NIH RePORTER lists application 11376382 under project number 3OT2OD032720-01S3' Three related identifiers are given — the base award, and two supplement project numbers — with the source of each attributed (PhysioNet release credit versus NIH RePORTER). Distinguishing which identifier appears in which source is more informative than a single unattributed number. NIH pattern validation passes: OT2OD032720 decomposes correctly into activity code OT2 (Other Transaction award, the mechanism the Common Fund uses for Bridge2AI), institute code OD (Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund programmes) and serial number 032720. The extended forms 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and -01S3 are well-formed NIH project numbers with application type 3 (supplement) and suffix S denoting a supplement, internally consistent with the base award.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: fifteen entries with principal_investigator, affiliations and, for several, credit_roles (funding_acquisition, software) and notes identifying their module role — e.g. Yaël Bensoussan (USF, co-PI, co-lead of data acquisition), Satrajit Ghosh (MIT McGovern, lead investigator mood disorders, corresponding author of the v3.1.0 release), Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon and Vardit Ravitsky (ethics module), Jordan Lerner-Ellis (genomic collection under separate Canadian approval); created_by: Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium; maintainers: three entries including PhysioNet and the consortium DACO Creators are individually attributed with institution and functional role, using CRediT-style credit_roles where applicable, so responsibility for each module is traceable to a person. source_caveats discloses that the PhysioNet release names 120 authors and that the fifteen recorded here are the co-PIs and lead investigators, which prevents the list being misread as complete. Creator affiliations are consistent with the multi-site structure described in the description and in human_subject_research (five North American sites, US single-IRB plus Canadian REBs); the Canadian institutions appearing among the creators match the separate-approval statement.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: three entries — 'A custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet collected acoustic tasks, surveys and validated questionnaires, and sent data over a secure HTTPS protocol to HIPAA-compliant cloud storage provided by NIH STRIDES partners'; 'Recordings were made on iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 head-mounted microphone connected through an Apple dongle; distinct iPad devices were used at each site'; REDCap maintenance and export. Supported by collection_timeframes (twelve months), data_collectors (three roles), direct_collection ('in clinic, with the assistance of a trained research assistant') Settings are described to the level of specific hardware models and the microphone part number, the transport security, the storage environment, the personnel present and the clinical setting. The disclosure that distinct devices were used at each site is the kind of detail that lets a reanalyst reason about site confounding, and it is picked up again as a measurement bias. Consistent with the measurement_bias entry in known_biases and with the anomaly about differing site configurations; three parts of the record describe the same device heterogeneity without contradiction. The 22-task protocol in notes complements the mechanism description.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: three typed entries — was_directly_observed/was_reported_by_subjects ('Acoustic tasks were recorded directly from participants with a tablet application, while demographics, confounders and validated questionnaires were self-reported'); was_validated_verified ('Clinical diagnoses were verified by clinicians reviewing audio and imaging data, electronic health records, or medication prescriptions, against cohort-specific gold standards such as laryngoscopy and stroboscopy, CT and MRI of the brain, and spirometry with flow-volume loops'); was_inferred_derived ('All released feature data were derived computationally from the raw waveforms with open-source toolkits'). raw_data_sources with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details The three acquisition modalities are distinguished with boolean flags and each is explained, so a user can tell for any given field whether it was observed, self-reported, clinically verified or computed. Naming the gold standard per cohort makes the provenance of the diagnostic labels auditable. The was_inferred_derived flag correctly characterises the released products, which are entirely derived features; this agrees with the description and with preprocessing_strategies. Gold standards named are clinically appropriate to their respective cohorts.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: eight entries with reproducible parameters (16 kHz monaural with Butterworth anti-aliasing; spectrograms 201×T via 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled 2× in time; 60 mel bins and 60 MFCCs; SPARC articulatory features at 50 Hz over six articulators; ppgs over 40 phonemes at 100 Hz; openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth/torchaudio static features; BIDS v1.9.0 conversion; b2aiprep v3.0.0). cleaning_strategies: 'No data cleaning was performed. An audit protocol was applied instead: missingness tables were generated, distributions and outliers checked, categorical responses checked against the schema, and quality control metrics run on the audio'. labeling_strategies: two entries with annotations_per_item: 1, data_annotation_protocol 'Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes' and annotator_demographics. annotation_analyses: 'No inter-annotator agreement analysis was performed. A single labeler provided the diagnostic label for each instance' The preprocessing pipeline is specified at a level that would permit reimplementation — every transform with its window, hop, dimensionality and frame rate. The cleaning and annotation-quality entries are candid negatives that still convey substance: no cleaning but a described audit protocol; no agreement statistic but a stated reason (single labeler) and an explicit warning that Whisper transcriptions were produced by unaudited off-the-shelf models. Preprocessing parameters agree exactly with the per-variable derivation strings in variables, so the two blocks corroborate rather than merely coexist. The single-labeler admission is consistent with annotation_bias in known_biases and with the methodological limitation in known_limitations. Imputation is addressed via missing_data_documentation ('No imputation is performed') though no structured imputation_protocols block exists; logged as a low-severity issue.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Evidence carried by preprocessing_strategies prose, machine_annotation_tools, variables.measurement_technique and external_resources. preprocessing_strategies: 'All processing was performed with the open-source b2aiprep library, which organizes and preprocesses the dataset, and senselab, which processes the audio files; version 3.1.0 was generated with b2aiprep v3.0.0'; 'Static acoustic, phonetic and prosodic features were extracted with openSMILE, Praat and parselmouth, and pitch contours with torchaudio'; 'Articulatory features were produced with the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package'; 'Phonetic posteriorgrams... generated at 100 Hz with the ppgs package'. machine_annotation_tools.tools: ['OpenAI Whisper Large'] with tool_descriptions and tool_accuracy. external_resources: b2aiprep at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab at https://github.com/sensein/senselab The threshold is comfortably met: the named software is squarely in the producing-and-transforming role, not in the excluded capture, hosting, packaging, validation or other-output roles. b2aiprep converted the raw waveforms into the Parquet files being distributed and merged the source data into the phenotype files; senselab processed the audio; openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc and ppgs each produced named released feature sets. Beyond the bare name the record supplies a pinned version (b2aiprep v3.0.0 generated this release), repository URLs and licences — the strengthening evidence the sub-element asks for. Tool-to-product attribution is traceable in both directions: each variable's measurement_technique names the tool that produced it and matches the corresponding preprocessing_strategies entry. Whisper Large is disclosed as a transformation applied to the data with an explicit statement that its accuracy is unaudited, which is honest rather than promotional. The pinned b2aiprep version means the release is reproducible from the stated toolchain.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: six entries with URLs, licences (MIT, Apache-2.0), archival flags and access restrictions, covering the REDCap data dictionary, b2aiprep, senselab, project documentation, Synapse controlled access and FHIR profiles; conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0 with scope caveat; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: 'No imputation is performed. A missingness table is included with the dataset'; related_datasets includes the Interspeech 2024 protocol paper (doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926) and the Zenodo-archived data dictionary (doi:10.5281/zenodo.12760724) All three limbs are addressed. External resources are not bare links: each carries its licence or access condition and an archival flag, so a user can judge persistence. The imputation limb is satisfied by an explicit statement that imputation was not used — which the sub-element accepts — backed by a shipped missingness table rather than silence. Standards references are used correctly and the published protocol paper provides an external, citable account of the collection methodology. source_caveats notes that the healthsheet describes the dataset as self-contained and that these resources are supporting material rather than dependencies, which correctly characterises their role.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: six typed entries — coverage_limitation (English-only, with Spanish protocols under development as recommended_mitigation); representativeness_limitation (five sites in the US and Canada, with scope_impact on generalization); scope_limitation (derived features only, raw recordings withheld, free-speech features removed, with the DACO route as mitigation); coverage_limitation (no imaging, genomic, laryngoscopy or EHR multimodal data released); temporal_limitation (protocol changed during the twelve-month collection, distribution shift expected); methodological_limitation (single labeler; psychiatric labels from EHR entry or active prescription rather than session assessment) Limitations are typed, specific, and several carry either a mitigation or a statement of the scope impact. They cover the dimensions that most affect reuse — language, geography, modality, time and label quality — and the methodological entry concedes a weakness in the labels that a less careful record would leave buried in the labeling section. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the English-only restriction matches human_subject_research.special_populations, the site count matches the description, the feature-only scope matches is_deidentified, and the single-labeler point matches annotation_analyses. No limitation contradicts a claim made elsewhere in the record.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: four entries using the BiasTypeEnum vocabulary — selection_bias (recruitment at high-volume expert clinics; 'Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in artificial intelligence, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, were less likely to be recruited', with a shift to remote collection as mitigation_strategy); representation_bias (unequal disease distribution, skew by site and demographics, with affected_subsets and mitigation); measurement_bias (site-specific devices and configurations, variable headset distance, noise artifacts, with affected_subsets); annotation_bias (single clinician, EHR or prescription-derived labels, varying diagnostic practice). future_use_impacts: three entries on generalization and unfair treatment, unaudited transcription models, and anticipated distribution shift Bias categories come from the controlled taxonomy and each carries a causal mechanism rather than an acknowledgement, with affected_subsets and mitigation_strategy where they apply. The selection_bias entry reaches beyond geography to trust in medicine and in AI, which is a substantive fairness analysis. The social-impact limb required by the source-rubric scope is covered by future_use_impacts. Taxonomy terms are applied correctly to their mechanisms: device heterogeneity is measurement bias, cohort imbalance is representation bias, single-labeler diagnosis is annotation bias. No miscategorisation. Consistent with sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and with the subpopulations distribution statements.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: five entries — differing site collection configurations and a protocol that changed during the study; 'Noise artifacts are present in the recordings; the head-mounted headset microphone could sit at slightly different distances from participant to participant'; varying diagnostic practice between sites and clinicians, and possibly inaccurate or under-reported questionnaire responses; recordings that could not produce particular features, so record counts differ between feature types; 'Some Parquet files distributed in version 3.0.0 were broken and were fixed in version 3.1.0' Anomalies span acquisition artifacts, protocol drift, label-practice variability, systematic feature absence and an outright file defect in a prior release. Disclosing the broken Parquet files rather than quietly fixing them is a meaningful act of transparency toward anyone who analysed v3.0.0. The cleaning_strategies audit protocol and the released audio_quality_metrics.tsv give users the means to assess quality themselves. The feature-absence anomaly is quantitatively corroborated by the differing per-feature counts in instances.notes and by variables.quality_notes; the Parquet defect is corroborated by the v3.1.0 erratum. Anomalies and known_biases overlap on device heterogeneity, which is appropriate since it is both a quality issue and a bias mechanism.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: content_warnings.content_warnings_present: true with warnings: 'The collection includes free speech tasks whose transcription may contain offensive or distressing content... Dense features and transcripts derived from free-speech prompts were removed from the released feature set, and audio recordings containing potentially identifying information or external voices were removed. Questionnaire content covers depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress and other psychiatric symptoms'; sensitive_elements: three entries (race and ethnic origin; sexual orientation; socioeconomic and health information including clinical diagnoses and psychiatric and respiratory questionnaire responses); confidential_elements with confidentiality_details Both limbs are populated and the warning is paired with the mitigation actually applied, so a user learns not only that free speech could contain distressing content but that the derived features and transcripts were removed on that account. The psychiatric questionnaire content is flagged, which matters for secondary analysts as well as for participants. A low-severity tension is logged between sensitive_elements_present: true for attributes such as sexual orientation and the notes on the same block stating that REDCap-flagged sensitive fields were removed before release; the scope of what survives into the published release is left ambiguous. This is a clarity defect rather than a contradiction, and the sub-element's requirement — that sensitive content be described and warnings given — is met.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: University of South Florida IRB with review_details covering the acquisition protocol, the sharing of collected data, single-IRB subsite approval, the observational design and the absence of a data monitoring committee; future_use_impacts: three entries — skew leading to poor generalization and potentially unfair treatment of groups; unaudited off-the-shelf transcription models whose errors may propagate downstream; anticipated distribution shift from changing site configurations, protocol and diagnostic practice. data_governance.notes cites the published memorandum 'Ethical Justification for Controlled Access to Raw Voice Data Samples' Both limbs are substantive. The social-impact analysis is forward-looking and specific about the mechanism of harm in each case, and the discouraged_uses entries on hiring, insurance and surveillance extend it to the misuse scenarios most plausible for voice biomarkers. A published ethics memorandum backs the governance design rather than leaving it asserted. future_use_impacts correctly implements the rai:dataSocialImpact concept the source rubric points at. The ethical review is consistent with human_subject_research.irb_approval, which names the same board and the same single-IRB arrangement. Conflicts of interest are not addressed, which is a minor gap against the fullest reading of the scope but does not undercut the documented review.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://physionet.org; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; maintainers[0]: 'PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and supported by NIBIB, NHLBI and the NIH Office of the Director, hosts the current releases and provides continued access to credentialed researchers'; maintainers[2] describes the Health Data Nexus (T-CAIREM, University of Toronto) which hosted v1.0 PhysioNet is a recognised domain repository and the record goes further than naming it, identifying its operator, its funding support and its access model. The platform history including the earlier Health Data Nexus hosting is preserved rather than overwritten, so citations to v1.0 remain resolvable in context. The publisher is consistent with the 10.13026 DOI prefix, which is PhysioNet's registrant prefix — platform identity is corroborated by the identifier rather than only asserted. source_caveats explains the preference for the PhysioNet statement over the project documentation's Health Data Nexus description.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., Dorr, D., Payne, P., Ravitsky, V., Belisle-Pipon, J., Bahr, R., Watts, S., Bolser, D., Siu, J., Lerner-Ellis, J., Rudzicz, F., Boyer, M., Abdel-Aty, Y., Ahmed Syed, T., Anibal, J., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 A complete, formatted citation string with author list, year, versioned title, publisher and resolvable DOI — directly usable without reconstruction. Both the version-pinned and the version-independent DOI are available, so a citing author can choose whether to pin. The citation's version (3.1.0), year (2026) and DOI all agree with the version, issued and doi fields. The embedded RRID:SCR_007345 is well formed but identifies PhysioNet rather than the dataset; logged as a low-severity semantic_understanding issue. Cross-referencing is fully served by the DOI.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0, applied to the audio dataset layout and the phenotype folder organization rather than to the Parquet feature files of the published feature-only release'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; external_resources includes 'FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, published by the consortium'; labeling uses ICD-10; instances use B2AI ontology codes Conformance spans a community data-organisation standard with a version number, a metadata schema with a named class, a clinical interoperability standard (FHIR profiles the consortium itself contributed), and clinical and domain vocabularies. Contributing FHIR profiles back is community integration in the strong sense, not merely consumption of a standard. The BIDS scope caveat is semantically precise and prevents an overclaim. The record candidly notes that the FHIR profile source repository URL is not captured in the bundle, distinguishing what it knows from what it does not.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: 'Project documentation and dashboards at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, with source code at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs' (MIT), plus the REDCap data dictionary and instrument PDFs at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived on Zenodo, b2aiprep and senselab repositories; page: the PhysioNet landing page; existing_uses: 'A restricted version of the dataset containing raw audio has been used in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon' and 'Training opportunities... through the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars program at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep Outreach is documented as an actual programme rather than a promise: a summer school, a hackathon and a named scholars programme with its own URL, alongside a documentation site with dashboards and openly licensed instrument PDFs. The extension mechanism invites contribution through repository issues and pull requests, which is a live community channel. All URLs are well formed with plausible domains. The documentation, training and contribution routes are mutually consistent and consistent with the open-source licences declared on the same resources.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_supplemented_by doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric dataset v1.1.0, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2–18, Hospital for Sick Children REB, parental consent with child assent); is_new_version_of doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0); is_version_of doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI); is_new_version_of doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 (v1.0, Health Data Nexus); is_documented_by doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926; is_documented_by doi:10.5281/zenodo.12760724 Six relationships, every one typed and DOI-resolvable, spanning a companion cohort, two prior versions, the concept identifier and two documenting works. Each carries a description substantial enough to tell a user whether the target is worth following, including the pediatric cohort's distinct ethics and assent arrangements. Relationship types are semantically correct throughout, with is_version_of reserved for the concept DOI and is_new_version_of for superseded releases. DOI prefixes are plausible for their targets: 10.13026 PhysioNet, 10.57764 Health Data Nexus, 10.21437 ISCA/Interspeech, 10.5281 Zenodo.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; citation includes 'RRID:SCR_007345' and 'https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 A versioned DOI and a version-independent DOI are both supplied, and id mirrors the versioned DOI, so the record is uniquely and stably identifiable at two granularities. name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description runs approximately 2,300 characters covering 833 participants, five North American sites, four disease cohorts plus controls, the full acoustic task battery, the questionnaire battery by cohort, the diagnostic gold standards, and the composition of the public release Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: named instruments (VHI-10, PHQ-9, GAD-7, PANAS, MoCA, Dyspnea Index, Leicester Cough Questionnaire), named validation modalities (laryngoscopy, stroboscopy, spirometry, brain CT and MRI) and the explicit statement that raw audio is withheld while derived features are released. Description content matches the claimed dataset type throughout. Technical terms are used correctly: spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, phonetic posteriorgrams and electromagnetic articulography estimates are all genuine acoustic feature families and are consistent with the tooling named in preprocessing_strategies. The participant count of 833 is consistent with instances[0].counts and with subsets.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai] - four terms only Below the five-term threshold and, more substantively, the four terms cover only the broadest domain framing plus the funding program. None of the conditions (laryngeal cancer, Parkinson's disease, ALS, depression, chronic cough, airway stenosis), methods (machine learning, acoustic features, MFCC, spectrogram), modalities (speech, cough, respiratory sound) or standards (BIDS) documented elsewhere in this record are discoverable through the keyword set. A user searching for any specific condition or method in this dataset would not retrieve it. The keywords present are individually relevant and correctly used, and 'bridge2ai' is a legitimate program tag corroborated by funders.grantor and the description. The failure is one of coverage rather than correctness: the record demonstrably contains the material for a rich keyword set and does not surface it.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; file_collections enumerates four collections with paths and collection_type (features/processed_data, metadata/metadata, phenotype/processed_data, b2ai-voice-audio/raw_data); subsets enumerates eight named components A version-pinned landing page plus a genuine hierarchical resource structure. Each file_collection names its constituent files (nine Parquet feature files by filename, audio_quality_metrics.tsv, static_features.tsv) and the phenotype collection enumerates all four subfolders and their tables, so a user can locate a specific file before downloading. The page URL is version-specific and matches version 3.1.0, the DOI and the access_urls in distribution_formats. Domain physionet.org is plausible and matches publisher. The BIDS path template for audio is syntactically well formed and consistent with the declared BIDS v1.9.0 conformance.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets carries six typed relationships: derives_from (Synapse syn72370534 raw audio), is_supplemented_by (doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 pediatric dataset), is_new_version_of (doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68 v3.0.0; doi:10.13026/249v-w155 v1.1; doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 v1.0), is_version_of (doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 version-independent DOI) The dataset is positioned within a full lineage: upstream raw audio, a sibling pediatric release, three predecessor versions and the concept DOI, each with a target identifier and an explanatory description rather than a bare link. name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms describes the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, credentialed access, permitted duplication, prohibition on sale, non-transfer of IP, the Fort Lauderdale Agreement and 'No fees are associated with these restrictions'; ip_restrictions.restrictions lists four specific provisions Both the access policy and the IP position are stated in operational terms. The IP restrictions go beyond boilerplate: they forbid using IP protection or database rights to block access to the data or to conclusions drawn from it, while explicitly permitting downstream IP on derivative work subject to non-obstructive licensing, and record that no third party has imposed restrictions. Restrictiveness is proportionate to the sensitivity documented elsewhere: registered access with a signed agreement for de-identified derived features, matching sensitive_elements and is_deidentified. The Fort Lauderdale reference is used correctly in its data-sharing sense. license_and_use_terms is consistent with the top-level license field and with third_party_sharing.is_shared: true.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance states no export controls apply, a Certificate of Confidentiality covers identifiable source data and must be asserted against subpoenas and court orders, recipients must apply administrative, physical and technical safeguards and notify the provider of unauthorized disclosure within five business days, and must meet PhysioNet requirements; data_governance.committee_name: 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org in access_review_process and in maintainers A sensitivity classification, a HIPAA status, an explicit negative finding on export control, a Certificate of Confidentiality with its legal effect described, concrete security and breach-notification obligations, and a reachable governance committee with a named contact address. This is the full scope of the sub-element including the governance-contact requirement. The governance contact is carried in data_governance.committee_name plus the email in access_review_process rather than in the dedicated committee_contact slot, which is a placement rather than a substance gap. confidentiality_level 'restricted' is consistent with registered-plus-controlled access, with a HIPAA-covered clinical source, and with prohibited_uses forbidding re-identification - the classification is not inflated relative to the safeguards described.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats[].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ (twice, for Parquet and TSV) and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ (for controlled-access WAV); page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; data_governance.access_review_process gives the step sequence for both tiers; raw_data_sources[0].access_details names Synapse syn72370534 and DACO@b2ai-voice.org The sub-element asks for direct download links or platform access instructions; both are present. A user is told the exact platform for each component and the precise sequence to obtain it: PhysioNet registration, identity confirmation, credentialing and signature of the Registered Access Agreement with no training requirement for features; Data Access Request Form, Data Use Agreement, DACO review and an authorized official's signature on a Data Use and Transfer Agreement before Synapse release for audio. The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated, which is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue, but the access point is unambiguous and appears in three mutually consistent places. URLs are structurally valid and the Synapse accession syn72370534 matches the identifier given in related_datasets.derives_from, so the two tiers cross-reference correctly.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats lists three entries: Apache Parquet for dense derived features and per-recording metadata; tab-separated values for static features, audio quality metrics and phenotype tables, each paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name; WAV audio organized per BIDS under controlled access. file_collections[].conforms_to: 'Apache Parquet and tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries', 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries', 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0' Formats are named specifically and mapped to the exact content each carries, down to which feature families are in Parquet and which tables are in TSV. Nine Parquet files are named individually in file_collections. Format choices are semantically appropriate to the content: columnar Parquet for dense per-frame feature arrays, TSV plus JSON dictionaries for participant-level tabular phenotype data, WAV for waveforms. MIME media_type values are not given, a minor gap, but format identification is unambiguous without them.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: six typed relationships with targets. external_resources: seven entries including b2aiprep (https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, Apache-2.0), senselab (https://github.com/sensein/senselab), the REDCap data dictionary (https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, MIT), the documentation site (https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, source archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, MIT), FHIR voice profiles, the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication, and the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars training program Each external resource carries a URL, most carry a license, and each carries an archival boolean distinguishing Zenodo-archived resources from live ones - which is precisely the persistence information a reuser needs. The honest recording that the healthsheet answered 'NA' on persistence guarantees is preserved rather than papered over. All domains are plausible and consistent with the actors named elsewhere: sensein hosts b2aiprep, which preprocessing_strategies credits with assembling the release; eipm corresponds to the Englander Institute for Precision Medicine, which creators names as Elemento's and Sigaras's institution. Zenodo DOIs use the correct 10.5281 prefix.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms permits duplication as reasonably required for the approved research project; intended_uses.usage_notes: 'intended for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by authorized researchers'; collection_consents records that consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, to a geographic location, to a research type, to genetic research, or away from methods and algorithm development Reuse permissions are stated affirmatively and their consent basis is documented, which is stronger than a bare license label: the record shows why commercial and algorithmic use is permissible by tracing it to what participants agreed to. This is a bespoke registered-access license rather than a standard CC instrument, so reuse rights must be read from license_terms; those terms are specific enough to act on. The permissions granted are consistent with consent scope and with prohibited_uses, which constrain re-identification, harm, IP obstruction, resale and participant contact - none of which conflict with general research reuse.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: Apache Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented binary data file format'), tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries, WAV organized per BIDS; conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; file_collections[].conforms_to repeats the format declaration per collection Every distributed component uses a widely supported open format, and the pairing of each tabular file with a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem is a stated convention a reuser can rely on programmatically. Formats are standard and correctly characterized. Character encoding is not stated for the TSV and JSON components, the one gap in the sub-element's stated scope; it does not undermine reuse because the formats themselves are unambiguous and JSON is UTF-8 by specification. Scored 1 on the strength of format standardization with the encoding gap recorded.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections[b2ai-voice-audio].conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; external_resources references FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker published by the consortium; instances carry ontology term identifiers B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, B2AI_TOPIC:4, B2AI_TOPIC:36 Conformance is declared at three levels - data organization (BIDS, versioned), metadata schema (the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema with a resolvable w3id URI and a named class), and vocabulary (B2AI substrate and topic CURIEs on instances) - plus a FHIR profile contribution. BIDS is named with a specific version, which matters because BIDS extended to audio only in recent releases; v1.9.0 is a plausible version for audio support. The w3id.org URI is a persistent-identifier service appropriate for schema identification. The B2AI CURIEs are well formed prefix:number identifiers consistent with the Bridge2AI program affiliation asserted in funders and description.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field is present anywhere in the record. The nearest content is file_collections[phenotype].description, which enumerates table names ('confounders.tsv', 'demographics.tsv', the 18 diagnosis tables, the 13 questionnaire instruments, the 7 task tables) and states each table is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name'; instances[1].label_description names participant_id, session_id and task name as the recording identifiers; participant_privacy.data_linkage names participant_id and session_id as the join keys The record establishes that variable-level documentation exists and where it lives, and it names the three linking variables, but supplies no variable metadata itself: no identifiers, types, units, permissible values or descriptions for any of the phenotype columns or feature fields. A reuser cannot assess whether a given measurement is present, or how it is coded, without obtaining the release. Given that the sub-element asks specifically for variable-level metadata with identifiers and descriptions, describing the existence of data dictionaries does not meet it. This is a genuine absence rather than a placement issue - no alternative slot in the record carries variable-level metadata. It is notable against the record's own claim of conformance to a metadata schema whose Dataset class provides a variables slot, and against the AI-readiness self-assessment in notes recording 'contextualized not met' under computability, which is consistent with this gap.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three use categories (clinical ML research, voice biomarker research, methods/standards/cohort construction) each with examples and usage_notes. prohibited_uses: five prohibitions each with a stated reason - re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatization, IP-based obstruction of access, resale, and contacting subjects without IRB approval, written provider approval and consent. discouraged_uses: three with reasons - hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment, surveillance. existing_uses: Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon. All three guidance categories are populated, and each entry gives a reason rather than a bare rule, so a user facing an unlisted use case can reason by analogy. The discouraged-use entries identify the specific harm mechanism in each case. The guidance is internally coherent and traceable to other fields: the re-identification prohibition follows from participant_privacy.reidentification_risk stating voice is inherently identifying; the harm and stigmatization prohibition follows from sensitive_elements covering psychiatric and substance-use content; the hiring and insurance discouragements follow from future_use_impacts on skew-driven unfair treatment. Guidance restrictiveness is proportionate to the documented sensitivity.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: two entries - University of South Florida IRB (single IRB with subsite IRBs approved through the sIRB process; approval covers both the clinical study and the data collection and sharing; not a drug or device study; no data monitoring committee) and the Canadian research ethics boards (Mount Sinai Hospital, The Hospital for Sick Children, University of Toronto, applying separately because Canadian institutions fall outside the US sIRB process, with copies submitted to the USF IRB; genomic work under a separate protocol). human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: true with irb_approval, ethics_review_board and regulatory_compliance (partial HIPAA waiver for chart review during screening; Certificate of Confidentiality). data_protection_impacts: ethicist team review identifying sensitive fields for removal, plus a published memorandum justifying controlled access for raw voice on re-identification and misuse grounds. data_governance.committee_name: DACO with contact address. Oversight is documented at the level of who approved what, under which regulatory mechanism, and how a cross-border complication was handled - the Canadian sIRB exception is the kind of detail that is normally omitted. The DPIA component is present in substance: a named review activity, a stated finding (which fields to remove) and a published justification for the access restriction that followed. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is true and IRB approval is populated as required. The record itself flags in data_protection_impacts.source_caveats that the healthsheet answered 'No' to whether a formal impact analysis was conducted; that tension is recorded as a low-severity issue rather than treated as a failure, because the activities described do constitute an impact assessment in substance and the discrepancy is disclosed rather than hidden. Ethics claims are plausible against scope: a five-site multinational clinical collection with psychiatric and neurological cohorts would be expected to carry exactly this oversight structure.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers, of highly sensitive non-identifying elements, and of all raw voice data from the public release'. identifiers_removed enumerates names, addresses and geographic locators, SSNs, dates finer than year, phone and fax, email and IP, medical record and health plan numbers, device and licence and account and vehicle identifiers, URLs, full-face photos and biometric identifiers, state and province with only country retained, narrative text and free-speech transcripts, household composition and cultural identity, household income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences, and raw voice recordings. deidentification_details describes the rationale for direct versus indirect identifier removal, transcript review for identifying content and external voices, removal of all REDCap-flagged sensitive fields, withholding of spectrogram-family features from open-response prompts, and states that k-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved. A named standard, an enumerated removal list that goes well beyond the eighteen Safe Harbor categories, the decision rule used for indirect identifiers, and - unusually - an explicit negative statement about the anonymity level achieved. The disclosure that k-anonymity is not achieved is more useful to a risk-assessing reuser than a bare compliance claim would be. Consistency checks pass: deidentification is claimed and the method is specified; identifiers_removed is listed.
