The method is appropriate to the data type - Safe Harbor addresses the tabular phenotype data, while the separate and stronger control of withholding raw waveforms addresses the biometric modality that Safe Harbor does not reach, which is the semantically correct response to voice data. The tension between identifiable_elements_present: false and the k-anonymity admission is recorded as a medium-severity consistency issue; it does not defeat the sub-element, whose subject is whether the method is described, and it is described with unusual candour.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method: removal of direct and Safe Harbor identifiers, removal of high-risk indirect identifiers, removal of narrative text, generalization of geography to country, exclusion of raw waveforms. privacy_techniques: tiered dissemination (registered access for derived features, controlled access for audio), retention of identifiable data behind institutional firewalls, study identifiers in place of institutional identifiers, transcript review, HTTPS transmission to HIPAA-compliant storage, federated learning infrastructure permitting training without data leaving the institution. data_linkage: released records joined by participant_id and session_id, with the re-identification key held at each institution and excluded from the release. reidentification_risk: 'Voice is inherently identifying and cannot be fully de-identified, so raw voice data was removed from the public release... K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved for the released tables.' The risk assessment states a mechanism (voice is inherently identifying), a mitigation tied to that mechanism (waveforms withheld, audio under controlled access) and a quantified residual limitation (k-anonymity not achieved). The privacy techniques span technical, organizational and architectural controls including federated training, which is a substantive rather than decorative measure. Consistency check passes: data_protection_impacts is present and reidentification_risk is assessed, as required. The assessment is technically correct - voice is a biometric and Safe Harbor explicitly lists biometric identifiers, so the decision to withhold waveforms rather than claim de-identified audio is the semantically appropriate conclusion. data_linkage is consistent with instances[1].label_description, which names the same two keys.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: 'Prospective written informed consent obtained before data collection, with parental permission and child assent used for the pediatric arm'; consent_documentation describes paper, in-app electronic, REDCap survey and in-app video modalities, upload of paper forms to REDCap, and retention for at least five years after study completion; consent_scope covers voice and health data collection, EHR access for gold-standard validation, sharing of non-directly-identifying data with external researchers, registered-access public release of low-risk data and controlled-access release of higher-risk data; withdrawal_mechanism specifies withdrawal at any point, exclusion of data if withdrawal precedes completion of voice collection, non-removal thereafter, and an optional satisfaction survey collecting no PHI. Corroborated by collection_consents (three entries), consent_revocations and collection_notifications. Consent is documented across type, modality, evidentiary record, scope and withdrawal, and the scope maps one-to-one onto the release tiers actually used. The frank statement that data cannot be withdrawn once voice collection is complete is a real limitation disclosed rather than elided. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is true and consent is documented, as required; IRB approval is documented and consent procedures are described alongside it, satisfying the second paired check. The video-consent modality is described as serving identity verification for submitted acoustic data, which is a coherent and modality-appropriate rationale. Consent scope is consistent with license_and_use_terms (commercial use permitted) and with data_governance's two access tiers - three fields agreeing on the same permission structure.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false; special_protections: adult cohort restricted to participants 18 or older able to read and speak English and to provide informed consent for themselves, with those unable to consent in English excluded; notes: the pediatric cohort under the same collection protocol was recruited only at pediatric sites with parental or guardian permission and verbal assent from approximately age seven where developmentally appropriate, and is published separately. participant_compensation.compensation_provided: true; compensation_type: 'Electronic gift cards'; compensation_amount: '40 US dollars for a data collection session taking less than 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for a session taking over 90 minutes, for no more than three sessions and a maximum total compensation of 120 US dollars.' Compensation is fully specified - form, tiered amount, session cap and total cap - which is the level of detail needed to judge whether an inducement is undue. The special_protections and notes describe real capacity and assent safeguards for both the adult and pediatric arms. The at_risk_groups_included: false flag is in tension with subsets, which enumerate cohorts including mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and substance use disorder - populations conventionally treated as at risk. Recorded as a medium-severity content_accuracy issue. The sub-element is nonetheless met: the record documents the protection actually relied on (self-consent capacity as an eligibility criterion, excluding those unable to consent) and the pediatric assent procedure, so the substantive documentation the sub-element asks for is present even though the boolean understates the cohort composition. The compensation amounts are modest and session-proportionate, consistent with the IRB approval documented in sub-element 1.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification names age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status from the demographics instrument plus the five disease-cohort groupings; distribution states the releases do not contain an equal distribution across cohorts and that skews exist by disorder, site and demographic factors. subsets carries five cohort entries each with is_subpopulation: true and paragraph-length inclusion and exclusion criteria - for example the neurological cohort specifies ages over 44 and under 85, English fluency, the eligible diagnoses down to subtype (sporadic versus familial ALS, MSA, PSP, corticobasal degeneration), the surgical-intervention exclusion, and validation by brain CT, brain MRI, whole genome sequencing and serum p-tau. Cohort definition is at protocol level rather than summary level: each of the five cohorts carries its own eligibility logic, exclusions and diagnostic gold standards. A reuser can determine whether a given patient would have been eligible. The cohorts named in subsets match the four disease groups plus controls named in the description, and the demographic axes match those listed as removed or generalized in is_deidentified, with no contradiction. Clinical terminology is used correctly throughout (Reinke's edema, adductor and abductor spasmodic dysphonia, glottic insufficiency, presbyphonia). The candid distribution statement agrees with known_biases.representation_bias.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances[0].counts: 833 adult participants. instances[1] reports per-feature record counts in notes: torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc electromagnetic articulography 28,640. version_access.version_details records that the initial release provided 12,523 recordings for 306 participants. subsets carry is_data_split: false and splits documents that no recommended splits are provided. Counts are given at both levels that matter, and the per-feature breakdown is more informative than a single recording total would be because it tells a reuser exactly how many records each feature file contains and why they differ (withheld sensitive records and audio checks, plus files that could not be processed). The participant count is consistent across description, instances and source_caveats. The absence of an aggregate recording count is explained in instances[1].source_caveats, which records that the project documentation cites approximately 61,937 recordings for v3.0 while the preferred PhysioNet v3.1.0 source gives only per-feature counts - a disclosed source conflict rather than an omission. The per-feature counts are internally plausible: the spectrogram family shares an identical 29,278 and sits below the pitch counts, consistent with the stated exclusion of spectrogram-family features from free-speech audio.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: subsets: all eight entries carry explicit is_data_split and is_subpopulation booleans - five cohorts as is_subpopulation: true / is_data_split: false, and the features, phenotype and metadata components as false / false. splits.split_details: 'No recommended training, validation or test splits are provided. Researchers are encouraged to create their own splits... taking into account the skews in the data by disorder category, site and demographic factors.' file_collections[phenotype].description enumerates the subfolders and names every table (18 diagnosis tables, 13 questionnaire instruments, 7 task tables, 3 enrollment tables, confounders and demographics) and states each is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name', with the row-inclusion rule 'A file contains a row for a participant only if at least one column is not missing'. file_collections[features] names all nine Parquet files and states static_features.tsv has one row per unique recording. The split and subpopulation flags - which this sub-element names explicitly - are present, complete and correctly assigned across all eight subsets, and the absence of recommended splits is documented with a reason rather than left blank. Column-level structure is documented by reference: the reuser learns the table inventory, the row granularity of each component and where the per-column dictionaries live. Two named components of this composite item are absent: no variables block (scored 0 at Element 3 sub-element 4, where variable metadata is the sole subject) and no is_tabular flag, recorded as a low-severity issue. Scored 1 because the flag and split components are fully and correctly documented and the structural account is detailed enough to support the element's question about understanding dataset structure, but the gap is material and is not treated as trivial. The row-inclusion rule is consistent with missing_data_documentation.missing_data_patterns, which states the same rule.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances[0].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4 with data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41; instances[1].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36 with data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; instances[].label: true with label_description explaining that each participant carries a clinician-assigned diagnostic label following Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes. Conditions are enumerated exhaustively in subsets: laryngeal cancer T1-T4, laryngitis by aetiology, pre-cancerous lesions, benign vocal fold lesions by type, muscle tension dysphonia, spasmodic dysphonia and laryngeal tremor, unilateral vocal fold paralysis, glottic insufficiency and presbyphonia, airway stenosis by level, unexplained chronic cough, MCI, Alzheimer's, frontotemporal and Lewy body and vascular dementias, ALS, Parkinson's and related parkinsonism, anxiety, bipolar I and II, depression, and named psychiatric comorbidities. Topics are represented both as controlled-vocabulary CURIEs on the instances and as an exhaustive clinical enumeration in the subsets, with ICD-10 named as the coding system for the labels. The diagnosis subfolder listing gives 18 condition table names that correspond to the enumerated cohorts. The controlled-vocabulary identifiers are well-formed B2AI CURIEs consistent with the program affiliation. The conditions enumerated are all genuinely conditions with voice, speech or respiratory manifestations, matching the description's stated recruitment basis ('conditions known to manifest in the voice waveform'), so the topic coverage is semantically coherent with the dataset's purpose. The 18 diagnosis table names in file_collections map onto the cohort conditions without orphans in either direction.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: six entries - differing site configurations and protocol change over time; noise artifacts and varying head-mounted microphone distance; inter-clinician and inter-site diagnostic variation with diagnosis sometimes taken from an EHR or an active prescription; possible questionnaire inaccuracy and underreporting; derived text such as transcription generated by unaudited off-the-shelf models; some audio files unable to generate certain derived features. sampling_strategies: is_sample true, is_random false, is_representative false, with purposive recruitment from clinics seeing more than 50 patients per month in the disease area, pre-visit screening against cohort criteria, why_not_representative and representative_verification. missing_data_documentation: missing_data_patterns (row-inclusion rule, cohort-specific instruments systematically absent outside the cohort, omitted feature records), missing_data_causes (optional items, collection irregularities, de-identification removal), handling_strategy ('No imputation was performed. A missingness table is generated as part of the audit protocol and is included with the dataset.'). All three named fields are populated substantively, and the missing-data account distinguishes structural missingness (cohort-specific instruments) from incidental missingness (unanswered optional items, collection irregularities) from deliberate removal (de-identification) - a distinction that determines whether missingness can be treated as ignorable. The anomalies are consistent with the collection design described in collection_mechanisms (distinct devices per site explains configuration variation and the measurement_bias entry) and with machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy (the same unaudited-transcription caveat appears in both, in agreement). is_representative: false agrees with known_limitations.representativeness_limitation and with subpopulations.distribution. The declaration that no imputation was performed, paired with a shipped missingness table, is the correct treatment for a dataset with structural missingness.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: 3.1.0; title and citation both cite '(version 3.1.0)'; page is pinned to /3.1.0/; issued: '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z' A semantic version number carried consistently in four places, including the resolvable landing page, so the version a user reaches matches the version documented. The version string follows semver and is consistent with the release sequence in version_access (1.0, 1.1, 2.0.0, 2.0.1, 3.0.0, 3.1.0). The issued date matches the v3.1.0 release date recorded in distribution_dates, so version and date do not disagree.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; versions_available lists six releases with dates and DOIs where assigned (1.0 on Health Data Nexus DOI 10.57764/qb6h-em84; 1.1 17 January 2025 DOI 10.13026/249v-w155; 2.0.0 16 April 2025; 2.0.1 18 August 2025; 3.0.0 16 December 2025 DOI 10.13026/k81f-qr68; 3.1.0 1 May 2026 DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66); version_details states each version has a unique DOI, a version-independent DOI resolves to the latest, older versions are by default supported and hosted though publishers reserve the right to withdraw them, and that v1.1 files are no longer available with users directed to the latest version This answers the practical question - can I still get version 1.1, and how - rather than merely asserting that versioning exists. The disclosure that v1.1 files have in fact been withdrawn, despite the default support policy, is the kind of honest exception that makes the rest of the policy statement usable. The version list agrees with the is_new_version_of relationships in related_datasets and with distribution_dates.release_dates on every shared date. The concept DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is distinct from every version DOI, which is the correct arrangement. The platform change at v1.0 (Health Data Nexus prefix 10.57764) is reflected by a different DOI prefix, which corroborates rather than contradicts the migration narrative in maintainers.source_caveats.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: three entries - spectrograms reprocessed in v2.0 to fix minor issues with all spectrograms and MFCCs derived from free-speech files removed; v2.0.1 corrected errors in the authorship list; v3.1.0 fixed broken parquet files present in v3.0.0. updates.update_details: v3.1.0 'added no new participants but released additional data for certain participants, fixed broken parquet files from the previous release, added audio quality metrics and per-recording metadata, back-filled validated diagnosis information across conditions, rearranged some phenotype files and renamed certain gold standard variables.' Errata are itemized per version with the defect and the remedy, and the v3.1.0 change list is specific enough for a user to know whether re-downloading is necessary and which of their existing analyses the renamed gold-standard variables would break. The errata are consistent with other fields: the free-speech spectrogram removal in the v2.0 erratum matches the corresponding exclusion in is_deidentified.deidentification_details and in known_limitations.scope_limitation; the addition of audio quality metrics matches file_collections[features] listing audio_quality_metrics.tsv and cleaning_strategies describing quality-control metrics; the addition of per-recording metadata matches the metadata file_collection marked 'Introduced in v3.1.0'. Four fields corroborate the change list. The source_caveats correctly distinguish PhysioNet release notes from the documentation's statement that no separate erratum document exists.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Semi-annual, that is twice a year.'; update_details: 'Further versions are released periodically as new versions of the dataset on the publishing platform, and users are notified through news items on the platform and through standard communication channels. Corrections and changes are communicated through a changelog published online with the dataset metadata for each version rather than through a separate erratum document.' A stated cadence plus the notification channel and the mechanism by which changes are communicated - a user knows not only how often to expect updates but how they will learn of one. The stated semi-annual cadence does not match the observed release dates (January, April, August and December 2025, then May 2026, which is closer to quarterly). The record discloses this itself in updates.source_caveats and attributes the figure to the project documentation, so it is recorded as a low-severity disclosed inconsistency rather than an undetected error. The sub-element is met: a schedule is indicated, the evidence for and against it is supplied, and a user can form an accurate expectation from the material given.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: three entries, each with source_description, source_type and raw_data_format - raw WAV waveforms from the acoustic protocol (prospective primary collection; retained but disseminated only through controlled access via Synapse syn72370534 after DACO review at DACO@b2ai-voice.org); participant-reported demographic, confounder and questionnaire responses (self-reported survey; REDCap export; released de-identified as TSV with identifiable source records remaining in the institution's REDCap); clinician validation records from assessment, laryngoscopy, stroboscopy, imaging, spirometry, EHR and prescriptions (REDCap clinical validation and diagnosis forms; released as de-identified diagnosis tables, with underlying imaging and genomic content retained at each site). updates.update_details carries release-specific derivation notes for v3.1.0. related_datasets.derives_from points at the Synapse raw audio. preprocessing_strategies traces the transformation from raw audio to each released feature family. Provenance is traceable end to end: for each released component the record states what the raw source was, what format it was in, who produced it, what happened to it and where the un-released original now sits. The upstream link is a resolvable accession, not a prose reference. The dedicated was_derived_from slot is unpopulated, but the concept is carried by raw_data_sources, the derives_from typed relationship and the preprocessing chain, which together supply more provenance than the slot alone would. Release-specific notes are read from updates.update_details, which carries actual derivation and release information for v3.1.0 rather than unrelated commentary. The three raw sources map cleanly onto the three released components (features from audio, phenotype tables from REDCap surveys, diagnosis tables from clinical validation forms) with no released component lacking a documented origin.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: three responses - to generate a large, multi-institutional, ethically sourced and diverse voice dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers so voice can be integrated as a biomarker in clinical care; to enable development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable ML models diagnosing health conditions from voice; to introduce and standardize the field of acoustic biomarkers (audiomics) by creating bioinformatics standards for acoustic data collection, interoperability and analysis. addressing_gaps: four responses - prior studies too small or lacking key metadata; absence of measurement and collection standards preventing pooling and comparison; industry holds vast private voice data without clinical or demographic annotation, preventing external audit; existing open datasets limited in size, quality and diversity, contributing to the absence of regulator-approved voice-based algorithms. Purpose and the research gap are documented separately and the gaps are stated as specific deficiencies in the prior literature and in industry practice, each of which the dataset design visibly answers. This is scientific rationale, not mission statement. The stated purposes are coherent with the dataset actually described: the diversity claim is tempered rather than contradicted by known_biases and sampling_strategies, which disclose the skews honestly; the standards-creation purpose is corroborated by the BIDS conformance, the FHIR profile contribution in external_resources and the Interspeech protocol publication. The ethical-sourcing claim is substantiated by the Element 4 material rather than merely asserted.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: three responses - training and evaluating ML models for disease detection and classification from voice, speech and respiratory sounds with labels drawn from vocal pathologies, neurological disorders, psychiatric conditions and respiratory disorders; pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking and validating AI models on the derived acoustic feature representations distributed with the dataset; cohort selection and phenotypic analysis using the questionnaire, demographic, confounder and diagnosis tables in the phenotype folder. Each task names the specific released artifacts it would be performed on - the derived feature representations for model work, the named phenotype subfolders for cohort work - so the tasks are operational against this release rather than generic to voice research. The tasks are consistent with what is actually distributed. Notably the second task is scoped to derived feature representations rather than to raw audio, which correctly reflects the withholding of waveforms documented in is_deidentified and known_limitations.scope_limitation - the task statement does not overpromise what the registered-access release supports. Tasks align with intended_uses without duplicating it.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, through the Bridge2AI program'; maintainers includes a government_agency entry recording NIH support via the Bridge2AI Common Fund program; data_governance.notes repeats the NIH Bridge2AI support; description states the dataset was produced 'under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grants[0].description names the awardee institution (University of South Florida), the PI (Yael Bensoussan) and the project period (1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026). The funder is identified at agency, fund and program level, and the awardee institution, principal investigator and project period are given - the mechanism and its administration, not just a sponsor name. The OT2 activity code in the award numbers is an Other Transaction mechanism, which is the mechanism the NIH Common Fund actually uses for Bridge2AI data generation projects, so the code and the stated program are mutually consistent. The awardee institution matches data_governance.accountable_organization (University of South Florida Board of Trustees) and the PI matches creators[0]. Funding goals align with purposes: a Bridge2AI data generation award and a dataset whose stated purpose is AI-ready data generation and standards.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants: OT2OD032720 (core project number, with title 'Bridge2AI: Voice as a Biomarker of Health...'); 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (cited in the PhysioNet v3.0.0 and v3.1.0 acknowledgements and the pediatric release); 1OT2OD032720-01 (cited in the feasibility publication funding statement); 3OT2OD032720-01S3 (NIH RePORTER application ID 11376382, FY2025, award amount 4,660,942 US dollars, organization University of South Florida). funders.source_caveats records that award identifiers differ across sources and that each is given as its source states it. Four award identifiers with the source of each and, for one, the RePORTER application ID and dollar amount. The decision to record each source's form rather than silently normalizing to one is the right one for a record whose sources disagree, and it is declared. All four numbers validate against the NIH pattern. OT2OD032720 decomposes as activity code OT2, administering institute OD (Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund awards), serial 032720. 1OT2OD032720-01 carries application type 1 (new) and support year 01; 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and 3OT2OD032720-01S3 carry type 3 (supplement) with supplement suffixes S1 and S3 - all well-formed. The institute code OD is consistent with the stated Common Fund sponsor, so the number is plausible and not merely pattern-valid. The two malformed strings in funders.notes (3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1, 3Tf-OTOD03272001S2) are explicitly labelled by the record as corrupted renderings of the same core award, which is correct handling; recorded as a low-severity observation.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: 17 named principal investigators with affiliations carrying stable ids and full institutional names, CRediT credit_roles for six of them (Bensoussan with twelve roles, Elemento, Sigaras, Rameau, Ghosh, Johnson), and notes giving each person's project role (co-PI, module co-lead, cohort lead investigator, genomic data lead, data integration lead). A final entry records that the PhysioNet author list names 117 further contributors and that over 50 investigators, clinicians, scholars and trainees contributed, with collective credit to the Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium. created_by names the consortium and its two co-leads. citation lists twenty named authors plus the final author. Attribution operates at three levels - individually credited leads with CRediT taxonomy roles and affiliations, a stated count of further named contributors, and collective consortium credit - so both individual accountability and the scale of the collaboration are visible. Affiliation conflicts (Ravitsky, Rudzicz) are recorded with the competing sources rather than silently resolved. CRediT role names are used correctly (conceptualization, funding_acquisition, investigation, methodology, project_administration, resources, software, supervision, validation, visualization, writing_original_draft, writing_review_editing). The one instance of inferred rather than sourced credit - Johnson's data_curation and software roles - is flagged in that entry's own source_caveats as inferred from the IRB protocol and b2aiprep authorship rather than from a CRediT statement, which is exactly the right disclosure. Creators are consistent with the citation author order and with the institutions named in ethical_reviews and collection sites.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: three entries - a custom Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application hosting the acquisition protocols and presenting acoustic tasks, demographic surveys, confounder questions and validated questionnaires; recording hardware of iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle, with distinct devices at each site; clinical, diagnostic and case report information entered into REDCap using the Bridge2AI-Voice instruments and data dictionary. collection_timeframes: 12 months. collection_notifications, collection_consents, data_collectors (research teams with trained assistants; clinicians listed as co-investigators under the IRB; five North American academic sites) and direct_collection.is_direct: true. Hardware is named to the model level for both tablet and microphone, the software environment and the clinical data capture system are identified, and the collection setting, personnel and duration are given. The disclosure that distinct devices were used at each site is what makes the measurement_bias entry in known_biases interpretable. The mechanism description is consistent with the anomalies entries (per-site configuration differences, varying head-mounted microphone distance) and with known_biases.measurement_bias (cohort membership confounded with site and device) - three fields describing the same physical arrangement without contradiction. collection_timeframes.source_caveats correctly notes that a duration is given but no calendar start or end date, which is a disclosed limitation of the source.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: four entries with typed booleans and details - was_directly_observed (acoustic data recorded during a supervised session on the tablet application with a head-mounted headset microphone where possible); was_reported_by_subjects (demographics, confounders such as smoking and hydration status, and validated questionnaires self-reported through the application); was_validated_verified (clinical diagnoses verified by clinicians reviewing audio and imaging, consulting EHRs or checking prescriptions against per-cohort gold standards); was_inferred_derived (all released features derived computationally from standardized audio using the b2aiprep pipeline). raw_data_sources supplies three matching source entries with formats and access details. Each acquisition modality is flagged and described, so a reuser can tell for any given variable whether it was observed, self-reported, clinically verified or computed - which is the distinction that determines how a variable should be treated in analysis. The four modalities partition the dataset's content without overlap or gap, and each maps onto a documented component: observed to audio, self-reported to the phenotype questionnaire tables, verified to the diagnosis tables, derived to the feature Parquet files. The derived flag correctly identifies that everything in the registered-access release is computed rather than observed, which is consistent with is_deidentified withholding waveforms.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: six entries - conversion to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, spectrograms downsampled by two in time, Mel spectrograms with 60 Mel bins and 60 MFCCs derived from them; sparc articulatory features at 50 Hz giving six vocal tract articulator traces plus loudness, periodicity and pitch, with torchaudio pitch over 80-500 Hz and sparc pitch over 50-550 Hz; openSMILE acoustic features and Parselmouth/Praat phonetic and prosodic features; de-identification removing Safe Harbor identifiers, state and province, narrative text and free-speech transcripts and withholding spectrogram-family features from free speech; conversion to BIDS v1.9.0 and assembly with b2aiprep version 3.0.0. cleaning_strategies: two entries, recording that no cleaning pre-processing was applied and describing the audit protocol instead (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, categorical validation against the schema, audio QC metrics including silence proportion, waveform duration and comparison of produced speech against the intended passage). labeling_strategies: clinical assessment per cohort with annotations_per_item: 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_platform (REDCap plus the tablet application), data_annotation_protocol (gold standard label, clinician-diagnosed, Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10) and inter_annotator_agreement. machine_annotation_tools: nine tools with tool_descriptions and tool_accuracy. Preprocessing is given at parameter level - window, hop, FFT size, Mel bin count, sample rate, pitch ranges - which is the threshold for actual replicability rather than narrative description. Annotation quality is addressed directly and unflatteringly: one labeler per instance, no adjudication, no inter-annotator agreement computable, and off-the-shelf derivation models unaudited for correctness. Parameters are internally consistent and technically coherent: a 25 ms window at 16 kHz corresponds to 400 samples, matching the stated 400-point FFT exactly; MFCCs derived from 60 Mel bins is a standard chain. The v1.1-versus-v3.1.0 parameter change (512-point FFT, no time downsampling) is disclosed in source_caveats rather than conflated. cleaning_strategies' claim that no cleaning was applied is consistent with missing_data_documentation stating no imputation was performed - the record is coherent in treating quality as audited-and-reported rather than corrected. imputation_protocols is not populated as a slot, but the absence of imputation is affirmatively documented.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: machine_annotation_tools.tools names openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc), ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab and OpenAI Whisper Large, with tool_descriptions stating what each produced. preprocessing_strategies names b2aiprep 'version 3.0.0 for this release' as the library that assembled the phenotype tables and derived features, and attributes specific outputs to specific tools (torchaudio for pitch, spectrograms, Mel spectrograms and MFCCs; sparc for articulography, loudness, periodicity and pitch; ppgs for phonetic posteriorgrams; openSMILE for eGeMAPS acoustic features; Praat via Parselmouth for fundamental frequency, formants and voice quality). external_resources gives repositories https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0) and https://github.com/sensein/senselab. The evidence is carried by machine_annotation_tools, preprocessing_strategies prose and external_resources, any one of which would satisfy the requirement that the field exist. A reader can tell exactly which software produced each distributed feature file, and for the principal pipeline can obtain the source and pin the version. Threshold met on transforming-role software, not on capture or hosting. b2aiprep 3.0.0 produced the released feature and phenotype files; torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, openSMILE and Praat/Parselmouth each produced named files in the distribution. These fall squarely inside the processing role rather than any of the excluded roles. The tablet acquisition application (role a, capture) and PhysioNet (role b, hosting) are also documented but are not what earns the point, and their presence neither adds nor subtracts. Whisper Large sits closest to role (e) since the transcripts it produced were removed from the release, so it is not relied on. A version is given for the principal pipeline and repositories are resolvable, which exceeds the naming threshold the sub-element sets.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: seven entries with URLs, licenses and archival flags - b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab, the REDCap data dictionary and instrument PDFs (MIT, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724), the documentation site and its source (MIT, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653), consortium FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication with its ISCA archive URL, and the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars training program. conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0. Imputation: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states 'No imputation was performed. A missingness table is generated as part of the audit protocol and is included with the dataset.' External resources are documented with the three things that determine whether they can actually be relied on - a location, a license and whether an archived copy exists. The imputation question is answered affirmatively in the negative, with the alternative (a shipped missingness table) named, which the sub-element explicitly accepts. Standards named are real and correctly applied: BIDS for the neuroimaging-derived organization of audio, FHIR for clinical interoperability, Zenodo DOIs with the correct 10.5281 prefix for archival copies. The record's honesty about persistence is preserved - one entry's future_guarantees records that the healthsheet answered 'NA' on persistence guarantees and official archival versions. The imputation statement is consistent with cleaning_strategies, which likewise records that no cleaning pre-processing was applied.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: six typed entries - coverage_limitation (English only; Spanish protocol under development and not in this release); representativeness_limitation (sample of a larger ongoing collection at five North American sites); temporal_limitation (changes in diagnostic criteria or clinical practice over the collection period as a source of distribution shift); scope_limitation (raw waveforms absent; spectrogram-family features withheld for sensitive records, audio checks and free speech, so analyses needing the original signal or open-response acoustic detail are impossible on the registered-access files); integration_limitation (laryngoscopy, brain imaging, respiratory function tests, genomic data and other EHR content extracted at sites and not included); methodological_limitation (internal audit for missingness and consistency, but the AI-readiness self-assessment records data quality as not met and human-level performance on the supported tasks varies widely). Six limitations across distinct axes, each typed and each stating the concrete analytical consequence rather than a generic caveat. The scope limitation tells a user precisely which analyses this release cannot support, and the methodological entry surfaces the consortium's own negative self-assessment. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the English-only constraint matches the neurological cohort eligibility in subsets and the representation_bias entry; the scope limitation matches is_deidentified and the v2.0 erratum; the integration limitation matches raw_data_sources[2].access_details. The methodological entry agrees with notes, which records data quality as not met in the AI-readiness self-assessment - the datasheet does not contradict its own scorecard.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: five entries using distinct bias_type values - selection_bias (recruitment from high-volume expert clinics at a limited number of academic institutions, reflecting specialty referral patterns rather than the general population; affected_subsets given); sampling_bias (non-probability sample from an ongoing collection at limited geographic locations; mitigation_strategy of shifting to remote collection and controlling for more variables); representation_bias (English fluency requirement; skews by disorder, site and demographics; groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI, or living further from sites, less likely to be recruited; mitigation_strategy advising users to consider the multivariate distribution); measurement_bias (screening for different disorders by site, confounding cohort membership with site and with the particular tablet device; affected_subsets given); annotation_bias (a single labeler per instance, so labels carry that clinician's judgment without adjudication). future_use_impacts records skew-driven risks of unfair treatment and quality-of-service harms. Five distinct taxonomy categories rather than one undifferentiated statement, with three carrying mitigation strategies and two carrying affected_subsets. The representation_bias entry identifies a recruitment mechanism - differential trust in the medical system and in AI - that most datasheets omit entirely. The bias_type values map onto the BiasTypeEnum categories and each is used correctly for the phenomenon described: measurement_bias is correctly applied to device and site confounding rather than being conflated with selection; annotation_bias correctly describes single-labeler judgment. The social-impact dimension required by the sub-element's RAI scope is carried by future_use_impacts, which names the harm classes (unfair treatment of groups, quality of service) rather than gesturing at risk. The biases are consistent with sampling_strategies (is_random false, is_representative false) and with subpopulations.distribution.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: six entries - differing collection configurations across sites and protocol change over the study; noise artifacts and varying recording distance from the head-mounted headset microphone; diagnostic practice varying between clinicians and sites, with diagnosis sometimes from a single clinician, an EHR or an active prescription; possible questionnaire inaccuracy and participant underreporting; derived text such as transcription produced by unaudited off-the-shelf models; some audio files unable to generate certain derived features because of length or other issues, and therefore absent from the corresponding feature files. The anomalies span acquisition, labeling, self-report and derivation, and the last one explains an observable property of the distributed files - the differing per-feature record counts - so a user encountering that discrepancy finds it already accounted for. The final anomaly is directly corroborated by instances[1].notes, where the per-feature counts differ (32,522 down to 28,640) for exactly the stated reasons, and by missing_data_documentation.missing_data_patterns. The transcription anomaly matches machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy verbatim in substance. The site-configuration anomaly matches collection_mechanisms' statement that distinct devices were used at each site. No anomaly is asserted without a corroborating mechanism elsewhere in the record.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: four entries each with sensitive_elements_present: true and sensitivity_details - race and ethnicity from the demographics instrument; sexual orientation; socioeconomic and health information including diagnosis, psychiatric history and validated questionnaire responses covering depression, anxiety, PTSD and ADHD symptoms; raw voice recordings as biometric data capable of identifying the speaker, excluded from the registered-access release. content_warnings: content_warnings_present: true with a warning that free speech tasks were recorded in open-response form and that offensive or distressing content, while unlikely, cannot be completely avoided since participants choose their own language, plus a source_caveat reconciling the healthsheet's framing with the v3.0.0 and v3.1.0 removal of free-speech transcripts and spectrogram-family features. confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present: false with the basis stated. Sensitivity is itemized by category rather than asserted in aggregate, and the content warning is qualified with the residual exposure actually remaining in the released files after the transcript removals - which is the practically useful statement. The sensitive categories align exactly with the removals listed in is_deidentified.identifiers_removed (household income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences, biometric identifiers), so the record identifies a risk and shows the corresponding control. The confidential_elements: false finding concerns legal privilege and non-public communications, a distinct concept from sensitivity, so it does not contradict the four sensitive_elements entries. Treating raw voice as biometric and therefore identifying is technically correct.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: two entries - the USF single IRB with subsite IRBs through the sIRB process, covering both the clinical study and the data collection and sharing, with the not-a-drug-or-device and no-DMC findings; and the Canadian research ethics boards at Mount Sinai Hospital, The Hospital for Sick Children and the University of Toronto, which applied separately because Canadian institutions fall outside the US sIRB process, with approved applications submitted to the USF IRB and a separate University of Toronto and Mount Sinai protocol covering genomic work. future_use_impacts: two entries - skews by disorder, site and demographics, with the warning that models trained without accounting for them risk unfair treatment of groups, quality-of-service problems or other harms; and the anticipated benefit that voice-based assessment integrated into digital health tools could advance early detection, continuous monitoring and personalized treatment, and extend screening to low-resource settings. data_protection_impacts adds the ethicist review and the published memorandum on controlled access, naming re-identification by voice, voice hacking and data ownership as challenges requiring a governance framework. Both halves of the sub-element are substantive: the ethical review is documented at the level of which body reviewed what under which regulatory framework, and the social impact analysis names both downside harm classes and upside benefits rather than only one direction. The downside impacts follow logically from the biases documented in known_biases, so the impact analysis is derived from the dataset's actual properties rather than generic. Conflicts of interest are not separately declared, a minor gap against the sub-element's full scope, but ethical review and social impact - its two named components - are both well covered. The governance-framework concerns named in data_protection_impacts (voice hacking, data ownership) are specific to the voice modality rather than boilerplate.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://physionet.org; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; status: published; maintainers records that the dataset is hosted on PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, 'which provides the technical infrastructure and continued access for credentialed researchers'; distribution_formats access_urls resolve to PhysioNet; the controlled-access tier is published through Synapse (syn72370534). PhysioNet is a recognized domain repository for clinical physiological data, and the record identifies not only the platform but the institution maintaining it and the access model it provides. A second recognized platform (Synapse) carries the controlled-access tier. The publisher is corroborated by the DOI prefix 10.13026, which is PhysioNet's, and by the page URL - identifier, publisher and landing page agree. The hosting conflict with the project documentation's Health Data Nexus claim is disclosed and resolved in maintainers.source_caveats, which attributes the Health Data Nexus description to the earlier v1.0 release; that resolution is independently corroborated by related_datasets, where v1.0 carries the Health Data Nexus DOI prefix 10.57764 while all later versions carry 10.13026.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: full formatted citation naming twenty authors plus the final author, the title, '(version 3.1.0)', the publisher PhysioNet, 'RRID:SCR_007345' and 'https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 for version-independent citation. external_resources cites the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication with its ISCA archive URL. A ready-to-use citation string in a recognized format, carrying author list, version, publisher, repository RRID and a resolvable DOI URL, plus a concept DOI for citing the dataset independently of version. Both citation needs - this version and the dataset as such - are served. The citation is internally consistent with title, version, publisher and doi, and its author order matches the creators list order. The RRID is well formed but scopes to PhysioNet as a resource rather than to this dataset, recorded as a low-severity correctness observation; dataset-level cross-referencing rests on the DOI, which is valid and prefix-plausible. The version-independent DOI is correctly distinguished from the versioned one.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections[b2ai-voice-audio] declares BIDS conformance with a BIDS-compliant path template and dataset_description.json; external_resources records consortium-published FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker; purposes states the intent to create bioinformatics standards for acoustic data; the Interspeech 2024 publication documents the multi-disorder protocol development. The dataset both conforms to community standards and contributes to them - BIDS organization for the audio, a public metadata schema for this record, FHIR profiles published back to the clinical interoperability community, and a protocol standardization paper. Standards are named with versions where versions matter (BIDS v1.9.0) and the declared conformance is substantiated by the concrete artifacts listed - CHANGES.md, README.md, dataset_description.json and the sub-/ses-/task- path template are genuine BIDS requirements, so the claim is evidenced rather than asserted. ICD-10 is named in labeling_strategies as the diagnostic coding standard, adding a clinical terminology standard to the organizational and metadata ones.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources includes the project documentation site and dashboards at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ (source at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653, MIT); training opportunities through the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars program at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/; the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication at its ISCA archive URL; the REDCap data dictionary, metadata and instrument PDFs at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724. page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, with discussion forums and issue pages for public discussion and pull requests accepted. A documentation site with dashboards, a named training program, a published protocol paper, downloadable survey instruments and an open contribution channel with forums and issue tracking. This covers the outreach dimension well beyond a single documentation link. URLs are structurally valid and their domains are consistent with the actors named elsewhere (eipm for the Weill Cornell institute named in creators, sensein for the b2aiprep maintainers). Archival status is stated per resource, so a user can distinguish the persistent copies from the live sites. The contribution mechanism in extension_mechanism corroborates the community-engagement claim with a concrete channel.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: six entries each with a relationship_type, a target_dataset identifier and a description - derives_from https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ (the controlled-access raw audio the features were computed from); is_supplemented_by doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (the Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2 to 18 at The Hospital for Sick Children); is_new_version_of doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0, 16 December 2025); is_new_version_of doi:10.13026/249v-w155 (v1.1, 17 January 2025); is_new_version_of doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 (v1.0 on Health Data Nexus, which provided cloud compute rather than downloads); is_version_of doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (the version-independent DOI). Four distinct relationship types across six links, every one resolvable and every one accompanied by a description that explains what the target is and why it relates - including the substantive detail that the pediatric sibling covers ages 2 to 18 and that v1.0 operated on a compute-only model. Relationship types are semantically correct in each case and the graph is internally consistent: the version chain matches version_access.versions_available and distribution_dates.release_dates; the derives_from target matches the Synapse accession in raw_data_sources and distribution_formats; the pediatric sibling is consistent with at_risk_populations.notes, which records that the pediatric cohort is published as a separate dataset, and with informed_consent's mention of parental permission and child assent for that arm. The platform change at v1.0 is reflected in a different DOI prefix, corroborating the migration.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; citation carries 'RRID:SCR_007345' and 'https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. A single persistent identifier is used consistently across id, doi, citation and the file_collections fragment identifiers (doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66#features). DOI matches 10.XXXX/... and the 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's, matching publisher and page. RRID matches RRID:SCR_XXXXX. Format valid and prefix plausible.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description ~1,300 characters covering cohort size, sites, condition families, collection protocol and the exact contents of the public release. Well above the 200-character threshold and specific rather than boilerplate: it names the four condition families, states that the release distributes derived features rather than waveforms, and says where raw audio lives. Description is semantically appropriate for a clinical voice-biomarker dataset and does not overstate the release scope; it matches file_collections and known_limitations.scope_limitation.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice] Four broad terms, below the five-keyword threshold and covering only the domain. No method terms (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory coding), no condition terms (Parkinson's disease, dysphonia, depression, COPD) and no modality or task terms, despite all being described in detail elsewhere in the record. Terms are individually accurate but the set does not support condition- or method-based discovery; a user searching for any represented disorder would not retrieve this record.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; file_collections defines three hierarchical collections (features, phenotype, metadata) with eleven enumerated resources under features, each with id, name, description and, for the TSV files, format and media_type. A version-pinned landing page plus a genuine resource hierarchy naming every distributed feature file and its dimensions and record count. Landing page URL is well formed and its version segment (3.1.0) matches the version field and issued date.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0); derives_from syn72370534 (controlled-access raw audio on Synapse); references 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric dataset); is_documented_by 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926. Four typed relationships, each with a note explaining what the target is and why it is related; parent_datasets is unused but the derives_from and is_new_version_of edges carry that information. Relationship types are used correctly — the raw audio is genuinely the source of the released features, and the pediatric release is genuinely a sibling rather than a part, consistent with source_caveats.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'released under the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License ... only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the files ... Duplication as reasonably required ... is permitted; sale of all or part of the data on any media is not. There are no fees'; ip_restrictions lists four restrictions including the Fort Lauderdale Agreement commitment. Both tiers are specified (registered access for features, Data Access Request Form plus DUA and DACO review for raw audio), with fees, duplication and resale addressed explicitly. Restrictiveness is proportionate to the sensitivity claimed in sensitive_elements and participant_privacy: the biometric tier is controlled, the derived tier is registered.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions: 'No export controls apply'; other_compliance describes HIPAA de-identification, a Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguard obligations and a five-business-day breach reporting duty; data_governance.notes gives the governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. Export control, confidentiality classification, HIPAA status, additional obligations and a governance mailbox are all present and specific. One unreconciled conflict is carried in source_caveats (the DTUA describes the data as 'not covered under HIPAA' while hipaa_compliant is 'compliant'); the conflict is disclosed rather than hidden, so the sub-element still informs the user, but it is recorded as a failed consistency check. The contact sits in data_governance.notes rather than the dedicated committee_contact slot.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats[*].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ for each of TSV, JSON and Parquet; data_governance.access_review_process gives step-by-step access instructions for both tiers; raw_data_sources.access_details gives https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ and DACO@b2ai-voice.org. The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element's purpose — telling a user where and how to obtain the data — is served in more detail than a bare URL would: platform link, credentialing requirement, agreement to sign, and a separate route for the raw audio. URLs are well formed and resolve to the stated platforms by construction; the access route is consistent with the registered-access license and with third_party_sharing.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: TSV (text/tab-separated-values), JSON (application/json), Parquet (media type omitted with the note 'No IANA media type for Parquet is stated by the sources'); file_collections.resources give format and media_type on static_features.tsv and audio_quality_metrics.tsv. Formats are specific and mapped to actual content (phenotype tables, dense feature tensors, JSON data dictionaries), with per-file dimensions and record counts. Format choices are appropriate to content: Parquet for dense time-varying tensors, TSV for per-recording scalars, JSON for dictionaries. The omitted Parquet media type is justified rather than fabricated.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets (4 typed entries) plus external_resources listing b2aiprep and SenseLab (github.com/sensein), the REDCap data dictionary (github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724), the documentation source (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653), FHIR profiles and the Interspeech 2024 protocol paper. Each external resource carries a license restriction (Apache-2.0, MIT) and a statement of its role in producing the release. Zenodo DOIs use the 10.5281 prefix correctly; GitHub organisation paths are plausible and match the software named in preprocessing_strategies.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License'; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; intended_uses: 'intended solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers'. Reuse is permitted for both commercial and non-commercial research, with the boundary conditions stated (no resale, no re-identification, duplication for the project permitted, no fees). The permission (general_research_use) is consistent with informed_consent.consent_scope, which states the consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes or to a research type — an unusually well-closed consent-to-license chain.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: TSV, JSON, Apache Parquet described as 'an open-source column-oriented data file format'; file_collections.resources.format: TSV with media_type text/tab-separated-values; every data file paired with a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem. All three formats are open and standard, and the dictionary-per-file convention makes the tables self-describing. Character encoding is nowhere stated, which is a real gap for TSV interchange; it is outweighed here by the format specificity and the dictionary convention, and is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology CURIEs data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:25 / B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 / B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes'. Conformance is stated at three levels — the metadata record's own schema, Bridge2AI topic/substrate ontology terms on instances, and ICD-10 for diagnostic labels. Partly qualified: source_caveats states that the 3.1.0 release 'does not state conformance to any data standard, so no standard is asserted for this release', explicitly declining to carry the earlier BIDS v1.9.0 claim forward. The stated conformances are real and correctly scoped; the honest non-assertion of a data standard is recorded as a low-severity semantic issue rather than a fabrication.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: participant_id (identifier, is_identifier: true), session_id (identifier, is_identifier: true), task_name (categorical), n_frames (integer), each with a description; file_collections describes 'a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem, giving a description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type'. The linking keys — which are what cross-file and cross-dataset integration depends on — are defined with explicit identifier flags, and the per-file dictionaries are documented as the route to column-level semantics. participant_id and session_id are consistently referenced in distribution_formats, file_collections and participant_privacy.data_linkage, so the declared keys match the described linkage. Coverage is thin relative to the phenotype tables (low-severity completeness issue).

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses (two entries, research, with examples AI model pretraining/fine-tuning/benchmarking/validation); discouraged_uses ('hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance'); prohibited_uses (three entries: re-identification attempts, uses causing harm or stigmatization, IP claims restricting access). All three categories are populated and each prohibition carries a stated reason rather than a bare rule. Guidance is internally coherent with future_use_impacts, which names the same misuse scenarios, and with ip_restrictions, which encodes the third prohibition contractually.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board, with review_details covering the Single IRB process, subsite IRBs and separate Canadian REB applications; human_subject_research.irb_approval repeats this and ethics_review_board names USF IRB; data_governance names the Data Access Compliance Office. Oversight is described at the level a replicator needs: which IRB, which mechanism (Single IRB), how non-US sites were handled, and where approval copies were filed. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated IRB detail. A content-accuracy warning is recorded because data_protection_impacts states that no impact analysis on data subjects was conducted, which is a governance gap for biometric and mental-health data even though the IRB record is strong.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but highly sensitive fields, and by withholding of all raw audio'; identifiers_removed enumerates the Safe Harbor categories plus state/province, household composition, income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences; deidentification_details records transcript review, removal of recordings with external voices, and 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved'. A named method, an explicit list of removed identifier classes, and a candid statement of the residual limitation — the strongest sub-element in the record. Method is appropriate to the data type: Safe Harbor addresses tabular phenotype data, and withholding raw audio addresses the biometric channel that Safe Harbor cannot. The is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false boolean reads more absolutely than the k<2 admission (low-severity consistency warning).

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (four listed, including removal of transcripts and derived representations of free speech), reidentification_risk: 'Voice is unique to the speaker and cannot be fully de-identified ... K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved for the released tables', data_linkage describing the participant identifier and EHR access for gold-standard validation. A genuine risk assessment rather than an assurance: it names the residual risk, the reason it cannot be eliminated, and the contractual control (recipients barred from contacting subjects) that substitutes for technical mitigation. Consistency check passes: data_protection_impacts present and reidentification_risk assessed. The assessment is proportionate to sensitive_elements, which flags voice as a biometric identifier.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: prospective written consent on paper, via REDCap e-consent, or by video of the participant reading the statement, with assent where applicable; consent_documentation: REDCap storage for a minimum of five years; consent_scope covering registered vs controlled sharing and the absence of commercial/geographic/method restrictions; withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, consent_revocations and collection_notifications. Consent is documented end to end, including the operationally important boundary that data cannot be removed once voice collection is complete and that withdrawal before completion excludes the data. Consistency check passes: IRB documented and consent procedures also described. consent_scope matches license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission (general_research_use) — the permission granted downstream does not exceed the permission obtained upstream.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.special_protections (adults only, 18-120; pediatric participants released separately; assent option for adults unable to consent; discomfort risk in mood/psychiatric instruments) and assent_procedures; participant_compensation: electronic gift cards, '40 US dollars for a session under 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for over 90 minutes ... maximum compensation of 120 US dollars'. Compensation is quantified with its schedule and cap, and the at-risk discussion identifies the specific populations at issue (cognitive impairment, dementia, mood and psychiatric diagnoses) rather than asserting none. at_risk_populations is consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations, which states the same age bounds and the same assent provision; source_caveats correctly declines to assert whether assent-enrolled participants appear in this release.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, and participants are assigned to disease cohort categories — voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders — or to the control group'; distribution: 'do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories, and the dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'; sampling_strategies gives per-diagnosis inclusion/exclusion screening. Cohort structure and the recorded demographic dimensions are explicit, and the skew is disclosed. Actual counts or proportions per cohort are not given, which limits a reader's ability to judge fit before download. Consistent with known_biases.representation_bias, which states the same skew, and with the phenotype directory listing, which enumerates the per-condition diagnosis tables that carry the cohort assignment.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances[0].counts: 833 human participants; instances[1].notes: 'torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640'; per-file counts repeated in file_collections.resources. Counts are given at both participant and recording-derivative level, with an explanation of why feature counts differ and an explicit refusal to invent a single recording total. Counts are internally consistent between instances.notes and the eleven file_collections resource descriptions. The 833 figure is attributed to 3.1.0 but sourced from v3.0 documentation per source_caveats (low-severity content-accuracy issue).

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables (4 entries with data_type and is_identifier); splits: 'No recommended train, validation or test splits are predefined. Researchers are encouraged to create their own data splits'; subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present: true; relationships describes the session-within-participant grouping and multiple rows per participant. The split question is answered explicitly rather than left blank, and the session/participant nesting — which is exactly what an incautious modeller would get wrong — is called out. is_tabular is not set, although the record distributes TSV phenotype tables and dense Parquet tensors, a mixture that would have been worth flagging explicitly (low-severity completeness issue).

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances[*].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:25 and B2AI_TOPIC:36; data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 and B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; file_collections phenotype description enumerates eighteen diagnosis tables (airway stenosis, ALS, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, control, COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia, laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained chronic cough, unilateral vocal fold paralysis) and fourteen questionnaire instruments. Condition coverage is enumerated at the level of individual diagnoses and validated instruments, not just cohort families. The enumerated conditions map coherently onto the four cohort families named in description and subpopulations; ontology CURIEs are used in the correct slots.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies (three entries: differing site configurations and protocol change over time; noise artifacts and diagnostic-practice variation; headset distance variation and single-clinician diagnosis); sampling_strategies (is_sample true, is_representative false, why_not_representative); missing_data_documentation with missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy ('a missingness table is included with the dataset'); cleaning_strategies releases audio_quality_metrics.tsv. Missing-data documentation distinguishes structural absence (cohort-specific branching, optional items) from incidental loss (collection irregularities, features that could not be generated), which is the distinction a reanalyst needs. missing_data_patterns is consistent with the differing per-feature record counts in instances.notes — the stated cause (features that could not be generated, sensitive records withheld) explains the observed count spread.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '3.1.0'; title-level and page-level agreement (https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/); issued: 2026-05-01. Semantic version, pinned in the landing page URL and matched to a release date. Version, page path, issued date and the last entry of distribution_dates all agree.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available lists five releases with dates and DOIs where known ('1.1 — 17 January 2025 — doi:10.13026/249v-w155' ... '3.1.0 — 1 May 2026 — doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'); version_details: 'Each version ... has a unique DOI, and by default older versions continue to be supported ... The files for version 1.1 are no longer available from PhysioNet. Version 1.0 was published on the Health Data Nexus platform under doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84'. Both the policy (older versions supported by default, publishers reserve removal rights) and the actual exception (1.1 files withdrawn) are stated, which is more useful than the policy alone. Failed consistency check: latest_version_doi (doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42) matches none of the listed version DOIs and conflicts with the record's own 3.1.0 DOI. The sub-element still documents version access substantively, so the defect is recorded as a medium-severity issue rather than a zero.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata.erratum_details: 'Version 2.0 reprocessed the spectrograms to fix minor issues ... and removed all spectrograms and MFCCs derived from free-speech files. Version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list. Version 3.1.0 fixed broken parquet files carried over from the previous release, updated validated diagnosis information ... rearranged some phenotypic files and renamed certain gold standard variable names.' Per-version, change-level detail including breaking changes (renamed gold-standard variables, rearranged phenotype files) that would silently break downstream code. source_caveats correctly notes that the project healthsheet claims no erratum exists and that these entries were reconstructed from per-version release notes — the provenance of the claim is disclosed.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.update_details: 'further versions ... will be released on a semi-annual (twice a year) basis ... with users notified through news items on the hosting platform ... that statement is a plan written against the Health Data Nexus platform and an earlier release, not an observed cadence', followed by the list of six published versions with dates. Both the stated cadence and the observed release history are given, with an explicit warning not to read the plan as an observation. The observed history (Jan 2025, Apr 2025, Aug 2025, Dec 2025, May 2026) is roughly consistent with the semi-annual plan for major versions; notification channel is named.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw audio recordings ... captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, together with questionnaire and clinical data captured in REDCap, collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol'; raw_data_sources (two entries with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details, including the Synapse accession); updates.update_details carries the release history; related_datasets.derives_from syn72370534. The derivation chain is complete and traversable: raw WAV and REDCap export, named preprocessing library, released feature tables, with the raw tier's access route given. was_derived_from, raw_data_sources and the derives_from relationship name the same source consistently; b2aiprep appears as the transforming agent in all three places.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes (three entries, including 'To generate a large multi-institutional, ethically sourced and diverse voice dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers'); addressing_gaps (three entries naming the specific deficiencies: small sample sizes, absent collection standards, no linkage to multi-modal health data).
