Comfortably at the 5-point band. Demographic characterisation is quantified rather than described, extends to the split level, and is accompanied by explicit eligibility criteria and exclusions. Every cross-tabulation was checked and reconciles: the three categorical distributions each sum to 2,280; the splits sum to 2,280 at the declared proportions; and each stratum reconstructs from its three split values (Hispanic 204+88+88=380, insulin 105+67+86=258, female 977+176+176=1,329, and so on for all ten strata). Mean age 60.8 ± 11.3 is plausible within a 40–85 eligibility window. The record also handles a subtle tension honestly: subpopulation_elements_present is false for race/ethnicity and sex because those variables are not released, yet the aggregate distributions are supplied from the README — the source_caveats make clear the reader is getting counts without record-level labels. That is the right disclosure and does not warrant a deduction.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; access route https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; external_resources spanning https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io and two publication DOIs; licence DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036; funder link https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10471118. Passes on every limb — registered DOI, versioned DOIs, landing page, access page, documentation site and a set of resolvable external resources. All URLs are structurally well formed with plausible domains matching the organisations they are attributed to (fairhub.io for the repository, aireadi.org for the project, doi.org for registered identifiers, reporter.nih.gov for the award). One caveat recorded elsewhere and not penalised here: the v2 DOI is stated to be no longer accessible, which affects Q13's persistence judgement but does not alter this pass, since the current version's identifiers are intact.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: data_governance.access_review_process: 'Accessing the dataset requires several steps: logging in through a verified ID system; agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research; and agreeing to the license terms ... The access route for version 3.0.0 is the FAIRhub access page at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access', plus the two-tier structure (public tier and a controlled-access tier 'available only to scientists whose institutions have completed legal and privacy use agreements'). third_party_sharing repeats the same three steps. distribution_formats give the four obtainable formats with media types. license_and_use_terms supply the terms to be accepted, and regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats records the source accessType verbatim as 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired', naming the tier precisely. The 5-point band asks for platform, login and policy, and all three are given: the platform (FAIRhub), the exact access URL, the authentication requirement (verified ID), the attestation requirement (T2DM-only research), the licence acceptance step, and the distinct route for the controlled tier. The record avoids the 'public means unrestricted' error the rubric warns about, stating the self-attestation tier explicitly. Licence-to-format consistency holds: the licence permits download and reuse and distribution_formats specify what is obtainable, so the FAIR logic check passes. No dedicated download_url field is populated, but the access page is given under data_governance and the tier is stated more precisely than a bare download link would convey; scoring is on record content rather than field presence, so no deduction. The access description is consistent with the restrictive licence and with confidentiality_level, allowing for the disclosed enum approximation.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: the full AI-READI v2.0 summary with a resolvable licence DOI. intended_uses: three use categories with usage_notes and worked examples (multimodal AI/ML model development; pseudotime manifold analysis; salutogenesis research; methodological reuse of the CDS specification and FAIRhub; and a model-distribution category permitting release of trained artefacts provided the licensee 'undertakes all reasonable efforts to minimise the likelihood that data can be memorized, derived, reconstructed or reconstituted'). prohibited_uses: six specific prohibitions — clinical treatment decisions, re-identification and any attempt to establish membership or contact a subject, sharing with third-party model vendors for training, reproduction beyond five illustrative figures per paper, onward transfer outside the licensee community, and watermark removal. discouraged_uses: two — treating the cohort as population-representative, and relying on interim releases for balanced demographics. future_use_impacts: ABSENT. Use guidance is exceptional: the prohibitions are operational enough to be enforced, the model-distribution clause addresses memorisation risk directly, and the discouraged uses name the two mistakes a reader of this dataset is most likely to make. Held at 4 because the 5-point band additionally requires social impact analysis with mitigation strategies, and future_use_impacts is empty. Social-impact material does exist but is dispersed: addressing_gaps records the meta-epidemiological finding that T2DM studies 'lacked racial and ethnic diversity' and frames the balanced recruitment as a response; known_biases carries mitigation_strategy on all three entries; participant_privacy names the AI-inference re-identification pathway and its deterrents; known_limitations notes that 'fairness analyses stratified by sex or race/ethnicity cannot be performed on the public release alone'; and ethical_reviews records CAB and bioethicist involvement. A reader reconstructing a social-impact assessment can do so from the record, but not from the field the rubric and CROISSANT RAI designate for it. One point deducted for the missing consolidation, not for absent thinking.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Derivation paths, per modality, from raw_data_sources plus preprocessing_strategies: REDCap export → one-to-one OMOP CDM table mapping → CSV in clinical_data; Philips TC30 .xml → WFDB conversion → cardiac_ecg; Topcon .fda and Heidelberg FLIO .sdt → DICOM conversion → retinal_oct / retinal_octa / retinal_flio, with Optomed, Eidon, Spectralis and Cirrus 'exported directly in DICOM'; Garmin .FIT and Dexcom .csv → Open mHealth → wearable directories; LeeLab Anura .csv → NASA ESDS → environment. Agents: 'A Data Manager at each data site was responsible for quality control of all data before uploading to FAIRhub'; 'Editing was only done under the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator'; 'Once data were sent from each study site to the central project team, all data were mapped to standardized terminologies'. Version lineage: version_access with three versioned DOIs and dates; related_datasets with typed is_new_version_of relationships; updates describing static re-release rather than in-place update; errata recorded as none. Quality and integrity: missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling), anomalies (six modality-specific entries including FLIO photon-distribution limits and Garmin charging gaps), cleaning_strategies with four named check classes, the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard with 3,500+ checks, splits with per-stratum counts, and raw_sources explaining why raw data are retained but not shared. The rubric accepts text or PROV-O and asks for entity-activity-agent relationships, processing lineage and derivation paths. All three are present and complete for every one of the nine modalities: each source entity is named with its native format, each transforming activity is named, the destination is named, and the responsible agents and their decision authority are identified. The distinction the rubric draws — version history alone is 3, full lineage is 5 — is decided here by the per-modality derivation chains, which go well beyond version history. was_derived_from and parent_datasets are not populated as named fields, but the information they would carry is present and typed elsewhere (raw_data_sources for source derivation, related_datasets for version ancestry), and this question is scored from record content rather than field presence. Lineage is internally consistent: the source formats named in raw_data_sources match the conversion steps in preprocessing_strategies, which in turn match the conforms_to_standard values on the destination file_collections, so the chain can be traced end to end without contradiction. Integrity is further supported by the arithmetic checks that hold across file counts, byte totals and demographic tables.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: three entries typed against the enum — selection_bias ('Participants are volunteers, so volunteer bias applies'), sampling_bias ('the pilot and interim releases are not balanced across these parameters'), representation_bias ('does not include other races and ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans ... Recruitment is predominantly urban and hospital-based ... The requirement that participants speak, read and understand English may also have created challenges in recruiting Hispanic and Asian participants') — each with a mitigation_strategy, and affected_subsets on the sampling_bias entry. Fairness-relevant material: the split design balancing validation and test sets on withheld demographic labels 'aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using the dataset'; sampling_strategies.why_not_representative explaining the deliberate triple balancing; known_limitations.scope_limitation noting fairness analyses stratified by sex or race cannot be run on the public release; addressing_gaps citing the diversity deficit in prior T2DM literature; and the Native Biodata Consortium engagement. future_use_impacts: absent. Above the 3-point band, which is basic identification without taxonomy: the biases here are typed against a standard enum, each carries a mitigation, and the fairness discussion is concrete. Held at 4 because the 5-point band asks for comprehensive categorisation with AIO/CROISSANT RAI mapping plus fairness analysis, and there is no AIO or ontology mapping, no future_use_impacts entry, and one bias class that this dataset plainly carries is not categorised. The omitted class is measurement or instrument bias. The record documents six retinal imaging device models across three sites, three blood-pressure device models, two lensometer models, device-specific image-quality variation ('Optomed Aurora fundus photographs are taken undilated with a handheld camera, so image quality varies from patient to patient and within the same patient'), manual Spectralis operation causing skipped modalities, and a site-dependent device mix — all of which create a device-by-site confound that a model developer would need in the bias taxonomy. That material sits in anomalies and collection_mechanisms instead. Bias typing that is present is used correctly and is consistent with sampling_strategies and known_limitations; nothing is mistyped. One point deducted for the taxonomy and social-impact gaps, recorded as a semantic_understanding issue.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; title 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~2,000 characters); keywords (10 terms); license_and_use_terms (license_terms plus data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'); doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; creators (consortium plus PI with ROR and ORCID); purposes (4 responses); instances (1 object, counts 2280); variables (25 objects with data_type, unit, measurement_technique); external_resources (6 entries, read here as the 'resources' requirement). Unpopulated: parent_datasets (version predecessors carried instead in related_datasets as is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (value 'HL7:2N (normal)' present only in regulatory_restrictions.notes). Twelve of fourteen named fields are populated with substantive content, and the two gaps have prose equivalents elsewhere in the record rather than being genuinely undocumented. On a field-presence count that is 85.7%, below the 90% threshold the 5 band requires, so 4. Field content is semantically appropriate to each slot rather than padded: variables carry units and measurement techniques, instances carries a real count and a labelling rationale, and the id/doi/page triple resolves consistently to the same FAIRhub object. The two unpopulated slots are recorded gaps rather than missing information, which is why this scores at the top of the 'minor gaps' band.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 2,000 characters and names the cohort size (2,280), the collection window (19 July 2023 to 1 May 2025), the three sites, the four diabetes categories, more than ten data domains, the file and byte totals (356,343 files, ~3.82 TB) and the governing standards. purposes contains four responses each of 200-400 characters, e.g. 'To develop a foundational dataset in T2DM that is agnostic to existing classification criteria or biases and that can be used to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal towards health.' Both narrative fields are far above the >200 character band and, more importantly, the length is carrying specifics rather than boilerplate. Every quantity asserted in the description is corroborated elsewhere in the record (2,280 matches instances.counts and all four demographic marginals; 356,343 matches total_file_count; the date range matches collection_timeframes), so the narrative is not merely long but verifiable against the structured fields.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 10 unique keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam', 'Type 2 Diabetes', 'Data Sharing', 'Exploratory Data Collection'. Ten distinct terms, meeting the >=8 band. The keyword set spans disease, method and modality axes and each term is discharged by actual content: Electrocardiography by the cardiac_ecg subcrate, Continuous Glucose Monitoring by the Dexcom G6 collection, Retinal imaging by four imaging subcrates. 'Diabetes mellitus' and 'Type 2 Diabetes' partly overlap, and the environmental-sensor and wearable-activity modalities - two of the more distinctive parts of the release - have no keyword of their own.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists four typed entries - application/dicom, text/csv, application/json, text/markdown - each with an access URL, and the notes add 'tab-separated manifest.tsv files for each data type and a participants.tsv file at the root'. total_file_count 356343; nine file_collections enumerate per-collection file_count and total_bytes (e.g. retinal_octa 173,721 files / 1,155,908,809,724 bytes; cardiac_ecg 4,515 files / 302,931,703 bytes). Five distinct media types with per-collection enumeration, comfortably above the >3 band. Format variety genuinely reflects the multi-modal claim in description and keywords rather than incidental packaging: DICOM for the five imaging subcrates, CSV for OMOP clinical tables, JSON for Open mHealth wearable records and the CDS metadata files, TSV for manifests and the participant split. The TSV format is described only in a note rather than given its own distribution_formats entry.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; total_file_count: 356343; instances.counts: 2280; nine file_collections each with total_bytes and file_count; splits give 1,576 / 352 / 352; version_access records that 'Version 2.0.0 comprised 165,051 files and 2.01 TB; version 3.0.0 comprises 356,343 files and 3.82 TB'. Numeric size and instance metadata are present at dataset, collection and version level - well beyond the pass threshold. Size metadata is not merely present but checkable: the nine collection byte totals sum to within 419,614 bytes of the declared total, the residual matching the nine root metadata files, and the file counts differ by exactly 9 for the same reason.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/; version_access.latest_version_doi doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 with per-version DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2; nine ARK identifiers of the form ark:59853/rocrate-b2ai-ai-readi-omop; ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648 for the PI; ROR:01yc7t268 for the affiliation. Multiple persistent identifiers at dataset, version, subcrate and person level. Identifiers are internally coherent - id, doi and latest_version_doi agree, and the page URL path (/datasets/3) matches the DOI suffix (fairhub.3). No RRID is asserted, which is consistent with the record's stated practice of not asserting identifiers no source supplies. The ROR is well formed but points at the institution this evaluation flags as a probable attribution error.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: National Institutes of Health with grants OT2OD032644 ('Awarded through the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program ... application ID 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, an award amount of $5,026,499 for fiscal year 2022 ... project period of 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2025'), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096, plus Research to Prevent Blindness. creators: 'AI-READI Consortium' (organizational) and principal_investigator 'Aaron Y. Lee' with affiliation id ROR:01yc7t268 and ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648 in notes. notes additionally acknowledges in-kind device support from Topcon, Optomed, iCare, Zeiss, Heidelberg, Dexcom and Garmin and cloud support from the Microsoft AI for Good Lab. Four funders, three grant numbers, an award amount, a project period and a RePORTER application ID, together with creator affiliations and an ORCID - the top band with room to spare. Grant formats validate against NIH conventions and the activity codes are plausible for the claims made (OT2/OD for a Common Fund Other Transaction, P30/DK for a NIDDK centre, UL1/TR for a CTSA). The one semantic defect is the affiliation: the RePORTER organization is recorded as University of Washington in the same funders.notes that sits beside a creators affiliation of Washington University in St. Louis. Because the funding content itself is complete and the conflict is disclosed in source_caveats, it is logged as an issue rather than scored down here; it is scored where it bears on governance attribution.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board, Human Subjects Division ... protocol number STUDY00016228, with initial approval on 20 December 2022 and reliance agreements with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego', plus a second review entry naming four named bioethicists and an eleven-person Community Advisory Board. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true with irb_approval, ethics_review_board contact (hsdrely@uw.edu, postal address), regulatory_compliance and special_populations. is_deidentified with method, identifiers_removed and deidentification_details. participant_privacy with anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (verified-ID login, strict license, static watermarking), reidentification_risk and data_linkage. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, written/electronic consent type, consent_scope, consent_documentation ('AI-READI Consent_Form_Standard_Mod17May2023_useforpilot.pdf') and withdrawal_mechanism; collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations add further detail. participant_compensation: US$200 stipend, payment conditions, plus transport reimbursement. at_risk_populations.special_protections covers the 40-85 age window, exclusion of pregnancy/gestational/type 1 diabetes, and an incidental-findings pathway. regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance covers HIPAA and the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy. Against this: data_protection_impacts states only 'No data protection impact analysis has been conducted for the dataset'; no hipaa_compliant term is asserted; no governance committee contact person is named (data_governance.source_caveats: 'No contact person is asserted for the governance committee'). Among the most complete ethics documentation the rubric contemplates - protocol number, approval date, reliance agreements, consent artefact filename, withdrawal terms, exact compensation and its conditions. It falls one band short because the 5 requires data protection impacts to be documented and the record documents that no such analysis exists, leaving the acknowledged re-identification risk unassessed. Cross-field logic holds where it matters: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent, and is_deidentified is matched by a stated method and by participant_privacy protections. Two semantic defects reduce confidence rather than coverage - the NoDeIdentification / Safe Harbor conflict in is_deidentified, and sensitivity flags set to false beneath an access regime (watermarking, BAA-only storage, GDS security standards) whose restrictiveness implies residual sensitivity. The ethics claims are otherwise plausible for the data type: withholding sex, race/ethnicity and medications is a stronger-than-Safe-Harbor step and is justified on stigmatization grounds.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms: 'AI-READI Data License Agreement version 2.0, published at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036', with grant scope (non-exclusive, non-transferable, research/commercial/non-commercial, derivative works permitted), sublicensing rules, automatic termination on breach, attribution duty, as-is warranty disclaimer and a one-dollar liability cap; data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'. ip_restrictions: title and all IP remain with the licensor, reserved rights, indemnity, the RO-Crate copyright notice, and referral of large-scale reproduction requests. regulatory_restrictions: compliance with applicable law, other_compliance covering the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy Best Practices and the HIPAA position, notes recording confidentialityLevel 'HL7:2N (normal)'. data_governance: committee name, accountable organization, access_review_process ('logging in through a verified ID system; agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research; and agreeing to the license terms ... FAIRhub access type ... PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired') and a separate controlled-access route via legal and privacy use agreements. All three elements of the top band are present, and the access review process distinguishes the public and controlled tiers with their respective requirements. Governance and licence terms are mutually consistent and proportionate to the claimed sensitivity: disease-specific permission matches the intended_uses restriction to type 2 diabetes research, the prohibition on third-party model-vendor sharing matches the watermarking rationale in participant_privacy, and the controlled-access tier holds exactly the elements sensitive_elements lists as withheld. The confidentiality classification is asserted only in a notes string rather than in the confidentiality_level slot, and no HIPAA compliance determination is asserted - both disclosed, and neither leaves the reuser without the substance.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to 'Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1' with the specification URL in external_resources; conforms_to_standard [CDS, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS]; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'; each of the nine file_collections carries its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard (e.g. cardiac_ecg -> WFDB + CDS; clinical_data -> OMOP_CDM + CDS with 'each CSV file in this directory is a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP CDM table' and a dqd_omop.json quality file). Integration: relationships records that 'files from different data types, modalities and devices are related by the participant identifier, which names the participant-level folder under every device folder'; preprocessing_strategies records RxNorm coding of medications; related_datasets carries typed links (is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and .1; is_documented_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449). Six standards, each bound to the modality it governs, plus LinkML schema conformance, a documented cross-modality join key and typed cross-dataset relationships - the full top band. The standards claims survive semantic checking rather than reading as a badge list: the native export format is named for each converted modality (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, Philips XML to WFDB, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth), so a reuser can tell what conversion was performed. Integration capability is real - one participant identifier joins survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental records - though harmonisation across the seven retinal devices is acknowledged in known_limitations as introducing between-device variation the user must handle. No ontology term identifiers (for example AIO or MeSH CURIEs) are attached to keywords or bias types, which is the one standardization axis left in prose.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (7 entries): OMOP CDM mapping with RxNorm medication coding; DICOM conversion naming which devices export DICOM natively and which are converted from .fda and .sdt; Open mHealth conversion of Garmin .FIT; WFDB conversion of Philips XML and ESDS for the environmental sensor; CDS v0.1.1 directory organization with manifest.tsv per data type; static watermarking; PHI and demographic removal. cleaning_strategies (3 entries): REDCap range flagging with coordinator and data-manager review, credibility/skip-pattern/missing/duplicate checks, edits only under site PI approval; internal PII review with 'The dataset has not undergone any formal external audits'; 'dqd_omop.json, supporting the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, which runs a set of more than 3,500 data quality checks'. missing_data_documentation supplies patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('Missing values are not imputed'). Labeling: instances.label false with 'No labeling was performed, because the dataset is hypothesis agnostic'. Absent: machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, and any named conversion software with a version or repository URL. Strategy documentation is comprehensive and the quality-control workflow is specific down to who may authorise an edit. It stops short of the top band because the tooling itself is largely unnamed: REDCap, the MoCA Duo application and the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard appear without versions, and no software or repository is identified for the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM, XML-to-WFDB or .FIT-to-Open-mHealth conversions that the release depends on. The absence of labeling and imputation is a documented design decision consistent with the hypothesis-agnostic framing in purposes and other_tasks, not an omission, and is credited as such. The GitHub organization is referenced but not tied to any named pipeline, so a reuser cannot reproduce the conversions from this record alone - the gap that separates 4 from 5 here.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: directly observed, subject-reported and validated flags all true, with verification 'by cross-referencing entered medications against medications that were physically brought in or photographed by each study participant'. collection_mechanisms: eleven entries naming device make, model and protocol - REDCap EDC; Philips PageWriter TC30 with chair angle recorded as 0/30/60/90 degrees; Dexcom G6 sampling every five minutes over ten days with participants masked; Garmin Vivosmart 5 at five-second intervals with wrist and handedness recorded; LeeLab Anura with its sensor list and explicit absence of video, audio and GPS; seven named retinal imaging systems; MoCA Duo on iPad; three named blood-pressure devices measured twice two minutes apart; M&S EVA at four metres with a 2.0 neutral density filter for mesopic testing; 10 g monofilament at three plantar locations ten times each; ~53 mL non-fasting blood draw with local CBC and central batch assay. data_collectors: six roles with training and certification requirements ('mandatory institutional compliance training for human subject research and successful administration of all protocol elements to at least three volunteer practice subjects'). collection_timeframes: start_date 2023-07-19, end_date 2025-05-01, with pilot and formal phases distinguished. raw_data_sources: eight entries with source_type and native format. sampling_strategies: non-probability wave-based recruitment with ICD-10 screening codes E11.X and R73.09. Protocol documentation is at the level of a manual of procedures: instrument, setting, timing, operator qualification and verification step are all recoverable. Comfortably the top band. Collection detail is consistent with every downstream claim: the ten-day concurrent wear of CGM, activity tracker and home sensor explains the per-collection file counts (2,246 CGM, 2,232 environment, 15,245 wearable); the device list matches the imaging subcrates one for one; the single-visit design matches the cross-sectional limitation in known_limitations and the absence of longitudinal linkage in relationships. The FAIRhub versus BMJ Open start-date discrepancy (19 versus 18 July 2023) is one day and is disclosed with its resolution.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.0.0'; version_access with latest_version_doi and all three versions with their DOIs and release dates (1.0.0 / 10.60775/fairhub.1 / 3 May 2024; 2.0.0 / .2 / 8 November 2024; 3.0.0 / .3 / 17 November 2025), per-version documentation via a version dropdown, and per-version scale (2.0.0: 165,051 files, 2.01 TB; 3.0.0: 356,343 files, 3.82 TB). updates: frequency 'Approximately once a year', static versions never updated in place, participant counts per version (204 / 1,067 / 2,280), changes recorded in a CHANGELOG. distribution_dates gives the three release dates. maintainers: 'The AI-READI team supports and maintains the dataset. It is hosted on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure', with contact routes. Repository and persistent ID: FAIRhub with a DOI per version; ARK identifiers per subcrate. retention_limit: 'There are no limits on the retention of the data'. Against this: no errata slot; raw_sources commits to preservation only 'at least for the duration of the project'; version_access states 'Version 2.0.0 is recorded on FAIRhub and in its documentation as no longer accessible'; notes records 'This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'. Versioning is exemplary - three DOIs, dated releases, per-version scale and documentation, and an explicit immutability policy. Sustainability is the weaker half: governance and a domain-appropriate repository are documented, but the institutional preservation commitment is bounded by the project period, a DOI-bearing prior version is already inaccessible, and the disclosed repository review notice is an unaddressed continuity risk. That combination is a clear 4 rather than the full sustainability band. Version metadata is internally consistent - participant counts across versions (204, 1,067, 2,280) rise monotonically and the 3.0.0 count matches instances.counts and every demographic marginal. The persistence defect is genuine rather than formal: a citable DOI whose object is withdrawn breaks the guarantee that the DOI is meant to carry, and the record surfaces it without describing a tombstone or retrieval-on-request path.

name: Associated Publications
text: Formal dataset citation identifying title, authors, version, publisher and DOI: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'. Distinct further references: related_datasets doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, both typed is_documented_by; external_resources entries for https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, the CDS specification at https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/, and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048. Well past the two-reference threshold, with a formal citation present, so the top band applies. The publication DOIs are semantically appropriate to their asserted roles - the BMJ Open item is described as the study protocol and the Nature Metabolism item as a comment, and both are cited elsewhere in the record for specific facts (funding statement, Safe Harbor description), so the references are load-bearing rather than ornamental. The record also flags that the BMJ Open paper misreports the ClinicalTrials.gov number as the IRB protocol string, a correctness catch in the source rather than in this datasheet.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 2,280 participants, each instance spanning survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental data. subpopulations: four objects with full distributions - race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836), sex (male 951, female 1,329), diabetes status (no diabetes 776, lifestyle 560, oral 686, insulin 258) and age (mean 60.8 +/- 11.3, eligibility 40-85). splits: per-partition demographic tables with means by partition. Inclusion/exclusion: age 40 and over with an 85 ceiling, English speaking, capacity to consent; exclusions pregnancy, gestational diabetes, type 1 diabetes. known_limitations names the absence of Pacific Islanders and Native Americans, the urban hospital-based recruitment base and the English-language requirement. missing_data_documentation explains modality-level non-coverage. Demographic characterisation is quantitative at both cohort and partition level and is paired with explicit eligibility criteria and named coverage gaps - the top band without reservation. All demographic marginals reconcile to 2,280 and to the split tables, so the representation claims are arithmetically sound. A substantive caveat the record itself raises: sex and race/ethnicity are withheld from the public release, so these distributions describe the cohort rather than variables a public reuser can access - which is why future_use_impacts concedes that models built on the public set cannot be audited directly for disparity across those groups. The documentation earns full marks; the dataset's own auditability limit is recorded under Q20 and in the issues list.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; distribution_formats access_urls 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; external_resources 'https://docs.aireadi.org/', 'https://aireadi.org/', 'https://github.com/AI-READI', 'https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi', 'https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/', 'https://classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06002048'; license at 'https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036'. Numerous well-formed persistent links across landing page, documentation, code, license and registration. Domains are plausible and consistent with the claimed publisher and program - fairhub.io for the release, zenodo.org for the license deposit, clinicaltrials.gov for the registration - and the DOI suffix matches the landing-page path. Link resolution was not exercised in this offline evaluation; the judgement is on structure and internal consistency.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: data_governance.access_review_process: 'logging in through a verified ID system; agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research; and agreeing to the license terms ... The FAIRhub access type is recorded as PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired', with the controlled-access tier requiring 'legal and privacy use agreements with the AI-READI research programme'. distribution_formats: four media types each with access_urls 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access' and the note 'All data files are in formats accessible with free software commonly used for such data types, so no specific software is required'. license_and_use_terms sets the terms a requester attests to. external_resources notes the version 3.0.0 documentation covers 'preliminary information on access and training prerequisites, the mini-subset version and Azure Storage access'; notes records a 'mini' version for pipeline development. Platform, authentication, attestation, licence gate, format accessibility, bulk-transfer route and a development-scale subset are all specified, and the public and controlled tiers are distinguished - the full band. The access path is consistent with the licence and with the sensitivity posture: self-attestation to disease-specific use matches data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research', and the controlled tier holds exactly the elements sensitive_elements lists as withheld. No download_url slot is populated, but per-format access_urls and the Azure Storage route make the obtaining path concrete. The only unquantified access risk is the disclosed 'under review for potential modification' notice on the repository.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms with a licence DOI and full grant and termination terms. intended_uses: three use_category objects with examples and usage_notes, including the model-dissemination condition to 'undertake all reasonable efforts to minimize the likelihood that data can be memorized, derived, reconstructed or reconstituted'. prohibited_uses: seven distinct prohibitions - clinical treatment decisions, any re-identification or group-membership inference, sharing with third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, onward transfer to non-licensees, republication beyond five illustrative figures per paper, watermark removal, and storage outside institutional or BAA-covered infrastructure. future_use_impacts: two entries covering the theoretical re-identification risk with mitigations (dissemination system, strict licence, watermarking) and the fairness consequence of withholding sex and race/ethnicity, mitigated by a validation/test split balanced on those variables 'stated as aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using this dataset'. Use guidance is unusually operational - the prohibitions name the specific reuse behaviours that matter for AI/ML, and the social impact entry pairs an identified harm with a concrete, checkable mitigation. Top band. Permissions and prohibitions are mutually coherent (models may be built and distributed, the data inside them may not travel; derivative and synthetic data inherit the restrictions), and the prohibitions align with the re-identification risk acknowledged in participant_privacy rather than exceeding or falling short of it. No discouraged_uses slot is populated - the record draws a binary permitted/prohibited line with no intermediate cautions - and the first impact entry's claim that the creators 'do not currently anticipate any uses that could result in unfair treatment or harm' is weaker than the analysis in the second entry. Neither is enough to drop a band given the depth elsewhere.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Entities and derivation paths: raw_data_sources gives eight native sources with formats and their fate - Philips XML 'released as WFDB after conversion', Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt 'Converted to DICOM for the dataset', Garmin .FIT 'Converted to the Open mHealth standard', REDCap exports, central laboratory CSV. Activities: preprocessing_strategies enumerates the mapping, conversion, organization, watermarking and PHI-removal steps; cleaning_strategies enumerates range flagging, credibility and skip-pattern checks, and OMOP DQD analysis. Agents: data_collectors names six roles with responsibilities, site data managers perform 'quality control of all data before uploading to FAIRhub', and edits are made 'only under the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator'. Dataset lineage: related_datasets is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and .1; version_access and updates document what each version contains. Quality and completeness: missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling), anomalies (six device- and participant-level failure modes), splits, and raw_sources on the retention and non-release of raw data. This is lineage rather than a changelog: for every modality one can trace native export to conversion activity to released standard, name the agent responsible at each stage, and see the quality checks applied. The rubric accepts text-form provenance with complete lineage, which this meets. The provenance is auditable against itself - the conversion targets named in raw_data_sources match the conforms_to_standard values of the corresponding file_collections in every case. Two integrity gaps keep this from being unimprovable rather than from being a 5: there are no file-level checksums or fixity information anywhere in the record, and no was_derived_from or errata slot is populated, so the version lineage and the derivation paths are expressed in prose and in related_datasets rather than as machine-actionable PROV relations. The inaccessibility of version 2.0.0 also breaks the retrievability of one node in that lineage.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: three objects typed with enumeration terms - selection_bias ('Participants are volunteers, so there is selection bias known as volunteer bias'), sampling_bias (ICD-10 screening of three academic health systems as the study base, with a mitigation_strategy of uniform protocols and site selection), representation_bias (deliberate equal-proportion recruitment of four race/ethnic groups, exclusion of Pacific Islanders and Native Americans, documented difficulty recruiting Black men, with a mitigation_strategy of wave-based monitoring and under/oversampling). future_use_impacts supplies the fairness analysis: the public release omits sex and race/ethnicity so 'models developed on it cannot be audited directly for disparity across those groups', mitigated by balanced validation and test partitions. known_limitations adds representativeness, coverage, temporal, scope and methodological limitation types, including between-device variation across the seven imaging systems. Bias types use standard enumeration terms, each is grounded in a specific recruitment or measurement fact, and a real fairness analysis with a concrete mitigation is present. It falls short of the top band because no AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology identifiers are attached to the bias types, the selection_bias entry carries no mitigation_strategy, and no measurement or device bias is typed despite known_limitations describing between-device variation as a methodological limitation. The bias entries are consistent with the sampling and limitation fields rather than generic - sampling_bias matches the ICD-10 codes E11.X and R73.09 in sampling_strategies, and representation_bias matches the four-group balanced design and the named excluded groups. The most consequential fairness issue is stated plainly rather than buried: balancing on sex and race/ethnicity while withholding those variables from the public release means the balance cannot be verified by public reusers, and the record concedes this. Bias is described in prose only; no quantitative fairness metric or per-subgroup performance baseline is supplied.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (12 of 14): id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; title 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~1,900 chars); keywords (9); license_and_use_terms (license_terms plus data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'); doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; creators (AI-READI Consortium, PI 'Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648)'); purposes (3 responses); instances ('Individual study participant', counts 2280); variables (9 entries, 8 substantive plus an explicit scope marker); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (2 of 14): resources (no nested sub-resource Dataset list; file_collections and subsets carry the structure instead) and parent_datasets (empty; version lineage is carried by related_datasets is_new_version_of to doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1). 12/14 = 85.7%, between the 70% (3) and 90% (5) bands and clearly nearer the top. The two absent fields are structural slots whose content exists elsewhere in the record rather than genuine documentation gaps, which is why this lands at 4 rather than 3; it does not reach 5 because the rubric counts the named slots and a consumer querying parent_datasets or resources retrieves nothing. Every populated field carries substantive rather than placeholder content — instances specifies a count and a topic code, variables distinguishes measured values from instrument reference ranges, and license_and_use_terms names three competing licence labels from the sources. The id is a DOI CURIE matching the bare doi field, so the two identification slots agree.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 1,900 characters, covering cohort ('2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus'), three named sites, the collection window, the AI/ML design rationale, each modality with its format standard (OMOP CDM, WFDB, DICOM, Open mHealth), scale ('356,343 files totalling approximately 3.82 TB'), directory organization under CDS v0.1.1, the deliberate absence of labels, and the public/controlled split of variables. purposes carries three responses of roughly 200, 270 and 210 characters respectively. Far beyond the >200 character threshold in both slots, and the length is informative rather than padded: the description would let a reuser decide suitability without opening any other field. Length here correlates with semantic density. The description states falsifiable specifics (participant count, file count, byte-scale, date range, named standards) that the rest of the record then corroborates, rather than the generic framing that inflates length without adding information.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: Nine unique keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam', 'Data Sharing', 'Exploratory Data Collection'. Nine distinct keywords clears the ≥8 band with no duplicates and no near-synonyms collapsing the effective count, so the threshold is met on substance as well as on arithmetic. Coverage is uneven against the record's own content: the keywords name the condition, the AI framing and three modalities, but omit OCT, OCT angiography and FLIO — which together account for the large majority of the 356,343 files — as well as wearable activity monitoring, environmental sensing and OMOP CDM. Scored at the band the rubric defines; the coverage gap is recorded as a low-severity discoverability issue rather than a deduction, since the question counts unique keywords.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats enumerates four media types — DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json), Markdown (text/markdown) — plus two access-mechanism entries (FAIRhub platform download with self-attestation; mini-subset for pipeline development). file_collections adds the per-directory format standards: WFDB for cardiac_ecg, OMOP CDM CSV for clinical_data, NASA ESDS ASCII for environment, DICOM for retinal_flio/oct/octa/photography, Open mHealth JSON for wearable_activity_monitor and wearable_blood_glucose. total_file_count 356343 and per-collection file_count values are given for all nine directories. Well beyond the >3 threshold, and unusually the enumeration is complete rather than illustrative: every one of the nine datatype directories carries its own file_count, total_bytes, conforms_to and conforms_to_standard, so the format variety is verifiable directory by directory. Format variety here genuinely indicates multimodality rather than incidental file-type spread, and the description independently claims the same modality set. Integration across modalities is supported by a shared participant-ID directory level ('one folder per participant named after the participant's study ID number'), which is the unified identifier this question's Bridge2AI note asks about.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes 3815969779678; total_file_count 356343; instances counts 2280; file_collections total_bytes for all nine directories (for example retinal_oct 1317625293027, retinal_octa 1155908809724, retinal_flio 1069466876718); splits gives 1,576 / 352 / 352; version_access gives prior-version sizes (165,051 files / 2.01 TB for v2.0.0). Passes on multiple independent grounds — byte totals, file counts, instance counts and per-split sizes — at both dataset and sub-collection granularity. The size figures are internally verifiable and were checked: the nine directory byte totals sum to exactly 3,815,969,360,064, matching the record's own stated sum, with the disclosed 419,614-byte residual against total_size_bytes. A pass here is therefore backed by arithmetic rather than by the mere presence of a number.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; publisher 'https://fairhub.io/'. Predecessor DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2 are recorded in version_access and related_datasets. Passes on both limbs the question asks for: a persistent identifier and an identified hosting repository, with the landing page resolving to the same repository that mints the DOI. The 10.60775 prefix is FAIRhub's DataCite prefix and is used consistently across all three versions, so the identifier scheme is coherent rather than ad hoc. No rrid is present, which is expected for a dataset rather than a research resource. The id/doi/page triple are mutually consistent — the CURIE form of the id resolves to the same object as the bare doi.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders lists four grantors. NIH carries a grant entry with a RePORTER project-details URI and the name 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project (award number OT2OD032644)', with notes giving the application ID 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, fiscal year 2022, awardee organization, PI, award amount 5,026,499 US dollars and project period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31, plus supplementary awards P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096. Also recorded: Research to Prevent Blindness; Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services); and named in-kind device contributions from Topcon, Optomed, iCare World, Carl Zeiss, Heidelberg Engineering, Dexcom and Garmin. creators gives affiliation 'AI-READI Consortium' with principal_investigator 'Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648)' and notes enumerating institutional collaborators (NIH, California Medical Innovations Institute, Johns Hopkins, OHSU, Stanford, UAB, UC San Diego). Meets the top band on both limbs. Funding documentation goes well past an agency name to award numbers, amounts, periods and a resolvable RePORTER URI, and separately captures non-monetary support (in-kind device loans and research discounts) that most datasheets omit entirely. OT2OD032644 parses correctly as an NIH award (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032644), the OT2 mechanism matches Common Fund Bridge2AI awards, and the stated programme name matches that award. Funding purpose aligns with purposes, which target AI/ML research on T2DM and the creation of a blueprint for ethically sourced AI-ready datasets — the stated aims of the Bridge2AI data generation awards. One weakness noted without deduction: the sole creator affiliation is the Consortium's own name, and the PI's institutional affiliation is left unresolved between two institutions in creators.source_caveats.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: three entries — University of Washington IRB protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 2022-12-20 with the approval letter published, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs; a named ethics panel (Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans) with contact_person; and engagement with the Native Biodata Consortium on Tribal data governance. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval, ethics_review_board with full address and reliance contact, regulatory_compliance (NCT06002048, not FDA-regulated, NIH GDS security best practices), special_populations (adults 40–85, able to consent, English-speaking; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes excluded). is_deidentified: HIPAA Safe Harbor, identifiers_removed enumerated. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (Level 3 security classification, encrypted servers, watermarking, privacy-by-design device selection — 'these devices do not capture video or audio, are not equipped with GPS location monitoring and are not synced with participant-owned devices'), reidentification_risk, data_linkage. participant_compensation: 200 US dollars, type, rationale, plus prorating and disbursement terms. at_risk_populations: three special_protections including rideshare transportation assistance. informed_consent: e-consent and in-person, consent_type, consent_scope, consent_documentation (approved form published), withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, consent_revocations ('any data that had been shared or used up to that point would stay in the dataset') and collection_notifications. regulatory_restrictions: hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance, and governance contact via data_governance plus contact@aireadi.org. Reaches the top band. Every protection area the question enumerates is populated with operational specifics rather than assertions — a protocol number and approval date, a published consent form, a named withdrawal limitation, a dollar compensation figure with disbursement conditions, and privacy engineering decisions at the device-selection level. The one named slot left empty, data_protection_impacts, has its substance delivered by two other fields the question also names: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states the residual risk and future_use_impacts states the risk and its mitigations. That is why the empty slot is recorded as a medium-severity completeness issue rather than taken as a deduction. Cross-field logic holds throughout: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a documented method and by participant_privacy protections. Deidentification method is appropriate to the data type — Safe Harbor is the correct US instrument for PHI in a health dataset, and the additional removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications goes beyond Safe Harbor with a stated rationale (preventing stigmatization of findings). Restrictiveness is proportionate: residual re-identification risk is acknowledged and answered with watermarking, a DUA tier and contractual limits on model vendors. One content-accuracy tension is flagged separately — 'NoDeIdentification' recorded alongside 'Safe Harbor applied' cannot both be literally true, though the record explains the provenance of each.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms describes the AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 (Licensor named, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with its operative provisions: non-exclusive non-transferable licence to download, reproduce, use and create derivative works; sharing only with identically bound licensees; storage restricted to institutional servers or cloud covered by a HIPAA BAA; derivative and synthetic data treated as data; acknowledgement obligation; automatic termination on breach with deletion of all copies. data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'. ip_restrictions: title and all IP rights remain with the Licensor, all rights not expressly granted reserved. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level 'restricted'; hipaa_compliant 'compliant'; other_compliance (not FDA-regulated, no DMC, Safe Harbor); regulatory_restrictions text requiring compliance with NIH GDS Policy security best practices and prohibiting removal of watermarking. data_governance: committee_name 'AI-READI Consortium', accountable_organization with ROR, access_review_process recording the FAIRhub tier 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' plus verified-ID login, disease-specific use attestation and a DUA for controlled access, three stewardship_roles including a Community Advisory Board of 11 persons, and an access conditions URL. Top band. The access tier is stated explicitly and in the terms this rubric's note asks for — openly accessible but gated by verified identity, a use attestation and, for the sensitive tier, a signed agreement — with none of the misleading 'open'/'public' framing the note warns against. Governance is documented as a standing structure (committee, accountable organization with ROR, stewardship roles, advisory board) rather than as a single contact line. Licence restrictiveness is consistent with the human-subjects and privacy content: a dataset with acknowledged residual re-identification risk is paired with contractual secondary-sharing controls, and the record states the reasoning ('secondary sharing controls are what protect the study participants'). Two values are evaluator-visible derivations that the record itself labels as such — confidentiality_level 'restricted' against the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)', and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' where no source uses that word. Both derivations are defensible on the stated access model and the Safe Harbor determination, and the disclosure of their derived status is a transparency strength; they are recorded as a low-severity consistency issue, not a deduction. The unresolved Licensor/IRB institution conflict is scored against Q9 only to the extent it muddies who is accountable, which the governance structure otherwise documents clearly.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. conforms_to narrates the standards stack: CDS v0.1.1 for organization, WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical data ('each CSV file a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP CDM table'), NASA ESDS for environmental data, DICOM for all four retinal modalities, Open mHealth for wearables, plus an RO-Crate metadata file conforming to RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRscape profile 0.1. conforms_to_standard enumerates CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE. Each of the nine file_collections repeats its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. related_datasets carries four typed relationships (two is_new_version_of to the predecessor DOIs, two is_described_by to journal DOIs). external_resources links the documentation site, the project site, the Zenodo community, the GitHub organization and the CDS specification. Integration capability: a per-participant directory level keyed on study ID, participants.tsv and participants.json at the root, OMOP CDM tables spanning all 2,280 participants, and a dqd_omop.json supporting the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard. Top band on all three limbs. Formats are standard and domain-appropriate for every modality; schema conformance is asserted at both the datasheet level (LinkML w3id URI) and the data level (seven named standards, repeated per directory); and integration capability is concrete — a shared participant identifier across modalities, a common-data-model mapping for the clinical tier, and machine-readable RO-Crate packaging. Technical terms are used correctly and consistently: OMOP CDM is applied to observational clinical data, DICOM to imaging, WFDB to waveform, Open mHealth to wearable streams and ESDS to environmental time series — each is the conventional standard for its modality, so the standards claims are semantically appropriate rather than decorative. The typed relationships resolve to real DOIs with registrar-consistent prefixes. Against the Bridge2AI AI-readiness criteria this record is strong on FAIRness, computability and statistical characterization; pre-model explainability support is thinner, but the question's named fields are fully satisfied.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (4 entries): mapping to OMOP CDM and DICOM; format conversions '.fda and Heidelberg .sdt files are converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT files are converted to the Open mHealth standard, and electrocardiogram data are stored in the WaveForm DataBase (WFDB) format'; HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications; CDS v0.1.1 directory organization with named root metadata files. cleaning_strategies (2 entries): REDCap range flagging with reports reviewed by data managers and coordinators, credibility and skip-pattern checks, editing only under site PI approval; and central QC before dissemination with 'An OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard file (dqd_omop.json) supporting the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard tool, which runs a set of more than 3,500 data quality checks'. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('where such a fill was possible the value was supplied, otherwise it was left missing... No instances were excluded from the dataset at the time of preprocessing'). Named tools with versions where given: CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape profile 0.1, REDCap, MoCA Duo, OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard. Absent: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols. Strategies are comprehensive and the cleaning documentation is specific about who could edit data and under what authority, which is more than most records supply. It stops short of 5 because the question's top band asks for software versions and URLs: the conversion pipelines (.fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG to WFDB) are described by input and output format but no converter, version or repository path is named, and the GitHub organization is referenced only generically in external_resources rather than linked to any specific processing step. The four empty fields are not equally meaningful. labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools and annotation_analyses are coherently absent: description states the release 'ships without labels or targets' and 'no annotation or labeling was performed', and instances sets label=false, so their omission agrees with an explicit assertion rather than hiding a gap. imputation_protocols is likewise consistent with the stated handling_strategy, which fills only from other portions of the same record and otherwise leaves values missing — a non-imputation policy, correctly described. The deduction therefore rests solely on the missing tool versions and links, not on the empty annotation slots.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: structured booleans (was_directly_observed true, was_reported_by_subjects true, was_inferred_derived false, was_validated_verified true) with details including a concrete verification practice ('cross-referencing entered medications with the medications that were physically brought in or photographed by each study participant'). collection_mechanisms: twelve entries naming instruments and settings — REDCap for questionnaires and clinical entry; EHR screening with ICD-10 codes R73.09 and E11.X; 'Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph, performed with the participant in a reclining chair or supine, with the chair position recorded (0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees relative to supine)'; Optomed Aurora IQ and iCare Eidon fundus imaging with field of view and dilation status; four OCT/OCTA platforms with scan protocols; FLIO with wavelength channels and sequencing rationale; Dexcom G6 for 10 days at 5-minute intervals; Garmin Vivosmart 5 for 10 days at 5-second sampling; LeeLab Anura environmental sensor; vision instruments; monofilament and MoCA testing; blood and urine collection with named laboratories and shipping regime. collection_timeframes: start_date 2023-07-19, end_date 2025-05-01, with project timeline, pilot window and planned recruitment end, plus a source_caveat on the competing 18 July 2023 date. data_collectors: two roles with training, certification ('before enrolling participants all coordinators had to successfully administer all protocol elements to at least three volunteer practice subjects') and the full staffing taxonomy. raw_data_sources: nine origin systems with native formats. Unambiguously top band. All four required elements are present, and the mechanism detail reaches the level of device model, scan protocol, wear duration, sampling frequency and participant positioning — enough for a reuser to interpret each modality's files and, in principle, to replicate the acquisition. Collection detail cross-validates other fields rather than standing alone: the 10-day Dexcom and Garmin wear periods explain the device-return failure modes listed in anomalies; the FLIO sequencing rationale explains the compliance caveat recorded for that modality; the multi-device acquisition explains the measurement_bias entry in known_biases. The timeframe is temporally consistent with IRB approval (2022-12-20) preceding collection and with the v3.0.0 release date following it.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.0.0'. version_access: latest_version_doi, three versions_available each with DOI, release date and scale (v1.0.0 2024-05-03, 204 participants; v2.0.0 2024-11-08, 1,067 participants, 165,051 files, 2.01 TB, now inaccessible with users directed to the latest; v3.0.0 2025-11-17, 2,280 participants, 356,343 files, 3.82 TB), and version_details describing static versioning, per-version documentation sets at docs.aireadi.org navigable by dropdown, and the substantive changes between versions (added participants, added imaging devices, Snellen dropped in favour of logMAR, move from ad hoc to automated processing, introduction of the recommended split). updates: frequency 'Approximately once a year' with the policy that versions are reissued rather than updated in place and changes documented in CHANGELOG. distribution_dates: three dated releases. maintainers: 'The AI-READI team supports and maintains the dataset. The dataset is hosted on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure', with three contact routes including contact@aireadi.org. doi and publisher present; retention_limit states no limits on retention. Sustainability: persistent DOIs per version, governance via data_governance (committee, ROR-identified accountable organization, access review process, stewardship roles), a domain-appropriate repository (FAIRhub, a biomedical data repository that mints DataCite DOIs), and institutional commitment via named maintainers, hosting arrangement and the funded project period. Top band. Versioning is comprehensive — three releases, each with its own DOI, date, scale and documentation set, plus an explicit and reasoned static-versioning policy — and all four sustainability indicators the question names are evidenced. errata is the only named slot empty, which is a minor gap given that inter-version changes are captured in version_details and a referenced CHANGELOG and that no erratum is recorded as having been issued. Version metadata is internally consistent and monotonic: participant counts (204, 1,067, 2,280), file counts and byte totals all increase across releases, and each release date follows its collection window. The statement that v2.0.0 'is no longer accessible' while retaining its DOI is honest about a real preservation weakness — a persistent identifier that no longer resolves to retrievable data — and is worth flagging to reusers who cite v2.0.0, though it does not contradict any other claim. Institutional commitment is the least firmly evidenced indicator: hosting and maintenance are asserted and funded through 2025-08-31, with no preservation guarantee stated beyond the project period.

name: Associated Publications
text: Formal dataset citation present and complete: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3' — identifying the dataset by title, version, publishing organization and authoring body — together with citation instructions at https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/citation described as the operative requirement. Distinct references beyond the dataset DOI: (1) Nature Metabolism, doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, 'AI-READI: rethinking AI data collection, preparation and sharing in diabetes research and beyond', 6:2210-2212; (2) BMJ Open, doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, Owsley C, Matthies DS, McGwin G, et al., 2025;15:e097449; (3) the AI-READI documentation site; (4) the project website, Zenodo community, GitHub organization and CDS specification; (5) the licence at doi:10.5281/zenodo.17555036. Meets the 5 condition squarely: well in excess of two distinct references, and a formal dataset citation that names the dataset by title and its publishing organization rather than presenting a bare DOI. Scored at 5 per the question's requirement to use only 0, 3 or 5. Both journal DOIs carry prefixes matching their stated publishers (10.1038 Springer Nature for Nature Metabolism, 10.1136 BMJ for BMJ Open), and the licence DOI carries Zenodo's 10.5281 prefix — the references are registrar-consistent and not fabricated-looking. The record is candid that the citation string it reproduces comes from the RO-Crate associatedPublication field while the operative requirement is the documentation-site instruction, which is the right precedence to record. Repeated links to the same resource were counted once.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 'Individual study participant', counts 2280, with the modality span per instance. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present false with a stated reason (sex, race and ethnicity withheld from the public release), and distribution giving cohort aggregates — 'by race/ethnicity, Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, white 836; by sex, male 951, female 1,329; by diabetes status, no diabetes 776, lifestyle-controlled 560, oral-medication-controlled 686, insulin-controlled 258. Mean age across the cohort is 60.8 years with a standard deviation of 11.3.' splits: full per-split demographic breakdowns with means and standard deviations. at_risk_populations: three special_protections. Inclusion/exclusion: 'Eligibility was restricted to adults aged 40 to 85 who are able to provide consent and who speak and read English, with pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes as exclusions' (known_limitations), repeated in human_subject_research.special_populations. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling. subsets.is_subpopulation false on all three subsets, correctly, since the subsets are access tiers. Top band. Demographic characterization is quantitative and complete on four axes (race/ethnicity, sex, diabetes severity, age with dispersion), inclusion and exclusion criteria are stated explicitly with the upper as well as lower age bound, and the record explains why per-instance subpopulation labels are absent rather than simply omitting them. All demographic arithmetic was recomputed and holds exactly: each of the three cohort breakdowns sums to 2,280, the splits sum to 2,280, each split's breakdowns sum to its own size, and every subgroup summed across the three splits reproduces its cohort figure. The subpopulation_elements_present=false flag is semantically correct rather than contradictory — the record distinguishes dataset-level aggregates from per-instance labels, and the distinction matters because the withheld attributes are exactly the ones a fairness audit would need. The limitation that Pacific Islanders and Native Americans are not represented is stated in the same record, so the demographic claim is bounded rather than overstated.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; distribution_formats access_urls including 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; external_resources listing https://docs.aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org (with team, goals and contact pages), https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI and https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/; predecessor DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2; licence DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036; publication DOIs 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449. Passes comfortably: a resolvable DOI, a landing page, an access page, versioned documentation and several supporting persistent links. All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains, and each domain matches the role it is given (fairhub.io for the repository and landing page, docs.aireadi.org for versioned documentation, zenodo.org for the licence deposit and community, github.com for code). Documentation is versioned in the path structure ('select "Dataset v3.0.0"', with v1 and v2 healthsheet URLs given), so findability persists across releases rather than tracking only the latest.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats entry 'FAIRhub platform download with self-attestation' with access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, and the note that 'Accessing it requires logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms', plus 'Version 3.0.0 of the documentation adds guidance on Azure Storage access' and 'All data files are in formats accessible with free software commonly used for such data types, so no specific software is required'. A second entry describes the mini-subset for pipeline development (FAIRhub child dataset id 4). data_governance.access_review_process records the FAIRhub tier verbatim as 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and states that the controlled tier 'is available only by entering into a data use agreement'. license_and_use_terms sets out the obligations a requester accepts. subsets documents what each tier contains. Top band. The access path is fully specified end to end: platform, landing and access URLs, authentication requirement, the attestation a user must make, the licence they accept, the software they need (none special), a bulk-transfer route via Azure Storage, and a smaller subset for pipeline development before committing to a 3.8 TB transfer. The record distinguishes access tiers precisely in the terms this rubric's note requires — registration-plus-attestation for the public release and a signed DUA for the controlled release — and never describes the dataset as unrestricted. The absence of a scalar download_url field is immaterial here because the access_urls within distribution_formats supply the same information, and a raw download link would in fact misrepresent an access model that is gated by attestation. The tiering is consistent with the ethics content: the variables behind the DUA are exactly those identified as sensitive.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: full terms as cited at Q9, with data_use_permission 'disease_specific_research'. intended_uses: two use_category entries with examples ('Pseudotime manifold analysis of disease trajectories; multimodal model development combining retinal imaging, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable activity, environmental and clinical data') and operational usage_notes, including the conditions under which a third-party model may analyze the data ('if the model vendor is party to a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement with the licensee's institution and the interaction is short-term, such as prompting or querying'). prohibited_uses: six entries covering clinical treatment decisions, re-identification and any attempt to contact or characterize data subjects, sharing with third-party model vendors for training, onward conveyance outside the licensee circle, reproduction beyond five illustrative figures per paper, and watermark removal. future_use_impacts: two entries — 'no uses of the dataset are currently anticipated that could result in unfair treatment or harm. However, there is a theoretical risk of future re-identification' and 'AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification. To prevent re-identification attempts, the project implements a robust data dissemination system, a strict licence agreement and data watermarking'. discouraged_uses: absent. Licence definition and use guidance are genuinely comprehensive — the prohibited_uses list is specific, enforceable and unusually well adapted to machine-learning reuse. Two things hold this below the top band. First, discouraged_uses is empty and, unlike the gaps at Q8 and Q11, its substance is supplied nowhere else: prohibited_uses states what is forbidden, not what is permitted but unwise, and this dataset has an obvious candidate — training on a deliberately non-representative, triple-balanced cohort as though it were a population sample. Second, the social impact analysis in future_use_impacts is confined to re-identification; the broader impacts this record itself surfaces elsewhere (equity consequences of models trained without Pacific Islander or Native American representation, the rationale that withholding race and sex prevents stigmatization of findings) are not carried into the impact analysis. The mitigations offered are concrete and verifiable against other fields — the dissemination system, licence and watermarking all reappear in regulatory_restrictions and participant_privacy — so the impact statement is not merely aspirational. The first future_use_impacts entry is in mild tension with the record's own bias and limitation documentation: 'no uses... currently anticipated that could result in unfair treatment or harm' sits awkwardly beside a representation_bias entry noting that whole population groups are unrepresented, which is a recognized pathway to inequitable model performance. The tension is between two well-documented fields rather than an error in either, and it is the narrowness of the impact analysis, not a false claim, that is penalized here.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
