text: Entities: raw_data_sources enumerates nine origin systems with source_type, native raw_data_format and access_details — REDCap capture; imaging device exports ('Topcon .fda files from the Maestro2 and Triton and Heidelberg .sdt files from FLIO'); Philips TC30 .xml; Garmin .FIT; Dexcom .csv; LeeLab Anura .csv; MoCA Duo .csv; laboratory results; and EHR used for screening only, with the explicit note that 'the EHR content itself is not the source of the released instance data, which was collected prospectively'. Activities: preprocessing_strategies gives the derivation paths (.fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG to WFDB, clinical to OMOP CDM, Safe Harbor stripping, CDS reorganization); cleaning_strategies gives the two QC stages. Agents: data_collectors (trained, certified coordinators and site data managers), cleaning_strategies (site data managers, site principal investigators approving every edit, central project team), data_governance.stewardship_roles. Version lineage: version_access with three DOIs and version_details; related_datasets is_new_version_of to doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1. Quality: missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling_strategy); anomalies (seven modality-specific entries); dqd_omop.json supporting 3,500-plus OMOP quality checks. splits fully specified; subsets.is_data_split false on the three access tiers. raw_sources records that raw data are preserved but not shared, with the reason. Top band. The rubric accepts textual provenance, and what is here is a complete lineage rather than a version history: for every modality a reuser can trace the originating device, its native format, the transformation applied, the standard it lands in, who performed and who authorized the quality control, and which prior release the version descends from. The disclosure that raw data are withheld, with the reason (unmapped terminologies and possible PHI in free text), completes the picture by stating where the traceable chain stops. Provenance is corroborated by arithmetic rather than asserted: the nine file_collections that the derivation paths terminate in reconcile exactly to the reported file count, and their byte totals reconcile to within the 419,614 bytes the record itself discloses. The empty was_derived_from and parent_datasets slots are a machine-readability gap — a consumer querying those fields gets nothing even though the lineage exists in related_datasets and raw_data_sources — and that gap is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue; it does not reduce the score because the question directs scoring from content rather than field presence, and the content is complete. errata is likewise empty with no erratum recorded as issued.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: four entries, each typed with a BiasTypeEnum value and each carrying a description and a mitigation_strategy — selection_bias (volunteer bias, mitigated by wave-based recruitment adjusted by under- and oversampling); sampling_bias (EHR-screened, 'predominantly urban and hospital-based', mitigated by uniform protocols and geographically varied site selection); representation_bias (interim imbalance, omission of Pacific Islanders and Native Americans, historic under-recruitment of Black men, Hispanic and Asian persons, and the English-language requirement) with affected_subsets enumerated and a five-part mitigation_strategy including 'recommended data splits with validation and test sets balanced as far as possible for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status'; measurement_bias (multiple device models per measure, operator-dependent image quality, mitigated by documenting device make and model 'to ensure repeatability'). future_use_impacts: re-identification risk and mitigations. Supporting fairness material: known_limitations with representativeness, coverage, scope and temporal limitations; sampling_strategies with is_representative false and a why_not_representative rationale; splits with balanced validation and test sets 'intended to reduce disparities in models developed using this dataset'; subpopulations with the cohort distribution. Top band. Biases are categorized systematically using the schema's standard taxonomy, not merely narrated; each category carries an actionable mitigation; and fairness analysis is present in operational form — a pre-computed balanced evaluation partition on attributes that are withheld from the public release, which is a concrete fairness affordance rather than a statement of intent. The bias taxonomy is used correctly: each label matches the mechanism described (volunteer self-selection as selection_bias, EHR-based frame construction as sampling_bias, group under-coverage as representation_bias, multi-device instrumentation as measurement_bias), so the categorization is semantically sound rather than label-shaped. No AIO ontology term identifiers are attached, which would strengthen machine-readable RAI alignment, but the taxonomy the rubric names is applied throughout. The bias documentation is candid in a way that cuts against the dataset's own marketing: it states that the balanced design is deliberately not population-representative and names the groups excluded, which is the disclosure a downstream fairness audit most needs.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id (doi:10.60775/fairhub.3); title ('Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'); description (~1,600 chars); keywords (7); license_and_use_terms (AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0, data_use_permission: disease_specific_research); doi (10.60775/fairhub.3); page (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3); creators (AI-READI Consortium with PI Aaron Lee, ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, nine ROR-identified affiliations); purposes (4 entries); instances (2280, data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:43); variables (20 entries with data_type, unit, measurement_technique); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level ('restricted'); resources (nine metadata_file entries nested under the root_metadata file collection). Absent: parent_datasets. 13 of 14 named fields carry meaningful content (~93%). Only parent_datasets is empty, and the version lineage it would express is captured by typed related_datasets entries (is_new_version_of to 10.60775/fairhub.2 and .1). Content is substantive rather than placeholder throughout. Field values are semantically appropriate to their slots: id and doi agree, page resolves to the publisher named in publisher, and confidentiality_level 'restricted' is consistent with the DUA-gated access mechanism described in data_governance. The resources list appears nested rather than at top level, which satisfies the hierarchical sub-resource intent but is a structurally weaker placement than a top-level list.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is approximately 1,600 characters and is specific rather than generic: it names the three collection sites, the 2280-participant count, the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window, 356,343 files, 3.82 TB, and enumerates thirteen modalities. Each of the four purposes entries exceeds 200 characters, e.g. 'To collect and publicly share a multimodal, AI-ready dataset for studying the pathogenesis and salutogenesis of T2DM, uniformly balanced for T2DM severity across a diverse group of participants recruited at three geographically distinct sites.' Average narrative length far exceeds the 200-character threshold, and length here reflects genuine information density rather than padding. The description carries quantitative specifics that are independently checkable against other fields (participant count matches instances.counts; file count and byte total match the stated totals; date range matches collection_timeframes), so its length corresponds to verifiable content. It also proactively discloses what was removed from the public release.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam' — 7 unique terms, all distinct with no near-duplicates. Seven keywords place the record at the top of the 3-7 band, one short of the ≥8 threshold. The set is genuinely diverse, spanning the disease, the analytic method and four acquisition modalities, which is why it scores above the band anchor rather than at it. The keyword set under-represents the record's own modality coverage: OCT angiography, FLIO, wearable activity monitoring, environmental sensing and OMOP conformance are prominent in description and file_collections but absent from keywords, so discoverability lags the actual content. No supplementary condition list or ontology-coded disease field is present to offset the count, though conforms_to_standard supplies standard-level terms.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 4 entries each with a media type: DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json), Markdown (text/markdown). Additional formats appear in resources (TXT, TSV, MD) and raw_data_sources (.xml, .fda, .sdt, .FIT). total_file_count: 356343. file_collections enumerates 10 collections with per-collection file_count and total_bytes, e.g. retinal_octa (173,721 files; 1,155,908,809,724 bytes), retinal_oct (56,478), retinal_photography (93,921). Well above the >3 threshold, and the enumeration is granular: each collection carries its own path, collection_type, description, file count, byte total and conformance standards. Format variety corresponds to genuine multimodality rather than incidental file-type spread — DICOM for imaging, CSV for OMOP tables and sensor streams, WFDB for waveforms — and the record documents the unifying participant-ID directory scheme that makes the modalities integrable, which is the Bridge2AI multimodality criterion. Only the root_metadata file_count is the record's own enumeration rather than a source-stated value, which it discloses.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; total_file_count: 356343; instances.counts: 2280; per-collection total_bytes for all nine data-type collections; splits giving 1576/352/352; subpopulation distributions with counts for diabetes status, sex and race/ethnicity. Size metadata is present at both dataset and collection granularity, and dimensional metadata is present at participant, split and subpopulation level — comfortably exceeding the pass condition. The stated totals are 9 files and 419,614 bytes larger than the sum over enumerated directories, a gap the record itself surfaces and which the nine root-level metadata files account for exactly. This does not affect the pass determination, since numeric size and count metadata are unambiguously present, but it is logged as a consistency finding.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/. Prior versions carry their own DOIs (10.60775/fairhub.2, 10.60775/fairhub.1), and the license text is separately archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036. Both halves of the identification requirement are satisfied: a registered persistent identifier and an explicitly named hosting platform, with per-version DOIs rather than a single floating identifier. The 10.60775 prefix is FAIRhub's DataCite registrant and is consistent with the named publisher and landing page, so the identifier and the platform corroborate one another. No RRID is present, which is unremarkable for a dataset record of this kind.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: NIH with grant_number OT2OD032644 (award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project', NIH RePORTER project 1OT2OD032644-01, $5,026,499 FY2022, project period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31), plus P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096; additional grantors Research to Prevent Blindness and Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services). creators: AI-READI Consortium with principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) and nine ROR-identified affiliations. data_collectors notes that collection effort was supported by OT2OD032644 by percentage of effort. Meets the top band on both limbs. Grant detail extends beyond award numbers to title, amount and period, and creator affiliations are machine-identified by ROR rather than free text. All three NIH numbers match agency format (OT2/OD, P30/DK, UL1/TR with correct institute codes), and the funding purpose aligns with purposes, which repeatedly invoke salutogenesis — the exact term in the award title. The record also discloses and adjudicates a tier-level disagreement about how many grants support the work, preferring the tier-1 funding reference while retaining the publication-sourced grants as research support. The unresolved Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington attribution affects the affiliation semantics but not the completeness of the funding record.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: UW IRB protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 2022-12-20, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs, approval letter published with v3.0.0 documentation, contact hsdrely@uw.edu; second entry records release-level ethics review by Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance (not FDA-regulated, no DMC, HL7:2N), special_populations (age 40-85, consent-capable, English-speaking; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and T1DM excluded). is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor', identifiers_removed, internal review for PII. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (variable removal, watermarking, license terms, encrypted servers and locked storage during collection), reidentification_risk, data_linkage. participant_compensation: $200 stipend, transport support, disbursement conditions. at_risk_populations: false, with prisoner and minor exclusions recorded. informed_consent: obtained true, e-consent or in-person, documentation, scope, withdrawal_mechanism. collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations all populated. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant. Absent: data_protection_impacts. Nearly every protection area is documented, and several to an unusual depth — the consent pathway, the withdrawal rule that already-shared data remain in the dataset, the compensation disbursement conditions, and the explicit prisoner and minor exclusions. Two gaps hold it below 5: no data_protection_impacts entry, and re-identification risk treated in a single qualitative sentence rather than as an assessment. Cross-field logic passes on the main gates: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews, informed_consent and participant_compensation, and is_deidentified is matched by a named method and listed privacy protections. Two semantic problems reduce the score. First, is_deidentified simultaneously asserts HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping and reports FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' finding that no identifiers were collected; these describe incompatible processing. Second, and more seriously, sensitive_elements_present=false and confidential_elements_present=false are implausible for retinal imaging, CGM and wearable biometric data whose release the record itself gates behind verified-ID login, license assent and watermarking, and for which it concedes a theoretical re-identification risk. Safe Harbor is an appropriate method for the clinical and survey strata, but the record does not address its known limits for high-dimensional imaging and continuous physiological signals, which is where a DPIA would have done the work.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms: AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with storage restrictions (institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud), derivative and synthetic data treated as data, acknowledgement obligations, NIH GDS security compliance, automatic termination on breach, as-is warranty disclaimer; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research. ip_restrictions: title and IP reserved to Licensor, model distribution permitted only where models do not contain the data and memorization is minimized. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant', NIH GDS Security Best Practices obligation, watermark non-removal, other_compliance (not FDA-regulated; HL7:2N reconciliation). data_governance: committee_name, accountable_organization, committee_contact (Aaron Lee, contact@aireadi.org), access_review_process ('PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired', verified-ID login, T2DM-research attestation, conditions at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access), stewardship_roles. Top band on every limb. The access tier is stated explicitly rather than left to the reader, avoiding the 'public means unrestricted' ambiguity, and the governance contact is a named person with ORCID and email rather than a generic mailbox. Restrictiveness is coherent across fields: a disease-specific use permission, a restricted confidentiality level, an attestation gate and watermarking all point the same direction and match the human-subjects posture. The record also explains rather than conceals its one divergence, recording that it chose 'restricted' over the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)' because access is gated, and that it took the license name from the FAIRhub API over the dataset page's 'Health Data License'. Stating the reconciliation rule is stronger practice than silently picking a value. The governance contact sits in data_governance rather than regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact, a placement difference only.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema (conforms_to_class: Dataset). conforms_to describes CDS v0.1.1 directory structure and per-modality standards: WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical data, DICOM for FLIO/OCT/OCTA/photography, Open mHealth for wearable and CGM, NASA ASCII Guidelines for Earth Science Data for environmental sensing, packaged as an RO-Crate conforming to RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRscape profile 0.1 with one subcrate per data type. conforms_to_standard enumerates CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE, and each file_collection repeats its own standards. related_datasets carries typed relationships (is_new_version_of x2, has_part). external_resources lists nine entries including GitHub, Zenodo community, docs site and ClinicalTrials.gov. Integration: participant-ID folder naming across every data type, modality and device; RxNorm-coded medication log; ICD-10 screening codes; dqd_omop.json supporting the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard. Exemplary. Standards are named at the modality level with versions, schema conformance is asserted against a resolvable w3id URI, and integration capability is evidenced by a concrete cross-modality join key rather than a general claim of interoperability. Each standard is correctly matched to its data type — WFDB genuinely is the waveform convention, Open mHealth genuinely is the mobile-health schema, ESDS is an unusual but defensible choice for environmental ASCII records — indicating accurate technical understanding rather than standard-name padding. The RO-Crate and FAIRscape packaging supplies machine-actionable metadata beyond the human-readable record, and the OMOP DQD artifact means quality characterization is computable. The one weakness relative to a fully harmonizable release is that the OMOP mapping is stated as applying 'where possible' without specifying which domains remain unmapped.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (2): mapping to OMOP CDM for clinical data and DICOM for imaging, transformation of proprietary exports before FAIRhub upload (Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth), automated plus custom processing in contrast to v1.0.0's custom/ad hoc approach; and an explicit statement that no instances were excluded at preprocessing. cleaning_strategies: REDCap min/max range flagging surfaced in coordinator and data-manager reports, checks for credibility against prespecified ranges, skip-pattern violations, fillable missing values, and omitted or duplicated records, with editing only under site PI approval. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy. Named tools: REDCap, MoCA Duo application, OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard (dqd_omop.json). Absent: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols. The strategy documentation is genuinely comprehensive and the four empty fields are each justified rather than merely missing: the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and carries no labels, so labeling and annotation tooling does not apply, and handling_strategy states that no imputation of missing modality data was performed. What keeps it from 5 is the absence of software versions and URLs — the conversion and mapping pipelines are described by effect, with no tool names, versions or links to the repositories in the linked GitHub organization. The cleaning description is methodologically coherent: range-flagging at entry, human adjudication, and a documented authority (the site PI) for edit-or-remove decisions, which is the appropriate governance for clinical data and is consistent with the data_collectors roles. The justification for absent labeling metadata is internally consistent with instances.label=false and other_tasks, which states researchers must define their own labels and that the project provides no guidelines. The transparency gap is reproducibility-relevant: a reader cannot re-run the .fda-to-DICOM or .FIT-to-Open-mHealth conversions from this record alone.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2) with provenance flags: directly observed measurements (was_directly_observed true) and participant-reported REDCap questionnaires (was_reported_by_subjects true, was_validated_verified true, with medication cross-referencing against physically presented or photographed medications). collection_mechanisms: 21 entries at device and protocol granularity — Philips PageWriter TC30 12-lead ECG with posture recorded; OMRON HEM 907XL / Medline MDS4001 / Welch Allyn 6000 BP with duplicate measurement; 10 g monofilament at three sites per foot; MoCA Duo on iPad with subscores and completion times; M&S EVA visual acuity at 4 m photopic and mesopic with 2.0 ND filter; MARS contrast sensitivity; Topcon KR 800 autorefraction; Optomed Aurora IQ 50-degree undilated fundus; iCare EIDON confocal; Heidelberg Spectralis ONH-RC, PPole-H and macular OCTA; Heidelberg FLIO acquired last; Topcon Triton 12x12/6x6 OCTA and 3D modes; Topcon Maestro2 widefield and 50 kHz OCTA; Zeiss Cirrus 5000 512x512 and 200x200; Dexcom G6 5-minute sampling over 10 days with participants masked; Garmin Vivosmart 5 at 5-second sampling with wrist and dominance recorded; LeeLab Anura home placement; CLIA-certified local CBC with remaining assays at the UW Nutrition and Obesity Research Center. data_collectors (3 roles) with training by the UAB data manager, a Manual of Procedures, compliance training and certification on at least three practice subjects. collection_timeframes: 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 with project timeline and a source caveat on the start date. Also direct_collection, sampling_strategies (ICD-10 R73.09 and E11.X screening, wave-based recruitment) and raw_data_sources. Among the most detailed collection documentation the rubric contemplates. Every named field is populated, and the mechanism detail reaches scan geometries, sampling rates, laterality and acquisition order — enough for a third party to reconstruct the visit protocol. Device and protocol descriptions are technically accurate and internally consistent with the file_collections, which list exactly the devices named here (heidelberg_spectralis, topcon_maestro2, topcon_triton, zeiss_cirrus, icare_eidon, optomed_aurora, dexcom_g6, garmin_vivosmart5, leelab_anura). Acquisition-order rationale is coherent with the anomalies section, which explains that FLIO is performed last because it is uncomfortable and lengthy. Collector qualification is described as a verifiable certification process rather than an assertion of competence. The start-date disagreement with the BMJ Open protocol is disclosed and adjudicated by source tier.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '3.0.0'. version_access: all three versions with DOIs, dates and participant counts (1.0.0 / 10.60775/fairhub.1 / 2024-05-03 / 204; 2.0.0 / 10.60775/fairhub.2 / 2024-11-08 / 1067; 3.0.0 / 10.60775/fairhub.3 / 2025-11-17 / 2280), latest_version_doi, and version_details summarising CHANGELOG differences (adds years two and three, adds imaging devices, moves from ad hoc to automated plus custom processing, drops Snellen acuity leaving logMAR). updates: frequency 'Approximately annually' with static-version release model stated. maintainers: AI-READI Consortium, hosted on FAIRhub via Microsoft Azure, contacts at README, aireadi.org/contact and docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact. distribution_dates: three dated releases. doi and publisher present. retention_limit: no limits on retention. extension_mechanism: no external extension mechanism. Absent: errata as a field. Versioning is comprehensive and unusually concrete, with per-version DOIs, counts and a change summary. Sustainability covers three of four indicators solidly — persistent identifiers, a domain-appropriate repository and a documented governance plan — but institutional preservation commitment is not stated, and two disclosed facts cut against long-term availability. Two record-internal signals prevent the top band. version_access states that version 2.0.0 is 'no longer accessible' even though it holds a minted DOI, which is a persistence failure for a citable release rather than a documentation gap; and notes records that the repository 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', an availability risk disclosed without a stated disposition. The funding period recorded under OT2OD032644 ends 2025-08-31, before the 2025-11-17 release, and no post-award preservation funding or institutional commitment is documented. Crediting the record for transparently surfacing all three, but they are exactly the sustainability facts the question asks about. The absence of an errata field is minor given CHANGELOG coverage.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3' — a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title with its authoring organization, version, publisher and DOI. Distinct further references in external_resources: the Nature Metabolism comment (https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x); the BMJ Open protocol, Owsley C, Matthies DS, McGwin G, et al. BMJ Open 2025;15:e097449, doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048; the license archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036; docs.aireadi.org; aireadi.org; the Zenodo community; and the GitHub organization. Top band on both limbs of the Q14 condition: well beyond two distinct references, and a formal dataset citation is present rather than a bare DOI. Citation instructions are additionally signposted, with the documentation resource described as covering citation. All publication DOIs are well formed and their prefixes match the stated publishers (10.1038 Springer Nature for the Nature Metabolism comment, 10.1136 BMJ for BMJ Open, 10.5281 Zenodo for the archived license), and the BMJ reference carries a complete author-volume-article citation. References are distinct resources rather than repeated links to one target, and they are functionally differentiated — protocol, project overview, trial registration, license text, documentation and code.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 2280 individual study participants with instance_type, data_topic, notes on cross-modality composition and two missing_information entries. subpopulations (4): race/ethnicity (380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White); biological sex (951 male, 1329 female); diabetes status in four recruitment groups (776 no diabetes, 560 lifestyle-controlled, 686 oral or non-insulin injectable, 258 insulin-controlled); age (eligibility 40-85, mean 60.8 ± 11.3). splits: 1576/352/352 with per-split age means and an explicit balancing rationale. at_risk_populations: false with minor, pregnancy and prisoner exclusions recorded. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling. Inclusion and exclusion criteria also in human_subject_research.special_populations and preprocessing_strategies (age ≥40, consent-capable, English-reading; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and T1DM excluded). sampling_strategies documents the triple-balanced design and why_not_representative. Top band. Demographics are quantified across four dimensions, inclusion and exclusion criteria are stated explicitly, and the population characterization extends to the recruitment design rationale and to what is deliberately absent from the cohort. Every subpopulation distribution sums exactly to 2280, as do the recommended splits, so the demographic characterization is arithmetically self-consistent. The record is candid about a real tension it does not hide: sex and race/ethnicity drove recruitment balance and split construction but are withheld at participant level, with subpopulation_elements_present=false for both, so downstream fairness auditing on those axes is not possible from the public release. That is a genuine limitation of the dataset rather than of its documentation, and the record discloses it, quantifies the aggregate distributions, and mitigates it by releasing splits pre-balanced on the withheld variables.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/; access conditions at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; external_resources with https://docs.aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036, https://classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06002048; per-version DOIs for v1.0.0 and v2.0.0. Well beyond the pass threshold, with resolvable identifiers at dataset, version, license, documentation and code level. All URLs are structurally well formed with plausible domains consistent with the entities they claim to represent, and the DOI, landing page and publisher corroborate one another. Findability of superseded versions is partially undercut by v2.0.0 being marked no longer accessible despite holding a DOI, which is recorded as a warning under Q13 rather than affecting this pass determination.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: data_governance.access_review_process: 'Accessing the dataset requires logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms', with FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and conditions published at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access. third_party_sharing: distributed for public use through FAIRhub under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 subject to verified-ID login, attestation and license assent, with onward conveyance limited to identically bound licensees. distribution_formats: four media-typed formats. license_and_use_terms: full terms with data_use_permission disease_specific_research. Platform, hosting (FAIRhub via Microsoft Azure) and documentation entry points all named. Top band. Platform, authentication step, attestation requirement and policy are each stated, and the access tier is characterized explicitly rather than described loosely as 'public'. A separate download_url field is absent, but the landing page and a dedicated access-conditions URL are given, so the obtain path is unambiguous. The record avoids the failure mode the rubric warns about: it identifies the release as publicly downloadable yet conditioned on verified identity and self-attestation, which is tier 2-3 rather than unrestricted, and it uses FAIRhub's own controlled term for that tier. The access mechanism is consistent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', with the disease-specific use permission, and with the prohibition on onward conveyance to non-licensees — the licensing, governance and access descriptions all encode the same restriction level.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: full AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 terms. intended_uses (2): type 2 diabetes research with the attestation requirement, and research and commercial AI/ML development, with an example permitting distribution of models that do not themselves contain the data. prohibited_uses (6): clinical treatment decisions; re-identification or contact of subjects, including membership inference; sharing with third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA; conveyance to non-licensees; reproduction beyond small samples in up to five figures per paper; removal of watermarking. future_use_impacts (1): creators do not currently anticipate uses causing unfair treatment, but note a theoretical re-identification risk from AI inference, mitigated by a data dissemination system, a strict license and watermarking. discouraged_uses: absent. Use guidance is genuinely comprehensive and unusually operational for the AI setting. Two things hold it below 5: discouraged_uses is empty, so no middle tier exists between permitted and forbidden, and the social impact analysis is confined to a single risk (re-identification) rather than spanning the societal impacts the record's own bias and limitation sections imply. The prohibited_uses reasoning is technically well targeted, anticipating memorization and membership inference rather than reciting generic confidentiality language, and the mitigations named in future_use_impacts (dissemination control, license, watermarking) map onto controls that actually appear in participant_privacy and regulatory_restrictions, so the impact analysis is not decorative. The deduction rests on a cross-field inconsistency: future_use_impacts asserts no anticipated uses resulting in unfair treatment of individuals or groups, while known_biases documents representation and sampling bias and known_limitations states that models may not generalize to populations the three health systems do not reach. Differential model performance on unrepresented groups is exactly an unfair-treatment pathway, and it is anticipated elsewhere in the same record.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: version_access and updates fully populated. raw_data_sources (2): EHR screening source used for recruitment only and not released; device-native exports with formats (.xml, .csv, .fda, .sdt, .FIT, DICOM) and an access statement that raw data are retained for the project duration but not shared because they are unmapped and may contain free-text PHI. preprocessing_strategies describes the transformation chain to DICOM, Open mHealth and OMOP CDM. data_collectors names the agents in sequence: site coordinators, site data managers responsible for QC before upload, and the central project team performing further processing. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes, handling_strategy. splits with per-set counts. related_datasets: typed is_new_version_of links to v2.0.0 and v1.0.0 and has_part to the mini-subset. conforms_to records RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with FAIRscape profile 0.1 and one subcrate per data type. Absent: was_derived_from, parent_datasets, errata. This clearly exceeds version history alone. A complete derivation path is recoverable — device-native export, format conversion, terminology mapping, site QC, central processing, FAIRhub release — with named agents and named activities, which the rubric accepts in textual form. It falls short of 5 because the three fields that would carry derivation (was_derived_from, parent_datasets, errata) are all empty, so the lineage must be reassembled by the reader across four unrelated sections rather than read as a graph. The entity-activity-agent triad is present in substance: entities are the raw exports and released collections, activities are conversion, mapping, cleaning and QC, and agents are the coordinators, site data managers and central team. The RO-Crate and FAIRscape packaging indicates a machine-readable provenance representation exists in the release, but the record references it as a packaging standard rather than exposing derivation relations. Data integrity is otherwise well supported: quality control is documented at entry and at site level, the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard artifact is shipped, anomalies are enumerated per modality with causes, and the unreconciled file-count and byte-total arithmetic is disclosed rather than smoothed over.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases (4), each typed from a controlled vocabulary: selection_bias (volunteer bias limiting generalizability); representation_bias (pilot phase unbalanced, ongoing enrollment, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with mitigation_strategy of triple-balanced recruitment targets, under- and oversampling, three geographically distinct sites and balanced recommended splits; sampling_bias (predominantly urban, hospital-based recruitment) with mitigation_strategy of uniform protocols across sites irrespective of race/ethnicity, sex or severity and deliberate site selection; selection_bias (English-language requirement creating recruitment difficulty for Hispanic and Asian persons). Supported by known_limitations (5 typed entries including representativeness_limitation with scope_impact), anomalies (6 modality-specific entries), future_use_impacts, splits balanced for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status and 'intended to reduce disparities in models developed using this dataset', and sampling_strategies.why_not_representative explaining the triple-balanced design as necessary for unbiased ML. Top band. Biases are categorized with BiasTypeEnum-style values rather than described loosely, mitigation strategies are attached to the two structural biases, and fairness analysis is present as a design property of the dataset — balanced recruitment and pre-balanced splits — rather than as a generic statement of intent. The bias taxonomy is applied correctly: volunteer bias is genuinely selection bias, urban hospital-based recruitment is genuinely sampling bias, and the demographic gaps are genuinely representation bias, so the categories are not mislabelled. The record also identifies a second-order bias most datasheets omit — that an English-language eligibility criterion interacts with the very ethnic-balance goal the study set for itself. Two limits stop short of ideal without displacing the top band: bias types are enum values without explicit AIO ontology URI mappings, and fairness analysis is design-level rather than a quantitative audit, which the withholding of participant-level sex and race from the public release would in any case prevent downstream. The tension between these documented biases and the 'no anticipated unfair treatment' statement in future_use_impacts is scored against Q18, where that field is central, rather than penalized twice.

name: Field Completeness
text: id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description: ~1,400 chars; keywords: 7 entries; license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission disease_specific_research plus ~2,000 chars of license_terms; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; creators: AI-READI Consortium with ROR affiliation and ORCID-identified PI; purposes: 3 responses; instances: 2,280 with instance_type and missing_information; resources: 9 file-level entries nested under the root-metadata file_collection (id/name/format/media_type/file_type each); variables: 14 entries with data_type, unit, measurement_technique; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted. Unpopulated: parent_datasets. 13 of the 14 named fields carry meaningful content, ~93%. The single unpopulated slot, parent_datasets, is substantively covered elsewhere by related_datasets with typed is_new_version_of links to fairhub.2 and fairhub.1, so no lineage information is actually lost. Content depth is well beyond token presence: variables carry units and reference ranges, instances carry a missing_information structure. Field values are semantically appropriate to their slots rather than padded. resources is used in its intended nested sense (files within a collection) rather than duplicated at top level. The confidentiality_level value is flagged by the record itself as its own enum mapping from 'HL7:2N (normal)', which is honest but means the field is an inference, not a source statement.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is approximately 1,400 characters, naming cohort size (2,280), age floor (40+), three named sites, version, collection window (2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01), nine modalities with their format standards, the recruitment balancing design across race/ethnicity, sex and four diabetes severity strata, the salutogenesis goal, and the public/controlled tier split. purposes carries three responses of roughly 180-300 characters each. Far above the >200 character threshold on both fields. Length here is carrying information rather than filler: the description alone supplies cohort, provenance, modality, standards and access-tier facts that a reuser would otherwise have to assemble from six other fields. Narrative content is internally consistent with the structured fields it summarizes: the 2,280 count matches instances.counts, the date range matches collection_timeframes, and the withheld-variable claim matches is_deidentified.identifiers_removed. No divergence between prose and structure was found.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam' — 7 unique entries, one short of the ≥8 band. Seven distinct, non-redundant keywords spanning condition, method and modality. The band is decided by count, and 7 falls squarely in the 3–7 range. Notably the keyword set under-represents the dataset's own breadth: home environmental sensing, wearable activity monitoring, OCT/OCTA, FLIO and the OMOP clinical tier all have no keyword, so discoverability is narrower than the holdings warrant. Considered the rubric note permitting supplementation by condition lists or ontology references. It does not lift this record into the top band: the note targets datasets spanning many conditions, whereas this dataset targets a single condition, and the only ontology-style reference available is the single instances.data_topic value B2AI_TOPIC:43, not a condition list. Scored on the keywords field as the rubric specifies.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists application/dicom, application/json, text/csv, text/markdown; nested resources add text/plain (TXT) and text/tab-separated-values (TSV) — 6 distinct media types. total_file_count: 356,343. file_collections enumerates 10 collections with per-collection file_count and total_bytes (e.g. retinal_octa 173,721 files; retinal_photography 93,921; retinal_oct 56,478; wearable_activity_monitor 15,245; retinal_flio 7,969; cardiac_ecg 4,515; wearable_blood_glucose 2,246; environment 2,232; clinical_data 7; root metadata 9). Well beyond the >3 threshold, with enumeration at collection granularity rather than a bare format list. The nine datatype file counts reconcile exactly against the stated total (356,334 + 9 root files = 356,343), which is a verifiable internal check that most records cannot support. Format variety genuinely reflects multimodality rather than incidental file-type spread: imaging (DICOM), waveform (WFDB), tabular clinical (OMOP CSV), sensor streams (Open mHealth JSON, ESDS ASCII) and documentation. The unified per-participant directory convention supplies the cross-modality identifier the rubric note asks about. DICOM is correctly recorded as media_type only, with the record explaining that DICOM is absent from the schema's format enum.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes: 3815969779678 (~3.82 TB); total_file_count: 356343; per-collection total_bytes for all nine datatype collections; instances.counts: 2280; splits totalling 1,576/352/352; three subsets with is_data_split: true; subpopulations with numeric distributions. Passes on multiple independent grounds. Size is given at both dataset and collection granularity, and instance counts are given at cohort, split and subpopulation level, so a reuser can size any subset of interest rather than only the whole. One arithmetic defect, disclosed by the record: the nine collection byte totals sum 419,614 bytes short of the stated total. The magnitude is negligible against 3.82 TB and the record flags it, so it does not affect the pass, but it is recorded as a correctness warning.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/; version-specific DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2; citation resolves the DOI as https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3. Passes with both components the rubric asks for: a persistent identifier and an identified hosting platform. Each release carries its own DOI, which is the correct granularity for a versioned dataset. The 10.60775 prefix is FAIRhub's registered DataCite prefix, so the DOI is not merely well-formed but attributable to a plausible registrar for this publisher. One unresolved point recorded as a warning: publisher is contested between FAIRhub (FAIRhub API) and AI-READI Consortium (RO-Crate), and the record carries the platform URI while documenting the conflict.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: National Institutes of Health with three grant entries — OT2OD032644 (Bridge2AI Salutogenesis Data Generation Project, application 10471118, FY2022, USD 5,026,499, 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096 — plus Research to Prevent Blindness. creators: AI-READI Consortium with affiliation Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) and principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) with two ROR-identified affiliations. source_caveats enumerates 15 further named study PIs with ORCID and ROR, and 7 ROR-identified collaborator organizations. Meets the top band fully: funders carry grant numbers, and creators carry institutional affiliations with persistent organizational identifiers. Award amount, period and program attribution exceed what the band requires. The record also distinguishes grants named in the dataset's own funding reference from those named only in publications, which is a meaningful provenance distinction. All three grant numbers validate against NIH structure: OT2OD032644 (OT2 other-transaction, OD Office of the Director — correct for a Common Fund Bridge2AI award), P30DK035816 (P30 center, NIDDK — appropriate for a diabetes center), UL1TR003096 (UL1, NCATS CTSA — appropriate for translational support). Funding purpose aligns with purposes, which name AI/ML readiness and Bridge2AI-style standards work. Two disclosed defects are recorded as low-severity warnings: divergent RePORTER project-detail IDs for one award, and the healthsheet's 'OT2ODO32644' letter-for-zero transcription, which the structured slot correctly does not reproduce.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: three entries — University of Washington IRB protocol STUDY00016228 approved 2022-12-20 with reliance agreements for UAB and UCSD and annual renewal within 90 days of expiration; a second entry naming four ethics reviewers (Nebeker, Mathews, Ferryman, Evans); and an 11-person Community Advisory Board that evaluates consent forms and protocols. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true with irb_approval, ethics_review_board contact (hsdrely@uw.edu, Human Subjects Division, full postal address), regulatory_compliance and special_populations. informed_consent: written consent, REDCap e-consent with electronic signature or in-person, consent form published with documentation, consent_scope recording the public-version restriction to T2DM research, and an explicit withdrawal_mechanism. collection_consents, consent_revocations (data already shared stays in the dataset, communicated in the consent document) and collection_notifications are all populated. is_deidentified: HIPAA Safe Harbor with identifiers_removed enumerated. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, six privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk, and data_linkage describing a Risk Level 3 security plan. participant_compensation: USD 200 stipend, not pro-rated, paid on device return, plus transport cost coverage. at_risk_populations: at_risk_groups_included false with special_protections enumerating exclusions of minors, prisoners, pregnant women and adults unable to consent. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance records non-FDA-regulated status. Unpopulated: data_protection_impacts; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact. Substantially above the '3' band, which asks only for IRB plus deidentification: this record documents consent mechanics including e-consent and withdrawal, revocation consequences, compensation with its payment trigger, community advisory review, re-identification risk and a tiered access design. Held at 4 rather than 5 because the top band names data protection impacts, and no DPIA exists — the record states in free-text notes that 'no data protection impact analysis has been conducted', leaving the structured data_protection_impacts slot empty and the gap machine-invisible. governance_committee_contact is likewise unpopulated within regulatory_restrictions, though a contact does exist elsewhere (contact@aireadi.org, data_governance.committee_name). Ethics claims are mostly plausible and proportionate: Safe Harbor is appropriate for this data type, and the additional withholding of sex, race/ethnicity and medications into a controlled tier is a stronger-than-required protection with a stated rationale. Two semantic problems reduced the score alongside the DPIA gap. First, is_deidentified is self-contradictory, asserting simultaneously that no de-identification was necessary, that Safe Harbor stripping was performed, and reproducing the FAIRhub enum 'NoDeIdentification'. Second, confidential_elements_present and sensitive_elements_present are both false while the governance regime (restricted confidentiality, watermarking, re-identification prohibition, HIPAA-BAA storage requirement) is that of a sensitive release; the flags are defensible only if read as scoped to the public tier, which the record does not state. The at_risk_groups_included false / special_protections populated pairing is a third, minor incoherence.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission disease_specific_research, with license_terms describing the AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036 — licensor, grant of rights for research and commercial use, Authorized Group and Authorized User mechanics with automatic termination on severance, derivative and synthetic data treated as Data, model distribution permitted where models do not contain the Data, attribution requirement, as-is warranty disclaimer, one-dollar liability cap, indemnity, and termination with deletion on breach. ip_restrictions: four restrictions including title retention, reserved rights, separate publication licensing, and the RO-Crate copyright notice. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level restricted; hipaa_compliant compliant; three regulatory restrictions covering NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security standards, applicable-law compliance, and watermarking; other_compliance recording non-FDA-regulated status. data_governance: committee_name AI-READI Consortium, accountable_organization with ROR, access_review_process naming the tier explicitly (verified-ID login, self-attestation of T2DM research purpose, license acceptance; FAIRhub access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired; DUA for the controlled tier), four stewardship_roles. All three components of the top band are present and detailed. The access tier is stated in the precise terms the rubric asks for rather than described loosely as 'public': self-attestation for the open tier, data use agreement for the controlled tier. Licence obligations that actually bite on AI reuse — the prohibition on sharing Data with third-party model vendors for training, and the requirement to minimize memorization in distributed models — are documented rather than left to the licence text. Restrictiveness is coherent with the human-subjects context and the acknowledged re-identification risk, so the ethics-plausibility check passes on this question. Two caveats recorded rather than penalized here: confidentiality_level 'restricted' is the record's own mapping from the source value 'HL7:2N (normal)' and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' is its own inference, both disclosed in source_caveats — transparent, but these are the record's judgements, not source statements. The licence is referred to by three different names across fields, which is a matching hazard noted as a low-severity correctness issue. Governance accountability inherits the Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington ambiguity.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to_standard: CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH. conforms_to: prose specifying the Clinical Dataset Structure v0.1.1 directory hierarchy (datatype → modality → device → participant) and the per-datatype format standard, plus an RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT package conforming to FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1 with nine sub-crates. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Each of the ten file_collections repeats its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. related_datasets: three typed relationships (is_new_version_of ×2 with DOIs, is_source_of to the mini subset). external_resources: seven, including docs.aireadi.org, github.com/AI-READI, the Zenodo community and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048. Integration: participant folders named by study ID across every datatype, participants.tsv carrying split assignment, manifest.tsv per datatype, dqd_omop.json supporting the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard's 3,500+ checks. Top band met on every component. Standardization is not a single blanket claim but a per-modality mapping to the discipline-appropriate standard, versioned where the standard is versioned (CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRSCAPE 0.1). Integration capability is concretely evidenced by a shared participant identifier realized in the directory layout, which is exactly the cross-modality join key the rubric note asks about. Standards are correctly matched to data types — WFDB for ECG waveforms, OMOP CDM for observational clinical tables with one CSV per CDM table, DICOM for all retinal imaging, Open mHealth for wearable and CGM streams, ESDS for environmental ASCII. No standard is misapplied and terminology is used correctly throughout. Two minor limits, neither sufficient to reduce the band: file_collections.compression is unpopulated for a 3.82 TB release, and the RO-Crate provenance package is described as distributed outside the release rather than included within it, so a reuser obtaining only the release does not automatically receive the machine-readable provenance.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: five entries covering mapping to OMOP CDM and DICOM for AI-readiness; conversion of proprietary exports (.fda → DICOM for Topcon Maestro2 and Triton, .sdt → DICOM for Heidelberg FLIO, .FIT → Open mHealth for Garmin, ECG → WFDB); HIPAA Safe Harbor removal plus withholding of sex, race/ethnicity and medications; CDS v0.1.1 organization with manifest.tsv per datatype and nine named root metadata files, including dqd_omop.json supporting the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard's 3,500+ checks; and an explicit maturity statement that processing moved from 'custom and ad hoc handling for the v1.0.0 pilot data to a combination of automated and custom processing' for v2.0.0 and v3.0.0. cleaning_strategies: two entries describing REDCap min/max range flagging surfaced in coordinator and data-manager reports, credibility checks on range, skip-pattern flow, fillable missing data and duplicate records, editing only under site PI approval, and PI adjudication of uncorrectable values; plus per-site data-manager QC before FAIRhub upload and an internal review for accidental PII. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy. Named software: REDCap, OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, MoCA Duo. Unpopulated: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols. Well above the '3' band of 'at least one strategy or tool listed': both preprocessing and cleaning are documented as auditable workflows with named responsible roles and decision rules. The four unpopulated slots are substantively justified rather than simply missing — instances.label_description states that 'no specific labeling was performed, as the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic' and that 'no software was used to label instances', which correctly implies no annotation tools and no annotation quality analysis; and the handling_strategy states that values not fillable from elsewhere in a participant's record were left missing, i.e. no imputation was performed, so an imputation protocol would be vacuous. Held at 4 because the top band asks for software versions and URLs: the format-conversion pipelines that produced the release (what converted .fda and .sdt to DICOM, and .FIT to Open mHealth) are nowhere named or versioned, and the GitHub organization is referenced without pointing to the specific conversion code. Where versions exist they are given, but they are standards versions (CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRSCAPE 0.1) rather than software versions, and no version is given for REDCap or for the Data Quality Dashboard. Preprocessing is semantically coherent with the stated AI-readiness purpose: mapping to OMOP and DICOM is the right operation for the claim that the data can be used 'without reformatting and preprocessing'. The Safe Harbor preprocessing step is consistent with is_deidentified, though it sharpens that field's internal contradiction, since a documented removal step is hard to reconcile with 'no active de-identification was necessary'.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: two entries with structured flags — was_directly_observed and was_validated_verified true for labs, vitals and imaging, with verification by cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed; was_reported_by_subjects true for the survey battery (demographics, depressive symptoms, diabetes distress and self-care, diet, smoking, alcohol, vaping, marijuana, general health, social determinants, visual impairment and eye care access). collection_mechanisms: thirteen entries at device granularity, each with manufacturer, model, location and protocol — Philips PageWriter TC30 with recorded recline angle; LeeLab Anura environmental sensor with its 10-day placement protocol and full analyte list; Dexcom G6 with 5-minute sampling, 10-day wear and participant masking; Garmin Vivosmart 5 with 5-second sampling, wrist recording and the battery-charging gap; Optomed Aurora, iCare EIDON, Heidelberg Spectralis, Heidelberg FLIO, Topcon Maestro2, Topcon Triton and Zeiss Cirrus with per-device scan protocols and output formats; plus REDCap and a consolidated in-clinic instrument entry naming MoCA Duo, M&S EVA at 4 m, Mars contrast chart with luminance range and termination rule, Topcon KR-800, 10 g monofilament protocol, three named BP monitors and three lensometers. data_collectors: four roles — site coordinators and research assistants with a certification process requiring compliance training and three practice subjects, site data managers, the UW Nutrition and Obesity Research Center central laboratory, and CLIA-certified local laboratories. collection_timeframes: 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 with pilot and formal phases distinguished. raw_data_sources: two, with access_details for the EHR-derived controlled-tier content. Supporting: direct_collection, sampling_strategies with wave-based recruitment and ICD-10 screening codes, collection_notifications, collection_consents. Comfortably the top band and among the most detailed collection documentation the rubric can encounter. The protocol is reproducible at device level: a reader could reconstruct the visit. Collector documentation goes past naming roles to training and certification requirements, which speaks directly to data comparability across three sites. Internally consistent with downstream fields: the Garmin battery-charging gap in collection_mechanisms reappears as an anomaly and as a missing-data cause; device-level organization matches the file_collections device directories exactly (philips_tc30, leelab_anura, dexcom_g6, garmin_vivosmart5, heidelberg_spectralis, topcon_maestro2, topcon_triton, zeiss_cirrus, icare_eidon, optomed_aurora). One disclosed date conflict is recorded as a warning: the protocol publication gives enrollment start 2023-07-18 against the FAIRhub 2023-07-19, and the record adopts the tier-1 value with the discrepancy stated. A second disclosed conflict concerns CGM duration, where the IRB protocol permits up to 100 days of retrospective data while the documentation describes a 10-day period; the record carries both.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: 3.0.0. version_access: latest_version_doi doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; three versions listed with DOI, release date and participant count (1.0.0, 10.60775/fairhub.1, 2024-05-03, 204; 2.0.0, 10.60775/fairhub.2, 2024-11-08, 1,067; 3.0.0, 2025-11-17, 2,280); version_details recording per-version documentation sets with a version dropdown, the dropping of Snellen visual acuity variables, the increase in imaging devices and the addition of the recommended split; notes pointing to healthsheets for versions 1 and 2. updates: frequency 'Approximately once a year', with static versioned releases rather than in-place updates and changes detailed in CHANGELOG. distribution_dates: three release dates. maintainers: two — the AI-READI team as academic_institution with contact routes (README, aireadi.org/contact, docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact, contact@aireadi.org), and FAIRhub as the hosting platform that mints the DOIs. Sustainability: DOI per version; FAIRhub as a domain-appropriate biomedical repository on Microsoft Azure; data_governance with accountable_organization and four stewardship_roles; retention_limit stating no retention limit and that data will not be destroyed until after records-retention requirements; notes recording Microsoft AI for Good Lab cloud support. Unpopulated: errata. The 5-band's three sustainability components — governance, repository and institutional commitment — are all documented, and versioning is thorough. Held at 4 for two reasons. First, errata is empty across three releases despite a documented corrective change (the Snellen variables were dropped), so corrections are discoverable only from version_details prose. Second, and more substantively, sustainability is impaired in fact: version_details states that versions 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 'are no longer accessible through FAIRhub', meaning two minted DOIs no longer lead to retrievable data. Withdrawing prior versions undercuts the persistent-identifier guarantee that the record's own FAIR framing relies on, and no preservation or tombstoning arrangement is described. The withdrawal also contradicts the same field's versions_available list, which presents 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 as available — an internal inconsistency recorded as a failed consistency check rather than merely a warning. Update cadence is credible and corroborated: three releases across 2024-05, 2024-11 and 2025-11 match the stated annual-ish frequency, and participant counts increase monotonically (204 → 1,067 → 2,280) consistent with ongoing enrollment. Repository choice is appropriate: FAIRhub is purpose-built for this program rather than a generic file host, though that also concentrates preservation risk in a single project-affiliated platform.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3' — a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, author organization, version, publisher and resolved DOI. Distinct references in external_resources: the Nature Metabolism comment at https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x (AI-READI Consortium 2024, 6:2210-2212); the BMJ Open protocol at https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 (Owsley, Matthies, McGwin et al., 2025;15:e097449); ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT06002048; docs.aireadi.org; aireadi.org; github.com/AI-READI; the Zenodo community. license_and_use_terms additionally directs licensees to citation instructions at docs.aireadi.org, and the licence requires acknowledgment of licensor, source and funder in papers reporting use. Top band met on both limbs of the rule: at least two distinct references are documented — here two peer-reviewed publications with resolvable DOIs plus a trial registration and four further non-publication resources, all distinct rather than repeated links to one target — and a formal dataset citation is present that names the dataset by title and its author organization. Citation instructions are additionally documented, which the rubric treats as a strengthening factor. Both publication DOIs are structurally valid and attributable to real registrars (10.1038 Springer Nature; 10.1136 BMJ), and each is annotated with authors, venue, volume and article identifier rather than being a bare link, which makes them independently verifiable. The references are semantically apt: one is the study design and protocol paper, the other the program rationale comment, and the trial registration ties the dataset to its registered study. Each external resource carries a note explaining its relationship to the dataset, and licence terms for the documentation (CC-BY 4.0) and the protocol paper (CC BY-NC 4.0) are recorded.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 2,280, instance_type defined as an individual patient with all modalities for that person, plus missing_information. subpopulations: three, each with identification and numeric distribution — race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836), sex (male 951, female 1,329), and diabetes severity in four strata (no diabetes 776, lifestyle 560, oral 686, insulin 258), each annotated for whether it is released publicly. subsets: three splits with is_data_split true, each carrying per-split race/ethnicity, sex, diabetes-status counts and mean age with standard deviation (train 1,576, mean 61.1 ± 11.3; validation 352, 60.3 ± 10.8; test 352, 60.5 ± 11.4). Inclusion/exclusion: adults 40 to 85 able to read and speak English and provide consent; exclusions of pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes; at_risk_populations recording exclusion of minors, prisoners and adults unable to consent. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling strategy. known_biases and known_limitations characterize who is absent (Pacific Islanders, Native Americans; predominantly urban and hospital-based recruitment). Top band clearly met. Demographic characterization is quantitative at both cohort and split level, and inclusion/exclusion criteria are explicit. The record goes further than the band requires by documenting who is not represented and why, and by recording that the balanced recruitment target (approximately 1,000 per group) has not yet been reached in this interim release. Counts reconcile: the three subpopulation breakdowns each sum to 2,280, and the split sizes sum to 2,280, so the demographic reporting is arithmetically coherent with the stated instance count. A genuine tension is handled well rather than hidden: sex and race/ethnicity are withheld from the public release, so the aggregate distributions are published in the README while the per-participant variables sit behind a DUA, and subpopulation_elements_present is correctly set false for those two and true for diabetes status. This means a public-tier reuser can see cohort composition but cannot stratify by sex or race — a real analytical limitation that the record states plainly, including its consequence for verifying the balance of the recommended splits.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; access URL https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; seven external_resources including https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, two publication DOIs and the ClinicalTrials.gov registration; licence DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036. Passes on many independent grounds. Findability extends past the dataset landing page to versioned documentation, code, publications and trial registration, each with a stated relationship to the dataset. All URLs are structurally well formed with plausible domains, and the DOI prefixes map to real registrars. One qualification against the persistence premise, scored under Q13 rather than here: the version 1 and version 2 DOIs are documented as no longer resolving to accessible data, so findability of the current release is solid while findability of the historical record is not.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats: four media types with access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, plus a delivery entry stating that the dataset is distributed through FAIRhub, that a mini-subset version and Azure Storage access exist, and that 'All data files are in formats accessible with free software commonly used for such data types, so no specific software is required.' license_and_use_terms: full terms with data_use_permission disease_specific_research. data_governance.access_review_process: 'logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms', FAIRhub access type recorded as PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired, conditions published at the access URL, and the controlled tier 'accessible by entering into a data use agreement'. known_limitations records precisely which variables require the DUA (sex, race/ethnicity, medications, 5-digit zip, genetic sequencing, past health records, traffic and accident reports). Top band met. The rubric's note warns against conflating 'public' with unrestricted and asks for the access tier to be distinguished; this record does exactly that, naming a self-attestation tier for the open release and a DUA tier for the controlled variables, and enumerating which data sit behind each. Platform, login mechanism, policy, formats and software requirements are all specified, so a prospective user can determine in advance both how to obtain the data and what they will not receive without an agreement. Access claims are consistent with the licence and with the governance fields: disease_specific_research permission matches the self-attestation of T2DM-related purpose, and the two-tier design matches the withheld-variable list in is_deidentified.identifiers_removed and sensitive_elements. No dedicated download_url slot is populated, but the access_urls within distribution_formats and the access-conditions page serve that function, so the access path is not left to inference. Mention of a mini subset for pipeline development is a practical accessibility affordance for a 3.82 TB release, though it is noted as having no DOI of its own.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: full AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 terms with a resolvable licence DOI. intended_uses: three entries with use_category, usage_notes and examples — AI/ML research on T2DM (with salutogenesis and multimodal model development as examples), disease trajectory modeling via pseudotime manifold analysis, and model training using the recommended splits. prohibited_uses: eight entries, each with a prohibition_reason — no clinical treatment decisions; no re-identification, contact or group-membership inference; no sharing with third-party model vendors for training, with the permitted short-term prompting exception spelled out; no onward conveyance except to identically bound licensees; no reproduction beyond five illustrative figures per paper; no use of the public set outside T2DM research; no watermark removal; no storage outside institutional or HIPAA-BAA-covered systems. future_use_impacts: two entries — the AI-driven re-identification risk with its mitigation set (robust dissemination system, strict licence, watermarking, and a licensee obligation to minimize memorization and reconstruction in distributed models), and residual demographic imbalance in interim releases with guidance that balance targets apply to the completed cohort. known_limitations: five entries with scope_impact and recommended_mitigation. Unpopulated: discouraged_uses. Top band met on substance. Use guidance is unusually operational: the prohibitions address the specific reuse pathway that matters for this dataset — third-party model training, memorization and reconstruction — rather than reciting generic terms, and each carries a stated reason, which tells a reuser what the restriction is protecting and therefore how to comply in spirit. Social impact analysis identifies a concrete risk and pairs it with named mitigations at three levels (technical watermarking, contractual licence obligations, and tiered access). The discouraged_uses slot is empty, which is noted as a structural gap, but the use-guidance requirement is satisfied in substance by eight reasoned prohibitions plus five limitations with recommended mitigations; nothing a discouraged-use entry would carry is absent from the record. Use guidance is coherent with the consent basis: the restriction of the public tier to T2DM research traces back to consent_scope, so the licence limit is grounded in what participants agreed to rather than imposed arbitrarily. The social impact treatment is honest about its own limits, recording that beyond re-identification 'the creators do not currently anticipate uses of the dataset that could result in unfair treatment or harm' — a claim sitting in some tension with the documented under-representation of Pacific Islander and Native American populations, since deploying models trained on this cohort to those groups is a foreseeable equity risk that the impact analysis does not address.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: the AI-READI observational study. raw_data_sources: two typed sources — direct prospective collection from participants, and the three health systems' electronic health records with access_details for the controlled tier. raw_sources: raw device and system exports enumerated by format (.xml ECG, MoCA .csv, Topcon .fda, Heidelberg .sdt, Garmin .FIT, Dexcom and sensor .csv, laboratory .csv, REDCap exports) with a retention and non-sharing statement and the reasons (not mapped to standard terminologies; may contain PHI in free text). Derivation paths: preprocessing_strategies traces each raw format to its released standard (.fda → DICOM, .sdt → DICOM, .FIT → Open mHealth, .xml → WFDB, clinical → OMOP CDM). Agents: data_collectors (coordinators, site data managers, central laboratory, CLIA laboratories), cleaning_strategies (site PI approval for edits and removals), data_governance.stewardship_roles (data manager QC before upload; central team standardization). version_access with three DOIs; updates with CHANGELOG; related_datasets with typed is_new_version_of and is_source_of links. missing_data_documentation with patterns, causes and handling_strategy; anomalies with five entries. splits and three subsets with is_data_split true. conforms_to describes an RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT package under FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1 with nine sub-crates. Unpopulated: errata, parent_datasets. Top band met. The rubric explicitly accepts text-form provenance where it supplies complete lineage, and this record does: entities (raw device exports, processed collections), activities (standardization to OMOP and DICOM, per-format conversion, range-check cleaning, Safe Harbor removal, CDS organization) and agents (named collector roles, data managers, site PIs, central team) are all identified, and the derivation path from each raw format to each released format is traceable per modality. A machine-readable RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE package is additionally referenced. Quality documentation is substantive — range checks, skip-pattern validation, duplicate detection, PI adjudication, and an OMOP Data Quality Dashboard configuration running 3,500+ checks. Lineage is corroborated across fields rather than asserted once: device formats in collection_mechanisms match the raw formats in raw_sources, which match the conversion steps in preprocessing_strategies, which match the per-collection conforms_to_standard values in file_collections. Two gaps limit but do not lower the band: errata is empty despite the Snellen variable removal, and parent_datasets is unused, though related_datasets carries the version lineage with typed relationships. The RO-Crate is described as distributed outside the release, so the machine-readable provenance is referenced rather than shipped.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: four entries typed with BiasTypeEnum values — selection_bias (volunteer bias limiting generalizability), representation_bias (predominantly urban and hospital-based recruitment; Pacific Islanders and Native Americans absent) with a mitigation_strategy naming the three-site geographic selection, sampling_bias (interim releases not yet balanced across race/ethnicity, sex and severity) with both affected_subsets and a mitigation_strategy citing uniform protocols across sites, and a second selection_bias (English-language eligibility creating recruitment challenges for Hispanic and Asian participants). future_use_impacts: residual imbalance guidance for model developers.
