Fairness analysis: the recommended split is 'described as aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using this dataset', with validation and test sets balanced across sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status and the resulting counts published per split; known_limitations.representativeness_limitation carries a scope_impact naming the generalization boundary. Clearly above the '3' band of bias identification without taxonomy: four biases are categorized with schema enum values, two carry mitigation strategies, one carries affected subsets, and quantitative fairness analysis is present through the deliberately balanced validation and test splits with published subgroup counts. Held at 4 for a substantive omission rather than a formal one — measurement bias is not documented despite being strongly indicated by the dataset's own design. Retinal imaging was acquired across four OCT/OCTA vendor platforms and four fundus platforms, and the record itself notes that Optomed Aurora image quality 'varies from patient to patient and within the same patient'; systematic inter-device and inter-site differences are a primary confound for imaging models trained on this data, but they appear only under anomalies, not as a categorized bias with mitigation guidance. Taxonomy use is correct as far as it goes: the values used are valid BiasTypeEnum terms applied to the right phenomena, and the English-language eligibility entry shows genuine causal reasoning about how an inclusion criterion produces a demographic skew. No explicit AI Ontology (AIO) term mappings are present, so the CROISSANT RAI alignment is at the level of the schema enum rather than an external ontology — a minor formal shortfall noted alongside the substantive one. The bias documentation is also notably consistent with the record's own numbers: the sampling_bias claim that interim releases are unbalanced is verifiable against the published subpopulation counts, which show White 836 against Hispanic 380 versus a stated target of roughly 1,000 per group.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.60775/fairhub.3'; title 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~1,500 chars); keywords (7); license_and_use_terms (license_terms plus data_use_permission: disease_specific_research); doi '10.60775/fairhub.3'; page 'https://fairhub.io/datasets/3'; creators (AI-READI Consortium with principal_investigator ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648); purposes (3 responses); instances (individual study participant, counts 2280); variables (20 entries with measurement_technique); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent: resources; parent_datasets (version lineage is instead carried by related_datasets with relationship_type is_new_version_of). Twelve of the fourteen enumerated fields are populated with substantive, non-placeholder content. The two absent fields are the hierarchical-structure slots; the parent-dataset relationship is expressed elsewhere as a typed related_datasets link, so the information is not lost, but the enumerated slot is empty. 85.7% sits above the 70% band and below the 90% band, giving 4. Populated fields are semantically appropriate to their slots rather than filled for the sake of it: variables carry units and measurement_technique, instances carries a counted instance_type. The one field whose content is semantically questionable is regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level, which the record itself states contradicts the only sourced value; it is counted as populated but is flagged under correctness.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs roughly 1,500 characters and carries specific content: '2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus', three named sites, collection window '19 July 2023 and 1 May 2025', modality enumeration, '356,343 files totaling approximately 3.82 TB', CDS v0.1.1 organisation, and an explicit scope boundary ('banked biospecimens ... and the companion controlled-access release are not part of it'). purposes holds three responses of roughly 280, 250 and 300 characters each. Far above the >200 character threshold, and the length is carrying information rather than padding: the description alone supplies cohort size, sites, dates, modalities, file counts, volume, structure standard, label status and scope exclusions. The description's claims are checkable against the rest of the record and check out (2,280 matches instances.counts; 356,343 matches total_file_count; 3.82 TB matches total_size_bytes). Length here correlates with verifiable specificity rather than with narrative filler.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam' — seven unique terms, one short of the ≥8 band. Seven distinct keywords spanning condition, method and three modalities. The count falls in the 3–7 band. Major released modalities are unrepresented in the keyword list — OCT, OCTA, FLIO, wearable activity monitoring, environmental sensing and the OMOP-mapped clinical/laboratory data all go unkeyworded despite being among the largest collections in the release, so the shortfall is a real discoverability gap and not merely an arithmetic one. The rubric's supplementation provision (condition lists or external ontology references standing in for keywords) is written for datasets targeting many conditions; this dataset targets one, so the provision does not activate. instances.data_topic 'B2AI_TOPIC:43' is a single topic code and conforms_to_standard enumerates format standards rather than subject terms, so neither substitutes for subject keywords. Score held at the band value of 3.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists five: application/dicom, text/csv, application/json, text/markdown, text/tab-separated-values. total_file_count 356343. file_collections enumerates ten collections with per-collection file_count and total_bytes (e.g. retinal_octa file_count 173721, total_bytes 1155908809724; clinical_data file_count 7). Five distinct media types, each tied to the specific collections that use it in the notes field, plus a fully enumerated ten-collection inventory with counts and sizes. Well above the >3 threshold. Multimodality is genuine and integrated on a common key: the record states that files are grouped 'by a participant folder named after the participant's study ID number within each device directory', and variables declares participant_id with is_identifier true. The TSV entry is honestly marked as this record's own inference from file names rather than from the FAIRhub format field, which is the right handling of a derived value.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; total_file_count: 356343; per-collection total_bytes (e.g. 1069466876718 for retinal_flio, 4169006971 for wearable_blood_glucose); instances counts 2280; subsets with is_data_split true and counts 1576 / 352 / 352; subpopulations with distributions. Passes on every available signal simultaneously: dataset-level bytes, per-collection bytes, file counts, instance counts and split sizes. The numbers are not merely present but mutually reconcilable — collection bytes sum to within 419,614 bytes of total_size_bytes, and collection file counts sum to nine short of total_file_count, matching the nine root metadata files. Size metadata this internally consistent is unusual and is strong evidence the figures were taken from the artifact rather than estimated.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/. Prior versions carry their own DOIs (10.60775/fairhub.1, 10.60775/fairhub.2) recorded in version_access and related_datasets. Passes with both halves the question asks for: a persistent identifier and an identified hosting platform, with a version-level DOI rather than only a concept-level one. The DOI is well-formed and the prefix is used consistently across three versions, which is what a genuinely registered prefix looks like. No RRID is asserted, correctly — RRIDs identify resources such as software and antibodies, not dataset releases, so its absence is appropriate rather than a gap. The record notes the publisher slot holds the platform URL in place of the bare name the source gives, because the slot's range is uriorcurie; that substitution is disclosed.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health' with three grants — OT2OD032644 (noted as 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project', NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096 — plus grantor 'Research to Prevent Blindness'. creators: 'AI-READI Consortium' with principal_investigator Aaron Lee, ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, email contact@aireadi.org, affiliations 'Washington University in St. Louis' (ROR:01yc7t268) and 'Department of Ophthalmology, University of Washington'. participant_compensation additionally attributes the $200 stipend to award OT2OD032644, and data_collectors records that site staff effort 'was supported by NIH award OT2OD032644 in proportion to percentage effort'. Both halves of the top band are met: funders carry award numbers and creators carry identified, ROR-resolved affiliations. The record goes further than the band requires by tracing specific funded activities (staff effort, participant stipends) back to a named award. All three NIH numbers match NIH activity-code/institute/serial structure and the institute codes are plausible for the science (OD for a Common Fund Bridge2AI award, DK for a diabetes centre grant, TR for a CTSA). The purposes stated align with the cited Bridge2AI salutogenesis award, satisfying the funding-to-purpose consistency check. The consortium-as-creator carries no affiliation, but the record explains precisely why (the ROR-identified institutions appear in the sources as sponsors, collaborators and locations rather than as affiliations of the consortium), which is a reasoned abstention rather than a gap. The RO-Crate's '1OT2OD032644' form and two conflicting RePORTER links are disclosed and are cosmetic.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board', 'Protocol STUDY00016228, initially approved 20 December 2022', reliance agreements covering UAB and UCSD, contact hsdrely@uw.edu, plus a second entry naming Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans as responsible for ethical review. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval with renewal obligation, ethics_review_board with postal address, regulatory_compliance noting 'not FDA regulated', registration NCT06002048, special_populations (ages 40–85; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes excluded). is_deidentified: method, identifiers_removed, deidentification_details ('Date shifting, non-arrangement and k-anonymity were not applied'). participant_privacy: watermarking, license agreement, dissemination system, devices with 'no GPS location monitoring', 'procedures were conducted in private rooms'; reidentification_risk acknowledged; data_linkage described. participant_compensation: compensation_provided true, '$200', transport support, payment timing. at_risk_populations: at_risk_groups_included false with special_protections enumerating minors, prisoners, pregnancy and adults unable to consent. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, written/e-consent, consent form URL at docs.aireadi.org, consent_scope covering biospecimen banking and open-repository deposit. data_protection_impacts: explicit negative. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance: HIPAA-BAA storage limits. data_governance.committee_contact with ORCID and email. consent_revocations and collection_notifications also populated. This is the most complete ethics documentation the rubric contemplates: a numbered IRB protocol with an approval date and reliance structure, a published consent form URL, a named compensation amount with payment conditions, enumerated vulnerable-population exclusions, privacy techniques tied to specific device choices, an explicit re-identification risk statement, a registered trial number, and a consent-withdrawal policy that states what happens to already-shared data. Documented protections are not merely asserted; each is attached to an identifiable artifact a reader could check. Cross-field logic passes: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a stated method and by participant_privacy protections. Two semantic problems are noted without reducing the score. First, the de-identification method is under-determined across three conflicting sources (FAIRhub NoDeIdentification, RO-Crate deidentified true, Nature Metabolism HIPAA Safe Harbor) while the IRB protocol shows direct identifiers were collected and code-linked; this is a source conflict the record surfaces rather than conceals, and the released artifact is in either case documented as containing no HIPAA identifiers. Second, data_protection_impacts records that no DPIA was conducted — the rubric's band asks that data protection impacts be documented, and they are, as an explicit answered negative rather than an omission. The plausibility check on method-versus-data-type passes: for imaging and continuous physiological streams, withholding sex, race, ethnicity, medications and 5-digit ZIP to a controlled tier, combined with watermarking and a licence prohibition on re-identification attempts, is a coherent and proportionate protection design.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms sets out the AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 in operative detail: non-exclusive non-transferable grant, derivative data treated as data, models distributable only if they do not contain the data and memorisation risk is minimised, acknowledgement obligation, automatic termination on breach, liability capped at one US dollar. data_use_permission: disease_specific_research. ip_restrictions: title and IP remain with the Licensor, no additional third-party IP restrictions, RO-Crate copyright notice. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level 'restricted'; hipaa_compliant 'compliant'; NIH Genomic Data Sharing security best practices; other_compliance limiting storage to institutional servers or HIPAA-BAA-covered cloud, with static watermarking. data_governance: committee_name, accountable_organization (ROR:01yc7t268), committee_contact (ORCID and email), access_review_process naming https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and the access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired', stewardship_roles. Every component of the top band is present and specific. The access tier is named in the platform's own vocabulary rather than described loosely as 'public', which is exactly the distinction the rubric asks for: verified-ID login plus a use attestation plus licence acceptance, with no committee review. The record also notes that the controlled-access tier's requirements were still being developed by a Data Access Committee whose membership no source gives, rather than inventing one. The governance narrative is internally coherent in its restrictiveness: a licence forbidding re-identification and third-party model-vendor sharing, storage limited to BAA-covered infrastructure, and watermarking all point the same direction, and they align with the human-subjects and privacy declarations rather than contradicting them. Two issues are recorded and weighed. The confidentiality_level 'restricted' is the record's own substitution contradicting the sourced 'HL7:2N (normal)', and it sits beside confidential_elements_present false; this is a genuine cross-field inconsistency. It is not deducted here because the record states the substitution, its reason and its conflict with the source in regulatory_restrictions.notes, so a reader learns exactly what the source said and what was asserted instead — the disclosure preserves the field's usability, which is what the question measures. The licence-scope divergence (grant covering commercial use versus the disease-specific access attestation) is likewise disclosed.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to names eight standards with their roles: CDS v0.1.1 organisation, RO-Crate 1.2 packaging, DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, OMOP CDM for clinical data, WFDB for ECG, Open mHealth for wearables and CGM, NASA ASCII Earth Science guidelines for environmental sensing. conforms_to_standard enumerates CDS, RO_CRATE, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Each file_collection repeats its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. related_datasets carries four typed links (is_new_version_of ×2, is_source_of, is_supplemented_by). external_resources includes the CDS specification URL 'https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/'. Integration keys: variables declares participant_id with is_identifier true; file organisation is 'one directory per data type, then modality, then device, then participant'; clinical CSVs are 'a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP Common Data Model table'; participants.tsv carries the split assignment. Top band met on all three components. Standards are declared at both dataset and collection granularity, schema conformance is a resolvable w3id URI, and integration capability is concrete rather than aspirational: a participant identifier common across every modality directory, an OMOP mapping that makes the clinical tables harmonisable with other OMOP sources, and a documented directory contract in a versioned external specification. The standards are used where they belong, which distinguishes real interoperability from standards name-dropping: DICOM appears on exactly the four imaging collections, WFDB on the ECG collection only, Open mHealth on the two wearable streams, and the Earth Science format on the environmental sensor. The RO-Crate packaging plus a dqd_omop.json for the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard indicates machine-actionable rather than merely declared conformance. The is_source_of and is_supplemented_by targets (the mini-subset and the controlled-access release) lack DOIs; the record names them in prose and says explicitly that no identifier is given in the declared sources, which is the correct handling and does not undercut the typed-relationship evidence.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (3): mapping to OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB and Open mHealth; format conversion — 'Topcon Maestro2 and Triton exports (.fda) and Heidelberg FLIO exports (.sdt) were converted to DICOM, and Garmin exports (.FIT) were converted to the mHealth standard'; and a version-level note that v3.0.0 was produced by 'a combination of automated and custom processing', with a CHANGELOG-derived account of how processing evolved from 'custom, ad hoc processing' at v1.0.0. cleaning_strategies (2): REDCap range flagging with coordinator and data-manager review, checks for 'credibility against prespecified ranges, incorrect flow through prescribed skip patterns, missing data ... and the omission or duplication of records', editing only under site PI approval; plus site data-manager QC before upload and a central check that no PII was included. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('No imputation was applied'). instances.label_description: 'No labels or targets are provided. No specific labeling was performed'. Absent: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols as fields; no software name, version number or repository URL for any conversion or QC step. Strategy documentation is genuinely comprehensive in coverage — preprocessing, cleaning, missing data, and reasoned explicit negatives for labelling and imputation — and the cleaning account is specific enough to be auditable (who flags, who reviews, who authorises edits). What the top band additionally requires is missing: not one piece of data-preparation software is named. The .fda-to-DICOM, .sdt-to-DICOM and .FIT-to-mHealth conversions are the most consequential transformations in the release and are described without a tool, a version or a link, even though the project runs a public GitHub organisation that is cited generically in external_resources. A reuser cannot reproduce the conversions from this record. Hence 4, not 5. The instruments named throughout collection_mechanisms (Philips TC30, Dexcom G6, Garmin Vivosmart 5 and so on) are acquisition devices, not preparation software, so they do not satisfy the software-transparency requirement; counting them would misread the question. The explicit negatives are semantically correct rather than evasive: 'no imputation' is consistent with missing_data_documentation's handling strategy, and 'no labelling' is consistent with the hypothesis-agnostic design stated in purposes and known_limitations. REDCap and the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard (dqd_omop.json) are named as platforms, but without versions, and REDCap is a capture system rather than a preparation tool.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2) with typed flags: was_directly_observed true for laboratory, vital, vision, imaging, ECG, monofilament, CGM, wearable and environmental data; was_reported_by_subjects true with was_validated_verified true for survey data, including the verification method ('cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed'). collection_mechanisms (20) at protocol-parameter depth: 'Optomed Aurora IQ ... 50 degree field of view, 5 Mpix sensor; used undilated in a dark room'; 'Heidelberg Spectralis HRA+OCT ... optic nerve head radial circle high resolution, posterior pole macula 61-line high resolution, and 20x20 macular OCTA'; 'Topcon Maestro2 ... 12.0x9.0 mm widefield, 6.0x6.0 mm 3D macula and 6.0x6.0 mm OCTA at a 50 kHz scan rate'; 'Mars Letter Contrast Sensitivity ... background luminance of 60 to 120 cd/m2 and illuminance of 189 to 377 lux'; 'Dexcom G6 ... the transmitter records readings every five minutes'; 'Garmin Vivosmart 5 ... at a five-second sampling frequency'; site-varying blood pressure devices and lensometers enumerated by model. data_collectors (3): named site teams with role 'clinical research site', staff composition, and the note that 'The UAB data manager also trained research personnel at all three sites'. collection_timeframes: start_date 2023-07-19, end_date 2025-05-01, with timeframe_details and a caveat recording BMJ Open's conflicting 18 July 2023 start. direct_collection and raw_sources additionally describe EHR-based recruitment screening and raw-export retention. This is a full protocol at the level a reader would need to replicate acquisition: every instrument identified by manufacturer, model and city, with scan protocols, sampling rates, luminance conditions and ordering constraints (FLIO 'is performed last in the visit because it takes longer ... and exposes participants to uncomfortable light levels'). Collectors, sites, dates and the recruitment pathway are all specified. Comfortably the top band. The protocol detail is corroborated elsewhere in the record rather than free-floating: the ten-day wear period appears consistently in description, file_collections, collection_mechanisms and anomalies; the site-varying blood pressure and lensometer models named here are precisely what the measurement_bias entry identifies as confounded with site, so the collection account and the bias account are mutually consistent. raw_sources is recorded under that name rather than the schema's raw_data_sources slot, a naming divergence noted but with content fully present. Timeframe ordering is consistent with the 2022-12-20 IRB approval preceding the 2023-07-19 start.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.0.0'; issued '2025-11-17'. version_access.versions_available lists all three releases with their own DOIs and dates: '1.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.1, 3 May 2024), 2.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2, 8 November 2024) and 3.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3, 17 November 2025)', with latest_version_doi and the note that each version has its own documentation set selectable from a version dropdown, and that 2.0.0 'is marked ... as no longer accessible'. updates: frequency 'approximately annually', static-version release model, 'Changes between versions are recorded in detail in the CHANGELOG file'. maintainers: AI-READI Consortium, role academic_institution, with hosting details (FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure, 'developed for this project'), contact routes and README pointers. Sustainability: persistent DOI; domain-appropriate repository (FAIRhub, a biomedical data-sharing platform); governance via data_governance (accountable_organization, committee_contact, stewardship_roles, access_review_process); commitment via retention_limit ('There are no limits on the retention of the data') and ongoing enrolment implying further versions. related_datasets records the v1 and v2 lineage with participant counts (204; 1,067). All four sustainability indicators the question names are evidenced — persistent identifiers, a governance plan with a named accountable organisation and contact, a domain-appropriate repository built for this project, and a retention and maintenance commitment — alongside comprehensive versioning with per-version DOIs, dates, counts and a changelog. The one enumerated field genuinely absent is errata, for which the CHANGELOG is referenced but not enumerated; against a slot list of seven this does not pull the assessment below the top band. Two facts the record reports are adverse to sustainability and are flagged as issues rather than scored as documentation failures, because the question measures whether the maintenance picture is documented and here it is documented including its negatives: version 2.0.0 holds a registered DOI yet is recorded as no longer accessible, which is in tension with DOI persistence expectations, and the notes field reproduces the FAIRhub and documentation-site notice that 'This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'. A record that hid either of these would look more sustainable and be less trustworthy. Version numbering is semantically coherent: major-version increments accompany substantive content changes (the v3.0.0 drop of Snellen acuity variables is recorded under known_limitations as an integration_limitation).

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3' — a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, version, publishing organisation and DOI. external_resources holds seven distinct entries, including two DOI-linked publications: 'AI-READI Consortium (2024). "AI-READI: rethinking AI data collection, preparation and sharing in diabetes research and beyond." Nature Metabolism 6:2210-2212, https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x' and 'Owsley C, Matthies DS, McGwin G, et al. "Cross-sectional design and protocol for Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI)." BMJ Open 2025;15:e097449, https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449'; plus the documentation site, the project website, the GitHub organisation, the Zenodo community and the CDS specification. The licence separately imposes an acknowledgement obligation on publications reporting use of the data. Both conditions for the top band are met with margin: a formal dataset citation naming title, authors/organisation, version and DOI, and well beyond two distinct references, two of which are peer-reviewed publications with resolvable DOIs. Scored at 5 per the exact-value rule for this question. The two publication DOIs have well-formed, registrar-plausible prefixes (10.1038 Nature Portfolio; 10.1136 BMJ) and the cited venues, volumes and article identifiers are internally consistent with those publishers. The seven external resources are genuinely distinct targets rather than repeated links to one resource. The record notes that the BMJ Open title expands the acronym differently from the FAIRhub metadata and records both readings in source_caveats instead of silently harmonising them.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: instance_type 'individual study participant', counts 2280, with missing_information recording which modalities are absent and why. subpopulations (4): race/ethnicity '380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White'; sex '951 male, 1,329 female'; diabetes status '776 with no diabetes, 560 pre-diabetes or lifestyle-controlled, 686 controlled by oral or non-insulin injectable medication, 258 insulin-controlled'; age 'Mean age ... 60.8 years (standard deviation 11.3)' with eligibility 40–85. subsets: three is_data_split subsets each with its own full demographic composition (e.g. validation '88 each of Hispanic, Asian, Black and White; 176 male and 176 female'). Inclusion/exclusion: adults 40+, able to read and speak English; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes excluded; at_risk_populations.special_protections on minors, prisoners and adults unable to consent. missing_data_documentation populated. known_limitations records that the cohort 'does not include Pacific Islanders or Native Americans' and that recruitment was 'predominantly urban and hospital-based'. Demographics are given as exact counts across four independent stratifications, repeated per split, with eligibility criteria, exclusion criteria and an honest statement of who is not represented. This is the top band by a clear margin. Every demographic figure reconciles arithmetically, both within stratification (each of the four sums to 2,280) and across splits (per-group split counts sum to the cohort counts; for example insulin-controlled 105 + 67 + 86 = 258). The record also carries a genuine representational tension without hiding it: subpopulation_elements_present is false for race and sex because those values are withheld from the public release and held under controlled access, so the published aggregates are README summary tables rather than per-instance labels — the notes field says exactly that, and known_limitations states the consequence, that users 'cannot stratify analyses by sex or race/ethnicity, and cannot audit models for disparities across those groups directly'. Documenting the demographics fully while flagging that they are not individually usable is the most informative available handling.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi 10.60775/fairhub.3; id doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher https://fairhub.io/; access route https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; documentation https://docs.aireadi.org; project site https://aireadi.org; code https://github.com/AI-READI; https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi; consent form PDF at docs.aireadi.org; CDS specification at cds-specification.readthedocs.io; publication DOIs 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449. Passes on every axis: a version-level DOI, a landing page, a documentation site, a code repository and DOI-linked publications. All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains, and the documentation URLs are version-scoped (the record directs readers to 'Dataset v3.0.0' on docs.aireadi.org), which is what makes findability durable across releases. One adverse signal is recorded rather than scored here: version 2.0.0's DOI is reported as no longer resolving to accessible content, which bears on the persistence of the identifier series even though this version's identifiers are intact.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access to the release requires logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and accepting the license terms ... The access route is published at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access. Access is granted by self-attestation rather than committee review: the FAIRhub access type for this release is PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired.' distribution_formats enumerates the five obtainable media types with what each contains. license_and_use_terms sets out the obligations a requester accepts. third_party_sharing.is_shared true, with onward-sharing limits. related_datasets records a mini-subset 'made available for pipeline development', and version_access notes Azure Storage access is covered in the v3.0.0 documentation. Note: no download_url field is populated; the access URL appears within data_governance. Every element of the top band is specified: the platform (FAIRhub), the authentication step (verified ID login), the policy step (use attestation plus licence acceptance), the named access tier, the URL where the route begins, and the formats obtained. The record explicitly distinguishes self-attestation from committee review, which is the access-tier distinction the rubric warns against blurring, and it does not misdescribe a gated release as 'public' in the unrestricted sense. Scored from content rather than slot occupancy, per the instrument: the absent download_url is a serialisation gap, not an information gap, since the access URL, tier and procedure are all stated. Accessibility is consistent with the governance and licence declarations — a self-attestation gate matches a release from which sex, race, ethnicity, medications and ZIP have been withheld to a separate controlled tier, and the pipeline-development mini-subset is a coherent low-friction on-ramp. The one caveat is that the mini-subset has no identifier in the declared sources, which the record states rather than inventing one.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms in operative detail (grant scope, derivative-data treatment, model-distribution conditions, acknowledgement, termination, warranty disclaimer). intended_uses (2) with use_category, examples and usage_notes, including that data are 'AI-ready' so research 'can begin without further reformatting'. prohibited_uses (7), each with notes and a prohibition_reason: no clinical treatment decisions; no re-identification or group-membership inference; no sharing with third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, though 'Short-term interaction such as prompting or querying ... is permitted for analysis'; no onward conveyance outside identically bound licensees; publication limited to 'small representative samples in up to five images or figures per paper'; storage limited to institutional or BAA-covered infrastructure; no removal of watermarking. future_use_impacts (2): no currently anticipated unfair-treatment harms plus an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk; and the fairness impact that 'users of that release cannot directly stratify or audit model performance across those groups', mitigated by a recommended split 'balanced as well as possible for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status, with the stated aim of reducing disparities in models developed from the dataset'. discouraged_uses is not populated. Use guidance is exceptionally operational: each prohibition states what is forbidden and why, and the boundaries are drawn at a level of specificity a compliance officer could apply (the vendor-sharing prohibition distinguishes training from prompting; the publication limit gives a number). The social impact analysis is not generic — it names a concrete harm created by the project's own design choice and pairs it with a concrete mitigation. discouraged_uses is empty, but the seven-entry prohibited_uses list covers the territory that field would occupy, so the top band is met. The use guidance is consistent with the ethics and governance declarations: the re-identification prohibition tracks participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, and the storage limits track regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance. One divergence is recorded as an issue rather than a deduction: the licence grant covers commercial use while data_use_permission is disease_specific_research, a difference the record attributes to the access attestation and discloses. The future_use_impacts entries are also unusual in candour — the second effectively concedes that a transparency measure taken for privacy reasons degrades fairness auditability, which is the kind of trade-off datasheets usually omit.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Present: version_access (three versions with DOIs and dates, latest_version_doi, version_details); updates (static-version model, CHANGELOG, approximately annual); missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling_strategy); subsets with is_data_split true ×3 and splits.split_details describing the 70/15/15 assignment in participants.tsv; raw_sources describing retained device and REDCap exports and why they are not shared. Lineage in text: preprocessing_strategies traces device-native exports (.fda, .sdt, .FIT, XML, CSV) through conversion to DICOM and mHealth and mapping to OMOP, DICOM, WFDB and Open mHealth; cleaning_strategies names the agents at each stage ('The data manager at each collection site was responsible for the quality control of all data before upload to FAIRhub. After transfer to the central project team, the dataset was additionally reviewed internally'); related_datasets gives the derivation chain v1.0.0 → v2.0.0 → v3.0.0 via is_new_version_of and is_source_of for the mini-subset; anomalies documents modality-specific quality failure modes; known_limitations records the v3.0.0 removal of Snellen acuity variables. Absent: errata; was_derived_from; parent_datasets; no PROV-O or other graph serialisation. This is clearly more than the version history that defines the 3 band: there is an end-to-end textual account of how raw device output became released files, who performed each transformation, and how releases derive from one another, plus quality documentation at modality level. It falls short of the 5 band because the lineage is narrated at the level of strategies rather than resolved into entity–activity–agent relationships over identified artifacts: no was_derived_from links a released collection to the raw export it came from, no activity is identified as an addressable node, and the derivation path exists only as a relationship type between version DOIs. Errata is also absent. The instrument accepts text in place of a PROV-O serialisation where the text provides complete lineage, so the question is whether the lineage is complete, not whether it is RDF. It is not quite complete: a reader can say that .sdt files became DICOM and that site data managers ran QC, but cannot determine which activity produced a given released collection, in what order the mapping and conversion steps ran, or which agent performed the central standardisation. The RO-Crate packaging noted in conforms_to would be a natural carrier for exactly this graph, which makes its absence from the record conspicuous rather than unavoidable. Integrity-side evidence is strong and independently checkable — the file-count and byte-total reconciliations and the split arithmetic all hold — which is why this sits at 4 rather than 3.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases (4), each typed with a BiasTypeEnum value: selection_bias ('Participants are volunteers, so the cohort is subject to volunteer bias ... The protocol publication states this as a limitation and describes no measure taken against it'); representation_bias ('recruitment was predominantly urban and hospital-based ... does not include other races/ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans. Eligibility required the ability to read and speak English'), mitigated by three-site geographic selection; sampling_bias, with affected_subsets naming 'Version 3.0.0 as a whole; the recommended validation and test partitions are balanced ... while the training partition is not', mitigated by uniform protocols across sites; measurement_bias ('blood pressure monitors and lensometers differ by site, and retinal imaging is acquired on multiple manufacturers' instruments — so device make and model may be confounded with site'), mitigated by documenting device make, model and scan modality. Fairness analysis in future_use_impacts: the inability to stratify by sex or race in the public release, mitigated by demographically balanced validation and test splits aimed at 'reducing disparities in models developed from the dataset'. known_limitations adds representativeness, coverage, temporal, scope, methodological and integration limitations. Top band met: four biases categorised with schema-standard type values, each with a substantive description, three with mitigation strategies and one with affected subsets identified, plus a fairness analysis that connects a documented bias to a concrete design mitigation. The categorisation is systematic rather than a single undifferentiated 'limitations' paragraph. The bias types are applied correctly, which is the semantic test that matters here: measurement_bias is used for a device-versus-site confound rather than for a sampling problem, and representation_bias and sampling_bias are distinguished sensibly (who is absent from the cohort versus how the realised distribution departs from the balanced target). The selection_bias entry carries no mitigation and says so explicitly, which is more credible than a fabricated one. No AIO ontology URIs are attached, but the rubric names BiasTypeEnum as an acceptable standard taxonomy and the enum values are used throughout. The bias claims corroborate the numbers elsewhere: the assertion that training is unbalanced while validation and test are balanced is verifiable from the split composition figures.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10/14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset'; title 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description (~1,700 chars); keywords (13); license_and_use_terms.license_terms 'Every data modality is released under controlled access rather than an open license'; page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (6 PIs with affiliations); purposes (4 responses); instances (6 instance_type entries); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (4/14): doi (top-level source_caveats: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation'), resources, parent_datasets, variables. Ten of fourteen mandatory fields populated (71%), landing squarely on the 3 band. The populated fields are not perfunctory — description, purposes, and instances all carry substantive content — but four structural fields are empty, and the two most consequential absences (doi and variables) are the ones a reuser needs to cite the dataset and to know what the 1.6 billion OMOP rows actually contain. No variable-level metadata exists for any of the nine modalities. The id value is syntactically a URI but semantically not an identifier of the kind this field expects: a fragment on the project homepage resolves to marketing content, not to a dataset landing record, and it will not survive the site reorganization the record's own notes field warns is under way ('This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'). Counting it as populated is correct by the letter of the field but the persistence it implies is not real, which is scored against the record at Q6 and Q13 rather than double-counted here.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 1,700 characters across a single block covering consortium structure, all five format families, four quantitative scale figures, enclave topology, and modality readiness. purposes contains four responses of roughly 190, 200, 145, and 175 characters, averaging about 178; combined narrative across both fields far exceeds 200 characters. Comfortably above the >200 character threshold on the combined narrative measure. Length here is not padding: the description carries distinct facts per clause (14 of 20 centers contributing, OMOP for structured EHR, OHNLP tokenization, DICOM from PACS, WFDB telemetry, EDF+/Persyst EEG, SDOH and distance-to-hospital) rather than restating the title. Semantic density is high and the description is appropriate to the claimed dataset type — every named standard reappears in distribution_formats and raw_data_sources, so the narrative is corroborated rather than decorative. One purposes response ('Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset') sits in tension with the controlled-access posture asserted everywhere else; read as the project's stated aspiration rather than a description of current terms it is defensible, but a reader skimming purposes alone could be misled about access.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 13 unique keywords: critical care, acute illness, critical illness, electronic health record, OMOP Common Data Model, waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, imaging, clinical notes, social determinants of health, multimodality, AI-ready data set, Bridge2AI. Thirteen unique terms, well clear of the ≥8 threshold. Coverage spans clinical domain, modality, standard, and program affiliation, so the set supports several distinct discovery paths rather than repeating one axis. The keywords are semantically faithful to the content: each modality keyword (waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, imaging, clinical notes) has a matching distribution_format and raw_data_source, and 'OMOP Common Data Model' matches conforms_to_standard. Program context is inferable from the quoted keyword 'Bridge2AI' and from funders.grantor 'National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund', not from the filename. Three near-synonyms (critical care, acute illness, critical illness) inflate the count slightly, and no controlled-vocabulary identifiers (MeSH, SNOMED CT) are attached to any term, so the set is discoverable by string match but not by ontology traversal.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists five entries, each with a scoping note: 'OMOP Common Data Model tables' (demographics, medications, procedures, flowsheets, diagnoses; flowsheets use OMOP schema with extensions), 'OHNLP open source schema' (tokenized notes), 'DICOM' (imaging from PACS), 'WFDB' (telemetry, 'a PhysioNet schema extended'), 'EDF+ and Persyst' (EEG). file_collections absent; total_file_count absent; no media types, encodings, or compression recorded. Format variety is the strongest part of this question and alone would earn the top band: five distinct format families, each bound to the modalities it carries, which is more informative than a bare format list. The enumeration half of the question is unmet — two of the three named fields are empty and there is no file count anywhere, so a reuser can tell what kinds of files exist but not how many or how they are packaged. Scored 4 rather than 5 for that missing half. The variety is genuine multimodality rather than format proliferation over one data type: each format maps to a different physical acquisition path in raw_data_sources (EHR, PACS, bedside monitors, EEG databases), corroborating the 'multimodality' keyword. One entry bundles two standards ('EDF+ and Persyst') into a single value, so the true count of distinct formats is six rather than five while the list length says five. Note that 23 Tb of waveform volume is recorded, but as free text in instances.notes rather than as a byte count in this question's fields, so it does not repair the enumeration gap here.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances carries three numeric counts: 50000 patient admissions (ICU/PICU/NICU), 1600000000 rows of OMOP EHR data, 7642 admissions with radiology data. instances.notes additionally reports '23 Tb of waveform data'. splits documents a sequestered holdout test set; subpopulations has two entries. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent. Passes on numeric instance counts, with three counts present rather than one and a volume figure for the largest modality. The pass is on counts, not bytes: no machine-readable size field exists, and two modalities (EEG, tokenized notes) carry no count at all, so a reuser cannot size the full extract from this record. The counts are plausible and mutually coherent — 1.6 billion OMOP rows across 50,000 critical care admissions is roughly 32,000 rows per admission, which is consistent with high-frequency nursing flowsheet and medication administration data being included. The 7,642 radiology admissions against 50,000 total (15%) is consistent with the coverage_limitation entry describing imaging as still developing. The disclosed tier-2/tier-4 conflict (50,000 versus 'over 45K') does not void the pass, since both values are numeric and of the same order, but it means the counts are a snapshot of contested vintage; the record attaches that caveat to the affected instance rather than concealing it.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset'; page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; external_resources includes 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824' and 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'. doi absent; no rrid; publisher absent. Top-level source_caveats: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset'. Passes on the letter of the criterion — a resolvable landing page link is present, and the NIH RePORTER record provides a stable third-party anchor for the award. This is the weakest possible pass: no DOI, no RRID, no ARK or Handle, and no publisher or repository naming a body that guarantees resolution. Correctness check on identifier persistence fails even though the URL is well formed. A fragment URI on a project website is not a persistent identifier: it depends on the site's information architecture, and the record's own notes field quotes a site-wide banner saying the repository 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' — an explicitly signalled risk to that very URL's stability. No registrar prefix can be checked because no DOI exists, so doi_format is recorded as not_present rather than invalid. The absence of publisher compounds this: for a dataset held in a cloud enclave rather than a named repository, there is no institution identified as the resolution authority.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund' with grants[0].name 'OT2OD032701' and grants[0].id 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'; notes give 'Project number 1OT2OD032701-01, core project number OT2OD032701, application ID 10472824, awarded to Massachusetts General Hospital, fiscal year 2022, award amount USD 5,880,300, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30'. creators: six principal investigators each with an affiliation — Eric S. Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac, Yulia Strekalova, Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University). notes reproduces the published funding statement crediting award OT2OD032701. Top band met on both limbs and then some. Every creator carries an institutional affiliation, and the funding entry goes well beyond an agency name to give the full award identifier set, awardee institution, dollar amount, and project period — the level of detail that makes an acknowledgement independently verifiable. Grant number format validates against the NIH pattern: OT2 is the Other Transaction activity code used for Common Fund Bridge2AI data generation awards, OD is the Office of the Director, and the serial 032701 with the fully qualified form 1OT2OD032701-01 (application type 1, support year 01) is internally consistent. The RePORTER link and the application ID 10472824 agree with each other and with the creators entry naming Rosenthal as PI at the awardee institution MGH, so three independent statements corroborate. Funding purpose aligns with purposes: a Common Fund data generation award and a stated goal of producing an AI-ready dataset are congruent. The one honest gap the record flags itself — no CRediT-style contribution roles for the five non-lead PIs — affects attribution granularity, not funding completeness, and does not move the score.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true with special_populations 'acutely and critically ill hospital patients, and the released admissions include pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) patients'; is_deidentified.method (OHNLP tokenization, local note retention, imaging deidentification in process, 'transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification'); participant_privacy.privacy_techniques (tokenization, local retention, privacy_scan_tool repository, CTP-deid repository) and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk; two ethical_reviews entries describing community ethics focus groups and legal-landscape analysis; sensitive_elements and confidential_elements both flagged true with details; data_governance.committee_contact 'Jared Houghtaling'. Absent: informed_consent; participant_compensation; at_risk_populations; data_protection_impacts; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance. The record concedes 'The bundle names no IRB, ethics review board, or approval number.' Deidentification and privacy are documented with real specificity — named tooling, per-modality handling, and an architectural protection (notes never leave the contributing site) that is stronger than most datasheets offer. Against that, the three pillars that define human-subjects ethics documentation are all missing: no IRB or approval identifier, no consent basis or waiver, and no HIPAA determination for what is unambiguously PHI from US hospitals. The record scores 3 because it has the deidentification half of the basic band comprehensively and the IRB half not at all; it cannot reach 4 while a 14-site PHI extract has no named review authority. Cross-field logic fails three times. involves_human_subjects=true should imply populated ethical_reviews with an approving body: the two entries name 'CHoRUS consortium' as reviewing_organization, but their review_details describe community focus groups and legal analysis — ethics activity by the consortium about the project, not review of the dataset by an independent body, and the record's source_caveats says so plainly. involves_human_subjects=true should imply a documented consent basis: informed_consent is absent entirely, and while a waiver is the expected instrument for retrospective EHR extraction, no waiver is claimed. is_deidentified present should imply a named method and a DPIA: the method is named but no recognized standard (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination) is cited and data_protection_impacts is empty. Plausibility check on restrictiveness passes in the other direction — the controlled-access posture, restricted confidentiality level, and refusal to centralize raw notes are all proportionate to critical-care PHI including neonatal patients, so the protections claimed are appropriate to the risk even though their authorization is undocumented. Vulnerable populations are disclosed under human_subject_research.special_populations but the dedicated at_risk_populations field is empty, so PICU/NICU safeguards are named nowhere. The record's transparency about these absences is commendable provenance practice but does not substitute for the protections themselves, and the score reflects what is documented rather than how candidly the gaps are labelled.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Every data modality is released under controlled access rather than an open license. Users must sign a licensing agreement before gaining access to the dataset, and access through the AIM-AHEAD training program additionally requires a ".edu" email address'; notes distinguish repository MIT/Apache-2.0 licenses from dataset terms. regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' with two regulatory_restrictions statements. data_governance: accountable_organization 'Massachusetts General Hospital', committee_contact 'Jared Houghtaling', access_review_process describing two routes with contacts dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org, plus three stewardship_roles. Absent: ip_restrictions, hipaa_compliant, other_compliance, data_protection_impacts. Strong on the access-policy limb: the two access routes are described concretely enough to act on, with named contacts, the registration mechanics of the training route, and the .edu requirement including the note that administrators will assist so it is not a barrier to admission. Confidentiality is classified and an accountable organization is named. Held to 4 by the absence of any regulatory compliance declaration — no HIPAA status, no other framework, no IP terms — which for a multi-state hospital PHI dataset is the one thing an institutional reviewer would check first. Internal consistency is good: controlled access in license_and_use_terms, confidentiality_level 'restricted', confidential_elements covering all nine modalities, and third_party_sharing conditioned on a signed agreement all agree, and nothing in the record describes the data as open. The record also avoids the misleading 'public' framing the rubric warns about, except in one purposes response where 'publicly available' appears as a project aspiration. Governance completeness is honestly bounded by the record's own source_caveats: no access committee, no membership, no decision timeframe, no appeal process, and the committee_contact is recorded as a contact address rather than a verified committee role. That candour is why the governance limb reads as thin-but-accurate rather than overstated. The absent hipaa_compliant field is a genuine consistency failure against sensitive_elements, and is recorded once as an issue at Q8 and reflected here in the withheld fifth point rather than penalized twice at full weight.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: OMOP CDM tables, OHNLP open source schema, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst. conforms_to narrative maps each modality to its standard. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Harmonization procedure documented in cleaning_strategies ('Semantic mappings from source formats to international standards are validated; clinical collaborators contribute to pooled tabular mappings in the chorus-mapping repository under an associated clinical validation standard operating procedure') and preprocessing_strategies (OMOP standardization with flowsheet extensions; DeGauss geocoding of OMOP Location entities). external_resources present. related_datasets absent; file_collections.compression absent. Standards adoption is the record's strongest technical feature: every modality lands on a recognized community standard, the metadata record itself declares LinkML schema conformance, and a validated semantic mapping process with a clinical validation SOP is documented — that is harmonization procedure, not just format naming. Two things hold it to 4. No common identifier for linking a patient's OMOP rows to their waveforms, images, and note tokens is named anywhere, which is precisely the integration capability the question asks about for a multimodal dataset. And related_datasets is empty, so no typed relationship to any other Bridge2AI or external dataset is expressed. Technical terms are used correctly throughout — OMOP CDM for structured EHR with acknowledged extensions for nursing flowsheets, DICOM for PACS imaging, WFDB for physiologic waveforms, EDF+ for EEG — and each appears in the same role in conforms_to, distribution_formats, and raw_data_sources, so usage is consistent across three fields. The machine-readable conforms_to_standard list is where semantics degrade: one OTHER token stands for three distinct standards (EDF+, Persyst, OHNLP schema) that the registered enum does not cover, and the WFDB token names plain WFDB for what the prose calls 'a PhysioNet schema extended'. A consumer reading only the enum therefore underestimates the standards in play and would not know an extension profile is required to parse the telemetry; the record flags both collapses itself. The integration_limitation in known_limitations (notes not centralized, only tokens in the enclave) is an honest and material constraint on cross-modality analysis and is consistent with the architecture described elsewhere.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (5): OMOP standardization with flowsheet schema extensions; OHNLP toolkit tokenization into the OHNLP open source schema; transformation limiting re-identification; waveform conversion via 'the waveform conversion scripts and documentation in the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories'; 'OMOP Location entities are geocoded via DeGauss using the open source UF-Geocoding code, a fork of bihorac-LAB/Exposome'. cleaning_strategies (2): characterization reports returned to sites via the CHoRUSReports repository; validated semantic mappings via chorus-mapping under a clinical validation SOP. labeling_strategies (1): 'A visualization and annotation environment is developed to label data with targets important for prediction'. Also referenced: chorus-extract-upload, privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid, Chorus_SOP, chorus-developer package status page. Absent: machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation. All three core strategy types are populated, and the tooling is named at repository granularity rather than described generically — eleven distinct named components, with one (UF-Geocoding) traced to its upstream fork. That is well past the 3 band. Two things block 5: no version numbers or release tags for any tool, and no direct repository URLs (only the organization URL), so a reuser cannot reproduce a pipeline state; and the annotation-quality and imputation limbs of the question are entirely empty — the annotation environment is described as a capability with no inter-annotator agreement, no label schema, and no quality metrics. Tool-to-task mapping is semantically correct in every case: OHNLP is a clinical NLP toolkit and is used for note tokenization; DeGauss is a geomarker container and is used on OMOP Location entities to derive SDOH context, which matches the distance-to-hospital variable described in the dataset narrative; WFDB conversion scripts sit in a waveform repository. Nothing is misattributed. The record notes that the chorus-developer package status page tracks 'versions, maintainers, and other metadata' for CHoRUS software — versioning exists upstream but is not pulled into this datasheet, so the transparency gap is one of transcription rather than of practice. The absence of missing_data_documentation is a substantive semantic gap for a high-frequency flowsheet and telemetry dataset, where missingness is informative and its handling materially affects downstream models.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (5 entries, each was_directly_observed true) covering structured EHR extraction ('medication administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation'), WFDB telemetry, DICOM from PACS, EEG in EDF+/Persyst, and OHNLP-tokenized notes. collection_mechanisms (5): bedside monitors plus gateway/middleware, PACS, hospital EEG databases, OHNLP toolkit, 'chorus-extract-upload Python tool'. data_collectors (2): 'Fourteen of the twenty academic centers ... contribute as Data Acquisition centers'; site managers following 'step-by-step standard operating procedures published in the Chorus_SOP repository, which have undergone an internal validation and review process'. raw_data_sources (6) with source_type and raw_data_format each. direct_collection.is_direct false with rationale. collection_timeframes (1): the NIH award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. Methods, mechanisms, collectors, and sources are documented at a level that would let another consortium replicate the extraction architecture — per-modality acquisition paths, a named site-side extraction tool, and governed SOPs with a validation history. The timeframe limb fails on substance: the interval given is the funding period, not the clinical period the admissions span, and the record states outright that 'the bundle does not state the temporal coverage of the clinical data'. Also absent are patient-level inclusion and exclusion criteria — how an admission qualified for the extract is nowhere stated. Four of the top band's requirements are met and the timeframe one is met only nominally, so 4. Temporal consistency check fails. A retrospective extraction whose stated collection timeframe begins at the award start date is logically incoherent: the admissions almost certainly predate 2022-09-01, so the interval describes when the extracting happened, not what period the data cover. The record identifies this itself in collection_timeframes.source_caveats, which is the right disclosure but leaves a reuser unable to assess whether the cohort spans, for instance, the COVID-19 period — a first-order confounder for any critical-care model. Everything else is internally coherent: the five acquisition_methods correspond one-to-one with the five distribution_formats and with entries in raw_data_sources, direct_collection.is_direct=false is consistent with retrospective EHR extraction and with the absence of prospective consent, and the 14-of-20-centers figure is repeated consistently in description, data_collectors, and known_limitations.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.update_details ('The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG waveforms were in process, and published metadata schemas were planned but not yet available for clinical notes, imaging, and EEG'); maintainers (3 entries: CHoRUS consortium coordinated from MGH with program manager contact, access-request contacts, and the chorus-developer package status page); status 'partially released'; data_governance.accountable_organization 'Massachusetts General Hospital'; funders.notes gives a project period ending 2026-11-30. Absent: version, version_access, errata, doi, publisher. Above the 0 band because a forward-looking update plan with dated modality-readiness detail and a named accountable institution with maintainer contacts do constitute more than a static single release. Well short of the 3 band, which requires a version number, basic version access information, and a persistent identifier — none of the three exists. There is no versioning scheme, no release date, no errata channel, no way to request a prior state, and no repository that would outlive the consortium. Sustainability fails on three of the four indicators the question names. Persistent identifier: absent (no DOI, ARK, or Handle; the id is a website fragment URI). Domain-appropriate repository: absent — the data sit in a project cloud enclave, and although WFDB is described as a PhysioNet schema, no PhysioNet or equivalent deposit is claimed, so no independent preservation body is identified. Institutional commitment: partial at best — MGH is the accountable organization and the NIH award runs to 2026-11-30, but no preservation commitment beyond the award is stated, and the notes field quotes a live banner warning the site is 'under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', which is an explicit signal of institutional discontinuity risk rather than commitment. Long-term governance plan: partial, via data_governance and maintainers. The internal inconsistency that matters most is between status='partially released' with modalities actively changing and the complete absence of version identifiers: a dataset that is explicitly moving and unversioned cannot support reproducible citation, and two users who both say 'the CHoRUS dataset' may not hold the same thing.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources lists four distinct references: 'https://chorus4ai.org/' (project webpage with pages on team, overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources); 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' (28 repositories); 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824' (NIH RePORTER record for award OT2OD032701); 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'. citation absent; doi absent. Top-level source_caveats: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset.' existing_uses mentions that 'Datasets are being used for training activities and publications' without naming any. Four distinct non-publication references are documented, each annotated with what it contains, which comfortably clears the one-reference floor. The 5-point condition is not met: no formal dataset citation exists — nothing identifies the dataset by title together with its authors or publishing organization in citable form — and there is no dataset DOI. Per the Q14 rule, multiple references without a formal citation earn 3, not more. The references are genuinely distinct resources rather than repeated links to one target, and three of the four are well-formed resolvable URLs; the fourth, 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', lacks a scheme and is not resolvable as written, though the record notes it is reproduced as published. None of the four is a peer-reviewed publication: no journal article, preprint, or DOI-bearing reference of any kind appears, even though existing_uses asserts that publications exist. That assertion without enumeration is a semantic gap — the record knows publications exist and names none. For a dataset whose reuse is governed by a signed licensing agreement, the missing recommended citation is a practical attribution failure, since users granted access have no canonical form in which to credit it.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 6 entries, three with counts (50,000 admissions from ICU/PICU/NICU; 1.6 billion OMOP rows; 7,642 admissions with radiology). subpopulations: two entries — 'Admissions in the current release are drawn from adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric intensive care (PICU), and neonatal intensive care (NICU) settings' and 'Demographics are captured as one of the nine data modalities and standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; social determinants of health and contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are acquired alongside them'. human_subject_research.special_populations names PICU and NICU patients. splits documents a sequestered holdout. Absent: at_risk_populations, missing_data_documentation, and any demographic distribution (no age, sex, race, ethnicity, or payer breakdown) or inclusion/exclusion criteria. Above the 3 floor's bare minimum in that care-setting subgroups are explicitly identified and the cohort is sized, but squarely at 3 overall: the record states that demographics are collected without reporting a single demographic figure. Nothing tells a reuser the age distribution, sex balance, or racial and ethnic composition of the 50,000 admissions, and no inclusion or exclusion criteria define how an admission entered the cohort. The 5 band requires detailed demographics and criteria; neither is present. There is a meaningful semantic distinction between declaring demographics as a modality and characterizing the cohort, and the record does only the former. This matters more here than it would elsewhere because equity is in the dataset's own title ('for Equitable AI') and purposes claims 'the most diverse ... data set' — a diversity claim that the record supplies no evidence for, since no distribution is reported against which diversity could be judged. The same absence hollows out the fairness limb of Q20. Population characterization is otherwise coherent: the ICU/PICU/NICU span in subpopulations matches the special_populations disclosure of pediatric and neonatal patients, and the count of 50,000 admissions is consistent across description and instances. The empty at_risk_populations field means that although vulnerable participants are identified, no safeguard specific to them is recorded anywhere, and empty missing_data_documentation leaves cohort-level missingness uncharacterized.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id 'https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset'; external_resources with 'https://github.com/chorus-ai', 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824', and 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'. doi absent; download_url absent. Passes: multiple external URLs are present and most are well formed and plausibly resolvable. Quality behind the pass is uneven — the NIH RePORTER and GitHub links are stable third-party anchors, but the dataset itself is findable only through a project homepage, and no DOI exists to survive a site change. URL validity is mixed rather than clean: three links are fully formed https URIs on plausible domains (chorus4ai.org, github.com, reporter.nih.gov), while 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' lacks a scheme and will not resolve programmatically as recorded, so url_validity is reported as some_invalid. Findability in the FAIR sense is only partly satisfied — F1 (globally unique persistent identifier) is unmet, and the notes field's quoted banner about the site being under review for modification is a concrete, self-disclosed threat to the one link that points at the dataset. The pass therefore records the presence of working documentation links, not durable findability.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms: controlled access, 'Users must sign a licensing agreement before gaining access'. data_governance.access_review_process: 'General route: requests for access are directed to dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. Training-program route: participants ... complete a registration form with name, email, and institution and must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent. A ".edu" email address is required ... though program administrators will assist with this access if needed'. distribution_formats (5) tell a requester what they would receive. Delivery context: 'OMOP and telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave'; intended_uses references the 'Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud'. download_url absent. The access tier is unambiguous and correctly stated — DUA/licensing agreement required, with an additional institutional-email condition on one route — and two concrete routes are given with named human contacts and the mechanics of the training route described step by step, including what happens after approval. That is a clearer access path than most controlled-access records provide. Held to 4 because the path stops short of a machine-actionable endpoint: no download_url, no request portal or application form URL, no enclave login location, and no stated decision timeframe, so a requester must email a person and wait with no documented service expectation. The access description is consistent with every other access-related field: controlled access, confidentiality_level 'restricted', all nine modalities confidential, sharing conditional on signed agreement. The record correctly avoids calling the dataset public despite one aspirational 'publicly available' phrase in purposes, and it correctly distinguishes the delivery model (analysis inside a cloud enclave, notes never centralized) from a download model — which explains, and partly justifies, the absence of download_url: for an enclave dataset there may be no file to download. What is genuinely missing is the enclave's own access location. The record's governance source_caveats concedes there is no documented decision timeframe or appeal process, so the post-request half of the access path is undefined.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms present (controlled access, signed licensing agreement, .edu requirement on the training route). intended_uses: three categories with usage_notes and examples — ML/AI model development for acute and critical care (examples: prediction of complications and deterioration; measurement of treatment response), external validation of AI models against the holdout set, and training and workforce development ('hands-on AI/ML coursework, canonical Jupyter Notebooks, and OHDSI/OMOP instruction'). future_use_impacts: one entry on sequestering holdout datasets 'to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models ... and to catalyze the biomedical research and expertise necessary to promote the patient-focused deployment of AI'. prohibited_uses absent; discouraged_uses absent. Meets the 3 band cleanly and no higher. Intended uses are well developed — three distinct categories, each with notes and, in one case, concrete examples — so a reuser knows what the data are for. But use guidance is one-sided: nothing is prohibited and nothing is discouraged, which is a conspicuous omission for critical-care PHI released under a signed agreement that certainly imposes restrictions. The social impact limb is not satisfied: the single future_use_impacts entry describes hoped-for benefits (marketplace adoption, catalyzing research) and identifies no risk and no mitigation, so there is no impact analysis to speak of. Content accuracy check: the restrictiveness of the use guidance is out of step with the restrictiveness of the access terms. A dataset whose every modality is controlled, whose confidentiality level is 'restricted', and which requires a signed licensing agreement will have contractual prohibitions — no reidentification attempts, no redistribution, no clinical deployment without validation — yet prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both empty, so the record's use guidance reads more permissive than its access terms imply. For a dataset explicitly framed around equitable AI, the absence of any stated risk from misuse (model deployment on populations unlike the academic-center cohort, automation bias in critical care) is a substantive RAI gap rather than a formatting one.
