Useful risk material does exist elsewhere in the record — the four typed known_limitations, including the representativeness limitation — but it is not surfaced as use guidance and does not fall within this question's fields.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: raw_data_sources: six entries each pairing a source_description with source_type and raw_data_format — hospital EHR (site formats mapped to OMOP), EHR free text ('extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit', access_details 'Notes are stored locally at the contributing site; only tokens are made available centrally'), hospital PACS (DICOM), bedside monitoring infrastructure (WFDB), hospital EEG database (EDF+ and Persyst), and contextual/geospatial data linked to OMOP Location entities. updates.update_details present. splits documents the sequestered holdout. Agents identified in data_collectors (14 Data Acquisition centers; site managers under Chorus_SOP). Activities identified in preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies (OMOP mapping, tokenization, waveform conversion, DeGauss geocoding, characterization reports, validated semantic mappings). Absent: version_access, errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation. The lineage this record does provide is unusually complete in text form: for every modality one can trace source system, to extracting agent, to transforming activity and named tool, to released format. Entity, activity, and agent are all identifiable even though no PROV-O serialization exists, and the rubric accepts textual provenance. What keeps it from 5 is that the formal derivation fields are empty — was_derived_from and parent_datasets record nothing, so the derivation paths are readable by a human and not by a machine — and the integrity half of the question is bare: no version_access, no errata channel, and no missing_data_documentation for a dataset built on high-frequency flowsheet and telemetry streams where missingness is pervasive and informative. This record inverts the usual pattern the scoring bands anticipate. The 3 band describes version history without provenance; here provenance lineage is strong and version history is absent entirely, which is why the score sits above 3 despite the empty integrity fields. Derivation is coherent and checkable: each of the six raw_data_sources maps onto exactly one acquisition_method, one or more preprocessing_strategies, and one distribution_format, with no orphaned source and no format lacking an origin. The quality-control loop is real and documented rather than asserted — characterization reports returned to sites via CHoRUSReports, and semantic mappings validated under a clinical validation SOP — which is evidence of integrity practice even though no integrity artifacts (checksums, errata, validation reports) are exposed to reusers. The note-token architecture is provenance-relevant and correctly recorded: the released entity is derived from, and is not, the source note.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: a single entry with bias_type 'representation_bias'; bias_description 'The project treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed: patient-focused efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health, and the stated goal is the most diverse AI-ready data set for improving recovery from acute illness'; mitigation_strategy 'Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort, and sampling at scale is designed to capture comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies'. future_use_impacts: one entry on holdout sequestration for marketplace adoption. Related but outside this question's fields: known_limitations.representativeness_limitation notes the cohort 'reflects the case mix and practice patterns of those participating academic centers'. Sits at 3 with one foot toward 4. In its favour: a BiasTypeEnum term is used rather than free text, and a mitigation_strategy is attached. Against: there is exactly one bias entry, the description states an intention to manage bias rather than characterizing a bias present in the data, and no fairness analysis exists in any form — no subgroup performance consideration, no comparison of cohort composition against a reference population, not even a demographic table. The 5 band asks for comprehensive categorization plus fairness analysis; neither limb is met. The taxonomy term is used correctly — representation_bias is the right category for a cohort-balance concern — but it labels an aspiration, not a finding, and the mitigation is written in the future tense ('Federated access will enable sampling methods'), so nothing recorded here has yet been applied to the released 50,000 admissions. Two biases that the record's own content makes obvious go uncategorized: selection bias, since data come from 14 academic centers of 20 in a consortium and academic critical care differs systematically from community practice (a fact the record states as a limitation but does not classify as bias), and measurement bias, since nursing flowsheet and telemetry documentation practices vary across 14 independent health systems feeding one harmonized model. The fairness gap compounds the Q15 finding: demographics and social determinants of health are collected modalities, so the material for a fairness analysis was acquired and simply is not reported, which is a weaker position than not having the data. Against the dataset's own 'for Equitable AI' framing and the CROISSANT RAI expectation, this is the widest gap between stated ambition and documented evidence anywhere in the record.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10/14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; title 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description (~1,600 chars); keywords (12); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (training-program licensing agreement, controlled access); page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (6 with affiliations); purposes (5 responses); instances (6 typed entries with counts 50000, 1600000000, 7642); resources via external_resources (chorus-ai GitHub organization, Bridge2AI CHoRUS page). Absent (4/14): doi; parent_datasets; variables; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (no regulatory_restrictions block — data_governance carries access_review_process and committee_contact instead). Populated fields carry substantive content rather than placeholders, but four of fourteen required slots are empty, including the two that most affect citation and machine-readable governance (doi, confidentiality_level). 10/14 ≈ 71% falls squarely in the band-3 range. No field is filled with content belonging to another field. The absent confidentiality_level is partly compensated in prose ('All data types are described as controlled access', confidential_elements_present true) but not as a classification value, so downstream machine governance cannot read it. No variables/schema-level description of the OMOP tables is given despite OMOP conformance being claimed.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description ≈ 1,600 characters covering consortium scale (20 academic centers, 60+ members, 14 Data Acquisition centers), released contents (50,000 admissions; 1.6 billion OMOP rows; 7,642 admissions with radiology; 23 Tb waveform), modality-by-modality standards, and the enclave/controlled-access model. purposes holds 5 responses averaging ≈ 230 characters each, e.g. 'To provision a holdout test set, accessible for model external validation, to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.' Both narrative fields exceed the 200-character threshold by a wide margin, and the length is carrying specific quantities and mechanisms rather than filler. Description content is semantically appropriate to a multicenter critical-care EHR/waveform/imaging resource and every quantity it cites reappears in instances or distribution_formats, so the narrative and the structured fields do not diverge. One purpose ('publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset') sits in tension with the controlled-access-only reality; that tension is scored under Q9, Q17 and Q18, not here.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 12 unique keywords: critical care; intensive care unit; acute illness; electronic health records; OMOP Common Data Model; physiologic waveforms; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; social determinants of health; Bridge2AI; AI-ready dataset. Twelve distinct keywords, none duplicated, spanning clinical domain, data modality, standard, program affiliation and intended use. Every keyword is discharged somewhere in the body: 'OMOP Common Data Model' by conforms_to and distribution_formats, 'electroencephalography' by the EDF+/Persyst instances, 'clinical notes' by the OHNLP tokenization entries. Only 'social determinants of health' is weakly supported — it appears in sensitive_elements and intended_uses as a topic of interest, but no SDOH variables or linkage are described, making that keyword partly aspirational.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 5 entries: OMOP CDM tables (demographics, medication administration, procedures, diagnoses, nursing flowsheets); tokenized clinical notes in the OHNLP open-source schema; DICOM imaging from PACS; WFDB waveform telemetry (23 Tb); EEG waveform in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Each entry carries an access note and its published metadata schema. Five distinct format families, well above the >3 threshold, each annotated with its access condition and metadata schema rather than merely named. The format variety corroborates the multi-modal claim in description and keywords instead of overstating it — DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst and OMOP each map to a declared modality and a declared raw_data_source. Neither total_file_count nor file_collections is populated, so per-format volumes are known only for waveforms (23 Tb); this limits enumeration but not type variety, which is what this question scores.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances.counts: 50000 admissions; 1600000000 OMOP rows; 7642 admissions with radiology. Volume: '23 Tb of waveform data' (description and distribution_formats). splits records a sequestered holdout test set. subpopulations records ICU/PICU/NICU provenance of admissions. Passes on explicit numeric counts plus one direct size figure; the counts also permit rough size estimation for the OMOP tier. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent, so dataset volume is known only for waveforms and must be inferred elsewhere. Counts for the EEG and clinical-note tiers are missing entirely (both marked in-process), and the released-versus-anticipated distinction (50,000 now, 100,000 planned) is stated clearly enough that a reader will not mistake the target for the holding.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; external_resources: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' and 'https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'; funders.grants.id: 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'. No doi and no publisher field. Passes on the presence of stable institutional links, but only barely: the pass turns on 'no persistent ID or link' being the failure condition, and the dataset has links without a persistent identifier. id duplicates page, so the record's identity is a project homepage rather than a dataset identifier — a homepage can be reorganized without redirect and cannot name a release. The RePORTER URL is a persistent grant identifier but identifies the award, not the data. The absence of a DOI for a resource already released to trainees is the single largest findability defect and is carried into the Q13 and Q16 notes.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders.grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grant name 'OT2OD032701' with description 'project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824 ... fiscal year 2022 award amount USD 5,880,300; project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30' and id 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'. Disclaimer recorded in funders.notes. creators: 6 entries, all with affiliations (Massachusetts General Hospital, University of Florida ×3, UTHealth Houston, Tufts University); only 'Eric S. Rosenthal' occupies a structured role field (principal_investigator). Content for the band-5 condition is present and unusually complete on the funding side — agency, award number, project number, application ID, dollar amount and period. One point withheld for the creator representation defect described below, which is a genuine machine-readability loss rather than a formatting preference. OT2OD032701 validates against the NIH pattern (OT2 activity code, OD institute, six-digit serial) and is consistent with both the project number and the RePORTER application ID. Funding goals align with purposes (AI-ready critical care data, ethics, workforce). Semantic deduction: five of six creators carry names only inside notes text ('Azra Bihorac, member of the Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team'), leaving affiliation-only creator records that no downstream system can attribute; the record is also careful not to assert PI status for them, which is correct but leaves their role undefined. No ORCIDs anywhere.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true with special_populations 'Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions' and 'Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions'; is_deidentified.method 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification; de-identification of imaging' with deidentification_details naming the privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid repositories; ethical_reviews ×2 (community ethics focus groups; consortium work on trustworthiness, provenance, privacy and bias, 'Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar'); data_governance.committee_contact 'Jared Houghtaling (jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org)'; sensitive_elements and confidential_elements both flagged present with details. Absent: informed_consent; participant_privacy and reidentification_risk; participant_compensation; data_protection_impacts; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant and other_compliance (only the vague 'established a legal framework for collecting data at scale' under regulatory_compliance). Roughly half the protection areas are covered, and the deidentification account is concrete about mechanism (tokenization, notes held locally, imaging de-id in process with named tooling). But the two anchors of the band-3 descriptor are split: deidentification is documented, IRB is not, and the record states outright that no ethics review board of record is named. Consent, HIPAA status, re-identification risk and DPIA are all missing for a PHI-bearing multicenter resource. Score held at 3 rather than 4. The record's honesty is real and worth noting — human_subject_research.source_caveats says plainly that IRB approval is not stated — but a declared gap is still a gap for a datasheet whose function is to let a reuser judge the ethical basis of the data. Two consistency checks fail here (human subjects without IRB; human subjects without consent or waiver), and a third at medium severity (deidentification claimed without re-identification risk or HIPAA designation). The pediatric and neonatal populations raise rather than lower the expectation on consent documentation, so the special_populations declaration slightly deepens the gap it discloses. Ethics claims are otherwise plausible and proportionate: nothing is overclaimed, and the restrictiveness of controlled access matches the sensitivity asserted.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms covers only the AIM-AHEAD program route: 'Participants ... must sign a licensing agreement, included in the program registration form, before gaining access to the dataset; that program also requires an institutional (".edu") email address ... All data types are described as controlled access', with source_caveats confirming 'The bundle states no general license for the data themselves'. data_governance.access_review_process is detailed (controlled access in a cloud enclave, notes local to sites, registration form capturing name/email/institution, licensing agreement, compute provisioning email, administrator assistance). committee_contact and two access-request addresses (dbold@emory.edu, jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org) are given. Absent: ip_restrictions; regulatory_restrictions block; confidentiality_level; data_protection_impacts; hipaa_compliant. The access mechanics are described more fully than most records manage, but the governance instrument itself is missing: there is no dataset-wide license, no confidentiality classification value, no IP terms, and no named data access committee. What exists exceeds 'license only' in operational detail while falling short of it in legal substance, so the two effects offset at 3. The scope mismatch is the substantive finding: registration, licensing agreement and the '.edu' requirement are attested only for training-program trainees, and data_governance.source_caveats says so explicitly rather than generalizing them to dataset policy — accurate reporting that nonetheless leaves external reuse terms undefined. Restrictiveness is internally consistent (sensitive and confidential elements flagged, controlled access asserted uniformly, notes withheld from the enclave), so nothing here is implausible; the MIT/Apache-2.0 licensing is correctly scoped to the software repositories and not misapplied to the data. The named contacts are individual email addresses rather than a standing committee, so accountability rests on persons, not an office.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to: structured EHR to 'the OMOP Common Data Model, with schema extensions used for nursing flowsheets; clinical notes follow the OHNLP open-source schema; imaging follows DICOM; waveform telemetry follows WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema; EEG follows the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas'. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Instances carry ontology term identifiers (B2AI_TOPIC:4, :9, :15, :32, :37; B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :43, :49). external_resources describes chorus-mapping (validated semantic mappings), Chorus_SOP, chorus-extract-upload and chorus-container-apps. distribution_formats names the published metadata schema for each modality. Every element of the band-5 condition is met with content rather than assertion: open community standards for all five modalities, an explicit LinkML schema URI, ontology-coded topics and substrates on instances, and a concrete harmonization pathway (site extracts mapped to OMOP under validated semantic mappings) that is what integration capability means for a 14-site federation. Standards are correctly matched to modality throughout — no misassignment such as DICOM for waveforms — and conforms_to_standard does not claim any standard the prose fails to support, with OTHER used honestly for EDF+/Persyst/OHNLP. The record declines to reconstruct the garbled per-modality metadata column rather than guessing, which preserves correctness. Weaker point, not enough to cost a band: related_datasets is empty and no common patient or encounter identifier is described for linkage to other Bridge2AI resources, so integration is demonstrated within CHoRUS (across sites and modalities) rather than across programs. The tokens-only treatment of notes also limits practical multimodal integration, which known_limitations itself concedes.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies ×4: OMOP standardization with flowsheet extensions; OHNLP tokenization with notes retained on site; 'Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification'; waveform conversion via 'the waveform conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories'. cleaning_strategies ×2: site characterization reports returned to contributors (CHoRUSReports); semantic mappings in chorus-mapping 'reviewed by clinical collaborators following an associated clinical validation standard operating procedure', with Chorus_SOP internally validated. labeling_strategies ×1: 'A visualization and annotation environment is used to label data with targets important for prediction'. machine_annotation_tools: OHNLP toolkit with description. Absent: imputation_protocols; missing_data_documentation. Strategy coverage is broad and the named repositories make most steps locatable, which clears band 3 comfortably. Held below 5 because no software version is given anywhere (the package status page is described as listing versions but no version is asserted), only the organization-level URL is provided rather than per-repository links, the annotation environment is unnamed, and imputation and missing-data handling are undocumented for a critical-care resource where missingness in flowsheets and telemetry is a first-order analytic concern. Tool-to-task assignments are technically coherent: OHNLP is a real clinical NLP toolkit appropriate to note tokenization, CTP is the standard DICOM de-identification pipeline for imaging, and WFDB conversion tooling matches the telemetry modality. Annotation quality is not evidenced — no inter-annotator agreement, no annotator qualifications, no annotation_analyses — so the labeling claim is the weakest link in an otherwise concrete account. The re-identification-limiting transformation is described only in the abstract, which is the same vagueness flagged under Q8.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: 'Retrospective extraction of clinical data recorded during routine hospital care ... delivered to CHoRUS as site-specific clinical data extracts prepared according to validated standard operating procedures and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling'. collection_mechanisms ×5, one per modality (EHR extraction including 'medication administration recorded at each infusion change or dose administration'; PACS; bedside monitors via gateway/middleware; hospital EEG database; OHNLP note tokenization). data_collectors ×2 with roles: 14 contributing hospitals as Data Acquisition centers; CHoRUS Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams. direct_collection.is_direct false with rationale. sampling_strategies: comprehensive condition coverage, 'Federated access enabling sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort'. collection_timeframes: 'Retrospective data collection from clinical records already generated during hospital care. Dataset contents reported in the cohort 2 webinar are stated as of August 2025.' Mechanisms, acquisition route, collectors and roles are all documented at modality granularity, which is well past the band-3 'mechanism only'. One point withheld: the timeframe entry gives a reporting date, not the admission date range the data cover, and no inclusion/exclusion criteria, per-site contribution volumes or eligibility rules are stated, so the cohort cannot be reconstructed. The five collection mechanisms correspond one-to-one with the five raw_data_sources and with the five distribution_formats, a three-way alignment that indicates the protocol description was built from the same modality model rather than assembled loosely. direct_collection.is_direct false is semantically correct for retrospective extraction from clinical systems and is consistent with the absence of recruitment or compensation fields — though not with the absence of a consent waiver, which is flagged under Q8. sampling_strategies asserts balance and diversity as a design intent with no evidence of achieved balance, which given the empty demographics is closer to aspiration than to method.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.update_details 'The dataset is growing from the current released 50,000 admissions toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions and 9 data modalities across 14 contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process ... The NIH project period runs to 2026-11-30.'; maintainers ×2 (MGH program management with a named program manager; chorus-ai GitHub organization whose 'package status page lists versions, maintainers, and other metadata for CHoRUS packages'); extension_mechanism with contribution_url. Absent: version; version_access; errata; doi; publisher. status notes the site banner 'This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives.' Above the band-0 floor because a forward-looking update plan, named maintainers and a contribution workflow exist. Well below band 3, which requires a version number, version access information and a persistent identifier — none of the three is present. Scored 2. The versioning that is described belongs to the software packages, not the data: the package status page tracks repository versions while the 50,000-admission release itself carries no identifier, no release date and no way to request a prior state. Sustainability fails on three of four indicators — no persistent ID, no domain repository deposit (the enclave is project infrastructure, not an archive), and no institutional preservation commitment past the 2026-11-30 award end — leaving only a maintenance plan that is coextensive with the funding period. The quoted status banner signals an external availability risk that no continuity plan addresses, compounding rather than mitigating the exposure.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources ×2 distinct: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' (chorus-ai GitHub organization, 28 repositories) and 'https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' (CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website). funders.grants.id adds 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'. No citation field, no doi, and no journal or preprint reference anywhere; existing_uses mentions that 'The datasets are being used for training activities and publications' and that trainees 'may submit conference abstracts or manuscripts', without naming any. Two distinct non-publication references are documented, which satisfies the two-reference half of the band-5 condition, but no formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title and its authors or publishing organization exists, and there is no dataset DOI. Per the Q14 rule this earns 3, not 5. Both external resources resolve to plausible, project-controlled domains and are described substantively rather than listed bare. The gap is structural: a consortium at this scale and stage almost certainly has associated publications, and existing_uses gestures at them generically without a single reference, so a reuser has no route from the datasheet to the methods literature. Absence of a citable form follows from the absence of a DOI flagged under Q6 and Q13.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 'Hospital admission of a critically ill patient (ICU, PICU, or NICU)', counts 50000, plus modality-level instance types. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true, identification 'Admissions in the released dataset are drawn from ICU, PICU, and NICU', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not give the distribution of admissions across ICU, PICU, and NICU, nor any demographic breakdown of the cohort.' human_subject_research.special_populations names PICU and NICU admissions. splits records the sequestered holdout test set. missing_data_documentation absent. Care-setting subgroups and two vulnerable populations are identified, which is more than 'general human data', but no age, sex, race, ethnicity, payer or geographic distribution is given, no counts per subgroup, and no inclusion/exclusion criteria. A reuser cannot assess who is represented. Score 3. The representation gap is directly acknowledged in subpopulations.source_caveats, so the record does not overstate diversity — the unit of analysis is also stated correctly as the admission rather than the patient, which matters for a critical-care cohort where readmissions inflate counts. The consequence is nonetheless serious for this dataset in particular: the project title claims equitable AI and intended_uses include 'Equity and social determinants research', yet nothing in the record supports an equity analysis of the cohort itself. That same emptiness is what prevents any fairness assessment under Q20.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; external_resources 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' and 'https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; funders.grants.id 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'. No download_url and no doi. Passes on several well-formed external links to project, code, program and award pages. All URLs are structurally valid and point to plausible organizational domains; the w3id URI is a genuinely persistent identifier, but for the schema rather than the data. Findability of the dataset object itself remains weak: no DOI, no repository landing page, no download endpoint, and the status banner warning of possible modification of the project site makes reliance on chorus4ai.org as the locator less safe than a resolver-backed identifier would be.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: One route is fully specified, for one audience: 'participants fill out a registration form giving name, email, and institution and must sign a licensing agreement included in that form before gaining access to the dataset; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant. That program also requires a ".edu" email address'. Access-request contacts: dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. distribution_formats records controlled access and the enclave for each of the five formats. No download_url, no application portal, no stated review criteria or turnaround, and license_and_use_terms.source_caveats confirms no access terms exist outside the training-program context. The platform (cloud enclave), the gating condition (controlled access), the per-modality access notes and one concrete end-to-end route are all documented, which is more than a bare statement of restriction. But an unaffiliated researcher is left with two email addresses and no defined application path, eligibility criteria or decision process, so the access path is not fully defined. Score 3. The record is precise about the limits of its own evidence, attributing the registration and '.edu' requirements to the training program rather than generalizing them — accurate, and the reason the score is not lower, since a fabricated general policy would have been worse. The '.edu' requirement, if it were dataset-wide, would exclude industry, health-system and international reusers, which sits awkwardly with the marketplace-adoption purpose for the holdout test set; that tension cannot be resolved from the record. Practical accessibility is further reduced by the notes-stay-on-site design, correctly disclosed as an integration_limitation.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: intended_uses ×4 with categories and notes: model development for acute and critical care; external validation against the sequestered holdout set; training and workforce development on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud; 'Equity and social determinants research ... Analyses that account for social determinants of health and contextual data elements such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital, supporting work on managing privacy and bias'. existing_uses documents Cohort 2 usage concretely. known_limitations ×3 (coverage, integration, scope). Absent: prohibited_uses; discouraged_uses; future_use_impacts. license_and_use_terms covers only the training-program agreement. Intended-use guidance is genuinely useful and is paired with honest limitations, clearing band 3. Band 5 is out of reach: nothing states what may not be done with critical-care PHI (no bar on re-identification attempts, redistribution, or clinical deployment of unvalidated models), no discouraged uses are named, and there is no social impact analysis with mitigation strategies despite the ethics activity described elsewhere. Ethics work is present in the record but sits in ethical_reviews as consortium activity — focus groups on what is appropriate to share, work on trustworthiness and bias — rather than being converted into use guidance a reuser can act on, so social impact is discussed about the project and not about downstream use of the data. The equity intended-use category is the clearest instance of the record's recurring pattern: equity is named as a purpose four times while the cohort characterization and bias documentation that equity analysis requires are absent. Combined with the missing general license, reusability rests on an incomplete legal and normative basis.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: raw_data_sources ×5 with source_type, format and access details (hospital EHR; unstructured notes 'Notes remain stored locally at contributing sites; only tokenized output is moved into the enclave'; PACS/DICOM; bedside monitoring telemetry; EEG database/EDF+ and Persyst). Activities: acquisition under validated SOPs with chorus-extract-upload, OMOP standardization with flowsheet extensions, OHNLP tokenization, imaging de-identification (CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool), waveform conversion scripts. Agents: 14 contributing hospitals, CHoRUS Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams, clinical collaborators validating chorus-mapping. Quality controls: CHoRUSReports characterization returned per submission; mapping review under a clinical validation SOP. splits: sequestered holdout test set. updates present. Absent: version_access; errata; was_derived_from; parent_datasets; missing_data_documentation. The rubric accepts textual provenance, and the record supplies a traceable path from each source system through named processing activities to the enclave, with responsible agents attached and two independent quality-control mechanisms — well past band 3, which describes version history without lineage. Held at 4 because derivation is narrative rather than recorded per artifact: no was_derived_from links, no parent dataset identifiers, no errata or version access, and no missing-data documentation, so a specific released file cannot be traced to a specific input or processing run. Derivation paths are individually reconstructable per modality (EHR→OMOP+extensions; notes→OHNLP tokens with source text withheld; PACS→DICOM→de-identification; monitors→gateway→WFDB; EEG→EDF+/Persyst) and the agent assignments are consistent with the collectors named under Q12, so the lineage is coherent rather than decorative. Integrity evidence is process-level only: characterization reporting and mapping validation are real controls, but no checksums, no record counts per submission and no validation results are given. Missing-data documentation is a notable omission precisely because high-frequency flowsheet and telemetry data are characteristically gappy, and its absence also cost a point under Q11.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: No known_biases field and no future_use_impacts field. Nearest content: known_limitations scope_limitation 'The dataset is restricted to retrospectively collected admissions of critically ill patients (ICU, PICU, NICU) at 14 contributing hospitals'; coverage_limitation on incomplete imaging and EEG availability; ethical_reviews 'Patient-focused efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'; intended_uses 'supporting work on managing privacy and bias'; sampling_strategies 'Federated access enabling sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort'. Above 0 because the limitations do disclose the sampling frame and coverage gaps that bear directly on representativeness, and bias is named as an object of project concern. Below 3 because no bias is actually identified as a bias: no taxonomy term, no direction or expected effect, no affected subgroup, and no fairness analysis. Score 2. The elements needed for a credible bias account are present as raw material and never assembled — a 14-site academic medical center sampling frame is a textbook selection bias, heterogeneous monitor and EHR vendors across sites imply measurement bias, and the imaging subset (7,642 admissions with radiology out of 50,000) is a large and undiscussed availability asymmetry. Because the demographics are empty (Q15), no fairness analysis is possible even in principle from this record. The gap is sharpest against the record's own framing: the dataset is titled 'for Equitable AI' and names equity research among its intended uses, so responsible-AI alignment is asserted at the level of mission while the documentation that would substantiate it is absent.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10 of 14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset'; title 'Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description (~1,400 chars); keywords (14); license_and_use_terms (contact_person, license_terms, notes); page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (2 entries, PI Eric S. Rosenthal with MGH affiliation); purposes (4 responses); instances (11 entries); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (4 of 14): doi, resources, parent_datasets, variables. 10/14 = 71% of the mandatory field set is populated, and the populated fields carry real content rather than placeholders. The four absent fields are consequential rather than incidental: doi removes citability, and variables removes any variable-level dictionary for a dataset whose selling point is 1.6 billion rows across nine modalities. resources and parent_datasets are defensibly empty for a primary, non-hierarchical collection. Field presence and field meaning agree here — no field is populated with content belonging to a different field, and no mandatory field is padded. The absence of variables is semantically material for an OMOP-standardised dataset, where a variable-level description would be straightforward to derive from the CDM tables named in distribution_formats. Scored at the 70% band without adjustment.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 1,400 characters, from 'CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset...' through '...support external validation of AI models developed for acute and critical care.' The four purposes responses run approximately 230, 170, 200 and 250 characters, averaging well above the 200-character threshold when combined with the description. Comfortably above the top band. More importantly, the length is carrying information rather than filling space: the description states participant counts, the number of contributing hospitals, every modality with its format, the access model and the planned holdout set. Length and substance coincide, which is not automatic — the description is specific and falsifiable (50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion rows, 7,642 radiology admissions, 23 Tb of waveforms, 14 hospitals, 20 centres) rather than adjectival. The four purposes are distinct rather than restatements of one another, covering AI development, AI-ready data production, ethical sourcing, and workforce development.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 14 unique keywords: critical care; acute illness; intensive care unit; electronic health record; OMOP Common Data Model; physiologic waveforms; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; social determinants of health; AI-ready dataset; Bridge2AI; multimodal data; controlled access. Well above the 8-keyword threshold with no duplicates or near-duplicates. The set spans four distinct discovery axes — clinical domain, data modality, standard, and access model — rather than restating one concept in several ways. Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record: each named modality appears in distribution_formats and instances, 'OMOP Common Data Model' in conforms_to and conforms_to_standard, 'controlled access' in license_and_use_terms and confidentiality_level, 'social determinants of health' in sensitive_elements and the DeGauss geocoding preprocessing step. No keyword is aspirational relative to the content.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: Five distribution_formats entries spanning distinct format families: OMOP CDM tables; OHNLP toolkit output for tokenized notes; DICOM for PACS imaging; WFDB for waveform telemetry; EDF+ and Persyst for EEG. file_collections and total_file_count are absent. Five format families, well beyond the three required for the top band, and the variety is genuine multimodality rather than repackaging of one data type. Each entry is annotated with its access condition and published metadata schema. The variety corroborates the multimodality claimed in description and keywords ('multimodal data'), satisfying the rubric's instruction that variety should indicate multi-modal data as indicated in description, purposes or keywords. Counted against, but not deducted for at this band: no media types, encodings, compression or per-format file counts are given, so the enumeration is of format families rather than of files. The question scores type variety, which is amply met; the packaging gap is recorded under Q5 and Q10.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances carry numeric counts: 50000 patient admissions, 1600000000 OMOP EHR rows, 7642 admissions with radiology data. description states '23 Tb of waveform data'. splits records a sequestered holdout test set; subpopulations records two subpopulation axes with subpopulation_elements_present: true. Passes on multiple independent grounds — three numeric instance counts, an aggregate byte-scale figure for the largest modality, plus split and subpopulation metadata. Counts are internally consistent with the description and are the right order of magnitude for one another (1.6 billion OMOP rows across 50,000 admissions is about 32,000 rows per admission, plausible for ICU data including high-frequency nursing flowsheets). The 23 Tb waveform figure sits in prose rather than in total_size_bytes, and no per-format byte sizes exist, so the pass is on instance counts primarily; a consumer can size the structured data but not the enclave footprint per modality.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: id 'https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset'; page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'. doi absent; no rrid; publisher absent. source_caveats: 'No version identifier, DOI, citation, release date, retention policy, or errata for the dataset appear anywhere in the bundle.' Passes on the stated fail criterion, which is 'No persistent ID or link' — a dereferenceable identifier URI and a landing page are both present. This is the weakest possible pass: there is no DOI, ARK, Handle or RRID, and no publisher or hosting repository is named. The id is a fragment identifier on the project's own website, so the identifier and the landing page are the same resource under project control, with no registry guarantee of persistence. The record's own notes field flags instability of that resource: the site 'carries a banner reading "This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives."' A single project-controlled domain is therefore the entire identification infrastructure. The binary passes; the deficiency is carried into Q13 (sustainability) and Q14 (citation) where it is scored.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund, Bridge2AI program' with grants name 'OT2OD032701' and notes giving 'Project number 1OT2OD032701-01 (core project number OT2OD032701), NIH application ID 10472824, awarded to Massachusetts General Hospital; award amount 5,880,300 for fiscal year 2022, with a project period running from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30' and the RePORTER URL. creators: principal_investigator 'Eric S. Rosenthal' with affiliation Massachusetts General Hospital; a second entry affiliated to the CHoRUS Consortium naming five further leadership members with their institutions (University of Florida, UTHealth Houston, Tufts University). Both limbs of the top band are satisfied and exceeded: the funder carries a grant number plus application ID, award amount, fiscal year, project period and a verifiable RePORTER link, and creators carry named individuals with institutional affiliations. Grant number validation passes: OT2OD032701 matches the NIH pattern of activity code (OT2, an other-transaction award appropriate to Common Fund programmes), institute code (OD, Office of the Director, which is where Common Fund awards sit), and six digits; the expanded form 1OT2OD032701-01 correctly adds application type and support year. Grantor, activity code and institute are mutually consistent, and funding purpose aligns with purposes ('one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium'). The only gap is the absence of ORCID and ROR identifiers, which the record explicitly attributes to the source bundle; since the question scores funders and creators content rather than registry identifiers, no deduction is applied.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: is_deidentified with method 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification of imaging prior to release; data transformations that limit re-identification' and deidentification_details naming the enclave/local-notes split and a privacy scan tool; participant_privacy with anonymization_method, privacy_techniques ('Controlled access to all data types through a cloud enclave, local retention of clinical notes at contributing sites...') and data_linkage; ethical_reviews describing the Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar and community ethics focus groups, reviewing_organization 'CHoRUS consortium ethics pillar'; sensitive_elements (3 entries) and confidential_elements; data_governance.committee_contact 'Jared Houghtaling'. Absent: human_subject_research; informed_consent; at_risk_populations; participant_compensation; data_protection_impacts; participant_privacy.reidentification_risk; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance. Five of twelve fields populated, and the split is the unfavourable one: the technical privacy limb (deidentification, privacy techniques, controlled access, sensitivity classification) is genuinely strong and specific, while the human-protections limb (human-subjects determination, IRB approval, consent or waiver, vulnerable populations, compensation, DPIA, re-identification risk, HIPAA status) is entirely empty. The 3 band anticipates 'IRB + deidentification'; here deidentification is better than the band implies and IRB is absent outright, so the two deviations roughly offset. Scored at 3 rather than 4 because the missing items are the ones a reuser of paediatric and neonatal PHI would need first, and rather than 2 because what is present is substantive and multi-field. Three consistency failures drive the score down from what field count alone would suggest. First, the human-subjects trigger is unambiguously met by description and collection_mechanisms, yet human_subject_research is unpopulated, so the expected ethical_reviews/informed_consent pairing cannot be checked. Second, ethical_reviews is populated but semantically mismatched to its name: it records ethics-pillar engagement activity, and the field's own source_caveats confirms no IRB, approval or protocol number is named — a field present and well-formed but not discharging its purpose. Third, the cohort includes NICU and PICU admissions, so at_risk_populations should be populated by construction, and its emptiness is a content-accuracy failure rather than a missing optional field. Deidentification method appropriateness is partly assessable and partly not: tokenization of notes and local retention is a defensible architecture for the highest-identifiability modality, but no identifier categories are enumerated, no Safe Harbor or Expert Determination standard is named, and the DeGauss geocoding of Location entities adds re-identification surface without a paired risk assessment. The record discloses each gap in source_caveats, which is correct practice and prevents a correctness penalty for fabrication, but disclosure does not supply the missing protections.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'All data types are made available under controlled access only. Users of the dataset through the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset, and must have a ".edu" email address'; contact_person 'Ciera McCrary'; notes distinguishing MIT/Apache-2.0 code licences from dataset terms. regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' with a narrative restriction entry. data_governance: accountable_organization Massachusetts General Hospital, committee_contact 'Jared Houghtaling', access_review_process naming request contacts and the registration workflow, and three stewardship_roles. Absent: ip_restrictions, hipaa_compliant, other_compliance, data_protection_impacts. All three components of the agent's 5 band are present — licence terms, restrictions, and a confidentiality classification — and governance goes further than the band requires with an accountable organisation, named contact, review process and stewardship roles. Held at 4 because the rubric's fuller 5 criterion also expects compliance coverage, and the two most load-bearing compliance facts for US hospital PHI (HIPAA status and the de-identification standard) are absent, as are IP restrictions for the dataset itself. Restrictiveness is consistent across every field that expresses it: controlled access in licence terms, 'Controlled access' on all five distribution formats, confidentiality_level 'restricted', and confidential_elements recording that every data type is controlled. Nothing overclaims openness, which is the failure mode this question's guidance warns about. Two semantic defects temper the score. The licence of record is scoped to one training programme rather than to the dataset generally, so a researcher outside AIM-AHEAD finds eligibility criteria that may not apply to them and a fallback of emailing one of two individuals. And committee_contact names an individual whom the record's own source_caveats says is recorded 'because he is one of two named access-request contacts... not because any source identifies him as a committee contact' — an honest disclosure that the governance contact is inferred, which is the right way to record an inference but leaves the formal access body unidentified.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats names five community standards (OMOP CDM, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB/PhysioNet extended, EDF+/Persyst). conforms_to gives a per-modality narrative: 'Structured clinical data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with nursing flowsheets using the OMOP schema with extensions; imaging follows DICOM; waveform telemetry follows WFDB with the PhysioNet schema extended; EEG follows the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas.' conforms_to_standard: OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER. conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class Dataset. Integration: participant_privacy.data_linkage states data from 14 hospitals are 'harmonized to the OMOP Common Data Model and linked across modalities at the admission level'; preprocessing_strategies describe 'validated semantic mappings' maintained in chorus-mapping. Instances carry B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE CURIEs. related_datasets absent. All three components of the top band are met concretely. Standard formats: five, each the recognised community standard for its modality. Schema and ontology compliance: an explicit LinkML schema URI, an enumerated standards list, and ontology CURIEs on every instance. Integration capability: a stated harmonisation target (OMOP) and a stated linking key (admission level across modalities) — the specific mechanism the question asks for, not a generic assertion of AI-readiness. Each format-to-modality assignment is technically correct, and the enum list is consistent with the prose, with 'OTHER' correctly absorbing EDF+, Persyst and OHNLP which have no enum member. This is the record's strongest dimension and the score is not reduced. Two gaps are recorded without deduction because they fall outside the stated band components: related_datasets is empty, so there are no typed relationships to the other three Bridge2AI generation projects despite a shared programme and schema; and no compression, media types or encodings are given. The integration claim is also located in participant_privacy.data_linkage rather than in an integration-specific field, which makes it harder to find than it should be but does not make it less true.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (5): OMOP standardisation via 'validated semantic mappings' in the chorus-mapping repository; OHNLP tokenization; transformations limiting re-identification plus imaging de-identification; waveform conversion via chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources; 'OMOP Location entities are geocoded via DeGauss using the UF-Geocoding tool'. cleaning_strategies (2): characterisation reports from the CHoRUSReports repository returned to sites after each submission; clinical validation of mappings under a clinical validation SOP within Chorus_SOP. labeling_strategies (1): 'A visualization and annotation environment labels data with targets important for prediction'. machine_annotation_tools (2): OHNLP toolkit and UF-Geocoding, each with tool_descriptions. Absent: imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation, annotation_analyses. Four of seven fields populated, and the populated ones are specific: named tools (OHNLP, DeGauss/UF-Geocoding), named repositories (chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, CHoRUSReports, Chorus_SOP, chorus-extract-upload), and a closed feedback loop in which characterisation reports go back to contributing sites. Short of 5 because no software versions or per-repository URLs are given, annotation quality is asserted without metrics or inter-annotator analysis, and imputation and missing-data handling are wholly undocumented for a critical care dataset where missingness is informative. Tool-to-task assignments are all appropriate: OHNLP is a recognised clinical NLP toolkit and is used for note tokenization; DeGauss is a recognised containerised geomarker tool and is used for geocoding Location entities; WFDB conversion is paired with the waveform modality. The tooling described is consistent across fields — machine_annotation_tools names OHNLP and UF-Geocoding and both reappear in preprocessing_strategies with matching descriptions, and the repositories named here match those in collection_mechanisms and extension_mechanism. The labeling entry is the weakest: it describes an environment in which labelling happens rather than a labelling strategy, with no label taxonomy, no annotator qualifications and no agreement statistics. The absence of missing_data_documentation is a substantive gap given that nursing flowsheets and waveform telemetry have structurally irregular sampling.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2): retrospective extraction across five source system types, plus a derived-data entry flagged was_inferred_derived: true. collection_mechanisms (5): one per modality plus a tooling entry ('Contributing sites create and upload CHoRUS data extracts using project tooling, including the chorus-extract-upload repository, and follow the interactive workflow described on the Chorus_SOP page; dockerized container applications support CHoRUS services deployed on Azure'). data_collectors (3) with roles: data contributing sites, site data managers, clinical collaborators. raw_data_sources (5) each with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. collection_timeframes (1): 'contents reported as of August 2025 and acquisition continuing under a project period running from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30', with source_caveats noting the encounter range is unstated. direct_collection: is_direct false. Among the most thoroughly documented dimensions of this record: five of five fields populated, with per-modality granularity, named roles, named tooling and an explicit statement that collection was indirect. Held at 4 solely because the top band requires timeframes and the timeframe given is the funding period, not the data period — the record itself concedes 'The calendar range of the underlying clinical encounters is not stated in any source.' Cross-field consistency is high: the five collection_mechanisms map one-to-one onto the five raw_data_sources and onto the five distribution_formats, so source system, extraction route and released format agree per modality. The local-notes constraint is stated identically in collection_mechanisms and raw_data_sources.access_details. direct_collection.is_direct false is consistent with retrospective acquisition and with the absence of recruitment fields, and correctly explains why no recruitment protocol appears. Temporal consistency is the one weakness: award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and the August 2025 snapshot are ordered sensibly, but a retrospective ICU cohort without an encounter date range leaves reusers unable to assess practice-era or COVID-19 period effects.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.frequency 'Ongoing during the project period, with regular status updates from contributing sites' and updates.update_details describing site status reporting via GitHub issues and a Google Form, plus growth toward '100,000 patient admissions and nine modalities, with imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process as of September 2025'; maintainers (2) — the consortium coordinated from MGH with a named program manager, and the chorus-ai GitHub organization whose 'package status page lists versions, maintainers, and other package metadata'. Absent: version, version_access, errata, doi, publisher. source_caveats: 'No version identifier, DOI, citation, release date, retention policy, or errata for the dataset appear anywhere in the bundle.' Two of seven fields populated. The 3 band requires a version number plus basic access info plus a persistent ID, and none of those three exists: the dataset carries no version, no version access mechanism and no DOI. What raises this above 0 is a real and specific update plan and two identified maintainers with an accountable institution — more than 'single version only, no sustainability plan', but clearly short of the 3 band. The versioning gap is aggravated rather than mitigated by the release model. status describes a 'Partial release... with acquisition and modality expansion continuing', and updates confirm the content is actively growing, so without versions or dated snapshots two researchers analysing 'the CHoRUS dataset' months apart hold different data with no way to say so. Note the asymmetry the record itself surfaces: the software packages have versions tracked on a package status page, while the data they produce has none. Sustainability is only partly evidenced — institutional commitment is implied by MGH as awardee and accountable_organization, and governance is real (stewardship roles, access review process), but there is no persistent identifier, no domain-appropriate repository (the data sit in a project cloud enclave rather than a preservation repository such as PhysioNet), no retention policy and no commitment beyond the award period ending 2026-11-30. The website banner about 'review for potential modification' recorded in notes adds a concrete near-term risk to the only access route documented.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources holds five distinct entries: the CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/); the chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai); the NIH RePORTER record for OT2OD032701 (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824); the Bridge2AI CHoRUS program page (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus); and the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program cohort 2 informational webinar of September 09, 2025. citation is absent and doi is absent; source_caveats confirms no citation or DOI appears in the bundle. existing_uses notes that 'CHoRUS datasets are being used for training activities and publications' without naming any. Scored 3 under the question's explicit rule that non-publication external resources count as references and that multiple such resources without a formal dataset citation earn 3 rather than 5. Five distinct resources are well past the one required for the band; the 5 band fails on its second limb, since no formal citation identifying the dataset by title with its authors or publishing organisation exists, and no DOI-linked reference of any kind is present. The five entries are genuinely distinct resources rather than repeated links to one target, so no de-duplication reduces the count. None is a peer-reviewed publication and none carries a DOI, so the references are documentation and administrative records rather than literature — adequate for the 3 band as defined, but they give a reuser no way to cite the dataset or to find methodological papers describing it. The gap is notable in context: existing_uses asserts that publications exist, yet none is referenced, so a claim made in one field is unsupported by the field designed to hold the evidence.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 11 entries, the first being 'Patient admission (hospital encounter of a critically ill patient in an adult ICU, pediatric ICU, or neonatal ICU)' with counts 50000. subpopulations (2): by care setting — 'adult intensive care unit (ICU), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)', whose distribution field states the 50,000 are reported 'combined without a per-unit breakdown'; and by contributing hospital, '14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers'. splits records the holdout test set. Absent: at_risk_populations, missing_data_documentation. No age, sex, race, ethnicity or socioeconomic distribution appears anywhere; no inclusion or exclusion criteria are stated. Three of five fields populated. The record exceeds the 3 band's 'general human data without subgroup description' by naming two subpopulation axes, but falls well short of 5, which requires detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria — neither exists even in outline. Held at 3 rather than 4 because the subpopulations are identified without any distribution (the record states the per-unit breakdown is unavailable), so a reuser learns which subgroups exist but nothing about their relative size or composition, and the question's core concern is demographic representation. The most consequential defect is a consistency failure rather than an absence: the subpopulation definition itself establishes that neonates and children are in the cohort, so at_risk_populations is empty for a population the adjacent field proves is present. 'Demographics' appears repeatedly as a data type (an OMOP instance type, listed in description and sensitive_elements), which means demographic variables exist in the data while no demographic summary of the cohort is documented — the difference between holding demographics and reporting representation. sampling_strategies gestures at diversity ('federated access enables sampling methods intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort') but states an intention without evidence of achieved balance, and known_limitations concedes the cohort is confined to 14 academic hospitals. Absent missing_data_documentation, the reader also cannot tell whether demographic fields are themselves complete.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id 'https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; external_resources give https://chorus4ai.org/, https://github.com/chorus-ai, https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824 and www.bridge2ai.org/chorus; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'. Passes clearly on the stated criterion of at least one working external URL, with several across independent domains including a third-party authoritative record (NIH RePORTER) and a w3id permanent identifier for the schema. Domains are plausible and consistent with the entities they claim to represent, and the RePORTER URL's numeric path matches the application ID 10472824 given under funders — an internal cross-check that passes. Two qualifications that do not defeat the binary: 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' is recorded without a scheme, and the only persistent-by-design identifier in the record (the w3id URI) resolves to the metadata schema rather than to the dataset. Findability of the dataset itself therefore depends on a project-controlled domain whose stability the record's notes field explicitly questions.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms: controlled access only; a licensing agreement must be signed within the registration form; a '.edu' email address is required for the training-programme route; contact_person 'Ciera McCrary'. data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access is requested from the named CHoRUS contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org)... participants complete a registration form giving name, email, and institution; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant.' distribution_formats (5) each annotated 'Controlled access'. third_party_sharing describes the cloud enclave. download_url absent. Better than 'partially described': the access tier is unambiguous (signed agreement plus approval, tier 3–4 on the rubric's scale), the formats delivered are enumerated, the review process and its endpoints are named, and provisioning of compute alongside data is described. Short of 5 because no download URL or application portal exists, no eligibility criteria are published for the general case, and no turnaround or approval criteria are stated. This record avoids the specific failure the question's guidance warns against — it never describes itself as public or open, and the access restriction is stated consistently on every format entry, in the licence, in confidential_elements and in confidentiality_level. The weakness is structural rather than rhetorical: the fully specified route is the AIM-AHEAD training programme, complete with registration form, licensing agreement and the '.edu' requirement, while the general researcher's route reduces to emailing one of two named individuals. An access path that depends on individual mailboxes is fragile in a way a portal is not, and one of the two contacts is given only as an email address with no name. The enclave-based delivery model is coherent with the PHI content and correctly implies that no bulk download will exist.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms as quoted at Q9 and Q17. intended_uses (3 categories with examples): clinical AI/ML model development; external model validation using the sequestered holdout set; education and workforce development including 'canonical Jupyter notebooks, workshops on the OHDSI tool stack'. future_use_impacts (2): methods 'intended to promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, and patient-focused ethical and legal work determines approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'; and 'Community-facing ethics focus groups determine what data is appropriate for public sharing'. existing_uses (2) and other_tasks (2) also populated. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses both absent. Squarely at the 3 band: a licence is defined and use guidance is present and well-organised, but two of the five fields — the entire negative half of the guidance — are empty, and the social impact content is programmatic framing rather than the risk identification with mitigation strategies the 5 band requires. The omission of prohibited_uses is a consistency failure against the licence itself: access is conditioned on signing a licensing agreement, and such an agreement for hospital PHI will invariably prohibit re-identification attempts and participant contact, so terms that exist in the signed instrument have not been surfaced into the metadata where a prospective user would read them. Nothing in the record tells a reuser what they may not do with the data. The future_use_impacts entries are genuine and specific about process — community ethics focus groups shaping what is shareable is a concrete governance mechanism rather than a platitude — but they describe how impact is deliberated rather than identifying risks (for example, models trained on 14 academic centres being deployed in community hospitals) and pairing each with a mitigation. Intended uses are well matched to the dataset's content and to tasks and purposes, with no misalignment between claimed purpose and documented capability.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: raw_data_sources (5) as entities, each with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. Activities: acquisition_methods (2, the second flagged was_inferred_derived: true — 'clinical notes are tokenized, source data are mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model, and data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification') and preprocessing_strategies (5, each naming the implementing repository). Agents: data_collectors (3 roles) and maintainers (2). splits records the sequestered holdout test set. updates is populated. Absent: version_access, errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation. Four of nine fields populated, but the question is scored on provenance substance and the rubric expressly accepts a textual representation. Entity, activity and agent are all recoverable and can be chained per modality — for example hospital PACS (entity) to de-identification and DICOM release (activity) by site data managers (agent). That is more than the 3 band, which describes version history without provenance; this record is the mirror image, with lineage but no versioning. Held at 4 because the 5 band needs a complete graph: there is no was_derived_from linking a specific released artefact to a specific source, no parent_datasets, and no missing-data documentation. The lineage is consistent wherever it can be cross-checked — the five raw_data_sources correspond one-to-one with the five collection_mechanisms and the five distribution_formats, and each preprocessing step names the repository that implements it, which is stronger evidence of a real pipeline than prose alone. Two integrity gaps matter for reuse. First, no errata or version access means a data defect discovered after release has no documented channel to reach users, which interacts badly with the growing partial release described in status. Second, missing_data_documentation is absent for modalities where missingness is structurally informative: nursing flowsheets and waveform telemetry are irregularly sampled by nature, and the record acknowledges elsewhere that imaging and EEG coverage is partial, so completeness varies by modality in ways a consumer cannot quantify. The derivation is directionally clear but not addressable: one cannot ask which source records produced a given released table.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases is entirely absent from the record. future_use_impacts mentions bias once and only in passing: 'patient-focused ethical and legal work determines approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. The substance of a selection bias sits in a different field — known_limitations records a representativeness_limitation, 'The cohort is drawn from 14 data contributing hospitals within a 20-center academic network and covers ICU, PICU, and NICU admissions only', with recommended_mitigation citing sampling designed for comprehensive coverage and federated access for a balanced cohort. sampling_strategies states an intention toward 'a balanced and diverse cohort'. Scored on the question's two fields. known_biases, the field a CROISSANT RAI consumer or BiasTypeEnum mapping reads, is empty, and future_use_impacts contains a single clause naming bias as something to be managed rather than identifying any bias in this dataset. That is below the 3 band's 'basic bias identification', which presupposes biases being identified in the bias fields. Above 0 because bias is not wholly unaddressed in the record's content: a representativeness statement with a mitigation does exist and is specific, and future_use_impacts does engage bias management as a programme commitment. This is the clearest instance in the record of content filed under the wrong field. The representativeness_limitation is, in substance, a selection-bias statement complete with mitigation, and known_limitations even uses a typed vocabulary — which makes the total absence of known_biases harder to excuse, since the record demonstrably knows how to categorise. No AIO or BiasTypeEnum mapping appears anywhere, and no fairness analysis exists: there is no measurement-bias discussion despite heterogeneous EHR vendors, monitoring hardware and EEG systems across 14 hospitals, no examination of documentation bias in nursing flowsheets, and no subgroup performance or representation analysis. The academic-centre-only composition combined with the absence of any demographic distribution (Q15) means neither the record nor a reuser can characterise who is under-represented, which is precisely the fairness question a Bridge2AI dataset is meant to answer. Scored 2; crediting known_limitations at 3 would score a field this question does not name.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10 of 14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; title 'CHoRUS Dataset'; description (~1,450 chars); keywords (13); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (controlled access + signed licensing agreement); page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (7 entries, 6 with affiliations); purposes (4 responses); instances (6 instance types with counts 50000 / 1600000000 / 7642); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (4 of 14): doi, resources, parent_datasets, variables. 10/14 = 71% of the enumerated mandatory fields carry meaningful content, landing squarely on the 70% band. The populated fields are substantive rather than token-filled. The four absences are not equally weighted in practice: doi is the consequential one, and variables is a real gap for a 1.6-billion-row OMOP release where no variable-level documentation is offered beyond modality-level narrative. Field presence and field meaning agree throughout the populated set; no placeholder or self-referential filler. The one semantic defect is that id and page hold the identical project-homepage URL, so the record technically populates id while providing no dataset-level identifier — presence without identifying function. Counted as present for the proportion but penalized at Q6/Q16/Q13.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is roughly 1,450 characters and carries specific figures (14 contributing hospitals from a network of 20 academic centers, 50,000 admissions from ICU/PICU/NICU, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb of waveforms, 100,000 anticipated admissions across 9 modalities). purposes holds four responses of roughly 180–260 characters each, e.g. 'Generate data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response...' and 'Provision a holdout test set accessible for model external validation...'. Far above the 200-character threshold, and the length is carrying information rather than padding: the description states modality-specific standards, the access model (enclave for OMOP and telemetry, local retention for notes), and the released-versus-anticipated distinction in a single pass. Length here correlates with semantic density rather than diluting it — nearly every clause is a checkable factual claim, and the claims agree with instances, file_collections and distribution_formats elsewhere in the record. The description also correctly hedges the holdout test set as an award-abstract statement rather than a released artifact.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 13 unique keywords: critical care; intensive care; acute illness; electronic health records; OMOP Common Data Model; waveform telemetry; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; multimodal clinical data; Bridge2AI; AI-ready dataset; social determinants of health. Comfortably above the 8-keyword threshold with no duplicates or near-duplicates beyond the acceptable 'critical care'/'intensive care' pair, and the set spans three useful axes: clinical domain, data modality, and program/standard. Keywords are semantically faithful to the content: every modality keyword (waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, medical imaging, clinical notes) maps to an actual file_collection, and 'OMOP Common Data Model' maps to conforms_to_standard. 'social determinants of health' is the one keyword whose backing is thin — SDOH appears only in sensitive_elements and participant_privacy.notes, with no SDOH variables or collection described, so it slightly oversells coverage. The 'Bridge2AI' and program-affiliation signals are drawn from keywords and funders as permitted.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 5 entries: OMOP Common Data Model; OHNLP; DICOM; WFDB; EDF+ and Persyst. file_collections enumerates 5 matching collections with ids (#collection-omop, #collection-waveform-telemetry, #collection-imaging, #collection-clinical-notes, #collection-eeg), each with collection_type 'processed_data' and its own conforms_to. total_file_count is absent. Five distinct formats, well past the >3 band, and each is documented with its access posture and metadata-publication status rather than merely named.
