Content accuracy: two of the three counts are qualified in the record itself — 50000 is disputed by a 45K webinar figure, and 1600000000 is the record's own expansion of a rounded '1.6 Billion' claim. Pass/fail is unaffected since meaningful numeric metadata is present, but the precision implied by the serialized integers exceeds source support (raised as separate issues).

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/' (identical string). doi: absent. rrid: absent. publisher: absent (created_by 'CHoRUS Consortium' and data_governance.accountable_organization 'Massachusetts General Hospital' are the nearest equivalents). Additional links: extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'. Passes on the stated fail condition ('No persistent ID or link') because a resolvable project link exists — but this is the weakest possible pass. There is no DOI, ARK, Handle or RRID, and the id is a duplicate of the landing-page URL rather than an independent identifier. Correctness: DOI format validation is not_present, not invalid — there is nothing to validate. Semantic understanding: id and page holding the same project-homepage string means the record has no dataset-level identifier distinct from the organization's website, so a citation to this dataset cannot distinguish it from the project. This binary pass materially overstates identification quality; the deficiency is carried into Q13 (sustainability) and Q19 (provenance anchoring) where it is scored rather than thresholded.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grants[0].grant_number 'OT2OD032701' with notes 'project number for the funded application is 1OT2OD032701-01, NIH application ID 10472824. Award amount 5,880,300 US dollars for fiscal year 2022; project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The awardee organization is Massachusetts General Hospital.' Plus the NIH disclaimer in funders.notes. creators: six named leaders each with affiliations — Eric S. Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University). Meets the top band on both limbs and exceeds the minimum: grant number, application number, application ID, award amount, project period, awardee organization, funder disclaimer, and six creators each with an institution and a stable id URI. Correctness: OT2OD032701 validates against the NIH pattern — OT2 is a legitimate Other Transactions activity code, OD correctly denotes the Office of the Director which administers the Common Fund, and the 1OT2OD032701-01 expansion is the correct application form of the core number. Consistency: the awardee organization (MGH) matches the PI's affiliation and data_governance.accountable_organization; funders align with purposes, which restate Bridge2AI's stated goals of ethically sourced AI-ready data. Semantic caveat noted and not penalized: source_caveats explains that all six leaders are carried under principal_investigator because it is the only person-valued field the Creator class declares, so the role assignment is a schema artifact, not a claim that all six hold the award — only Rosenthal is independently attested.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true, with regulatory_compliance ('establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape') and special_populations (PICU and NICU patients). is_deidentified.method ('Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; unstructured EHR text is tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit...') with deidentification_details. participant_privacy.anonymization_method and .privacy_techniques ('Local retention of clinical note text at contributing sites, with only tokens shared. Controlled access to all modalities within a cloud enclave.'). at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included true. ethical_reviews (two entries: community-facing ethics focus groups; community-perspective evaluation of clinical care AI). sensitive_elements and confidential_elements both populated. Absent: informed_consent (no field); participant_compensation; data_protection_impacts; participant_privacy.reidentification_risk; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact; and no named IRB or approval number (human_subject_research.source_caveats: 'The bundle does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the dataset.'). Roughly half the twelve ethics fields carry content, and the content present is genuine rather than boilerplate — the tokenization-and-local-retention architecture is a real, specific privacy control. But the 3 band is defined as IRB plus deidentification, and here the IRB limb fails outright: no review board, no approval number, and the ethical_reviews entries describe community engagement rather than regulatory review. Deidentification is documented but unspecified as to standard. For a dataset of 50,000 critical-care admissions including neonates, the simultaneous absence of IRB identification, any consent or waiver documentation, and any HIPAA determination is a serious deficiency that caps this well below the top bands. Scored 3 rather than 2 because deidentification, privacy techniques, at-risk identification, sensitive/confidential element declarations and ethics-activity documentation are all substantively present; scored no higher because the three load-bearing regulatory elements are all missing. Four consistency failures were detected here and are recorded in issues_detected: involves_human_subjects=true without IRB; involves_human_subjects=true without informed_consent or a documented waiver; is_deidentified without reidentification_risk or a named standard; and PHI-derived restricted data without a HIPAA determination. A fifth, medium-severity concern is method appropriateness: geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss appears under preprocessing_strategies and increases re-identification risk, with no offsetting protection recorded in participant_privacy. A sixth: at_risk_groups_included=true with no assent or guardian-permission procedures. These semantic failures, not mere field absence, are what hold the score at 3 — the record's own source_caveats correctly flag several of them, which is good documentation practice but does not substitute for the missing protections.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Access to the dataset is controlled. Participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset.' regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: 'restricted'. regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'All nine documented data types are marked as controlled for access control, and access requires a signed licensing agreement and an institutional (".edu") email address. Data are worked with inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files.' data_governance.accountable_organization 'Massachusetts General Hospital' and a detailed access_review_process naming contacts dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org, the registration flow, the .edu requirement and compute provisioning. license_and_use_terms.notes distinguishes MIT/Apache-2.0 software licensing from the clinical dataset. Absent: ip_restrictions; data_protection_impacts; hipaa_compliant; other_compliance; governance_committee_contact. All three elements of the top band are nominally present — access terms, restrictions and a confidentiality classification — and the governance narrative goes further than most, naming an accountable organization, two access contacts, the credential requirement and the enclave model. Held at 4 rather than 5 because the licence instrument governing the data is never named or reproduced (the record's own source_caveats concede this), no regulatory compliance determination is recorded, and data_governance.source_caveats notes there is no named access committee, decision timeframe or appeal process. A prospective user learns whom to email but not the terms they would be agreeing to. Content accuracy: the restrictiveness of the access terms is well aligned with the sensitivity declarations — sensitive_elements and confidential_elements both true, confidentiality_level 'restricted', all nine modalities controlled, analysis-in-place in an enclave. That alignment is a genuine consistency pass. The residual inconsistency, recorded as an issue, is scope: the only licence described is embedded in a training-programme registration form, while third_party_sharing.is_shared=true implies a general sharing route whose terms are undocumented. The MIT/Apache-2.0 note is correctly scoped to software and explicitly disclaimed as covering the clinical dataset, which avoids a common licence-conflation error.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to (prose): structured EHR standardized to OMOP CDM 'with published OMOP-schema metadata and OMOP schema extensions for nursing flowsheets'; notes follow 'the OHNLP open-source schema'; imaging 'the DICOM schema'; telemetry 'WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema'; EEG 'the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas'. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. distribution_formats: five standard formats. Integration: preprocessing_strategies cites 'validated semantic mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository'; collection_mechanisms cites 'the OHDSI tool stack'; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC ontology codes. Absent: related_datasets (no typed relationships); no common cross-dataset linking identifier. Two of the three top-band elements are exemplary. Standard formats are correct per substrate; schema conformance is stated at a level of detail (named extensions, named schema URIs) that is rare in these records. Integration capability across the 14 contributing hospitals is real and operationalized — OMOP CDM plus validated semantic mappings plus the OHDSI tool stack is precisely a harmonization procedure, and the ontology-coded instances support machine interpretation. Held at 4 because the question also calls for cross-platform dataset linkages with typed relationships: related_datasets is empty, no common identifier for linking to other datasets is described, and the record's own source_caveats confirm that although CHoRUS collaborates with three sibling Bridge2AI projects, no dataset relationship is recorded. Secondary drag: metadata publication was only 'planned' for notes, imaging and EEG, so schema conformance is asserted but not yet realized for a third of the modalities. Correctness: every named standard is real and correctly matched to its substrate; the w3id.org schema URI is well formed. Consistency: conforms_to prose, conforms_to_standard enums and distribution_formats agree with each other modality by modality — a clean three-way check. Semantic caution: interoperability is documented as harmonization *into* the enclave rather than interoperability *out of* it, since no files are distributed; combined with the absent related_datasets this means the dataset is internally harmonized but externally unlinked, which is what separates 4 from 5 here.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (five entries): OMOP standardization with validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping; OHNLP-toolkit extraction and tokenization; 'Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, including de-identification of imaging'; WFDB conversion 'using the waveform conversion scripts'; 'Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using the open source UF-Geocoding code'. cleaning_strategies: 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, and site status tracking is used to identify and resolve blocking issues'. labeling_strategies: annotation environment (future tense) with data_annotation_protocol 'Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping and validation under a clinical validation SOP'. machine_annotation_tools: tools ['OHNLP toolkit'] with tool_descriptions. missing_data_documentation: detailed patterns and causes. Named tools overall: OHNLP toolkit, OHDSI tool stack, DeGauss, chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-container-apps, privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid, UF-Geocoding, CHoRUSReports, Azure. Absent: annotation_analyses; imputation_protocols; any version number. Five of seven fields populated, with strategies documented per modality rather than generically, and roughly a dozen named tools with an organization-level URL (https://github.com/chorus-ai) plus a stated package status page tracking 'versions, maintainers and other package metadata'. That is strong transparency. Held at 4 because the top band requires software versions or URLs at tool granularity: not a single version number appears anywhere, individual repositories are named in prose without their own URLs, and imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses are absent entirely — so a reader cannot reproduce the pipeline as configured. Consistency pass: the preprocessing tools map coherently onto the declared outputs — OHNLP tokenization produces the OHNLP-schema tokens in distribution_formats, and the waveform conversion scripts produce the WFDB format. Consistency gap carried to the issues list: privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid are listed as existing repositories, but is_deidentified.source_caveats explicitly states the bundle does not say either was applied to the released data — so a de-identification tool is named without a verified link to the artifact it supposedly processed. Semantic caution: labeling_strategies is written in the future tense and its own source_caveats confirm 'the bundle does not report labels present in the released data', so the labeling limb describes intent rather than a realized pipeline.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: 'Retrospective collection: clinical data generated during routine care are extracted at contributing hospitals, standardized, tokenized, stored, visualized and labeled through a multi-center network, then delivered as a CHoRUS data extract to the shared cloud enclave.' collection_mechanisms: six entries, one per modality plus site tooling (OMOP extraction via the OHDSI tool stack; OHNLP tokenization with text remaining on site; PACS retrieval in DICOM; telemetry capture via gateway/middleware converted to WFDB; EEG as EDF+/Persyst; chorus-extract-upload and dockerized container apps on Azure). data_collectors: two entries — 'Fourteen data acquisition centers, drawn from a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers... Site data managers follow the step-by-step extraction and contribution workflow documented in the Chorus_SOP repository' (role: Data contributing sites) and consortium sub-teams for Standards, Data Acquisition and Tooling. raw_data_sources: five typed sources with native formats and access details. direct_collection.is_direct false with rationale. sampling_strategies present. collection_timeframes: 'Data collection is retrospective. As of August 2025 the assembled dataset covered 14 different hospitals. The funded project period runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not state the calendar range of the clinical encounters represented in the data'. All five fields populated, and the methods and collectors limbs are as detailed as this rubric's top band asks for — per-modality mechanisms, named SOP repository, named tooling, typed source systems, and an explicit statement that collection was not direct. The timeframes limb, however, does not deliver a data collection timeframe: what is recorded is the award period and an August 2025 status snapshot, not the calendar range of the ICU admissions represented. For a retrospective EHR dataset the encounter date range is load-bearing — it determines comparability of coding practice, care protocols and any COVID-era effects — so its absence is a substantive reusability gap, not a formality. Scored 4: two of three top-band limbs fully met, the third only nominally. Consistency pass: collection_mechanisms and raw_data_sources agree modality by modality on origin system and native format, and both agree with distribution_formats on the resulting format. The '14 hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers' figure is stated consistently in data_collectors, known_limitations and description. Semantic caution: sampling_strategies asserts 'sampling methods intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort' while its own notes concede the bundle 'does not describe the sampling frame or selection criteria in operational detail' — so the selection mechanism that determines which of a hospital's ICU admissions entered the 50,000 is undocumented, which compounds the timeframe gap and is directly relevant to the selection bias not documented under Q20.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.update_details 'The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process, and metadata publication for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was planned', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not state an update frequency or a versioning policy.' maintainers: three entries — Ciera McCrary, Program Manager, MGH; access contacts at Emory and Tufts Medicine; and the chorus-ai organization maintaining 28 repositories with 'versions, maintainers and other package metadata... tracked on a package status page'. status describes the release state and the award period. Absent: version; version_access; errata; doi; publisher. Well below the 3 band, which requires a version number plus basic access info plus a persistent ID — of those three, only access info exists. Against the four sustainability criteria: (1) persistent identifier — absent; (2) long-term governance plan — partial only, via data_governance's accountable organization and access process, with no preservation commitment; (3) domain-appropriate repository — no; the holding is a project cloud enclave, not a persistent domain repository such as PhysioNet, notwithstanding that the waveform schema derives from PhysioNet; (4) institutional commitment — partial, limited to the OT2OD032701 award period ending 2026-11-30 with nothing stated beyond it. Scored 2 rather than 0 because maintainers are named with working roles and contacts, a substantive forward-looking update plan exists, and package-level version tracking is at least asserted for the software; scored no higher because a dataset that is actively changing — 50,000 now, 100,000 anticipated, three modalities incomplete — with no version identifier and no DOI cannot be cited reproducibly at all. This is the sharpest sustainability exposure in the record, and two independent signals compound it. First, the award period ends 2026-11-30 with no stated successor arrangement for hosting or preservation. Second, the record faithfully captures a site-wide banner in notes: 'This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' (typo as printed on the source site), which is an explicit governance-continuity risk sitting alongside an absent preservation plan. Consistency: the record does not overclaim — updates.source_caveats concedes the missing versioning policy rather than inventing one, which is honest documentation of a genuine deficiency.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources holds nine entries, of which the distinct references include: the CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/); the chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai, 28 repositories); Chorus_SOP (centralized SOP documentation site with interactive workflow diagram); chorus-mapping; chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources; chorus-extract-upload and chorus-container-apps; privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid and UF-Geocoding; CHoRUSReports; and the Bridge2AI project page (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) plus the AIM-AHEAD call for applications. citation: absent. doi: absent. existing_uses notes only that 'As of August 2025, the datasets are being used for training activities and publications' without naming any publication. Well past the two-distinct-references threshold — there are at least nine distinct non-publication references, all genuinely distinct resources rather than repeated links to the same target. But the 5 band additionally requires a formal citation for this dataset, and none exists: there is no citation field, no dataset DOI, and no entry that identifies the dataset by title together with its authors or publishing organization in citable form. Per the Q14 rule this is exactly the documented case of multiple non-publication resources without a formal citation, which earns 3. No peer-reviewed publication is cited either, despite existing_uses alluding to publications in the abstract. Correctness: URLs are mostly well formed; 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' is recorded without a scheme and several named repositories (Chorus_SOP, chorus-mapping, CHoRUSReports) appear in prose without individual URLs, so they resolve only by navigating the organization page. Consistency: the absence of a citation is coherent with the absence of a DOI — the record has no citable identifier to cite with, so Q14's ceiling here is a direct downstream consequence of the Q6/Q13 identifier gap rather than an independent omission.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 'Patient admission from an intensive care unit (ICU), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)', counts 50000; a 'Demographics record' modality standardized to OMOP; 7,642 admissions with radiology data. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true, identification 'Released admissions are identified by care setting as adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) admissions', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not report the distribution of admissions across these settings.' at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included true (minors via PICU/NICU). splits: holdout intention, size and composition unstated. missing_data_documentation: uneven modality coverage. sampling_strategies: aim of 'a balanced and diverse cohort'. Above the 3 floor in that subgroups are identified at all — care setting, and by implication a pediatric and neonatal population — and the at-risk flag is derived from the data rather than asserted. But the top band requires detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria, and neither exists: no age, sex, race, ethnicity or payer distributions are reported even though a demographics modality is part of the dataset; the split across ICU/PICU/NICU is explicitly unreported; and no inclusion or exclusion criteria for admissions are stated anywhere. A reader cannot assess whether the cohort is representative of the population they intend to deploy a model on. Consistency pass: PICU/NICU appear coherently across subpopulations, human_subject_research.special_populations and at_risk_populations, so the vulnerable-population identification is internally sound. Semantic gap with direct downstream effect: the record contains a demographics modality and keywords 'social determinants of health', and sampling_strategies claims an aim of a diverse cohort — yet no demographic characterization is reported, so the diversity claim is unverifiable from the datasheet. That unverifiability is the same deficiency that makes the Q20 fairness analysis impossible, and the two should be remedied together.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; external_resources also cite 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' and 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'. download_url and doi absent. Passes on the stated criterion of at least one external URL — several are present, structurally sound and on plausible domains, and the w3id.org URI is itself a persistent-identifier service. Correctness: one URL is schemeless ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus') and several named repositories lack individual URLs, hence the some_invalid url_validity flag; these do not defeat the pass. Semantic caution worth recording: none of these links is a persistent identifier for the dataset itself — they point at a project website, a code organization and a schema. 'Findable' is satisfied here in the weak sense of reachable-today, not in the FAIR sense of a globally unique persistent identifier, which the binary criterion cannot distinguish and which Q6, Q13 and Q19 penalize instead.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms: controlled access; signing a licensing agreement in the registration form is a precondition. data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access requests are directed to named CHoRUS contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org). For the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form giving name, email and institution and sign the licensing agreement included in that form; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant. A ".edu" email address is required.' third_party_sharing: Cohort 2 runs 2025-11-17 to 2026-07-31 for up to 30 trainees working 'on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud'. regulatory_restrictions: analysis inside a cloud enclave, not file distribution. distribution_formats: five in-enclave formats. download_url absent. The three components of a fully defined access path are each partly present: platform (the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud, Azure-hosted enclave), login/credential gate (institutional .edu email plus signed licensing agreement, with provisioning confirmation by email), and policy (controlled access across all nine modalities). For the training-programme route this is genuinely actionable — a reader knows what to do. Held at 4 because the general route is only 'email one of two people': no application portal, no DUA document, no eligibility criteria outside the programme, and data_governance.source_caveats confirms no access committee, no decision timeframe and no appeal process. The formats also cannot be obtained as files at all, which the distribution_formats listing does not itself convey. Consistency pass: the access mechanism is coherent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', with all modalities marked controlled, and with the absence of a download_url — the record does not claim downloadability anywhere. Consistency gap raised as an issue: license_and_use_terms describes terms only for training-programme participants while third_party_sharing asserts general availability, so the terms attaching to the general route are undocumented. Semantic note: the enclave model is appropriate for PHI-derived critical-care data, so the restriction is well matched to the sensitivity — the deduction concerns documentation completeness, not excessive restriction.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: intended_uses: three categories with examples and usage_notes — 'Clinical AI/ML model development' (characterizing critical illness, predicting complications and deterioration, measuring treatment response); 'External validation of clinical AI models' (evaluating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset); 'Workforce training and AI literacy' (trainee research on the Collaborative Cloud, canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP workshops, clinical deep learning exercises). future_use_impacts: three entries covering marketplace adoption via the holdout set; 'privacy, accountability and clinical benefit as conditions on future use, with patient-focused work determining the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'; and community ethics focus groups determining 'what data is appropriate for public sharing, so the shareable scope of future releases depends on those findings'. license_and_use_terms present but the dataset licence is unnamed. Absent: prohibited_uses; discouraged_uses. Three of five named fields populated, two of them well. intended_uses is genuinely comprehensive — three distinct categories, each with concrete examples and a usage note — and future_use_impacts contains real social-impact reasoning rather than a platitude, notably the point that community consultation determines the shareable scope of future releases. But the top band needs comprehensive use guidance plus a social impact analysis with mitigation strategies, and two limbs fail: prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are entirely absent, so the boundaries of acceptable use are nowhere stated for a restricted dataset of critically ill patients' records including neonates; and no mitigation strategies are articulated as such — the enclave and tokenization function as controls but are never presented as risk mitigations tied to identified risks. The licence limb is also weak, since license_and_use_terms.source_caveats concedes no data use licence is named. Scored strictly against the five named fields, as the rubric directs. Adjacent content exists elsewhere and was noted but not credited here: known_limitations records that 'analyses requiring full note text cannot be performed on the shared data', which is a de facto use limitation, and regulatory_restrictions confines work to the enclave. Their placement outside Q18's fields means a consumer reading the use-guidance block alone would find no statement of what must not be done — for example, no prohibition on re-identification attempts, on linkage to external identified data, or on clinical deployment without prospective validation, all of which are standard for a dataset of this type. The gap is one of guidance, not of intent: the record's ethics narrative is plainly protective.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Present: raw_data_sources — five typed origin systems with native formats ('Structured electronic health record systems at 14 data contributing hospitals'; unstructured notes; 'Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS)' in DICOM; 'Bedside physiologic monitors and their gateway/middleware'; 'Hospital EEG databases' as EDF+/Persyst). updates.update_details (expansion plan). missing_data_documentation with both missing_data_patterns and missing_data_causes. splits (holdout intention, composition unstated). Quality control via cleaning_strategies: 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions'. Absent: version_access; errata; was_derived_from; parent_datasets. An unusual profile: lineage is strong where versioning is absent. Read across raw_data_sources → acquisition_methods → collection_mechanisms → preprocessing_strategies → cleaning_strategies → distribution_formats, the record does supply entities (source systems, site extracts, the enclave holdings), activities (extraction, OMOP mapping, OHNLP tokenization, WFDB conversion, de-identification, DeGauss geocoding) and agents (14 acquisition centers, site data managers, Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams) — which is the textual form of provenance the question expressly permits. What prevents a higher score is that this lineage is not anchored to any identified released artifact: there is no version, no version_access, no errata, no was_derived_from and no parent_datasets, so derivation paths terminate in an unversioned, unidentified 'current release'. Equally, the 3 band's own descriptor — version history — is itself not met, since no version number or erratum exists. Scored 3 as the balance of a well-documented process lineage against an absent integrity and versioning layer. Consistency pass: the lineage is internally coherent at every hop — each raw source's native format matches the mechanism that extracts it and the preprocessing that transforms it into the stated output format. Quality signals are real: CHoRUSReports characterization returned to sites is a genuine data-quality feedback loop, and missing_data_documentation distinguishes data availability from metadata publication per modality, which is precisely the integrity information an AI/ML user needs. Structural gap: was_derived_from is unpopulated even though raw_data_sources contains exactly the derivation content it would carry, so the provenance is human-readable but not machine-traversable. Compounding issue already raised: with no DOI and no version, no analysis performed on this data can be pinned to a reproducible state of it.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: absent entirely. future_use_impacts contains one bias-adjacent clause: 'patient-focused work determining the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. Related content sits outside Q20's named fields — known_limitations includes a representativeness_limitation ('Data come from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers and cover acute and critical care admissions only, so the population is not a general hospital or general population sample') and two coverage_limitations on incomplete imaging and EEG; sampling_strategies states an aim of 'a balanced and diverse cohort'. No bias is typed, no BiasTypeEnum or AIO mapping appears, and no fairness analysis across any subgroup is reported. Above zero because bias is named as an object of management in future_use_impacts and because the record does acknowledge representativeness constraints, but well short of the 3 band, which requires basic bias identification: no bias is actually identified as a bias in the designated field. This is the record's weakest area relative to its own framing — the dataset is titled '...for Equitable AI', carries 'social determinants of health' as a keyword, and is explicitly intended for clinical AI model development and marketplace adoption, all of which raise the expected standard for bias documentation rather than lowering it. The obvious candidates are all documentable from material already in the record: selection bias from 14 academic critical-care centers; measurement bias across heterogeneous site EHR instrumentation and monitor vendors; and differential missingness, which missing_data_documentation already quantifies qualitatively across modalities. Completeness issue of high severity, recorded in issues_detected. The gap also interacts with Q15: because no demographic distribution is reported and the ICU/PICU/NICU split is explicitly unreported, a fairness analysis could not be substantiated even if attempted — the two deficiencies are causally linked. Consistency note: nothing here is inconsistent, and the record does not overclaim fairness; it simply omits the analysis. Scoring was driven by the named fields (known_biases, future_use_impacts) as the rubric directs, with the known_limitations content acknowledged as mitigating but not sufficient to reach the 3 band.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,900 chars); keywords (27); license_and_use_terms (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with full terms and contact); doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/'; creators (45 with affiliations, most with ORCIDs); purposes (4); instances (3 typed with B2AI_SUBSTRATE/B2AI_TOPIC terms). Absent: variables; parent_datasets; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level; resources. Partial proxies: 7 'subsets' entries and 10 'file_collections' stand in for resources; four 'is_new_version_of' related_datasets stand in for parent_datasets. Ten of fourteen listed fields are strictly populated (71%); crediting subsets/file_collections as the resource decomposition and the typed is_new_version_of links as parent lineage raises the effective count to twelve of fourteen (86%). Populated fields are substantive rather than token, so the record sits above the 70% band but short of 90% because variables and the confidentiality classification are genuinely missing. The populated fields are mutually coherent — id, doi and version_access.latest_version_doi all resolve to the same Dataverse deposit, and publisher ROR matches the DOI prefix registrant. The gaps are not arbitrary: variables is empty because the release ships ZIP archives whose internal tables are not enumerated, which is the same root cause as the Q4 format-variety limitation.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is ~1,900 characters and names modalities, cell lines, treatment conditions, packaging format and the nine partner institutions. The four purposes entries run ~200–330 characters each, e.g. 'To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders…'. Both narrative slots far exceed the 200-character threshold, and the length carries information rather than padding: the description enumerates which modality covers which cell system and condition. Narrative content is semantically appropriate to the claimed dataset type — a multi-modal functional-genomics resource — and the description's scope statement matches the modality breakdown later given in subsets and file_collections, with no length-inflating restatement of boilerplate.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 27 unique keywords spanning assay terms (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, single-cell RNA sequencing, size exclusion chromatography, mass spectroscopy, subcellular imaging), biological entities (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, iPSC, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte, protein-protein interaction, protein localization), perturbagens (paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPR/Cas9) and program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI, AI, machine learning). Well above the eight-keyword threshold, with no duplicates and with abbreviation/expansion pairs (AP-MS / affinity purification; NPC / neural progenitor cell) that genuinely aid retrieval. Keywords are semantically accurate for the content: every assay named in keywords has a corresponding acquisition_methods entry and file collection, and no keyword claims a modality the release does not contain. Program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is inferred here from quoted keyword values and the ROR publisher, not from the filename.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists two entries: 'ZIP Archive' (media_type application/zip, access_urls to the UVA Dataverse deposit) and 'RO-Crate' (packaging with provenance graphs via FAIRSCAPE). total_file_count: 10, with all ten file_collections enumerated by name, path, compression 'zip', collection_type (raw_data / processed_data / metadata), human-readable size and MD5. File enumeration is excellent — every archive is individually named, typed and checksummed — but format variety at the distribution layer is limited to one container plus one packaging convention. The payload media types (confocal microscopy images, mass-spectrometry outputs, sequence data) are described in prose but never declared as formats, so a consumer cannot tell from the metadata what they will find inside each archive. The multi-modality asserted in description and keywords is real at the content level but is not expressed in the format metadata, so format variety understates the dataset. This is a presentation gap rather than a contradiction; scoring follows the declared formats, as the rubric's file-type band requires.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: Per-archive sizes in file_collections descriptions: 4.6 GB (untreated IF images), 4.2 GB (vorinostat IF), 3.8 GB (paclitaxel IF), 1.1 MB (release metadata), 171.8 KB, 135.8 KB, 113.3 KB, 93.9 KB, 73.3 KB, 30.2 KB. total_file_count: 10. Dimensional counts: 464 proteins of interest imaged per MDA-MB-468 condition; 11,739 targeted genes in the CRISPRi atlas; 7 subsets flagged is_subpopulation: true. Passes on both limbs — numeric sizes for every distributed file and numeric instance dimensions for the imaging and perturbation components. Sizes are plausible for the modalities: multi-gigabyte archives for four-channel confocal image sets, kilobyte-scale archives for processed mass-spectrometry and atlas tables. source_caveats correctly flags that total_size_bytes is omitted because exact byte counts are not in the source; the pass rests on stated values, with the machine-readability gap recorded as a separate low-severity issue. The record also states honestly that the number of profiled cells is not given.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; publisher: ROR:0153tk833; distribution access URL https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C. Clear pass: a registered DOI, a resolvable Dataverse landing page, a project portal page, and a ROR-identified publishing organization. Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse registrant and matches publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu access URL — the identifier, the platform and the institution corroborate one another rather than merely coexisting.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: Three funders: NIH award '1OT2OD032742-01, "Bridge2AI: Cell Maps for AI (CM4AI) Data Generation Project"' with RePORTER core project OT2OD032742, application ID 11211616, PI Trey Ideker, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 and FY2025 award amount 5,289,382; NIH award 5U54HG012513-02 (Bridge2AI Bridge Center); and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia. 45 creators, each with at least one affiliation and most with ORCID iDs, plus an explicit principal_investigator annotation for Trey Ideker. Top band: award numbers, award title, administering PI, project period and an award amount are all present, and creator affiliations are complete. Only the packaging is imperfect — award numbers sit in free-text notes rather than a structured award-number slot. Grant syntax validates: 1OT2OD032742-01 parses as NIH application type 1, activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742, support year 01; 5U54HG012513-02 parses as type 5, U54 center award, NHGRI. The funding also aligns with purposes — a data-generation award matched by purposes describing AI-ready data delivery. One minor tension is recorded separately: the stated project end (November 2026) postdates the funder project period end (2026-08-31).

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: two entries — an Ethics Module review covering 'ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets', contact Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org), and a second contact Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca). human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false, with notes recording 'Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No' and ethical sourcing of MDA-MB-468 from ATCC and KOLF2.1J from HipSci 'available for access by not-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA'. is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false with rationale that the data 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'. confidential_elements and sensitive_elements both present: false with narrative. data_governance names the CM4AI Data Access Committee, its contact, its access review process and stewardship roles. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: not_applicable. Absent: informed_consent, participant_privacy, participant_compensation, at_risk_populations, data_protection_impacts. For an in vitro dataset the documentation is substantive — named ethics reviewers with contacts, an explicit non-human-subjects determination with supporting provenance of both cell lines, a de-identification rationale, and a standing Data Access Committee with a described review process. The absent participant-protection slots are largely appropriate to the data type, but the top band also requires a data protection impact assessment and an explicit re-identification risk statement, neither of which is present. Cross-field logic is coherent: involves_human_subjects=false is consistent with direct_collection.is_direct=false, with hipaa_compliant=not_applicable, and with the absence of consent and compensation fields. The residual semantic gap is that the release includes donor-derived sequence data (Perturb-seq raw reads in SRA) and discloses donor attributes in sampling_strategies, so the 'cannot be matched to a human subject' claim is asserted for genomic material rather than assessed; that gap is what holds the score at 4 rather than 5.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms gives the full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms ('free to share and adapt… not used for commercial purposes, and contributions are distributed under the same license'), data_use_permission: no_commercial_use, and a named contact (Trey Ideker, tideker@health.ucsd.edu). ip_restrictions: 'Copyright is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; spatial proteomics raw image data is copyright the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University. Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation'. regulatory_restrictions: 'FDA Regulated: No', hipaa_compliant: not_applicable, governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker. data_governance: committee_name 'CM4AI Data Access Committee', access_review_process, stewardship_roles. Confidentiality determination via confidential_elements_present: false and sensitive_elements_present: false with rationale. All three limbs of the top band are met in substance: a fully stated license with a permission code, layered IP restrictions that correctly distinguish the Stanford-held image copyright, regulatory status, a governance committee with a named contact and a described review process, and an explicit non-confidential / non-sensitive classification. Restrictiveness is consistent across fields: a non-commercial license, a matching commercial-use prohibition, and a committee route for dual licensing all point the same direction, with no 'open data' overclaim. The only shortfall is expressive rather than substantive — the confidentiality determination is narrative and the schema's confidentiality_level enum is unset, which is recorded under Q1's completeness gap rather than penalised twice here.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. distribution_formats include RO-Crate packaging 'with provenance graphs and rich metadata… using the FAIRSCAPE framework'. related_datasets carries six typed relationships (four is_new_version_of to prior release DOIs, is_described_by to the CM4AI preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, is_referenced_by to doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734). external_resources link the Cell Mapping Toolkit (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io), FAIRSCAPE (fairscape.github.io), IMP (integrativemodeling.org), and deposits in MassIVE, SRA and Figshare. Ontology/identifier use: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/63, B2AI_TOPIC:12/15/26, ORCID, ROR, RRID:CVCL. Strong on standardization — an explicit packaging standard, a resolvable metadata schema URI, controlled-vocabulary terms on instances, and typed cross-dataset relationships. Held below the top band because integration capability is asserted rather than operationalised: the payload is opaque ZIP archives with unstated internal formats, the external repository deposits carry no accessions, and no common identifier scheme (e.g. UniProt or gene identifiers) is named for joining the imaging, interaction and perturbation modalities. Technical terms are used correctly — RO-Crate is a packaging standard and is described as such, FAIRSCAPE as the framework producing it — and the schema URI is the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema this record itself instantiates, so the conformance claim is self-consistent. A consumer could locate and cite the parts but would still need to open the archives to harmonise across modalities, which is what separates 4 from 5 here.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: four entries covering node2vec dimensionality reduction of PPI networks, a Human Protein Atlas deep-learning model for image embeddings, contrastive co-embedding of the two, and community detection over the co-embedding space. cleaning_strategies: one thin entry — CRISPR screen data 'were reported as undergoing quality control at the time of the CM4AI preprint'. labeling_strategies: alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome plus LLM naming with confidence scores, data_annotation_platform 'Gene Set AI (GSAI) pipeline guiding the GPT-4 model'. machine_annotation_tools: node2vec, DenseNet-121, GPT-4, HiDeF, each with a functional description. Absent: imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation, annotation_analyses; no version numbers or per-tool URLs. Well above the one-strategy floor in volume, but the documentation is aimed at the wrong artifacts: what is described is the downstream MuSIC map-construction pipeline, while known_limitations states the release contains no predicted cell maps. Processing of the data that is actually shipped — MS search and elution-profile handling, image acquisition QC beyond antibody scoring, Perturb-seq alignment and guide calling — is undocumented, and the cleaning entry reports an in-progress state from a preprint rather than what was done. Tool versions and links are absent from the tool entries. This is the clearest semantic issue in the record and it reduced the score from 4 to 3: the tools named are real, correctly described and correctly attributed to their roles, but they operate on a product this release excludes, so a reuser cannot reconstruct how the released files were produced. Antibody-quality scoring 'according to a standard Human Protein Atlas protocol' in acquisition_methods is the one quality control that does attach to released data.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: four entries (SEC-MS for proteome-wide complex mapping; AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines; ICC-IF confocal imaging with the four-channel scheme spelled out — 'Nuclei were stained with DAPI (blue channel); endoplasmic reticulum with a calreticulin antibody (yellow channel); microtubules with tubulin antibody (red channel); and antibody against protein of interest (green channel)', flagged was_validated_verified: true with HPA antibody scoring; single-cell CRISPRi Perturb-seq using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit). collection_mechanisms: four entries naming the performing laboratories and protocol details ('a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9'; 'automated fixation and permeabilization protocols on a pipetting robot'). data_collectors: three entries (Krogan lab UCSF, Lundberg lab Stanford, UCSD) each with role academic_institution. raw_data_sources: two entries with source_type and raw_data_format. collection_timeframes: absent, with source_caveats stating 'No collection start or end date is stated for the underlying experiments'. Methods, reagents, instruments and performing laboratories are all documented at a level that would let a specialist reproduce the assay design; only collection timeframes are missing, and their absence is disclosed rather than concealed. That maps to 4 — the top band explicitly requires methods, collectors and timeframes together. Assay descriptions are technically correct and internally consistent: each modality named in acquisition_methods has a matching collection_mechanism, a named collector, and corresponding file collections, and the lab attributions agree with the copyright split in ip_restrictions (Stanford holding the raw image copyright matches Lundberg-lab image generation). Sampling strategy is candidly described as targeted and non-representative, consistent with the documented representation bias.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '2.0'. version_access.versions_available enumerates the May 2024, March 2025 (v1.4), June 2025 (v2.1) and October 2025 (v2.1) releases and states that 'Version history is maintained in the University of Virginia Dataverse'; latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C. related_datasets gives the DOI of each prior release with relationship_type is_new_version_of. updates: frequency quarterly, 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026'. maintainers: three named with institutions, roles and contact emails (Swathi Thaker, program manager; Zhandos Sembay, website; Trey Ideker, dataset point of contact). retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds'. publisher ROR:0153tk833; distribution_dates record publication dates for this and prior releases. errata: absent. All four sustainability indicators are present — persistent DOIs per version, a governance and maintenance structure, an institutional repository appropriate to the data, and an explicit institutional funding commitment for preservation — which is more than most records supply. Held at 4 by the version-numbering contradiction (a 2026 release labelled 2.0 behind 2.1 predecessors) and by the absence of any errata slot for a release explicitly marked Beta with embargoed components. The maintenance narrative is temporally coherent apart from the version string: quarterly updates, a stated project end, superseded releases linked by typed relationships, and an update commitment consistent with the Beta status and the embargo note. The version inconsistency is a genuine consistency failure rather than a formatting quibble, because version_access is precisely the field a consumer would use to pick the current release.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: a complete formal dataset citation naming 45 authors, the title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)', the year 2026, the DOI https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, the publishing organization 'University of Virginia Dataverse' and the deposit version 'V2'. Distinct additional references: the CM4AI preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (is_described_by), the Perturbation Cell Atlas preprint doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (is_referenced_by), four prior-release DOIs, and non-publication resources including the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository and documentation, FAIRSCAPE, and IMP. Meets the top band unambiguously: the dataset citation identifies the dataset by title, authors and publishing organization, and at least two further distinct references with DOIs are documented. Counted once per resource, the record supplies far more than the two-reference minimum. DOI syntax validates throughout — 10.18130 (UVA Dataverse) for the dataset and its predecessors, 10.1101 (bioRxiv) for the two preprints — and the relationship types are used correctly, with is_described_by reserved for the methods preprint rather than conflated with is_new_version_of. The citation's author list matches the creators block.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: direct_collection.is_direct: false — 'Data were not collected from human subjects. All data were generated in vitro from commercially available, de-identified human cell lines: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), available from ATCC, and KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3)'. sampling_strategies.source_data gives donor-level attributes: 'MDA-MB-468 is a triple negative breast cancer cell line established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma. KOLF2.1J iPSCs were derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.' subpopulations: one entry identifying cell type and treatment condition with a distribution statement; subsets: seven entries with is_subpopulation: true covering the three MDA-MB-468 conditions and the four KOLF2.1J states. instances: three typed entries with counts (464 proteins imaged per condition; 11,739 targeted genes). known_biases records that the lines 'do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'. Absent: at_risk_populations, missing_data_documentation. The record supplies essentially all the human-provenance information that exists for an in vitro dataset — donor age, sex, ancestry and disease state for both source lines, cell-line RRIDs, a fully enumerated subgroup structure, and an explicit representation caveat. It falls short of the top band because inclusion/exclusion criteria and demographic distributions are not meaningful for two donors, so the evidence cannot reach 'detailed demographics'. Scoring here reflects donor-provenance documentation rather than participant demographics, and the frame fits the data type poorly — flagged explicitly so the score is not read as a claim about human-participant characterisation. The subgroup structure is semantically consistent across subsets, subpopulations.distribution and file_collections, with the same seven cell-state/treatment combinations appearing in each.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C and id doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; page https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; distribution access URL https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; external_resources URLs https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, http://integrativemodeling.org; four prior-release DOIs and two preprint DOIs. Comfortable pass on both the identifier and the external-link limbs, with the DOI resolvable to a specific versioned deposit rather than a generic project page. URL structures are well formed and the domains are plausible and consistent with the named organizations. The one findability shortfall is on the external raw deposits — MassIVE, SRA and Figshare are named without accessions — which is recorded as a separate issue and reflected in Q10 rather than overturning this pass.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats notes: 'All ten files in the June 2026 release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Individual files below the download size limit may be downloaded directly; the Data Access API is available for programmatic access', with access_urls to the Dataverse deposit. license_and_use_terms sets CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with attribution and non-commercial conditions and a named contact for commercial licensing. known_limitations and external_resources record that some Perturb-seq data are 'under temporary pre-publication embargo'. No download_url field is populated. Platform, container format, both interactive and programmatic retrieval routes, licence conditions and embargo caveats are all documented — clearly beyond a partial description. Short of the top band because the access tier is never stated in the terms the rubric asks for (no authentication? registration? no DUA?), and because a direct download endpoint is not given, leaving the multi-gigabyte image archives' retrieval path partly implicit in the 'download size limit' remark. The access description is consistent with the licence: a permissive non-commercial licence with no DUA mentioned implies open retrieval, and the record avoids the common overclaim of calling this 'public' or 'unrestricted'. The embargo disclosure is a point of accuracy — it tells a reuser that part of the advertised scope is not yet obtainable.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms with attribution requirements and a commercial-licensing contact. intended_uses: five categorised entries (AI-ready research data; AI model training; cellular process analysis; perturbation and disease-context analysis; bioinformatics analysis of component datasets, with the honest note that 'The current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets, as computed cell maps are not included'). prohibited_uses: two entries — no clinical decision-making or patient care 'without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', and no commercial use without separate licensing. discouraged_uses: two entries — use without domain expertise, and use as a complete cell-map resource at this interim stage. future_use_impacts: two entries on anticipating applications of derived AI/ML systems, 'integrating them into data governance frameworks to optimize benefits and mitigate potential risks', and an Ethics-team tool suite on ethical, legal and social ramifications. known_limitations: four typed entries, one with a recommended_mitigation. All five slots are populated with specific, non-boilerplate guidance, and the impact analysis names both a risk-mitigation mechanism (governance-framework integration) and a concrete deliverable (ELSI tooling). The intended-use and discouraged-use entries are unusually candid about what this interim release can and cannot support. Guidance is mutually consistent and consistent with the rest of the record: the clinical-use prohibition matches the non-clinical, cell-line nature asserted in sensitive_elements; the commercial prohibition matches the licence code and the Data Access Committee's dual-licensing role; the 'not a complete cell-map resource' discouragement matches the known_limitations scope entry and explains the Q11 preprocessing mismatch from the dataset's own point of view.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: version_access with the full release series and latest_version_doi; updates with quarterly frequency; raw_data_sources: two entries ('Protein-protein interaction networks generated by SEC-MS and AP-MS, downloaded from the Krogan Laboratory's deposition archive'; immunofluorescence images from the Lundberg Laboratory's archive, with raw_data_format). raw_sources: four external deposits (MassIVE for iPSC and cancer-cell MS, SRA via NCBI BioProject, Figshare). Derivation lineage across releases via four is_new_version_of relationships with DOIs. Integrity: MD5 checksums for all ten archives (e.g. 6c1a86520eec2696ec19444eb8a8b428) plus per-file publication dates. Provenance packaging: description states output data are 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework', and file_collections includes cm4ai_release_metadata.zip 'including RO-Crate metadata and provenance graphs'. Absent: errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation, splits/is_data_split. Entity–activity–agent structure is recoverable in substance — entities (raw sources, ten named archives), activities (four acquisition methods and processing steps), agents (three named laboratories, maintainers, creators) — and file-level checksums give real integrity verification. It stays at 4 because the PROV-O graph itself lives inside a packaged metadata archive rather than in the record: no was_derived_from edges connect individual released archives to their raw sources, and errata, missing-data documentation and split indicators are absent. The provenance claim is credible and consistently expressed — FAIRSCAPE/RO-Crate is the right vehicle, and the release metadata archive is actually enumerated with a size and checksum rather than merely alluded to. What a consumer cannot do from this record alone is trace a specific archive to its specific raw deposit, since the raw deposits lack accessions; that combination of an asserted graph plus unresolvable endpoints is what separates this from the top band.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: one entry with bias_type 'representation_bias', description 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', and affected_subsets naming all data in the release across MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J derivatives. Supporting material: sampling_strategies.is_representative: false with why_not_representative; known_limitations coverage_limitation noting that 'SEC-MS, IF imaging, and CRISPRi Perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'; future_use_impacts on governance-framework integration and ELSI tooling. Above the untaxonomised band: the single bias is typed with a BiasTypeEnum-style term, scoped to affected subsets, and corroborated by an explicit non-representativeness flag in sampling_strategies. Short of the top band because only one bias category is recorded, there is no AIO/CROISSANT RAI mapping, and no fairness analysis is offered. The documented bias is the semantically correct one for immortalized human cell lines, and it is consistent with the donor provenance disclosed elsewhere. The notable omission is selection bias: sampling_strategies describes targeted selection of '100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes' and an incompletely overlapping protein coverage across modalities, which is a selection/coverage bias affecting any model trained on the released data but is recorded only as a limitation, not as a typed bias.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10/14): id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,450 chars); keywords (29); license_and_use_terms (full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms + data_use_permission: no_commercial_use); doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; creators (38, mostly with ORCID and affiliation); purposes (5); instances (4 typed instance records with B2AI_SUBSTRATE/B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs). Absent (4/14): resources; parent_datasets (related_datasets is used instead); variables; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (regulatory_restrictions is present but carries only a free-text statement and governance_committee_contact). 10 of 14 required fields populated (71.4%), landing squarely on the ≈70% band rather than the ≥90% band. The populated fields are not merely present but substantive. The four gaps are not cosmetic: the absence of variables leaves every tabular distribution without column-level semantics, and no confidentiality classification is asserted despite documented embargoes. Field presence and field meaning agree here: id, doi, page and publisher are four independent expressions of the same deposit and all four resolve consistently to the UVA Dataverse. parent_datasets is empty but its function is discharged by related_datasets with typed is_new_version_of relationships, so the lineage information exists under a different slot; the count is not adjusted for this because the rubric names the field.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description ≈1,450 chars, enumerating all four modalities, both cell lines, the treatment conditions and the differentiated derivatives. purposes: 5 responses of roughly 200-330 chars each, e.g. 'To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions.' Average narrative length well above 200 chars. Comfortably exceeds the >200 char band on both fields. Length here is carrying information rather than padding: the description names specific cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J), specific drugs (paclitaxel, vorinostat), specific assays (Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, IF) and specific packaging (RO-Crate via FAIRSCAPE), and each purpose states a distinct objective (AI-ready maps, spatiotemporal architecture, visible ML, FAIR data management, ethical AI) rather than restating the others.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 29 keywords: AI, affinity purification, AP-MS, artificial intelligence, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, induced pluripotent stem cell, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, machine learning, mass spectroscopy, MDA-MB-468, neural progenitor cell, NPC, neuron, paclitaxel, perturb-seq, perturbation sequencing, protein-protein interaction, protein localization, single-cell RNA sequencing, scRNAseq, SEC-MS, size exclusion chromatography, subcellular imaging, vorinostat. Far above the ≥8 threshold. Coverage spans assay, cell line, compound, cell type, disease area and programme, which is the right spread for discoverability. Four abbreviation/expansion pairs are counted separately (AI/artificial intelligence, iPSC/induced pluripotent stem cell, NPC/neural progenitor cell, scRNAseq/single-cell RNA sequencing); deduplicating them still leaves 25 distinct concepts, so the band is unaffected. One term is incorrect: 'mass spectroscopy' names a different technique from the mass spectrometry actually used, and is logged as a low-severity correctness issue. Because the count is far above threshold and the error is a single term, no deduction is applied.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 2: 'ZIP archive' (media_type application/zip) and 'RO-Crate metadata package' (media_type application/ld+json). total_file_count: 10. All ten file_collections carry compression: zip and a .zip path (cm4ai_ifimages_MDA-MB-468_untreated.zip, cm4ai_apms_MDA-MB-468_paclitaxel.zip, cm4ai_mass-spec_KOLF2.zip, cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip, cm4ai_release_metadata.zip, and five others). Unique media types: 2. Two distinct media types places this in the 2–3 band. File enumeration itself is strong: all ten archives are individually named, typed by collection_type (raw_data, processed_data, metadata), dated, checksummed and described. The underlying content is genuinely multi-modal (confocal images, mass-spectrometry outputs, single-cell sequencing), which the description and keywords confirm, but the datasheet describes only the outer containers. Every payload is wrapped in ZIP and no inner format is enumerated anywhere in the record, so the format variety a consumer can act on is 2, not the modality count. Scored on what is documented rather than what is inferable.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: Per-collection sizes stated numerically in notes: 4.6 GB, 4.2 GB, 3.8 GB (IF archives), 113.3 KB and 135.8 KB (AP-MS), 171.8 KB and 93.9 KB (SEC-MS), 30.2 KB and 73.3 KB (Perturb-seq), 1.1 MB (release metadata). total_file_count: 10. Instance counts: 'approximately 7,000 proteins for both the iPSC and TNBC flagship datasets'; '11,739 targeted genes'; '464 proteins of interest per condition' (June 2025 release); subpopulations documents strata by cell line and treatment. Passes on both limbs of the criterion — numeric sizes and numeric instance counts are both present. The pass is qualified by machine-readability: total_size_bytes and every file_collections.total_bytes are deliberately omitted, and source_caveats explains that the repository publishes only rounded human-readable units so no exact byte count exists in the source bundle. Declining to present a conversion of a rounded figure as exact is the correct call, but the consequence is that size is legible only to a human reader. Logged as a completeness issue; the pass/fail criterion as written is met.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; id: 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page: 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; publisher: 'ROR:0153tk833'. Cell-line RRIDs additionally present in subpopulations.notes (RRID:CVCL_0419, RRID:CVCL_B5P3). Passes on both limbs: a registered persistent identifier and an identified hosting platform. The four identification fields cross-validate. Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Library's Dataverse prefix; ROR:0153tk833 resolves to the University of Virginia; the landing page is on dataverse.lib.virginia.edu. Three independent statements of the same host agree. The only weakness is presentational: publisher carries no human-readable label, so the agreement is visible only after resolving the CURIE.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: four entries. NIH with grant '1OT2OD032742-01' (Bridge2AI: Cell Maps for AI Data Generation Project); NIH with grant '3OT2OD032742-01S2' plus RePORTER application 11211616, core project OT2OD032742, FY2025 award amount 5289382, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, awardee UC San Diego; NIH with grant '5U54HG012513-02' (Bridge2AI Bridge Center); and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia (acknowledged in the preprint, no award number). creators: 38 entries, effectively all with institutional affiliations (UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA with ROR:0153tk833, Yale, UT Austin, UAB, KTH, Simon Fraser, Montreal) and the large majority with ORCID iDs. Meets the top band on both limbs and exceeds it in specificity: award amounts, project periods, RePORTER application number and awardee institution are supplied beyond the bare grant identifiers. All three NIH award numbers validate against NIH format and are semantically correct for the programme: OT2/OD is the Other Transaction activity code and institute used for Bridge2AI Data Generation Projects, the -01S2 suffix correctly marks a type-3 administrative supplement on the same core project OT2OD032742, and 5U54HG012513-02 correctly identifies the NHGRI-administered Bridge Center as a type-5 continuation. Funding goals align with purposes (AI-ready data, ethical AI, workforce development), satisfying the funding/purpose consistency check. One structural redundancy: three separate funders entries repeat the same grantor 'National Institutes of Health' rather than nesting three grants under one grantor; this is a modelling choice, not an accuracy defect, and is not penalized.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Reported but not scored. The record does populate ethics-adjacent slots, all with coherent negative declarations: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false with regulatory_compliance 'Human Subjects — No; De-identified Samples — Yes; FDA Regulated — No'; is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false with the rationale that the data are 'non-clinical, deriving from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'; at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=false; ethical_reviews naming Vardit Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon as review contacts; sensitive_elements_present=false; confidential_elements documenting pre-publication embargoes; data_governance naming a Data Access Committee, contact Jillian Parker, and an access review process. informed_consent, participant_privacy, participant_compensation and data_protection_impacts are unpopulated — correctly so for immortalized cell-line material. Excluded from the denominator per the 'Applies to' condition: the gating fields show cell-line rather than human-subject research. Scoring this question would penalize a datasheet for the absence of IRB protocols, consent forms, compensation schedules and vulnerable-population safeguards that cannot exist for work on established cell lines, which is exactly what the N/A convention prevents. Ethics documentation that is present is reported here and is, for what it covers, coherent and well-attributed. The anti-circular rule is satisfied: the exclusion rests on description, keywords and collection_mechanisms, none of which belong to Q8, and would stand even if every Q8 field were blank. The ambiguity rule was considered and does not fire — the cell lines derive from human donors (subpopulations.notes records a 51-year-old black female donor for MDA-MB-468 and a healthy male Northern European donor for KOLF2.1J), but donor-derived immortalized lines are not human subjects, no living individual is studied, and no recruitment occurs. This reading is independently corroborated by direct_collection.is_direct=false, 'Data were not collected from individuals'.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with each of the four licence limbs spelled out (Attribution, NonCommercial, ShareAlike, No additional restrictions), data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use', and notes that commercial use requires separate negotiation with UCSD/Stanford/UCSF and that the Tools pipeline (BSD-3) and FAIRSCAPE (MIT) carry distinct software licences. ip_restrictions: copyright held by the Regents of the University of California except spatial proteomics raw images, copyright The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University; KOLF2.1J available to not-for-profits via a simple MTA. regulatory_restrictions: 'not FDA regulated, not involving human subjects, and comprising de-identified samples', with governance_committee_contact 'Jillian Parker'. data_governance: committee_name 'Data Access Committee', access_review_process covering dual licensing, stewardship_roles naming the governance and ethics contacts. Absent: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant, other_compliance. Governance documentation is detailed and operationally useful — a reader learns who holds copyright over which component, who to contact, and what commercial reuse requires. Held to 4 because the confidentiality classification the top band names is not asserted, and no non-US compliance framework is identified. Ethics-claims plausibility passes: the licence, IP restrictions and regulatory declarations agree in scope and restrictiveness with the human_subject_research and is_deidentified declarations — a non-clinical, de-identified, non-FDA-regulated cell-line dataset released under a permissive non-commercial licence with a commercial carve-out is a coherent package, with no over-claiming of protection and no under-claiming of restriction.
