The gap worth noting is jurisdictional: the collaboration includes Simon Fraser University and the University of Montreal, yet other_compliance names no Canadian framework, and confidential_elements records active embargoes without a corresponding confidentiality_level.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. file_collections entry cm4ai_release_metadata.zip carries conforms_to 'RO-Crate' and conforms_to_standard [RO_CRATE]. distribution_formats includes an RO-Crate/JSON-LD package. related_datasets: five typed relationships by DOI (is_new_version_of ×3 to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX; is_described_by to doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311; is_referenced_by to doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734). external_resources spans MassIVE, NCBI BioProject/SRA, Figshare, NDEx, cm4ai.org, github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, fairscape.github.io and integrativemodeling.org. Ontology grounding: B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs on all four instances; annotation aligned to Gene Ontology and Reactome. Cross-dataset identifiers: Cellosaurus RRIDs CVCL_0419 and CVCL_B5P3. Standard formats and schema/ontology conformance are both clearly satisfied, and cross-platform linkage is genuinely strong — typed DOI relationships plus depositions in four external repositories. Held to 4 because integration capability is asserted more than operationalized. The gap to 5 is specific. conforms_to is asserted only on the metadata archive; source_caveats explains that the bundle states no content standard for the image, mass-spectrometry and sequencing payloads, so nine of ten collections declare no content standard. Everything ships as opaque ZIP with no inner format and no variables, so harmonization across the four modalities cannot be performed from this record. No integration procedure is documented, and known_limitations concedes that the modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap' — the very obstacle an integration procedure would need to address. The cell-line RRIDs and B2AI CURIEs are real common identifiers and are credited accordingly.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: five entries (node2vec dimensionality reduction of PPI networks; Human Protein Atlas deep learning model for image embeddings; contrastive deep learning co-embedding with reconstruction objective; community detection over co-embedding similarities; annotation by alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome plus an LLM naming approach). labeling_strategies: one entry with data_annotation_protocol describing the Gene Set AI (GSAI) pipeline using 'an engineered prompt following chain-of-thought and one-shot strategies' to return a name, confidence score and reasoning essay. machine_annotation_tools: four (GPT-4, node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF) each with a tool_description. Absent: cleaning_strategies, imputation_protocols, annotation_analyses, missing_data_documentation. No version numbers or URLs attached to any tool record. Substantially more than the one-strategy floor of the 3 band, but two independent shortfalls keep it from 4. The top band requires software versions and URLs: 'GPT-4' carries no snapshot or date, DenseNet-121 is an architecture rather than a versioned artifact, and the repository URLs live in external_resources rather than in the tool records. Cleaning, imputation, annotation-quality and missing-data documentation are all absent. A semantic mismatch drove this from 4 to 3 and is recorded as a medium-severity consistency issue. Every documented strategy describes cell-map construction, yet known_limitations states this release 'does not contain predicted cell maps' and discouraged_uses says the release 'is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets' because maps are absent. So the pipeline documented is for a product not shipped, while the processing actually applied to the shipped artifacts — MS search and quantification, image processing, scRNA-seq alignment and QC — is nowhere described. The rubric allows preprocessing to be carried in provenance graphs rather than text, and the record does claim RO-Crate provenance graphs in the metadata archive; that claim is credited in Q19 but cannot substitute here, because the record never states that those graphs contain the per-modality processing parameters.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: four entries with was_directly_observed flags and quantitative specifics — 'Seventeen genes were endogenously tagged in MDA-MB-468 and AP-MS data acquired under three conditions... with 34 additional genes in the tagging process'; SEC-MS 'identified 72 of 100 chromatin modifiers, 52 of them integral components of protein complexes' and 'uncovered more than 700 protein complexes in both parental iPSCs and differentiated neurons'; 'A CRISPR lentiviral library targeting 100 chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene'. collection_mechanisms: four entries naming the instrument classes and the four IF channels (DAPI nucleus, anti-calreticulin ER, anti-tubulin microtubules, antibody against the protein of interest). data_collectors: three, each attributing a modality to a named lab and institution (Lundberg Lab/Stanford for IF; Krogan lab/UCSF for SEC-MS; UCSD for Perturb-seq). raw_data_sources: four, each with source_type and access_details naming the destination repository. collection_timeframes: states 'The declared bundle does not state a data collection start or end date', giving only the Dataverse creation date 2025-02-27 and the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 as bounds. Methods and collectors are documented to a level that supports real understanding of how each modality was produced, with per-modality institutional attribution. Held to 4 because the top band requires timeframes, and no collection window is asserted. The timeframe gap is disclosed rather than concealed — source_caveats explains that neither the RePORTER end date (2026-08-31) nor the Dataverse maintenance statement (November 2026) is a collection date, so no start_date or end_date is asserted. That is the right handling of absent evidence, but the information is still missing and the score reflects the record's informational content, not its candour. A reproducibility gap also remains within the documented methods: no antibody catalogue numbers or RRIDs, no instrument models, and no MS acquisition parameters, so a reader could not repeat these assays from this record alone.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '2.0', status Beta. version_access.versions_available lists four prior releases with DOIs and version strings (March 2025 doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX v1.4; June 2025 doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R v2.1; October 2025 doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM v2.1; May 2024); latest_version_doi and version_details noting that 'the Dataverse record exposes version differences and per-version publication dates'. updates: frequency quarterly, 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026'. distribution_dates gives the full publication history including 2025-03-03, 2025-07-01, 2025-10-31 (files added 2025-12-22), 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-15. maintainers: four, with names, institutions, emails and roles (Swathi Thaker/UAB programme manager; Zhandos Sembay/UAB portal support; Trey Ideker/UCSD point of contact; UVA Dataverse as archival repository). retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds'. doi and publisher present. Absent: errata (though related_datasets notes that the June 2025 release was revised 'to add RGB immunofluorescent images, correct RO-Crate metadata, and change naming conventions'). All four sustainability indicators are explicitly documented — persistent identifiers (DOI per release, plus ARK identifiers from FAIRSCAPE noted in notes), a long-term governance plan (Data Access Committee with an access review process), a named repository (UVA Dataverse, described as 'an NIH-approved generalist repository', complemented by domain deposits at MassIVE, SRA, Figshare and NDEx), and institutional commitment ('committed institutional funds'). On content alone this reaches the top band. Reduced from 5 to 4 by a defect in precisely the thing this question measures. The version sequence is non-monotonic: this release, issued 2026-06-17, is version '2.0', while the June 2025 and October 2025 releases it supersedes are both recorded as version '2.1'. A consumer sorting the series by version string would order it wrongly, and the citation's 'V2' token adds a third form. The absent errata slot is a lesser matter, since its substance appears in related_datasets notes.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: a complete formal dataset citation naming ~40 authors, the year 2026, the title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)', the DOI https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, the publishing organization 'University of Virginia Dataverse' and the version V2 — it identifies the dataset by title and by both its authors and its publisher. Distinct further references: doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (Clark T et al., CM4AI bioRxiv preprint, related_datasets is_described_by, 'required for citation by users of the data'); doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (Nourreddine S et al., 'A Perturbation Cell Atlas of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells', PMCID PMC11580897); doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3 (Schaffer et al., Nature, noted in source_caveats). use_repository: https://cm4ai.org/publications/ as a maintained publications page. Non-publication resources: the cellmaps_pipeline repository, its ReadTheDocs documentation, FAIRSCAPE and IMP. Comfortably satisfies the 5 condition: a formal dataset citation is present and at least two distinct DOI-linked references accompany it, with citation instructions ('publications referencing this data or derived products should cite the related publication as well as directly citing the data collection') stated in license_and_use_terms. All cited DOIs are well formed and the prefixes match their claimed registrars: 10.1101 for bioRxiv preprints and 10.1038 for Nature. The Nature reference is handled with unusual care — source_caveats explains that it describes a U2OS map from the same investigators and pipeline, is not a CM4AI data release, and that its U2OS-specific figures are therefore not attributed to this dataset. The only blemish is the 'V2' versus '2.0' token mismatch between citation and version, logged separately as a low-severity issue and not deducted here, since Q14 is restricted to 0, 3 or 5 and the reference content plainly meets the top condition.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: Reported but not scored. The record does stratify its material: subpopulations.identification describes strata by cell line and treatment condition (MDA-MB-468 untreated/DMSO, paclitaxel, vorinostat; KOLF2.1J undifferentiated and as NPCs, neurons, cardiomyocytes), distribution notes the per-condition IF archive sizes and that AP-MS covers treated MDA-MB-468 only, and notes records donor characteristics of the source lines: 'MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) was established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma. KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.' instances carries four typed records; at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=false. Excluded from the denominator per the 'Applies to' condition. The subgroup structure documented here is experimental (cell line × treatment), not demographic; the two donor descriptions characterize the provenance of immortalized lines, not a study population with inclusion and exclusion criteria. Scoring demographic diversity against a two-cell-line experiment would measure the wrong thing. The exclusion is non-circular: it rests entirely on description, keywords and collection_mechanisms and would hold even if subpopulations and instances were empty. Worth recording as a positive observation rather than a score: for a dataset with no human subjects, the record nevertheless documents donor ancestry, sex and age for both source lines and identifies them by Cellosaurus RRID, which is the appropriate analogue of population characterization for cell-line work and supports downstream reasoning about generalizability — a point the record itself makes in known_biases and future_use_impacts.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'. external_resources carries resolvable URLs to https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, https://integrativemodeling.org and https://ndexbio.org; use_repository gives https://cm4ai.org/publications/; extension_mechanism.contribution_url gives the pipeline repository. Related releases and publications are addressed by DOI. Passes decisively — persistent identification is layered across dataset DOI, landing page, related-release DOIs, publication DOIs, ORCIDs, a ROR and cell-line RRIDs. All URLs are structurally well formed with plausible domains that match the organizations they are attributed to (github.com/idekerlab for the Ideker lab toolkit, dataverse.lib.virginia.edu for a UVA deposit, ndexbio.org for NDEx). The persistentId query parameter on the landing page correctly embeds the same DOI recorded in the doi and id fields. notes additionally records that FAIRSCAPE assigns ARK-scheme identifiers with DOIs planned as supplementary identifiers for final-state work, which is a candid statement of the current identifier architecture.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats.notes: 'All ten files in the June 2026 release are distributed as ZIP archives from the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData). Per-file MD5 checksums are published with each archive. Individual files below the repository's 1.9 GB download limit may be downloaded directly; the dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP, and the Dataverse Data Access API is offered for programmatic access.' page gives the landing page; each file_collection gives a filename, path and MD5. license_and_use_terms states the permissions and the commercial carve-out; ip_restrictions notes that the KOLF2.1J line itself requires a simple MTA for not-for-profits. external_resources records that the Perturb-seq depositions are embargoed at their external repositories. download_url is not populated. Unusually practical for this question: it warns about the 1.9 GB per-file limit, notes that the whole dataset cannot be pulled as one archive, points to the Data Access API for programmatic retrieval, and supplies checksums for verification. Held to 4 by two gaps — no download_url field, and the access tier is left to be inferred. FAIR logic passes: a DOI is present and the landing page it points to is publicly described, and the reuse-permitting licence is matched by specified distribution formats. The tier question the rubric insists on is nonetheless unanswered in words — nothing states whether a Dataverse account, registration or click-through is required before download, so a reader must infer tier 1 from the absence of any stated barrier. The picture is further complicated, honestly but incompletely, by the embargo on the external Perturb-seq depositions coexisting with distributed Perturb-seq archives here, logged as a medium-severity consistency issue under Q10/Q19 evidence.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with all four limbs enumerated and attribution requirements stated. intended_uses: five categories with examples and usage_notes — AI-ready research data, model training, biological analysis, perturbation and disease analysis, and interpretable machine learning ('visible' ML systems and VNNs 'built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture, rather than black-box models'). prohibited_uses: 'These laboratory data are not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval.' discouraged_uses: two — integrated cell-map analysis is unsuitable because maps are not included, and use without domain expertise. future_use_impacts: three — generalization risk from cell-line derivation, the Ethics module's integration of anticipated applications 'into data governance frameworks to optimize benefits and mitigate potential risks' with tools 'to enhance awareness and comprehension of the ethical, legal, and social ramifications', and clinical misuse as an anticipated harm. known_limitations additionally carries a recommended_mitigation ('Consult the External Data Links... for the current availability status of embargoed depositions'). All five field groups are populated with substantive, dataset-specific content rather than boilerplate, and risk is paired with mitigation at both the governance level (Ethics module, Data Access Committee) and the operational level (regulatory-oversight requirement for clinical use, embargo-status check). Meets the top band. The guidance is internally coherent and traceable to the record's own limitations: discouraged_uses cites the absence of cell maps, which known_limitations independently states; the generalization impact restates the cell-line selection bias recorded in known_biases and sampling_strategies. One soft spot, noted without deduction: parts of the mitigation are prospective ('Tools are being developed'), and prohibited_uses carries a single entry. Both are outweighed by the specificity and cross-field consistency of the rest.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Multimodal experimental interrogation of the MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cell line and the KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cell line and their differentiated derivatives, by AP-MS, SEC-MS, CRISPRi Perturb-seq, and immunofluorescence confocal microscopy.' Provenance packaging declared twice: description states 'CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework', and cm4ai_release_metadata.zip is described as 'comprising RO-Crate metadata and provenance graphs', with conforms_to 'RO-Crate' and conforms_to_standard [RO_CRATE]; distribution_formats notes that earlier releases 'exposed RO-Crate metadata as individual ro-crate-metadata.json files and HTML provenance graph renderings'; notes records FAIRSCAPE ARK persistent identifiers. raw_data_sources: four entries with source_type and destination repositories. version_access and updates as cited in Q13. related_datasets supplies release lineage by DOI. Per-file MD5 checksums on all ten archives. Absent: errata, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation, splits / is_data_split. Clearly exceeds the 3 band, which is version history alone: a provenance-graph artifact is declared and shipped as a release component, and the textual lineage supplies the three PROV roles in reconstructable form — entities (checksummed, DOI-addressed file collections), activities (four acquisition_methods and five preprocessing_strategies) and agents (named labs in data_collectors, 38 ORCID-identified creators, four maintainers). Integrity is independently supported by MD5 checksums. Held to 4 because the graph is asserted rather than expressed here. The record never wires specific activities to specific outputs — no collection carries a was_generated_by, and a reader cannot tell from this datasheet which acquisition produced which of the ten archives, even though the filenames imply it. Three quality slots are also empty: missing_data_documentation is absent although known_limitations concedes incompletely overlapping protein sets across modalities, and no data-split indicators are given for a dataset explicitly intended for model training. Version-history provenance is itself degraded by the non-monotonic version sequence flagged at Q13.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: two entries. bias_type 'selection_bias' — 'Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.' bias_type 'sampling_bias' with affected_subsets ['AP-MS, SEC-MS and immunofluorescence targets in the MDA-MB-468 arm'] — 'Proteins interrogated were selected for their involvement in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders — specifically 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes — rather than sampled without regard to disease relevance.' future_use_impacts carries the generalization consequence forward. No AIO or CROISSANT RAI term mappings; no fairness analysis of any kind. Above the letter of the 3 band in that both entries use BiasTypeEnum values correctly and one identifies its affected subsets, but two of the three components of the top band are wholly missing and the gaps are not minor. Two bias entries is thin for a four-modality multi-omics release, and measurement bias — the dominant class here — is entirely undocumented: antibody specificity and cross-reactivity in IF, abundance-dependent detection bias in AP-MS and SEC-MS, and variable knockdown efficiency in CRISPRi. The record's own known_limitations notes incompletely overlapping protein coverage across modalities without carrying that forward as a documented bias. What is documented is accurate and consistent: the selection-bias statement is repeated verbatim in sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and echoed in future_use_impacts, so three fields agree rather than conflict, and the sampling-bias entry correctly characterizes the targeted 100+100 protein design as non-random. The shortfall is coverage and instrumentation, not correctness — no AIO CURIEs appear anywhere, and nothing quantifies differential coverage or performance across the strata the record itself defines (cell line, treatment condition, differentiation state), which is what a fairness analysis for this data type would require.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (12/14): id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,700 chars); keywords (29 terms); license_and_use_terms (full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms + data_use_permission: no_commercial_use); doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; creators (47 entries); purposes (4 responses); instances (4 typed instance descriptions with data_substrate/data_topic CURIEs); resources — external_resources (5 grouped blocks: preprints, MassIVE/Figshare deposits, embargoed links, portal, code); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'unrestricted'. Absent (2/14): parent_datasets (lineage instead expressed via related_datasets is_new_version_of and raw_data_sources) and variables (no variable-level dictionary for any of the four modalities). 12 of the 14 listed fields are populated, and populated means substantively populated rather than stub-filled — description, license terms and instances all carry paragraph-scale content. 85.7% sits above the 70% band and below the 90% band, so 4 rather than 5. The two gaps are real: parent_datasets is empty even though the lineage exists elsewhere in the record, and the absence of any variables/data-dictionary content is the single largest structural omission for a dataset intended for machine learning reuse. Field presence was checked against content, not keys. `resources` was credited to external_resources, whose entries are substantive (resolvable DOIs, repository names, code URLs) rather than placeholders. parent_datasets is scored absent even though related_datasets carries four is_new_version_of edges, because the rubric names the field and the semantically equivalent content is only partially substitutable: version predecessors are not the same relation as source parents. No field was found to be present-but-meaningless, which is the more common failure mode.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is approximately 1,700 characters and names the program ('the Functional Genomics Data Generation Project of the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge2AI program'), both cell lines and all perturbation conditions ('MDA-MB-468 triple-negative breast cancer cells, untreated or treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat, and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), undifferentiated or differentiated into neural progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons and cardiomyocytes'), all four modalities with their scope, the packaging ('RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'), the archive, and the nine collaborating institutions. purposes has 4 responses of roughly 150-330 characters each, e.g. 'To stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems that are informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than being black boxes.' Comfortably above the >200 character threshold on both fields, and the length is carrying information rather than padding. The description is dense with specifics a reuser needs — which cell line received which drug, which modality covers which condition — and it is accurate to the rest of the record. Length was checked for informational density, not character count alone. Every clause in the description is corroborated elsewhere in the record: the modality/condition matrix matches file_collections exactly (AP-MS for treated MDA-MB-468 only; SEC-MS for both lines; IF for MDA-MB-468 only), and the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE claim matches conforms_to. The four purposes are distinct rather than restatements, covering scientific aim, data product, downstream ML goal and FAIR/ethical packaging.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 29 keywords: AI, affinity purification, AP-MS, artificial intelligence, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, induced pluripotent stem cell, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, machine learning, mass spectroscopy, MDA-MB-468, neural progenitor cell, NPC, neuron, paclitaxel, perturb-seq, perturbation sequencing, protein-protein interaction, protein localization, single-cell RNA sequencing, scRNAseq, SEC-MS, size exclusion chromatography, subcellular imaging, vorinostat. Far above the 8-keyword threshold. Coverage spans program (Bridge2AI, CM4AI), biological system (both cell lines, four derived cell types), disease context (breast cancer), perturbagens (paclitaxel, vorinostat), all four assay modalities, and the AI/ML framing — so the set genuinely describes the dataset rather than inflating a count. Six abbreviation/expansion pairs are present (AI/artificial intelligence, iPSC/induced pluripotent stem cell, NPC/neural progenitor cell, perturb-seq/perturbation sequencing, scRNAseq/single-cell RNA sequencing, SEC-MS/size exclusion chromatography). Collapsing each pair still leaves roughly 22 distinct concepts, so the score is unaffected; including both forms aids retrieval. One correctness defect: 'mass spectroscopy' is the wrong term for the mass spectrometry actually performed, and is logged as a low-severity correctness issue — it did not change the score because diversity remains far above threshold. Every other keyword is corroborated by content elsewhere in the record; none are aspirational.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats declares a single media_type: 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata', media_type 'application/zip', plus a second access route rather than a second format ('Programmatic file access through the Dataverse data access API'). All five file_collections carry compression 'zip'. total_file_count is 10, enumerated as 3 IF archives, 2 AP-MS, 2 SEC-MS, 2 perturb-seq, 1 release metadata. Further serializations are named only in conforms_to: '...serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema'. Enumeration is a strength and variety is the weakness. The file inventory is excellent — every archive is accounted for by collection, with counts, per-archive sizes, conditions and producing laboratory. But at the distribution layer only application/zip is declared, so a consumer cannot tell from distribution_formats what is inside the archives. Credit above the '1 file type only' floor is given because the record does name JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema as the packaged serializations, and because the description evidences genuinely multi-modal content (confocal imaging, mass spectrometry, single-cell sequencing) as the rubric permits; the archives are containers over heterogeneous data, not one format. The one-media-type finding is a documentation artifact rather than a property of the data: the underlying content spans image, mass-spectrometry and sequencing modalities, which the description, keywords and instances all establish. The rubric's allowance that 'variety can indicate multi-modal data if indicated in description, purposes, or keywords' is what lifts this to the 2-3 band; it does not reach 5 because the per-modality formats (e.g. TIFF/OME-TIFF for the confocal images, mzML/RAW for mass spectrometry, MTX/H5AD for perturb-seq matrices) are nowhere stated, leaving a reuser unable to assess tooling requirements before downloading a 4.6 GB archive.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: Per-archive sizes appear in every file_collections description: IF archives 'untreated (4.6 GB), paclitaxel-treated (3.8 GB) and vorinostat-treated (4.2 GB)'; AP-MS 'paclitaxel treatment (113.3 KB) and one for vorinostat treatment (135.8 KB)'; SEC-MS '(171.8 KB)' and '(93.9 KB)'; perturb-seq '(30.2 KB)' and '(73.3 KB)'; release metadata 'ZIP archive (1.1 MB)'. total_file_count: 10, with file_count per collection (3, 2, 2, 2, 1). Scale counts also appear: '11,739 targeted genes' in instances and sampling_strategies, and project-wide '21.4 TB of data volume' in notes. Pass. Numeric sizes are available for all ten archives and counts for every collection, which is what the criterion asks for. The sizes are internally plausible and modality-consistent: multi-gigabyte confocal image archives against kilobyte-scale mass-spectrometry and perturb-seq result tables is the expected ratio for processed interaction data versus raw imaging. Logged as a low-severity completeness issue: the values sit in prose while total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are unpopulated, so they are not machine-readable. This is a pass/fail item and the information is present, so the placement does not change the score. Also noted from source_caveats: the author compared MD5 checksums across releases and found the IF archives regenerated at identical sizes — evidence the size figures were actually inspected rather than copied forward.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; version_access.latest_version_doi 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; four predecessor DOIs (10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5); ARK identifiers asserted for packaged outputs in conforms_to ('each RO-Crate is assigned an ARK persistent identifier'); RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for the source cell lines; 38 ORCID iDs and ROR:0153tk833 for contributors. publisher is omitted. Pass, with margin. Identification is layered — dataset DOI, resolvable landing page, per-package ARKs, versioned predecessor DOIs, plus RRIDs and ORCIDs identifying the biological materials and the people. The DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia LibraData/Dataverse prefix and matches both the stated archive and the page hostname, so the identifier, registrar and landing page corroborate one another rather than merely coexisting. The id field correctly expresses the DOI as a CURIE. Nine creators without ORCIDs are given fragment identifiers minted on the release DOI (e.g. 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#creator-polacco-b'), a defensible local-identifier practice that avoids fabricating ORCIDs. The omitted publisher is logged as a low-severity completeness issue, since the citation itself names 'University of Virginia Dataverse'; it does not affect this pass/fail item.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: Three funders. (1) 'National Institutes of Health' with two grant entries: award '1OT2OD032742-01' and core project 'OT2OD032742', the latter annotated with NIH RePORTER detail — 'application 11211616, project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2, awarded to the University of California, San Diego with Trey Ideker as principal investigator, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, fiscal year 2025 award amount 5,289,382'. (2) 'National Institutes of Health, Bridge2AI Bridge Center' with award '5U54HG012513-02'. (3) 'Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia', explicitly noted as having no grant identifier. creators lists 47 people, 38 with ORCID iDs; structured `affiliations` appear for only 5 (all ROR:0153tk833), with the other 42 affiliations in free-text notes, e.g. 'Lundberg E, Stanford University.' Funding documentation is at the top of the range: three distinct funders, four grant identifiers, and administrative detail (PI, project period, award amount, application number) well beyond what the rubric asks. The single deduction is on the affiliation half of the criterion — affiliations exist for all 47 creators but only 5 are machine-resolvable, the rest being embedded in a notes string. Substantively complete, structurally uneven, hence 4 rather than 5. All four grant identifiers pass NIH pattern validation and, more tellingly, pass plausibility: OT2 is the other-transaction activity code used for Bridge2AI data generation projects and OD is the correct administering institute, while U54 with HG (NHGRI) is the correct pairing for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center — the two awards are coded consistently with the roles the record assigns them. Funding-to-purpose alignment holds: the Bridge2AI program goal of ethical, AI-ready data generation is directly restated in purposes ('To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets, packaged with provenance and rich metadata, that demonstrate FAIR data management'). The third funder is recorded without an identifier and says so, which is preferable to inventing one. ROR:0153tk833 is correctly the University of Virginia, consistent with the caveat explaining why those five entries carry a ROR instead of a name.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: a paragraph-length review_details, reviewing_organization 'CM4AI Ethics module', contact_person 'ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801' (Vardit Ravitsky), describing 'a methodology inspired by Value-Sensitive Design to create normative standards and expectations, an axiological repository of values, and a CM4AI Life Cycle framework elucidating governance milestones'. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects false, regulatory_compliance quoting 'Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No', and ethics_review_board explaining 'no institutional review board approval is recorded for the release, consistent with its statement that no human subjects are involved'. is_deidentified: identifiable_elements_present false with the rationale that the data 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'. sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false with a reasoned negative finding. regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance names the Data Governance Committee contact 'Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu)'. data_governance.stewardship_roles names two ethical review contacts with emails. Absent: informed_consent, participant_privacy, participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, participant_compensation, at_risk_populations, data_protection_impacts, regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant, regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact. Scored against what ethics coverage should look like for this substrate, not against a human-participant checklist. The participant-facing fields (compensation, at-risk populations, participant privacy) are genuinely inapplicable to established cell lines and their absence is not penalised. What is present is strong and unusual: a named ethics body with an ORCID-identified contact, a reasoned deidentification argument, an explicit negative sensitivity finding, and governance contacts — a record that documents negatives rather than leaving fields blank. Two substantive gaps hold it to 4: no consent or ethical-sourcing provenance for the donor material underlying either line, and no data_protection_impacts, which the rubric names explicitly in its 5 band. Cross-field logic checks pass. involves_human_subjects=false is consistent with the absence of IRB approval, and the record explains the absence rather than leaving it to inference — the stronger form. is_deidentified is accompanied by a method rationale, and that rationale is appropriate to the data type: no Safe Harbor or k-anonymity claim is made where none would apply, and non-identifiability is instead argued from the nature of commercial cell lines. sensitive_elements corroborates independently. One content-accuracy tension is logged at medium severity: the record discloses donor age, sex, race and diagnosis for MDA-MB-468 while asserting deidentification. This is standard and acceptable cell-line provenance rather than PHI, so it is not scored as a contradiction — but it does make the absent consent documentation more conspicuous, since the record describes the lines as 'ethically sourced' without citing the basis. A completeness issue is also logged for governance and reidentification content residing in prose rather than in the designated structured fields.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms gives the full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 grant with its URL and enumerates all four conditions (attribution, non-commercial, ShareAlike, no additional legal or technological measures), plus 'Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder (UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF depending upon the specific data package in question)'; data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use'. ip_restrictions lists four restrictions including 'Copyright to the datasets is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise indicated' and 'Raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University'. regulatory_restrictions gives confidentiality_level 'unrestricted', two regulatory statements ('the dataset does not involve human subjects... not FDA regulated'; clinical use 'requires appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'), and other_compliance covering FAIR compliance and the governance contact. data_governance.access_review_process states 'All files in the release are publicly accessible... no access request is required for the published files', alongside the Data Access Committee's role in commercial dual licensing. stewardship_roles names five distinct roles with contacts. Every element of the 5 band is present and each is specific rather than nominal: the license is enumerated condition by condition rather than cited by name, the copyright allocation is split correctly between institutions and data types, the confidentiality level is classified, and the access process is stated explicitly including the fact that no request is required. The governance layer — DAC, Data Governance Committee contact, ethics contacts, point of contact, archival steward — exceeds what the question asks. Internal alignment holds across the governance block: data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use' matches the license text, matches the ip_restrictions commercial-licensing route, and matches prohibited_uses, which independently forbids commercial use and non-ShareAlike redistribution. The restrictiveness is proportionate to the ethics profile — a non-human-subjects cell-line dataset carrying IP rather than privacy constraints is correctly governed by copyright and commercial terms rather than access controls. One low-severity consistency issue is logged: the token 'unrestricted' for confidentiality_level sits beside a documented commercial prohibition, a ShareAlike obligation and two embargoed external resources. It did not reduce the score, because the record disambiguates access from reuse explicitly in access_review_process and because 'unrestricted' is the correct classification for access confidentiality here. The source_caveats' honesty about the copyright wording being transcribed from the March 2025 release, since 'the June 2026 landing page does not restate it', is a provenance strength rather than a weakness.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to describes the full packaging stack: 'RO-Crate (Research Object Crate)... each RO-Crate is assigned an ARK persistent identifier and carries an end-to-end provenance record expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema'. conforms_to_standard 'RO_CRATE'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. distribution_formats gives application/zip plus a programmatic API route. file_collections.compression 'zip' throughout. related_datasets carries seven typed edges across three relationship types (is_new_version_of ×4, is_described_by ×2, references ×1), each with a resolvable DOI target. external_resources links MassIVE deposits per modality, a Figshare atlas, the Cell Mapping Toolkit (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline), its ReadTheDocs documentation, FAIRSCAPE and the Integrative Modeling Platform. instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs; raw_data_sources carry Cellosaurus RRIDs; creators carry ORCIDs and a ROR. All three components of the 5 band are met with real content. Standard formats: RO-Crate, JSON-LD, RDF-XML, JSON-Schema, ZIP. Schema/ontology compliance: a w3id-resolvable LinkML schema URI with a declared target class, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, and Bridge2AI substrate/topic CURIEs on every instance. Integration capability: typed, DOI-resolvable cross-dataset relationships, cross-platform deposits at MassIVE and Figshare, ARK identifiers per package, and shared entity identifiers (RRID, ORCID, ROR) that permit linking to external resources without string matching. The judgement is about how well interoperability is supported, and on that axis this is at the top of the range. Two countervailing findings were weighed and did not lower the band. First, the declared distribution media type is application/zip alone, so per-modality formats are opaque at the distribution layer — scored at Q4, where it is the operative weakness, rather than double-counted here, since Q10 concerns standards conformance and linkage rather than format enumeration. Second, actual cross-modality integration is limited by the data themselves: known_limitations states that 'SEC-MS, protein localization (IF imaging) and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap', and computed cell maps are excluded from the release. That is a property of an interim release, disclosed by the record, not a documentation deficiency — and the harmonizing apparatus needed to integrate the modalities once they align (common gene/protein identifiers, ontology-typed instances, a shared schema) is documented. The w3id.org schema URI and the EVI ontology are both genuine, resolvable standards rather than invented references, and conforms_to_class 'Dataset' is the correct class for this record.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: four steps naming specific methods — 'the node2vec deep learning model to reduce dimensionality, producing a PPI embedding'; 'a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model... producing an image embedding'; 'integrated into a co-embedding for each protein using contrastive deep learning'; 'Community detection... on the all-by-all similarities of pairs of proteins in the co-embedding space'. cleaning_strategies: 'Each segment of the MuSIC pipeline calls the FAIRSCAPE client package to validate inputs and to create the output RO-Crate package for that segment, with complete schemas and validation procedures... expressed in JSON-Schema', plus a QC statement. labeling_strategies: alignment to 'the Gene Ontology and Reactome' plus 'a large language model approach that names sets of proteins and assigns a name confidence score'. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy all populated. Tool URLs in external_resources as quoted above. Absent: machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols; no version string for any tool. Strategy documentation is detailed and names real, identifiable software with resolvable URLs, which puts it well above the 'at least one strategy or tool listed' band. Two things hold it to 4. First, no tool is versioned; version_access says versions 'are referenced in that dataset's metadata', which relocates the information rather than providing it. Second, and more consequentially, every preprocessing and labeling entry carries a source_caveat that the step belongs to the MuSIC pipeline whose outputs are 'not included in this release' — so the richest documentation describes processing not applied to the distributed archives, leaving the actual per-modality preparation (MS search parameters, image QC, guide assignment) undocumented. The caveats are themselves the strongest transparency signal in this question: the record could have presented MuSIC pipeline steps as the release's provenance and did not, instead flagging each one. Credit is given for that honesty while still deducting for the resulting coverage gap, since a reuser cannot learn from this record how the ZIP contents were produced. The named tools are all real and correctly attributed — node2vec is a genuine graph-embedding method appropriate to PPI networks, the Human Protein Atlas model is the right provenance for the IF embedding, GO and Reactome are the correct annotation resources, and the Integrative Modeling Platform matches the structure-modeling task described in other_tasks. The LLM annotation approach is noted with a confidence score, which is appropriate quality-control disclosure for machine annotation, even though machine_annotation_tools is not separately populated. Absence of imputation_protocols is not penalised: no imputation is claimed anywhere in the record.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: four entries, each with was_directly_observed true and was_reported_by_subjects false — AP-MS 'on endogenously tagged cell lines'; SEC-MS 'used as an orthogonal mass spectrometry-based approach to AP-MS'; 'immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) using Human Protein Atlas antibodies followed by confocal microscopy'; single-cell CRISPRi screens. collection_mechanisms: four entries with operational specifics — 'tagging 17 genes in MDA-MB-468 with AP-MS acquired under untreated, paclitaxel and vorinostat conditions, with 34 additional genes in progress'; 'automated fixation and permeabilization protocols implemented on a pipetting robot... followed by confocal microscopy in four colour channels'; 'a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 lines engineered to express inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit'. data_collectors: four named institutional collectors with roles — 'Lundberg Lab, Stanford University' (imaging), 'Nevan Krogan laboratory, University of California San Francisco' (SEC-MS and AP-MS), UCSD (CRISPRi screens and MuSIC integration), University of Virginia (FAIRSCAPE packaging and deposit). collection_timeframes: two entries giving the project period '2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31', the creation date 2025-02-27, publication dates, and the explicit statement that 'no source states a data collection start or end date for this release'. raw_data_sources: four entries with RRIDs and access_details. All three named components — methods, collectors, timeframes — are present, and each is specific rather than generic. The protocol descriptions carry numbers a reuser can act on (17 tagged genes, 6 guides per gene, four colour channels, named kit), the collectors are attributed per modality to named laboratories rather than to 'the consortium', and the raw material is identified by RRID with access routes. This meets the 5 band. The instance/staining detail is technically coherent and internally consistent: the four-channel configuration described in instances (DAPI nuclei, calreticulin ER, tubulin microtubules, target protein) matches the 'four colour channels' in collection_mechanisms, and dCas9 with 6 guides per gene is the correct configuration for CRISPR interference as claimed. The timeframe entry is notable for recording a limitation rather than papering over it — it states plainly that no release-scoped collection window is available, and separates the project period from the Dataverse creation date instead of conflating them. Residual gaps were weighed and judged not to drop the band, since the rubric's 5 criterion is methods + collectors + timeframes rather than full wet-lab reproducibility: absent are antibody catalogue numbers, mass spectrometer models, chromatography column specifications and imaging objectives.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '2.0'; status 'Beta'. version_access: latest_version_doi, five versions_available each with a DOI, and version_details explaining that 'Quarterly releases are published as separate Dataverse datasets, each with its own DOI and its own internal version history; within a release, minor and major version updates are recorded by the repository and files are not removed from previously published versions'. updates: frequency 'Quarterly', with 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026' and named future content ('computed cell maps, iPSC immunofluorescence images, and further AP-MS interactomes'). maintainers: three entries with roles — Trey Ideker (point of contact and PI), Swathi Thaker (program manager, snthaker@uab.edu), and 'University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), School of Medicine collection... long-term preservation supported by committed institutional funds'. retention_limit repeats the preservation commitment and the no-removal policy. doi and ARK identifiers present. distribution_dates records both release waves (2026-06-17 and 2026-07-15) with a source_caveat. Absent: errata, publisher, last_updated_on. Measured against the four sustainability indicators the question names: persistent identifiers — yes (DOI, predecessor DOIs, per-crate ARKs); long-term governance plan — yes (data_governance with stewardship roles, DAC, quarterly update commitment with an end date); domain-appropriate repository — partly (UVA Dataverse is a general-purpose institutional repository, but modality-appropriate deposits exist at MassIVE for mass spectrometry and Figshare for the atlas); institutional commitment — yes, and unusually explicit ('supported by committed institutional funds'). Versioning is comprehensive, with five DOIs and a stated no-deletion policy. Three gaps hold it to 4: no errata field and no statement that none are known; publisher omitted though the citation names the publishing organization; and the version-number inversion described below. A low-severity consistency issue is logged for the inversion: the current release is '2.0' while superseded October 2025 and June 2025 releases are listed at 'Version 2.1'. The record supplies the explanation (per-dataset internal version histories under separate DOIs), so this is confusing presentation rather than an error, and it cost part of the deduction rather than a band. Cross-checks pass: the five DOIs in versions_available reconcile exactly with the four is_new_version_of edges in related_datasets plus the current DOI; the November 2026 update horizon is consistent with the NIH project period ending 2026-08-31 plus close-out; and the two-wave publication dates are consistent with distribution_dates and with the source_caveat resolving the portal's conflicting '2025' statement. The maintainer set is well-formed for sustainability purposes in covering scientific, programmatic and archival stewardship as distinct roles rather than listing one contact.

name: Associated Publications
text: Formal dataset citation present and complete: 'Clark T; Parker J; Al Manir S; ... Ideker T, 2026, "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)", https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' — identifying the dataset by title, its 47 authors, the publishing organization and the version. Distinct additional references: (1) Clark T et al., 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence: AI-Ready Maps of Human Cell Architecture from Disease-Relevant Cell Lines', bioRxiv 2024, doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311; (2) Nourreddine S et al., 'A perturbation cell atlas of human induced pluripotent stem cells', bioRxiv 2024.11.03.621734, PMCID: PMC11580897, doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; (3) Schaffer LV et al., 'Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics', Nature 642, 222-231 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3, via related_datasets relationship_type 'references'; (4) non-publication resources — the CM4AI portal, the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository and documentation, FAIRSCAPE, and the Integrative Modeling Platform. The two preprints also appear as typed is_described_by edges in related_datasets. The 5 condition is met twice over: at least two distinct references (three DOI-bearing publications plus several non-publication resources) together with a formal dataset citation that identifies title, authors and publishing organization. Scored using the permitted values 0/3/5 only. Duplicate links were collapsed before counting: the two preprints appear in both external_resources and related_datasets and were counted once each. All three publication DOIs pass registrar plausibility — 10.1101 for bioRxiv preprints, 10.1038 with the s41586 journal segment for Nature — and the PMCID is well formed. The bibliographic details are internally coherent: the preprint author list overlaps heavily with the dataset creators, as expected. The relationship typing is semantically discriminating rather than uniform: the two preprints are is_described_by while the Nature paper is references, and the source_caveats explain exactly why — that paper 'reports a multimodal cell map of U2OS osteosarcoma cells... it is a separate study rather than a description of the cell lines and conditions in this release'. Drawing that distinction, rather than claiming the Nature paper as the dataset's own publication, is a correctness strength.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: Donor characterisation in raw_data_sources: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) 'established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma'; KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) 'an induced pluripotent stem cell line derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'. known_biases.representation_bias names both donors in affected_subsets and states the data 'do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'; sampling_strategies.why_not_representative states the same. instances describes four assay-level instance types with substrate/topic CURIEs. missing_data_documentation is populated. Absent: subpopulations, at_risk_populations, subsets.is_data_split, splits. For a dataset whose human dimension is two donor-derived cell lines, the representation content is close to complete: both donors are characterised by age, sex, ancestry or health status and disease state, each line is pinned by RRID, and the consequences for generalizability are analysed explicitly and repeated into discouraged_uses. What is missing is missing because it does not exist — with n=2 lines there is no subgroup structure to describe, and there are no participant inclusion/exclusion criteria because no participants were enrolled. The score stops at 4 rather than 5 because the rubric's top band asks for detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria, and the cell-line selection rationale (disease relevance) is a substitute for the latter rather than an instance of it. A placement finding that was weighed and did not reduce the score: the demographic content sits in raw_data_sources and known_biases, while the fields the question names (instances, subpopulations, subsets, at_risk_populations) are either assay-level or empty. The rubric directs scoring from the record's content rather than field presence, so the content was credited where it actually lives; the absence of structured subpopulation entries is noted as a machine-readability limitation rather than a substantive omission. The demographic disclosure is accurate to the published provenance of both lines and is appropriate rather than privacy-infringing, since it is established cell-line metadata. The representation-bias analysis is the semantically important element here: the record connects two-donor provenance to a concrete generalizability limit for downstream models, which is what this question is ultimately probing.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; id as a DOI CURIE; distribution_formats.access_urls giving both the landing page and 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/'; external_resources giving 'https://cm4ai.org/', 'https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/', 'https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline', 'https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/', 'https://fairscape.github.io' and 'http://integrativemodeling.org'; license URL 'https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/'; four predecessor release DOIs; three publication DOIs. Pass with substantial margin. Findability is supported at several layers — a DOI-backed landing page, a programmatic endpoint, project documentation, code repositories and the licence deed. All URLs are structurally well formed and point to plausible, institution-appropriate domains: the repository host matches the DOI's registering institution, cm4ai.org matches the project name given in the description and keywords, and github.com/idekerlab matches the laboratory named as PI. The DOI-plus-landing-page pairing satisfies the FAIR expectation that a persistent identifier resolve to an accessible description. One minor note that does not affect the pass: the Dataverse API entry is a base path without file identifiers, so it indicates the access route rather than resolving to a specific file; and the IMP link uses http rather than https.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats gives two routes: 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata' with access_url at the Dataverse landing page, and 'Programmatic file access through the Dataverse data access API, recommended for archives above the web download size limit' with access_url 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/'. data_governance.access_review_process states 'All files in the release are publicly accessible from the University of Virginia Dataverse under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; no access request is required for the published files', and describes the separate route for commercial use. license_and_use_terms states the reuse conditions in full. third_party_sharing adds alternate deposits: 'the underlying mass spectrometry data are additionally deposited in the MassIVE repository. The CRISPR interference perturbation atlas of iPSCs is additionally available on Figshare.' external_resources marks the two perturb-seq links 'Embargoed' with a restrictions note. The access path is fully defined and, importantly, unambiguous about what is not required: the platform is named, no login or DUA is needed for the published files, the licence policy governing reuse is stated, a programmatic route is provided with guidance on when to prefer it, and alternate repositories are given for the underlying raw data. The record also states precisely which resources are unavailable and why, so a user can determine before downloading what they will and will not obtain. The access description is consistent with every related field: public downloadability matches confidentiality_level 'unrestricted', the absence of an access request matches the CC licence, and the commercial-licensing exception is routed to the copyright holders consistently across license_and_use_terms, ip_restrictions and data_governance. The embargo disclosure is handled well and does not reduce the score — it applies to external repository links for raw perturb-seq sequence data, not to the ten released archives, and the record both scopes the embargo correctly and records in source_caveats that it supersedes the earlier June 2025 statement listing SRA/BioProject links. The practical note about the web download size limit is exactly the guidance a user of a 4.6 GB archive needs, and indicates the access route was considered rather than boilerplated.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms enumerates CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 condition by condition with its URL. intended_uses: four entries with usage_notes, e.g. 'AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics' noted as 'packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata in RO-Crate format so that inputs, computations, software and outputs are machine-resolvable'. prohibited_uses: three with reasons — clinical decision-making 'without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; commercial use; and 'Redistribution of adapted material under terms other than the same CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license, or with additional legal or technological measures that restrict what the license permits'. discouraged_uses: three with details — analyses requiring computed cell maps, 'Analysis without relevant domain expertise', and 'Generalization from these data to the population at large'. future_use_impacts: three, covering the generalizability risk from two cell lines, the Ethics module framework that 'anticipates potential applications of the data and derived AI and machine learning systems and integrates them into data governance frameworks in order to optimize benefits, mitigate potential risks and promote use for the collective good', and the foreseeable clinical misuse. Every element of the 5 band is present and substantive. The guidance is unusually well differentiated: prohibited, discouraged and intended uses are three genuinely distinct categories here rather than restatements, with prohibition tied to licence or regulation, discouragement tied to the release's actual limitations, and intent tied to the stated scientific goals. The social impact analysis identifies concrete risks — non-generalizable models, clinical misuse — and names mitigations rather than gesturing at them: the Ethics module's guidelines, value repository, CM4AI Life Cycle governance milestones, the Bridge2AI Code of Conduct, and the Data Access Committee. Use guidance propagates coherently from the record's own findings rather than being asserted independently: the discouragement of population generalization traces directly to known_biases.representation_bias and sampling_strategies.why_not_representative; the discouragement of cell-map-dependent analyses traces to missing_data_documentation and known_limitations.scope_limitation; and the prohibitions trace to license_and_use_terms and regulatory_restrictions. That traceability is what distinguishes real use guidance from a boilerplate block. The clinical-use prohibition is proportionate and correctly scoped — these are laboratory cell-line measurements, and flagging clinical application as foreseeable misuse is appropriate anticipation rather than overreach. The mitigation content is specific enough to be checkable, naming institutional mechanisms with contacts rather than aspirations.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Provenance graph: conforms_to states that each RO-Crate 'carries an end-to-end provenance record expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema', and that 'each RO-Crate is assigned an ARK persistent identifier'; intended_uses adds that 'inputs, computations, software and outputs are machine-resolvable'; file_collections includes a 'Release metadata archive... including RO-Crate metadata and provenance material for the June 2026 release'; cleaning_strategies describes per-segment crate generation by the FAIRSCAPE client. Entities, activities and agents are separately identified: archives (file_collections), assays (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms) and producing laboratories (data_collectors — Lundberg Lab, Krogan laboratory, UCSD, UVA). Derivation paths: raw_data_sources gives four upstream sources with RRIDs and repository deposits; related_datasets gives four is_new_version_of edges; version_access lists five releases with DOIs. Quality and integrity: cleaning_strategies QC and JSON-Schema validation; source_caveats records an MD5 comparison — 'the three immunofluorescence image archives in the June 2026 release report the same file sizes as those in the October 2025 release but different MD5 checksums, indicating the archives were regenerated'. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy. Absent: errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, splits. This clears the rubric's distinction between version history alone (3) and a full provenance graph (5). Version history is present, but so is a named provenance ontology with a declared serialization and per-package persistent identifiers, a processing lineage in which each pipeline segment emits a validated crate, and derivation paths running from identified upstream materials through named producing laboratories to enumerated archives. The rubric accepts provenance as text or as W3C PROV-O graphs provided the lineage is complete, and the lineage here is complete for what is released. EVI is a genuine PROV-derived evidence graph ontology and JSON-LD/RDF-XML are the correct serializations to claim for it, so the assertion is technically coherent rather than a standards name-drop. Two deductions were considered and judged insufficient to drop a band. First, was_derived_from and parent_datasets are unpopulated, so the derivation is expressed narratively and via related_datasets rather than in the designated typed fields — a machine-readability gap, already logged against Q1 where field completeness is the operative criterion. Second, the most elaborate provenance description attaches to the MuSIC pipeline whose outputs are excluded from this release; but the released artifacts' own lineage (source material → assay → producing laboratory → packaged archive) is fully traceable from the record, and the exclusion is disclosed. The MD5 observation deserves specific credit: the author performed an actual integrity comparison across releases, detected regenerated archives, and then declined to carry forward the earlier per-file protein counts — provenance reasoning applied rather than merely described. The absence of splits is not penalised, since no train/test partition is claimed.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases has two entries with enumerated bias_type values. representation_bias: 'Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', with affected_subsets naming both donor lines and their demographics. selection_bias: 'Proteins and genes were selected for interrogation on the basis of their role as chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders, rather than sampled at random from the proteome', with mitigation_strategy 'The perturbation component was extended to an expressed genome-scale CRISPR interference screen of 11,739 targeted genes in KOLF2.1J iPSCs, broadening coverage beyond the initial targeted panels.' future_use_impacts adds that 'models trained on them may not generalize across donors, populations or cellular contexts' and describes the Ethics module's risk-mitigation framework. Reinforced by five typed known_limitations entries (scope, coverage ×2, temporal, methodological) and by discouraged_uses. Above the 'basic bias identification without taxonomy' band: the bias_type values are drawn from a standard enumeration, each bias has a substantive description tied to the actual study design, one carries a concrete and verifiable mitigation, and the representativeness consequence is analysed and carried into use guidance. Three things hold it short of 5. No AIO or CROISSANT RAI term identifiers accompany the bias_type values, so the taxonomy alignment is by vocabulary rather than by mapping. The representation_bias entry has no mitigation_strategy and no statement that none is available. And the bias inventory omits measurement and technical bias, which are material for these modalities — antibody specificity and cross-reactivity in the IF panel, abundance-dependent detection bias in SEC-MS and AP-MS, and guide-efficiency variance in the CRISPRi screens. The two documented biases are correctly typed rather than mislabelled: donor-derived non-generalizability is genuinely representation bias, and targeted protein-panel construction is genuinely selection bias. The selection_bias mitigation is checkable and consistent with the rest of the record — the 11,739-gene genome-scale screen appears identically in instances, sampling_strategies and notes, and does broaden coverage as claimed, though only for the iPSC line. Fairness analysis exists in the population-representativeness sense and is propagated into discouraged_uses and future_use_impacts, but there is no quantitative or subgroup-level analysis; with two donor lines, quantitative fairness analysis is arguably not meaningful, which is why the absence weighs less than the missing measurement-bias coverage. The omission of assay-level bias is the more consequential gap for a dataset explicitly prepared for machine learning, since those effects propagate directly into any model trained on the released matrices.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,290 chars); keywords (30 terms); license_and_use_terms (full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms plus data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use' and a named contact); doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; creators (46, mostly with ORCID and affiliation); purposes (3 responses); instances (5 typed instance descriptions with substrate/topic CURIEs); resources (10 enumerated under six file_collections, each with format, media_type, md5, issued). Absent: variables (no variable-level documentation anywhere); parent_datasets (unpopulated — related_datasets carries only an is_new_version_of link to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (no classification value; confidential_elements narrates an embargo instead). Eleven of the fourteen enumerated fields are populated and the populated ones carry real content rather than placeholders, putting the record near the top of the 70% band but short of the ≥90% needed for 5. The three gaps are not cosmetic: no variable-level documentation exists for any of the four modalities, provenance to prior releases is expressed only as a sibling relationship rather than a parent link, and confidentiality is described in prose without a classification value a system could act on. Populated fields are mutually coherent — id, doi and page resolve to the same Dataverse object, and the citation repeats the same DOI and version. The missing variables field is the most consequential gap semantically: a record claiming AI-ready multi-modal data with no variable documentation cannot support the variable-level reuse it advertises. No credit was withheld for field presence alone; each counted field was checked for meaningful content.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs ~1,290 characters and is substantive throughout: it names the program role ('the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge of the NIH Bridge2AI program'), the three modalities ('protein-protein interaction, spatial protein localization, and genetic perturbation'), the biological systems ('MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with or without paclitaxel or vorinostat) and in KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells'), the delivery channel ('ten ZIP archives through the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData)'), a per-modality inventory, and the interim status ('computed cell maps are not included, and some component datasets remain under temporary pre-publication embargo'). The three purposes responses run ~290, ~230 and ~280 characters respectively. Every narrative field exceeds the 200-character threshold by a wide margin, and the length is carried by specifics — named compounds, named cell lines, named repository, an explicit statement of what is absent — rather than by padding. Length here correlates with information density rather than diluting it. The description's closing admission that the release is 'explicitly interim' is a rare instance of a narrative field spending its length on a limitation; it aligns with known_limitations and with the Beta status field rather than contradicting them.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 30 unique keywords spanning assay modalities ('AP-MS', 'SEC-MS', 'perturb-seq', 'scRNAseq', 'size exclusion chromatography', 'affinity purification', 'mass spectroscopy', 'subcellular imaging'), biological systems ('MDA-MB-468', 'KOLF2.1J', 'iPSC', 'neural progenitor cell', 'cardiomyocyte', 'neuron', 'breast cancer'), perturbagens ('paclitaxel', 'vorinostat', 'CRISPR/Cas9'), analysis targets ('protein-protein interaction', 'protein localization'), program identifiers ('Bridge2AI', 'CM4AI') and a subject classification ('Medicine, Health and Life Sciences'). Nearly four times the ≥8 threshold, and the set is genuinely diverse across facets rather than being one concept restated. Both spelled-out and abbreviated forms are supplied for several concepts (perturbation sequencing/perturb-seq; single-cell RNA sequencing/scRNAseq; neural progenitor cell/NPC), which is a deliberate discoverability choice. Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record — each named modality appears in collection_mechanisms, each cell line in raw_data_sources, each drug in the description — so the keyword set inflates neither scope nor coverage. 'mass spectroscopy' is a minor terminological slip for 'mass spectrometry' but does not affect matching, since the correct forms AP-MS and SEC-MS are also present.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats contains exactly one entry: 'format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip'. Every one of the ten enumerated resources repeats 'format: ZIP', 'media_type: application/zip', 'compression: zip'. The only typing distinction is file_type 'data_file' (9 resources) versus 'metadata_file' (cm4ai_release_metadata.zip), and collection_type 'raw_data'/'metadata' on two collections. total_file_count is 10 and matches the enumeration; file_collections groups the ten into six named collections with per-collection descriptions and sizes (AP-MS 113.3 KB / 135.8 KB; IF images 4.6 GB / 3.8 GB / 4.2 GB; SEC-MS 171.8 KB / 93.9 KB; perturb-seq atlas 30.2 KB; perturb-seq raw 73.3 KB; metadata 1.1 MB). The enumeration half of this question is done about as well as it can be — ten files named individually, grouped into meaningful collections, each with MD5, issue date and size. The variety half fails outright: one container format for the entire release, with no statement of what formats lie inside the archives. The rubric band for a single file type is 0; 1 rather than 0 credits the complete, checksummed, per-collection enumeration, which is real evidence of file-level documentation even though it yields no format diversity. The rubric's note asks for unified participant/sample identifiers across modalities as the marker of multimodality; none exist here. Cross-modality linkage is implicit in the cell-line names (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J) embedded in filenames, which is a weak join key and cannot distinguish treatment arms without parsing the filename. Semantically this matters more than the format count: a reuser cannot tell from this record how to align an immunofluorescence image with a SEC-MS elution profile for the same condition. The ZIP-only declaration also sits awkwardly against the record's RO-Crate and AI-ready claims, which is recorded as a separate semantic_understanding issue.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: Per-archive sizes appear in every file_collections description: '113.3 KB', '135.8 KB', '4.6 GB', '3.8 GB', '4.2 GB', '171.8 KB', '93.9 KB', '30.2 KB', '73.3 KB', '1.1 MB'. Counts: total_file_count 10; file_count per collection (2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1). notes gives project-scale figures: '1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 total proteins investigated, 11,739 genes targeted and 21.4 TB of data volume'. distribution_formats notes a '1.9 GB' web download limit. Passes comfortably on the presence test: numeric sizes exist for all ten deliverables and instance-scale counts exist at project level. Two qualifications, neither defeating the pass. First, sizes live in free-text descriptions rather than in total_size_bytes or file_collections.total_bytes, so they are human-readable but not machine-computable and no release-level total is given. Second, and more serious, several stated sizes are implausible for their described contents — a 30.2 KB 'cell atlas' for an 11,739-gene screen — which is recorded as a content_accuracy issue; the size metadata is present, but its plausibility is in question. The 21.4 TB figure is project-cumulative by the record's own flagged inference and must not be read as this release's volume.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
