text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health' with grants.grant_number '1OT2OD032742-01'; notes add 'NIH award 5U54HG012513-02 (Bridge2AI Bridge Center) and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia'. creators: 45 entries, each with at least one affiliation (University of Virginia with ROR:0153tk833; UCSD; UCSF; Stanford; KTH Royal Institute of Technology; Yale; UAB; University of Alabama; University of Texas at Austin; Simon Fraser; University of Montreal). Ideker T carries a principal_investigator block with ORCID 0000-0002-1708-8454 and email tideker@health.ucsd.edu. Both halves of the 5-point condition are met and exceeded: a named grantor with a structured award number, two additional acknowledged funding sources, and complete affiliation coverage across a 45-author list with ORCIDs for most and a ROR identifier for the lead institution. The PI is separately identified rather than left implicit in the author list. Grant-pattern validation passes: 1OT2OD032742-01 decomposes correctly as NIH application type 1 / activity code OT2 / awarding institute OD / serial 032742 / support year 01, the expected shape for a Bridge2AI Other Transaction award; 5U54HG012513-02 is likewise well formed (type 5, U54, NHGRI). Funding-to-purpose alignment holds: the purposes (AI-ready cell maps, visible machine learning) match the stated Bridge2AI Functional Genomics Grand Challenge remit of the OT2 award. Affiliations are consistent with data_collectors, which attributes IF imaging to the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and SEC-MS to the Krogan lab at UCSF — the same institutions that appear in those authors' affiliation entries.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false, with notes 'The release records Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No. CM4AI data are described as non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false with matching deidentification_details. ethical_reviews: two entries with named contacts and addresses — Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca) — the second describing a Value-Sensitive Design methodology and an axiological repository. sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: false with rationale. data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) with an access_review_process. Absent: informed_consent, participant_privacy, participant_compensation, at_risk_populations, data_protection_impacts, regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant. Comprehensiveness must be judged against what is in scope. Most unpopulated fields — compensation, at-risk populations, participant privacy — are genuinely inapplicable to immortalized and iPSC lines, and inventing them would be worse than omitting them. What is present is strong: an explicit and reasoned human-subjects determination, a de-identification claim with the correct standard, two named ethical reviewers, and a standing governance contact. The point withheld is for the one in-scope gap: no statement of the consent or ethical-sourcing basis for the donor material, and no data_protection_impacts entry recording that such an assessment was considered and found unnecessary. Cross-field logic checks out in the direction the rubric specifies: because involves_human_subjects is false, the absence of IRB protocol numbers is consistent rather than a contradiction, and the is_deidentified claim is paired with a method rationale as required. The deidentification argument is also appropriate to the data type — for tissue-culture data the operative standard is non-matchability, which is what is asserted. The residual tension is that direct_collection records the KOLF2.1J line as 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor' available through HipSci, so identifiable donor provenance exists upstream of the not-human-subjects determination and is left undocumented; this is logged as a low-severity consistency issue and is the basis for the one-point reduction.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms gives CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in full operative detail ('free to share ... and adapt ... under the conditions that appropriate credit is given with a link to the license and an indication of changes; that the material is not used for commercial purposes; and that contributions built upon the material are distributed under the same license'), with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use. ip_restrictions states 'Copyright for CM4AI data is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University', plus commercial relicensing via UCSD/Stanford/UCSF and a Data Access Committee. data_governance provides a named committee_contact with email, an access_review_process and stewardship_roles. regulatory_restrictions records only 'FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated'. regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is absent, as are hipaa_compliant, other_compliance and data_protection_impacts. License and restrictions are documented to a standard well beyond 'license only' — the copyright split between UC and Stanford for different data types is the kind of detail that actually governs downstream reuse, and a named governance contact with a review process makes the policy actionable. The fifth point is withheld solely because the confidentiality classification, which the 5-point condition names explicitly, is never set. Restrictiveness is coherent across fields: a non-commercial share-alike license, a reserved commercial-licensing pathway, and a Data Access Committee together describe a consistent posture of open academic reuse with commercialization held back. That posture is also consistent with the ethics fields — because no human subjects and no sensitive elements are declared, the absence of HIPAA and DPIA content is logically expected rather than a contradiction. The one incongruity is that a record this careful about governance leaves confidentiality_level unstated when the obvious value (public/open) follows directly from its own CC BY-NC-SA distribution.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE, with conforms_to narrating FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate packaging and provenance graphs. instances are typed with ontology term IDs (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, :58, :59, :64; B2AI_TOPIC:15, :26, :34). related_datasets carries typed relationships — is_new_version_of (three predecessor DOIs), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3). external_resources names NDEx with Cytoscape/HiView/ndex2 access, the Cell Mapping Toolkit at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, FAIRSCAPE and IMP. notes describes ARK persistent identifiers and the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, and GO/Reactome alignment of assemblies. distribution_formats: ZIP only. Integration capability is real and specific: a LinkML schema URI with a declared class, ontology-typed instances, four distinct relationship predicates linking this release to its predecessors and to three publications, and named cross-platform endpoints (NDEx, MassIVE, Figshare) with tooling to consume them. That is materially beyond 'standard format but no schema reference'. Full marks are withheld because the distribution layer itself is a bare ZIP container with no internal format declared, so harmonization with another dataset still requires opening the archives to discover what is inside. The RO-Crate conformance claim is the weak link and the record itself flags it: conforms_to states that the June 2026 release page 'does not itself restate the packaging format', yet conforms_to_standard asserts RO_CRATE unqualified, so the structured standards claim outruns its evidence. That mismatch is logged as a medium consistency issue and contributes to the one-point reduction alongside the format gap. Cross-platform linkage is otherwise genuine rather than nominal — the external endpoints are named with the tools that read them, and the typed related_datasets predicates are used correctly (is_new_version_of for prior releases of the same collection, references for the distinct U2OS cell map).

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: All seven scoring fields are unpopulated: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation. Tool documentation exists only outside them — external_resources gives the three repository URLs above, and notes describes 'the Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) pipeline, which integrates protein-protein interaction and immunofluorescence image data by node2vec and Human Protein Atlas deep learning embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, and multi-resolution community detection, and which annotates resulting assemblies by alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome and by a large language model naming approach'. No version number is given for any tool. Seven of the ten archives are labelled collection_type: processed_data. Named tools with resolvable repositories and documentation sites earn credit above the 0 band, but this falls short of 'at least one strategy or tool listed' in the sense the question intends, because the tooling that is described is not the tooling that produced these files. The MuSIC pipeline builds the computed cell maps, which known_limitations states are explicitly absent from this release. How the seven processed_data archives were derived from the raw acquisitions — search engines, databases, QC thresholds, guide calling, image processing — is nowhere documented. This is the record's largest substantive gap and it is a reproducibility gap, not a formatting one. The internal inconsistency is telling: the record labels seven archives processed_data, which asserts that processing occurred, while documenting none of it. No software versions appear anywhere, so even the tools that are named cannot be pinned to a state. Missing-data handling and annotation quality are likewise undocumented, which matters for the perturb-seq atlas in particular. Logged as a high-severity completeness issue.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods gives three entries with was_directly_observed: true, e.g. 'Genetic perturbation data acquired by single-cell CRISPR (CRISPRi) perturbation screens by cell type, using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.' collection_mechanisms adds channel-level imaging detail: 'DAPI for nuclei (blue), calreticulin antibody for endoplasmic reticulum (yellow), tubulin antibody for microtubules (red), and antibody against the protein of interest (green)'. data_collectors names the performing laboratories — 'Immunofluorescence imaging was performed in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford University', 'Size exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry was performed in the Nevan Krogan laboratory at the University of California San Francisco' — plus four production institutions. raw_data_sources lists seven upstream sources with access_details. direct_collection and sampling_strategies document the cell-line sourcing (ATCC; HipSci KOLF2.1J). collection_timeframes is absent. Three of the four named field groups are documented at a level that would let a domain reader reconstruct the assay design: specific reagents, specific kits, specific antibody channels, guides per gene, and the named laboratory responsible for each modality. The missing element is the fourth: no collection_timeframes, so the period over which the acquisitions ran is unknown. Deposit and publication dates exist elsewhere but describe the record's lifecycle, not the data's collection window. Technical terminology is used correctly and consistently throughout — AP-MS, SEC-MS, ICC-IF, CRISPRi, dCas9, 10x 3'HT are each deployed in the right context and each maps to a matching instances entry with its Bridge2AI substrate term. Attribution of modalities to laboratories is consistent with the creators' affiliations (Lundberg at Stanford, Krogan at UCSF). The timeframe gap compounds the created_on problem noted in the temporal issue: with created_on inherited verbatim from an earlier release, there is no reliable statement anywhere of when this release's data were generated.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta. version_access.versions_available enumerates the full release lineage with identifiers — 'May 2024, March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, Version 1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, Version 2.1), and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, Version 2.1)' — with latest_version_doi set. updates.frequency: 'Quarterly', update_details: 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'. maintainers names four people with roles and working emails (Swathi Thaker snthaker@uab.edu, programme manager; Zhandos Sembay zsembay8@uab.edu, web support; Trey Ideker, point of contact; Justin Niestroy, depositor). retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds.' distribution_dates records per-tranche release dates (Jun 17 2026 and Jul 15 2026). errata is absent. All four sustainability indicators the question enumerates are present and evidenced rather than gestured at: a persistent DOI, a long-term governance arrangement (Data Access Committee plus named stewardship roles), a domain-appropriate institutional repository, and an explicit institutional funding commitment for preservation. Versioning is equally complete — every predecessor release is named with its own DOI, the update cadence has a stated end point, and four maintainers are individually contactable. The absent errata field is the only shortfall and does not offset documentation this thorough; nothing suggests errata exist and are being withheld. One semantic defect does not reduce the score but is recorded: the declared version '2.0' is lower than the '2.1' recorded for both the June 2025 and October 2025 predecessors that this release supersedes, so the version strings do not order the series. This is almost certainly an artifact of per-deposit Dataverse numbering rather than an error of fact, and the record supplies DOIs and dates that do order the series correctly — but a consumer sorting on version alone would misread the lineage. Logged as a medium consistency issue. The repository choice is domain-appropriate and the preservation commitment is specific about its funding basis, which is rarer than the claim itself.

name: Associated Publications
text: A formal dataset citation is present and complete, identifying authors, title, DOI, publisher and version: 'Clark T; Parker J; Al Manir S; ... Ideker T, 2026, "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)", https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'. Distinct additional references: doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (CM4AI preprint, recorded as the Related Publication); doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (Nourreddine et al., perturbation cell atlas of human iPSCs, PMCID PMC11580897); doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3 (Schaffer et al., Nature 642, 222-231, 2025). Seven external_resources entries add cm4ai.org, MassIVE, Figshare, NDEx, the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository and docs, FAIRSCAPE and IMP. The 5-point condition is met with margin: three distinct DOI-identified publications plus seven external resources, and a formal citation that names the dataset by title and identifies both its authors and its publishing organization — not a bare DOI. Each reference is annotated with what it contains and how it relates to this release, so a reader can tell which publication describes the data and which merely overlaps in authorship. Reference DOIs validate by registrar: 10.1101 is bioRxiv for the two preprints, 10.1038 is Springer Nature for the journal article. The relationship typing is semantically precise — the CM4AI preprint is is_described_by, the iPSC atlas preprint is is_referenced_by, and the Nature U2OS paper is references with an explicit note that it concerns 'a separate multimodal cell map of U2OS osteosarcoma cells produced by overlapping investigators', which correctly prevents a reader from attributing that dataset to this release. That distinction is exactly the kind of over-claim this question can otherwise reward, and the record declines to make it.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: subpopulations.identification: 'Cell type and treatment condition. The release spans MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells under untreated, paclitaxel-treated, and vorinostat-treated conditions; undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes', with a distribution statement giving per-modality coverage. Nine subsets carry is_subpopulation: true and is_data_split: false. instances lists four typed measurement types. direct_collection records the only donor-level fact in the record: 'the KOLF2.1J iPSC line was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor and is available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource', and MDA-MB-468 as ATCC-sourced. known_biases records that the data 'does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'. at_risk_populations and missing_data_documentation are absent. Subgroup characterization is detailed and well structured, but the subgroups are biological (cell line, differentiation state, treatment arm) rather than human-demographic. Donor demographics amount to a single line — sex, health status and broad ancestry for one of the two lines, nothing for the other — and there are no inclusion/exclusion criteria because there was no participant selection. A 3 reflects general human-derived data whose population characterization is thin, while crediting the precise and internally consistent subgroup structure the record does provide. Scoring here must not penalize the record for lacking demographics it could not have: with no human participants, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria would be semantically inappropriate. What is properly expected — provenance and representativeness of the human-derived material — is partly met. The record is candid that the sample is non-representative (sampling_strategies.is_representative: false with why_not_representative, echoed in known_biases), which is the honest statement for two cell lines. The gap is that donor characteristics for MDA-MB-468 are absent entirely and KOLF2.1J's are minimal, so a reuser assessing ancestry coverage for a model has almost nothing to work with.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C' and id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://cm4ai.org/'; publisher 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/'; distribution_formats.access_urls 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; external_resources 'https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline', 'https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/', 'https://fairscape.github.io', 'http://integrativemodeling.org'. Passes comfortably. A registered DOI, a project landing page, a repository publisher URL, a w3id schema URI and four resolvable tool/documentation URLs give several independent routes to the dataset and its context. All URLs are structurally well formed and point to plausible, well-known domains for this field; w3id.org is a persistence service and github.com/readthedocs are stable hosting for the named toolkit. Two minor notes that do not affect the pass: integrativemodeling.org is given as http rather than https, and the DOI's own Dataverse landing page is never given as a URL, with page instead pointing at the project portal.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats: format ZIP, media_type application/zip, access_urls 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/', notes 'All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Files above the 1.9 GB browser download limit are obtained through the Data Access API.' license_and_use_terms sets CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with no_commercial_use, implying open access without a DUA or login for the non-embargoed material. third_party_sharing.is_shared: true, with MassIVE and Figshare as alternative sources. raw_data_sources marks two perturb-seq sources 'Embargoed'. No download_url field. The access path is largely defined: the hosting platform is named, the retrieval mechanism is specified, and the record anticipates the practical obstacle a reuser will actually hit — the 1.9 GB browser limit that affects the three multi-gigabyte image archives — and gives the API workaround. Access policy follows unambiguously from an open CC license with no registration requirement stated. Full marks are withheld because the API endpoint is a bare stem with no file identifiers, and because the embargoed subsets are flagged without any route to request them. Consistency between license and access holds: an open reuse license is matched by an open retrieval mechanism with no DUA, which is the coherent pairing. The practical shortfall is that the documented path stops one step short of retrieval — a consumer following 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/' without a file ID reaches nothing, and the record supplies file names and MD5s but never the Dataverse file identifiers that would complete the URL. Naming MassIVE and Figshare as alternative sources without accessions has the same shape: an access route stated but not made actionable.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms sets out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 operatively, including the attribution, non-commercial and share-alike conditions, the no-further-restrictions clause and a requirement to cite both the related publication and the data collection. intended_uses gives four use_category entries with examples ('AI-ready data for functional genomics research', 'AI model training', 'Cellular process analysis', 'Analysis of cell architecture under perturbation'). prohibited_uses gives two entries with reasons: clinical decision-making and patient care 'without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', and commercial use, tied to both the NC clause and the separate-negotiation requirement. known_limitations adds four scoped caveats including the absence of computed cell maps and the need for domain expertise. discouraged_uses and future_use_impacts are both absent. License plus use guidance is met well beyond the 3-point band — prohibitions carry reasons rather than bare assertions, intended uses are categorized with examples, and the limitations section tells a reuser what the release cannot support. The fifth point requires social impact analysis with mitigation strategies, and that is absent: future_use_impacts is empty, so no downstream risk is identified and no mitigation proposed. The nearest thing to impact analysis sits in fields belonging to other questions — data_governance describes an Ethics team plan for 'ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision' and a 'CM4AI Life Cycle' governance framework, and ethical_reviews describes a Value-Sensitive Design methodology. These are governance processes for producing the data, not an analysis of the societal risks of reusing it, so they do not substitute. The clinical-use prohibition is the one place where a downstream harm is named, and it is correctly reasoned from the absence of regulatory approval for laboratory data.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: version_access lists the full predecessor lineage with DOIs and latest_version_doi. updates gives a quarterly cadence through November 2026. raw_data_sources enumerates seven upstream sources with type and access_details, mapping each released modality to its origin repository (MassIVE, Figshare) or embargo state. related_datasets supplies typed lineage (three is_new_version_of links, is_described_by, is_referenced_by, references). subsets record is_data_split: false explicitly for all nine entries, and each subset names the file_collection that distributes it while each file_collection names the subset it contains. Every file_collection carries an MD5 checksum. conforms_to describes FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate packaging with 'provenance graphs and rich metadata', and notes describes ARK identifiers with 'provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology'. Absent: errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation, splits. This goes well past 'version history only'. Derivation is documented in two directions — upstream to the raw acquisitions and their repositories, and laterally to predecessor releases through typed relations — and file-level MD5 fixity gives integrity checking that most records omit entirely. The elements of an entity-activity-agent structure are all present but scattered across fields: entities in subsets and file_collections, activities in acquisition_methods, agents in data_collectors and creators. Full marks require a provenance graph with those relationships expressed as such, and this record describes one rather than containing one: the RO-Crate and EVI Evidence Graph claims are narrative, carried from the preprint and earlier releases, and the record itself concedes that the June 2026 release page does not restate the packaging format. The explicit subset↔file_collection ID linkage is a genuine in-record graph fragment and is why this sits at 4 rather than 3. Quality documentation is the weaker half: missing_data_documentation is empty and no QC metrics are reported for any modality, so integrity is well evidenced at the byte level and unevidenced at the measurement level.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases contains exactly one entry: bias_type 'representation_bias', bias_description 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.' future_use_impacts is absent. Related but separately located material: sampling_strategies records is_random: false, is_representative: false and why_not_representative repeating the same sentence, plus 'Targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets rather than random sampling'; known_limitations records that 'Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging), and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap.' The single bias is correctly identified, correctly typed against a taxonomy enum value, and explained in terms a modeller can act on. But one entry is thin coverage for a multi-modal release, there is no fairness analysis of any kind, no AIO mapping, and no statement of downstream impact. This sits at the 3-point 'basic bias identification' band, lifted to the top of that band by the correct use of a taxonomy term rather than free text. The record documents two further biases without categorizing them, which is the substantive shortfall. Its own sampling_strategies field describes non-random targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets — a textbook selection bias — and known_limitations describes incompletely overlapping protein coverage across the three modalities, which will systematically bias any integrative model toward the intersection. Both are stated as facts elsewhere and omitted from known_biases, so a consumer reading the bias field alone receives an incomplete picture. Logged as a medium consistency issue.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (12/14): id='doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title='Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,900 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission='general_research_use' with a full license_terms paragraph; doi='10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page='https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (15 principal investigators, each with affiliations); purposes (5 responses); instances (2 types, 'counts: 833'); variables (4 entries); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level='restricted'. Absent (2/14): resources, parent_datasets. 12 of 14 named fields are populated with substantive rather than placeholder content, which lands at 85.7% - above the 70% anchor for 3 and below the 90% anchor for 5. Two structural containment fields are missing, and variables, while present, enumerates only four columns for a release whose phenotype tables span confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata, so the field is populated but thin relative to the data it describes. Field content is semantically appropriate to its slot throughout: id and doi agree, page resolves to the version-matched PhysioNet path, and confidentiality_level='restricted' is consistent with the credentialed and controlled access tiers described in data_governance. The missing parent_datasets is partly compensated semantically by related_datasets.is_new_version_of pointing at doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84, but that is a sibling relationship field, not the containment field the rubric names, so it does not restore the count.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is approximately 1,900 characters, covering cohort structure, protocol, participant count (833), release contents, the withheld raw audio, and the AI-readiness self-assessment. purposes contains five responses averaging roughly 230 characters each, e.g. 'To introduce the field of acoustic biomarkers by developing new standards of acoustic and voice data collection and analysis for voice AI research, including interoperable bioinformatics standards for voice data.' Both narrative fields are an order of magnitude above the 200-character threshold, and the length is informative rather than padded: the description carries specific counts, named formats and an explicit statement of what is excluded from the release. Length here correlates with genuine information density - the description states what the release contains, what it does not contain, and why. The one semantic caveat is that the description's five-cohort list includes the pediatric category that is in fact distributed separately, which is a scoping imprecision rather than a length deficiency and is therefore recorded as an issue rather than scored here.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: ['health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'] - four unique terms. Supplementary topical anchors exist outside keywords: instances carry data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:25 and B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; labeling_strategies states 'Labels follow the Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes'; conforms_to_standard lists BIDS. Four keywords places the record squarely in the 3-7 band. The terms are also low in discriminative power: 'health' and 'biomarkers' would match a large share of the biomedical corpus, and none of the five clinical cohorts, the acoustic modalities (cough, breathing, speech) or the derived feature families appears as a searchable term. Per the rubric note, I checked whether condition lists or external ontology references supplement the keyword field. They do exist (B2AI_TOPIC / B2AI_SUBSTRATE codes on instances, ICD-10 referenced in labeling_strategies) but they are embedded in composition and labeling structures rather than exposed as topical descriptors, and the ICD-10 reference names a coding system without enumerating codes. They therefore mitigate the discoverability gap slightly but do not lift the count into the 8+ band.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists three entries spanning four distinct media types: (1) 'Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format, holding the dense derived audio features'; (2) 'Tab-separated values with accompanying JSON data dictionaries'; (3) 'WAV audio files with accompanying JSON sidecars, organized per the Brain Imaging Data Structure'. Unique types: Parquet, TSV, JSON, WAV. file_collections, total_file_count and total_size_bytes are absent; per-feature counts appear only in source_caveats ('32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files'). Four distinct file types exceed the >3 threshold for 5, and each format entry is described by payload rather than by extension alone, so a reuser can tell which format carries which content. The enumeration half of the question is weaker: no structured file counts or byte totals are given, and the counts that exist are buried in a caveats paragraph. Format variety here reflects genuine multi-modality documented elsewhere in the record - dense numeric feature arrays in Parquet, tabular phenotype data in TSV with JSON dictionaries, and waveform audio in WAV under BIDS - rather than incidental format proliferation. The banding for this question is defined on file-type count, which is met; the missing enumeration fields are recorded as a separate completeness issue and are the substance of Q5's evidence base.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[0].counts: 833 ('research participant'); description: 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants across five North American sites'; source_caveats gives per-feature file counts (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram files) and an alternative documentation figure of approximately 61,937 voice-derived recordings; splits and subpopulations are both populated. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent. Pass: an explicit numeric instance count (833 participants) is present in a structured field and corroborated in the description, and dimensional metadata (splits, subpopulations) is populated. No byte-level size is available, so a reuser can estimate scale only indirectly from recording counts. The participant count is internally consistent between instances.counts and the description. The recording-level counts conflict across sources (approximately 61,937 in project documentation versus per-feature counts on PhysioNet), but the record resolves the conflict explicitly and states that the PhysioNet figures were preferred as the higher-ranked source - disclosure that preserves the credibility of the numbers rather than undermining it.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id: 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page: 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; version_access.latest_version_doi: 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'; version_access.version_details lists 10.13026/249v-w155 (v1.1), 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0) and 10.57764/qb6h-em84 (initial Health Data Nexus release); citation carries 'PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345.' Hosting platform is named in citation, maintainers ('PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology') and data_governance.stewardship_roles. Pass on every limb of the question. The identifier set is unusually complete for a versioned dataset: a version-pinned DOI identifying this record, a version-agnostic DOI for the latest release, and per-version DOIs for the release history. The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's DataCite prefix and matches the declared host, so identifier and platform corroborate each other. Two minor points that do not affect the pass: there is no top-level publisher field (PhysioNet is identified only in citation, maintainers and stewardship_roles), and RRID:SCR_007345 identifies PhysioNet as a resource rather than this dataset, so it functions as repository provenance rather than a dataset identifier.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund'; funders[0].grants: [OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1]; funders[0].notes: 'The funded project period runs from 1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026, with the project administered by the University of South Florida.' creators lists 15 principal investigators each with an affiliations entry, e.g. Yael Bensoussan / USF Health Morsani College of Medicine, Olivier Elemento / Englander Institute for Precision Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine, Satrajit Ghosh / Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Jennifer Siu / The Hospital for Sick Children. Both limbs of the 5 band are fully satisfied and then exceeded: award numbers are given (not just the agency), the funded period and administering institution are stated, and every one of the 15 named creators carries an institutional affiliation, with two flagged as co-principal investigators via notes. OT2OD032720 validates against the NIH pattern (OT2 other-transaction activity code, OD for Office of the Director, six-digit serial), which is the correct activity code and institute for a Common Fund Bridge2AI award, and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 is a well-formed supplement rendering of the same core award. Funding purpose and dataset purpose align: purposes describe generating a diverse voice dataset and building audiomics infrastructure, which is what a Bridge2AI data generation project is funded to do. source_caveats discloses five divergent renderings of the award number across sources, including an evidently corrupted footer variant; the two carried in funders.grants are the well-formed ones, so the variance is handled correctly and does not reduce the score.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: three reviewing organizations (USF IRB as single IRB; Research Ethics Board, The Hospital for Sick Children; Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group, which 'identified the sensitive fields removed from the release and produced a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for controlled access to raw voice data samples'). human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects=true with irb_approval, ethics_review_board (including Canadian REB arrangements), regulatory_compliance (HIPAA de-identification, NIH STRIDES hosting) and special_populations. is_deidentified: method='HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers...', with a full identifiers_removed enumeration and deidentification_details ('Dates are rebased and replaced by integers... K-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved'). participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (two-tier access model), reidentification_risk, data_linkage ('Participants are identified by internal study numbers... not shared between sites'). participant_compensation: $40 under 90 minutes, $80 over, capped at $120 across three sessions, adults only. at_risk_populations: at_risk_groups_included=true with special_protections (cognitive impairment, dementia, psychiatric conditions, pediatric), guardian_consent and assent_procedures including the under-seven exception. informed_consent: consent_obtained=true with consent_type (four modalities including a video-read statement to verify voice provenance), consent_scope, consent_documentation, withdrawal_mechanism. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant='compliant'; other_compliance records a Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguard obligations and five-business-day breach reporting. Supporting: collection_consents, collection_notifications, consent_revocations, retention_limit. This is the most complete ethics documentation the rubric contemplates. Every protection area named in the question is populated with operational specifics rather than assertions: compensation is quantified with caps, assent has an age-based exception rule, withdrawal distinguishes pre- and post-collection cases, and the ethics working group's role in field-level redaction is documented. There is no field literally named data_protection_impacts, but its substance is present across participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, the sensitive-field redaction memorandum, and the safeguard and breach-reporting obligations in other_compliance. Cross-field logic holds on every check: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a named method and by participant_privacy protections; sensitive_elements (race, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health data, voice itself) are matched by the corresponding access controls. The de-identification method is appropriate to the data type and is in fact stricter than Safe Harbor, correctly recognising that voice is biometric and withholding it. One semantic tension is recorded as an issue: the boolean is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false sits against the prose admission that k-anonymity k>=2 is not achieved and that voice re-identification cannot be excluded, and the released spectrogram and MFCC features retain speaker-discriminative signal. I did not deduct for it, because the record discloses the residual risk explicitly and gates the release behind registered access - the defect is in the expressiveness of one boolean, not in the coverage the question measures.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission='general_research_use' with license_terms specifying the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, mandatory approval and signature of the Registered Access Agreement, permitted duplication, prohibition on sale, non-assertion of IP against access, adherence to the Fort Lauderdale Agreement and 'no fees associated with these restrictions'. ip_restrictions.restrictions sets out third-party rights disclaimers, non-transfer of IP, and downstream IP subject to non-obstructive licensing. regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level='restricted'; hipaa_compliant='compliant'; regulatory_restrictions ('No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply'); other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguards, five-business-day breach reporting, PhysioNet.org requirements). data_governance.committee_name='Bridge2AI-Voice Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with a full access_review_process for both tiers, accountable_organization 'University of South Florida', and stewardship_roles giving the contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. All four components of the 5 band are present and operational. The documentation distinguishes the two access tiers, names the reviewing body, gives a contact address, states the confidentiality classification, and covers both the licence and the residual IP position - including the unusual and useful statement that no fees attach. The governance posture is coherent with the sensitivity claims: confidentiality_level='restricted' matches a two-tier gated release of health data with a Certificate of Confidentiality, and would have been implausible had it read 'public'. The licence terms and the prohibited_uses entries agree with one another (both prohibit sale and re-identification, both require non-obstructive downstream licensing). There is a mild internal tension between prohibited_uses' invocation of 'Open Science principles' and 'future use of the dataset remains unrestricted' on the one hand and the gated access model on the other, but read in context the clause restrains IP-based blocking rather than describing open access, so it is consistent. governance_committee_contact is not a literal field name, yet the contact is unambiguously supplied.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: Apache Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format'), tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries, WAV with JSON sidecars. conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. related_datasets carries typed relationships: is_supplemented_by -> doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric), is_new_version_of -> doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. Integration keys are documented in variables: participant_id 'present in every Parquet feature file and used to join the phenotype tables' and session_id. instances carry ontology terms B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30. external_resources names the Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker and the b2aiprep and senselab processing libraries; labeling_strategies references ICD-10 coding. The 5 band requires all three limbs and each is independently evidenced. Formats are open and non-proprietary; schema conformance is asserted at three levels (BIDS for audio layout, a versioned w3id LinkML schema for the datasheet, JSON data dictionaries for the tables); and integration capability is concrete rather than aspirational, since the join keys are named and their presence across files is stated. The claimed standards are the right ones for the data type - BIDS is the established layout standard for this class of recordings, Parquet is appropriate for dense feature arrays, and TSV with JSON sidecars follows the same BIDS idiom for tabular data - so the conformance claims are semantically plausible rather than decorative. Cross-platform linkage is real: the record links PhysioNet, Synapse and the Health Data Nexus with typed relationships and version-specific DOIs. Minor gaps that do not displace the 5: file_collections.compression is unspecified, and the FHIR profile entry concedes 'does not give a repository URL in the captured text', so one interoperability artefact is named without a resolvable location.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: eight entries with named tools and explicit parameters - monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT spectrograms at 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled by two in time; 60 MFCCs and 60-bin Mel spectrograms at the same parameters; articulatory features via 'the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package... all gathered at 50 Hz'; 'Acoustic features were extracted with openSMILE, and phonetic and prosodic features... computed with Parselmouth and Praat'; phonetic posteriorgrams over '40 acoustic units of speech at 100 Hz' via the ppgs package; transcriptions via 'OpenAI's Whisper Large model'; BIDS v1.9.0 conversion with the ReproSchema-UI to REDCap to BIDS path for pediatric data. cleaning_strategies: two entries including a per-release audit protocol (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema checks on categorical responses, silence and duration QC on audio, produced-versus-intended passage comparison). labeling_strategies: labeling_details, annotations_per_item=1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol (ICD-10), data_annotation_platform (REDCap diagnosis forms). machine_annotation_tools: tools=[OpenAI Whisper Large], tool_descriptions, tool_accuracy='...generated using off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'. missing_data_documentation: causes, patterns and handling_strategy ('A missingness table is generated as part of the audit protocol... no imputation is applied'). imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses are absent as fields. Strategy coverage is excellent and unusually reproducible - the signal-processing parameters given are sufficient for an independent party to regenerate comparable features, and the QC protocol is described step by step. What holds this below 5 is the versions-and-URLs limb of the band: not one tool carries a version number (openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, sparc and ppgs are named bare, and 'Whisper Large' names a model size rather than a pinned revision), and the tool URLs that exist sit in external_resources for the wrapper libraries rather than against the tools themselves. Annotation quality is explicitly unmeasured. Tool-to-task assignment is technically correct throughout: openSMILE for static acoustic descriptors, Parselmouth/Praat for F0, formants and voice quality, sparc for articulatory kinematics, ppgs for posteriorgrams, Whisper for transcription. The stated parameters are mutually consistent (25 ms window with 10 ms hop implies the usual 100 Hz frame rate, matching the 100 Hz posteriorgram rate) and consistent with the 16 kHz resampling and the 400-point FFT. The absence of imputation_protocols is semantically coherent rather than a gap, because handling_strategy states no imputation is applied. The tool_accuracy disclosure that transcriptions were not audited is credited as honest documentation, but it does mean no annotation quality evidence exists to satisfy the top band.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: four typed entries (was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified, was_inferred_derived) each with acquisition_details, e.g. 'Clinical diagnoses were verified by clinicians reviewing audio and/or imaging data, consulting electronic health records, or examining medication prescriptions, in accordance with established gold standards for each disease cohort.' collection_mechanisms: four entries covering the adult tablet application, reproschema-ui for pediatrics, REDCap capture and export, and hardware ('iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; a head-mounted headset with microphone was used where possible'). data_collectors: three entries (research teams including students, clinicians providing gold standard assessment and listed as IRB co-investigators, hospital staff assisting logistics). raw_data_sources: two entries with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details including the Synapse location. sampling_strategies and direct_collection further characterise recruitment. collection_timeframes: 'The data were collected over a period of 12 months', with source_caveats recording the conflicting four-year IRB protocol, pilot collection from November 2023 ongoing into November 2024, and a feasibility window of 5 June to 28 July 2023. Four of the five named field groups are documented to a standard well above the rubric's 5 anchor - the hardware detail in particular is the kind of information that determines whether acoustic results replicate. The timeframe component, which the 5 band names explicitly alongside methods and collectors, is the weak limb: a bare '12 months' with no anchor dates does not tell a reuser when the data were collected, and the record's own caveat states the sources do not settle whether those 12 months sit inside the wider study period. I scored 4 on that basis; the deduction is for the unresolved and unanchored timeframe, not for the disclosure, which is to the record's credit. Acquisition typing is used correctly: directly observed for the in-clinic recordings, subject-reported for questionnaires, validated for clinician diagnoses, and inferred/derived for the released acoustic features - the last of which correctly signals that the public release is a derivation rather than a primary observation. Collector roles are differentiated in a way that matters for bias interpretation (students administering the protocol, clinicians assigning labels), and this connects coherently to the annotation_bias entry in known_biases. The temporal check is the one that fails: the 12-month figure cannot be reconciled with the four-year protocol on the evidence given, and issued (2026-05-01) sits about 18 months after the November 2024 collection activity described, a gap the record does not explain.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '3.1.0'. version_access: versions_available ('Version 1.0 on the Health Data Nexus, and versions 1.1, 2.0.0, 2.0.1, 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 on PhysioNet'), latest_version_doi 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42', and version_details listing per-version DOIs plus the policy that 'older versions of the dataset continue to be supported, hosted and made available to researchers'. errata: three substantive entries (v2.0.0 reprocessed spectrograms and removed free-speech-derived spectrograms and MFCCs; v2.0.1 corrected the authorship list; v3.1.0 fixed broken Parquet files from v3.0.0 and back-filled validated diagnosis information). updates: frequency 'Semi-annual (twice a year)' with update_details covering triggers, notification channels and per-version DOIs. distribution_dates gives dated release notes for all six versions. maintainers: three entries with roles (government_agency for NIH via Bridge2AI; academic_institution for PhysioNet / MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; academic_institution for the Health Data Nexus / T-CAIREM at the University of Toronto). Sustainability limbs: persistent identifiers (multiple DOIs), governance (data_governance with DACO and accountable_organization 'University of South Florida'), domain-appropriate repository (PhysioNet for biomedical data), institutional commitment (NIH funding to 30 November 2026, retention_limit 'Indefinite, for as long as the data remain useful for research purposes', extension_mechanism for derivative datasets). Every component of the 5 band is present with specifics. The errata in particular are exemplary: they name what changed, in which version, and why, including a data-integrity fix (broken Parquet files) that a reuser of v3.0.0 would need to know about. The sustainability picture is complete across all four indicators the rubric lists. Version identifiers, DOIs and release dates are mutually consistent: version 3.1.0 matches the page URL path, the DOI recorded in version_details for 3.1.0, and the 1 May 2026 release date, which in turn matches issued='2026-05-01T00:00:00Z'. The version-agnostic and version-pinned DOIs are correctly distinguished, which is the distinction most often botched. Two observations that I weighed but did not deduct for: there is no top-level publisher field, though PhysioNet is named in three other fields; and known_limitations records that the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment fails 'the domain-appropriate and associated criteria under sustainability' (50 percent), which sits oddly against a record that documents a domain-appropriate repository and indefinite retention. I read the self-assessment as applying to the wider programme's preservation funding beyond the November 2026 award end rather than contradicting the documented facts, and scored the documentation in front of me.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation is a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, authors, year, version and publisher: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. Distinct additional references in external_resources: (1) eipm/bridge2ai-redcap with Zenodo archive https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724; (2) sensein/b2aiprep at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep; (3) sensein/senselab at https://github.com/sensein/senselab; (4) eipm/bridge2ai-docs at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ with Zenodo archive https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; (5) Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles; (6) the Bridge2AI-Voice Scholars programme at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/. related_datasets adds two DOI-identified datasets. The 5 condition is met twice over: a formal dataset citation naming title, authors and publishing organization is present, and there are six distinct external references (two of them DOI-archived on Zenodo) plus two DOI-identified related datasets, well beyond the two required. Repeated links to the same resource were counted once. The citation is well formed for a versioned PhysioNet deposit - it pins the version, resolves through the version-specific DOI, and matches the authorship recorded in creators (the record even notes in errata that v2.0.1 corrected the authorship list, and in source_caveats that PhysioNet spellings were preferred over the documentation's 'Jennifer Sui' and 'Frank Rudzizc'). One substantive gap that does not change the band: no journal publications are cited. The feasibility study is mentioned three times in source_caveats and collection_timeframes but is never given a citation or DOI, and the AI-readiness recommendations quoted at length in the description are likewise uncited. A reuser therefore cannot follow the literature this dataset rests on from the record alone.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 'research participant' with counts 833 and a label_description assigning each participant to a disease cohort or the control group; 'audio recording' identified by participant, session and task. subpopulations: entry 1 - 'Demographic sub-populations are identified by age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status in the demographics table', with distribution noting skews 'based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors' and that under-recruited groups include those with 'less trust in the medical system or in AI'; entry 2 - the five disease cohort categories plus controls, with distribution noting the releases 'do not contain an equal distribution of these disease categories'. at_risk_populations: cognitive impairment, dementia, psychiatric conditions and pediatric participants, with special_protections, guardian_consent and assent_procedures. missing_data_documentation: causes, patterns (rows present only where at least one column is non-missing; multiple rows per participant across visits) and handling_strategy. Criteria: sampling_strategies refers to 'the corresponding inclusion and exclusion criteria' without enumerating them; known_limitations supplies concrete exclusions (English-only, Spanish protocols still under development) and the description confines the release to adults. Population characterisation is well above 'general human data without subgroup description': two structured subpopulation framings, an at-risk population inventory with tailored protections, and honest skew disclosure. It falls short of the 5 band on two counts - the demographic axes are named but never quantified, so no stratum count for sex, age, race or ethnicity appears anywhere in the record, and the inclusion/exclusion criteria are referenced rather than enumerated per cohort. The subpopulation account is semantically consistent with known_biases: the recruitment-trust and proximity skew appears both as subpopulations.distribution and as selection_bias, and the site-and-device confound appears both here and as measurement_bias, so the two sections corroborate rather than contradict each other. The at-risk inventory is consistent with the consent machinery in Q8 (assent procedures for children, comprehension checks for cognitive impairment). One scoping wrinkle noted at Q2 recurs here: subpopulations lists the pediatric category among the five cohorts before stating that the adult dataset contains adults only, which a reuser could misread as a stratum available in this release.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page: 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; doi: '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id: 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; citation resolves via 'https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; distribution_formats.access_urls give the PhysioNet landing page and 'https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/'; external_resources give GitHub, Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.12760724, 10.5281/zenodo.13834653), https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ and https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/; version_access lists five further DOIs. Pass with margin. The record supplies a version-pinned DOI, a version-agnostic DOI, a landing page on a domain-appropriate repository, a controlled-access location, archived code DOIs and a documentation site - findability is served for the dataset, its history, its code and its documentation. All URLs are structurally well formed and point at plausible, appropriate domains (physionet.org, synapse.org, github.com, zenodo.org, and consortium subdomains). The PhysioNet path embeds the version 3.1.0, so the landing page is consistent with the version-pinned DOI it accompanies. The only findability blemish is the FHIR profiles entry, which names a resource and states that no repository URL was available in the captured text.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats: each of the three entries carries access_urls and a note stating why no direct endpoint exists, e.g. 'No direct download URL is published: the PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing and a signed data use agreement, so the access URL is the project landing page rather than a file endpoint', and for the WAV tier 'access requires review by the Data Access Compliance Office and an institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement'. license_and_use_terms: 'credentialed users must be approved and must sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement before accessing the files'. data_governance.access_review_process: 'Registered access to the feature-only data requires registration on PhysioNet, confirmation of identity, and signature of the Bridge2AI-Voice Registered Access Agreement. Controlled access to raw audio requires completion of a Data Access Request Form and a Data Use Agreement, submission... to the Data Access Compliance Office for review and, upon approval, a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the applicant's institution.' Contact: DACO@b2ai-voice.org. download_url is absent by design. The access tier is stated explicitly and separately for each of the two distribution tiers, with the required artefacts, the reviewing body, the signing authority and a contact address. This is precisely the distinction the rubric warns is usually elided: nothing here is described as 'public' or 'open', and the registered tier is clearly separated from the DACO-reviewed controlled tier. The absence of download_url is not a documentation gap but an accurate reflection of a gated release, and the record says so in three places rather than leaving a reuser to infer it - which is better documentation than an unresolvable URL would be. The access description is consistent with confidentiality_level='restricted', with the consent scope (which anticipates both registered and controlled release), and with the sensitivity rationale for withholding raw audio. One friction point for reuse, noted but not deducted: collaborators at other organisations and even other teams at the same organisation 'must apply independently', which is restrictive but clearly stated in advance.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms: Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License with data_use_permission='general_research_use' and detailed terms. intended_uses: two categories - research (AI/ML model development, clinical research in screening, diagnosis and monitoring, pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking, validation) with usage_notes restricting use to approved Authorized Researchers, and cohort selection via the phenotype questionnaire features. prohibited_uses: five entries covering re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatization, IP-based blocking of access, sale of data, and contacting subjects without IRB approval and consent. discouraged_uses: two entries covering hiring, insurance premium adjustment and surveillance uses 'to prevent unethical or biased outcomes', and uses that ignore the dataset's skews. future_use_impacts: two entries covering skew-driven 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups' and the ELSI landscape of voice AI (voice re-identification, voice AI hacking, data sharing and privacy, gender and racial diversity effects). Mitigations appear as known_biases.mitigation_strategy (remote collection, controlled recruiting, Spanish expansion) and known_limitations.recommended_mitigation ('Assess the multivariate distribution of disorder category, site and demographics before using the data for a given question'). All three limbs of the 5 band are satisfied with specificity. The prohibited and discouraged use lists are concrete and domain-aware - naming insurance pricing, hiring and surveillance as the realistic misuse vectors for health-linked voice data rather than reciting generic terms - and each carries a stated reason, so a reviewer can apply them to a novel case. Use guidance and risk analysis are mutually reinforcing rather than duplicative: the skew documented in subpopulations and known_biases is what discouraged_uses tells reusers to account for, and the re-identification risk documented in participant_privacy is what prohibited_uses forbids exploiting. The distinction between prohibited (agreement-backed) and discouraged (advisory) is used correctly. The intended_uses note that research may be 'commercial and non-commercial' is consistent with collection_consents, which states the consent does not restrict data to non-commercial use - a consent-to-licence check that many records fail and this one passes.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Entities: raw_data_sources names 'Raw audio waveforms of the acoustic tasks... recorded from participants with the Bridge2AI-Voice application' (WAV under BIDS) and 'Demographic, confounder, clinical validation and validated questionnaire responses captured in REDCap... and in ReproSchema-UI' (REDCap export to TSV with JSON dictionaries), each with source_type and access_details. Activities: acquisition_methods.was_inferred_derived ('The released acoustic features... were derived computationally from the raw audio waveforms') plus the eight-step preprocessing_strategies chain from resampling through feature extraction to BIDS v1.9.0 conversion, and the de-identification activity in is_deidentified.deidentification_details. Agents: named software (b2aiprep 'used to organize and preprocess the dataset, convert the raw audio waveforms into the Parquet feature files and merge the source data into the phenotype files', senselab, sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, ppgs, Whisper Large) and human agents (research teams, site clinicians, the ethics working group). Version integrity: version_access, three errata including 'Version 3.1.0 fixed broken Parquet files carried in the version 3.0.0 release', updates with semi-annual cadence. Quality: missing_data_documentation (causes, patterns, handling), cleaning_strategies audit protocol, anomalies (three entries). splits: 'No recommended training, validation or test splits are provided.' Derivation linkage: related_datasets.is_new_version_of -> doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. This exceeds version history alone, which is the rubric's 3 band. The full path from participant to released artefact is recoverable: which entity was collected, by which agent, through which activity with which parameters, into which released format, under which version. The rubric expressly accepts text provenance where lineage is complete, and it is complete here. The lineage is internally consistent - the raw WAV entity named in raw_data_sources is the input to the preprocessing chain, whose outputs are exactly the Parquet and TSV products enumerated in distribution_formats, and the withheld-audio policy is stated identically in raw_data_sources.access_details, distribution_formats and is_deidentified. Quality documentation is unusually candid: anomalies concede protocol drift across sites and time and that some audio could not generate features, and that concession is consistent with missing_data_documentation and with the measurement_bias entry. The structural weakness, recorded as an issue rather than a deduction, is that was_derived_from and parent_datasets are empty, so the derivation path is machine-readable only through the typed is_new_version_of link and must otherwise be reconstructed by a human reading four separate prose fields - which also undercuts the description's claim of 100 percent on provenance in the consortium self-assessment.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: four entries with enumerated bias_type values - representation_bias ('collected at a limited number of geographic locations across five recording sites in the United States and Canada, and includes only fluent English speakers'), with mitigation_strategy (remote collection, controlled recruiting, Spanish expansion); selection_bias ('Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited'); measurement_bias ('different disease groups also had their data collected on different devices and under different collection configurations'), with affected_subsets 'Disease cohorts recruited at distinct recording sites'; annotation_bias ('Diagnostic labels were assigned by a single labeler per instance, and the basis of the diagnosis varied by disorder'). future_use_impacts: skew-driven risk of 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups' and the voice AI ELSI landscape including 'the influence of gender and racial diversity on the development and application of these technologies'. Supporting: known_limitations (six entries, including the consortium's own failed AI-readiness criteria), anomalies (three entries), subpopulations.distribution. Categorisation uses four distinct taxonomy-conformant values with mechanistic, dataset-specific descriptions rather than boilerplate, which is beyond the 3 band's 'basic bias identification without taxonomy'. It stops short of 5 on three counts: only one of four biases carries a mitigation_strategy and only one carries affected_subsets; no AIO or other ontology identifiers are attached to the bias_type values; and fairness analysis is entirely qualitative, with no subgroup counts or parity measures anywhere in the record to support quantitative assessment. The bias types are applied correctly to the right phenomena - device and site confounding is genuinely measurement bias, single-labeler variation is genuinely annotation bias, and English-only multi-site recruitment is genuinely representation bias - so the taxonomy is used with understanding rather than as labels. The measurement_bias entry is the most valuable because it identifies a confound (disease cohort aligned with recording site and device) that would let a model learn site rather than pathology, which is the central validity threat for this data type. The bias account is consistent with subpopulations.distribution, sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and known_limitations, and the absence of stratum counts noted at Q15 is precisely what prevents the fairness analysis here from becoming quantitative.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (12/14): id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,480 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, data_use_permission general_research_use); doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (15 named investigators with affiliations); purposes (4 responses); instances (2 entries, 833 participants plus per-feature record counts); variables (13 entries with data types and derivations); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (2/14): resources, parent_datasets. Twelve of fourteen named fields are populated and every one of them carries substantive rather than token content — variables give per-column derivations, instances give both participant and per-feature record counts, creators give institutional affiliations. The two gaps are the hierarchical fields, which places coverage at 85.7%, between the 70% band for 3 and the 90% band for 5. The missing hierarchical fields are a placement gap, not missing knowledge: related_datasets carries six typed relationships with resolvable DOIs (is_new_version_of, is_version_of, is_supplemented_by, is_documented_by) and was_derived_from names the raw audio and REDCap origin. I did not credit that content under Q1, because Q1 scores the named fields, but I note it did not cost the record anything under Q19, where the lineage is scored on its substance.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 1,480 characters, covering provenance ('generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program'), scale ('833 adult participants recruited at five sites in North America'), cohort composition, protocol, and an explicit statement of what is and is not released ('The original voice recordings are withheld from this release and distributed only under controlled access'). The four purposes responses run approximately 380, 250, 280 and 240 characters. Average narrative length is far beyond the 200-character threshold, and the length is informative rather than padded: the description alone conveys scale, cohorts, acquisition protocol, the full feature inventory and the release boundary. Length and specificity coincide here, which is the case the rubric's length proxy is trying to detect. The description names concrete artifacts (spectrograms, MFCCs, SPARC articulatory traces, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth/torchaudio static features) that recur consistently in preprocessing_strategies, variables and distribution_formats, so the narrative is corroborated by the structured fields rather than floating free of them.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice (4 unique). Supplementary topical coding exists outside the keywords field: instances carry data_topic 'B2AI_TOPIC:4' and 'B2AI_TOPIC:36' and data_substrate 'B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30'; conforms_to_standard lists 'BIDS'; labeling_strategies references ICD-10 codes; subpopulations enumerates the five disease cohorts. Four unique keywords place this squarely in the 3-7 band. The rubric permits supplementation by schema-defined condition lists and ontology references, and some exists (B2AI topic/substrate codes, ICD-10, BIDS), but it is sparse and indirect — the cohort names themselves are never exposed as retrievable terms — so it does not lift the record toward the 8-keyword band. This is the clearest findability weakness in an otherwise strong record. Three of the four keywords ('health', 'biomarkers', 'voice') are so general that they do not discriminate this dataset from most of the voice-biomarker literature, and the fourth is a program name. A reader searching for 'Parkinson', 'dysphonia', 'laryngeal', 'depression' or 'spirometry' would not reach this record through its keywords, even though the record's own description and subpopulations establish that all are in scope.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists three entries: 'Apache Parquet' (nine named files: ppgs.parquet, sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet, plus per-recording metadata); 'Tab-separated values' (static_features.tsv, audio_quality_metrics.tsv, and phenotype tables); 'JSON' (a data dictionary per data file). file_collections and total_file_count are absent. WAV appears only in raw_data_sources.raw_data_format as the unreleased source format. Exactly three released formats, which is the top of the 2-3 band and short of the '>3 file types' required for 5. What is present is unusually well enumerated — individual file names are given for the Parquet and TSV tiers — but enumeration quality cannot substitute for the format count the question measures. The three-format count is a truthful consequence of the release design rather than a documentation shortfall: this is a feature-only release, so WAV audio is legitimately excluded and appears only as the source format under controlled access. I scored the released inventory as the question directs. The multi-modality the description claims (voice, speech, breathing, cough) is real but is expressed as distinct feature families within Parquet, not as distinct file types, and the unified participant_id/session_id keys the rubric note asks about are documented in variables and relationships.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[0].counts: 833 study participants. instances[1].notes gives per-feature record counts for v3.1.0: '29,278 records each for spectrograms, mel spectrograms and mel-frequency cepstral coefficients; 32,522 torchaudio pitch records; 28,640 sparc electromagnetic articulography records; 31,855 sparc loudness records; 31,872 sparc periodicity and sparc pitch records; and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram records'. subpopulations (2 entries) and splits are populated. version_access.version_details adds '12,523 recordings for 306 participants' for v1.0. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent. Passes on instance and record counts, which are given at a granularity well beyond the threshold — per-feature-type rather than a single aggregate. No byte size is stated anywhere, so a user can estimate scale but cannot plan storage. The differing per-feature counts are not noise: instances, anomalies and missing_data_documentation independently explain that some recordings could not yield certain features because of length or other issues, so the counts are expected to diverge. That mutual corroboration is a point in the record's favour; the absent byte totals are the one dimension of the question left unserved.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id: 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page: 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; publisher: 'https://physionet.org'; citation includes 'RRID:SCR_007345'; version_access.latest_version_doi: 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'. Passes decisively. Both components the question asks for are present: persistent identifiers (version DOI, concept DOI, RRID) and an explicitly named hosting platform (PhysioNet), with the landing page pinned to the exact version being described. The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's registered DataCite prefix and agrees with both publisher and page — identifier, repository and URL corroborate one another rather than merely coexisting. The record also keeps version and concept DOIs distinct and explains the distinction in source_caveats, which is the correct discipline for a dataset on its sixth release.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
