text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund', with award 'OT2OD032720', the full award title, PhysioNet-credited project number '3OT2OD032720-01S1', NIH RePORTER application 11376382 under '3OT2OD032720-01S3', PI 'Bensoussan, Yael Emilie' at the University of South Florida, FY2025 amount 4,660,942, project start 1 September 2022 and end 30 November 2026. creators: 15 investigators each with a named institutional affiliation (USF, Weill Cornell, Vanderbilt, Hospital for Sick Children, WashU, OHSU, Simon Fraser, The Hastings Center, MIT, Toronto, Sinai Health, Florida), several with credit_roles (funding_acquisition, software) and role notes identifying cohort leads and module co-leads. Both halves of the 5-band are fully satisfied: funders carry grant numbers, and every creator carries an affiliation. The funding entry goes beyond the band by supplying award amount, award period and the RePORTER application ID, which makes the claim independently checkable. OT2OD032720 parses correctly as NIH (OT2 other-transaction activity code, OD for Office of the Director, six-digit serial), and the supplement suffixes -01S1 and -01S3 follow NIH convention. The funding aligns semantically with purposes: the award title 'Voice as a Biomarker of Health' maps directly onto the stated goals of building an ethically sourced voice-health dataset and developing acoustic-biomarker standards. Absence of ORCIDs and of the full 120-author list is noted in source_caveats with a stated rationale, so it is a disclosed scoping choice rather than an omission.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: USF IRB, 'Reviewed and approved the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol and the sharing of the collected data', subsites via single IRB. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval naming USF with separate Canadian REB approvals, regulatory_compliance citing HIPAA with a partial authorization waiver for recruitment plus a Certificate of Confidentiality, special_populations covering cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's and psychiatric diagnoses. is_deidentified: HIPAA Safe Harbor method, an enumerated identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details conceding 'K-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved'. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (federated learning, institution-local REDCap for PHI), reidentification_risk ('a participant's voice cannot be fully de-identified'), data_linkage. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, consent_type (paper/electronic/video), consent_documentation (five-year retention), consent_scope, withdrawal_mechanism. participant_compensation: gift cards, '40 US dollars ... 80 US dollars ... maximum of 120 US dollars'. at_risk_populations: at_risk_groups_included true with named protections. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant 'compliant'; other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, NIH STRIDES). data_governance supplies the committee contact 'DACO@b2ai-voice.org'. data_protection_impacts is populated but states no DPIA was conducted. Every protection area named by the question is populated, and populated with checkable specifics rather than assurances — named IRB, exact compensation amounts and caps, an enumerated identifier-removal list, four distinct consent modalities, and a governance contact address. This is comprehensive coverage and earns the top band. All four ethics consistency rules hold: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and by informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a documented method and by participant_privacy protections. The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type — Safe Harbor for tabular phenotype data, plus withholding of waveforms on the correct reasoning that voice is irreducibly identifying — and the restrictiveness of license_and_use_terms and confidentiality_level 'restricted' matches the stated re-identification risk rather than under- or over-claiming. I weighed reducing this to 4 because data_protection_impacts records that no impact analysis was performed; I did not, because the field is populated, the absence is disclosed rather than concealed, and it is partly substituted by ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published ethical-justification memorandum. The gap is recorded as a medium-severity content_accuracy issue instead, since it is a property of the underlying ethics work rather than of the documentation.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License. Only credentialed PhysioNet users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement may access the files; no additional training is required', with duplication permitted, sale prohibited, Fort Lauderdale Agreement respected and 'no fees'; data_use_permission 'general_research_use'. ip_restrictions: a full paragraph on copyright, no transfer of rights, no IP claims on the data, downstream IP permitted subject to non-obstructive licensing, and 'No third party has imposed intellectual property based restrictions'. regulatory_restrictions: hipaa_compliant 'compliant', confidentiality_level 'restricted', other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, NIH STRIDES agreements). data_governance: committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)', accountable_organization 'University of South Florida Board of Trustees', a two-tier access_review_process, stewardship_roles listing recipient obligations (named authorized persons, safeguards, five-business-day breach notification, destruction or return), and a linked ethical-justification memorandum. All three components of the 5-band are present and specific. Multi-jurisdiction compliance is addressed (US single-IRB plus separate Canadian REB approvals), the confidentiality classification is explicit, and a named governance body with a working contact address is supplied — the access tier is unambiguous rather than described as vaguely 'open'. The governance description is internally coherent across an unusually wide span: the registered-access tier for features and the DACO-reviewed controlled tier for audio recur identically in license_and_use_terms, data_governance.access_review_process, third_party_sharing, raw_data_sources.access_details and informed_consent.consent_scope, so the consent participants gave matches the sharing actually performed. The one blemish is the blanket phrase 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply' sitting immediately above documented HIPAA and Certificate of Confidentiality obligations; I logged it as low severity and did not reduce the score, since the enumerated compliance obligations are stated plainly in the adjacent subfields and no reader would be misled about them.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: Apache Parquet, TSV, JSON — all open, non-proprietary, tool-agnostic. conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: ['BIDS']; conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. Ontology coding: data_topic 'B2AI_TOPIC:4' / 'B2AI_TOPIC:36', data_substrate 'B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30', ICD-10 in data_annotation_protocol. related_datasets: six typed relationships (is_supplemented_by, is_new_version_of x2, is_version_of, is_documented_by x2), each with a resolvable DOI. external_resources: b2aiprep (github.com/sensein/b2aiprep), senselab, the REDCap dictionary (github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, archived on Zenodo), docs.b2ai-voice.org, Synapse, and 'FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker'. Integration keys: variables documents participant_id 'present in every dense feature file and in the phenotype tables' and session_id, with relationships explaining the one-to-many linkage; every data file carries a same-stem JSON data dictionary. Standard formats, schema and ontology references, typed cross-platform linkages and documented integration keys are all present, which satisfies the 5-band on each of its three limbs. Integration is demonstrated concretely — named join keys, documented cardinality, per-file dictionaries — rather than asserted. I examined whether the conformance claims attach to the released artifacts and found they partly do not: conforms_to itself states BIDS applies to the audio layout and phenotype organization 'rather than to the Parquet feature files of the published feature-only release', and conforms_to_schema names the LinkML schema for this datasheet rather than a schema for the data. I weighed reducing to 4 on that basis and did not, because the column-level semantics of the released files are in fact covered by the per-file JSON dictionaries described in distribution_formats, the join keys are explicit, and the FHIR profiles and B2AI ontology codes supply genuine semantic anchoring. The narrowness of the BIDS claim is recorded as a low-severity semantic issue, and it is to the record's credit that it states the limit rather than overclaiming blanket BIDS conformance.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: eight entries with reproducible parameters — monaural 16 kHz with Butterworth anti-aliasing; spectrograms '201 by T ... 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a factor of two'; 60 mel bins and 60 MFCCs; 'Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package at 50 Hz' over six named articulators; 'Phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories ... at 100 Hz with the ppgs package'; static features via openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth and torchaudio; BIDS v1.9.0 conversion; and 'the open-source b2aiprep library ... version 3.1.0 was generated with b2aiprep v3.0.0'. cleaning_strategies: audit protocol (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema checks on categorical responses, audio QC for silence, duration and passage agreement). labeling_strategies: two entries with gold-standard modalities per cohort, annotations_per_item 1, data_annotation_protocol 'Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes', annotator_demographics. machine_annotation_tools: 'OpenAI Whisper Large', with tool_accuracy 'Not audited'. annotation_analyses: no IAA possible with a single labeler, plus annotation_quality_details. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('No imputation is performed. A missingness table is included'). Every component of the 5-band is served: strategies are comprehensive across preprocessing, cleaning and labeling; the principal tool carries both a version (b2aiprep v3.0.0) and a URL; annotation quality is addressed through annotation_analyses; and the imputation question is answered explicitly rather than left blank. The parameters given are sufficient for a third party to regenerate the features. Tool names are used correctly and consistently with the artifacts they produce — torchaudio for spectrogram/mel/MFCC/pitch, sparc for articulatory and loudness/periodicity traces, ppgs for posteriorgrams — and the same attributions recur in variables.measurement_technique without contradiction. imputation_protocols as a named field is absent, but the substantive question is answered under missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy, so I treated it as addressed rather than missing. Minor residual gap: openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth and torchaudio are named without version pins, which would matter for exact reproduction; this was not enough to displace the top band given the depth elsewhere. The candid 'Not audited' on Whisper is a transparency credit, not a deduction.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: three entries with typed flags — was_directly_observed/was_reported_by_subjects for tablet-recorded tasks and self-reported questionnaires; was_validated_verified for clinician-verified diagnoses 'against cohort-specific gold standards such as laryngoscopy and stroboscopy, CT and MRI of the brain, and spirometry with flow-volume loops'; was_inferred_derived for computed features. collection_mechanisms: three entries naming the custom tablet application, 'secure HTTPS protocol to HIPAA-compliant cloud storage provided by NIH STRIDES partners', exact hardware ('iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 head-mounted microphone connected through an Apple dongle'), and REDCap instrument management. data_collectors: three roles (research teams with a trained research assistant present; clinicians as co-investigators providing gold-standard validation, uncompensated but credited on consortium publications; hospital staff assisting logistics). raw_data_sources: source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. Supporting: sampling_strategies (non-probability, chart screening, published inclusion/exclusion criteria), direct_collection.is_direct true. collection_timeframes: 'The healthsheet states that the data were collected over a period of twelve months', plus per-release accrual of 306, 136 and 391 participants. Two of the three components named by the 5-band — methods and collectors — are documented to an exemplary standard, down to microphone model and dongle. The third, timeframes, is the weak limb: a single relayed twelve-month figure with no absolute start or end date, and it cannot be reconciled with the accrual schedule recorded in the same field and in distribution_dates. This is a case where a semantic check reduced the score. Releases run from November 2024 (306 participants) through April 2025 (+136) to December 2025 (+391), which implies roughly two years of accrual, yet collection_timeframes and known_limitations both state twelve months. The record attributes the figure to the healthsheet rather than asserting it independently, which is honest sourcing, but it does not resolve the conflict and no absolute dates are supplied to let a reader resolve it. Because timeframes is one of the three elements the top band explicitly requires, I scored 4 rather than 5 and logged the conflict as a medium-severity consistency issue.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.1.0'; status 'published'; issued '2026-05-01'. version_access: versions_available lists six releases; version_details gives a per-version changelog ('Version 1.0 provided 12,523 recordings for 306 participants; version 1.1 added mel-frequency cepstral coefficients; version 2.0 added 136 participants ... version 3.1.0 ... fixed broken Parquet files, added audio quality metrics and per-recording metadata, and back-filled validated diagnosis information'), states older versions remain hosted with unique DOIs, and records latest_version_doi 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'. errata: four entries. updates: frequency 'Semi-annual (twice a year)' with a notification mechanism. maintainers: three — 'PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and supported by NIBIB, NHLBI and the NIH Office of the Director'; the consortium with the DACO contact; T-CAIREM at the University of Toronto for the Health Data Nexus era. doi and publisher present; retention_limit gives an indefinite retention commitment for shared data and a ten-year institutional limit; extension_mechanism provides a contribution_url. distribution_dates gives dated release notes for all six versions. All four sustainability indicators the question names are satisfied: persistent identifiers (version and concept DOIs), a long-term governance plan (DACO, stewardship roles, retention policy), a domain-appropriate repository (PhysioNet for biomedical data), and institutional commitment (MIT LCP with named NIH institute support, plus an indefinite retention statement). Versioning is comprehensive — six releases, each dated, each with a DOI and an itemized changelog. Dates are ordered coherently across the release history and the v3.1.0 date agrees across issued, distribution_dates and the version-pinned page URL. The choice of PhysioNet is domain-appropriate and its stewardship is independently named rather than assumed. One low-severity blemish: the last errata entry says 'No formal erratum is published' immediately after three concrete errata, which reads as self-contradictory even though the intended meaning — corrections are carried in the changelog — is recoverable. Not enough to move the band, given that the corrections themselves are individually documented.

name: Associated Publications
text: Formal dataset citation present and complete: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66' — identifying the dataset by title, authors, version, publishing organization and DOI. Distinct additional references: the protocol publication 'Rameau et al., Developing Multi-Disorder Voice Protocols ... Proc. Interspeech 2024' (doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926); the archived REDCap dictionary (doi:10.5281/zenodo.12760724); the pediatric companion dataset (doi:10.13026/h995-bt35); prior releases (doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68, doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84); and non-publication resources in external_resources (b2aiprep, senselab, docs.b2ai-voice.org, Synapse). The 5-band condition is met twice over: far more than two distinct references are documented, and a formal citation for this dataset is present that names it by title and identifies both its authors and its publishing organization. Q14's permitted values are 0, 3 and 5; this is unambiguously 5. Each cited DOI prefix matches a registrar consistent with the claimed target — 10.21437 for an ISCA/Interspeech proceedings paper, 10.5281 for Zenodo, 10.13026 for PhysioNet, 10.57764 for the Health Data Nexus — so the references are not merely numerous but plausibly resolvable. Repeated links to the same resource were counted once (the REDCap dictionary appears in both related_datasets and external_resources and was counted as one reference). The citation correctly pins the version described by this record.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 833 study participants with label_description tying each to a disease cohort or control, and a note that a participant may have multiple sessions. subpopulations: two entries — disease cohorts ('voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, pediatric voice and speech disorders, and controls') and demographic axes ('age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status'), each with a distribution statement noting the release 'does not contain an equal distribution of these disease categories' and 'is skewed by site and by demographic factors'. at_risk_populations: inclusion criteria ('participants aged 18 to 120 who can provide informed consent in English'), cohorts with cognitive impairment and psychiatric diagnoses, and protections. Exclusions: known_limitations records that 'participants who do not read or speak English were excluded' and that the adult release contains no pediatric participants. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling. sampling_strategies adds recruitment setting and chart screening against 'published inclusion and exclusion criteria'. Subgroup structure is well characterized and inclusion/exclusion criteria are stated, which clears the 3-band comfortably. What the 5-band's 'detailed demographics' requires is not present: the demographic axes are named but no counts, proportions or ranges are reported for age, sex, gender, ethnicity or socioeconomic status, and no per-cohort participant breakdown of the 833 is given. The record is candid that the sample is skewed and tells users to weigh the multivariate distribution, but it supplies no distribution against which to do so — the qualitative warning is not backed by the numbers that would make it actionable. The inclusion criteria are also partly general (a confirmed diagnosis in one of five cohorts) rather than the per-cohort diagnostic thresholds a reuser would need, though the gold-standard modalities in labeling_strategies partly compensate. Scored 4: the characterization is sound and honest, the quantification is absent. This gap compounds with Q20, where the missing distributions prevent any real fairness analysis.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; version_access.latest_version_doi 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'; external_resources give https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, https://github.com/sensein/senselab, https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn73617068; existing_uses adds https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/. Passes on every count: a version-pinned repository landing page, both version and concept DOIs, and a dozen well-formed supporting URLs spanning code, documentation, archives and the controlled-access route. All URLs are structurally valid and use plausible, verifiable domains that match their described purpose (physionet.org for the release, github.com for named repositories, synapse.org for controlled distribution, zenodo for archival). The landing page is pinned to v3.1.0, matching the version this record describes, so a reader following it reaches the artifact actually documented rather than a moving target.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms states the tier without ambiguity: 'Only credentialed PhysioNet users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement may access the files; no additional training is required' and 'There are no fees'. data_governance.access_review_process describes both tiers end to end: 'Registered access ... requires registration on PhysioNet, confirmation of identity and signature of the Bridge2AI-Voice Registered Access Agreement. Controlled access to raw audio requires a completed Data Access Request Form and Data Use Agreement, submission ... to the Data Access Compliance Office for review at DACO@b2ai-voice.org and, on approval, a Data Transfer and Use Agreement signed by an authorized official ... approved users then receive the data through Synapse.' distribution_formats enumerate what is obtained; page gives the platform URL; raw_data_sources.access_details and external_resources give the Synapse URLs. download_url is not populated. The access path is fully defined on every dimension the 5-band names: platform (PhysioNet), authentication (credentialed registration with identity confirmation), policy (Registered Access Agreement, no fees, no training), and the distinct escalation path for raw audio with a named reviewing body and contact. The access tier is stated explicitly rather than glossed as 'open' or 'public'. The record avoids exactly the error the rubric warns against — it never calls the dataset public, and it separates the registered tier from the controlled tier consistently across five fields. The formal download_url field is unpopulated, but on PhysioNet a direct download link is not meaningful before credentialing, and the version-pinned landing page plus the Synapse URLs give a reader every actionable entry point; I did not treat that empty field as a substantive access gap. The two-tier design is also consistent with the re-identification reasoning in participant_privacy, so the restriction is justified rather than arbitrary.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms as above, with data_use_permission 'general_research_use'. intended_uses: three research entries, the first carrying usage_notes 'No recommended splits are supplied; researchers should construct their own and should account for the skews in disorder category, site and demographics'. prohibited_uses: five specific prohibitions — re-identification attempts, uses foreseeably causing 'harm or stigmatization to research participants, their families, communities or specific populations', obstructive IP use and resale, contacting subjects without IRB approval and consent, and onward disclosure to third parties. discouraged_uses: two entries naming 'hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance that could lead to discrimination or harm', and uses that assume representativeness. future_use_impacts: three entries covering skew and unfair treatment, inherited errors from unaudited transcription models, and distribution shift. Mitigations appear in usage_notes, known_biases.mitigation_strategy and known_limitations.recommended_mitigation. All three limbs of the 5-band are satisfied. The use guidance is unusually concrete — prohibited uses name mechanisms rather than gesturing at 'misuse', and discouraged uses identify the specific downstream harms (employment, insurance, surveillance) that a voice-health dataset actually invites. The social impact analysis is genuinely risk-identifying rather than boilerplate, and each named risk traces to a documented property of the dataset: the skew warning traces to sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, the inherited-error warning to machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy 'Not audited', and the distribution-shift warning to anomalies and known_limitations. Mitigations are attached, though they are largely advisory (construct your own splits, weigh the distribution) rather than structural. The prohibitions are also consistent with the consent terms, which collection_consents records as imposing no non-commercial, geographic or research-type restriction — so the record does not prohibit what participants in fact permitted, nor permit what they did not.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw voice, speech, breathing and cough audio recordings captured with the Bridge2AI-Voice application, together with questionnaire and clinical data exported from REDCap'. raw_data_sources: source_description, source_type, raw_data_format ('WAV audio, converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz before feature extraction; REDCap and ReproSchema exports converted to tab-delimited phenotype tables') and access_details. Processing lineage: eight preprocessing_strategies steps in order, each with parameters, terminating in 'version 3.1.0 was generated with b2aiprep v3.0.0'. Agents: b2aiprep v3.0.0, senselab, sparc, ppgs, torchaudio, openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, Whisper Large, and human clinicians in labeling_strategies. Per-entity derivation: nine variables carry an explicit derivation plus measurement_technique (e.g. sparc_pitch 'Estimated fundamental frequency ... computed with a different algorithm from the torchaudio pitch, over a range of 50 to 550 Hz'). version_access, errata (4), updates, missing_data_documentation and splits are all populated; anomalies records five quality issues. parent_datasets is empty, with version lineage carried instead in related_datasets (is_new_version_of, is_version_of) with DOIs. This exceeds the 3-band, which is version history alone, on every axis. The chain from raw WAV through each named transformation to each released column is traceable end to end, with the transforming agent and its version identified and the derivation recorded per released variable — the entity-activity-agent structure the 5-band describes, expressed in text, which the rubric expressly accepts. Lineage integrity holds under cross-checking: the tools named in preprocessing_strategies match the measurement_technique values in variables without contradiction, and the de-identification step that removes free-speech-derived features is reflected consistently in variables.quality_notes, missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes and instances' differing per-feature record counts — three independent fields telling the same story about why counts diverge. Quality is documented rather than asserted, including audio QC metrics released from v3.1.0. Two residual gaps, both low severity and neither band-changing: parent_datasets as a named field is empty though its content sits in related_datasets, and no machine-readable PROV-O serialization is offered — which the rubric does not require.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: four entries typed against BiasTypeEnum values — selection_bias ('recruited at a limited number of high-volume expert clinics in North America. Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in artificial intelligence, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, were less likely to be recruited'), representation_bias (unequal disease-category distribution, skew by site and demographics, with affected_subsets), measurement_bias (per-site devices and configurations, headset distance variation, noise artifacts, with affected_subsets), and annotation_bias (single-clinician diagnosis, EHR- or prescription-derived labels, inter-site variation in diagnostic practice). mitigation_strategy is present on selection_bias ('shift to remote collection and to design its recruitment approach so as to control for more variables') and representation_bias, and absent on measurement_bias and annotation_bias. future_use_impacts: three entries including 'models derived from it may not generalize and could treat groups unfairly'. No AIO term URIs; no quantitative fairness metrics or demographic breakdowns. Bias identification is systematic and taxonomy-aligned — four distinct standard categories, each with a substantive causal description and two with affected_subsets — which is well past the 3-band's untaxonomized identification. The 5-band additionally requires fairness analysis, and what is present is a qualitative acknowledgement of skew rather than an analysis: no subgroup counts, no disparity measures, and no AIO ontology mappings. The bias types are applied correctly rather than as labels of convenience — measurement_bias genuinely describes instrumentation variance, annotation_bias genuinely describes labeling process variance — and each traces to a corroborating field elsewhere (anomalies, sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, labeling_strategies). The limiting factor is the same absence noted under Q15: without demographic or per-cohort distributions, the record can warn about unfairness but cannot demonstrate or quantify it, and two of four biases carry no mitigation. Scored 4.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (11/14): id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description ~2,400 chars; keywords (4); license_and_use_terms with data_use_permission 'general_research_use'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (17 entries with affiliations and CRediT roles); purposes (3); instances (2 types, counts 833); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (3/14): resources, parent_datasets, variables. The populated fields are not merely present but substantive - creators carry institution-level affiliations and credit roles, instances carry counts and label descriptions. Three slots are empty: no resources list, no parent_datasets (version predecessors appear only as related_datasets typed links), and no variables element despite the record stating that every released table is paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name. 11/14 = 78.6% sits between the 70% (3) and 90% (5) bands. The missing variables element is the semantically significant gap: column-level semantics exist in the distribution but are not surfaced in the datasheet, so a machine reader cannot recover variable meaning from this record alone. parent_datasets is partly compensated by related_datasets is_new_version_of links carrying predecessor DOIs, which is why the omission was not penalised twice.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs roughly 2,400 characters across two paragraphs, naming cohort structure, seventeen acoustic tasks, thirteen validated instruments and the derived-feature release contents. purposes contains three responses of roughly 230, 250 and 240 characters each ('To generate a large, multi-institutional, ethically sourced and diverse voice, speech and respiratory sound dataset...', '...enable the development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable machine-learning models...', '...introduce and standardize the field of acoustic biomarkers, or audiomics...'). Average narrative length far exceeds the 200-character threshold, and the length is informative rather than padded: the description carries specific protocol content (task names, instrument names, gold-standard validation modalities) that a reuser would otherwise have to seek elsewhere. Length and specificity coincide here. The description's claims are checkable against other elements - 833 participants matches instances.counts, five North American sites matches data_collectors, the Parquet/TSV split matches file_collections and distribution_formats - so the narrative is not decorative.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: ['voice', 'health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai'] - four unique terms. Four keywords places the record squarely in the 3-7 band. The terms are apt but coarse: none names the modality beyond 'voice' (no speech, respiratory sounds, acoustic features), none names a cohort or condition, and none names a standard the dataset conforms to. This is the sharpest mismatch in the record between the controlled vocabulary and the content it indexes. The subsets element enumerates more than fifty conditions with inclusion and exclusion criteria, and ICD-10 is cited as the labelling vocabulary, so the topical coverage exists - it is simply not reachable through keywords. Scored on the keywords field as the rubric directs; the supplemental condition coverage is recorded here rather than used to lift the band.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists three entries (Apache Parquet for dense derived features and per-recording metadata; tab-separated values for static features, audio quality metrics and phenotype tables; WAV audio under controlled access). file_collections names four collections (features, metadata, phenotype, b2ai-voice-audio) and enumerates individual files: ppgs.parquet, sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet, audio_quality_metrics.tsv, static_features.tsv, plus JSON data dictionaries, JSON sidecars, dataset_description.json, CHANGES.md and README.md. Distinct media types exceed three comfortably (Parquet, TSV, JSON, WAV, Markdown). Enumeration is at filename granularity for the features collection, which is unusually specific; total_file_count is not given. Format variety here reflects genuine multi-modality of representation rather than incidental file sprawl - dense numeric arrays in a columnar binary format, tabular phenotypes in text with paired dictionaries, and waveforms in a BIDS tree. The pairing of every data file with a same-stem JSON dictionary is consistent across the features and phenotype collections.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[0].counts: 833. Per-feature record counts in instances[1].notes: 'torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc electromagnetic articulography 28,640'. version_access.version_details: 'The initial release provided 12,523 recordings for 306 participants.' subsets contains eight entries with is_data_split and is_subpopulation flags; splits is present with split_details. Passes on instance counts. Byte-level sizing is absent throughout - no total_size_bytes and no file_collections.total_bytes - so a user can estimate scale from counts but cannot size a download. The omission of an aggregate recording count is deliberate and explained: instances[1].source_caveats states that the preferred PhysioNet v3.1.0 source gives only per-feature counts, so no aggregate was invented. Declining to carry over the documentation site's ~61,937 figure is the correct handling of a source-rank conflict even though it leaves the field thinner.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id: 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page: 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; publisher: 'https://physionet.org'; version_access.latest_version_doi: 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42' (version-independent); citation embeds 'RRID:SCR_007345'. Both halves of the requirement are met - persistent identifiers and an identified hosting platform - and a version-independent DOI is supplied alongside the version-specific one, which is the stronger practice. The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's and agrees with the declared publisher and landing page, so the identifier and the host corroborate each other rather than merely coexisting. The RRID is well-formed but sits inside the citation string and most plausibly names the hosting repository rather than the dataset; flagged as a low-severity correctness note, not enough to affect a pass.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, through the Bridge2AI program', with four grant entries: OT2OD032720 (core project, USF, PI Bensoussan, 1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026), 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (cited in the PhysioNet v3.0.0/v3.1.0 acknowledgements), 1OT2OD032720-01 (feasibility publication funding statement), 3OT2OD032720-01S3 (NIH RePORTER application ID 11376382, FY2025, $4,660,942, University of South Florida). creators lists 17 named investigators with institution-level affiliations (USF Health Voice Center; Englander Institute for Precision Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine; McGovern Institute, MIT; Vanderbilt; OHSU; WashU; The Hastings Center; Simon Fraser; University of Florida; SickKids; Mount Sinai/Sinai Health; University of Toronto) and CRediT roles for six of them. Both halves of the band-5 condition are satisfied with margin: grants carry award numbers, amounts, dates and awardee organisation, and creators carry department-level affiliations plus role taxonomies. The record also states that 117 further PhysioNet authors are attested by name only and explains why they are not given individual entries. Grant identifiers parse correctly against NIH conventions (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720; application-type prefixes 1 and 3 with support year -01 and supplement suffixes S1/S3). The record does not normalise the variants into one canonical string but attributes each to its source, and explicitly marks the two garbled documentation strings ('3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1') as corrupted renderings rather than distinct awards - correct handling that avoids fabricating an award number. Funding purpose also aligns: the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI goal of AI-ready biomedical data matches the stated purposes.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: two reviewing organisations (USF IRB single-IRB with subsite approvals; Canadian REBs at Mount Sinai, SickKids and University of Toronto, with copies filed to the USF IRB). human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, named ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance noting partial HIPAA waiver for chart review and a Certificate of Confidentiality, special_populations describing 18-120 eligibility. is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers...', an itemised identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details stating 'The dataset does not achieve k-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two.' participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (tiered dissemination, institutional firewalls, HTTPS to HIPAA-compliant storage, federated learning), data_linkage via participant_id/session_id, and reidentification_risk 'Voice is inherently identifying and cannot be fully de-identified'. participant_compensation: gift cards, $40 under 90 minutes / $80 over, capped at $120. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, four documentation modalities, consent_scope covering EHR access and both release tiers, withdrawal_mechanism. data_protection_impacts: ethicist review of sensitive fields plus a published controlled-access memorandum. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant 'compliant'; other_compliance covering the Certificate of Confidentiality, five-business-day breach notification and safeguards; data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. Every named protection area is populated, most of them with operational specificity a reuser could act on (compensation schedule, consent modalities, withdrawal cut-off, named IRB). Two accuracy defects hold this back from 5 rather than any absence. Reduced from 5 to 4 on semantic grounds. First, at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while subsets enrol participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and substance use disorder - populations ordinarily treated as at risk; the capacity-to-consent restriction mitigates but does not make the boolean accurate. Second, data_protection_impacts asserts an impact review while its own source_caveats records the healthsheet answering 'No' to whether such an analysis was conducted, leaving the element self-contradictory. Positively, the de-identification method is well matched to the data type: the record recognises that Safe Harbor cannot neutralise voice biometrics and responds structurally by withholding waveforms from the registered tier, and it discloses the k-anonymity failure rather than implying anonymity it does not have.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission 'general_research_use'; license_terms describing the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, credentialed access via a signed Registered Access Agreement, permitted duplication for the approved project, prohibition on sale, no IP transfer, adherence to the Fort Lauderdale Agreement, and 'No fees are associated with these restrictions.' ip_restrictions: four enumerated restrictions including downstream IP allowed only under non-obstructive licensing and a statement that no third parties imposed restrictions. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance covering the Certificate of Confidentiality, compulsory-process assertion, safeguards, five-business-day breach notification and PhysioNet requirements. data_governance: committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)', accountable_organization 'University of South Florida Board of Trustees', a two-tier access_review_process, four stewardship_roles, and contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. Governance is described operationally, not nominally: the reader learns which agreement governs which tier, who signs, who is accountable at the receiving institution, and what obligations survive transfer (retention, destruction certification, independent application by collaborators). The restrictiveness of the licence is proportionate to the sensitivity the ethics elements describe - restricted classification and registered access for derived features, controlled access with institutional sign-off for biometric waveforms - so the governance and ethics claims corroborate rather than contradict each other. Multi-jurisdiction handling is genuine: US single-IRB plus Canadian REB approvals, with the Certificate of Confidentiality named as the instrument to assert against subpoenas.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: Formats: Apache Parquet and TSV with paired JSON data dictionaries; WAV in a BIDS tree. conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: ['BIDS']; conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. file_collections carry their own conforms_to values ('Apache Parquet and tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries'; 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries'; BIDS v1.9.0 for the audio tree). Ontology terms on instances: data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 and :30, data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:4 and :36; diagnostic labels follow ICD-10. related_datasets: six typed relationships (derives_from to Synapse syn72370534; is_supplemented_by to doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 pediatric; three is_new_version_of; is_version_of to the version-independent DOI). external_resources: b2aiprep and senselab repositories, the REDCap data dictionary archived at Zenodo, the documentation site archived at Zenodo, and published FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker. Integration keys: participant_privacy.data_linkage and relationships state that records join across features and phenotype tables by participant_id and session_id. All three band-5 components are present and specific. Integration capability is not asserted abstractly but named at key level, and cross-platform linkage is typed rather than a bare list of related URLs. Standards are used correctly in context: BIDS for the audio tree is the appropriate community standard, LinkML/w3id for the metadata schema, ICD-10 for diagnoses, FHIR for clinical exchange. The one gap against the rubric's field list is file_collections.compression, which is never specified - immaterial for Parquet, which carries codec metadata internally, and not enough to move the band.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: six entries with executable-level parameters - monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT with a 25 ms window, 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT, spectrograms downsampled by two in time, 60 Mel bins, 60 MFCCs; sparc at 50 Hz yielding six articulator traces plus loudness, periodicity and pitch; torchaudio pitch over 80-500 Hz versus sparc pitch over 50-550 Hz; openSMILE, Parselmouth/Praat, and phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories at 100 Hz; de-identification transforms; and BIDS v1.9.0 conversion assembled 'with the open-source b2aiprep library, version 3.0.0 for this release'. cleaning_strategies: states that no cleaning pre-processing was applied and describes the audit protocol instead (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema validation of categorical responses, silence and duration QC, comparison of produced speech against the intended passage). labeling_strategies: annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_platform (REDCap plus the tablet app), data_annotation_protocol (clinician diagnosis to Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10), inter_annotator_agreement stated as not reportable for single labelling. machine_annotation_tools: nine named tools (Whisper Large, openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab) with tool_descriptions and a tool_accuracy caveat. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy 'No imputation was performed.' This is the strongest technical element in the record. Parameters are specific enough to reproduce the feature extraction, the version change between v1.1 and v3.1.0 (512-point versus 400-point FFT, time downsampling) is flagged rather than silently superseded, and the pipeline library is version-pinned at 3.0.0 with a public repository. Structured imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses elements are absent, but both concerns are answered in substance - no imputation was performed, and the single-labeller design makes inter-annotator agreement inapplicable, which the record states rather than leaving blank. Scoring follows the instruction to judge content over field presence. The tool_accuracy caveat that off-the-shelf transcription models 'have not been audited for correctness' is an honest limit on the derived text and is consistent with the anomalies element. Partial weakness: only b2aiprep carries a version; Whisper is given as 'Large' and openSMILE, Praat and torchaudio are unversioned, which slightly limits exact reproducibility without moving the band.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: four entries with typed flags - was_directly_observed (supervised tablet session with a head-mounted headset microphone), was_reported_by_subjects (demographics, confounders such as smoking and hydration, validated questionnaires), was_validated_verified (clinician review of audio, imaging, EHR and prescriptions against per-cohort gold standards), was_inferred_derived (all released features derived via b2aiprep). collection_mechanisms: the custom tablet application; hardware named to model level - 'iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle', distinct devices per site; REDCap instruments for clinical and case report data. data_collectors: researcher role (research teams including students, coordinating with clinicians, with a trained research assistant) and academic_institution role (clinicians listed under the IRB as co-investigators; five North American academic sites). collection_timeframes: 'The data was collected over a period of 12 months.' raw_data_sources: three sources with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. Supported by sampling_strategies (non-probability purposive recruitment from clinics seeing >50 patients/month in a disease area), collection_notifications, collection_consents and direct_collection. All three band-5 components are present, and the protocol is described at a level that would let another site replicate it - device models, microphone placement, screening rule, who administers and who diagnoses. The collection description is internally consistent with the bias and limitation elements: purposive clinic recruitment in acquisition and sampling explains the selection and representation biases declared later, and per-site device differences appear both in collection_mechanisms and in the measurement-bias entry. One residual thinness: collection_timeframes gives a 12-month duration with no calendar start or end, and its source_caveats says so explicitly rather than inventing dates - a disclosed gap, not an undisclosed one, so the band is unaffected.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '3.1.0'. version_access: latest_version_doi 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'; six versions listed with dates and DOIs (1.0 on Health Data Nexus DOI 10.57764/qb6h-em84; 1.1 17 Jan 2025 DOI 10.13026/249v-w155; 2.0.0 16 Apr 2025; 2.0.1 18 Aug 2025; 3.0.0 16 Dec 2025 DOI 10.13026/k81f-qr68; 3.1.0 1 May 2026 DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66); version_details on continued support of older versions and the withdrawal of v1.1 files. errata: three entries (v2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and removal of free-speech spectrograms/MFCCs; v2.0.1 authorship corrections; v3.1.0 repair of broken parquet files). updates: frequency 'Semi-annual', with a detailed changelog of what v3.1.0 altered and the notification route. maintainers: three roles - PhysioNet/MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology for infrastructure, the consortium via DACO for curation and access, and NIH as the supporting agency. Sustainability: persistent DOIs per version plus a version-independent DOI, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository (PhysioNet), a governance plan (data_governance, retention_limit, extension_mechanism), and institutional commitment via NIH Bridge2AI funding through 30 November 2026. All four sustainability indicators named in the rubric are documented and the versioning record is unusually complete, with per-version DOIs, dates and changes rather than a single version string. Two tensions are present and both are disclosed rather than concealed. The notes element reports the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment scoring sustainability at 50 percent, and maintainers carries a source_caveats reconciling the Health Data Nexus attribution against the PhysioNet record by assigning it to v1.0. The stated semi-annual cadence is checkable against the observed release dates (Jan, Apr, Aug, Dec 2025, May 2026), which run somewhat faster than semi-annual - the record notes the discrepancy itself. Scoring the documentation, which is comprehensive, rather than the self-assessed maturity of the sustainability arrangements.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: a complete formal dataset citation naming twenty-plus authors, the dataset title, version 3.1.0, the publishing organisation PhysioNet, RRID:SCR_007345 and https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66. Distinct additional references in external_resources: (1) the Interspeech 2024 protocol-development paper, Bensoussan et al., 'Developing Multi-Disorder Voice Protocols', at isca-archive.org; (2) the b2aiprep repository at github.com/sensein/b2aiprep; (3) senselab at github.com/sensein/senselab; (4) the REDCap data dictionary at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724; (5) the documentation site docs.b2ai-voice.org archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; (6) published FHIR profiles; (7) the Voice Scholars training programme. related_datasets adds five further DOIs. Far more than the two distinct references the band requires, together with a formal dataset citation that identifies the dataset by title, version, authors and publisher. Two of the external resources carry their own Zenodo DOIs. References are of mixed kind - one peer-reviewed publication, several code and documentation resources, and archived snapshots - which the rubric counts as references. Duplicate links to the same resource were counted once. The record is candid that persistence guarantees for external resources are unresolved: external_resources notes the healthsheet answers 'NA' to guarantees of persistence, which is why archival flags are set false for the non-Zenodo repositories.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: participant instance with counts 833, label true, and a label_description tying diagnoses to clinician assignment and ICD-10. subsets: five subpopulation cohorts (voice disorders, respiratory, neurological/neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, controls), each with condition-level inclusion and exclusion criteria and named gold standards - for example the neurological cohort 'aged over 44 and under 85, able to read and speak English' validated with 'brain CT, brain MRI and whole genome sequencing, and additionally serum p-tau biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease'. subpopulations: identification by 'age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status' plus disease cohort; distribution noting unequal cohort representation and skews by site and demographic factors. at_risk_populations: 18+, capacity to consent in English, with a pediatric cohort described and excluded to a separate release. missing_data_documentation: cohort-specific instruments systematically absent outside their cohort. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are the most detailed part of the record and would let a reuser reconstruct cohort eligibility precisely. What is missing is quantity: no participant counts per cohort, and no age, sex, race, ethnicity or socioeconomic distribution despite those being named as the subpopulation identification variables. Scored 4 rather than 5 because the subpopulations.distribution sub-element is answered qualitatively where the question asks for demographic diversity. The record asserts skews exist and warns users to consider the multivariate distribution, but supplies no numbers with which to do so, which limits the practical value of the warning. The at_risk_groups_included false declaration sits uneasily against the cognitive-impairment and psychiatric cohorts described here; that defect is charged once, against Q8, and noted rather than double-counted here.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; version-independent doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; distribution_formats access_urls to physionet.org and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; external_resources links to github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, docs.b2ai-voice.org, two Zenodo DOI links, isca-archive.org and b2aivoicescholars.org. Findability is supported at several levels - version-specific DOI, version-independent DOI, landing page, controlled-access repository handle, and archived documentation snapshots. All URLs are well-formed and the domains are plausible for the resources they claim to host (PhysioNet for the release, Synapse for controlled audio, Zenodo for archival snapshots of GitHub repositories, ISCA for an Interspeech paper). The Synapse identifier syn72370534 follows Synapse's syn-prefix convention and is used consistently in both related_datasets and raw_data_sources.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats: three entries each carrying access_urls - Parquet and TSV at https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/, WAV at https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ 'available only under controlled access'. license_and_use_terms: access limited to credentialed users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement. data_governance.access_review_process spells out both tiers: 'a user registers on PhysioNet, confirms their identity, becomes a credentialed user and signs the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement; no additional training is required' for features, and for raw audio 'the applicant completes a Data Access Request Form and a Data Use Agreement and submits the application to the Data Access Compliance Office for review at DACO@b2ai-voice.org; upon approval, a Data Use and Transfer Agreement must be signed by an authorized official at the applicant's institution before the data are released through Synapse.' third_party_sharing confirms distribution under registered and credentialed access with a signed DUA. The access path is fully specified end to end for both tiers, including who must sign, what must be reviewed, and where the data appear after approval. A reader can determine before applying which tier their intended analysis requires. The record avoids the common error the rubric warns about: it never describes itself as 'public' or 'open', and it names the tier precisely (registered/credentialed with agreement; controlled with institutional sign-off). No separate download_url field is populated, but access_urls inside distribution_formats serve that role and are tier-specific, which is more informative than a single bare URL would be.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms as above. intended_uses: three use_category entries (clinical machine-learning research; voice biomarker research; methods, standards and cohort construction) each with examples and usage_notes, including the instruction that 'The process for deriving any new labels should be described alongside any release of a model or publication, including the exact variables used for that determination.' prohibited_uses: five prohibitions with reasons - re-identification attempts, uses foreseeably causing harm or stigmatisation, IP protection used to block access, sale of the data, and contacting subjects without IRB approval and provider consent. discouraged_uses: three with justification - hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment, and surveillance. future_use_impacts: two entries, one identifying skew-driven harms ('models trained without accounting for those skews risk unfair treatment of groups, quality of service problems, or other harms') with the mitigation of considering the multivariate distribution, and one describing positive impacts including screening in low-resource settings. existing_uses records prior use in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon. Every band-5 component is present. The prohibitions and discouragements are reasoned rather than boilerplate, each tied to a specific harm pathway, and the discouraged-use list anticipates realistic misuse of voice-based health inference. The use guidance is coherent with the ethics and governance elements: the re-identification prohibition follows from the stated reidentification_risk and consent scope, and the anti-blocking IP clause matches ip_restrictions and the Fort Lauderdale commitment in the licence. Social impact analysis is qualitative but names both harm and mitigation, satisfying the CROISSANT RAI framing the question invokes.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Entities: raw WAV recordings (raw_data_sources 'Raw audio waveforms recorded during the acoustic tasks', format WAV), REDCap exports, and released Parquet/TSV artefacts enumerated in file_collections. Activities: the preprocessing_strategies chain from standardisation (monaural, 16 kHz, Butterworth) through STFT/Mel/MFCC derivation, sparc articulatory coding, openSMILE and ppgs extraction, de-identification transforms, and BIDS v1.9.0 conversion. Agents: b2aiprep version 3.0.0 and senselab as software agents, site clinicians as labelling agents (labeling_strategies), and research teams as collection agents (data_collectors). Derivation paths: related_datasets derives_from https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ with the description 'The released features were derived from the raw audio recordings of the adult cohort'; acquisition_methods was_inferred_derived 'All features distributed in the release were derived computationally from the standardized audio'. Version lineage: version_access with six versions and DOIs, errata with three corrections, updates with a v3.1.0 changelog. Quality: missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling), anomalies (six entries), splits with split_details, and eight subsets carrying explicit is_data_split and is_subpopulation flags. Provenance goes well beyond version history. The three PROV-O components are recoverable in text, the derivation target is an addressable identifier rather than prose, and quality documentation (anomalies, missingness, audit metrics released as a file) accompanies the lineage. No was_derived_from field and no PROV-O serialisation are present, and parent_datasets is empty; the rubric accepts text-form lineage where it is complete, and here it is - each released artefact can be traced to a source, an activity with parameters, and a responsible agent. The provenance is also self-correcting: the v1.1 versus v3.1.0 FFT parameter change and the v2.0 removal of free-speech spectrograms are recorded, so a user of an older version can tell what changed and why.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: five entries with enum-style bias_type values - selection_bias (recruitment from high-volume expert clinics reflecting specialty referral patterns), sampling_bias (non-probability sample at limited geographic locations, with a mitigation_strategy of shifting to remote collection), representation_bias (English fluency requirement, skews by disorder, site and demographics, and reduced recruitment of groups with less trust in the medical system or living further from sites, with user-facing mitigation), measurement_bias (cohort membership confounded with site and tablet device, affected_subsets named), annotation_bias (single labeler per instance without adjudication). future_use_impacts names skew-driven harms including 'unfair treatment of groups, quality of service problems, or other harms'. Reinforced by known_limitations (six typed entries), sampling_strategies is_representative false with why_not_representative, and anomalies. Bias identification is systematic and well beyond 'basic': each bias is typed, described with a causal mechanism, and three carry mitigation strategies or named affected subsets. The taxonomy vocabulary matches the schema's BiasTypeEnum conventions. Held at 4 rather than 5 because the band-5 condition names taxonomy mappings to the AI Ontology and a fairness analysis; no AIO term identifiers are attached to any bias_type, and fairness is addressed as qualitative guidance rather than measured subgroup representation or performance. The gap compounds the missing quantitative demographics noted at Q15: users are told the skews matter but given no distribution against which to assess them. The bias claims are nonetheless consistent with the sampling and limitation elements, and the annotation_bias entry correctly follows from labeling_strategies annotations_per_item 1.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,100 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (Registered Access License, credentialing, DUA, fee statement) with data_use_permission 'general_research_use'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (16 entries, all with affiliations, one with PI block and email); purposes (3); instances (2 types, counts 833); resources (11 named file resources nested under file_collections[0].resources, each with id, file_type and description); variables (4: participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames with data_type and is_identifier); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent: parent_datasets (derivation instead carried by was_derived_from and related_datasets derives_from 'syn72370534'). 13 of 14 named fields are populated (~93%) and the content is substantive rather than placeholder: creators carry institutional affiliations individually, variables carry types and identifier flags, and the license field describes an actual access procedure rather than naming a license. Only parent_datasets is unpopulated. Field values are semantically appropriate to their slots: id and doi agree; page resolves to the version-specific PhysioNet landing page matching version '3.1.0'; confidentiality_level 'restricted' is consistent with a registered-access license rather than overstated. The missing parent_datasets is a placement issue, not missing information, since the parent is named in two other fields.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 1,100 characters and is specific: '833 adult participants recruited at five North American sites', an enumeration of the four condition families, the collection modality ('standardized protocol of acoustic tasks on a tablet application, with a headset where possible'), and an explicit statement of what is and is not distributed ('spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch and periodicity traces, Speech Articulatory Coding articulatory estimates, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE, Praat and parselmouth static features ... rather than the original waveforms'). purposes has three responses averaging roughly 200 characters each. Both narrative fields are far above the >200 character band, and length here reflects information density rather than padding: the description alone supplies participant count, site count, cohort structure, instrument, and release scope. The description's claims are corroborated elsewhere in the record rather than free-standing: 833 matches instances.counts, the feature list matches the eleven enumerated resources, and the waveform exclusion matches is_deidentified.deidentification_details and known_limitations.scope_limitation. Length is therefore backed by verifiable content.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: ['health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'] — four unique terms. Supplementary topical coverage exists outside the keywords field: instances carry ontology CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, and the phenotype file_collection description enumerates roughly eighteen conditions (airway stenosis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia, laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained chronic cough, unilateral vocal fold paralysis) plus thirteen named instruments. Four keywords sits at the low end of the 3-7 band and the terms are broad; none names a condition, a modality beyond 'voice', or a method. The rubric's note permitting supplementation by condition lists and ontology references was applied, but the supplementary condition terms appear inside a prose folder description rather than as indexable metadata, and the ontology references amount to two coded topic terms, so the supplementation does not reach the >=8 threshold. The keywords are individually accurate and none is misleading, but as a discovery surface they under-describe the record: a researcher searching for 'dysphonia', 'Parkinson', 'speech', 'acoustic features' or 'machine learning' would not retrieve this dataset on keywords alone, despite all of those being central to its content as documented elsewhere in the same record. This is an indexing gap rather than a correctness defect.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists three: TSV (media_type 'text/tab-separated-values'), JSON (media_type 'application/json'), Parquet (no media type, with the note 'No IANA media type for Parquet is stated by the sources, so none is recorded'), each with access_urls. file_collections enumerates three collections (features, phenotype, metadata) and eleven individually named resources with dimensions and record counts, e.g. 'torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet ... Spectrograms of dimension 201 by T ... 29,278 records'; 'sparc_ema.parquet ... dimension T by 12 ... 28,640 records'; 'static_features.tsv'; 'audio_quality_metrics.tsv'. total_file_count is absent. Exactly three distinct formats places the count in the 2-3 band. The score is lifted one point because the question also weighs file enumeration, and the enumeration here is exceptional: every dense feature file is named, dimensioned and counted, and every data file is documented as paired with a JSON data dictionary. It does not reach 5 because there is no fourth format and no total_file_count. Format choice is semantically coherent with content type: Parquet for dense variable-length tensors, TSV for per-recording scalar tables and phenotype data, JSON for data dictionaries. The refusal to invent a media type for Parquet is correct behaviour rather than an omission. The three formats reflect a single-modality feature release, consistent with known_limitations.integration_limitation stating that imaging, genomic and spirometry data are not part of this release, so low format variety is an accurate signal about scope rather than a documentation failure.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[0].counts: 833. instances[1].notes gives per-feature record counts: 'torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640'. Each file resource repeats its own count. subpopulations and splits are present (splits: 'No recommended train, validation or test splits are predefined'). total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are both absent. Passes on instance and record counts, which are numerous and file-specific. Byte sizes are entirely absent, so the criterion is met by the count route only. Counts are internally consistent across three places (instances.notes, individual resource descriptions, and the description's scope statement), and the record explains why counts differ between features rather than leaving the discrepancy unexplained: 'representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks were withheld, and ... some files could not generate certain features'. It also declines to compute a total the sources do not state. As the rubric notes, sample size supports only an estimate of file size, so download planning remains approximate.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; publisher: https://physionet.org/; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345. Sibling and predecessor DOIs are also given (10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/h995-bt35, 10.13026/249v-w155, 10.57764/qb6h-em84). Passes comfortably: a DOI, an RRID, a version-specific landing page and a named hosting platform are all present, exceeding the single-identifier threshold. The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's actual DataCite prefix and matches the named publisher, so identifier and platform corroborate one another rather than merely coexisting. RRID:SCR_007345 matches the RRID:SCR_ pattern. One defect is noted against Q13 rather than here, since it concerns version pointing rather than identification of this record: version_access.latest_version_doi names 10.13026/37yb-1t42, which is not this DOI and appears nowhere else.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program' with two grants: '3OT2OD032720-01S1' (the acknowledgement in the PhysioNet release) and 'OT2OD032720' (the RePORTER core project, 'held at the University of South Florida with Yael Emilie Bensoussan as principal investigator, running from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 with a fiscal year 2025 award amount of 4,660,942 US dollars'). All 16 creators carry affiliations (USF, Weill Cornell, Vanderbilt, SickKids, WashU, OHSU, Simon Fraser, The Hastings Center, MIT, Toronto, Sinai Health, University of Florida); the consortium entry carries a principal_investigator block with name, email and department-level affiliation. maintainers separately names NIH support under OT2OD032720. Meets the 5 band fully and then exceeds it: grant numbers are accompanied by award period, host institution, PI and dollar amount, and every creator carries an institutional affiliation rather than a bare name list. Both grant strings parse correctly against NIH conventions (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720; the type-3 prefix and -01S1 suffix denote a supplement to support year 01), and the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 brackets the 2026-05-01 issue date consistently. Where sources disagree the record says so rather than choosing silently: funders.source_caveats records that RePORTER lists application -01S3 while PhysioNet acknowledges -01S1, and the top-level caveat identifies two further transcriptions ('3Tf-OTOD03272001S2', '3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1') as corrupted. Recording an unresolved identifier conflict explicitly is stronger evidence practice than presenting one variant as settled, and no score reduction is warranted.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: USF IRB, with subsite IRBs through the Single IRB process and Canadian institutions applying to their own REBs. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval, ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA de-identification, Certificate of Confidentiality assertable against subpoenas, no DMC, not a drug/device study), special_populations (adults 18-120; assent option; cohorts including mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's and other dementias). is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers ... and by withholding of all raw audio', a full identifiers_removed enumeration, and deidentification_details ending 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved'. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, four privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk, data_linkage. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, three consent modalities, documentation retained five years, consent_scope, withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, consent_revocations, collection_notifications. participant_compensation: gift cards, '40 US dollars ... 80 US dollars ... maximum compensation of 120 US dollars', adults only. at_risk_populations: three special_protections and assent_procedures. regulatory_restrictions: hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance, and a governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org via data_governance. data_protection_impacts: 'no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'. Every ethics field in the rubric's list is populated, most with operational specificity (dollar amounts, retention periods, breach-reporting windows, named board). The score stops at 4 because the 5 band requires DPIA alongside the other protections, and the record states plainly that no impact analysis on data subjects was performed. The honest negative answer is better documentation than an empty field, but it does not supply the protection the band asks for. Consistency logic passes throughout: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a stated method and by participant_privacy protections; sensitive_elements flagging voice as a biometric is matched by the raw-audio withholding and the separate controlled-access tier. The de-identification method is appropriate to the data type, and unusually the record states where it fails (k-anonymity not achieved; voice 'cannot be fully de-identified'), which is what makes the residual-risk claim credible. One content-accuracy tension is logged separately: hipaa_compliant='compliant' sits against the record's own quotation of the DTUA describing the data as 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws'. Because the record discloses rather than conceals the conflict, it is treated as a flagged inconsistency and is reflected in the Q9 and Q8 reasoning without a further deduction here.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms sets out the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, the requirement to sign the Registered Access Agreement, the PhysioNet policy from version 3.0.0 that 'only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the files; no additional training is required', the separate raw-audio regime (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, DTUA signed by an authorized institutional official), permitted duplication, prohibited sale, and 'There are no fees associated with these restrictions'; data_use_permission 'general_research_use'. ip_restrictions gives four clauses covering non-transfer of IP, non-blocking of downstream access, downstream IP with Fort Lauderdale Agreement obligations, and absence of third-party restrictions. regulatory_restrictions: export controls ('No export controls apply'), confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance (HIPAA de-identification, Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguards, authorized-persons restriction, 'report any unauthorized use or disclosure to the provider within five business days'). data_governance names the Data Access Compliance Office, the accountable organization 'University of South Florida Board of Trustees', a step-by-step access_review_process, five stewardship_roles, and the contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
