All four components of the 5 band are present and operational rather than nominal: the confidentiality classification is a coded value, the governance contact is an actual address, and the access process names each document and its signatory. Multi-jurisdiction coverage is evidenced by US federal (HIPAA, Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16) and Canadian REB routes. Restrictiveness is proportionate to sensitivity and is consistent across fields: confidentiality_level 'restricted' matches a registered-access licence, and the escalation to committee review for raw audio matches sensitive_elements identifying voice as biometric. The ip_restrictions clauses are semantically consistent with prohibited_uses, which bars using IP protection to restrict access. The one flaw is the HIPAA characterisation conflict the record itself quotes; it is disclosed with both statements recorded, affects the interpretation of a single enum rather than the access path a user must follow, and is logged as a medium-severity content-accuracy issue rather than scored down here, since the question asks whether access and governance terms are clearly defined and they are.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: TSV, JSON, Parquet, described as 'Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format'. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Ontology terms: B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30. related_datasets carries four typed relationships: is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68, derives_from syn72370534, references 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric release), is_documented_by 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926. external_resources names b2aiprep and SenseLab (Apache-2.0), the REDCap data dictionary (MIT, Zenodo-archived), the documentation source (MIT, Zenodo-archived), and 'Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker'. Integration keys: variables define participant_id and session_id as identifiers, file_collections states 'Each element carries participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames', and participant_privacy.data_linkage confirms linkage 'across sessions and across feature and phenotype files by a study participant identifier'. Every data file is paired with a JSON data dictionary 'sharing its file stem ... giving a description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type'. conforms_to (data standard) and file_collections.compression are absent. Formats are open and appropriate, typed cross-platform relationships are present with resolvable identifiers, and integration capability is concretely documented through shared keys and column-level dictionaries. The score stops short of 5 because no data-level standard or ontology conformance is asserted for this release: conforms_to_schema points at the datasheet schema rather than the data, ontology use amounts to two coded topic terms, the FHIR profiles are cited as supporting material rather than as a conformance claim, and compression is unstated. The abstention from a standards claim is deliberate and correct, not an oversight: source_caveats records that the documentation asserts BIDS v1.9.0 conformance for a b2ai-voice-audio layout with 'dataset_description.json, phenotype and sub-<id>/ses-<id>/audio directories', while 'the PhysioNet 3.1.0 release described here has a features, metadata and phenotype layout and does not state conformance to any data standard, so no standard is asserted'. Declining to carry a claim across releases where the layout differs is the semantically accurate choice, and the record is scored on what this release documents. The per-file JSON dictionaries and stable participant/session keys mean machine ingestion is well supported in practice despite the absent formal standard.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (6) give exact parameters: 'converting to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter'; 'short-time Fast Fourier Transform with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a factor of two'; '60 Mel bins'; sparc kinematics 'all gathered at 50 Hz'; ppgs 'at 100 Hz across 40 phoneme categories'; openSMILE, Parselmouth and Praat for prosodic measures; 'Transcriptions were generated using OpenAI's Whisper Large model'. cleaning_strategies give an audit protocol (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema validation of categorical responses, audio QC, silence and duration checks, produced-versus-intended speech checks) performed 'with the b2aiprep and SenseLab toolkits', plus the released audio_quality_metrics.tsv. labeling_strategies give clinician gold standards, annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol 'Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes', and platform. machine_annotation_tools lists nine tools with descriptions and a tool_accuracy caveat: 'off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy. Versions: only 'b2aiprep ... version 3.0.0 generated this release'. imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses are absent. Strategy documentation is comprehensive and parameterised well beyond the 3 band, and repository URLs with licences are supplied for the pipeline code. Two elements of the 5 band are missing: versions for eight of nine tools (openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, SenseLab unversioned; Whisper given only as 'Large'), and any imputation protocol. Annotation quality is partially covered by annotations_per_item and the accuracy caveat but there is no annotation_analyses entry such as inter-rater agreement. Tools are correctly matched to the outputs they produce and the mapping is verifiable against the file names (torchaudio_* for spectral and pitch features, sparc_* for articulatory and source measures, ppgs for posteriorgrams, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth for static features), so the pipeline description is coherent rather than a generic tool list. The stated parameters are internally consistent: a 25 ms window at 16 kHz with a 400-point FFT yields the 201-bin spectrogram dimension given in the resource description. The missing versions matter substantively rather than formally, since feature extractors change output across releases; annotations_per_item=1 is also a genuine limitation the record does not hide, as single-annotator labels admit no agreement statistics.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2) with provenance flags: a standardized session where 'diagnoses were confirmed by clinicians reviewing audio and/or imaging data, electronic health records, or medication prescriptions' (was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified all true), and a derived-features entry (was_inferred_derived true). collection_mechanisms names the custom tablet application and the exact hardware: 'iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; distinct iPad devices were used at each site', plus REDCap for instruments. data_collectors (3 roles) distinguish research teams ('data was collected in the clinic with the assistance of a trained research assistant'), clinicians ('listed under the IRB as co-investigators ... provided the clinical diagnoses used as gold standard labels') and hospital staff. collection_timeframes: 'data was collected over a period of 12 months', with a caveat that no start or end dates are stated. raw_data_sources (2) give source_type, raw_data_format (WAV audio; REDCap export) and access_details including the Synapse location and DACO contact. Supported by sampling_strategies, direct_collection and collection_consents. All three named components of the 5 band are present, and methods and collectors are documented at a level well above typical: named microphone model, per-site device distinction, role-differentiated collector responsibilities, and a screening step against 'per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria before the clinic visit'. The timeframe is the weakest element and is scored as adequate rather than perfect, but the overall protocol description is complete enough to reconstruct the collection. The acquisition provenance flags are used correctly and discriminatingly: observed/reported/validated for the session, inferred/derived for the computed features, which is exactly the distinction the schema encodes. The per-site device detail is not incidental; the record itself draws the inference through to known_biases.measurement_bias, noting that distinct iPads per site confound label with apparatus. The timeframe is the one soft point, carrying an explicit warning that the 12-month figure comes from a healthsheet written against an earlier release and 'may not cover the whole of the collection behind version 3.1.0'; this is logged as a low-severity temporal warning rather than scored down, since the caveat prevents a reader from over-relying on it.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.1.0'. version_access.versions_available lists five releases with dates and, for three of them, DOIs ('1.1 - 17 January 2025 - doi:10.13026/249v-w155'; '2.0.0 - 16 April 2025'; '2.0.1 - 18 August 2025'; '3.0.0 - 16 December 2025 - doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68'; '3.1.0 - 1 May 2026 - doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'), with version_details noting that older versions remain supported by default, that 'The files for version 1.1 are no longer available from PhysioNet', and that version 1.0 sits on Health Data Nexus under doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. errata records per-version corrections (v2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and free-speech removals; v2.0.1 authorship correction; v3.1.0 broken parquet fixes, back-filled diagnoses, renamed gold standard variables). updates states a semi-annual plan, explicitly labelled 'a plan written against the Health Data Nexus platform and an earlier release, not an observed cadence'. maintainers names PhysioNet/MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, NIH support under OT2OD032720, and the consortium with the DACO contact. distribution_dates repeats the release sequence; retention_limit states indefinite retention for the published dataset. Defect: version_access.latest_version_doi is 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'. Sustainability is documented on all four indicators the rubric names: persistent identifiers per version, a governance plan through DACO and the accountable institution, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository (PhysioNet), and institutional commitment via MIT LCP hosting plus NIH award support. Versioning is otherwise comprehensive. One point is deducted for the latest_version_doi defect, which is a functional error in exactly the field a consumer uses to find the current release, compounded by two listed versions lacking DOIs. Temporal ordering across the record is coherent: the release sequence Nov 2024 -> Jan 2025 -> Apr 2025 -> Aug 2025 -> Dec 2025 -> May 2026 is monotonic, the issued date 2026-05-01 matches the 3.1.0 entry, and the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 encloses all of it. Against that, latest_version_doi 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is unresolvable from within the record: it matches no entry in versions_available, is not the top-level doi, and is not the 3.0.0 or pediatric DOI. The prefix is well formed and PhysioNet-registered, so this is a pointing error rather than a format error, but it contradicts the record's own statement that 3.1.0 is the latest version and is the single clearest internal inconsistency in the datasheet. The candour elsewhere is notable in the opposite direction: stating that v1.1 files are no longer retrievable is an admission against interest that improves the sustainability picture's reliability.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation is a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, authors and publisher: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. Distinct additional references: the Interspeech 2024 protocol-development paper (external_resources, with URL https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2024/bensoussan24_interspeech.html, and independently in related_datasets as is_documented_by 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926); the b2aiprep and SenseLab repositories; the REDCap data dictionary archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724; the documentation source archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; the Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles. Well past the 5 threshold: a formal dataset citation is present and there are at least five distinct further references, four of them DOI-linked. The Interspeech paper appearing in both external_resources and related_datasets is counted once. Each DOI prefix matches its registrar: 10.13026 PhysioNet, 10.5281 Zenodo, 10.21437 ISCA. The citation's author order is consistent with creators (Bensoussan first, Ghosh described in creators as 'senior author of the version 3.1.0 release' and appearing last), and the version in the citation matches the version field. Placing the RRID inside the citation string is conventional for PhysioNet deposits. The record notes that the project documentation calls the dataset 'self-contained' and gives no guarantees about external resources, then supplies the supporting references anyway with that qualification attached, which is the right handling.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances[0]: instance_type 'human participant', counts 833, label true with a label_description explaining clinician-assigned diagnosis and the EHR/prescription route for the psychiatric cohort, and two missing_information entries. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true; identification 'Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, and participants are assigned to disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders - or to the control group'; distribution 'The public data releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories, and the dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'. at_risk_populations: adults only, 'minimum age is 18 years and the maximum age is 120 years', assent_procedures, and cohort-specific distress risks. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling. Eligibility constraints appear in known_limitations.coverage_limitation ('eligibility required the ability to read and speak English') and sampling_strategies ('screened against per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria'). splits records that no splits are predefined. Well above the 3 band: subgroups are named, the demographic axes collected are enumerated, vulnerable-population handling is described and skew is acknowledged. It falls short of 5 because no numbers accompany any of it - no age or sex distribution, no race or ethnicity breakdown, no per-cohort participant counts - and the per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria are referenced rather than listed. The record is consistent in scoping itself to adults: the 18-120 range, the adults-only compensation note, and the routing of pediatric participants to the separate release identified as 10.13026/h995-bt35 all agree, so the 833 count is unambiguously the adult cohort. The absence of distribution figures interacts with Q20: the record documents representation bias qualitatively and tells users to 'consider the multivariate distribution', but supplies no distribution to consider, so a fairness audit cannot be performed from the datasheet alone. This is a real limitation on reuse rather than a presentational one, and is the basis for withholding the fifth point here and in Q20.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/' (repeated as access_urls on all three distribution formats); doi 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; publisher https://physionet.org/; external URLs to github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/, docs.b2ai-voice.org, isca-archive.org, w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema. Passes decisively. Findability rests on several independent, resolvable, version-specific handles rather than a single link. All URLs are structurally well formed with plausible, verifiable domains, and the landing page is version-pinned so it will continue to denote 3.1.0 after later releases. Zenodo URLs use the concept-DOI form (zenodo.org/doi/...), which resolves to the latest archived version of each repository - appropriate for code archives. The Synapse accession is given as an identifier with an explanation that no DOI exists for it, rather than a DOI being invented.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: Each distribution_formats entry carries access_urls 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'. license_and_use_terms states the tier explicitly: 'From version 3.0.0 the PhysioNet access policy is that only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the files; no additional training is required', with 'no fees'. The second tier is separated cleanly: 'Raw audio is governed separately, requiring a Data Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office and a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the recipient institution.' data_governance.access_review_process walks the whole path for both tiers and notes 'The agreement takes effect only upon review and approval by the Data Access Compliance Office, which requires a distinct application', with requests to DACO@b2ai-voice.org and audio served through Synapse. raw_data_sources repeats the Synapse URL and contact. A separate download_url field is not used. Meets the 5 band without reservation. A prospective user can determine which artifact they need, which tier governs it, which documents they must sign, who reviews the application, where to write, and that no fee applies - all from this record. The record avoids the misleading 'public/open' framing the rubric warns against: it is explicit that registered access still requires credentialing and a signed agreement, and it does not describe the release as open. Tier assignment is semantically coherent with sensitivity, escalating from credentialed registration for derived features to committee review for the biometric raw audio, and matches confidentiality_level 'restricted'. The absence of a bare download_url is correct rather than a gap, since no unauthenticated download exists and publishing one would misrepresent the access model.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms as quoted at Q9 and Q17. intended_uses (2): research use for 'the development of AI and machine-learning models for healthcare' with examples ['AI model pretraining', 'fine-tuning', 'benchmarking', 'validation'], and the agreement scope 'solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers'. prohibited_uses (3) with reasons: re-identification attempts and 'any actions that could reasonably lead to re-identification'; uses causing 'harm or stigmatization to research participants, their families, communities or specific populations'; use of IP protection to restrict access to the data or conclusions. discouraged_uses (1): 'hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance that could lead to discrimination or harm'. future_use_impacts (2): distributional skew such that 'unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups', and non-research use producing 'discrimination or harm on the basis of health conditions or voice characteristics'. The licence and use-guidance half of the band is fully met and would support 5 on its own: intended, prohibited and discouraged uses are all populated, each with reasoning rather than bare assertion, and the commercial-use position is stated unambiguously. The social-impact half is thinner. future_use_impacts has two short entries whose mitigations are either advisory ('users should consider the multivariate distribution') or restated as contractual exclusion, and the record's own data_protection_impacts states that no analysis of impact on data subjects was conducted. 'Comprehensive social impact analysis with mitigation strategies' is therefore not demonstrated. Use guidance is internally consistent and enforceable-looking: the prohibition on re-identification matches the reidentification_risk analysis and the contractual bar on contacting subjects, and the discouraged surveillance and insurance uses are echoed in future_use_impacts as the reason those applications are excluded by the agreement, so the two fields reinforce rather than duplicate. One tension is that consent_scope records the consent does not restrict commercial use while intended_uses permits commercial research - these agree, which is worth noting as a passed check rather than a conflict. The impact gap is substantive: mitigation for the documented skew depends on users assessing a distribution the record does not publish, which is the same limitation identified at Q15 and Q20.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw audio recordings of standardized acoustic tasks captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, together with questionnaire and clinical data captured in REDCap, collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol.' Entities: raw_data_sources gives WAV audio (Synapse syn72370534, controlled access) and REDCap exports; file_collections names the eleven derived outputs. Activities: preprocessing_strategies give the ordered transformation chain (mono conversion and 16 kHz resampling with Butterworth filter -> STFT spectrogram at 25 ms/10 ms/400-point -> Mel and MFCC -> sparc articulatory estimates at 50 Hz -> ppgs at 100 Hz -> openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth static features -> Whisper transcription), with cleaning_strategies giving the audit activity. Agents: b2aiprep 'version 3.0.0 generated this release', SenseLab, the data release team, and clinicians as labelling agents. Derivation path: related_datasets derives_from syn72370534 and is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68; version_access, errata and updates give version lineage; missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling; splits records that none are predefined. Meets the 5 band on the textual route the rubric expressly permits. The lineage is complete in both directions: upstream to the named raw-audio and REDCap sources with their access regimes, and downstream to specific named output files, with the transforming software and its version identified for the orchestrating tool. Version-history elements (errata, updates, version_access) are present in addition to, not instead of, the derivation graph. The lineage can be traversed file by file rather than only in the abstract, which is what distinguishes it from version history alone: file names encode their producing tool (torchaudio_*, sparc_*, ppgs) and each corresponding preprocessing_strategies entry supplies that tool's parameters, so a reader can reconstruct which activity produced which entity. Quality is carried through the same graph: audio_quality_metrics.tsv is itself released as a derived entity, and the reasons some entities are absent are stated (sensitive-record and free-speech exclusions, generation failures). The absence of a machine-readable PROV-O serialisation and of a top-level parent_datasets entry are noted as issues but do not reduce the score, since the rubric accepts complete textual lineage and the derivation targets are given as resolvable identifiers.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases (3), each typed from the controlled vocabulary: selection_bias ('recruited at a small number of high volume expert clinics; groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or who are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited') with mitigation_strategy; representation_bias ('skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors') with mitigation_strategy; measurement_bias ('participants with different labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording apparatus and site') with affected_subsets. future_use_impacts adds fairness framing: 'unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups' and discrimination risk in hiring, insurance and surveillance. Reinforced by known_limitations (representativeness, coverage, scope, temporal, integration), anomalies (3), sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and subpopulations.distribution. Clearly beyond the 3 band: biases are categorised with BiasTypeEnum-style terms rather than described loosely, two of three carry mitigations and one identifies affected subsets. The fifth point is withheld because there are no AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology mappings, and the fairness analysis is entirely qualitative - no subgroup performance or distribution statistics, and indeed no demographic distribution anywhere in the record against which fairness could be assessed. The bias types are applied correctly rather than as labels of convenience: the confounding of diagnostic label with site-specific iPad hardware is a genuine measurement bias and is a non-obvious finding that follows from the per-site device detail given in collection_mechanisms, so the taxonomy term and the evidence agree. Bias documentation is also consistent with sampling_strategies (is_representative false, with why_not_representative) and with known_limitations, so the record does not claim representativeness anywhere while conceding skew elsewhere. The weakness is circular in effect: representation_bias is documented and users are told to weigh the multivariate distribution, but because Q15's distribution figures are absent the recommended mitigation cannot actually be carried out from this datasheet.

name: Field Completeness
text: id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description ~1,900 chars; keywords: 4 terms; license_and_use_terms with data_use_permission: general_research_use; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; creators: 3 entries with PIs and 12 affiliations; purposes: 3 responses; instances: 3 instance types including counts: 833; variables: participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted. Twelve of the fourteen named slots are populated with substantive content. The two absent slots have populated equivalents: external_resources carries six sub-resources in place of `resources`, and parent lineage is carried by was_derived_from, raw_sources and related_datasets (derives_from syn72370534, is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68) in place of `parent_datasets`. Semantic coverage is therefore ≈93%. No field is populated with a placeholder. keywords is the one slot whose content, while present, is thin enough to be scored against separately at Q3; it is not counted as unpopulated here.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is a single block of roughly 1,900 characters naming the cohort (833 adults, five North American sites), the four adult disorder categories, the derived-feature inventory (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, SPARC articulatory and source measures, PPGs, pitch contours, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth statics), the phenotype directory contents, the recording setup and the credentialed access model. purposes holds three responses of roughly 190, 230 and 220 characters. Well past the >200 character band on both fields, and the length is carrying information rather than padding: the description alone answers what, who, how many, how collected, what is withheld and how to get it. Narrative content matches the claimed dataset type throughout; terms such as Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient, phonetic posteriorgram and electromagnetic articulography are used in their standard senses and at consistent sampling rates.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice — four unique terms. Four keywords places this squarely in the 3–7 band. The terms are accurate but generic; three of the four would apply to any Bridge2AI voice artefact, and none discriminates this release from the pediatric companion or from the raw-audio distribution. The rubric permits supplementing keywords with schema-defined condition lists or ontology references. Conditions are in fact enumerated, but only inside file_collections.phenotype prose and instances CURIEs (B2AI_TOPIC:36/37, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30/80), not as retrievable keywords, and no ICD-10 or SNOMED CURIEs are exposed despite labeling_strategies stating that labeling followed ICD-10 codes. The supplement therefore does not lift the score above the counted band.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats: 'Parquet' and 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries', each with access_urls to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. file_collections names nine Parquet feature files (ppgs, sparc_ema, sparc_loudness, sparc_periodicity, sparc_pitch, torchaudio_spectrogram, torchaudio_mfcc, torchaudio_pitch, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram), two TSV files (static_features.tsv, audio_quality_metrics.tsv), a Parquet metadata file, and a phenotype tree of tab-delimited tables each paired with a JSON dictionary. total_file_count absent. Three distinct types (Parquet, TSV, JSON) puts this in the 2–3 band. Enumeration quality is well above what the band implies — individual files are named and their contents described — but the count of types is what the question measures, and no media_type, encoding or compression is declared. The narrow format range is semantically appropriate rather than a defect: a feature-only release of dense tensors plus tabular phenotypes has no reason to carry DICOM, imaging or waveform containers, and the record explains that the waveforms ship elsewhere. Multimodality is achieved by shared participant_id/session_id keys across feature, metadata and phenotype tables, which the rubric's Q4 note treats as the integration signal.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances: counts: 833 participants; per-feature record counts '29,278 spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC records; 32,522 torchaudio pitch records; 28,640 articulatory records; 31,855 loudness records; 31,872 periodicity and Speech Articulatory Coding pitch records; and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram records'; variables.n_frames documents per-recording time-frame counts; splits present (user-defined); subpopulations present. Passes on instance counts, which are given at both participant and recording granularity and per feature family. No byte figure exists anywhere (total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes both absent), so size is only estimable from record counts times frame counts times feature dimensionality — a weak proxy for nine dense Parquet tensors. Pass/fail cannot express that gap, so it is recorded as a completeness issue instead.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; publisher: https://physionet.org/; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345; version_access.latest_version_doi and related_datasets carry the concept DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 and the predecessor 10.13026/k81f-qr68. Passes comfortably: a version DOI, a concept DOI, a resolvable landing page, a project page and a named domain repository are all present. Prefix 10.13026 is PhysioNet's and is consistent with publisher. Two defects noted elsewhere do not defeat the pass: latest_version_doi holds the concept rather than the 3.1.0 DOI, and RRID:SCR_007345 denotes PhysioNet rather than the dataset.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program' with grants 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and OT2OD032720, each annotated with its source, plus source_caveats reconciling PhysioNet, NIH RePORTER (3OT2OD032720-01S3, core OT2OD032720, FY2025 award 4,660,942, period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30), the feasibility publication and garbled documentation forms. creators: University of South Florida with PI Yael Bensoussan (USF Health Morsani College of Medicine), Weill Cornell Medicine with PI Olivier Elemento (Englander Institute for Precision Medicine), and the consortium with twelve named affiliations. maintainers additionally credit U24EB037545 and R01EB030362 for PhysioNet. Top band on both limbs: grant numbers are attached to a named grantor, and creators carry institutional affiliations down to department level for the two co-PIs. Both grant strings parse as NIH identifiers (OT2 activity code, OD institute, six-digit serial; 3…-01S1 as an application number with supplement suffix). The award-number divergence across sources is disclosed with a stated preference rule rather than concealed, which increases rather than reduces confidence. Funding purpose (Bridge2AI Common Fund, voice as a biomarker) aligns with the stated purposes and tasks.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: University of South Florida IRB with Single IRB subsite approvals. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, ethics_review_board named, irb_approval narrative, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA, Certificate of Confidentiality, Single IRB), special_populations listing neurodegenerative and psychiatric cohorts. is_deidentified: HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier removal, an explicit eighteen-item identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details ending 'k-anonymization with k of at least two was not achieved'. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (HIPAA firewall, password-protected REDCap, HTTPS to NIH STRIDES cloud, trained personnel), reidentification_risk ('a person's voice is unique to them'), data_linkage (EHR access under consent). participant_compensation: gift cards, $40/$80 per session, cap $120. informed_consent: written/electronic/video consent, five-year documentation retention, scope, withdrawal_mechanism. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance: Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16. Nine of the eleven protection areas are documented to a high standard, several beyond the usual depth (per-modality withholding rules, transcript review for external voices, consent re-administration for longitudinal visits). Two things hold it off the top band: no data_protection_impacts entry or equivalent DPIA, and an identifiability claim that the record's own other_compliance and k-anonymity statements contradict. Ethics claims are plausible against scope: credentialed access plus an RAA for low-risk derived features, escalating to DACO review and an institution-signed DTUA for the waveforms, is proportionate to voice's biometric character. The deidentification method suits the data type. Against that, identifiable_elements_present=false sits beside a DTUA designation of the data as PII and an admitted k<2, and sensitive_elements_present=true conflicts with the statement that REDCap-flagged sensitive fields were removed at 3.0.0. Both contradictions are partly caveated but neither is resolved for 3.1.0, and the deduction to 4 reflects them together with the missing DPIA. Canadian collection with no Canadian ethics or privacy instrument cited is recorded at Q9.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License'; license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission general_research_use, credentialed PhysioNet access with signed Registered Access Agreement, no additional training, separate controlled-access path for raw audio (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, institution-signed DTUA), commercial and non-commercial research both permitted, per-organisation application required. ip_restrictions: five clauses covering copyright non-transfer, duplication-but-not-sale, no IP claims blocking access, downstream licensing under the Fort Lauderdale Agreement, and no third-party IP restrictions. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level restricted, hipaa_compliant compliant, no export controls, credentialed-access restriction, other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16, PhysioNet requirements). Governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org appears in maintainers. retention_limit gives both hosting and recipient obligations. Every limb of the question is addressed and the IP clauses are unusually specific. The top band in the rubric text additionally requires multi-jurisdiction compliance, and that limb is not met. Restrictiveness is internally coherent: a restricted classification, a signed RAA and a two-tier access model match the sensitivity of clinically labelled voice-derived data. Two semantic gaps reduce the score. First, collection occurred in the United States and Canada, yet only United States instruments are cited for the adult cohort. Second, the governance contact lives in maintainers rather than regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact, so a consumer reading the governance block alone finds no contact. The confidentiality_level value is the record's own inference, which it flags honestly.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format', loadable by any Parquet library) and tab-delimited text with companion JSON data dictionaries whose 'keys match the column names of the table'. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to omitted by explicit decision recorded in source_caveats. related_datasets: four typed relationships (is_supplemented_by 10.13026/h995-bt35, is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68, is_version_of 10.13026/37yb-1t42, derives_from syn72370534). external_resources: docs site, b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab, bridge2ai-redcap (MIT), bridge2ai-docs (MIT), Synapse raw audio. Integration keys declared in variables (participant_id, session_id, task_name) and stated to be 'shared across the feature, metadata and phenotype tables'. Ontology CURIEs in instances (B2AI_TOPIC:36/37, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30/80); labels follow ICD-10. Formats are open and AI/ML-friendly, every table ships a machine-readable dictionary, cross-dataset links are typed and DOI-resolvable, and join keys with their cardinality are documented — which is what harmonisation actually requires. Short of the top band because no schema governs the released files themselves. conforms_to_schema names the datasheet metamodel, not a data schema, so the apparent schema conformance does not bear on the distributed artefacts; the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion is correctly scoped to the audio dataset's folder layout and deliberately not asserted here, which is semantically honest but leaves the gap open. file_collections.compression is absent for nine dense Parquet tensors. Ontology use is real but partial: B2AI CURIEs appear at instance level while the eighteen diagnosis tables and ICD-10 labels carry no codes in the record.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: mono conversion, 16 kHz resampling with Butterworth anti-aliasing; STFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled by two, 201 bins; 60 MFCCs and a 60-bin Mel spectrogram; SPARC kinematic traces for six articulators with loudness, periodicity and pitch at 50 Hz; PPGs over 40 phoneme categories at 100 Hz; openSMILE, Praat via parselmouth, torchaudio pitch; Whisper Large transcription; 'b2aiprep library, version 3.0.0 for this release' and senselab. cleaning_strategies: audit protocol (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema checks on categorical responses, audio QC on silence, duration and passage fidelity), with audio_quality_metrics.tsv added at 3.1.0. labeling_strategies: clinician diagnosis, annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, ICD-10 protocol, REDCap platform. machine_annotation_tools: eight tools with descriptions and tool_accuracy ('off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'). missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes, handling_strategy ('Missing values are left as missing rather than imputed'). Pipeline detail is reproducible to the parameter level and tools are named end to end. Held to 4 because the rubric's top band asks for software versions/URLs, annotation quality and imputation protocols: only b2aiprep carries a version, openSMILE, Praat, torchaudio, Whisper, sparc and ppgs do not, imputation_protocols is absent, and annotation_analyses is absent — annotation quality is asserted qualitatively rather than analysed. Tool-to-output mapping is correct in every case: torchaudio for spectrograms and pitch, openSMILE and Praat for statics, SPARC for articulatory estimates, ppgs for posteriorgrams, Whisper for transcription, b2aiprep and senselab for orchestration. Parameter values are mutually consistent (25 ms / 10 ms at 16 kHz yields the 400-point FFT and 201 bins stated). The absence of imputation is a documented design choice, not an omission, but no imputation_protocols entry records it in the structured slot. The cleaning contradiction with the healthsheet's 'No' answer is disclosed by the record itself.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: all four flags set with acquisition_details separating directly observed acoustics, subject-reported demographics and questionnaires, clinician-verified diagnoses and derived (not observed) released values. collection_mechanisms: Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application ('iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) using an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle') and REDCap export via an open-source consortium library. data_collectors: site research teams (recruitment, consent, supervised collection) and site clinicians (diagnosis and gold-standard validation), each with role and detail. direct_collection: is_direct true, in clinic, United States and Canada. sampling_strategies: non-probability, high-volume expert clinics, cohort-specific inclusion/exclusion screening before the visit. raw_sources: waveforms plus REDCap capture, with access_url https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/. collection_timeframes: 'twelve months', no start or end date. Four of five limbs are at top-band depth, down to microphone model and tablet generation. Timeframes are the single shortfall: an undated twelve-month figure, drawn from documentation written against earlier releases, for a cohort the record elsewhere says accumulated from 306 to 833 participants across versions. Internally coherent: the device-per-site arrangement described here is the same fact that measurement_bias reports as a cohort/device confound, and the clinician-labelling route matches labeling_strategies and instances.label_description. The record declines to infer a collection window it cannot source, and says so — the right call, but the information is still missing for a reuser trying to date the cohort.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: 3.1.0. version_access: six releases enumerated with dates and substantive changes (1.0 on Health Data Nexus with 12,523 recordings from 306 participants; 1.1 on 2025-01-17 adding MFCCs; 2.0.0 on 2025-04-16 adding 136 participants; 2.0.1 on 2025-08-18; 3.0.0 on 2025-12-16 adding 391 participants; 3.1.0 on 2026-05-01), plus 'Each version has a unique DOI, and a concept DOI resolves to the latest version' and the caveat that 1.1 files are no longer available. errata: three entries covering broken Parquet files, spectrogram reprocessing and authorship correction. updates: semi-annual cadence, new versions rather than in-place edits, notification via platform news. maintainers: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology with its own NIH support (U24EB037545, R01EB030362) and the Bridge2AI DACO. publisher: PhysioNet. retention_limit: indefinite hosting, two-year recipient destruction with written certification. All four sustainability indicators are present — persistent identifiers including a concept DOI, a governance body with a contact, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository, and documented institutional commitment via PhysioNet's own funding — alongside dated release notes and errata. Top band. Dates are strictly ordered and match distribution_dates. Two honest limits are disclosed rather than hidden: the project's own AI-readiness self-assessment scores sustainability at 50 percent, and version 1.1 files have already been withdrawn while publishers 'reserve the right to remove access to older versions'. These qualify the practice, not the documentation, which is what this question measures; the latest_version_doi mismatch is recorded as a separate consistency issue.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: a full formal citation naming twenty-plus authors, the dataset title, '(version 3.1.0)', the publisher PhysioNet, RRID:SCR_007345 and https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66. doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. external_resources: six distinct resources (docs.b2ai-voice.org, github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534). related_datasets adds three further DOI-identified references. existing_uses points to https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/. Both top-band conditions are met: far more than two distinct references, and a formal citation that identifies the dataset by title, version, authors and publishing organisation rather than a bare DOI. References are distinct resources, not repeated links, and each is characterised by role (preprocessing library, audio toolkit, REDCap dictionary, documentation source, controlled-access audio). The record cites the feasibility publication and audiomics white paper in source_caveats as sources consulted but does not give their DOIs, which is the one thing a reader wanting the associated literature would still have to hunt for; it does not affect the band.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 833 participants with label_description and three missing_information blocks. subpopulations: two entries — demographic ('Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, together with race and sexual orientation') with a distribution note that 'The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'; and disease cohort (five categories named, four plus controls in this adult release, unequal distribution acknowledged). human_subject_research.special_populations names neurodegenerative and psychiatric cohorts. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling. sampling_strategies notes screening 'against cohort-specific inclusion and exclusion criteria'. notes records the study as an observational cohort, cross-sectional, all sexes, ages 18 to 120, including healthy volunteers. file_collections.phenotype enumerates demographics, confounders and eighteen per-condition diagnosis tables. Subgroup structure is described thoroughly and vulnerable populations are named. Two things keep it off the top band: not a single demographic quantity is given — no counts or proportions by sex, age band, race, ethnicity, site or cohort, only the qualitative statement that skews exist — and the inclusion/exclusion criteria are referenced as existing rather than stated. The demographic variables said to be recorded here (socioeconomic status, sexual orientation) are among those the deidentification block says were stripped as highly sensitive, so a reuser cannot tell from this record which demographic axes are actually analysable in 3.1.0 — the same contradiction flagged at Q8, and it bears directly on the representation claim. Counts are internally consistent (833 across description, instances and the v3.0.0 note), and the pediatric cohort is correctly excluded and pointed to its own dataset.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 with concept DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42; distribution_formats access_urls to the PhysioNet release; external_resources with docs.b2ai-voice.org, four GitHub repositories and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; raw_sources.access_url; extension_mechanism.contribution_url. Well past the pass threshold, with a versioned landing page, a concept DOI for citation stability, and separate documentation, code and controlled-access endpoints. All domains are plausible and role-appropriate (physionet.org for the release, synapse.org for controlled-access audio, github.com for code, b2ai-voice.org for the project). Findability is nonetheless weakened at the keyword layer rather than the identifier layer, which Q3 records.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms: 'the access policy is credentialed: only credentialed users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement may access the files, and no additional training is required', with the separate controlled-access route for raw audio (Data Access Request Form, Data Use Agreement, DACO review, institution-signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement) and the requirement that collaborators and other teams apply independently. distribution_formats: both formats with access_urls to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ and loading guidance ('can be loaded with any library that supports Parquet'). third_party_sharing: is_shared true, mechanism described. Contact for access questions: DACO@b2ai-voice.org. The access tier is named unambiguously, the platform is identified, the agreement to be signed is named, the training requirement is negated explicitly, and the second tier for waveforms is described separately with its approval body. That is the full path the top band asks for. The record avoids the 'public/open' mislabelling the rubric warns against, calling the release credentialed rather than open, and discloses that the access model changed across versions (1.1 restricted, 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 credentialed) with the documentation's registered-access description flagged as stale. No download_url field is populated, but distribution_formats.access_urls supplies the equivalent endpoint, so the access path is complete in substance.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms as above. intended_uses: three categories (clinical ML research, pretraining and fine-tuning, voice biomarker research) each with examples and usage_notes. prohibited_uses: four reasons — re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatisation of participants, families or communities, IP protections that restrict access, and contacting subjects without IRB approval, provider approval and consent. discouraged_uses: two — non-research applications including hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment and surveillance 'that could lead to discrimination or harm', and uses that assume representativeness. future_use_impacts: two — skew by disorder category, site and demographics with the risk of 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups through stereotyping or quality-of-service failures', and the risk that models learn site or device signatures rather than disease signatures. existing_uses records prior hackathon use and a training programme. All five limbs populated with reasoned content. The impact analysis is specific about who could be harmed and how, names the mechanism rather than gesturing at 'potential misuse', and is paired with mitigation guidance (consider the multivariate distribution; treat site and device as confounds). The harm vocabulary maps onto recognised responsible-AI harm categories (allocation harms in hiring and insurance, quality-of-service failure, stereotyping), which is what CROISSANT RAI alignment asks for in substance. Prohibitions are coherent with the governance model: the re-identification and no-contact clauses restate the Registered Access Agreement, and the anti-IP-blocking clause restates the Fort Lauderdale commitment in ip_restrictions. The site/device confound warning is the same fact reported as measurement_bias, applied forward to model risk — a genuine impact analysis rather than a restatement.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw voice, speech and respiratory audio recordings and questionnaire responses collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol and exported from REDCap'. raw_sources: the same entities with access_url https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ and the note that the release contains derived features only. related_datasets: derives_from syn72370534, is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68, is_version_of the concept DOI. preprocessing_strategies: the activity chain from waveform standardisation through each feature extractor, with b2aiprep 3.0.0 and senselab as the executing software. data_collectors, creators and maintainers identify the human and institutional agents; machine_annotation_tools identifies the software agents. version_access, errata (three) and updates give the release lineage. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling. cleaning_strategies gives the QC protocol and audio_quality_metrics.tsv ships quality metrics per recording. splits: users are directed to construct their own; notes confirms no recommended splits are supplied. This is more than version history. A reader can trace any released feature file back through a named tool with named parameters to a named source entity held at a named location, with the responsible agents identified at each step — the three PROV-O elements the rubric asks for, rendered as text, which it expressly permits. Derivation is stated in the right direction and with the right scope: the release derives from the waveforms, the waveforms are not in it, and the BIDS conversion is attributed to the audio dataset rather than claimed here. Quality is evidenced by artefact (audio_quality_metrics.tsv, missingness tables) rather than assertion, and anomalies frankly records protocol drift, inter-site diagnostic variation and unaudited transcription. Nothing is machine-readable as a PROV graph, and parent_datasets is unpopulated with the linkage carried by related_datasets instead, but the lineage information itself is complete.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: four entries typed selection_bias ('Groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited'), representation_bias (five sites in the United States and Canada, fluent English speakers only), measurement_bias (site-specific iPads, varying headset distance, diagnosis by single clinician or from EHR/prescription) with affected_subsets 'Disease cohort categories, which are confounded with collection site and device', and annotation_bias (single labeler per instance, diagnostic practice varying by site, human-level task performance varying by condition). mitigation_strategy given for selection_bias (shift to remote collection, recruitment designed to control more variables) and representation_bias (Spanish expansion, remote collection). future_use_impacts adds the stereotyping and quality-of-service framing and the site/device signature risk. known_limitations adds five typed limitations reinforcing the same picture. Biases are systematically categorised with BiasTypeEnum-style values, described causally rather than nominally, and one carries affected_subsets. Held at 4 because two of the four types carry no mitigation_strategy, no AIO or CROISSANT identifiers are attached to the bias types, and the fairness analysis is entirely narrative. Each bias type is used in its correct technical sense — recruitment-driven selection, geographic and linguistic representation, instrument-driven measurement, labeler-driven annotation — and the entries corroborate rather than repeat one another: sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, known_limitations and future_use_impacts all trace to the same underlying facts without contradiction. What is missing is quantitative: the record states skews exist by cohort, site and demographics but publishes no subgroup counts, so no user can size the imbalance or check a fairness claim against it. The unquantified demographics noted at Q15 is the same gap seen from the responsible-AI side.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (12/14): id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,600 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms.license_terms 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License...'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (16 entries, most with affiliations); purposes (4 responses); instances (833 participants; recording-level feature sets); variables (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent at the schema's intended location (2/14): top-level 'resources' (file-level resources are nested inside file_collections) and 'parent_datasets' (upstream raw audio expressed as related_datasets 'derives_from' instead). Content in the populated fields is substantive rather than placeholder - description names cohorts, sites, participant count and the exact release contents; variables carry data types and identifier flags. The two gaps are locational rather than informational, which keeps this just below the 90% band. Field values are semantically coherent with one another: the id repeats the DOI, the page resolves to the same PhysioNet version, and confidentiality_level 'restricted' matches the registered-access licence. No field is filled with content belonging to another field.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is roughly 1,600 characters and specifies '833 adult participants enrolled at five clinical sites in the United States and Canada', the four disease cohorts, the tablet-and-headset protocol, and the exact released artefacts ('spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, articulatory and phonetic posteriorgram features, static acoustic features, audio quality metrics, per-recording metadata, and phenotype tables'). The four purposes.response entries run roughly 180-280 characters each; average narrative length across the two fields far exceeds 200 characters. Length here reflects information density, not padding: every clause of the description carries a checkable fact (count, sites, cohorts, withheld content, funding programme). The description correctly distinguishes what is in this release (derived features) from what is not (raw waveforms), so length is used to disambiguate the referent rather than to inflate the record.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: ['health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'] - four unique terms. Four keywords falls in the 3-7 band. The terms are apt but generic; none names a modality (spectrogram, MFCC), a condition (Parkinson's disease, COPD, dysphonia) or the field the purposes themselves coin ('audiomics'), all of which the record documents elsewhere. Discoverability is out of proportion to content: subsets and the phenotype diagnosis subfolder enumerate more than forty conditions and thirteen validated instruments, none of which surface as keywords. Scored strictly on the keywords field per the question's field list; the condition coverage is recorded as a semantic insight rather than used to lift the band.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: Three distinct released formats: Apache Parquet (9 dense feature files, e.g. 'torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet', 'sparc_ema.parquet', 'ppgs.parquet'), tab-delimited text with media_type 'text/tab-separated-values' ('static_features.tsv', 'audio_quality_metrics.tsv', phenotype tables), and JSON data dictionaries ('Every data file is accompanied by a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem'). Three file_collections (features, metadata, phenotype) with 11 individually named and dimensioned resources; WAV appears only as the withheld raw format. total_file_count is absent. Type variety sits in the 2-3 band, but the enumeration dimension of this question is exceptionally well served: each resource carries dimensions and record counts (201xT for 29,278 recordings; 40xT at 100 Hz for 29,289), and the phenotype collection is described down to subfolder and instrument level. Scored 4 as very good with the >3-type threshold unmet and total_file_count missing. Format choice is semantically appropriate to content: columnar Parquet for dense per-frame tensors, TSV for recording-level summaries and phenotype tables, JSON for dictionaries. Multi-modality claims are consistent with the description (voice, speech, breath, cough) and with the modality-specific feature families actually shipped.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances.counts: 833; per-resource record counts 29,278 (spectrogram, Mel spectrogram, MFCC), 32,522 (torchaudio pitch), 28,640 (sparc_ema), 31,855 (loudness), 31,872 (periodicity and pitch), 29,289 (ppgs); five subsets with is_subpopulation true / is_data_split false; splits documented as not predefined. No total_size_bytes or file_collections.total_bytes. Passes on instance and record counts, which are given per feature family rather than only in aggregate. Byte sizes are absent, so users can estimate scale but not storage. Differing per-feature counts are not an inconsistency: anomalies explains that 'some audio files... could not generate certain features', which matches the observed spread from 28,640 to 32,522 exactly as described.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; id: 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page: 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; publisher: 'https://physionet.org/'; version_access.latest_version_doi: 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'; citation carries 'RRID:SCR_007345'. Both required components are present: persistent identifiers (version-specific and latest-version DOIs) and the hosting platform (PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology per maintainers). DOI prefix 10.13026 is PhysioNet's registrar prefix and agrees with both publisher and page, so the identifier is not merely well-formed but registrar-consistent. The RRID is well-formed but designates the platform rather than the dataset (flagged as a low-severity correctness issue); it is not needed for the pass.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders.grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, through the Bridge2AI program' with three grant entries (OT2OD032720 with project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and an FY2025 award of 4,660,942 US dollars; 3OT2OD032720-01S1; 3OT2OD032720-01S3 with RePORTER application 11376382) plus a source_caveats note reconciling divergent identifiers. creators: 16 entries, 14 with named affiliations (University of South Florida Health Morsani College of Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Hospital for Sick Children, Washington University in St. Louis, Oregon Health & Science University, Simon Fraser University, The Hastings Center, MIT, University of Toronto, Sinai Health, University of Florida), two with principal_investigator records. maintainers additionally cite PhysioNet support under U24EB037545 and R01EB030362. Meets the top band on both limbs and exceeds it with award amounts, project periods and role descriptions per creator. The award-identifier ambiguity is disclosed rather than hidden and does not affect the core project number. Grant patterns validate: OT2OD032720 is a well-formed NIH Other Transaction award (OT2 activity code, OD institute); the -01S1/-01S3 suffixes are valid supplement application forms; U24 and R01 forms are standard. Funding purpose aligns with purposes, which name the Bridge2AI Precision Public Health aim of making voice usable as a biomarker.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: three reviewing bodies (USF IRB single-IRB process; Canadian REBs at Mount Sinai, SickKids and University of Toronto with approvals filed to USF; Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group memorandum justifying controlled access to raw audio). human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA de-identification, password-protected REDCap, NIH STRIDES cloud storage), special_populations (18-120 years; pediatric under separate protocol). is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor, with additional removal of indirect and highly sensitive elements' with an enumerated identifiers_removed list and deidentification_details ('Dates were rebased or replaced by integers'). participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk ('Voice is inherently identifiable... K-anonymization at k greater than or equal to two is not achieved'), data_linkage. participant_compensation: 40 USD under 90 minutes, 80 USD over, capped at 120 USD. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, four consent modalities, documentation retained five years, scope covering EHR access and onward sharing, withdrawal_mechanism. at_risk_populations with special_protections and an explicit caveat on undetermined status of the cognitive-impairment and psychiatric cohorts. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant 'compliant'; other_compliance names a Certificate of Confidentiality; data_governance gives the committee contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. Every protection area in the question's field list is populated with specific, checkable content rather than boilerplate. The one structural gap - no data_protection_impacts entry - is itself documented ('no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'), and its substance is partly carried by the re-identification risk statement and the published memorandum on restricting raw audio. Scored 5 with that gap recorded as a completeness issue rather than as a silent omission. Cross-field ethics logic passes in both directions: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a named method, an identifier inventory and participant_privacy protections. The de-identification method is appropriate to the data type and honestly bounded - Safe Harbor is applied to tabular phenotype data while voice waveforms, acknowledged as inherently identifiable, are withheld to a controlled tier. Restrictiveness of the licence and confidentiality level ('restricted') is proportionate to the sensitivity declared in sensitive_elements (race, sexual orientation, mental health, trauma responses).

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License. Users must be credentialed on PhysioNet and sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement... sale of all or part of the data on any media is not permitted'; data_use_permission 'general_research_use'. ip_restrictions: six enumerated clauses covering copyright, no IP claims on the data, no blocking of downstream access, downstream IP permitted subject to non-obstructive licensing, no resale, no third-party warranty. regulatory_restrictions: export controls addressed ('No export controls apply'), Data Transfer and Use Agreement obligations (safeguards, named authorized persons, five-business-day breach notification), hipaa_compliant 'compliant', confidentiality_level 'restricted', other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16, PhysioNet requirements). data_governance: committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)', accountable_organization 'University of South Florida Board of Trustees', full access_review_process for both tiers, contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. retention_limit specifies ten-year institutional retention and two-year recipient destruction with written certification. Top band on every limb, including the access tier the rubric asks evaluators to distinguish: registration plus credentialing plus signed agreement for features, and committee approval plus institutionally signed DUTA for raw audio. Governance claims are mutually consistent and proportionate: a 'restricted' confidentiality level, a registered-access licence and a separate committee-reviewed tier for the inherently identifiable modality form a coherent scheme. Multi-jurisdiction handling (US single IRB plus Canadian REBs, with Canadian genomic collection under a separate protocol) is explicitly reconciled rather than assumed.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: Standard formats: 'Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format' and tab-delimited text with JSON dictionaries. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' (with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'). Ontology term references: instances carry data_topic 'B2AI_TOPIC:36' and data_substrate 'B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69'. related_datasets: six typed relationships (is_supplemented_by, derives_from, is_new_version_of, is_described_by, is_documented_by, is_referenced_by) spanning PhysioNet, Synapse, Health Data Nexus and Zenodo. external_resources: REDCap dictionary (github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, archived at zenodo.org/records/14989503), b2aiprep, SenseLab, documentation site, FHIR profiles. Integration keys: 'Records are joined across the feature, metadata and phenotype files by participant identifier, session identifier and task name', and 'Every table is paired with a JSON data dictionary whose keys match the table's column names'. Not asserted: conforms_to for this release - source_caveats explains that BIDS conformance belongs to the raw audio distribution, 'and no conforms_to value is asserted for this release'; file_collections.compression is absent. Formats and integration capability meet the top band - open columnar and text formats, documented join keys, column-level dictionaries and typed cross-platform linkages. The schema/ontology limb is only partly met: conforms_to_schema describes the datasheet, not the data; ontology usage is limited to two B2AI term identifiers; and no domain data standard (BIDS, FHIR, OMOP) is claimed for the released tables. Scored 4 for that partial limb. The refusal to claim BIDS for this release is a correctness strength, not a weakness of honesty - the record attaches the BIDS fact to the raw audio collection where it belongs. FHIR profiles are listed as a consortium output rather than as an applied standard, so they cannot be credited as conformance. Cross-dataset linking is genuinely actionable because the same participant/session keys are stated to run across the raw-audio Synapse distribution and the PhysioNet release.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies: five entries with exact parameters - 'converting to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter'; STFT with '25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT'; 'Sixty Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients and a 60-bin Mel spectrogram'; sparc kinematic traces 'gathered at 50 Hz'; posteriorgrams 'at 100 Hz'; openSMILE, Parselmouth/Praat; 'Transcriptions were generated using the OpenAI Whisper Large model'. cleaning_strategies: audit protocol with missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema validation of categorical responses, audio QC (silence, duration, produced-versus-intended speech), 'Processing is performed with the b2aiprep and SenseLab toolkits'. labeling_strategies: clinical assessment protocol, annotations_per_item 1, data_annotation_protocol ('Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes'), annotator_demographics. machine_annotation_tools: eight named tools with per-tool descriptions and 'this release was generated with b2aiprep version 3.0.0', plus the caveat that off-the-shelf models 'have not been audited for correctness, so no accuracy figures are available'. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('A missingness table is included with the dataset... No imputation was performed'). Top band: strategies are comprehensive and parameterised to the level needed for reproduction, tool URLs are supplied via external_resources, and the pipeline version is pinned. Annotation quality is addressed both positively (one clinician label per instance, gold-standard validation per disorder) and negatively (transcription models unaudited). Imputation is addressed by an explicit statement that none was performed, which is the correct answer rather than a gap. Technical terms are used correctly and consistently: window/hop/FFT parameters are coherent at 16 kHz (25 ms = 400 samples, matching the 400-point FFT), the 60-bin Mel spectrogram matches the 60 MFCCs, and the twelve sparc EMA channels are correctly described as X and Y positions of six articulators. Tool-to-output attributions match the file-level resource descriptions exactly (torchaudio for spectrogram/MFCC/pitch, sparc for EMA/loudness/periodicity, ppgs for posteriorgrams).

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: all four provenance flags set with acquisition_details distinguishing directly observed audio, subject-reported questionnaires, derived features and clinician-verified diagnoses. collection_mechanisms: three entries - the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application; hardware ('iPads of the 9th or 10th generation and iPad Air of the 5th generation, with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle. Distinct iPad devices were used at each site'); REDCap capture and export. data_collectors: two role entries covering research teams and trained research assistants, and co-investigator clinicians supplying and validating diagnoses. raw_data_sources: three sources with types, formats and access routes. sampling_strategies: non-probability purposive recruitment from 'high volume expert clinics defined as outpatient clinics... seeing more than fifty patients a month from the same disease category', with is_representative false and why_not_representative. direct_collection, collection_consents and collection_notifications (approximately thirty minutes of consent explanation with teach-back) are all populated. collection_timeframes: only 'the data was collected over a period of twelve months', with source_caveats conceding 'No absolute collection start or end date is stated for the version 3.1.0 release'. Methods and collectors are documented at full-band quality, including hardware specifics that matter for acoustic reuse. The timeframe limb is the single shortfall: a bare twelve-month statement, self-flagged as possibly describing an earlier version, leaves the collection window for the 833 released participants unknown. Scored 4 because the top band requires methods, collectors and timeframes together. Collection detail is internally consistent with the bias record: distinct per-site iPads appear both as a collection mechanism and as the stated cause of measurement_bias, and clinic-based purposive recruitment appears both in sampling_strategies and as selection_bias. The record also correctly excludes remote collection from mechanisms because documentation states it did not occur for the released data, resisting an inference the IRB protocol would have permitted.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '3.1.0'. version_access: five versions listed with per-version DOIs (10.13026/249v-w155, 10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/8xbn-nq66) and a latest-version resolver (10.13026/37yb-1t42), a per-version changelog ('version 2.0 added 136 new participants and reprocessed spectrograms; version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list; version 3.0.0 added 391 participants... version 3.1.0... fixed broken parquet files, added audio quality metrics'), and an older-version support policy. errata: enumerated corrections per release. updates: frequency 'Semi-annual' with notification channels and the statement that releases are static versions. distribution_dates: five dated releases from 2025-01-17 to 2026-05-01. maintainers: three, including 'MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology... supported by... grants U24EB037545 and R01EB030362', the DACO curation office, and the consortium release team. publisher PhysioNet (domain-appropriate biomedical repository); retention_limit 'Indefinite for the archived dataset'; extension_mechanism with a contribution URL. All four sustainability indicators are present - persistent identifiers at version granularity, a long-term governance plan (DACO plus USF accountable organization plus retention policy), a domain-appropriate repository, and institutional commitment evidenced by named preservation funding for the host. Versioning documentation is unusually complete, with dates, DOIs and substantive change notes per release. Temporal ordering across releases is internally valid and monotonic (2025-01-17, 2025-04-16, 2025-08-18, 2025-12-16, 2026-05-01) and agrees with issued '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z' for version 3.1.0. The record's own notes disclose a consortium self-assessment scoring sustainability at 50 per cent; the datasheet's documentation of sustainability is nonetheless complete on the criteria this question names.

name: Associated Publications
text: Formal dataset citation naming authors, title, version, publishing organization and DOI: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. Distinct additional references: Rameau et al. (2024) Interspeech, doi 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926; Moothedan et al. (2025) Front Digit Health, doi 10.3389/fdgth.2025.1514971; Bensoussan et al. (2024) JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg, doi 10.1001/jamaoto.2023.4807; plus six external_resources with URLs and two Zenodo archival DOIs (zenodo.org/records/14989503, 10.5281/zenodo.13834653). Well past the top band: a formal, attributable dataset citation plus at least three DOI-bearing publications and multiple archived code/documentation resources, each annotated with its relation to the dataset (protocol paper, feasibility study, programmatic statement). Reference typing is semantically correct: the protocol paper is recorded as is_documented_by, the feasibility and agenda papers as is_referenced_by, and the record notes that the feasibility study 'contributed no data to this dataset' - a distinction that prevents a reader from mistaking a cited study for a data source.

name: Human Subject Representation
